children.translated_text: May the lotus feet of <s>Bhava</s>, by whom the elephants of the quarters were flung aside in the display of his fierce <s>tāṇḍava</s> dance,
serve for the breaking of obstacles.
When, from the blow of whose tail as he sprang up from <s>Pātāla</s>, the abodes of makaras were driven upward and fell in confusion amid the fragments of the cosmic egg,

children.text: viṣṇormatsyāvatāre sakalavasumatīmaṇḍalaṃ vyaśnuvānās tasyāsyodīritānāṃ dhvanir apaharatād aśriyaṃ vaḥ śrutīnām
children.translated_text: may the sound uttered from the mouth of that fish incarnation of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, spreading over the whole circle of the earth, remove the misfortune of your ears.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and also to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,

children.text: devīṃ sarasvatīṃ caiva tato jayam udīrayet ||
children.translated_text: and likewise to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, one should then proclaim victory.
Though unborn, he is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> through his connection with action;
homage to that self-born one, who consists of the three qualities and the three Vedas.
The sages dwelling in <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s> approached <s>Sūta</s>, who was seated with concentrated mind,
and at the end of the long sacrificial session asked about the extensive compilation.
When the ancient stories, righteous and graceful, had begun
and <s>Śaunaka</s> and the others had again and again expressed their delight in them,
they said: The purāṇas which you have told us, sinless one,
those very nectar-like accounts we wish to hear again.
How did the blessed lord, lord of the worlds, create the moving and unmoving universe,
and for what reason did the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> assume the form of a fish?

children.text: bhairavatvaṃ bhavasyāpi purāritvaṃ ca kena hi
children.translated_text: And by what means did <s>Bhava</s> become <s>Bhairava</s>, and how did he become the destroyer of the cities?
For what reason did the bull-bannered one take on the state of a skull-bearer?

children.text: sarvam etat samācakṣva sūta vistaraśaḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: Tell all this fully, <s>Sūta</s>, in order;
from your words, as from nectar, no satisfaction arises here.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: puṇyaṃ pavitram āyuṣyam idānīṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Now listen, twice-born ones, to the meritorious, purifying, life-giving
entire <s>Matsya</s> Purāṇa, which <s>Gadādhara</s> proclaimed.

children.text: purā rājā manur nāma cīrṇavān vipulaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: In former times there was a king named <s>Manu</s>, who practiced great austerity;
having installed his son in the kingdom, the patient son of the Sun did so.
In one region of <s>Malaya</s>, endowed with all virtues of the self,
the hero, equal in sorrow and happiness, attained supreme yoga.
After a hundred myriad years had passed, the boon-giver appeared to him,

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva provāca prītaḥ sa kamalāsanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the lotus-seated one, pleased, said, Choose a boon.
Thus addressed, the king bowed to the grandsire and said:
I desire from you only one unsurpassed boon.
When the dissolution has arrived, may I be able to protect
the whole multitude of beings, both stationary and moving.
So be it, said the soul of the universe, and he disappeared there itself.
A great shower of flowers, offered by the gods, fell from the sky.
Once, while he was performing the offering to the ancestors in his hermitage,
a small fish with water fell upon his hands.
Seeing it in the form of a little fish, that compassionate king
made an effort to protect it in the hollow of his hand.
In a single day and night it became sixteen finger-breadths wide
in the form of a fish, and said, Protect me, protect me.
Taking that water-moving creature, he put it into a jar,
and there too, in a single night, it grew to three cubits.
Again, with a cry of distress, that fish addressed the son of the thousand-rayed Sun:

children.text: sa matsyaḥ pāhi pāhīti tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Protect me, protect me; I have gone to you for refuge.

children.text: tataḥ sa kūpe taṃ matsyaṃ prāhiṇod ravinandanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the son of the Sun sent that fish into a well;

children.text: yadā na māti tatrāpi kūpe matsyaḥ sarovare ||
children.translated_text: when the fish did not fit even there in the well, he put it in a lake.
Thrown there, it again attained a vastness measuring a yojana,

children.text: tatrāpyāha punar dīnaḥ pāhi pāhi nṛpottama ||
children.translated_text: and there too, helpless, it again said, Protect me, protect me, best of kings.
Then, when <s>Manu</s> had thrown it into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, it grew even there;
thereupon the lord of the earth cast it into the ocean.
When it had filled the entire ocean and stood there,
then <s>Manu</s>, frightened, said: Who indeed are you, mighty lord?
Or are you <s>Vāsudeva</s>? How could anyone else be such as this?
Whose body could be equal to twenty thousand yojanas?
I know you: in fish form you are troubling me, <s>Keśava</s>.
<s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, lord of the world, abode of the world, homage to you.
Thus addressed, that blessed <s>Janārdana</s> in fish form
said, Good, good; you have recognized me correctly, sinless one.
In a very short time, O lord of the earth, the earth,
with its mountains, forests, and groves, will be submerged in water.
This boat has been fashioned by the whole company of all the gods
for the protection of the great multitude of living beings, O lord of the earth.

children.text: svedāṇḍajodbhido ye vai ye ca jīvā jarāyujāḥ
children.translated_text: Those beings born from sweat, eggs, sprouts,

children.text: asyāṃ nidhāya sarvāṃs tān anāthān pāhi suvrata ||
children.translated_text: and those living beings born from wombs: place all those helpless ones in it and protect them, good-vowed one.
When the boat, O king, is struck by the winds at the end of the age,
then, great king, you shall fasten it to this horn of mine.

children.text: tato layānte sarvasya sthāvarasya carasya ca
children.translated_text: Then, at the end of the dissolution of all things, stationary and moving,
you will become the <s>Prajāpati</s> of the world, O lord of the earth.
Thus, at the beginning of the <s>Kṛta</s> age, all-knowing and steadfast king,
you will also become the lord of a <s>manvantara</s>, worshipped by the gods.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus addressed by him, <s>Manu</s> asked <s>Madhusūdana</s>:
Blessed lord, after how many years will the destruction of the interval occur?

children.text: sattvāni ca kathaṃ nātha rakṣiṣye madhusūdana
children.translated_text: And how, lord, shall I protect the beings, <s>Madhusūdana</s>?

children.text: tvayā saha punaryogaḥ kathaṃ vā bhavitā mama ||
children.translated_text: And how will my reunion with you
come about?
The Fish said: From today onward there will be drought upon the earth.
For a full hundred years and more there will be a famine bringing misfortune.
Then seven terrible rays, causing the destruction of beings of little strength,
belonging to the seven-horsed sun, will become showers of heated embers.
The <s>Aurva</s> fire too will undergo transformation at the end of the age,
and the poisonous fire, fallen from the mouth of <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, will come from the netherworld,
as will the fire of the third eye, arisen from the forehead of <s>Bhava</s>.
Burning the three worlds, it will burst forth in upheaval, O great sage.

children.text: evaṃ dagdhā mahī sarvā yadā syādbhasmasaṃnibhā ||
children.translated_text: When the whole earth, thus burned, has become like ashes,
the sky, heated by the heat, will become intensely hot, O scorcher of foes.
Then the world, together with the gods and the stars, will go to destruction.
<s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Bhīmanāda</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, fierce <s>Caṇḍa</s>, and <s>Balāhaka</s>,
<s>Vidyutpatāka</s> and the red <s>Śoṇa</s>: these seven are the rain-clouds of dissolution.
Born from the sweat of the fire, they will flood the earth.
The oceans, having entered into turbulence and standing as one,
will make all this threefold world a single ocean.
Taking this boat of the <s>Vedas</s> and all the seeds of beings,
placing them on board with the rope given by me, O man of good vows,
and fastening the boat to my horn, you will be protected by me in fish-form.
You alone will remain among the gods, even when they have been burned, O scorcher of foes.
<s>Brahmā</s>, bearing the moon and sun and accompanied by the four worlds,

children.text: narmadā ca nadī puṇyā mārkaṇḍeyo mahānṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: the holy river <s>Narmadā</s>, and the great seer <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>,
<s>Bhava</s>, the <s>Vedas</s>, and the Purāṇas, surrounded on every side by the sciences,
this universe will remain together with you during the intermediate dissolution.
When the single ocean has thus arisen at the dissolution of the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> interval,
I shall set the <s>Vedas</s> in motion at the beginning of your creation, O king.
Having spoken thus, the blessed one vanished on that very spot.
<s>Manu</s> too entered into yoga born from the grace of <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
practicing it until the previously foretold flood of beings.
When the time described had arrived, just as it had been spoken from the mouth of <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
<s>Janārdana</s>, horned and in the form of a fish, then appeared.
A serpent, in the form of a rope, came to <s>Manu</s>'s side.
Drawing all beings together and placing them on board by yoga, the knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
fastened the boat to the fish's horn with the serpent-rope.
Standing upon it, he bowed down to <s>Janārdana</s>.
When that flood of beings had passed, by the one who reclines in yoga,
the Purāṇa was spoken in fish-form, after he had been questioned by <s>Manu</s>.
That I shall now recite; listen, best of seers.
That creation and the rest about which you formerly asked me, O twice-born ones,
that very thing <s>Manu</s> asked <s>Keśava</s> in that single ocean.
<s>Manu</s> said:
Creation and dissolution, lineages and manvantaras,
the accounts of those born in the lineages, and the extent of the world,
the rule concerning the <s>dharma</s> (duty) of gifts and the eternal procedure for śrāddha,
the division of varṇas and āśramas, and likewise what is called iṣṭāpūrta,
the installation of deities and whatever else exists upon the earth,
all that <s>dharma</s> (sacred law) you should explain in detail.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
At the end of the time of the great dissolution this was filled with darkness,
as if asleep, beyond reasoning, unrecognized, without distinguishing mark.

children.text: avijñeyam avijñātaṃ jagat sthāsnu cariṣṇu ca
children.translated_text: The world, both stationary and moving, was unknowable and unknown.
Then the self-born, unmanifest source of meritorious deeds,
manifesting all this, appeared as the dispeller of darkness.

children.text: yo 'tīndriyaḥ paro vyaktād aṇur jyāyān sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: He who is beyond the senses, higher than the manifest, subtler than an atom, greater, and eternal,

children.text: nārāyaṇa iti khyātaḥ sa ekaḥ svayam udbabhau ||
children.translated_text: known as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, arose by himself alone.
He, reflecting from his own body and desiring to create the manifold world,

children.text: apa eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryam avāsṛjata ||
children.translated_text: first created the waters and cast his seed into them.
That became a great egg made of gold and silver,
shining like ten thousand suns after a thousand years.
Entering inside it, the self-born one of great splendor,

children.text: prabhāvād api tadvyāptyā viṣṇutvam agamat punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: again attained the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by his power and by pervading it.
Within it this blessed one formerly became the sun,
and, being <s>Āditya</s> because he was the first being, he became <s>Brahmā</s>, reciting brahman.
He made heaven and earth from the two halves of that egg,

children.text: sa cākaroddiśaḥ sarvā madhye vyoma ca śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: and he made all the directions, with the eternal sky in the middle.
<s>Manu</s> said:
Ah, this union with one born from one's own limb is very difficult, O lord.
How did the lotus-born one not incur fault through this act?

children.text: parasparaṃ ca sambandhaḥ sagotrāṇām abhūt katham
children.translated_text: And how was there a mutual marital relation among those of the same gotra,
among their children? Remove my doubt, O lord.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
This primordial creation is divine, arising from the quality of rajas,
with senses beyond the senses, and likewise with bodies beyond the senses.
It is made of divine splendor, O king, and born from divine knowledge.

children.text: na martyairabhitaḥ śakyā vaktuṃ vai māṃsacakṣubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It cannot be fully described by mortals with eyes of flesh.
Just as serpents know the path of snakes, and birds know the sky,

children.text: vidanti mārgaṃ divyānāṃ divyā eva na mānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so divine beings alone know the path of divine beings, not humans.
For the gods there is no distinction of what should or should not be done that yields auspicious or inauspicious fruit.
Therefore, O king of men, inquiry into that is not beneficial for human beings.
Moreover, the four-faced one is the presiding lord of all the <s>Vedas</s>,
and <s>Gāyatrī</s> likewise is declared to be a limb of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Whether formless or possessing form, they call that a pair.
Where the blessed <s>Viriñci</s> is, there is the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: bhāratī yatra yatraiva tatra tatra prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and wherever <s>Bhāratī</s> is, there indeed is <s>Prajāpati</s>.
Just as sunlight is nowhere seen to be without shadow,
so <s>Gāyatrī</s> never leaves the side of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> is remembered as the mass of the Vedas, and <s>Sāvitrī</s> presides over that;
therefore, lord, there should be no fault in going to <s>Sāvitrī</s>.
Even so, in ancient times <s>Prajāpati</s>, bent down with shame,
<s>Brahmā</s>, because he had approached his own daughter, cursed <s>Kusumāyudha</s>.
"Because my mind, overpowered by you, has been agitated by your arrows,
therefore <s>Rudra</s> will soon burn your body to ashes."
Then <s>Kāmadeva</s> tried to appease the four-faced one:
"Honorer of others, you ought not to curse me here without cause.
Four-faced lord, I was created in just this form by you yourself,
as one who produces agitation in the senses of all embodied beings.
By me, everywhere and always, without distinction between women and men,

children.text: kṣobhyaṃ manaḥ prayatnena tvayaivoktaṃ purā vibho ||
children.translated_text: the mind is to be stirred with effort; lord, this was formerly commanded by you yourself.
Therefore I am without offense, though cursed by you, lord.
Blessed one, show favor so that I may regain my own body."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
"When the <s>Vaivasvata</s> age has arrived, one born in the lineage of <s>Yadu</s>,
a mortal named <s>Rāma</s>, relying on my essential strength,
will descend as a destroyer of demons and dwell in <s>Dvārakā</s>;
then you will become the son of his brother, who is equal to him.
Having obtained a body in this way and enjoyed pleasures completely,
then, at the end of the <s>Bharata</s> lineage, becoming the son of king <s>Vatsa</s>,
and obtaining the lordship of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> and enjoyments, in accordance with <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
until the dissolution of beings, you will come to my presence."
Thus <s>Kusumāyudha</s>, affected by both curse and favor,
joined with sorrow and joy, went away as he had come.
<s>Manu</s> said:
"Who is that one called <s>Yadu</s>, in whose lineage <s>Kāma</s> is to be born?

children.text: kathaṃ ca dagdho rudreṇa kimatha kusumāyudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And how was <s>Kusumāyudha</s> burned by <s>Rudra</s>, and for what reason?

children.text: bharatasyānvaye kasya kā ca sṛṣṭiḥ purābhavat
children.translated_text: In the lineage of <s>Bharata</s>, whose son was he, and what creation took place in ancient times?

children.text: etatsarvaṃ samācakṣva mūlataḥ saṃśayo hi me ||
children.translated_text: Tell me all this from the root, for I have a doubt."
<s>Matsya</s> said:
That <s>Gāyatrī</s>, speaker of sacred knowledge, who was born from half his body,
the goddess <s>Śatarūpā</s>, mother of <s>Manu</s>, possessed of a hundred powers of sense,
was pleasure, mind, austerity, intellect, greatness, and bewilderment in the directions;
then he begot seven children on <s>Śatarūpā</s>.
The mind-born sons of that wise one, beginning with <s>Marīci</s>,
were in ancient times this world whose nature was all knowledge.
Then he created <s>Vāmadeva</s>, bearer of the boon-giving trident,
and the powerful <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, the ancestor even of the ancients.
But the blessed <s>Vāmadeva</s> created Brahmins from his mouth,
Kṣatriyas from his arms, and Vaiśyas and Śūdras from his thighs and feet.
He also created lightning, thunderbolts, clouds, ruddy lights, and rainbows,

children.text: chandāṃsi ca sasarjādau parjanyaṃ ca tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: and in the beginning the meters; after that he created <s>Parjanya</s>.
Then the lord again created the hosts of <s>Sādhyas</s>, three-eyed ones,
eighty-four crores of them, free from old age and death.
When <s>Vāma</s> created those immortals, he was restrained by <s>Brahmā</s>:
"Creation should not be of this kind, free from old age and death.

children.text: śubhāśubhātmikā yā tu saiva sṛṣṭiḥ praśasyate
children.translated_text: Only that creation which has the nature of both good and bad is praised."

children.text: evaṃ sthitaḥ sa tenādau sṛṣṭeḥ sthāṇurato'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: Thus he remained at the beginning of creation; because of that he became <s>Sthāṇu</s>.
The wise <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>, having performed very difficult austerity,
obtained as wife a woman rich in beauty, named <s>Anantā</s> by name.
On her <s>Manu</s> begot <s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s>,

children.text: dharmasya kanyā caturā sūnṛtā nāma bhāminī ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Dharma</s>'s clever daughter, the lovely one named <s>Sūnṛtā</s>.
From <s>Uttānapāda</s> that slow-stepping woman obtained sons:
<s>Apasyati</s>, <s>Apasyanta</s>, <s>Kīrtimanta</s>, and also <s>Dhruva</s>.
<s>Uttānapāda</s>, the <s>Prajāpati</s>, begot them on <s>Sūnṛtā</s>.

children.text: dhruvo varṣasahasrāṇi trīṇi kṛtvā tapaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: In ancient times <s>Dhruva</s>, after practicing austerity for three thousand years,
obtained a divine, immovable station by the boon of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: tameva purataḥ kṛtvā dhruvaṃ saptarṣayaḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Setting that very <s>Dhruva</s> before them, the Seven Seers stand fixed.

children.text: dhanyā nāma manoḥ kanyā dhruvācchiṣṭam ajījanat
children.translated_text: <s>Dhanyā</s>, a daughter of <s>Manu</s>, begot <s>Śiṣṭa</s> from <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: agnikanyā tu succhāyā śiṣṭātsā suṣuve sutān ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Succhāyā</s>, daughter of <s>Agni</s>, bore sons from <s>Śiṣṭa</s>:

children.text: kṛpaṃ ripuṃ jayaṃ vṛttaṃ vṛkaṃ ca vṛkatejasam
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Ripu</s>, <s>Jaya</s>, <s>Vṛtta</s>, <s>Vṛka</s>, and <s>Vṛkatejas</s>.
On <s>Vīriṇī</s>, granddaughter of <s>Brahmā</s>, that conqueror of enemies begot <s>Cakṣuṣa</s>.
On the daughter of <s>Vīraṇa</s>, <s>Cakṣuṣa</s> begot <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: manur vai rājakanyāyāṃ naḍvalāyāṃ sa cākṣuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Cākṣuṣa Manu</s>, on the royal daughter <s>Naḍvalā</s>,
begot ten sons, heroic and stainless:
<s>Ūru</s>, <s>Pūru</s>, <s>Śatadyumna</s>, <s>Tapasvī</s>, <s>Satyavāk</s>, and <s>Havi</s>;
<s>Agniṣṭut</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Sudyumna</s>, and <s>Aparājita</s>;
and <s>Abhimanyu</s>, the tenth, was born from <s>Naḍvalā</s>.

children.text: ūror ajanayat putrān ṣaḍ āgneyī tu suprabhān
children.translated_text: The <s>Āgneyī</s> <s>Suprabhā</s> bore six sons from <s>Ūru</s>:
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Sumanas</s>, <s>Khyāti</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and <s>Gaya</s>.
<s>Sunīthā</s>, daughter of the Fathers, bore <s>Vena</s> from <s>Aṅga</s>.
Because <s>Vena</s> was unjust, the Brahmins churned him; from his hand arose

children.text: pṛthurnāma mahātejāḥ sa putrau dvāv ajījanat ||
children.translated_text: the greatly brilliant one named <s>Pṛthu</s>; he begot two sons.
<s>Antardhāna</s> begot <s>Mārīca</s> on <s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s>.
From <s>Havirdhāna</s>, the <s>Āgneyī</s> <s>Dhiṣaṇā</s> bore six sons:

children.text: prācīnabarhiṣaṃ sāṅgaṃ yamaṃ śukraṃ balaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>, <s>Sāṅga</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Bala</s>, and <s>Śubha</s>.
There was the blessed and great <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>.
Through him many offspring called the <s>Havirdhānas</s> were brought forth.
And in <s>Savarṇā</s>, daughter of the ocean, the lord begot ten sons.
All of them were named the <s>Pracetases</s>, and they had mastered the science of archery.
The trees, protected by their austerity, grew everywhere in the world.
But at the command of the gods, fire burned them, O delight of the <s>Draviṇas</s>.
The daughter of <s>Soma</s>, famous by the name <s>Mārīṣā</s>, became their wife.

children.text: tebhyastu dakṣamekaṃ sā putram agryam ajījanat ||
children.translated_text: From them she bore one excellent son, <s>Dakṣa</s>.
After <s>Dakṣa</s>, the daughter of <s>Soma</s> produced the trees and all the herbs
in every way, and also the river <s>Candravatī</s>.
And that <s>Dakṣa</s>, who was a portion of <s>Soma</s>, had eighty crores of daughters.

children.text: vakṣye tāsāṃ tu vistāraṃ loke yaḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell the extent of them, which is well established in the world.
Some became two-footed, and some men became many-footed.
Some had wrinkled faces, some had pointed ears, and some had ears serving as coverings.
Some had faces of horses or bears, and some had faces of lions.
Some had faces of dogs or boars, and some had faces of camels.
That righteous one produced all the <s>mlecchas</s> in many forms.

children.text: sa sṛṣṭvā manasā dakṣaḥ striyaḥ paścādajījanat ||
children.translated_text: Having first created by mind, <s>Dakṣa</s> afterwards produced women.

children.text: dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa
children.translated_text: He gave ten to <s>Dharma</s> and thirteen to <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
He gave twenty-seven, known as the lunar mansions, to <s>Soma</s>.
From them the whole world arose, including gods, asuras, and human beings.
The seers said:
Tell us in full, <s>Sūta</s>, the origin of the gods, <s>Dānavas</s>,
<s>Gandharvas</s>, serpents, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, exactly as it occurred.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The creation of the earlier beings is said to have come from resolve, sight, and touch.
After <s>Dakṣa Prācetasa</s>, creation arose from sexual union.

children.text: prajāḥ sṛjeti vyādiṣṭaḥ pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ svayambhuvā
children.translated_text: Previously <s>Dakṣa</s> had been commanded by <s>Svayambhū</s>, Create offspring.

children.text: yathā sasarja caivādau tathaiva śṛṇuta dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Listen, brahmins, to how he first created them.
When, as he was creating hosts of gods, seers, and serpents,
the world did not increase, then through sexual union
<s>Dakṣa</s> begot thousands of sons in <s>Pāñcajanī</s>.

children.text: tāṃs tu dṛṣṭvā mahābhāgaḥ sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing them, the very fortunate <s>Nārada</s>, wishing for varied creatures to be created,
spoke to the assembled <s>Haryaśvas</s>, the sons of <s>Dakṣa</s>:

children.text: bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvatra jñātvordhvam adha eva ca
children.translated_text: First learn the measure of the earth everywhere, above and below,
and then, best of seers, perform creation in its distinct forms.

children.text: te tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prayātāḥ sarvato diśam
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech, they set out in every direction.
Even today they do not return, like rivers from the ocean.
When the <s>Haryaśvas</s> had disappeared, <s>Dakṣa</s> the <s>Prajāpati</s> again
created a thousand sons in <s>Vairiṇī</s> herself, O lord.

children.text: śabalā nāma te viprāḥ sametāḥ sṛṣṭihetavaḥ
children.translated_text: Those brahmins, named the <s>Śabalas</s>, assembled as causes of creation.
<s>Nārada</s> followed them and again spoke to them just as before:

children.text: bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvatra jñātvā bhrātṝn atho punaḥ
children.translated_text: Learn the measure of the earth everywhere, and then again learn about your brothers.

children.text: āgatya cātha sṛṣṭiṃ ca kariṣyatha viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After returning, you will then perform creation in its distinct forms.
They too went then by that very path, the path of their brothers.

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti na bhrātuḥ kanīyānmārgam icchati
children.translated_text: From that time onward a younger brother does not desire the path of his elder brother.
Seeking him out, he meets with suffering; therefore one should avoid that course.
Then, when they too had vanished, <s>Dakṣa Prācetasa</s> the <s>Prajāpati</s>
begot sixty daughters in <s>Vairiṇī</s>.
He gave ten to <s>Dharma</s> and thirteen to <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
He gave twenty-seven to <s>Soma</s> and four to <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>.

children.text: dve caiva bhṛguputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya dhīmate
children.translated_text: He gave two to the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and two to wise <s>Kṛśāśva</s>.
Likewise he gave two to <s>Aṅgiras</s>. Hear their names in full,
and the expansion of the mothers of the gods from the beginning.

children.text: marutvatī vasur yāmī lambā bhānur arundhatī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Marutvatī</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Yāmī</s>, <s>Lambā</s>, <s>Bhānu</s>, and <s>Arundhatī</s>,

children.text: saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca bhāminī
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃkalpā</s>, <s>Muhūrtā</s>, <s>Sādhyā</s>, <s>Viśvā</s>, and <s>Bhāminī</s>
are declared to be the wives of <s>Dharma</s>. Learn of their sons.
The <s>Viśve Devas</s> came from <s>Viśvā</s>, and <s>Sādhyā</s> gave birth to the <s>Sādhyas</s>.
From <s>Marutvatī</s> came the <s>Marutvants</s>, and from <s>Vasu</s> likewise came the <s>Vasus</s>.
From <s>Bhānu</s> came the <s>Bhānus</s>, and likewise from <s>Muhūrtā</s> the <s>Muhūrtakas</s>.
From <s>Lambā</s> came those named <s>Ghoṣas</s>, while <s>Nāgavīthī</s> was born from <s>Yāmī</s>.
That which arose on the surface of the earth was born from <s>Arundhatī</s>.
From <s>Saṃkalpā</s> came <s>Saṃkalpa</s>. Now learn the creation of the <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: jyotiṣmantastu ye devā vyāpakāḥ sarvato diśam
children.translated_text: Those gods who are luminous and pervade all directions
are called the <s>Vasus</s>; learn their creation.
<s>Āpa</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Dhara</s>, <s>Anila</s>, <s>Anala</s>,
<s>Pratyūṣa</s>, and <s>Prabhāsa</s> are proclaimed as the eight <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: āpasya putrāś catvāraḥ śānto vai daṇḍa eva ca
children.translated_text: The four sons of <s>Āpa</s> were <s>Śānta</s>, <s>Daṇḍa</s>,
<s>Śāmba</s>, and <s>Maṇivaktra</s>; they were charged with guarding the sacrifice.
The son of <s>Dhruva</s> was <s>Kāla</s>, and from <s>Soma</s> was born <s>Varcas</s>.
<s>Draviṇa</s> and <s>Havyavāha</s> are remembered as the two sons of <s>Dhara</s>.

children.text: kalyāṇinyāṃ tataḥ prāṇo ramaṇaḥ śiśiro'pi ca
children.translated_text: Then in <s>Kalyāṇī</s> were born <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Ramaṇa</s>, and <s>Śiśira</s>.
<s>Manoharā</s>, daughter of <s>Hari</s>, obtained sons from <s>Dhara</s>.
<s>Śivā</s> obtained from <s>Anala</s> two sons, <s>Manojava</s>
and <s>Avijñātagati</s>, again having qualities like fire.
<s>Kumāra</s>, the son of fire, was born in a thicket of reeds.

children.text: tasya śākho viśākhaśca naigameyaś ca pṛṣṭhajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: His sons, born from his back, were <s>Śākha</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, and <s>Naigameya</s>.

children.text: apatyaṃ kṛttikānāṃ tu kārttikeyas tataḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as the offspring of the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, he is remembered as <s>Kārttikeya</s>.

children.text: pratyūṣasa ṛṣiḥ putro vibhur nāmnātha devalaḥ
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Pratyūṣa</s> was the seer named <s>Vibhu</s>, and then <s>Devala</s>.
<s>Viśvakarmā</s>, son of <s>Prabhāsa</s>, was the artisan and <s>Prajāpati</s>.
In temples, mansions, gardens, images, ornaments, and the like,
and in ponds, parks, and wells, he is remembered as the carpenter of the immortals.
<s>Ajaikapād</s>, <s>Ahirbudhnya</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, and then <s>Raivata</s>,
<s>Hara</s>, <s>Bahurūpa</s>, <s>Tryambaka</s>, and <s>Sureśvara</s>,
<s>Sāvitra</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Pinākī</s>, and <s>Aparājita</s>:
these are named as the eleven <s>Rudras</s>, lords of the hosts.
Of these mind-born ones, bearers of trident and boon-bestowing hand,
their sons are considered inexhaustible, eighty-four crores in number.

children.text: dikṣu sarvāsu ye rakṣāṃ prakurvanti gaṇeśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: In all the directions those lords of hosts provide protection.
These sons, grandsons, and descendants were born from the womb of <s>Surabhī</s>.
I shall tell of the sons and grandsons born to <s>Kaśyapa</s> from his wives:
<s>Aditi</s>, <s>Diti</s>, <s>Danu</s>, <s>Ariṣṭā</s>, and likewise <s>Surasā</s>,
<s>Surabhi</s>, <s>Vinatā</s>, similarly <s>Tāmrā</s>, <s>Krodhavaśā</s>, and <s>Irā</s>,

children.text: kadrūrviśvā munis tadvat tāsāṃ putrān nibodhata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kadrū</s>, <s>Viśvā</s>, and likewise <s>Muni</s>; hear of their sons.
Those gods called <s>Tuṣitas</s> in the interval of <s>Cākṣuṣa Manu</s>
are remembered in the interval of <s>Vaivasvata</s> as these twelve <s>Ādityas</s>:

children.text: indro dhātā bhagas tvaṣṭā mitro'tha varuṇo yamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Dhātā</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭā</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and then <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: vivasvānsavitā pūṣā aṃśumān viṣṇur eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Savitā</s>, <s>Pūṣā</s>, <s>Aṃśumān</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
These thousand-rayed ones are remembered as the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>.
<s>Aditi</s> obtained these excellent sons from <s>Kaśyapa</s>, son of <s>Marīci</s>.
The sons of the seer <s>Bhṛśāśva</s> are remembered as the weapons of the gods.
These hosts of gods, O brahmins, in each <s>manvantara</s>

children.text: utpadyante pralīyante kalpe kalpe tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: come into being and dissolve away, and so too in every <s>kalpa</s>.

children.text: ditiḥ putradvayaṃ lebhe kaśyapād iti naḥ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Diti</s> obtained two sons from <s>Kaśyapa</s>; so we have heard:
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and likewise <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
Likewise from <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> there was born a group of four sons:

children.text: prahlādaś cānuhlādaśca saṃhlādo hlāda eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Anuhlāda</s>, <s>Saṃhlāda</s>, and <s>Hlāda</s>.

children.text: prahlādaputra āyuṣmān śibir bāṣkala eva ca ||
children.translated_text: The sons of <s>Prahlāda</s> were long-lived <s>Śibi</s> and <s>Bāṣkala</s>,
and <s>Virocana</s> was the fourth; he obtained <s>Bali</s> as his son.

children.text: baleḥ putraśataṃ tv āsīd bāṇajyeṣṭhaṃ tato dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bali</s> had a hundred sons, O brahmins, with <s>Bāṇa</s> as the eldest.
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Candra</s>, and <s>Candrāṃśutāpana</s>,
<s>Nikumbhanābha</s>, <s>Gurvakṣa</s>, <s>Kukṣibhīma</s>, and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
and many others like these, with <s>Bāṇa</s> as the eldest, were rich in qualities.
<s>Bāṇa</s> had a thousand arms and was furnished with every class of weapon.

children.text: tapasā toṣito yasya pure vasati śūlabhṛt
children.translated_text: The trident-bearer, pleased by his austerity, dwells in his city.
He attained the state of <s>Mahākāla</s> and equality with <s>Pinākin</s>.
The sons of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> were <s>Ulūka</s> and likewise <s>Śakuni</s>,
<s>Bhūtasaṃtāpana</s> and also <s>Mahānābha</s>.
From these came seventy-seven crores of sons and grandsons,
very strong, huge-bodied, of many forms, and of great vigor.
<s>Danu</s> obtained a hundred sons from <s>Kaśyapa</s>, proud in their strength.
Among them <s>Vipracitti</s>, very mighty, was the foremost.
<s>Dvimūrdhā</s>, <s>Śakuni</s>, and likewise <s>Śaṅkuśirodhara</s>,
<s>Ayomukha</s>, <s>Śambara</s>, and one named <s>Kapiśa</s>,
<s>Mārīci</s>, <s>Meghavān</s>, and likewise <s>Irā</s> and <s>Garbhaśiras</s>,
<s>Vidrāvaṇa</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, <s>Ketuvīrya</s>, and <s>Śatahrada</s>,
<s>Indrajit</s>, <s>Saptajit</s>, and likewise <s>Vajranābha</s>,
<s>Ekacakra</s>, <s>Mahābāhu</s>, <s>Vajrākṣa</s>, and <s>Tāraka</s>,
<s>Asiloman</s>, <s>Puloman</s>, <s>Bindu</s>, and the great Asura <s>Bāṇa</s>,
<s>Svarbhānu</s>, <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>: these and others were the sons of <s>Danu</s>.

children.text: svarbhānostu prabhā kanyā śacī caiva pulomajā
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhā</s> was the daughter of <s>Svarbhānu</s>, and <s>Śacī</s> was born from <s>Puloman</s>.
<s>Upadānavī</s> belonged to <s>Maya</s>, and likewise <s>Mandodarī</s> and <s>Kuhū</s>.

children.text: śarmiṣṭhā sundarī caiva candrā ca vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, <s>Sundarī</s>, and <s>Candrā</s> were the daughters of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.

children.text: pulomā kālakā caiva vaiśvānarasute hi te ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pulomā</s> and <s>Kālakā</s> were indeed the daughters of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
They were of many offspring and great being, taken in marriage by the son of <s>Marīci</s>.
From those two there formerly arose sixty thousand <s>Dānavas</s>.
The son of <s>Marīci</s> formerly begot the <s>Paulomas</s> and <s>Kālakeyas</s>,
who were invulnerable to the immortals and dwelt in <s>Hiraṇyapura</s>.
They had received a boon from the Four-faced one, but were slain by <s>Vijaya</s>.
<s>Vipracitti</s> begot the <s>Saiṃhikeyas</s> on <s>Siṃhikā</s>,
the thirteen nephews of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>:

children.text: vyaṃsaḥ kalpaśca rājendra nalo vātāpireva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vyaṃsa</s>, <s>Kalpa</s>, O king, <s>Nala</s>, and <s>Vātāpi</s>,
<s>Ilvala</s>, <s>Namuci</s>, <s>Śvasṛpa</s>, and likewise <s>Ajana</s>,
<s>Naraka</s>, <s>Kālanābha</s>, and likewise <s>Saramāṇa</s>,
and the famous <s>Kālavīya</s>; these increased the lineage of <s>Danu</s>.
From the Daitya <s>Saṃhrāda</s> came those remembered as the <s>Nivātakavacas</s>,
invulnerable to all gods, Gandharvas, serpents, and Rākṣasas.

children.text: ye hatā bhargam āśritya tv arjunena raṇājire ||
children.translated_text: They were slain by <s>Arjuna</s> on the battlefield after he had resorted to <s>Bharga</s>.
<s>Tāmrā</s> gave birth to six daughters from the seed of the son of <s>Marīci</s>:

children.text: śukī śyenī ca bhāsī ca sugrīvī gṛdhrikā śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śukī</s>, <s>Śyenī</s>, <s>Bhāsī</s>, <s>Sugrīvī</s>, <s>Gṛdhrikā</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>.
<s>Śukī</s> duly gave birth to parrots and owls.
<s>Śyenī</s> gave birth to hawks, and likewise <s>Bhāsī</s> to ospreys.
<s>Gṛdhrī</s> gave birth to vultures, doves, pigeons, and birds,
and <s>Śuci</s> gave birth to swans, sarasas, cranes, and waterbirds.
<s>Sugrīvī</s> also gave birth to goats, horses, sheep, camels, and donkeys.
This lineage of <s>Tāmrā</s> has been declared; now hear of that of <s>Vinatā</s>.
<s>Garuḍa</s> was the lord of flying creatures, and <s>Aruṇa</s> of birds.

children.text: saudāmanī tathā kanyā yeyaṃ nabhasi viśrutā ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Saudāmanī</s> was the daughter who is renowned in the sky.

children.text: sampātiś ca jaṭāyuśca aruṇasya sutāv ubhau
children.translated_text: <s>Sampāti</s> and <s>Jaṭāyus</s> were both sons of <s>Aruṇa</s>.
And <s>Babhru</s>, son of <s>Sampāti</s>, and also the famed <s>Śīghraga</s> were known.
<s>Karṇikāra</s> and the famed <s>Śatagāmī</s> were sons of <s>Jaṭāyus</s>.
<s>Sārasa</s>, <s>Rajjuvāla</s>, and <s>Bheruṇḍa</s> also were his sons.
Their progeny of sons and grandsons among the birds became endless.
And from <s>Surasā</s> in ancient times there arose a thousand serpents.
<s>Kadrū</s>, O virtuous one, also produced a thousand thousand-headed serpents.
Among them the chief ones, famed, were twenty-six, O subduer of foes.
<s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Karkoṭa</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Airāvata</s>, and <s>Kambala</s>;
<s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, <s>Mahānīla</s>, <s>Padma</s>, <s>Aśvatara</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s>;
<s>Elāpattra</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, and <s>Balāhaka</s>;
<s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, <s>Mahāśaṅkha</s>, <s>Puṣpadaṃṣṭra</s>, and <s>Śubhānana</s>;
and <s>Śaṅkuromā</s>, <s>Bahula</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, and <s>Pāṇin</s> likewise;
<s>Kapila</s>, <s>Durmukha</s>, and <s>Patañjali</s> are also remembered.
The progeny of sons and grandsons of all these became endless.
Most of it, however, was burned long ago in <s>Janamejaya</s>'s sacrificial hall.
<s>Krodhavaśā</s> gave birth to a host of rākṣasas bearing her own name.
A niyuta of those fanged ones came to destruction through <s>Bhīmasena</s>.

children.text: rudrāṇāṃ ca gaṇaṃ tadvad gomahiṣyo varāṅganāḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, the beautiful <s>Surabhi</s> produced the host of <s>Rudras</s>, cows, and buffalo-cows
from <s>Kaśyapa</s>, while she was firm in her vow.
<s>Muni</s> gave birth to the host of sages and likewise to the host of apsarases.
And <s>Ariṣṭā</s> gave birth to many kiṃnaras and gandharvas.
<s>Irā</s> gave birth to all grass, trees, creepers, and shrubs.
But <s>Viśvā</s> produced yakṣas and rākṣasas by the crore.
Then <s>Diti</s> bore from <s>Kaśyapa</s> the forty-nine <s>Maruts</s>,
all knowers of dharma and beloved of the immortals.
The sages said:

children.text: diteḥ putrāḥ kathaṃ jātā maruto devavallabhāḥ
children.translated_text: How were the sons of <s>Diti</s> born as <s>Maruts</s>, beloved of the gods?
And why did they enter into supreme friendship with the gods, though they were their rivals?
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: purā devāsure yuddhe hṛteṣu hariṇā suraiḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago, in the war between the gods and the Asuras, when her sons and grandsons had been taken away by <s>Hari</s> and the gods,
she was afflicted with grief and went to the excellent earthly realm.
At the sacred field of <s>Syamantapañcaka</s>, on the auspicious bank of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: bhartur ārādhanaparā tapa ugraṃ cacāra ha ||
children.translated_text: intent on propitiating her husband, she performed fierce austerity.
Then <s>Diti</s>, mother of the Daityas, virtuous and in the form of a seer,
lived on fruit and practiced difficult austerities such as the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
For more than a hundred years she remained beset by old age and grief.
Then, worn by austerity, she asked <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others:
"Please tell me a vrata (vow) that will destroy my grief for sons,
that grants the fruit of good fortune in this world and in the next."
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others spoke of the <s>Madana-dvādaśī</s> vrata,
by whose power she became free from sorrow over her sons.
The sages said:
We wish to hear, O <s>Sūta</s>, the <s>Madana-dvādaśī</s> vrata,
by which <s>Diti</s> again obtained forty-nine sons.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
That excellent rite which was formerly taught to <s>Diti</s> by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others,
hear that very thing in detail from me.

children.text: caitre māsi site pakṣe dvādaśyāṃ niyatavrataḥ
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Caitra</s>, in the bright fortnight, on the twelfth lunar day, one who is steady in the vow
should set up an unblemished jar filled with white rice.
It should be furnished with various fruits and likewise provided with sugarcane stalks,
covered with a pair of white cloths and smeared with white sandalwood.
It should be supplied with various foods and with gold according to one's ability.
One should place a copper vessel containing jaggery on top of it.
Above that, one should place <s>Kāma</s> set on a banana leaf,
and to his left one should fashion <s>Rati</s>, supplied with sugar.

children.text: gandhaṃ dhūpaṃ tato dadyādgītaṃ vādyaṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: Then one should offer perfume and incense, and have singing and music performed.
If these are absent, a man should recite the story of <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Keśava</s>.
He should bathe the image of <s>Hari</s> under the name <s>Kāma</s> with scented water,
and worship <s>Madhusūdana</s> with white flowers, unbroken rice, and sesame.

children.text: kāmāya pādau sampūjya jaṅghe saubhāgyadāya ca
children.translated_text: Having worshiped the feet with "to <s>Kāma</s>," and the shanks with "to the giver of good fortune,"
the thighs with "to <s>Smara</s>," and then the waist with "to <s>Manmatha</s>,"
the belly of <s>Hari</s> with "to the pure-bellied one," and the chest with "to <s>Anaṅga</s>,"
the face with "to the lotus-faced one," and the arms with "to the five-arrowed one,"
one should worship <s>Keśava</s>'s head with "obeisance to the All-Self."

children.text: tataḥ prabhāte taṃ kumbhaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: Then in the morning one should present that jar to a Brahmin.
He should feed Brahmins with devotion, and himself eat without salt.
After eating, he should give a dakṣiṇā (honorarium) and utter this mantra:
"May the blessed <s>Janārdana</s>, taking the form of <s>Kāma</s>, be pleased here,
he who is called joy in the hearts of all beings."

children.text: anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi vrataṃ caret
children.translated_text: In this manner one should perform the whole vrata month after month.
Fasting on the thirteenth lunar day, he should worship imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: phalamekaṃ ca saṃprāśya dvādaśyāṃ bhūtale svapet
children.translated_text: Having eaten a single fruit, he should sleep on the ground on the twelfth lunar day.
Then, in the thirteenth month, together with a ghṛta-dhenu offering,
he should give a bed to <s>Anaṅga</s>, furnished with all accessories.

children.text: kāñcanaṃ kāmadevaṃ ca śuklāṃ gāṃ ca payasvinīm ||
children.translated_text: He should also give a golden <s>Kāmadeva</s> and a white milk-giving cow.
Having honored a Brahmin couple with garments and ornaments according to his ability,
he should give the bed, perfumes, and the rest, saying, "May he be pleased."
A homa should be performed with white sesame seeds, and the names of <s>Kāma</s> should be recited.
Likewise it should be done with oblations from cow products and with milk-rice, O knower of dharma.
One should give food to Brahmins, avoiding deceit concerning one's wealth.
Then one should give sugarcane stalks and flower garlands according to one's ability.
Whoever performs this <s>Madana-dvādaśī</s> according to this rule
Freed from all sins, he attains likeness to <s>Hari</s>.
In this world he enjoys excellent sons and the fruit of good fortune.

children.text: yaḥ smaraḥ saṃsmṛto viṣṇur ānandātmā maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who, when remembered as <s>Smara</s>, is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose self is bliss, the great lord,
one who desires happiness should remember that lord, the body-born one, in the form of <s>Kāma</s>.
Having heard this, <s>Diti</s> did all of it completely, without remainder.
Through the greatness of the <s>vrata</s> (vow), <s>Kaśyapa</s> came with supreme joy.
Again he made the austere woman endowed with beauty and youth.

children.text: varair āchandayāmāsa sā tu vavre tato varam
children.translated_text: He invited her to choose boons, and then she chose a boon:
"I choose as my son one capable of killing <s>Śakra</s>, immeasurably powerful,
a great-souled destroyer of all the immortals."
<s>Kaśyapa</s> spoke these words: "Here I myself shall give you a mighty slayer of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: pradāsyāmyahameveha kiṃ tv etat kriyatāṃ śubhe
children.translated_text: But this must be done, fair one:
let <s>Āpastamba</s> perform today the <s>putrīyā iṣṭi</s> (son-producing sacrifice), O woman of good vows.
After that I shall place in you a fetus that will destroy <s>Indra</s>, the foe."
Then <s>Āpastamba</s> performed the <s>putreṣṭi</s> (sacrifice for a son), rich in sacrificial gifts,
and he made the oblation in full detail, saying, "May he become the enemy of <s>Indra</s>."

children.text: devā mumudire daityā vimukhāḥ syuśca dānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods rejoiced, while the <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s> became downcast.

children.text: dityāṃ garbham athādhatta kaśyapaḥ prāha tāṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kaśyapa</s> placed the embryo in <s>Diti</s> and spoke to her again:

children.text: tvayā yatno vidhātavyo hy asmingarbhe varānane ||
children.translated_text: "Effort must be made by you with regard to this embryo, fair-faced one,
for one full hundred years here in this very grove of austerity.
A pregnant woman must not eat at the junction times, lovely one.

children.text: na sthātavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ vṛkṣamūleṣu sarvadā
children.translated_text: She must not remain or walk at the roots of trees at any time.
She should not sit on implements, on pestles, mortars, and the like.

children.text: jale ca nāvagāheta śūnyāgāraṃ ca varjayet
children.translated_text: She should not immerse herself in water, and she should avoid an empty house.

children.text: valmīkāyāṃ na tiṣṭheta na codvignamanā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: She should not stand on an anthill, nor should she be anxious in mind.
She should not scratch the ground with her nails, nor with charcoal, nor with ashes.

children.text: na śayāluḥ sadā tiṣṭhedvyāyāmaṃ ca vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: She should not remain constantly given to sleep, and she should avoid exertion.
She should not sit among husks, charcoal, ashes, bones, or skulls.
She should avoid quarrels with people and also the straining of her limbs.
She should not remain with hair loosened, nor should she ever be impure.
She should not sleep with her head to the north, nor ever with her head to the west.

children.text: na vastrahīnā nodvignā na cārdracaraṇā satī
children.translated_text: She should not be without clothing, nor agitated, nor have wet feet.

children.text: nāmaṅgalyāṃ vadedvācaṃ na ca hāsyādhikā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: She should not utter inauspicious speech, nor be excessive in laughter.
She should serve her elders and always be intent on auspicious observances.
She should bathe with all herbs in lukewarm water.
Protected by rites, well adorned, and intent on worship of the dwelling,
she should remain with a cheerful face, devoted to what is dear and beneficial to her husband.
Generous by nature, she should observe the night-fast on the third lunar day and on parvan days.
Such should be a woman's conduct, and especially that of a pregnant woman.
The son who is born of her will be endowed with good conduct, long life, and growth.
Otherwise she obtains a miscarriage; there is no doubt.
Therefore, by this mode of conduct, take care with this embryo.
May there be well-being for you. I shall go." When she replied, "So be it,"
he vanished there itself while all beings were looking on.
Then she remained according to the rule stated by <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
Then <s>Indra</s> too, being afraid, went to <s>Diti</s>'s side.
Leaving the abode of the gods, he stayed there wishing to serve her.
<s>Pākaśāsana</s> was seeking an opening in <s>Diti</s>'s conduct.
Outwardly he was humble, unagitated, and of tranquil countenance.
As if unaware of that purpose of his, he performed what was beneficial to himself.

children.text: tato varṣaśatānte sā nyūne tu divasais tribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, at the end of the hundred years, lacking only three days,
she thought herself fulfilled, her mind amazed with joy.
Without washing her feet, she fell asleep with her hair loosened,
overcome by the weight of sleep in the daytime, with her head toward the west.
Then, having obtained that opportunity, the lord of <s>Śacī</s> entered.

children.text: vajreṇa saptadhā cakre taṃ garbhaṃ tridaśādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: With his thunderbolt the lord of the thirty gods cut that fetus into seven parts.

children.text: tataḥ saptaiva te jātāḥ kumārāḥ sūryavarcasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those seven boys were born, with the brilliance of the sun.

children.text: rudantaḥ sapta te bālā niṣiddhā giridāriṇā
children.translated_text: Those seven children cried, and they were restrained by the mountain-splitter.
When they cried again, <s>Hari</s>, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>,
cut each one of them again into seven, while they were still in that womb.
Thus, having become forty-nine, they cried intensely.

children.text: indro nivārayāmāsa māṃ rodiṣṭa punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> restrained them again and again: "Do not cry."
Then the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> thought, "What is this?
By the greatness of what <s>dharma</s> (sacred observance) have these been revived again?
Having learned through meditative yoga the fruit of <s>Madana-dvādaśī</s>,
surely this has now ripened through the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: vajreṇāpi hatāḥ santo na vināśam avāpnuyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though struck even by the thunderbolt, they do not meet destruction.
Though one, even while in the womb, he has fully become many.
Surely these are invulnerable; therefore let them become gods."
Because, while crying in the womb, they were told, "Do not cry,"

children.text: maruto nāma te nāmnā bhavantu makhabhāginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let them by name be called the <s>Maruts</s>, and let them have shares in the sacrifice.

children.text: tataḥ prasādya deveśaḥ kṣamasveti ditiṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the lord of gods appeased <s>Diti</s> again, saying, "Forgive me.
Relying on statecraft, I committed this evil deed."
Having made the host of <s>Maruts</s> equal to the gods, the lord of the immortals
placed <s>Diti</s> in an aerial car and brought her, together with her sons, to heaven.
From then on, O twice-born ones, the <s>Maruts</s> became enjoyers of sacrificial shares.
They did not make common cause with the <s>Asuras</s>; therefore they are dear to the gods.
The seers said:

children.text: ādisargaśca yaḥ sūta kathito vistareṇa tu
children.translated_text: "O <s>Sūta</s>, you have told in detail the primordial creation

children.text: pratisargaśca ye yeṣām adhipās tānvadasva naḥ ||
children.translated_text: And tell us the counter-creations, and who were the overlords over each of them.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When <s>Pṛthu</s> had been consecrated to universal kingship and became lord over the earth,

children.text: tadauṣadhīnāmadhipaṃ cakāra yajñavratānāṃ tapasāṃ ca candram ||
children.translated_text: then he made <s>Candra</s> the lord of herbs, sacrifices, vows, and austerities.
And over the lunar mansions, stars, twice-born beings, trees, shrubs, and spreading creepers, the golden-germed one appointed him.

children.text: apāmadhīśaṃ varuṇaṃ dhanānāṃ rājñāṃ prabhuṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ ca tadvat ||
children.translated_text: Likewise he made <s>Varuṇa</s> lord of the waters, and <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> lord of wealth and of kings.

children.text: viṣṇuṃ ravīṇāmadhipaṃ vasūnām agniṃ ca lokādhipatiścakāra
children.translated_text: He made <s>Viṣṇu</s> lord of the suns, and <s>Agni</s> lord of the <s>Vasus</s> and of the worlds.

children.text: prajāpatīnāmadhipaṃ ca dakṣaṃ cakāra śakraṃ marutāmadhīśam ||
children.translated_text: He made <s>Dakṣa</s> lord of the <s>Prajāpatis</s>, and <s>Śakra</s> lord of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: daityādhipānāmatha dānavānāṃ prahlādamīśaṃ ca yamaṃ pitṝṇām
children.translated_text: Then he made <s>Prahlāda</s> lord over the <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s>, and <s>Yama</s> lord of the Fathers.
And he made the trident-bearing <s>Śūlapāṇi</s> king over <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, beasts, <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Vetālas</s>.

children.text: prāleyaśailaṃ ca patiṃ girīṇām īśaṃ samudraṃ sasarinnadānām
children.translated_text: He made the snowy mountain lord of mountains, and the ocean lord of rivers together with their streams.
Again he made <s>Citraratha</s> lord of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and <s>Kiṃnaras</s>.
He appointed mighty <s>Vāsuki</s> lord of the <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s> lord of serpents.
He made the elephant-king named <s>Airāvata</s> lord of the elephants of the quarters.
Then he made <s>Suparṇa</s> lord of flying creatures, and <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> king of horses.

children.text: siṃhaṃ mṛgāṇāṃ vṛṣabhaṃ gavāṃ ca plakṣaṃ punaḥ sarvavanaspatīnām ||
children.translated_text: He made the lion lord of wild animals, the bull lord of cattle, and again the plakṣa tree lord of all forest trees.
Formerly the Grandfather consecrated these also again as lords over all the directions.
In the east he consecrated as guardian of the quarter one named <s>Sudharmā</s>, whose banner was hostile to enemies.
Then in the south he made an overlord, the universal lord called <s>Śaṅkhapada</s>.

children.text: sa ketumantaṃ ca digīśamīśaścakāra paścād bhuvanāṇḍagarbhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the lord, the one containing the cosmic egg, afterward made <s>Ketumanta</s> lord of a quarter.
The <s>Prajāpati</s> made <s>Hiraṇyaromā</s>, a son of the gods, lord of the northern quarter.

children.text: adyāpi kurvanti diśām adhīśāḥ śatrūn dahantastu bhuvo'bhirakṣām ||
children.translated_text: Even today the lords of the directions, burning up enemies, protect the earth.

children.text: caturbhir ebhiḥ pṛthunāmadheyo nṛpo'bhiṣiktaḥ prathamaṃ pṛthivyām
children.translated_text: By these four, the king named <s>Pṛthu</s> was first consecrated upon the earth.

children.text: gate'ntare cākṣuṣanāmadheye vaivasvatākhye ca punaḥ pravṛtte
children.translated_text: When the interval named <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> had passed and that called <s>Vaivasvata</s> had begun again,
he became the <s>Prajāpati</s> of this moving and unmoving world, the emblem of the solar lineage.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ śrutvā manuḥ prāha punareva janārdanam
children.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Manu</s> again said to <s>Janārdana</s>:
"Tell me the deeds of the former <s>Manus</s>, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>."
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: manvantarāṇi rājendra manūnāṃ caritaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: O king, the manvantaras and the deeds of the <s>Manus</s>,

children.text: pramāṇaṃ caiva kālasya tāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ ca samāsataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the measure of time, and that creation too, I shall tell in brief.
With one-pointed mind and tranquil self, listen, O son of <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>.

children.text: yāmā nāma purā devā āsan svāyambhuvāntare ||
children.translated_text: In the interval of <s>Svāyambhuva</s>, there were formerly gods called the <s>Yāmas</s>.

children.text: saptaiva ṛṣayaḥ pūrve ye marīcyādayaḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: The seven former seers are remembered as those beginning with <s>Marīci</s>.
<s>Āgnīdhra</s>, <s>Agnibāhu</s>, <s>Saha</s>, and <s>Savana</s>,

children.text: jyotiṣmān dyutimān havyo medhā medhātithir vasuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Jyotiṣmān</s>, <s>Dyutimān</s>, <s>Havya</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Medhātithi</s>, and <s>Vasu</s>:
these ten were increasers of the lineage of this <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>.
Having performed these counter-creations, they went to the supreme state.
This <s>Svāyambhuva</s> interval has been declared; after it comes the <s>Svārociṣa</s>.
The sons of <s>Svārociṣa</s>, radiant with divine splendor, were four:
<s>Nabha</s>, <s>Nabhasya</s>, <s>Prasṛti</s>, and <s>Bhānava</s>, increasers of renown.

children.text: datto niścyavanastambaḥ prāṇaḥ kaśyapa eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Datta</s>, <s>Niścyavana</s>, <s>Stamba</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s>, and also <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
together with <s>Aurva</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>: these seven are remembered as the seers.
And the gods in the <s>Svārociṣa</s> interval are remembered as called the <s>Tuṣitas</s>.
<s>Hastīndra</s>, <s>Sukṛta</s>, <s>Mūrti</s>, <s>Āpas</s>, <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Ayaḥ</s>, and <s>Smaya</s>,

children.text: vasiṣṭhasya sutāḥ sapta ye prajāpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: the seven sons of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, are remembered as <s>Prajāpatis</s>.
This second manvantara has been told; next after it,
I shall proclaim the auspicious manvantara of <s>Uttama</s>.
There <s>Manu</s> named <s>Uttami</s> begot ten sons:

children.text: īṣa ūrjaśca tarjaś ca śuciḥ śukrastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Īṣa</s>, <s>Ūrja</s>, <s>Tarja</s>, <s>Śuci</s>, and likewise <s>Śukra</s>,
and <s>Madhu</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Nabhasya</s>, and then <s>Nabhas</s> as well.
<s>Saha</s>, the youngest of these, was noble and an increaser of renown.

children.text: bhāvanās tatra devāḥ syur ūrjāḥ saptarṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the gods were the <s>Bhāvanas</s>; the <s>Ūrjas</s> are remembered as the seven seers.
<s>Kaukuruṇḍi</s>, <s>Dālbhya</s>, <s>Śaṅga</s>, <s>Pravahaṇa</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,
and <s>Sita</s> and <s>Sasmita</s> too: these seven increased yoga.

children.text: manvantaraṃ caturthaṃ tu tāmasaṃ nāma viśrutam
children.translated_text: The fourth manvantara is famed by the name <s>Tāmasa</s>.

children.text: kaviḥ pṛthus tathaivāgnir akapiḥ kapireva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kavi</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s>, likewise <s>Agni</s>, <s>Akapi</s>, and <s>Kapi</s>,
and likewise the sages <s>Jalpa</s> and <s>Dhīmān</s> were the seven in the <s>Tāmasa</s> interval.
There, in the <s>Tāmasa</s> interval, the hosts of gods are said to have been the <s>Sādhyas</s>.
<s>Akalmaṣa</s>, also <s>Dhanvī</s>, <s>Tapomūla</s>, and <s>Tapodhana</s>,
<s>Taporati</s>, <s>Tapasya</s>, <s>Tapodyuti</s>, and <s>Paraṃtapa</s>,
<s>Tapobhāgī</s> and <s>Tapoyogī</s>, always devoted to the conduct of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
all these ten sons of <s>Tāmasa</s> were increasers of the lineage.
In the same way, hear the interval of the fifth <s>Manu</s>, <s>Raivata</s>.
<s>Devabāhu</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Somapa</s>, and <s>Muni</s>,
<s>Hiraṇyaromā</s> and <s>Saptāśva</s>: these seven are remembered as the seers.
And the gods were the stainless <s>Abhūtarajas</s>, and likewise the auspicious <s>Prakṛtis</s>.
<s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Tattvadarśin</s>, <s>Vittavān</s>, <s>Havyapa</s>, and <s>Kapi</s>,
<s>Yukta</s>, <s>Nirutsuka</s>, <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Nirmoha</s>, and then <s>Prakāśaka</s>:
these ten sons of <s>Raivata</s> were endowed with the heroic strength of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: bhṛguḥ sudhāmā virajāḥ sahiṣṇurnāda eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Sudhāmā</s>, <s>Virajas</s>, <s>Sahiṣṇu</s>, and <s>Nāda</s>,
and <s>Vivasvān</s> and <s>Atināman</s> are the other seven seers in the sixth interval.
In the interval of <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>, the gods called the <s>Lekhās</s> were renowned.
The <s>Ṛbhus</s>, the <s>Ṛbhādyas</s>, and the heavenly beings called <s>Vārimūlas</s>
are declared to be the five classes of gods in the interval of <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>.
Likewise, beginning with <s>Ruru</s>, the ten sons of <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>

children.text: proktāḥ svāyambhuve vaṃśe ye mayā pūrvameva tu ||
children.translated_text: have already been mentioned by me before, in the lineage of <s>Svāyambhuva</s>.
This interval of <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> has thus been fully recounted to you by me.
I shall now proclaim the seventh, which is called that of <s>Vaivasvata</s>.
<s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and likewise <s>Gautama</s>,
and <s>Bharadvāja</s>, the yogin, and mighty <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
and <s>Jamadagni</s>: these seven are the present great seers.
Having established the order of <s>dharma</s>, they go to the supreme state.

children.text: sādhyā viśve ca rudrāśca maruto vasavo'śvinau
children.translated_text: The <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>,
and the <s>Ādityas</s>, together with the gods, are remembered as seven groups of deities.
His ten sons on earth are remembered as beginning with <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.
In all the <s>manvantaras</s>, there are seven great seers each.
Having established the order of <s>dharma</s>, they go to the supreme state.
I shall now proclaim the future interval of <s>Sāvarṇi Manu</s> as well.
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>, <s>Śaradvān</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, and likewise <s>Gālava</s>,
<s>Śatānanda</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and <s>Rāma</s> are remembered as the seers.

children.text: dhṛtir varīyān yavasaḥ suvarṇo vaṣṭireva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Varīyān</s>, <s>Yavasa</s>, <s>Suvarṇa</s>, and also <s>Vaṣṭi</s>,

children.text: cariṣṇur īḍyaḥ sumatir vasuḥ śukraśca vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Cariṣṇu</s>, <s>Īḍya</s>, <s>Sumati</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, and mighty <s>Śukra</s>

children.text: bhaviṣyā daśa sāvarṇer manoḥ putrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: are proclaimed as the ten future sons of <s>Sāvarṇi Manu</s>.
Other Manus too, beginning with <s>Raucya</s>, are also proclaimed.

children.text: ruceḥ prajāpateḥ putro raucyo nāma bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: The son of the Prajāpati <s>Ruci</s> will be named <s>Raucya</s>.

children.text: manur bhūtisutas tadvad bhautyo nāma bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, the son of <s>Bhūti</s> will be the Manu named <s>Bhautya</s>.
After that, <s>Merusāvarṇi</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, is remembered as a Manu.

children.text: ṛtaśca ṛtadhāmā ca viṣvakseno manus tathā ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Ṛta</s>, <s>Ṛtadhāman</s>, and likewise the Manu <s>Viṣvaksena</s> are named.
These Manus, past and future, have been recounted.
O lord of men, six less than a thousand yugas are pervaded by these.
In their own respective intervals, having brought forth all this world, moving and unmoving,
when the dissolution at the end of the kalpa has taken place, they are released together with <s>Brahmā</s>.
At the end of a thousand yugas, these perish again and again.

children.text: brahmādyā viṣṇusāyujyaṃ yātā yāsyanti vai dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: O twice-born ones, those beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> have gone, and will go, to union with <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The seers said:

children.text: bahubhir dhāriṇī bhuktā bhūpālaiḥ śrūyate purā
children.translated_text: We have heard that the earth was formerly enjoyed by many kings.
Kings are connected with the earth; but through whose connection is the earth what it is?

children.text: kimarthaṃ ca kṛtā saṃjñā bhūmeḥ kiṃ pāribhāṣikī
children.translated_text: And for what reason was the name of the earth made? What is its technical designation?

children.text: gaur itīyaṃ ca vikhyātā sūta kasmād bravīhi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: And why is it famed as 'cow'? Tell us, O <s>Sūta</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In the lineage of <s>Svāyambhuva</s> there was a Prajāpati named <s>Aṅga</s>.
He married the very ill-faced daughter of <s>Mṛtyu</s>.

children.text: sunīthā nāma tasyāstu veno nāma sutaḥ purā
children.translated_text: Her name was <s>Sunīthā</s>, and of her a son named <s>Vena</s> was born in ancient times.
He was devoted to unrighteousness, powerful, and lord of the earth.
In the world too he became a doer of unrighteousness and a taker of others' wives.
Then, for the sake of establishing righteous conduct in the world, by the great seers,

children.text: anunīto'pi na dadāv anujñāṃ sa yadā tataḥ
children.translated_text: though conciliated, when he would not give permission,
they slew him with a curse, afflicted by fear of anarchy.
The stainless brahmins then churned his body by force.
From his body as it was being churned, peoples of mleccha birth fell forth.
Through the portion of his mother's body they were dark, with a radiance like black collyrium.
But from the portion belonging to his father, one righteous and practicing <s>dharma</s>
was born from the right hand, bearing bow and arrow and a mace.
His body was made of divine splendor, and he wore a jeweled cuirass and armlets.
Through the effort connected with <s>Pṛthu</s>, therefore <s>Pṛthu</s> was born.
Though anointed by the brahmins, he performed very severe austerity.
By a boon from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he again obtained lordship over all.
Seeing the earth without Vedic recitation, without vaṣaṭ-calls, and without <s>dharma</s>,
he, of immeasurable valor, angrily raised his arrow as if to burn it up.

children.text: tato gorūpam āsthāya bhūḥ palāyitum udyatā ||
children.translated_text: Then the earth, taking the form of a cow, set out to flee.
<s>Pṛthu</s>, with his blazing bow, followed after her from behind.

children.text: tataḥ sthitvaikadeśe tu kiṃ karomīti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then, stopping in one place, she said, 'What shall I do?'

children.text: pṛthur apyavadad vākyam īpsitaṃ dehi suvrate
children.translated_text: <s>Pṛthu</s> too spoke this sentence: 'Give what is desired, O virtuous one,

children.text: sarvasya jagataḥ śīghraṃ sthāvarasya carasya ca ||
children.translated_text: quickly, for the whole world, both unmoving and moving.'

children.text: tathaiva sābravīd bhūmir dudoha sa narādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: The earth spoke in the same way, and that king milked her.

children.text: svake pāṇau pṛthurvatsaṃ kṛtvā svāyambhuvaṃ manum ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pṛthu</s> made <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s> the calf and milked into his own hand.
That became pure food, by which creatures live.
Then she was milked by the seers; <s>Soma</s> was then the calf.

children.text: dogdhā bṛhaspatirabhūt pātraṃ vedas tapo rasaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> became the milker, the Veda was the vessel, and austerity was the essence.
The earth was also milked by the gods; <s>Mitra</s> was then the milker.
<s>Indra</s> became the calf, and the milk was strength that produces vigor.

children.text: devānāṃ kāñcanaṃ pātraṃ pitṝṇāṃ rājataṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: The vessel of the gods was golden, while that of the ancestors was silver.
<s>Antaka</s> became the milker, <s>Yama</s> the calf, and <s>svadhā</s> the essence.
For the serpents the vessel was a gourd, and <s>Takṣaka</s> became the calf.
The milk was poison; then <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> again became the milker.
This earth was also milked by the Asuras into an iron vessel, the force that torments <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: pātre māyām abhūd vatsaḥ prāhlādis tu virocanaḥ
children.translated_text: Magic power was the milk; the Prahlāda-descended <s>Virocana</s> became the calf.
<s>Dvimūrdhā</s> was the milker there, by whom illusion was set in motion.
And the earth was milked by the Yakṣas, who desired disappearance in ancient times.
having made <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> the calf, in an unbaked vessel, O lord of the earth.
The earth was milked by hosts of <s>pretas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> for fierce blood.
<s>Raupya-nābha</s> became the milker, while <s>Sumālī</s> himself was the calf.
And formerly the earth was milked by the <s>Gandharvas</s> together with hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>.
They made <s>Caitraratha</s> the calf and milked fragrances, likewise into a lotus petal.
The milker was named <s>Vararuci</s>, one who had mastered the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>.
By the mountains the earth was milked for various jewels

children.text: auṣadhāni ca divyāni dogdhā merur mahācalaḥ
children.translated_text: and for divine herbs; the milker was <s>Meru</s>, the great mountain.
<s>Himavān</s> was the calf there, and again the vessel was made of mountain-stone.
By the trees the earth was milked for milk that makes cut shoots grow again.
In a <s>palāśa</s> vessel, the milker was <s>Śāla</s>, covered with flowers and creepers.
Then <s>Plakṣa</s> became the calf, lord of the wealth of all trees.
Thus by others too the earth was then milked for whatever each desired.

children.text: āyur dhanāni saukhyaṃ ca pṛthau rājyaṃ praśāsati
children.translated_text: While <s>Pṛthu</s> governed the kingdom, there were long life, wealth, and happiness.

children.text: na daridrastadā kaścinna rogī na ca pāpakṛt ||
children.translated_text: At that time no one was poor, no one was sick, and no one committed sin.
There was no fear at all of calamity while king <s>Pṛthu</s> ruled.
The people were always joyful and free from suffering and grief.
With the tip of his bow that mighty one pushed aside the lordly mountains
and made the surface of the earth level, desiring the welfare of the worlds.
There were no cities, villages, or forts, and no men bearing weapons.
There was no misery from loss or excess, and no concern for <s>arthaśāstra</s> (statecraft).
The people had a disposition of steadiness while <s>Pṛthu</s> governed the kingdom.

children.text: kathitāni ca pātrāṇi yatkṣīraṃ ca mayā tava ||
children.translated_text: I have told you the vessels and the milk that was drawn from each.
Whatever a given group delights in should be given to them by one who understands.
This has been explained by me to you for all sacrifices and <s>śrāddhas</s> (ancestral rites).
Because the earth attained the status of daughter to righteous <s>Pṛthu</s>,
and because of the bond of affection arising from that, she is known among the wise as <s>Pṛthivī</s>.
The seers said:
Tell us the entire lineage of <s>Āditya</s> in order, O <s>Sūta</s>,
and also the lunar lineage, O knower of truth; you ought to describe it correctly.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
First <s>Vivasvān</s> was born as a son from <s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: tasya patnītrayaṃ tadvat saṃjñā rājñī prabhā tathā ||
children.translated_text: He had three wives likewise: <s>Saṃjñā</s>, <s>Rājñī</s>, and <s>Prabhā</s>.

children.text: raivatasya sutā rājñī revataṃ suṣuve sutam
children.translated_text: <s>Rājñī</s>, daughter of <s>Raivata</s>, bore a son, <s>Revata</s>.

children.text: prabhā prabhātaṃ suṣuve tvāṣṭrī saṃjñā tathā manum ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhā</s> bore <s>Prabhāta</s>, and <s>Saṃjñā</s>, daughter of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, likewise bore <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: yamaśca yamunā caiva yamalau tu babhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> and <s>Yamunā</s> too were born as twins.
Then, unable to bear the radiant form of <s>Vivasvān</s>,
that woman produced from her own body an irreproachable woman.
The daughter of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> made her in her own likeness, a beautiful woman named <s>Chāyā</s>.

children.text: purataḥ saṃsthitāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjñā tāṃ pratyabhāṣata
children.translated_text: Seeing her standing before her, <s>Saṃjñā</s> addressed her:
'<s>Chāyā</s>, attend upon that husband of ours, fair-faced one.
Protect my children with a mother's affection.'

children.text: tathetyuktvā tu sā devamagamat kvāpi suvratā ||
children.translated_text: After saying, 'So be it,' that virtuous woman went away from the god to some place.
The god too desired her with affection, thinking, 'This is <s>Saṃjñā</s>,'

children.text: janayāmāsa tasyāṃ tu putraṃ ca manurūpiṇam ||
children.translated_text: and begot upon her a son resembling <s>Manu</s>.
Because he had the same appearance as <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>, he was <s>Sāvarṇi Manu</s>.

children.text: tataḥ śaniṃ ca tapatīṃ viṣṭiṃ caiva krameṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: Then in sequence he begot <s>Śani</s>, <s>Tapatī</s>, and <s>Viṣṭi</s> as well.
<s>Bhāskara</s> begot them on <s>Chāyā</s>, thinking that she was <s>Saṃjñā</s>.

children.text: chāyā svaputre 'bhyadhikaṃ snehaṃ cakre manau tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Chāyā</s> showed greater affection toward her own son, the <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: pūrvo manustu cakṣāma na yamaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
children.translated_text: The earlier <s>Manu</s> tolerated it, but <s>Yama</s>, overcome by anger, did not.
Then he threatened her, raising his right foot.

children.text: śaśāpa ca yamaṃ chāyā sakṣataḥ kṛmisaṃyutaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Chāyā</s> cursed <s>Yama</s>: 'Wounded and full of worms,
this one foot shall become one that oozes pus and blood.'
<s>Yama</s>, angered by the curse, reported it to his father:
'For no reason I have been cursed by my angry mother, O god.
Because of childishness my foot was lifted a little, just once.

children.text: manunā vāryamāṇāpi mama śāpam adād vibho ||
children.translated_text: Although <s>Manu</s> tried to restrain her, she gave me a curse, O lord.

children.text: prāyo na mātā sāsmākaṃ śāpenāhaṃ yato hataḥ
children.translated_text: She is probably not our mother, since I have been struck down by her curse.'

children.text: devo'pyāha yamaṃ bhūyaḥ kiṃ karomi mahāmate ||
children.translated_text: The god again said to <s>Yama</s>, 'What can I do, great-minded one?
Through foolishness, who would not come to grief? Or rather, the succession of <s>karma</s> (deeds and their results)
is unavoidable even for <s>Bhava</s>; what need be said of other creatures?
I have given a <s>kṛkavāku</s> bird, which will eat the worms

children.text: kledaṃ ca rudhiraṃ caiva vatsāyam apaneṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and will remove the moisture and the blood, my child.'
Thus addressed, <s>Yama</s> of great renown practiced severe austerity.
At the <s>Gokarṇa</s> ford, out of detachment, he lived on fruit, leaves, and air,
worshiping <s>Mahādeva</s> for ten thousand times ten thousand years.
Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, the trident-bearer, was pleased and granted a boon.
He chose guardianship of the world, kingship in <s>Pitṛloka</s>,
and the examination of the world, whose nature includes <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
Thus he obtained world-guardianship from <s>Śūlapāṇi</s>,
and lordship over the <s>Pitṛs</s> and over <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, O sinless one.
Then <s>Vivasvān</s>, having learned of <s>Saṃjñā</s>'s action and conduct,
went to the presence of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> and angrily told him.
Then <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> spoke to him, first conciliating him, O best of twice-born ones:
'Unable to bear your fierce splendor, O blessed darkness-dispeller,
she assumed the form of a mare and came here to my presence.

children.text: nivāritā mayā sā nu tvayā caiva divākara ||
children.translated_text: She was restrained by me, and by you too, O maker of day.
Because she came here to my presence without being known,
therefore you are not entitled to enter my dwelling.'
Thus addressed, the faultless woman then went to the desert region.
Having assumed the form of a mare, she settled upon the earth.
Therefore show me favor, if I am fit to receive your grace.

children.text: apaneṣyāmi te tejo yantre kṛtvā divākara ||
children.translated_text: I shall remove your radiance, placing you in the machine, O <s>Divākara</s>.
I shall make your form one that brings joy to the worlds, O lord.

children.text: tathetyuktaḥ sa raviṇā bhramau kṛtvā divākaram ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Ravi</s> had said, 'So be it,' he set <s>Divākara</s> on a lathe.
He separated that radiance and fashioned the discus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
And also the trident of <s>Rudra</s> and the mighty thunderbolt of <s>Indra</s>,
made of a thousand rays, for destroying <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s>.

children.text: rūpaṃ cāpratimaṃ cakre tvaṣṭā padbhyāmṛte mahat ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> made his great, incomparable form, except for the feet.

children.text: na śaśākātha taddraṣṭuṃ pādarūpaṃ raveḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he was not able to look again at the form of <s>Ravi</s>'s feet.

children.text: arcāsvapi tataḥ pādau na kaścitkārayet kvacit ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in images, no one should ever have the feet made.

children.text: yaḥ karoti sa pāpiṣṭhāṃ gatimāpnoti ninditām
children.translated_text: Whoever does so obtains the most sinful and blameworthy fate.
In this world he contracts leprosy and is joined with suffering.
Therefore one who desires <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), pleasure, and wealth, in paintings and in temples alike,
should never have the feet of the wise god of gods made anywhere.
Then that blessed lord, the chief of the immortals, went to the earthly world.
Desire-stricken, <s>Divākara</s> desired her at her mouth alone.
He was in the form of a great horse and enveloped in radiance.
And <s>Saṃjñā</s>, shaken in mind and bewildered with fear,
expelled it through her nostrils, suspecting, 'This is another male.'

children.text: tadretasas tato jātāv aśvināv iti niścitam ||
children.translated_text: From that semen, then, the two <s>Aśvins</s> were born; so it is certain.
Because they were born as good sons they became the two <s>Dasras</s>; because they came from the tip of the nose, the two <s>Nāsatyas</s>.

children.text: jñātvā cirācca taṃ devaṃ saṃtoṣam agamat param ||
children.translated_text: After a long time, recognizing that god, she attained supreme satisfaction.
Joyful, she went by aerial car to heaven together with her husband.
<s>Sāvarṇi Manu</s> too, rich in austerity, still remains on <s>Meru</s>.
<s>Śani</s>, through the power of austerity, then again obtained equality with the planets.
<s>Yamunā</s> and <s>Tapatī</s> again became rivers.
Likewise fearsome <s>Viṣṭi</s> took her place as a form of time.
There were ten mighty sons of <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>.
<s>Ila</s>, the first of them, was born in the sacrifice for obtaining a son.

children.text: ikṣvākuḥ kuśanābhaśca ariṣṭo dhṛṣṭa eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, <s>Kuśanābha</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, and <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>,
<s>Nariṣyanta</s>, <s>Karūṣa</s>, and mighty <s>Śaryāti</s>,
and then <s>Pṛṣadhra</s> and <s>Nābhāga</s>: all of them were divine men.

children.text: abhiṣicya manuḥ putram ilaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ sa dhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: After consecrating his eldest son <s>Ila</s>, righteous <s>Manu</s>
went again for austerity to the abode called <s>Mahendravana</s>.
Then <s>Ila</s> set out over this earth to accomplish conquest of the quarters,
wandering through all the continents and overwhelming the rulers of the earth.
Powerful, drawn on by his horse, he went to <s>Śambhu</s>'s pleasure-grove,
the great <s>Śaravaṇa</s> by name, strewn with wish-fulfilling trees and creepers.
There the lord of gods, <s>Śambhu</s>, whose crest bears the half-moon, takes his pleasure.
There in <s>Śaravaṇa</s>, long ago, an agreement had been made with <s>Umā</s>:

children.text: puṃnāma sattvaṃ yatkiṃcid āgamiṣyati te vane
children.translated_text: Whatever being bearing a male name comes into that forest of yours,
all of it, within a circle of ten yojanas, shall become female.
King <s>Ila</s>, unaware of the agreement, once entered <s>Śaravaṇa</s>.
Just as he entered, he became female, and his horse at that time became a mare.

children.text: puruṣatvaṃ hṛtaṃ sarvaṃ strīrūpe vismito nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: With all his masculinity taken away, the king, astonished, was in a woman's form.
As a woman she became <s>Ilā</s>, with full, high, firm breasts.
She had high hips and loins, and eyes long like lotus petals.
She was slender, with a full-moon face and eyes bright with charm.
Her arms were long and full from the shoulders, and her hair was dark and curly.
She had fine body hair, beautiful teeth, and a soft, deep voice.
Her complexion was dusky-fair, and she moved like a goose and an elephant.
She had a pair of bow-like brows and delicate coppery nail-sprouts.

children.text: bhramantī ca vane tasmiṃś cintayāmāsa bhāminī
children.translated_text: Wandering in that forest, the beautiful woman thought,

children.text: ko me pitāthavā bhrātā kā me mātā bhavediha ||
children.translated_text: 'Who is my father, or my brother? Who might my mother be here?'
'To what husband have I been given? How long shall I dwell upon the earth?'
