As she was thinking thus, that woman was seen by the son of <s>Soma</s>.
<s>Ilā</s>, lovely in complexion, captivated his mind by her beauty.
Then <s>Budha</s>, tormented by desire, made an effort to obtain her.
Taking on a distinctive appearance, with staff, water-pot, and book,
with many clusters of triple pavitrakas made from bamboo staffs,
in the form of a twice-born student, with a topknot, reciting sacred formulas, and wearing earrings,
accompanied by suitable brahmacārins bearing fuel-sticks, flowers, kuśa grass, and water,
as if searching in that forest, he called out to that <s>Ilā</s>.
He was hidden outside the forest, within a circle of trees.
Suddenly, in agitation, he spoke to her as though with reproach:
'Leaving the service of the agnihotra, where have you gone from my house?'

children.text: iyaṃ vihāravelā te hy atikrāmati sāmpratam
children.translated_text: 'This present hour for your recreation is passing by.'
'Come, come, broad-hipped one; for what reason are you alarmed?'
'This is the evening time for recreation here.'
'After smearing the floor, adorn my house with flowers.'
But she said, 'I have forgotten all this, O treasure of austerity.'

children.text: ātmānaṃ tvāṃ ca bhartāraṃ kulaṃ ca vada me 'nagha ||
children.translated_text: 'Tell me about myself, about you as my husband, and about my family, O sinless one.'

children.text: budhaḥ provāca tāṃ tanvīmilā tvaṃ varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: <s>Budha</s> said to slender <s>Ilā</s>, 'You are <s>Ilā</s>, lovely-complexioned,

children.text: ahaṃ ca kāmuko nāma bahuvidyo budhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and I, called <s>Kāmuka</s>, am remembered as <s>Budha</s>, skilled in many sciences.

children.text: tejasvinaḥ kule jātaḥ pitā me brāhmaṇādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: I was born in a radiant family; my father is the lord of brahmins.'
At these words of his, she entered <s>Budha</s>'s dwelling,
joined with pillars, divine, and fashioned by māyā.
Dwelling in that house, <s>Ilā</s> considered herself fulfilled.
Ah, what conduct, ah, what beauty, ah, what wealth, ah, what family!

children.text: mama cāsya ca me bharturaho lāvaṇyam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: And ah, the excellent charm of me and of this husband of mine!

children.text: reme ca sā tena samamatikālamilā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Ilā</s> enjoyed herself together with him for a very long time,
in a house filled with every enjoyment, just as in the palace of <s>Indra</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then his brothers, men searching for the king,
led by <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, went then to the vicinity of <s>Śaravaṇa</s>.

children.text: tataste dadṛśuḥ sarve vaḍabām agrataḥ sthitām
children.translated_text: Thereupon all of them saw a mare standing before them,
her peerless body shining with the rays of a jeweled saddle.
From recognizing the saddle, they all fell into astonishment:

children.text: ayaṃ candraprabho nāma vājī tasya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "This is the horse of that great-souled one, named <s>Candraprabha</s>.
For what reason has he assumed this excellent form of a mare?"
Then they asked <s>Maitrāvaruṇi</s>, their family priest:
"Why has this wonder occurred? Tell us, best of those who know yoga."
And <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, having seen everything with the eye of meditation, spoke.
"A condition was made long ago in <s>Śaravaṇa</s> by the beloved of <s>Śambhu</s>:
whatever male enters here will obtain womanhood.
This horse too has gone to womanhood together with the king himself.
It will return again to maleness, as will that one who is like <s>Dhanada</s>.
Therefore effort must likewise be made after worshipping <s>Pinākin</s>."
Then those men went to the place where the god <s>Maheśvara</s> was.
With various hymns they praised <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: tāv ūcatur alaṅghyo 'yaṃ samayaḥ kiṃtu sāmpratam ||
children.translated_text: The two said, "This condition cannot be transgressed; but at present,
whatever fruit there may be from <s>Ikṣvāku</s>'s horse sacrifice,
after giving that to us, the hero will without doubt become a <s>kimpuruṣa</s>."
When they had said, "So be it," those sons of <s>Vaivasvata</s> went away.
And through <s>Ikṣvāku</s>'s horse sacrifice, <s>Ilā</s> became a <s>kimpuruṣa</s>.
For one month the hero was a man, and again for one month a woman.
While staying in the house of <s>Budha</s>, <s>Ilā</s> became pregnant.
She gave birth to a single son endowed with many virtues.
After fathering that son, <s>Budha</s> then went to the heavenly world.
At that time that region, named from <s>Ilā</s>, became <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.
At the beginning of the Lunar and Solar lineages, <s>Ilā</s> was the delight of <s>Manu</s>.
Thus <s>Purūravas</s> was born, increaser of the lineage, from the male-female one.
And <s>Ikṣvāku</s> has likewise been declared to belong to the Solar lineage, O rich in austerity.

children.text: ilaḥ kimpuruṣatve ca sudyumna iti cocyate
children.translated_text: In the state of being a <s>kimpuruṣa</s>, <s>Ilā</s> is also called <s>Sudyumna</s>.
Again, <s>Sudyumna</s> had three unconquered sons:

children.text: utkalo vai gahas tadvaddharitāśvaś ca vīryavān
children.translated_text: <s>Utkala</s>, <s>Gaya</s>, and likewise the mighty <s>Haritāśva</s>.

children.text: utkalasyotkalā nāma gayasya tu gayā matā ||
children.translated_text: The land of <s>Utkala</s> is called <s>Utkalā</s>, and that of <s>Gaya</s> is regarded as <s>Gayā</s>.
The eastern quarter of <s>Haritāśva</s> became famous, together with the <s>Kurus</s>.
Then, after consecrating his son <s>Purūravas</s> at <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>,
he went to enjoy the <s>Ilāvṛta</s> region, where divine fruits were food.
<s>Ikṣvāku</s>, the eldest heir, obtained the <s>Madhyadeśa</s>.
<s>Nariṣyanta</s>'s son was named <s>Śuci</s>, a man of great strength.
From <s>Nābhāga</s> came <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, and <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s> had three sons:
<s>Dhṛtaketu</s>, <s>Citranātha</s>, and mighty <s>Raṇadhṛṣṭa</s>.

children.text: ānarto nāma śaryāteḥ sukanyā caiva dārikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ānarta</s> was the son of <s>Śaryāti</s>, and <s>Sukanyā</s> was his daughter.
<s>Ānarta</s> had a son, the powerful <s>Rocamāna</s>.
The country of <s>Ānarta</s> was <s>Nābha</s>, and its city was <s>Kuśasthalī</s>.
<s>Rocamāna</s>'s son was <s>Reva</s>, also called <s>Raivata</s>.

children.text: kakudmī cāparaṃ nāma jyeṣṭhaḥ putraśatasya ca ||
children.translated_text: His other name was <s>Kakudmī</s>; he was the eldest of a hundred sons.

children.text: revatī tasya sā kanyā bhāryā rāmasya viśrutā
children.translated_text: His daughter was <s>Revatī</s>, famed as the wife of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: karūṣasya tu kārūṣā bahavaḥ prathitā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Karūṣa</s> came many <s>Kārūṣas</s>, renowned on earth.
<s>Pṛṣadhra</s>, because of killing a cow, was born a <s>Śūdra</s> through his guru's curse.
I shall tell the lineage of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>; listen, best of seers.

children.text: ikṣvākoḥ putratām āpa vikukṣir nāma devarāṭ
children.translated_text: <s>Vikukṣi</s>, named <s>Devarāṭ</s>, obtained the status of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>'s son.
He was the eldest of a hundred sons, and his own sons were fifteen.
North of <s>Meru</s>, those best of kings were born.
And another hundred and fourteen belonged to him likewise.
Those kings who are proclaimed south of <s>Meru</s>
had as their eldest one named <s>Kakutstha</s>; his son was <s>Suyodhana</s>.
His son was named <s>Pṛthu</s>, and <s>Viśvaga</s> was <s>Pṛthu</s>'s son.
<s>Indu</s> was his son, and after him came <s>Yuvanāśva</s>.
Then came <s>Śrāvasta</s>, of great brilliance, and <s>Vatsaka</s> was his son,
by whom <s>Śrāvastī</s> was founded in the <s>Gauḍa</s> country, O best twice-born.
From <s>Śrāvasta</s> came <s>Bṛhadaśva</s>, and from him came <s>Kuvalāśva</s>.
He attained the name <s>Dhundhumāra</s>, because the one named <s>Dhundhu</s> was slain in ancient times.

children.text: tasya putrās trayo jātā dṛḍhāśvo daṇḍa eva ca
children.translated_text: Three sons were born to him: <s>Dṛḍhāśva</s>, <s>Daṇḍa</s>,
and the renowned <s>Kapilāśva</s>, the powerful son of <s>Dhundhumāra</s>.
<s>Dṛḍhāśva</s>'s son was <s>Pramoda</s>, and <s>Haryaśva</s> was his son.
From <s>Haryaśva</s> came <s>Nikumbha</s>, and after him came <s>Saṃhatāśva</s>.
<s>Akṛtāśva</s> and <s>Raṇāśva</s> were both sons of <s>Saṃhatāśva</s>.
<s>Yuvanāśva</s> was the son of <s>Raṇāśva</s>, and from him came <s>Māndhātā</s>.
From <s>Māndhātā</s> came <s>Purukutsa</s> and the king <s>Dharmasena</s>;
also the famous <s>Mucukunda</s> and the powerful <s>Śatrujit</s>.
<s>Purukutsa</s>'s son was <s>Vasuda</s>, lord of the <s>Narmadā</s>.
<s>Sambhūti</s> was his son, and after him came <s>Tridhanvan</s>.
The son of <s>Tridhanvan</s> was born and is remembered as <s>Trayyāruṇa</s>.
From him came one named <s>Satyavrata</s>; from him <s>Satyaratha</s> is remembered.
His son was <s>Hariścandra</s>, and from <s>Hariścandra</s> came <s>Rohita</s>.
From <s>Rohita</s> <s>Vṛka</s> was born, and from <s>Vṛka</s> <s>Bāhu</s> arose.
His son was king <s>Sagara</s>, exceedingly devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: dve bhārye sagarasyāpi prabhā bhānumatī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sagara</s> had two wives, <s>Prabhā</s> and <s>Bhānumatī</s>.
The two of them formerly worshiped <s>Aurva</s>, the fire, desiring sons.
When <s>Aurva</s> was pleased, he granted them an excellent boon according to their wish.
Let one receive sixty thousand sons, and the other a single son,
a founder of the lineage; then <s>Prabhā</s> accepted the many sons.
<s>Bhānumatī</s> accepted one son, <s>Asamañjasa</s>.
Then <s>Prabhā</s>, the Yādavī, gave birth to sixty thousand sons.
While digging up the earth in search of the horse, they were burned by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
But the son of <s>Asamañjasa</s> was the famous one named <s>Aṃśumān</s>.

children.text: tasya putro dilīpas tu dilīpāttu bhagīrathaḥ
children.translated_text: His son was <s>Dilīpa</s>, and from <s>Dilīpa</s> came <s>Bhagīratha</s>,
by whom, after he had performed austerity, the <s>Gaṅgā</s> called <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> was brought down.
The son of <s>Bhagīratha</s> is famed as <s>Nābhāga</s>.
From <s>Nābhāga</s> came <s>Ambarīṣa</s>; after him came <s>Sindhudvīpa</s>.
His son was <s>Ayutāyu</s>; after him came <s>Ṛtuparṇa</s>.
His son was <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>, and after him <s>Sarvakarman</s> is remembered.
His son was <s>Anaraṇya</s>; his son was <s>Nighna</s>.
Two sons of <s>Nighna</s> were born, the kings <s>Anamitra</s> and <s>Raghu</s>.

children.text: anāmitro vanamagād bhavitā sa kṛte nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Anamitra</s> went to the forest; he was to be a king in the <s>Kṛta</s> age.
From <s>Raghu</s> came <s>Dilīpa</s>, and from <s>Dilīpa</s> came <s>Aja</s>.
From <s>Aja</s> was born <s>Dīrghabāhu</s>, and after him came king <s>Ajapāla</s>.
From him <s>Daśaratha</s> was born; he had four sons.
All were of the nature of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; among them <s>Rāma</s> was the eldest.
He was the destroyer of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and likewise the increaser of the lineage of the <s>Raghus</s>.
<s>Vālmīki</s>, best of Bhārgavas, composed his story.
His two sons, <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, increased the family of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.
From <s>Kuśa</s> was born <s>Atithi</s>, and his son was <s>Niṣadha</s>.
From him came <s>Nala</s> the Naiṣadha, and from him <s>Nabhas</s> was born.
From <s>Nabhas</s> came <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>; after him <s>Kṣemadhanvan</s> is remembered.
His son was the heroic and mighty <s>Devānīka</s>.
His son was <s>Ahīnagu</s>; after him came <s>Sahasrāśva</s>.
Then came <s>Candrāvaloka</s>, and after him <s>Tārāpīḍa</s>.
His son was <s>Candragiri</s>; from him came <s>Bhānu</s>, and then <s>Candra</s>.
From him came <s>Śrutāyu</s>, who was struck down in the <s>Bhārata</s>.

children.text: nalau dvāv eva vikhyātau vaṃśe kaśyapasambhave
children.translated_text: Only two <s>Nalas</s> are renowned in the lineage descended from <s>Kaśyapa</s>:
the son of <s>Vīrasena</s>, and likewise the Naiṣadha king.
These kings in the lineage of <s>Vaivasvata</s> gave abundant gifts.
Those born in the lineage of <s>Ikṣvāku</s> have been chiefly proclaimed.
<s>Manu</s> said:
Blessed lord, I wish to hear the excellent lineage of the <s>Pitṛs</s>,
and especially how the sun and the moon became deities of the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite).
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Come then, I shall tell you the excellent lineage of the <s>Pitṛs</s>.
In heaven there are seven groups of <s>Pitṛs</s>; of them, three are without bodily form.
The four others have form, and all of them are of immeasurable splendor.
The bodiless groups of <s>Pitṛs</s> belong to <s>Vairāja Prajāpati</s>.
They whom the hosts of gods worship are famed as the <s>Vairājas</s>.
Those who have fallen from yoga, after attaining the eternal worlds,
are born again at the end of <s>Brahmā</s>'s day as expounders of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: samprāpya tāṃ smṛtiṃ bhūyo yogaṃ sāṃkhyamanuttamam ||
children.translated_text: Recovering that memory again, and the unsurpassed yoga of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>,
they attain perfection through yoga, from which return is difficult.
Therefore <s>śrāddhas</s> (ancestral offerings) should be given by donors only to yogins.

children.text: eteṣāṃ mānasī kanyā patnī himavato matā
children.translated_text: Their mind-born daughter is regarded as the wife of <s>Himavat</s>.
<s>Maināka</s> was his heir; <s>Krauñca</s> was his elder brother.
By him the fourth island, <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s>, surrounded by ghee, is remembered.

children.text: menā ca suṣuve tisraḥ kanyā yogavatīstataḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Menā</s> then gave birth to three daughters possessed of yoga:
<s>Umā</s>, <s>Ekaparṇā</s>, and <s>Aparṇā</s>, all devoted to severe vows.
One was given to <s>Rudra</s>, one to <s>Asita</s>, and the other to <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>.

children.text: dattā himavatā bālāḥ sarvā loke tapo'dhikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those maidens were given by <s>Himavat</s>; all were supreme in austerity in the world.
The seers said:
Why did <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> formerly burn herself by her own self?
And how was she likewise born on earth as the daughter of <s>Himavat</s>?
What did she say while ending herself, or what was said by <s>Dakṣa</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>?
O <s>Sūta</s>, tell in detail about the mother of the world.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
At the great sacrifice of <s>Dakṣa</s>, rich in excellent gifts,
when the gods had been invited, <s>Satī</s> spoke to her father:
"Father, why has my husband not been invited to this sacrifice?"

children.text: ayogya iti tāmāha dakṣo yajñeṣu śūlabhṛt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dakṣa</s> said to her, "The trident-bearer is unfit for sacrifices.
<s>Rudra</s> causes dissolution; therefore he has a share in inauspiciousness."
Then <s>Satī</s> became angry: "I shall abandon this body born from you.
And you shall become the only son among ten <s>Pitṛs</s>.
In a kṣatriya birth, and at an <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), you shall meet destruction from <s>Rudra</s>."
Having spoken thus, she entered yoga, and with the fire born from her own body
she then burned herself, before gods, asuras, and kiṃnaras.
"What, what is this?" cried the hosts of gandharvas and guhyakas.
Then <s>Dakṣa</s> approached and, bowing down, spoke in distress:
"You are the mother of this world, the deity of the world's good fortune."
O goddess, you have become my daughter because you wished to show me favor.
There is nothing in the universe, with its moving and unmoving beings, that is without you.

children.text: prasādaṃ kuru dharmajñe na māṃ tyaktumihārhasi ||
children.translated_text: Show favor, O knower of <s>dharma</s>; you ought not to abandon me here.

children.text: prāha devī yadārabdhaṃ tatkāryaṃ me na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The goddess said: What has been begun is indeed my task; there is no doubt about this.
But you must necessarily, in the mortal world, through <s>Śūlin</s> who destroyed the sacrifice,
perform austerity near me, for the sake of favor and for the creation of the worlds.
You will become a <s>Prajāpati</s>, and also the bodily father of ten.
By a portion of me, sixty women will become your bodily daughters.
Practicing austerity in my presence, you will attain the highest yoga.
Thus addressed, <s>Dakṣa</s> said: In which places, O sinless one,

children.text: tīrtheṣu ca tvaṃ draṣṭavyā stotavyā kaiśca nāmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and at which tīrthas should you be seen, and by what names should you be praised?
The goddess said:
I should always be seen in all beings, everywhere on earth.
In all the worlds, whatever exists is not without me.
Nevertheless, I shall tell truly the places in which I should be seen by those who desire perfection,

children.text: smartavyā bhūtikāmair vā tāni vakṣyāmi tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or remembered by those who desire prosperity.
In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> I am <s>Viśālākṣī</s>; in <s>Naimiṣa</s>, <s>Liṅgadhāriṇī</s>.
At <s>Prayāga</s> I am the goddess <s>Lalitā</s>; on <s>Gandhamādana</s>, <s>Kāmākṣī</s>.
At <s>Mānasa</s> I am named <s>Kumudā</s>, and likewise <s>Viśvakāyā</s> in <s>Ambara</s>.
At <s>Gomanta</s> I am named <s>Gomatī</s>; on <s>Mandara</s>, <s>Kāmacāriṇī</s>.
In <s>Caitraratha</s> I am <s>Madotkaṭā</s>; in <s>Hastināpura</s>, <s>Jayantī</s>.
At <s>Kānyakubja</s> I am likewise <s>Gaurī</s>; on <s>Malaya</s> mountain, <s>Rambhā</s>.
At <s>Ekāmbhaka</s> I am <s>Kīrtimatī</s>; at <s>Viśveśvara</s> they know me as <s>Viśvā</s>.
At <s>Puṣkara</s> I am called <s>Puruhūtā</s>; at <s>Kedāra</s>, <s>Mārgadāyinī</s>.
On the back of <s>Himavat</s> I am <s>Nandā</s>; at <s>Gokarṇa</s>, <s>Bhadrakarṇikā</s>.
At <s>Sthāneśvara</s> I am <s>Bhavānī</s>; at <s>Bilvala</s>, <s>Bilvapattrikā</s>.

children.text: śrīśaile mādhavī nāma bhadrā bhadreśvare tathā ||
children.translated_text: On <s>Śrīśaila</s> I am named <s>Mādhavī</s>; likewise at <s>Bhadreśvara</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>.
On <s>Varāhaśaila</s> I am <s>Jayā</s>; at <s>Kamalālaya</s>, <s>Kāmalā</s>.

children.text: rudrakoṭyāṃ ca rudrāṇī kālī kālañjare girau ||
children.translated_text: At <s>Rudrakoṭi</s> I am <s>Rudrāṇī</s>; on <s>Kālañjara</s> mountain, <s>Kālī</s>.
At <s>Mahāliṅga</s> I am <s>Kapilā</s>; at <s>Markoṭa</s>, <s>Mukuṭeśvarī</s>.
At <s>Śālagrāma</s> I am <s>Mahādevī</s>; at <s>Śivaliṅga</s>, <s>Jalapriyā</s>.

children.text: māyāpuryāṃ kumārī tu saṃtāne lalitā tathā
children.translated_text: At <s>Māyāpurī</s> I am <s>Kumārī</s>; at <s>Saṃtāna</s>, likewise <s>Lalitā</s>.
At <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> I am <s>Utpalākṣī</s>; at <s>Kamalākṣa</s>, <s>Mahotpalā</s>.
At the <s>Gaṅgā</s> I am named <s>Maṅgalā</s>; at <s>Puruṣottama</s>, <s>Vimilā</s>.
At <s>Vipāśā</s> I am <s>Amoghākṣī</s>; at <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>, <s>Pāṭalā</s>.
At <s>Supārśva</s> I am <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>; at <s>Vikūṭa</s>, <s>Bhadrasundarī</s>.
At <s>Vipula</s> I am named <s>Vipulā</s>; on <s>Malayācala</s>, <s>Kalyāṇī</s>.

children.text: koṭavī koṭitīrthe tu sugandhā mādhave vane
children.translated_text: At <s>Koṭitīrtha</s> I am <s>Koṭavī</s>; in <s>Mādhava</s> forest, <s>Sugandhā</s>.
At <s>Godāśrama</s> I am <s>Trisaṃdhyā</s>; at <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>, <s>Ratipriyā</s>.
At <s>Śivakuṇḍa</s> I am <s>Śivānandā</s>; on the bank of the <s>Devikā</s>, <s>Nandinī</s>.

children.text: rukmiṇī dvāravatyāṃ tu rādhā vṛndāvane vane ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Dvāravatī</s> I am <s>Rukmiṇī</s>; in the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Rādhā</s>.
In <s>Mathurā</s> I am <s>Devakī</s>; in the underworld, <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
At <s>Citrakūṭa</s> I am likewise <s>Sītā</s>; in the <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Vindhyādhivāsinī</s>.

children.text: sahyādrāv ekavīrā tu hariścandre tu candrikā
children.translated_text: On <s>Sahyādri</s> I am <s>Ekavīrā</s>; on <s>Hariścandra</s>, <s>Candrikā</s>.
At <s>Rāmatīrtha</s> I am <s>Ramaṇā</s>; at the <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Mṛgāvatī</s>.
At <s>Karavīra</s> I am <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>; at <s>Vināyaka</s>, the goddess <s>Umā</s>.
At <s>Vaidyanātha</s> I am <s>Arogā</s>; at <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Maheśvarī</s>.
At the hot tīrthas I am called <s>Abhayā</s>; in the cave of the <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>.

children.text: māṇḍavye māṇḍavī nāma svāhā māheśvare pure ||
children.translated_text: At <s>Māṇḍavya</s> I am named <s>Māṇḍavī</s>; in the city of <s>Māheśvara</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>.
At <s>Chāgalāṇḍa</s> I am <s>Pracaṇḍā</s>; at <s>Makarandaka</s>, <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.
At <s>Someśvara</s> I am <s>Varārohā</s>; at <s>Prabhāsa</s>, <s>Puṣkarāvatī</s>.
At <s>Sarasvatī</s> I am regarded as <s>Devamātā</s>, and on the shore of the ocean too.
At <s>Mahālaya</s> I am <s>Mahābhāgā</s>; at <s>Payoṣṇī</s>, <s>Piṅgaleśvarī</s>.
At <s>Kṛtaśauca</s> I am <s>Siṃhikā</s>; at <s>Kārttikeya</s>, <s>Yaśaskarī</s>.
At <s>Utpalāvartaka</s> I am <s>Lolā</s>; at the confluence of the <s>Śoṇa</s>, <s>Subhadrā</s>.
At <s>Siddhapura</s> I am <s>Mātā</s>; at <s>Bharatāśrama</s>, <s>Lakṣmīraṅganā</s>.
At <s>Jālaṃdhara</s> I am <s>Viśvamukhī</s>; on <s>Kiṣkindha</s> mountain, <s>Tārā</s>.
In the <s>Devadāru</s> forest I am <s>Puṣṭi</s>; in the region of <s>Kāśmīra</s>, <s>Medhā</s>.

children.text: bhīmā devī himādrau tu puṣṭirviśveśvare tathā ||
children.translated_text: On <s>Himādri</s> I am the goddess <s>Bhīmā</s>; at <s>Viśveśvara</s>, likewise <s>Puṣṭi</s>.
At <s>Kapālamocana</s> I am <s>Śuddhi</s>; at <s>Kāyāvarohaṇa</s>, <s>Mātā</s>.
At <s>Śaṅkhoddhāra</s> I am named <s>Dhvani</s>; and at <s>Piṇḍāraka</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>.
At <s>Candrabhāgā</s> I am <s>Kālā</s>; at <s>Acchoda</s>, <s>Śivakāriṇī</s>.
At <s>Veṇā</s> I am named <s>Amṛtā</s>; at <s>Badarī</s>, likewise <s>Urvaśī</s>.
In <s>Uttarakuru</s> I am <s>Oṣadhī</s>; on <s>Kuśadvīpa</s>, <s>Kuśodakā</s>.
On <s>Hemakūṭa</s> I am <s>Manmathā</s>; at <s>Mukuṭa</s>, <s>Satyavādinī</s>.
At the aśvattha tree I am <s>Vandanīyā</s>; in the abode of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Nidhi</s>.
In the mouth of the Veda I am <s>Gāyatrī</s>; in the presence of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Pārvatī</s>.
In the world of the gods I am <s>Indrāṇī</s>; in the mouths of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>.

children.text: sūryabimbe prabhā nāma mātṝṇāṃ vaiṣṇavī matā ||
children.translated_text: In the disk of the sun I am named <s>Prabhā</s>; among the Mothers I am considered <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>.

children.text: arundhatī satīnāṃ tu rāmāsu ca tilottamā
children.translated_text: Among faithful wives I am <s>Arundhatī</s>; among lovely women, <s>Tilottamā</s>.
In the mind I am named <s>Brahmakalā</s>; I am the power of all embodied beings.
This excellent hundred of names has been stated in summary.
And this has been declared as the hundred and eight tīrthas.
Whoever remembers or hears it is freed from all sins.

children.text: eṣu tīrtheṣu yaḥ kṛtvā snānaṃ paśyati māṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The man who, having bathed at these tīrthas, sees me,
freed from all sins, dwells for a kalpa in the city of <s>Śiva</s>.
But the human being who makes his final time devoted to me in these places,
piercing beyond the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, reaches the <s>Śāṃkara</s> state.
Whoever recites the hundred and eight names in the presence of <s>Śiva</s>,
on the third lunar day or on the eighth, becomes a man with many sons.

children.text: godāne śrāddhadāne vā ahany ahani vā budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the wise man, at a gift of cows, at a gift for the ancestors, or day after day...
A learned man, reciting this in the rite of worshiping the gods, attains <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: evaṃ vadantī sā tatra dadāhātmānam ātmanā ||
children.translated_text: Speaking thus there, she burned her own self by her own power.
In time, <s>Dakṣa</s>, the <s>Svāyambhuva</s>, also became <s>Prācetasa</s>.
And that goddess became <s>Pārvatī</s>, bearer of half of <s>Śiva</s>'s body.
Born from the womb of <s>Menā</s>, she grants the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.
<s>Arundhatī</s>, reciting this, attained unsurpassed yoga.
And <s>Purūravas</s> attained preeminence in the world of royal sages.

children.text: yayātiḥ putralābhaṃ ca dhanalābhaṃ ca bhārgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yayāti</s> obtained sons, and <s>Bhārgava</s> obtained wealth.
So too many other gods and daityas, and likewise brahmins and kṣatriyas,
many vaiśyas and śūdras, attained the success they desired.
Where this is written down and remains, worshiped in the presence of the gods,

children.text: na tatra śoko daurgatyaṃ kadācidapi jāyate ||
children.translated_text: there neither grief nor misfortune ever arises at any time.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
There are worlds named <s>Somapatha</s>, where the sons of <s>Marīci</s>,
the divine <s>Pitṛs</s>, dwell, whom the gods greatly honor.

children.text: agniṣvāttā iti khyātā yajvāno yatra saṃsthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those known as the <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>, the sacrificers, are established there.

children.text: acchodā nāma teṣāṃ tu mānasī kanyakā nadī ||
children.translated_text: Their mind-born maiden is the river named <s>Acchodā</s>.

children.text: acchodaṃ nāma ca saraḥ pitṛbhirnirmitaṃ purā
children.translated_text: And a lake named <s>Acchoda</s> was made by the <s>Pitṛs</s> long ago.
<s>Acchodā</s> performed divine austerity for a thousand years.

children.text: ājagmuḥ pitarastuṣṭāḥ kila dātuṃ ca tāṃ varam
children.translated_text: The satisfied <s>Pitṛs</s> came, it is said, to give her a boon,
all bearing divine forms, divine garlands, and divine unguents.
All were young and strong, resembling <s>Kusumāyudha</s>, the flower-armed god of love.
In their midst that maiden saw the <s>Pitṛ</s> named <s>Amāvasu</s>.
Seeking a boon and afflicted by <s>Kusumāyudha</s>, she chose union with him.

children.text: yogādbhraṣṭā tu sā tena vyabhicāreṇa bhāminī ||
children.translated_text: Through that transgression the lovely woman fell from yoga.
Though before she had not touched the earth, she then fell upon the ground's surface.

children.text: tithāv amāvasur yasyām icchāṃ cakre na tāṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: On the lunar day when <s>Amāvasu</s> did not direct desire toward her,
because of his firmness that day became famous among people as <s>Amāvāsyā</s>.
Therefore it is dear to the <s>Pitṛs</s>, and on it offerings become inexhaustible.
<s>Acchodā</s>, downcast, wretched, and ashamed because her austerity had been lost,
prayed to the <s>Pitṛs</s> there for the restoration of her own standing.
As she lamented, the ascetic woman was addressed by the <s>Pitṛs</s>,
who then perceived the future event and the divine task appointed for her.
The greatly fortunate ones spoke these words with gracious and auspicious speech:

children.text: divi divyaśarīreṇa yat kiṃcit kriyate budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is done by the wise in heaven with a divine body,
by that very deed one enjoys the fruit of that act, O lovely woman.

children.text: sadyaḥ phalanti karmāṇi devatve pretya mānuṣe ||
children.translated_text: Actions bear fruit immediately in divine existence, but among humans after death.

children.text: tasmāttvaṃ putri tapasaḥ prāpsyase pretya tatphalam
children.translated_text: Therefore, daughter, after death you will obtain that fruit of your austerity.
In the twenty-eighth <s>Dvāpara</s> age you will be born from a fish-womb.
Because of your transgression against the <s>Pitṛs</s>, you will enter a difficult family.

children.text: tasmādrājño vasoḥ kanyā tvam avaśyaṃ bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you will certainly become the daughter of King <s>Vasu</s>.
Having become a maiden, you will regain your own worlds, hard to obtain.
Through the seed of <s>Parāśara</s> you will obtain a single son.
On an island abounding in badarī trees he will be the unfailing <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: sa vedamekaṃ bahudhā vibhajiṣyati te sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That son of yours will divide the single <s>Veda</s> into many parts.
And there will be two sons of <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, the <s>Paurava</s> who is a portion of the ocean:
<s>Vicitravīrya</s> and King <s>Citrāṅgada</s>, his sons.
Having produced those two sons, born for that wise man through the field,
you will dwell in the <s>Pitṛ</s>-world in the form of the <s>Prauṣṭhapadī Aṣṭakā</s>.
By name you will be <s>Satyavatī</s> in the world, and likewise <s>Aṣṭakā</s> in the <s>Pitṛ</s>-world.
You will always grant longevity and health, and bestow the fruit of every desire.

children.text: bhaviṣyasi pare kāle nadītvaṃ ca gamiṣyasi
children.translated_text: In a later time you will also become a river.
As the holy and satisfying best of rivers, you will be known in the world as <s>Acchodā</s>.
Having spoken thus, that group of theirs vanished on that very spot.

children.text: sāpyavāpa ca tatsarvaṃ phalaṃ yaduditaṃ purā ||
children.translated_text: And she obtained all the fruit that had been declared before.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: vibhrājā nāma cānye tu divi santi suvarcasaḥ
children.translated_text: There are also other brilliant ones in heaven, named <s>Vibhrājas</s>.

children.text: lokā barhiṣado yatra pitaraḥ santi suvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are the worlds where the well-vowed <s>Barhiṣad</s> <s>Pitṛs</s> dwell.
There are thousands of aerial cars furnished with sacrificial grass.
There, by mere intention, the <s>Barhiṣads</s> stand as bestowers of fruits.
There the givers of <s>śrāddha</s> rejoice in halls of prosperity,
and hosts of gods and asuras, and groups of gandharvas and apsarases,
as well as hosts of yakṣas and rakṣases, worship them in heaven as deities.
Hundreds of sons of <s>Pulastya</s>, endowed with austerity and yoga,
great-souled and greatly fortunate, grant fearlessness to their devotees.

children.text: eteṣāṃ pīvarī kanyā mānasī divi viśrutā ||
children.translated_text: Their mind-born daughter, <s>Pīvarī</s>, is renowned in heaven.
A yoginī and mother of yoga, she performed very severe austerity.

children.text: prasanno bhagavāṃstasyā varaṃ vavre tu sā hareḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the blessed lord was pleased with her, she chose a boon from <s>Hari</s>.
Give me a husband possessed of yoga, handsome, and master of his senses,

children.text: dehi deva prasannastvaṃ patiṃ me vadatāṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: O god, if you are pleased: a husband for me, O best of speakers.

children.text: uvāca devo bhavitā vyāsaputro yadā śukaḥ
children.translated_text: The god said: When <s>Śuka</s>, son of <s>Vyāsa</s>, comes to be,

children.text: bhavitā tasya bhāryā tvaṃ yogācāryasya suvrate ||
children.translated_text: you will become the wife of that teacher of yoga, O woman of good vows.

children.text: bhaviṣyati ca te kanyā kṛtvī nāma ca yoginī
children.translated_text: And you will have a daughter, a yoginī named <s>Kṛtvī</s>.
At that time she is to be given by you to the human lord of <s>Pāñcāla</s>.

children.text: jananī brahmadattasya yogasiddhā ca gauḥ smṛtā
children.translated_text: She will be the mother of <s>Brahmadatta</s>, perfected in yoga and remembered as <s>Gauḥ</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇo gauraḥ prabhuḥ śambhur bhaviṣyanti ca te sutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Gaura</s>, <s>Prabhu</s>, and <s>Śambhu</s> will be your sons.
Great-souled and greatly fortunate, they will go to the highest state.
Having produced them, you will again attain liberation through yoga together with your husband.
The <s>Sumūrtimant</s> <s>Pitṛs</s> are remembered as sons of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: nāmnā tu mānasāḥ sarve sarve te dharmamūrtayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By name they are all <s>Mānasa</s>; all of them are embodiments of <s>dharma</s> (sacred order).

children.text: jyotirbhāsiṣu lokeṣu ye vasanti divaḥ param
children.translated_text: Those who dwell in shining worlds beyond heaven,
there the givers of śrāddha, radiant, sport and rejoice.
Even those born from the feet dwell in aerial palaces endowed with every desire;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ śrāddhadā viprā bhaktimantaḥ kriyānvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: how much more, O brahmins, do śrāddha-givers who are devoted and furnished with rites do so.

children.text: gaur nāma kanyā yeṣāṃ tu mānasī divi rājate
children.translated_text: Their mind-born daughter, named <s>Gauḥ</s>, shines in heaven;
she is the beloved wife of <s>Śukra</s> and increases the fame of the <s>Sādhyas</s>.
The worlds named <s>Marīcigarbha</s> are in the disk of <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, the sun;
there the Pitṛs called <s>Haviṣmants</s>, sons of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, remain.
Those best kṣatriyas who bestow śrāddha at tīrthas go there;
they are the Pitṛs of kings, bestowing the fruits of heaven and liberation.
Their mind-born daughter is <s>Yaśodā</s>, renowned in the worlds;

children.text: patnī hy aṃśumataḥ śreṣṭhā snuṣā pañcajanasya ca ||
children.translated_text: she is the excellent wife of <s>Aṃśumat</s> and the daughter-in-law of <s>Pañcajana</s>.
She was the mother of <s>Dilīpa</s> and the paternal grandmother of <s>Bhagīratha</s>.
The worlds called <s>Kāmadughā</s> grant the fruit of desired enjoyments.

children.text: susvadhā nāma pitaro yatra tiṣṭhanti suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: There dwell the well-vowed Pitṛs named <s>Susvadhās</s>;
in the worlds they are called <s>Ājyapas</s>, belonging to the Prajāpati <s>Kardama</s>.
Vaiśyas honor them, the descendants and heirs of <s>Pulaha</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>;
there all who have performed śrāddha, having gone there, see at once
their mothers, brothers, fathers, paternal aunts, friends, relations, and kinsmen,
even those seen through ten thousand births and experienced by the thousands.

children.text: eteṣāṃ mānasī kanyā virajā nāma viśrutā
children.translated_text: Their mind-born daughter is famed by the name <s>Virajā</s>;
she was the wife of <s>Nahuṣa</s> and also the mother of <s>Yayāti</s>.
Afterward she became <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>, a virtuous woman who went to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: traya ete gaṇāḥ proktāścaturthaṃ tu vadāmyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: These three groups have been declared; now I shall describe the fourth.
The worlds called <s>Mānasa</s> are situated above the cosmic egg;

children.text: yeṣāṃ tu mānasī kanyā narmadā nāma viśrutā ||
children.translated_text: their mind-born daughter is renowned by the name <s>Narmadā</s>.

children.text: somapā nāma pitaro yatra tiṣṭhanti śāśvatāḥ
children.translated_text: There dwell the eternal Pitṛs named <s>Somapās</s>;
all are said to bear the form of <s>dharma</s>, beyond <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: utpannāḥ svadhayā te tu brahmatvaṃ prāpya yoginaḥ
children.translated_text: Born from <s>Svadhā</s>, those yogins attained brahmahood,

children.text: kṛtvā sṛṣṭyādikaṃ sarvaṃ mānase sāmprataṃ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, having accomplished creation and all the rest, now abide in the mental realm.

children.text: narmadā nāma teṣāṃ tu kanyā toyavahā sarit
children.translated_text: Their daughter named <s>Narmadā</s> is a river bearing water;
flowing through the southern region, she purifies living beings.

children.text: tebhyaḥ sarve tu manavaḥ prajāḥ sargeṣu nirmitāḥ
children.translated_text: From them all the Manus and creatures were fashioned in the creations;
knowing this, people always perform śrāddhas, even when <s>dharma</s> has declined.
And in order to obtain from them again, through their favor, an unbroken line of yoga,
at the first creation of the Pitṛs, śrāddha itself was instituted.
For all of them, a silver vessel, or one furnished with silver,

children.text: dattaṃ svadhā purodhāya pitṝn prīṇāti sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: when given with <s>svadhā</s> placed before it, always pleases the Pitṛs.
A wise man should perform the nourishing rite for those consisting of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Yama</s>;
even in the absence of fire, he may do it in a brahmin's vital breaths, or in water.
At an <s>ajākarṇa</s> tree, an <s>aśvakarṇa</s> tree, in a cow-pen, or beside water,
the open sky is the place of the Pitṛs, and the southern direction is praised.
The sacred thread worn over the right shoulder, water, sesame seeds, and the leftward limb posture,

children.text: darbhā māṃsaṃ ca pāṭhīnaṃ gokṣīraṃ madhurā rasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: darbha grass, meat, pāṭhīna fish, cow's milk, and sweet juices,
rhinoceros flesh, iron, meat, honey, kuśa grass, śyāmāka and śāli rice,
barley, wild rice, mung beans, sugarcane, white flowers, and ghee
are always dear and approved for the Pitṛs here.

children.text: dveṣyāṇi sampravakṣyāmi śrāddhe varjyāni yāni tu ||
children.translated_text: I shall now declare the things hated by them, which must be avoided in śrāddha.
Lentils, hemp, niṣpāva beans, black gram, and safflower,
lotus, bilva, arka, dhattūra, pāribhadra, and aṭarūṣaka
should not be given in rites for the Pitṛs; nor should goat's or sheep's milk.
Kodrava grain, udāra, chickpeas, kapittha fruit, madhuka, and flax
should likewise not be given to the Pitṛs by one who desires what is dear to them.

children.text: pitṝn prīṇāti yo bhaktyā te punaḥ prīṇayanti tam ||
children.translated_text: The man who pleases the Pitṛs with devotion is in turn pleased by them.
The Pitṛs grant nourishment, heaven, health, and the fruit of offspring.
The rite for the Pitṛs is superior even to the rite for the gods.
For the gods, the Pitṛs' prior nourishment is remembered.
Quickly gracious, free from anger, weaponless, and firm in friendship,
tranquil in self, devoted to purity, and always speaking kindly,
attached to their devotees and bestowing happiness, the Pitṛs are the earlier deities.
The sun, <s>Ravi</s>, is remembered as the śrāddha-deity in the lordship over the <s>Haviṣmants</s>.
This entire recitation of the lineage of the Pitṛs has been told to you;

children.text: puṇyaṃ pavitram āyuṣyaṃ kīrtanīyaṃ sadā nṛbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is meritorious, purifying, life-giving, and should always be recited by men.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: śrutvaitat sarvam akhilaṃ manuḥ papraccha keśavam
children.translated_text: Having heard all this in full, <s>Manu</s> asked <s>Keśava</s>

children.text: śrāddhakālaṃ ca vividhaṃ śrāddhabhedaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: about the various times for śrāddha and also the distinctions among śrāddhas,

children.text: śrāddheṣu bhojanīyā ye ye ca varjyā dvijātayaḥ
children.translated_text: about which twice-born men should be fed at śrāddhas and which should be avoided,
and in what part of the day one should perform śrāddha for the Pitṛs.

children.text: kasmindattaṃ kathaṃ yāti śrāddhaṃ tu madhusūdana
children.translated_text: 'When it is given in what way, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>, does śrāddha reach them?

children.text: vidhinā kena kartavyaṃ kathaṃ prīṇāti tatpitṝn ||
children.translated_text: By what rule should it be performed, and how does it please those Pitṛs?'
<s>Matsya</s> said:
One should perform śrāddha every day, bringing satisfaction to the Pitṛs
with food and water, or with milk, roots, and fruits.
Śrāddha is said to be threefold: regular, occasional, and desire-prompted.
First I shall explain the regular śrāddha, which is without arghya and invocation.
One should understand that to be without offering to the gods; the pārvaṇa rite is remembered for lunar junction days.
The pārvaṇa rite is declared to be threefold. Listen to that now, O king.
Now listen, O king, to those who should be appointed for the parvan rite.
One who maintains the five fires, a snātaka, a trisuparṇa, and one who knows the six Vedāṅgas;
a śrotriya, the son of a śrotriya, skilled in the sentences of injunction;
one who knows all, knows the Veda, knows mantras, whose lineage is known and who belongs to a good family;
a knower of the Purāṇas, a knower of <s>dharma</s> (sacred law), devoted to recitation and study;
a devotee of <s>Śiva</s>, devoted to the ancestors, a devotee of <s>Sūrya</s>, or a Vaiṣṇava;
devoted to Brahmins, knowing yoga, calm, self-controlled, and virtuous;
one should also carefully feed one's daughter's son, one's own friends, and teachers.
One should feed a maternal uncle, a relative, officiating priests, teachers, and soma-drinkers;
also one who expounds the sacred sentence and one who investigates the sacrifice.
One who knows the rules of Sāman accents is a purifier even of those who purify the row;
a chanter of Sāmans, a brahmacārin, one furnished with the Veda, and a knower of brahman.
Where these men eat at a <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestor rite), that rite is truly meaningful.
These should be fed with care; now learn from me those who are to be avoided.
A fallen man, one accused of grave sin, an impotent man, slanderers, the deformed, and the diseased;
one with bad nails, one with black teeth, kuṇḍas and golas, and horse-keepers;
a parivitti, one whose self is improperly appointed, the negligent, the mad, and the cruel;
one with a cat-like or heron-like livelihood, a hypocrite, temple-priests, and others of that kind;
the ungrateful and atheists, likewise those dwelling in mleccha lands;
<s>Triśaṅkus</s>, <s>Barbaras</s>, <s>Drāvas</s>, <s>Vītas</s>, <s>Draviḍas</s>, and <s>Koṅkaṇas</s>;
one should avoid all bearers of sectarian marks, especially at the time of a <s>śrāddha</s>.
On the previous day or on the following day, with disciplined self, he should invite them.
For the ancestors attend those invited Brahmins.
Having become wind, they follow them and attend upon them as they sit.

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ jānumālabhya tvaṃ mayā tu nimantritaḥ
children.translated_text: Touching his right knee, he should say, 'You have been invited by me.'
Having invited them in this way, he should make the kinsmen of the ancestors hear the rule:
'You must be free from anger, devoted to purity, and constantly celibate,
as must I, the performer of the <s>śrāddha</s>.'
A man who maintains the sacred fire, after completing the ancestor-sacrifice called <s>tarpaṇa</s> (satiating offering),
should always perform the <s>piṇḍānvāhāryaka</s> <s>śrāddha</s> at the waning of the moon.
On a place plastered with cow dung and sloping southward,
he should perform the <s>śrāddha</s> with devotion, either in a cow pen or near water.
The fire-holder should offer the ancestral <s>caru</s> (oblation porridge) in equal handfuls,
saying, 'I offer to the ancestors,' and should place everything to the south.
Then, after sprinkling it with ghee, he should make three offerings in front.
Those too should be made long, four fingers broad.
He should make three ladles of khadira wood, fitted with silver,
a ratni in length, very smooth, with an excellent hand-shaped tip.

children.text: udapātraṃ ca kāṃsyaṃ ca mekṣaṇaṃ ca samitkuśān
children.translated_text: He should bring a water vessel, a bronze vessel, a ladle, fuel-sticks, and kuśa grass,
sesame seeds, vessels, good cloth, perfume, incense, and unguent.
Wearing the sacred thread in the apasavya manner, he should slowly bring everything to the south.
Having arranged all that in this way on the ground before the house,
on the spot plastered with cow dung, he should make a maṇḍala with cow urine.
With unbroken grains and flowers he should worship it in the apasavya manner.

children.text: viprāṇāṃ kṣālayet pādāv abhinandya punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: He should wash the feet of the Brahmins, honoring them again and again,
when seats furnished with darbha grass have been prepared according to rule.
After seating the Brahmins, who have sipped water, he should address them with the invitation:
two for the divine rite and three for the ancestor rite, or one for each in both cases.
Even if he is able, a wise man should not make an elaborate spread here when feeding them.
Then, after first appointing the Brahmins for the divine rite with arghya and the like, the wise man,
authorized by the Brahmins, should perform the rite in the fire as prescribed.
Then, after preparing the <s>caru</s> in a bronze vessel according to the rule stated in his own gṛhya tradition,
the wise man should make an offering for <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Yama</s>.
This is to be done in the southern fire, or, for the best twice-born man with one fire, in the established fire.
Having completed that while wearing the sacred thread in the normal manner, then the sprinkling and the rest
should all be done by one who knows, with the thread worn in the prācīnāvīta manner.
Then, from the remainder of that oblation, having made six <s>piṇḍas</s> (rice-balls),
he should give water with sesame from water vessels, using the left hand.

children.text: jānv ācya savyaṃ yatnena darbhayukto vimatsaraḥ
children.translated_text: Carefully bending the left knee, furnished with darbha grass and free from resentment,
having carefully drawn lines, he should perform the washing at the offering-places.
Facing south, placing the ladle in his hand,
he should place each <s>piṇḍa</s> in order upon all the darbha grasses.
Then he should pour them upon the darbhas, reciting the names and gotras.
On those darbhas he should wipe that hand for those who receive the smears.
Then likewise he should again perform the subsequent washing.
Having honored all six seasons with perfume, incense, offerings, and the like,
having invoked all this with Vedic mantras as prescribed,
for one who has a single fire there should be just one offering and one small ladle.
Then, after making an interval, he should give food on kuśa grasses to the wives.
Likewise, for the <s>piṇḍa</s> and related rites, he should perform invocation and dismissal.

children.text: tato gṛhītvā piṇḍebhyo mātrāḥ sarvāḥ krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: Then, taking portions from all the <s>piṇḍas</s> in sequence,
the man should first carefully cause those same Brahmins to eat them.
Because twice-born men eat portions taken from that food,
therefore it is called <s>anvāhāryaka</s> at the waning of the moon.

children.text: pūrvaṃ dattvā tu taddhaste sapavitraṃ tilodakam
children.translated_text: First, having placed sesame-water with a pavitra in his hand,
he should offer the foremost part of that <s>piṇḍa</s>, saying, 'May svadhā be theirs.'
Praising it, he should always feed them sweet and pure food.
One should avoid being overcome by anger, remembering <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>.
Then, knowing that they are satisfied, he should perform the scattering meant for all the varṇas.
Having taken up food together with water, he should pour water upon the ground.
When they have sipped, he should again give water containing water, flowers, and unbroken rice.
He should gather the whole blessing-recitation over the piṇḍa.
He should perform it with the gods at the beginning and end; otherwise the śrāddha is ruined.
Having dismissed the brāhmaṇas in the same way and circumambulated them,
a man, facing the southern direction, should petition the ancestors:
"May our givers increase, and may the Vedas and our lineage increase as well.

children.text: śraddhā ca no mā vyagamadbahu deyaṃ ca no 'stviti
children.translated_text: May faith not depart from us, and may there be much for us to give.

children.text: annaṃ ca no bahu bhavedatithīṃśca labhemahi ||
children.translated_text: May we have abundant food, and may we obtain guests.

children.text: yācitāraśca naḥ santu mā ca yāciṣma kaṃcana
children.translated_text: May there be people who ask from us, and may we not beg from anyone."
This formula, "May this be so," has been stated; it is the anvāhārya pārvaṇa.
As at the waning of the moon, so it is also taught elsewhere.
He should give the piṇḍas to cows, goats, or brāhmaṇas, or into fire or water.
Or he may scatter them before the brāhmaṇas, or have them eaten by birds.

children.text: patnī tu madhyamaṃ piṇḍaṃ prāśayed vinayānvitā ||
children.translated_text: The wife, however, should respectfully eat the middle piṇḍa.
"O ancestors, place here a womb that increases offspring."
The leftovers should remain only so long as the brāhmaṇas have not been dismissed.
Then, when the rite for the ancestors is finished, he should perform the Vaiśvadeva rite.

children.text: iṣṭaiḥ saha tataḥ śānto bhuñjīta pitṛsevitam ||
children.translated_text: After that, calm and together with his loved ones, he should eat what has been served to the ancestors.
The performer and the eater of śrāddha should avoid eating again, travel, riding, exertion, and sexual intercourse,
all of these without exception.
They should also always avoid Vedic recitation, quarrelling, and sleeping by day.
By this procedure one should perform śrāddha here, properly completing the dismissal.
Whenever the sun is in Virgo, Aquarius, or Taurus, and always in the dark fortnights,
wherever it is to be given after the sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite,
there it should always be given by one who maintains the sacred fire, according to this procedure.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Next I shall proclaim what was declared by <s>Viṣṇu</s>:
the śrāddha called ordinary, which grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
At the solstices, at the equinox, at the pair of ayanas, and at ordinary solar transitions,
on new-moon days, aṣṭakās, dark fortnights, and fifteenth lunar days,
under <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, and <s>Rohiṇī</s>, when materials and brāhmaṇas come together,
at gajacchāyā and vyatīpāta, and on days of viṣṭi and vaidhṛti,
on the third day of <s>Vaiśākha</s> and the ninth of <s>Kārttika</s>,

children.text: pañcadaśī ca māghasya nabhasye ca trayodaśī ||
children.translated_text: on the fifteenth of <s>Māgha</s> and the thirteenth in <s>Nabhasya</s>,
these are remembered as beginnings of yugas, making what is given inexhaustible.

children.text: tathā manvantarādau ca deyaṃ śrāddhaṃ vijānatā ||
children.translated_text: So too, at the beginning of a manvantara, śrāddha should be given by one who understands.
The bright ninth day of <s>Aśvayuj</s>, and likewise the twelfth in <s>Kārttika</s>,
the third day of the month of <s>Caitra</s>, and likewise of <s>Bhādrapada</s>,
the new-moon day of <s>Phālguna</s>, and the eleventh of <s>Pauṣa</s>,
the tenth of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> too, and the seventh day of the month of <s>Māgha</s>,
the dark eighth of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, and also the full moon of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>,
<s>Kārttikī</s>, <s>Phālgunī</s>, <s>Caitrī</s>, and the bright fifteenth of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>:
these too are the beginnings of manvantaras, making what is given inexhaustible.
On the seventh day of the month of <s>Māgha</s>, on which the sun mounts his chariot at the beginning of a manvantara,
that is called <s>Rathasaptamī</s>.
Here even water mixed with sesame should be given to the ancestors by a purified person.

children.text: śrāddhaṃ kṛtaṃ tena samāḥ sahasraṃ rahasyametatpitaro vadanti ||
children.translated_text: By that, śrāddha has been performed for a thousand years; the ancestors declare this secret.
On the <s>Vaiśākhī</s>, during eclipses, and likewise at festivals and at <s>Mahālaya</s>,
at tīrthas, sanctuaries, cattle-stations, lamp-sites, gardens, and houses,
in secluded and well-plastered places, śrāddha should be given by one who understands.
With disciplined self, he should invite brāhmaṇas on the preceding or following day,
men endowed with character, conduct, and virtue, and possessing maturity and good form.

children.text: dvau daive trīṃstathā pitrya ekaikamubhayatra vā ||
children.translated_text: He should feed two for the divine rite and three for the ancestral rite, or one each in both.
Even if he is very prosperous, he should not become attached to excessive elaboration.
Having worshipped the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> with barley and flowers, beginning with seats,
he should fill a pair of vessels and place a darbha-purifier there.

children.text: śaṃ no devīty apaḥ kuryādyavo'sīti yavānapi ||
children.translated_text: With the formula "Śaṃ no devīḥ" he should prepare the waters, and with "Yavo'si" the barley as well.
Having fully worshipped with fragrances and flowers, he should set it down for the Vaiśvadeva rite.
With the two verses beginning "Viśve devāsaḥ," he should invite them and scatter barley.
Having adorned it with fragrances and flowers, he should offer the arghya with the formula beginning "Yā divyā."
After worshipping, when the offering to them has been made, he should begin the rite for the ancestors.

children.text: darbhāsanaṃ tu dattvādau trīṇi pātrāṇi pūrayet
children.translated_text: First giving a seat of darbha grass, he should fill three vessels.

children.text: khapavitrāṇi kṛtvādau śaṃ no devīty apaḥ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having first made them with purifiers, he should pour in the waters with "Śaṃ no devīḥ."
With "Tilo'si" he should put in the sesame, and again fragrances, flowers, and the rest.
A vessel may be made of wood, and again of leaves,
or he may make one water-born or sea-born.
A golden or silver vessel is prescribed for the ancestors.

children.text: rajatasya kathā vāpi darśanaṃ dānameva vā
children.translated_text: Even mention of silver, or the sight of it, or the gift of it,
or vessels of silver for them, or vessels furnished with silver,
make even water given with faith serve for inexhaustible merit.
So too, for arghya, piṇḍa, food, and the like, silver is considered proper for the ancestors.
Because it arose from the eye of <s>Śiva</s>, it is therefore dear to the ancestors.
Since that is inauspicious, one should carefully avoid it in rites for the gods.
Having thus arranged the vessels according to what is available and without envy,
With the formula beginning "yā divyā," the one holding darbha should set down the father's name along with the gotras.
When he says, "I shall invite the ancestors," and is again told by them, "Do so,"
he should invite the ancestors with the two Ṛg-verses beginning "uśantas tvā" and "āyantu."
Having poured out the arghya with the formula beginning "yā divyā," he should then give fragrances and the other offerings.
First, having given that water from his hand, beginning with the dripping water,
he should place it in the ancestor-vessel and then set it down inverted to the north.
After setting it down, saying, "You are a place for the ancestors," he should sprinkle water around it.
There too, free from envy, he should perform the fire-rite as before.
Having brought the food with both hands, he should serve it.
With a peaceful mind at all times, holding darbha in his hand, in full detail,
he should serve it especially with excellent soups and vegetables and with various kinds of food.
Food together with curds and milk, cow's ghee, and sugar
pleases all the ancestors for one month, so <s>Keśava</s> says.
With fish-meat it pleases them for two months, and with deer-meat for three months.
With sheep-meat it pleases them for four months, and with bird-meat for five.
The ancestors are likewise satisfied for six months with goat-meat,
for seven with the meat of a spotted deer, and for eight with that of the black antelope.
They are satisfied for ten months with the flesh of boar and buffalo,
and for eleven months with meat born of hare and tortoise.

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ tu gavyena payasā pāyasena ca
children.translated_text: For a year they are satisfied with cow's milk and with milk-rice,
and with raurava meat they are satisfied for fifteen months.
With the meat of a vārdhrīṇasa there is satisfaction for twelve years,
and with kālaśāka and rhinoceros meat it is indeed endless.
Whatever is mixed with honey, cow's milk, ghee, or milk-rice,
when given, is said to be inexhaustible by the ancestors, the former deities.
He should have recited the ancestral <s>svādhyāya</s> (sacred recitation) and all the Purāṇas,
and the various hymns of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Sun, and <s>Rudra</s>,
as well as the purifying hymns to <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Soma</s>, according to his ability.
Likewise he should recite the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> chants, the <s>Jyeṣṭhasāman</s>, and the <s>Rauhiṇa</s>,
and also the chapter on pacification and the <s>Madhu-brāhmaṇa</s>.
Likewise he should recite the <s>Maṇḍala-brāhmaṇa</s>, and whatever else brings pleasure
to the Brahmins and to himself; he should proclaim all of that.
Then, when they have eaten, near the end of the meal, O king,
he should gather together food and eatables suitable for all classes and sprinkle them with water.
He should cast them forth in front of those who have eaten, scattering them on the ground.

children.text: agnidagdhāstu ye jīvā ye 'pyadagdhāḥ kule mama
children.translated_text: "Let those beings in my family who were cremated, and those who were not cremated,

children.text: bhūmau dattena tṛpyantu prayāntu paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: be satisfied by what is given on the ground, and let them go to the highest state.

children.text: yeṣāṃ na mātā na pitā na bandhurna gotraśuddhirna tathānnam asti
children.translated_text: For those who have no mother, no father, no relative, no purity of gotra, and no food,

children.text: tattṛptaye 'nnaṃ bhuvi dattametatprayāntu lokeṣu sukhāya tadvat ||
children.translated_text: this food has been given on the ground for their satisfaction; let them likewise go to happiness in the worlds."
For those who died without rites and for the women of the family who were abandoned,
the share in the leavings and in the scattering on the ground is their portion in the rite.
Knowing them to be satisfied, he should give water once, likewise into the hands of the Brahmins.
On the surface of the ground smeared with cow dung, urine, and water,
he should carefully lay down darbha grass according to rule, with the tips pointing south.
Then, with food of every kind, he should make piṇḍas as in the ancestor-sacrifice.
After first performing the washing, the man should use the name and gotra,
and give sandal-paste, incense, and the other offerings, after performing the counter-washing.
Having announced it, with the left hand and then in the proper clockwise manner,
he should bring the ancestor-rite to completion according to rule, holding darbha in his hand.
The wise man should likewise light the lamp and perform the worship with flowers.
Then, when they have sipped, he himself should sip and give water once to each.
After that he should give flowers, unbroken grains, and the imperishable water,
with sesame and with the name and gotra, and he should give the fee according to his ability.
Cows, land, gold, garments, and fine beds
he should give, according to what is desired by the Brahmins, by himself, and by his father.
Free from dishonesty about wealth, bringing affection to the ancestors,
he should then give the recitation of <s>svadhā</s> and water to the <s>Viśvadevas</s>.
Having given these, the wise man, facing east, should receive blessings from the twice-born.

children.text: aghorāḥ pitaraḥ santu santvityuktaḥ punar dvijaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "May the ancestors be gentle," and the twice-born again say, "May it be so,"

children.text: gotraṃ tathā vardhatāṃ nastathetyuktaśca taiḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: then he should say, "May our gotra increase," and when they again say, "So be it,"
he should also utter, "May our givers increase."

children.text: etāḥ satyāśiṣaḥ santu santvityuktaśca taiḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When he says, "May these true blessings come to pass," and they again say, "May they be so,"
he should perform the auspicious recitation, and then devoutly lift up the piṇḍas.
The leavings should remain there until the Brahmins have been dismissed.
Then he should perform the offering to the household spirits; such is the settled rule of <s>dharma</s>.
The leavings that have fallen on the ground are declared to be the ancestral share
of the sincere believer and of the class of servants.
This refreshment was made in ancient times by the ancestors, and it is always
for those without sons and those with sons, and also for women, O ruler of men.
Then, standing before them and taking up the water-vessel,
he should dismiss them with the tip of kuśa grass while reciting, "vāje vāje."
Outside he should circumambulate clockwise, following them for eight steps,
together with his circle of relatives, accompanied by his son and wife.
Returning, he should bow down and then sprinkle the fire with the proper mantra.
He should perform the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and the daily bali-offering.
Then, after the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, together with his servants, sons, and kinsmen...
He should eat, together with guests, all the food that has been used in service of the ancestors.
Even one who has not been initiated should perform this on all festival days:
the rite called the common <s>śrāddha</s>, which bestows the fruits of every desire.
Even if he is without his wife, even if he is living abroad, if he is devoted,
and even if he is a <s>śūdra</s>, the wise man should perform it without mantras according to this rule.
The third is the <s>ābhyudayika</s>; it is called the <s>vṛddhiśrāddha</s>, the prosperity śrāddha,
on occasions of festival, joy, abundance, sacrifices, marriages, and other auspicious events.
The mothers are to be honored first, and the fathers immediately after them;
then, O king, the maternal grandfathers, and likewise the <s>Viśvadevas</s>.
With clockwise service, using curds, unbroken grains, fruits, and water,
he should face east and offer the piṇḍas, together with dūrvā grass and kuśa grass.
At an abhyudaya rite he should give the arghya to them two by two, saying, 'It is accomplished.'
Pairs of twice-born men are to be honored with garments, gold, and the like.
The place of sesame should be taken by barley, preceded by the word <s>nāndī</s>,
and he should have all auspicious things proclaimed by the foremost twice-born men.
Thus even a <s>śūdra</s>, always, in the common prosperity śrāddha as well,
should perform it with the mantra of salutation and always with uncooked food.
A <s>śūdra</s> should be chiefly devoted to giving; so has the blessed Lord declared,
because through giving the attainment of all his desires arises.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Now I shall explain the <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> rite, as it was taught by <s>Cakrapāṇi</s>,
how it should be performed by sons when a father has died, and also the impurity after a father's death.
Among Brahmins, impurity from a corpse is prescribed for ten days;

children.text: kṣatriyeṣu daśa dve ca pakṣaṃ vaiśyeṣu caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: among Kṣatriyas for twelve days, and among Vaiśyas for a fortnight.
Among <s>śūdras</s>, impurity for a sapiṇḍa relative is prescribed for a month.
For one whose tonsure has not been performed it is for a night; after that, three nights are remembered.
At a birth the rule is exactly the same, always for all classes,
and bodily contact is prescribed after the gathering of the bones.
One should perform the giving of piṇḍas to the departed for twelve days;

children.text: pātheyaṃ tasya tatproktaṃ yataḥ prītikaraṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: that is said to be his provisions for the road, since it gives him great satisfaction.
Therefore the departed is not taken to the city of the pretas for twelve days;

children.text: gṛhaṃ putraṃ kalatraṃ ca dvādaśāhaṃ prapaśyati ||
children.translated_text: for twelve days he looks upon his house, his son, and his wife.
Therefore milk should be set out in the open for ten nights,
to quiet all the burning and to remove the weariness of the journey.
Then on the eleventh day he should feed eleven Brahmins,
while a Kṣatriya and the other classes, at the end of the birth-or-death impurity, should feed an odd number of Brahmins.
On the second day, again in the same way, he should perform the <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> rite,
according to rule, without invocation, without the fire-offering, and without the divine portion.
One purifier, one arghya, and one piṇḍa are prescribed.
The formula 'Let him be present' is to be given, and afterwards sesame-water.
He should scatter the relished food and say, at the dismissal, 'Be pleased.'
The rest here too is to be done as before by one who knows the Veda, for the father.
According to this rule he should perform everything month by month.
On the second day after the end of the impurity he should give a distinctive bed,
and likewise a golden figure, furnished with fruits and garments.
Having worshiped a Brahmin couple with many ornaments and adornments,

children.text: vṛṣotsargaṃ prakurvīta deyā ca kapilā śubhā
children.translated_text: he should carry out the release of a bull, and an auspicious tawny cow is to be given.
A water-pot also should be given, supplied with foods to be eaten and enjoyed.
For a full year, O best of men, it should be preceded by sesame-water;
then, when the year is complete, the <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s> should take place.
After the <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s>, the preta becomes a recipient of the regular ancestral rite,
and thereafter he becomes eligible for prosperity rites and for the householder's rites.
In the śrāddha of <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s>, he should assign the gods first;
he should seat the ancestors there, and designate the preta separately.
He should prepare four vessels furnished with scented water and sesame,
and for the arghya he should pour the preta-vessel into the vessels of the ancestors.
In the same way, after resolving upon it, the giver of piṇḍas should make four piṇḍas;

children.text: ye samānā iti dvābhyāmantyaṃ tu vibhajettridhā ||
children.translated_text: with the two verses beginning 'Those who are equal,' he should divide the last one into three parts.

children.text: caturthasya punaḥ kāryaṃ na kadācidato bhavet
children.translated_text: Thereafter a fourth one is never again to be made.
Then, having attained the status of an ancestor, he has reached satisfaction on every side.
He attains the supreme immortality of being among the <s>Agniṣvāttas</s> and the others.
After the <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s>, therefore, no offering is given to him separately.

children.text: pitṛṣveva tu dātavyaṃ tatpiṇḍo yeṣu saṃsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Rather, it should be given among the ancestors, among whom his piṇḍa has been established.
From then onward, at transitions of the sun and on eclipse-days and other festival days,
one should perform a three-piṇḍa śrāddha; on the day of death, an <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> rite.
He who, on the death-day, abandons the <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> and performs a regular ancestral rite
is always a slayer of the ancestors and a destroyer of mother and brother.
A man who performs a regular ancestral rite on the death-day goes lower and lower.
Among those who have been mixed together, disorder would arise among the pretas.
Therefore every year he should perform the <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> rite.
The man who, without envy, gives a water-pot for a full year,
together with food for the preta, obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.
When the giver of śrāddha, knowing the rule, performs an uncooked <s>śrāddha</s>,
with that he should perform the fire-offering, and with that alone he should offer the piṇḍas.
At the <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s>, with three, when the father, in due time, reaches the complete triad,

children.text: yadā prāpsyati kālena tadā mucyeta bandhanāt ||
children.translated_text: then he is released from bondage.
Even when released, he obtains the status of one sharing in the lepa through the wiping with kuśa grass;
those from the fourth onward share in the lepa, while the fathers and the rest share in the piṇḍa.
The seventh among them is the giver of the <s>piṇḍa</s> (funeral ball); <s>sāpiṇḍya</s> (kinship through funeral offerings) extends through seven generations.
The seers said:

children.text: kathaṃ kavyāni deyāni havyāni ca janairiha
children.translated_text: How are the offerings to the ancestors and the offerings to the gods to be given by people here?
How do they go to those who dwell in the world of the ancestors? Who is said here to convey them?

children.text: yadi martyo dvijo bhuṅkte hūyate yadi vānale
children.translated_text: If a mortal twice-born man eats, or if an oblation is offered in the fire,
how is that gift eaten by the departed, who have auspicious and inauspicious natures?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Vedic revelation calls the fathers <s>Vasus</s>, and the grandfathers <s>Rudras</s>,
and likewise the great-grandfathers <s>Ādityas</s>; so indeed is the Vedic <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: nāma gotraṃ pitṝṇāṃ tu prāpakaṃ havyakavyayoḥ
children.translated_text: The name and gotra of the ancestors are what convey the offerings to gods and ancestors,
along with the mantras of the <s>śrāddha</s> and faith, employed with the utmost devotion.
The <s>Agniṣvāttas</s> and the others are established in lordship over them.
Name, gotra, time, and place, even for beings who have passed into another birth,
gladden those living beings, having become suitable as their food.
If a father has been born as a god through the operation of good karma,
his food becomes ambrosia and follows him even in his divine condition.

children.text: daityatve bhogarūpeṇa paśutve ca tṛṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: In the state of a <s>Daitya</s> it becomes enjoyment, and in the state of an animal it becomes grass.
The food of a <s>śrāddha</s> attends him as wind even in the state of a serpent.
It becomes drink in the state of a <s>Yakṣa</s>, and likewise flesh in the state of a <s>Rākṣasa</s>.
In the state of a <s>Danuja</s> it becomes magic power, and in the state of a ghost, blood-water.
In the human state it becomes food and drink, with many enjoyments and flavors.
It becomes the power of delight, beloved women, food, and the capacity to eat,
the power of giving together with wealth, and also beauty and health.
Faith is declared to be this flower; union with <s>Brahman</s> is the fruit.

children.text: āyuḥ putrān dhanaṃ vidyāṃ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ sukhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Long life, sons, wealth, learning, heaven, liberation, and pleasures,

children.text: rājyaṃ caiva prayacchanti prītāḥ pitṛgaṇā nṛṇām
children.translated_text: and also kingship: the hosts of ancestors, when pleased, bestow these upon men.

children.text: śrūyate ca purā mokṣaṃ prāptāḥ kauśikasūnavaḥ
children.translated_text: And it is heard that in ancient times the sons of <s>Kauśika</s> attained liberation,
and, through connections over five births, went to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The seers said:
How did the heirs of <s>Kauśika</s> attain that highest yoga?
How can the exhaustion of karma come about through connections over five births?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
There was a righteous great seer named <s>Kauśika</s> in <s>Kurukṣetra</s>.
Learn now of his seven sons, by name and by deed.

children.text: śvasṛpaḥ krodhano hiṃsraḥ piśunaḥ kavireva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Śvasṛpa</s>, <s>Krodhana</s>, <s>Hiṃsra</s>, <s>Piśuna</s>, and <s>Kavi</s>,
as well as <s>Vāgduṣṭa</s> and <s>Pitṛvartin</s>, were then pupils of <s>Garga</s>.
After their father had died, a terrible famine arose for them,
and a great drought, bringing fear to all people.
By <s>Garga</s>'s command those ascetics were guarding a milch cow in the forest.
"Let us eat this tawny cow; we are severely afflicted by hunger."

children.text: iti cintayatāṃ pāpaṃ laghuḥ prāha tadānujaḥ
children.translated_text: As they were thinking this sinful thought, the younger brother then said something slight:
"If she must necessarily be killed, let her be assigned to the form of a <s>śrāddha</s>.
Being assigned in a <s>śrāddha</s>, she will surely rescue us from sin."
Permitted by his brothers with the words, "Do this," <s>Pitṛvartin</s> then

children.text: cakre samāhitaḥ śrāddhamupayujya ca tāṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: performed the <s>śrāddha</s> with collected mind, and then made use of her.

children.text: dvau daive bhrātarau kṛtvā pitre trīnapyanukramāt ||
children.translated_text: He made two brothers the representatives of the gods, and three in succession for his father,
and likewise made one a guest, while he himself was the giver of the <s>śrāddha</s>.
Intent on the ancestors and remembering them, he performed the <s>śrāddha</s> according to the mantras.
In the absence of the cow, the calf too was reported to the guru:
"The cow has been killed by a tiger; please receive this calf."
Thus that cow was eaten by those seven ascetics,
who relied on the power of the Veda and were fearless in a cruel act.
Then, drawn onward by time, they became hunters in <s>Dāśapura</s>.
They obtained memory of former births, having been shaped by their disposition toward the ancestors.
Because that cruel deed had then been done by them in the form of a <s>śrāddha</s>,

children.text: tena te bhavane jātā vyādhānāṃ krūrakarmiṇām ||
children.translated_text: therefore they were born in the house of hunters, men of cruel deeds.
Yet by the greatness of the ancestors they were born with memory of former births.
Then, resorting to the yoga of dispassion, they again undertook fasting unto death.

children.text: jātismarāḥ sapta jātā mṛgāḥ kālañjare girau
children.translated_text: The seven, remembering their former births, were born as deer on Mount <s>Kālañjara</s>,
before <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, still influenced by their disposition toward the ancestors.
There too, from knowledge and dispassion, they righteously gave up their lives,
while people looked on, at the end of the sacred ford, through fasting.
At <s>Mānasa</s> they were born as seven <s>cakravāka</s> birds, yogins.
Hear all of them by name and by deed, O best of twice-born men.
<s>Sumanas</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Śuddha</s>, <s>Chidradarśin</s>, <s>Sunetraka</s>,
<s>Sunetra</s>, and <s>Aṃśumān</s>: these seven had reached the far shore of yoga.
Three of them, fallen from yoga and of little awareness, wandered about,
after seeing him shining brilliantly in a garden, accompanied by women,
playing in various ways, endowed with great strength and valor,
born in the lineage of <s>Pañcāla</s>, and possessing abundant troops and vehicles.
One among those water-birds came to desire kingship.

children.text: pitṛvartī ca yo vipraḥ śrāddhakṛt pitṛvatsalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He had been the Brahmin <s>Pitṛvartin</s>, the performer of the <s>śrāddha</s>, affectionate toward the ancestors.
When two others saw the ministers, who possessed abundant troops and vehicles,
they formed a desire for ministership in this mortal world, O best of twice-born men.

children.text: tanmadhye ye tu niṣkāmāste babhūvur dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: But those among them who were without desire became, O best of twice-born men,
one the son of <s>Vibhrāja</s>, remembered as <s>Brahmadatta</s>.
And the two sons of the ministers were <s>Kaṇḍarīka</s> and <s>Subālaka</s>.
When <s>Brahmadatta</s> had been consecrated by the learned priest,
he became the valiant king of <s>Pañcāla</s>, versed in all the śāstras.
Being skilled in yoga, he then became a knower of the sounds of all creatures.
That king had an auspicious wife, the daughter of <s>Devala</s>,
famous by the name <s>Saṃnati</s>, who had formerly been <s>Kapilā</s>.
Because she was engaged in the work for the ancestors, she became a speaker of brahman.

children.text: tayā cakāra sahitaḥ sa rājyaṃ rājanandanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with her, O delight of kings, he ruled the kingdom.
Once that ruler went into the garden together with her,
and saw a pair of insects distressed by a quarrel of love.
A male ant, intent on love, was coaxing a female ant on every side.
His limbs burned by the five-arrowed god, he spoke with a faltering voice:

children.text: na tvayā sadṛśī loke kāminī vidyate kvacit
children.translated_text: "Nowhere in the world is there a woman equal to you,
slender in the waist, very broad in the hips, and moving with a full breast,
golden in color, fine-hipped, sweet-spoken, and charming in smile,
with well-marked eyes and tongue, fond of molasses and sugar.

children.text: bhokṣyase mayi bhukte tvaṃ snāsi snāte tathā mayi
children.translated_text: When I have eaten, you will eat; when I have bathed, you likewise bathe.

children.text: proṣite sati dīnā tvaṃ kruddhe'pi bhayacañcalā ||
children.translated_text: When I am away you are miserable; even when I am angry, you tremble with fear.
Tell me, lovely one, why do you stand with an angry face?"

children.text: sā tamāha sakopā tu kim ālapasi māṃ śaṭha ||
children.translated_text: But she said to him angrily, "Why are you addressing me, rogue?

children.text: tvayā modakacūrṇaṃ tu māṃ vihāya vineṣyatā
children.translated_text: You, leaving me aside and carried away by passion,
gave powdered sweet-cake to another after the day had passed, O love-struck one."
The ant said:
"Because she resembled you, I gave it to another, O fair-colored one.
You should forgive this single offense of mine, O lovely woman.
I shall never again do this anywhere here, O virtuous one.

children.text: spṛśāmi pādau satyena prasīda praṇatasya me ||
children.translated_text: I touch your feet; by truth, be gracious to me as I bow before you."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Hearing that speech of his, she then became pleased,
and the female ant offered herself to the enchanting ant.
<s>Brahmadatta</s> too, knowing all of this, was filled with amazement,
because, through the grace of <s>Cakrapāṇi</s>, he knew the speech of all beings.
The sages said:
How did <s>Brahmadatta</s> on earth become a knower of the speech of beings?
And that group of four <s>cakravākas</s>, in whose family did it arise?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In that very city they were then born, known as <s>Cakrāhvayas</s>,
as heirs of an aged Brahmin, Brahmins who remembered their former births.
<s>Dhṛtimat</s>, <s>Tattvadarśin</s>, <s>Vidyācaṇḍa</s>, and <s>Tapotsuka</s>
were these sons of the very poor man, so named and so acting.
Then the thought of austerity arose among those twice-born men:

children.text: yāsyāmaḥ paramāṃ siddhim ity ūcus te dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "We shall attain the highest perfection," said those best of the twice-born.
Then, hearing their words, the greatly austere <s>Sudaridra</s>
spoke in a pitiful voice: "What is this, my sons?

children.text: adharma eṣa iti vaḥ pitā tān abhyavārayat
children.translated_text: This is <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) for you." Their father tried to restrain them,
"If you abandon your aged, poor father and become forest-dwellers,

children.text: ko nu dharmo'tra bhavitā mattyāgādgatireva vā
children.translated_text: what <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty) will there be in this, or what path will come from abandoning me?"

children.text: ūcuste kalpitā vṛttistava tāta vadasva tat ||
children.translated_text: They said, "A livelihood has been arranged for you, father; tell this

children.text: vittametatpuro rājñaḥ sa te dāsyati puṣkalam
children.translated_text: before the king. He will give you abundant wealth,
money and thousands of villages, when you recite it at dawn:

children.text: ye vipramukhyāḥ kurujāṅgaleṣu dāśāstathā dāśapure mṛgāśca
children.translated_text: 'Those chief Brahmins among the <s>Kurujāṅgalas</s>, the fishermen in <s>Dāśapura</s>, and the deer

children.text: kālañjare sapta ca cakravākā ye mānase te vayamatra siddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: at <s>Kālañjara</s>, and those seven <s>cakravākas</s> at <s>Mānasa</s>: we are here, perfected.'"

children.text: ityuktvā pitaraṃ jagmuste vanaṃ tapase punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having said this to their father, they again went to the forest for austerity.
The old man too went to the royal palace to accomplish his own purpose.
Formerly there was a <s>Vaibhrāja</s> named <s>Anagha</s>, lord of <s>Pāñcāla</s>.
Desiring a son, he worshiped <s>Hari</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lord, god of gods.
Devoted to severe vows, he propitiated the all-pervading lord.
Then, after a long time, <s>Janārdana</s> was pleased with him.

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te hṛdayenepsitaṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: "Choose a boon, O king; may it be well with you, whatever is desired in your heart."
Thus addressed by the god, he chose the highest boon:
