"Give me a son, O lord of gods, of great strength and valor,
learned in all <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), righteous, and supreme among yogins.
Give me as a son a yogin who knows the speech of all beings."
"So be it," the lord, the soul of the universe, said to him.
There, before the eyes of all the gods, he disappeared.
Then <s>Brahmadatta</s>, mighty in splendor, became his son,
compassionate toward all beings and surpassing the strength of all beings,
a knower of the speech of all beings and a supreme lord among the lords of beings.
Because of that, the yogic-minded one laughed at the passion of the ants,
where that pair of insects was standing, delighting in each other.

children.text: tataḥ sā saṃnatirdṛṣṭvā taṃ hasantaṃ suvismitā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Saṃnati</s>, seeing him laughing and greatly astonished,
suspecting something in her mind, asked the lord of men.
<s>Saṃnati</s> said:
Why, O king, did this sudden great laughter arise in you?

children.text: hāsyahetuṃ na jānāmi yadakāle kṛtaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: I do not know the cause of the laughter that you made at an improper time.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The prince then told her the speech of the ants:
"This laughter arose from words of passion, O beautiful-faced one.
There is no other cause at all for my laughter, O pure-smiling one."

children.text: na sāmanyat tadā devī prāhālīkamidaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But then the queen did not accept it; she said, "This speech is false.
I alone have been laughed at today. I shall not live with you now.

children.text: kathaṃ pipīlikālāpaṃ martyo vetti vinā surān ||
children.translated_text: How can a mortal know the conversation of ants, except through the gods?
Therefore I alone have been laughed at by you here. What more is there than this?"
Then the king, left without an answer and wishing to inquire, went before <s>Hari</s>.
Undertaking an observance, he remained there sinless for seven nights.
In a dream <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> said, "At dawn, while going about the city..."
From the words of that aged twice-born man you will know everything completely.
Having said this, <s>Viṣṇu</s> disappeared. Then, at dawn, the king, from the city,
coming out with his ministers and with his wife, saw in front of him

children.text: gadantaṃ vipram āyāntaṃ taṃ vṛddhaṃ saṃdadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: that aged Brahmin approaching, speaking as he came.
The Brahmin said:

children.text: ye vipramukhyāḥ kurujāṅgaleṣu dāśāstathā dāśapure mṛgāśca
children.translated_text: Those foremost Brahmins in <s>Kuru-Jāṅgala</s>, the <s>Dāśas</s> in <s>Dāśapura</s>, and the deer

children.text: kālañjare sapta ca cakravākā ye mānase te vayamatra siddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: at <s>Kālañjara</s>, and the seven cakravāka birds at <s>Mānasa</s>: we are they, perfected here.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ityākarṇya vacastābhyāṃ sa papāta śucā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words from those two, he then fell down through grief,
and both of those excellent ministers attained memory of former births.
<s>Bābhravya</s>, the propounder of the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s>, was <s>Subālaka</s>,
famous in the worlds as <s>Pāñcāla</s>, a knower of all śāstras.
<s>Kaṇḍarīka</s> too, righteous in soul, a promulgator of Vedic śāstra,
having become one who remembered former births, fell down then in front of him from grief.
"Alas, we have fallen from yoga, bound by karma because of desire."
After lamenting thus at length, those three, who had reached the far shore of yoga,
marveling, praised again and again the greatness of the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestor rite).
Then, having given that Brahmin wealth together with many villages,

children.text: visṛjya brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ ca vṛddhaṃ dhanamudānvitam
children.translated_text: and having dismissed that aged Brahmin, delighted with wealth, the king
consecrated his own son, endowed with the marks of a king,
named <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, in the kingship.

children.text: mānase militāḥ sarve tataste yogināṃ varāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then all those best of yogins met at <s>Mānasa</s>,
<s>Brahmadatta</s> and the others, devoted to the ancestors and free from envy.
<s>Saṃnati</s> too had fallen, saying, "This indeed has been brought about by me.
All this is the fruit of abandoning the kingdom, which is desired."
"So be it," the king said, honoring her again:
"By your favor all this fruit is obtained by me."
Then all those forest-dwellers, taking up yoga,
through the brahmarandhra attained the supreme state by the power of their austerity.

children.text: evamāyurdhanaṃ vidyāṃ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ sukhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when pleased, the grandfathers grant to men life, wealth, knowledge,
heaven, liberation, pleasures, sons, and kingship.

children.text: ya idaṃ pitṛmāhātmyaṃ brahmadattasya ca dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever, O twice-born ones, causes this greatness of the ancestors and of <s>Brahmadatta</s>

children.text: dvijebhyaḥ śrāvayedyo vā śṛṇotyatha paṭhettu vā
children.translated_text: to be heard by Brahmins, or himself hears it or recites it,
is honored in <s>Brahmaloka</s> for more than a hundred crores of kalpas.
The sages said:
At what time does that <s>śrāddha</s>, giver of endless fruit, take place?
In what part of the day should the performer of a <s>śrāddha</s> perform the <s>śrāddha</s>?

children.text: tīrtheṣu keṣu ca kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ bahuphalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And at which tīrthas, when performed, does a <s>śrāddha</s> become very fruitful?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When the afternoon has arrived, at the rising of <s>Abhijit</s> or <s>Rohiṇī</s>,
whatever is given there is declared to be imperishable.

children.text: tīrthāni yāni śastāni pitṝṇāṃ vallabhāni ca
children.translated_text: The tīrthas that are praised and beloved of the ancestors
I shall tell by name, in brief, O best of the twice-born.
The ancestral tīrtha called <s>Gayā</s> is auspicious, the best of all tīrthas,
where the lord of the gods himself, <s>Pitāmaha</s>, abides.
There this verse was sung by the ancestors, desiring a share:

children.text: eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyeko'pi gayāṃ vrajate
children.translated_text: "Many sons should be desired, if even one of them goes to <s>Gayā</s>,
or sacrifices with a horse-sacrifice, or sets loose a blue bull."

children.text: tathā vārāṇasī puṇyā pitṝṇāṃ vallabhā sadā
children.translated_text: Likewise holy <s>Vārāṇasī</s> is always beloved of the ancestors,
where the presence of <s>Avimukta</s> grants the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.
Similarly holy <s>Vimaleśvara</s> is beloved of the ancestors,
and the ancestral tīrtha <s>Prayāga</s> grants the fruit of all desires.
The blessed <s>Vaṭeśvara</s>, together with <s>Mādhava</s>,
and likewise <s>Keśava</s>, lying in yogic sleep, dwell there always.
Holy <s>Daśāśvamedhika</s>, and likewise <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>,
then <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Lalitā</s>, and likewise the auspicious tīrtha <s>Māyāpurī</s>,
and the place called <s>Mitrapada</s>; after that, the excellent <s>Kedāra</s>,
and <s>Gaṅgāsāgara</s>, they say, is auspicious and made of all tīrthas.
Likewise there is the tīrtha <s>Brahmasaras</s>, a lake in the waters of the <s>Śatadru</s>,
and the tīrtha called <s>Naimiṣa</s>, which grants the fruit of all tīrthas.
There, in the <s>Gomatī</s>, is the ancient emergence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
and likewise <s>Yajñavarāha</s>, and the god of gods, the bearer of the trident.
There is that golden gate, and <s>Hara</s> with eighteen arms,
where in ancient times the rim of <s>Hari</s>'s discus became worn away.
This is that <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>, served by all tīrthas.
There too, the sight of the god of gods, <s>Vārāha</s>,

children.text: yaḥ prayāti sa pūtātmā nārāyaṇapadaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: is such that whoever goes there, purified in soul, reaches the abode of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Kṛtaśauca</s> is very holy and destroys all sins,
where <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, <s>Janārdana</s> himself, abides.
The tīrtha called <s>Ikṣumatī</s> is always beloved of the ancestors,

children.text: saṃgame yatra tiṣṭhanti gaṅgāyāḥ pitaraḥ sadā
children.translated_text: where the ancestors always stand at the confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
<s>Kurukṣetra</s> is very holy and endowed with all tīrthas.
Likewise holy <s>Sarayū</s> is honored by all the gods,
and the river <s>Irāvatī</s> likewise is inhabited by ancestral tīrthas.
<s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Devikā</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Candrabhāgā</s>, and <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>,

children.text: nadī veṇumatī puṇyā parā vetravatī tathā ||
children.translated_text: the holy river <s>Veṇumatī</s>, and also the further <s>Vetravatī</s>:

children.text: pitṝṇāṃ vallabhā hy etāḥ śrāddhe koṭiguṇā matāḥ
children.translated_text: these are indeed beloved of the ancestors and are regarded as yielding a crorefold result in <s>śrāddha</s>.

children.text: jambūmārgaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ yatra mārgo hi lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jambūmārga</s> is very holy, where the path is indeed perceived;
even now that ancestral tīrtha grants the fruit of all desires.
Known as <s>Nīlakuṇḍa</s>, it is a <s>pitṛtīrtha</s> (ancestor-tīrtha), O best of the twice-born.

children.text: tathā rudrasaraḥ puṇyaṃ saro mānasameva ca
children.translated_text: Likewise there are holy <s>Rudrasaras</s> and Lake <s>Mānasa</s> itself,
the <s>Mandākinī</s>, likewise <s>Acchodā</s>, then <s>Vipāśā</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Pūrvamitrapada</s>, likewise <s>Vaidyanātha</s>, of great fruit,
the river <s>Kṣiprā</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and auspicious <s>Kālañjara</s>.
<s>Vaṃśodbheda</s>, <s>Harodbheda</s>, and <s>Gaṅgodbheda</s>, of great fruit,
<s>Bhadreśvara</s>, <s>Viṣṇupada</s>, and the gateway of the <s>Narmadā</s>.
The great seers say these are equal to offering piṇḍas at <s>Gayā</s>.
These are ancestor-tīrthas, and they remove all sin.

children.text: smaraṇādapi lokānāṃ kim u śrāddhakṛtāṃ nṛṇām
children.translated_text: They do so even by being remembered by people; how much more for men who perform śrāddha there.
<s>Oṃkāra</s>, the ancestor-tīrtha, and the <s>Kāverī</s> with <s>Kapilodaka</s>;
the confluence of <s>Caṇḍavegā</s>, and likewise <s>Amarakaṇṭaka</s>.
Bathing and the other rites there are a hundred times greater than at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>.

children.text: śukratīrthaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ someśvaraṃ param
children.translated_text: The renowned <s>Śukratīrtha</s>, and the supreme tīrtha <s>Someśvara</s>,
holy, remover of every illness, and greater than the fruit of a hundred crores,

children.text: śrāddhe dāne tathā home svādhyāye jalasaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: for śrāddha, gifts, oblations, recitation, and rites in the presence of water.
<s>Kāyāvarohaṇa</s> by name, and likewise the river <s>Carmaṇvatī</s>;
<s>Gomatī</s>, <s>Varaṇā</s>, and likewise the supreme <s>Auśanasa</s> tīrtha;
<s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Bhṛgutuṅga</s>, and the unsurpassed <s>Gaurītīrtha</s>;
the tīrtha named <s>Vaināyaka</s>, and after that supreme <s>Bhadreśvara</s>;

children.text: tathā pāpaharaṃ nāma puṇyātha tapatī nadī ||
children.translated_text: likewise the place named <s>Pāpahara</s>, and then the holy river <s>Tapatī</s>;
<s>Mūlatāpī</s>, <s>Payoṣṇī</s>, and likewise the confluence of the <s>Payoṣṇī</s>;
<s>Mahābodhi</s>, <s>Pāṭalā</s>, <s>Nāgatīrtha</s>, and <s>Avantikā</s>;

children.text: tathā veṇā nadī puṇyā mahāśālaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: and likewise the holy river <s>Veṇā</s>, and <s>Mahāśāla</s> as well;

children.text: mahārudraṃ mahāliṅgaṃ daśārṇā ca nadī śubhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahārudra</s>, <s>Mahāliṅga</s>, and the auspicious river <s>Daśārṇā</s>;

children.text: śatarudrā śatāhvā ca tathā viśvapadaṃ param
children.translated_text: <s>Śatarudrā</s>, <s>Śatāhvā</s>, and likewise the supreme <s>Viśvapada</s>;
similarly <s>Aṅgāravāhikā</s>, and those two rivers, <s>Śoṇa</s> and <s>Gharghara</s>;

children.text: kālikā ca nadī puṇyā vitastā ca nadī tathā
children.translated_text: the holy river <s>Kālikā</s>, and likewise the river <s>Vitastā</s>;
these ancestor-tīrthas are praised for bathing and gifts.
A śrāddha offered at these is remembered as having endless fruit.
<s>Droṇī</s>, the river <s>Vāṭanadī</s>, <s>Dhārāsarit</s>, and <s>Kṣīranadī</s>;

children.text: gokarṇaṃ gajakarṇaṃ ca tathā ca puruṣottamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gokarṇa</s>, <s>Gajakarṇa</s>, and also <s>Puruṣottama</s>;
<s>Dvārakā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇatīrtha</s>, and likewise the <s>Arbudasarasvatī</s>;

children.text: nadī maṇimatī nāma tathā ca girikarṇikā
children.translated_text: the river named <s>Maṇimatī</s>, and also <s>Girikarṇikā</s>;
likewise the tīrtha <s>Dhūtapāpa</s>, and the southern ocean;
at these ancestor-tīrthas, śrāddha obtains endless reward.
The tīrtha named <s>Meghakara</s>, which is <s>Janārdana</s> himself,
where <s>Viṣṇu</s>, bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s>, is established in <s>Mekhalā</s>;

children.text: tathā mandodarītīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ campā nadī śubhā ||
children.translated_text: also <s>Mandodarītīrtha</s>, and the tīrtha that is the auspicious river <s>Campā</s>;
likewise <s>Sāmalanātha</s>, and the river <s>Mahāśāla</s> as well;
<s>Cakravāka</s>, <s>Carmakoṭa</s>, and likewise great <s>Janmeśvara</s>;
<s>Arjuna</s> and <s>Tripura</s>, and after that supreme <s>Siddheśvara</s>;
<s>Śrīśaila</s>, the tīrtha of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, and after that supreme <s>Nārasiṃha</s>;
also holy <s>Mahendra</s>, and then the place called <s>Śrīraṅga</s>;
at these too, śrāddha is always remembered as giving endless fruit.
Even by seeing them, they immediately remove sin.

children.text: tuṅgabhadrā nadī puṇyā tathā bhīmarathī sarit ||
children.translated_text: The holy river <s>Tuṅgabhadrā</s>, and likewise the stream <s>Bhīmarathī</s>;
<s>Bhīmeśvara</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇā</s>, the <s>Kāverī</s>, and the river <s>Kuḍmalā</s>;
the river named <s>Godāvarī</s>, and the excellent tīrtha <s>Trisaṃdhyā</s>;
the tīrtha named <s>Traiyambaka</s>, honored by all tīrthas,
where the blessed Lord, the three-eyed <s>Īśa</s> himself, dwells;
at all these, śrāddha becomes many crores upon crores in merit.
Even from remembering them, sins perish a hundredfold, O twice-born.
<s>Śrīparṇī</s> and <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, and the unsurpassed tīrtha <s>Jayā</s>;

children.text: tathā matsyanadī puṇyā śivadhāraṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: likewise the holy river <s>Matsyā</s>, and <s>Śivadhāra</s> as well;

children.text: bhadratīrthaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ pampātīrthaṃ ca śāśvatam
children.translated_text: the famous <s>Bhadratīrtha</s>, and the eternal <s>Pampātīrtha</s>;
holy <s>Rāmeśvara</s>, likewise <s>Elāpura</s>, the excellent city;
the renowned <s>Aṅgabhūta</s>, <s>Āmardaka</s>, and <s>Alambhuṣa</s>;
<s>Āmrātakeśvara</s>, likewise <s>Ekāmbhaka</s>, after that supreme;
<s>Govardhana</s>, <s>Hariścandra</s>, <s>Kṛpucandra</s>, and <s>Pṛthūdaka</s>;

children.text: sahasrākṣaṃ hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathā ca kadalī nadī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sahasrākṣa</s>, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, and also the river <s>Kadalī</s>;
there also is <s>Rāmādhivāsa</s>, and likewise the confluence of <s>Saumitri</s>;
<s>Indrakīla</s>, <s>Mahānāda</s>, and also <s>Priyamelaka</s>;
these too are always praised in śrāddha, and are even more excellent,
because the presence of all the gods is seen at these places.
A gift given at all these is greater than a hundred crores.

children.text: bāhudā ca nadīpuṇyā tathā siddhavanaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: The holy river <s>Bāhudā</s>, and likewise auspicious <s>Siddhavana</s>;

children.text: tīrthaṃ pāśupataṃ nāma nadī pārvatikā śubhā
children.translated_text: the tīrtha named <s>Pāśupata</s>, and the auspicious river <s>Pārvatikā</s>;
a śrāddha offered at all these is greater than a hundred crores.

children.text: tathaiva pitṛtīrthaṃ tu yatra godāvarī nadī
children.translated_text: Likewise there is the ancestor-tīrtha where the river <s>Godāvarī</s>
is joined with a thousand liṅgas and carries water through all hidden channels.
That excellent tīrtha of <s>Jāmadagnya</s> has come down in succession.
There the river <s>Godāvarī</s>, split apart from fear of <s>Pratīka</s>,
is that tīrtha for offerings to gods and ancestors, known as <s>Apsaroyuga</s>.
For śrāddha, fire-rites, and gifts it is likewise more than a hundred crores in merit.
Likewise <s>Sahasraliṅga</s> and the excellent <s>Rāghaveśvara</s>;

children.text: sendraphenā nadī puṇyā yatrendraḥ patitaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: the holy river <s>Sendraphenā</s>, where <s>Indra</s> once fell,
after slaying <s>Namuci</s>; <s>Śakra</s> attained heaven by austerity.
There, a <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite) given by men becomes one that grants endless fruit.

children.text: tīrthaṃ tu puṣkaraṃ nāma śālagrāmaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: The <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford) called <s>Puṣkara</s>, and <s>Śālagrāma</s> likewise,
and the famed <s>Somapāna</s>, where there is the shrine of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>;

children.text: tīrthaṃ sārasvataṃ nāma svāmitīrthaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Sārasvata</s>, and <s>Svāmitīrtha</s> likewise,

children.text: malaṃdarā nadī puṇyā kauśikī candrikā tathā ||
children.translated_text: the holy river <s>Malaṃdarā</s>, and <s>Kauśikī</s>, and <s>Candrikā</s> too;

children.text: vaidarbhā vātha vairā ca payoṣṇī prāṅmukhā parā
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidarbhā</s>, or else <s>Vairā</s>, and <s>Payoṣṇī</s>, facing east, the farther one,

children.text: kāverī cottarā puṇyā tathā jālaṃdharo giriḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the holy northern <s>Kāverī</s>, and likewise Mount <s>Jālaṃdhara</s>;
at these <s>śrāddha</s>-<s>tīrthas</s>, a <s>śrāddha</s> obtains endlessness.
And there is the <s>tīrtha</s> <s>Lohadaṇḍa</s>, and <s>Citrakūṭa</s> likewise;
<s>Vindhyayoga</s> of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and the auspicious bank of the river,
and the <s>tīrtha</s> <s>Kubjābhra</s>, and likewise the sandbank of <s>Urvaśī</s>;
the <s>tīrtha</s> <s>Saṃsāramocana</s>, and likewise <s>Ṛṇamocana</s>;
at these ancestral <s>tīrthas</s>, a <s>śrāddha</s> obtains endlessness.
And there is the <s>tīrtha</s> <s>Aṭṭahāsa</s>, and <s>Gautameśvara</s> too,

children.text: tathā vasiṣṭhatīrthaṃ nu hārītaṃ tu tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Vasiṣṭhatīrtha</s>, then after that <s>Hārīta</s>;
<s>Brahmāvarta</s>, <s>Kuśāvarta</s>, and <s>Hayatīrtha</s> likewise,

children.text: piṇḍārakaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ śaṅkhoddhāraṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: and the famed <s>Piṇḍāraka</s>, and <s>Śaṅkhoddhāra</s> likewise;
<s>Ghaṇṭeśvara</s>, <s>Bilvaka</s>, and <s>Nīlaparvata</s> too,

children.text: tathā ca dharaṇītīrthaṃ rāmatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Dharaṇītīrtha</s>, and <s>Rāmatīrtha</s> likewise;
and the renowned <s>Aśvatīrtha</s>, endless in respect to <s>śrāddha</s> and gifts,
the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Vedaśiras</s>, and likewise the river <s>Oghavatī</s>;

children.text: tīrthaṃ vasupradaṃ nāma chāgalāṇḍaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Vasuprada</s>, and <s>Chāgalāṇḍa</s> likewise;
those who give <s>śrāddha</s> at these places go to the supreme state.
And likewise there is <s>Badarītīrtha</s>, and <s>Gaṇatīrtha</s> too,

children.text: jayantaṃ vijayaṃ caiva śakratīrthaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jayanta</s> and <s>Vijaya</s>, and <s>Śakratīrtha</s> likewise;

children.text: śrīpateśca tathā tīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ raivatakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: and also the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Śrīpati</s>, and the <s>tīrtha</s> <s>Raivataka</s> as well,
and likewise <s>Śāradātīrtha</s>, and <s>Bhadrakāleśvara</s>;
and the supreme <s>Vaikuṇṭhatīrtha</s>, or else <s>Bhīmeśvara</s> too;
those who give <s>śrāddha</s> at these places go to the supreme goal.
The <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Mātṛgṛha</s>, and <s>Karavīrapura</s> likewise,
and the famed <s>Kuśeśaya</s>, and <s>Gaurīśikhara</s> too;

children.text: nakuleśasya tīrthaṃ ca kardamālaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Nakuleśa</s>, and <s>Kardamāla</s> likewise,
and similarly <s>Diṇḍipuṇyakara</s>, and <s>Puṇḍarīkapura</s> too;
the <s>Saptagodāvarītīrtha</s>, the lord over the lords of all <s>tīrthas</s>;
there <s>śrāddha</s> should be given by those who desire endless fruit.
This collection of <s>tīrthas</s> has been stated by me in summary form.

children.text: vāgīśo'pi na śaknoti vistarāt kim u mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even <s>Vāgīśa</s> cannot do it in detail; how much less a human being?
Truth is a <s>tīrtha</s>; compassion is a <s>tīrtha</s>; restraint of the senses is a <s>tīrtha</s>.
For people of the classes and life-stages, even the home is declared to be a <s>tīrtha</s>.
Whatever <s>śrāddha</s> is performed at these <s>tīrthas</s> is held to be multiplied ten million times.
Therefore, for that reason, one should carefully perform <s>śrāddha</s> at a <s>tīrtha</s>.

children.text: prātaḥkālo muhūrtāṃs trīn saṃgavas tāvadeva tu
children.translated_text: Morning lasts three <s>muhūrtas</s>; the forenoon lasts just as long.
Midday is three <s>muhūrtas</s>; after that comes the afternoon.
Evening is three <s>muhūrtas</s>; one should not have <s>śrāddha</s> performed then.

children.text: rākṣasī nāma sā velā garhitā sarvakarmasu ||
children.translated_text: That time is called <s>Rākṣasī</s>, and it is condemned in all rites.

children.text: ahno muhūrtā vikhyātā daśa pañca ca sarvadā
children.translated_text: The <s>muhūrtas</s> of the day are always known as fifteen in number.

children.text: tatrāṣṭamo muhūrto yaḥ sa kālaḥ kutapaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among them, the eighth <s>muhūrta</s> is remembered as the time called <s>Kutapa</s>.
Because at midday the sun always becomes subdued,
therefore beginning then is especially distinguished as granting endless fruit.
Midday, a rhinoceros-horn vessel, and likewise a Nepalese blanket,
silver, darbha grasses, sesame seeds, cows, and a daughter's son are remembered as the eighth.
They say that <s>pāpa</s> is what is bad and despised, and these cause it to burn away.
Since these eight do that, therefore they are famed as <s>kutapas</s>.
The four <s>muhūrtas</s> above and beyond the <s>Kutapa</s> <s>muhūrta</s>,
this set of five <s>muhūrtas</s> is regarded as the dwelling-place of <s>svadhā</s>.
Kuśa grasses, and likewise black sesame seeds, have arisen from the body of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The gods say that this is sufficient for the protection of the <s>śrāddha</s>.
A handful of sesame-water should be given by those dwelling at a <s>tīrtha</s>, while standing in water.
With one hand holding darbha grass, <s>śrāddha</s> is thus made especially excellent.
At the time of arranging the means of <s>śrāddha</s>, it is given with one hand,
but the <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) is with both hands; this rule is always remembered.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
It is meritorious, purifying, life-giving, and destructive of all sin,
this recounting of <s>tīrtha</s>-<s>śrāddha</s>, not told before on <s>Malaya</s>.
A man who hears it or recites it becomes prosperous.
It should be spoken at the time of <s>śrāddha</s>, and likewise by those dwelling at <s>tīrthas</s>,
for the pacification of all sins, the supreme destruction of misfortune.

children.text: idaṃ pavitraṃ yaśaso nidhānamidaṃ mahāpāpaharaṃ ca puṃsām
children.translated_text: This is holy, a treasury of fame; this is a remover of great sin for men.

children.text: brahmārkarudrairapi pūjitaṃ ca śrāddhasya māhātmyamuśanti tajjñāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is worshiped even by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Arka</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>; those who know declare it the greatness of <s>śrāddha</s>.
The sages said:
How is <s>Soma</s> the overlord of the ancestors, O one skilled in the śāstra?

children.text: tadvaṃśyā ye ca rājāno babhūvuḥ kīrtivardhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And who were the kings of his lineage, increasers of renown?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago, ordered by <s>Brahmā</s> in the rite of creation, <s>Atri</s>, the lord,
undertook an unsurpassed austerity named for the sake of creation.
That bliss-producing <s>brahman</s>, the destroyer of the world's affliction,
is internal to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Arka</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>, and beyond the senses.
For the peaceful-minded one who brought peace, it stood within his eye,
by the greatness of his tapas, O Brahmins, producing supreme bliss.
Because <s>Umāpati</s>, together with <s>Umā</s>, had occupied it,
and because he saw him through an eighth portion, from that <s>Soma</s> became a child.
From his two eyes that radiance, born from water, streamed downward,
lighting the entire universe, moving and unmoving, with its moonlight.
The quarters seized that radiance in female form, desiring a son,
and it became an embryo lodged in their wombs for three hundred years.
Then, unable to bear it, the quarters released that embryo.
Thereupon the four-faced one took up that embryo and made it one.
<s>Brahmā</s> made it into a young man, a person bearing every weapon,
and the lord set him on a chariot with a thousand horses, made of Vedic power.
Then <s>Pitāmaha</s> led him to his own world.
There the Brahmin seers declared, 'Let this one be our lord.'
By seers, gods, Gandharvas, and herbs as well,
he was praised with collections of mantras sacred to <s>Soma</s>, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.
As he was being praised, a greater radiance arose from him,
and from the expanse of that light a host of divine herbs came into being on earth.
Because of that, his brilliance is always greater at night.
Therefore <s>Soma</s> became lord of herbs, and he is also called lord of the twice-born.
This disk of the moon is also the essence and radiance of the Vedas,

children.text: kṣīyate vardhate caiva śukle kṛṣṇe ca sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: and it constantly wanes and waxes in the bright and dark fortnights.

children.text: viṃśatiṃ ca tathā sapta dakṣaḥ prācetaso dadau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dakṣa Prācetasa</s> gave him twenty-seven
splendid daughters, endowed with beauty and charm.
After that the cool-rayed one performed tapas
for ten thousand thousands of lotuses of years, devoted solely to meditation on <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Then the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>, was pleased with him,
and <s>Janārdana</s>, the supreme self, said, 'Choose a boon.'
Then <s>Soma</s> chose boons: 'May I conquer the world of <s>Śakra</s>.
May the enjoyers be directly present in my dwelling.

children.text: rājasūye suragaṇā brahmādyāḥ santu me dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: At my rājasūya, O Brahmins, may the hosts of gods headed by <s>Brahmā</s> be present,
and may <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Hara</s>, bearer of the trident, remain as our guardian against demons.'

children.text: tathetyuktaḥ sa ājahre rājasūyaṃ tu viṣṇunā
children.translated_text: When <s>Viṣṇu</s> had said, 'So be it,' he performed the rājasūya.
<s>Atri</s> was the Hotṛ, <s>Bhṛgu</s> the Adhvaryu, and the four-faced one became the Udgātṛ.
He attained the office of Brahman at that rite, and <s>Hari</s> himself was the overseer.
The members of the assembly in the rite of rājasūya are remembered as <s>Sanaka</s> and the others.
There the ten <s>Viśve Devas</s> were the Camasa-Adhvaryus,
and by him the three worlds were assigned as the sacrificial fee to the priests.
Then, when the avabhṛtha bath was completed, nine goddesses,
their limbs scorched by the arrows of desire and longing to behold his beauty, served him.
<s>Lakṣmī</s> abandoned <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and <s>Sinīvālī</s> abandoned <s>Kardama</s>.
Likewise <s>Dyuti</s> abandoned <s>Vibhāvasu</s>, and <s>Tuṣṭi</s> abandoned the imperishable <s>Dhātṛ</s>.

children.text: prabhā prabhākaraṃ tyaktvā haviṣmantaṃ kuhūḥ svayam
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhā</s> abandoned <s>Prabhākara</s>, and <s>Kuhū</s> herself abandoned <s>Haviṣmant</s>.
<s>Kīrti</s> abandoned her husband <s>Jayanta</s>, and <s>Vasu</s> abandoned <s>Marīci-Kaśyapa</s>.
<s>Dhṛti</s>, abandoning yellow-hued <s>Nandin</s>, then resorted to <s>Soma</s> alone.
And <s>Soma</s> too desired them then as though they were his own.
Although he had committed such an offense against them, their husbands at that time
were unable to punish the offense with curses, weapons, or other means.
Even so the moon shone, illuminating the quarters tenfold.
Then <s>Soma</s>, having obtained an almost unobtainable lordship, sanctioned by the seers,
attained through tapas the sole sovereignty over the seven worlds.
Once he saw, in a garden, a woman adorned with many flowers and ornaments,
her limbs very delicate, wearied by the weight of her broad hips and breasts even as she broke a flower.
She was the wife of the teacher of the gods, charming with love's arrows, with long lovely eyes.

children.text: tārāṃ sa tārādhipatiḥ smarārtaḥ keśeṣu jagrāha viviktabhūmau ||
children.translated_text: Love-stricken, the lord of the stars seized <s>Tārā</s> by the hair in a secluded place.

children.text: sāpi smarārtā saha tena reme tadrūpakāntyā hṛtamānasena
children.translated_text: She too, love-stricken, sported with him, her mind stolen by the splendor of his form.

children.text: ciraṃ vihṛtyātha jagāma tārāṃ vidhurgṛhītvā svagṛhaṃ tato'pi ||
children.translated_text: After sporting for a long time, the moon took <s>Tārā</s> and then went on to his own house.

children.text: na tṛptirāsīcca gṛhe'pi tasya tārānuraktasya sukhāgameṣu
children.translated_text: Even at home he found no satisfaction in the pleasures that came to him, for he was attached to <s>Tārā</s>.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, burned by the fire of separation from her, became single-mindedly fixed on thoughts of her.

children.text: śaśāka śāpaṃ na ca dātum asmai na mantraśastrāgniviṣairaśeṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: He could not give him a curse, nor by mantras, weapons, fire, or poisons
could the lord of speech harm him in any way, nor even by various rites of sorcery.
Then, wretched and tormented by love, he begged <s>Soma</s> for his own wife.

children.text: sa yācyamāno'pi dadau na tārāṃ bṛhaspatestatsukhapāśabaddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But even when entreated, he did not give <s>Tārā</s> to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, bound by the bond of that pleasure.

children.text: maheśvareṇātha caturmukheṇa sādhyair marudbhiḥ saha lokapālaiḥ
children.translated_text: When, through <s>Maheśvara</s> and the four-faced one, together with the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, and the guardians of the worlds,

children.text: dadau yadā tāṃ na kathaṃcid industadā śivaḥ krodhaparo babhūva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indu</s> still in no way gave her back, then <s>Śiva</s> became filled with anger.
He who is famed on earth as <s>Vāmadeva</s>, whose lotus feet are worshiped by many Rudras,
then <s>Giriśa</s>, the bearer of the Pināka, with his disciples, was bound by affection for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Taking up the bow <s>Ajagava</s>, <s>Purāri</s>, attended by the lord of beings and Siddhas, went
to battle with <s>Soma</s>, his face terrible with the fire of his especially blazing third eye.
Together with him went the companies beginning with <s>Gaṇeśaka</s>, equipped with twenty and sixty-four groups of weapons.
The lord of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, accompanied by many hundreds of crores, followed among those who stood in chariots.
There was one padma and likewise an arbuda of <s>Vetālas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, serpents, and <s>Kiṃnaras</s>;

children.text: lakṣais tribhir dvādaśabhī rathānāṃ somo'pyagāttatra vivṛddhamanyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with thirty-six lakhs of chariots, <s>Soma</s> too went there, his anger greatly increased.
He was joined by armies of constellations, <s>Daityas</s>, and <s>Asuras</s>, with <s>Śanaiścara</s> and <s>Aṅgāraka</s> grown mighty in splendor.

children.text: jagmurbhayaṃ sapta tathaiva lokāścacāla bhūr dvīpasamudragarbhā ||
children.translated_text: The seven worlds likewise fell into fear, and the earth, holding islands and oceans in her womb, trembled.
Then <s>Pinākin</s> went straight against <s>Soma</s>, bearing blazing weapons with vast flames.
Then there arose that great battle between the two armies, fearful and terrible in force.
It swelled to the destruction of every being, taking a single form as the blaze of sharp weapons and missiles.
Then the entire armies of the two sides came to destruction by one another's fierce, keen weapons.
Blazing weapons fell, burning heaven, earth, and then the netherworld.
In anger <s>Rudra</s> released the <s>Brahmaśīrṣa</s>; <s>Soma</s> too released the unfailing and mighty <s>Somāstra</s>.
At the fall of those two weapons, fear arose in the oceans, the earth, and the midspace.
Seeing that pair of weapons increased for the destruction of the worlds, even <s>Pitāmaha</s>

children.text: antaḥ praviśyātha kathaṃ kathaṃcinnivārayāmāsa suraiḥ sahaiva
children.translated_text: entered between them and, somehow or other, restrained them together with the gods.

children.text: akāraṇaṃ kiṃ kṣayakṛjjanānāṃ soma tvayāpīttham akāri kāryam ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Soma</s>, why has this causeless, destructive deed against living beings been done by you in this way?

children.text: yasmātparastrīharaṇāya soma tvayā kṛtaṃ yuddhamatīva bhīmam
children.translated_text: Since you have made this exceedingly dreadful war for the sake of taking another's wife, O <s>Soma</s>,

children.text: pāpagrahastvaṃ bhavitā janeṣu śānto'pyalaṃ nūnamatho sitānte
children.translated_text: you shall become a malefic <s>graha</s> among people, though at the end of the bright fortnight you are indeed pacified.
Give this wife back to <s>Vākpati</s>; is there not disgrace in seizing what belongs to another?"
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tatheti covāca himāṃśumālī yuddhād apākrāmadataḥ praśāntaḥ
children.translated_text: "So be it," said the moon-crested one, and, pacified, he withdrew from the battle.

children.text: bṛhaspatiḥ svāmapagṛhya tārāṃ hṛṣṭo jagāma svagṛhaṃ sarudraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, having recovered his own <s>Tārā</s>, went joyfully to his own house together with <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then, at the end of a year, one resembling the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>,
wearing divine yellow garments and adorned with divine ornaments,
came forth from <s>Tārā</s>'s womb: a boy resembling the moon,
wise, knowing all treatises on worldly aims, and the founder of the science of elephants.
The elephant-medicine called <s>Rājaputrīya</s> became renowned;

children.text: rājñaḥ somasya putratvād rājaputro budhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because he was the son of King <s>Soma</s>, <s>Budha</s> is remembered as <s>Rājaputra</s>.
As soon as he was born, that strong one conquered all splendors.
The gods, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, came there together with the divine seers.
At that birth-rite celebration in <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s house, all the gods
asked <s>Tārā</s>, "By whom was this little boy begotten?"

children.text: tataḥ sā lajjitā teṣāṃ na kiṃcidavadattadā
children.translated_text: Then she, ashamed before them, said nothing at that time.
Questioned again and again then, the lovely woman grew embarrassed.
After a long while she said, "He is <s>Soma</s>'s." Then <s>Vidhu</s> took his son,
gave him the name <s>Budha</s>, and granted him kingship on the earth.
Then, having performed the consecration, the powerful one made him chief.
After granting equal standing in the household, <s>Brahmā</s>, together with the <s>Brahmarṣis</s>,
vanished right there while all the gods were watching.
In <s>Ilā</s>'s womb <s>Budha</s> begot a most righteous son,
who by his own splendor performed a full hundred horse-sacrifices.
He was known as <s>Purūravā</s>, honored by all the worlds.
Having worshiped <s>Janārdana</s> on the lovely peak of <s>Himavat</s>,
the king then attained lordship over the worlds and became ruler of the seven islands.
By him <s>Daityas</s> beginning with <s>Keśin</s> were torn apart by the crore.
<s>Urvāśī</s>, enchanted by his beauty, became his wife.
The earth with its seven islands, together with its mountains, forests, and groves,
was ruled with <s>dharma</s> by him, who sought the welfare of all the worlds.
Fame always held his chowrie and attended upon his body.
By the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Devendra</s> then gave him half his throne.
He protected <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, and <s>Kāma</s> equally, and he did so through <s>dharma</s>.
Once <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, and <s>Kāma</s> came out of curiosity to see him,
desiring to know his conduct: "How does he regard us as equal?"
Then the king, with devotion, offered them arghya, water for the feet, and the other honors.
He brought three divine seats adorned with gold,
and, seating them, performed worship, but again made it slightly greater for <s>Dharma</s>.
Because of that, <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Artha</s> became very angry toward the king.
<s>Artha</s> gave him a curse: "Through greed you will go to destruction."
<s>Kāma</s> too said, "Madness will be yours on <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
when, having resorted to <s>Kumāravana</s>, you suffer separation from <s>Urvāśī</s>."
<s>Dharma</s> also said, "You shall be long-lived, and you shall be righteous.
Your lineage, O king of kings, as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure,

children.text: śataśo vṛddhimāyātu na nāśaṃ bhuvi yāsyati
children.translated_text: shall increase hundreds of times and shall not perish on earth."
Having spoken thus, they all disappeared, and the king enjoyed that kingdom.

children.text: ahanyahani devendraṃ draṣṭuṃ yāti sa rājarāṭ
children.translated_text: Day after day that king of kings went to see <s>Devendra</s>.
Once, mounting a chariot that moved through the southern sky,
together with <s>Arka</s> he saw, being carried through the sky,
<s>Citralekhā</s> and <s>Urvāśī</s> by <s>Keśin</s>, lord of the <s>Dānavas</s>.
Having conquered him in battle while holding various weapons,
the son of <s>Budha</s>, desiring fame, released the <s>Vāyavya</s> missile.

children.text: tathā śakro'pi samare ā caivaṃ vinirjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Śakra</s> too was involved in the battle and was overcome in that way.

children.text: mitratvam agamad devair dadāv indrāya corvaśīm ||
children.translated_text: He entered into friendship with the gods and gave <s>Urvāśī</s> to <s>Indra</s>.
From that time onward <s>Pākaśāsana</s> entered into friendship with him.
surpassing all worlds, strength, vigor, fame, and prosperity.
The wielder of the thunderbolt, pleased also with <s>Bharata</s>, bestowed it.

children.text: sā purūravasaḥ prītyā gāyantī caritaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: Out of love for <s>Purūravas</s>, she sang his great deeds.
A performance called <s>Lakṣmīsvayaṃvara</s>, the self-choice of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, was then set in motion.
He ordered <s>Menakā</s>, <s>Urvaśī</s>, and <s>Rambhā</s>, saying, "Dance."
There <s>Urvaśī</s> danced in rhythm in the role of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
While dancing, she saw <s>Purūravas</s> and was afflicted by desire.
She forgot the whole performance that <s>Bharata</s> had previously taught.
In anger <s>Bharata</s> cursed her: because of separation from him, on earth
for fifty-five years you shall become a fine creeper.
And there <s>Purūravas</s> shall experience the state of a <s>piśāca</s> (spirit).
Then <s>Urvaśī</s> went to him and made him her husband for a long time.
When <s>Bharata</s>'s curse had ended, <s>Urvaśī</s> bore sons to the son of <s>Budha</s>.
She gave birth to eight sons; learn their names.
<s>Āyu</s>, <s>Dṛḍhāyu</s>, <s>Aśvāyu</s>, <s>Dhanāyu</s>, <s>Dhṛtimat</s>, and <s>Vasu</s>,
<s>Śucividya</s> and <s>Śatāyu</s>; all had divine strength and vigor.

children.text: āyuṣo nahuṣaḥ putrau vṛddhaśarmā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: The sons of <s>Āyu</s> were <s>Nahuṣa</s>, and likewise <s>Vṛddhaśarman</s>,

children.text: rajirdambho vipāpmā ca vīrāḥ pañca mahārathāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Raji</s>, <s>Dambha</s>, and <s>Vipāpmā</s>, five heroes and great chariot-warriors.
A hundred sons were born to <s>Raji</s>, famed as the <s>Rājeyas</s>.
<s>Raji</s> worshiped stainless <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Pleased by his austerity, <s>Viṣṇu</s> granted him boons, O king.
Then he became victorious over gods, asuras, and men.
Then a war between gods and asuras lasted for three hundred years.
It was terrible, between <s>Prahlāda</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, and neither of the two was victorious.
Then, questioned by the gods and asuras, the four-faced god spoke.
When asked, "Who will be victorious between these two?" he said, "The side on which <s>Raji</s> stands."

children.text: jayāya prārthito rājā sahāyastvaṃ bhavasva naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeking victory, they asked the king, "Be our ally."

children.text: daityaiḥ prāha yadi svāmī vo bhavāmi tatastvalam
children.translated_text: To the <s>Daityas</s> he said, "If I become your lord, then that will be enough."
The asuras did not accept that, but the gods did accept it.

children.text: svāmī bhava tvamasmākaṃ saṃgrāme nāśaya dviṣaḥ
children.translated_text: "Be our lord; in battle destroy our enemies."
Then all those who had been invulnerable to the wielder of the thunderbolt were destroyed.
Pleased by his deed, mighty <s>Indra</s> entered into the status of his son.

children.text: dattvendrāya tadā rājyaṃ jagāma tapase rajiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After giving the kingdom then to <s>Indra</s>, <s>Raji</s> went away to perform austerity.
At that time <s>Indra</s>'s power was forcibly seized by the sons of <s>Raji</s>.
Endowed with the power and merit of austerity, they took his share in sacrifice and his kingdom.
Then <s>Śakra</s>, deprived of his kingdom and oppressed by the sons of <s>Raji</s>,

children.text: prāha vācaspatiṃ dīnaḥ pīḍito'smi rajeḥ sutaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke in distress to <s>Vācaspati</s>: "I am oppressed by the sons of <s>Raji</s>.

children.text: na yajñabhāgo rājyaṃ me nirjitaśca bṛhaspate
children.translated_text: My share of sacrifice and my kingdom are gone; I have been defeated, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Devise an effort for me to recover my kingdom, O lord of wisdom."
Then <s>Bṛhaspati</s> made <s>Śakra</s> strong and proud again
by a rite for pacifying the planets and by a rite for increase and prosperity.
Then <s>Bṛhaspati</s> went and deluded the sons of <s>Raji</s>.
Though he knew the Veda, he adopted <s>Jina-dharma</s>, a teaching outside the Veda.
The lord of wisdom caused them to fall away from the threefold Veda.
Recognizing that they were outside the Veda and furnished with doctrines of reasoning,
<s>Śakra</s> struck them all down with the thunderbolt, since they had been cast outside <s>dharma</s> (sacred order).
I shall now tell the seven righteous sons of <s>Nahuṣa</s>.
<s>Yati</s>, <s>Yayāti</s>, <s>Saṃyāti</s>, <s>Udbhava</s>, and <s>Pāci</s>,
<s>Śaryāti</s> and <s>Meghajāti</s>: these seven increased the lineage.
Even in boyhood <s>Yati</s> became a yogin of the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> order.
And <s>Yayāti</s> ruled the kingdom, always taking <s>dharma</s> as his sole refuge.
His wife was <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.
So too was the virtuous <s>Devayānī</s>, daughter of the <s>Bhārgava</s>.
I shall tell by name the five heirs of <s>Yayāti</s>.
<s>Devayānī</s> bore him the sons <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Turvasu</s>.
Likewise <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> bore the sons <s>Druhyu</s>, <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Pūru</s>.
Among them <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Pūru</s> became increasers of their lineages.
<s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, was a king of true valor.
He protected the earth and sacrificed with rites performed according to rule.
With great devotion he always worshiped the ancestors and the gods, remaining pure.
Then undefeated <s>Yayāti</s> conquered all peoples.

children.text: sa śāśvatīḥ samā rājā prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
children.translated_text: The king protected his subjects by <s>dharma</s> for many lasting years.
The son of <s>Nahuṣa</s> then incurred very terrible old age, destroyer of beauty.
Overcome by old age, the king spoke these words to his sons,

children.text: yaduṃ pūruṃ turvasuṃ ca druhyuṃ ca pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Yadu</s>, <s>Pūru</s>, <s>Turvasu</s>, and <s>Druhyu</s>, O king:
"With youth, as a young man together with young women, I wish to enjoy fleeting pleasures.
I desire to sport with them; help me, my sons."
His son, the firstborn <s>Yadu</s>, son of <s>Devayānī</s>, said to him,
"Help must indeed be given to you by us, but what have we to do with our youth?"
<s>Yayāti</s> said to his sons, "Let my old age be accepted.
Then, with the youth of one of you, I would pursue the objects of sense.
Because I have sacrificed with long sacrificial sessions, and because of the curse of the sage <s>Uśanas</s>,
my purpose of desire has been diminished; I am unsatisfied, and therefore, my sons,
let this old age of mine rule over you in your own body.
With a newly young body I would obtain pleasures."
<s>Yadu</s> and the others did not accept that old age of his.
Thus, we have heard, the royal sage cursed those four.
Then the youngest, <s>Pūru</s>, whose valor was true, said to him,

children.text: jarāṃ mā dehi navayā tanvā me yauvanātsukhī ||
children.translated_text: "Give your old age to me; with my body made new by my youth, be happy."

children.text: ahaṃ jarāṃ tavādāya rājye sthāsyāmi cājñayā
children.translated_text: I will take your old age and, at your command, I will remain in the kingdom.
Thus addressed, that royal sage, relying on the power of his austerity,
then placed his old age upon his great-souled son.
And with the age of the <s>Paurava</s>, the king took on youth.
Then <s>Pūru</s>, with the age of <s>Yayāti</s>, governed the kingdom.
Thereafter, when a thousand years had passed, unconquered <s>Yayāti</s>,

children.text: atṛpta iva kāmānāṃ pūruṃ putramuvāca ha
children.translated_text: as though still unsated with pleasures, spoke to his son <s>Pūru</s>:

children.text: tvayā dāyādavān asmi tvaṃ me vaṃśakaraḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through you I have heirs; you, my son, are the maker of my lineage.

children.text: pauravo vaṃśa ityeṣa khyātiṃ loke gamiṣyati
children.translated_text: This lineage will be known in the world as the <s>Paurava</s> line.

children.text: tataḥ sa nṛpaśārdūlaḥ pūruṃ rājye'bhiṣicya ca ||
children.translated_text: Then that tiger among kings consecrated <s>Pūru</s> in the kingdom,
and afterward, after a long time, he met the law of time.
I shall proclaim the lineage of <s>Pūru</s>; listen, best of seers,
in which those <s>Bhāratas</s> were born, increasers of <s>Bharata</s>'s line.
The seers said:

children.text: kimarthaṃ pauravo vaṃśaḥ śreṣṭhatvaṃ prāpa bhūtale
children.translated_text: For what reason did the <s>Paurava</s> lineage attain supremacy on earth?
And why was the lineage of <s>Yadu</s>, though he was the eldest, deprived of prosperity?
Tell us in full, <s>Sūta</s>, the further story of <s>Yayāti</s>,
for it is meritorious, life-giving, and worthy of praise even by the gods.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago <s>Śaunaka</s> was asked this very question by <s>Śatānīka</s>:
the great story of <s>Yayāti</s>, meritorious, purifying, and life-giving.
<s>Śatānīka</s> said:
<s>Yayāti</s> was our forefather, the tenth from <s>Prajāpati</s>.
How did he obtain the daughter of <s>Śukra</s>, who was so very hard to win?
I wish to hear this in detail, treasure of austerity.
Tell me also, in order, of the kings who upheld the lineage of <s>Pūru</s>.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
<s>Yayāti</s> was a royal sage, equal in splendor to the king of the gods.

children.text: taṃ śukravṛṣaparvāṇau vavrāte vai yathā purā ||
children.translated_text: How <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s> chose him in ancient times,
that I shall fully tell you as you ask, best of kings,
along with the union of <s>Devayānī</s> and <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>.
Between the gods and the asuras there arose, one against the other,
a conflict over sovereignty in the three worlds, with all that moves and does not move.
Then, desiring victory, the gods chose the sage descended from <s>Aṅgiras</s>

children.text: paurohitye ca yajñārthe kāvyaṃ tūśanasaṃ pare ||
children.translated_text: for priesthood and sacrificial office; the others chose <s>Kāvya</s> <s>Uśanas</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇau tāv ubhau nityamanyonyaṃ spardhinau bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Those two brahmins were always fiercely in rivalry with one another.
There the gods struck down the <s>Dānavas</s> when they met in battle,
but <s>Kāvya</s>, relying on the power of his knowledge, brought them back to life.
Then they rose up again and fought the gods.
But when the asuras slew gods on the front of battle,
high-minded <s>Bṛhaspati</s> did not restore them to life,

children.text: na hi veda sa tāṃ vidyāṃ yāṃ kāvyo veda vīryavān
children.translated_text: for he did not know that knowledge which mighty <s>Kāvya</s> knew,

children.text: saṃjīvanīṃ tato devā viṣādam agaman param ||
children.translated_text: the <s>saṃjīvanī</s> (reviving knowledge). Therefore the gods fell into the deepest despair.
Then the gods, terrified by <s>Kāvya</s> <s>Uśanas</s>,
approached <s>Kaca</s>, the eldest son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and said:
Favor us who favor you; render us the highest assistance.
That knowledge which resides in the brahmin of immeasurable splendor,
in <s>Śukra</s>, bring it here quickly; you shall become a sharer in our portion.

children.text: vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ samīpe'sau śakyo draṣṭuṃ tvayā dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That twice-born one can be seen by you near <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.
There he protects the <s>Dānavas</s>; he does not protect those who are not <s>Dānavas</s>.

children.text: tam ārādhayituṃ śakto nānyaḥ kaścidṛte tvayā ||
children.translated_text: No one except you is able to win his favor.

children.text: devayānī ca dayitā sutā tasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Devayānī</s>, the beloved daughter of that great-souled one,

children.text: tām ārādhayituṃ śakto nānyaḥ kaścana vidyate ||
children.translated_text: no one else at all is able to win her favor.
By good conduct, kindness, sweetness, proper behavior, and self-restraint,

children.text: devayānyāṃ tu tuṣṭāyāṃ vidyāṃ tāṃ prāpsyasi dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Devayānī</s> is pleased, you will certainly obtain that knowledge.

children.text: tadā hi preṣito devaiḥ samīpe vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, thus sent by the gods to the vicinity of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>,
<s>Kaca</s>, the son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, said, 'So be it,' and set out.

children.text: sa gatvā tvarito rājandevaiḥ sampūjitaḥ kacaḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone swiftly, O king, <s>Kaca</s>, honored by the gods,
bowed to <s>Śukra</s> in the city of the lord of asuras and said this:
I am the grandson of the seer <s>Aṅgiras</s>, the direct son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: nāmnā kaceti vikhyātaṃ śiṣyaṃ gṛhṇātu māṃ bhavān ||
children.translated_text: renowned by the name <s>Kaca</s>; let your honor accept me as a pupil.
I will practice supreme brahmacarya with you, revered teacher.
Permit me, brahmin, to do so for a thousand full years.
<s>Śukra</s> said:

children.text: kaca susvāgataṃ te 'stu pratigṛhṇāmi te vacaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kaca</s>, welcome to you. I accept your words.
I will honor you who deserve honor; let <s>Bṛhaspati</s> too be honored.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Then <s>Kaca</s>, saying 'So be it' to him, accepted that vow,
as it had been prescribed by <s>Śukra</s> <s>Uśanas</s> himself, the son of <s>Kavi</s>.

children.text: vrataṃ ca vratakālaṃ ca yathoktaṃ pratyagṛhṇata
children.translated_text: He undertook the vow and the period of the vow exactly as stated,
serving his teacher and <s>Devayānī</s>, O <s>Bhārata</s>.
Always wishing to please her, he, a youth in the sphere of youth,
delighted <s>Devayānī</s> by singing, dancing, and playing instruments.
Cultivating the friendship of <s>Devayānī</s>, a maiden who had reached youth,
he pleased the <s>Bhārgavī</s> with flowers, fruits, and errands.
<s>Devayānī</s> too attended on that brahmin, who observed rules and vows,
singing along with him; as a young woman, she served him in private then.
When <s>Kaca</s> had thus practiced for five hundred years,

children.text: tattattīvraṃ vrataṃ buddhvā dānavāstaṃ tataḥ kacam ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Dānavas</s>, perceiving that severe vow of his, then
saw <s>Kaca</s> guarding the cows in the forest, secretly and in anger.
They killed him out of hatred for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and also for their own protection.
Having killed him and cut him into small pieces, they gave him to the wild dogs.
Then the cows returned to their own enclosure without their cowherd.

children.text: tā dṛṣṭvā rahitā gāstu kacenābhyāgatā vanāt
children.translated_text: Seeing that the cows had come back from the forest without <s>Kaca</s>,
<s>Devayānī</s> then spoke these words at the proper time to the <s>Bhārgava</s>:

children.text: hutaṃ caivāgnihotraṃ te sūryaścāstaṃ gataḥ prabho
children.translated_text: "Your <s>agnihotra</s> has indeed been offered, and the sun has set, lord.
The cows have come back without a cowherd; father, <s>Kaca</s> is not seen.

children.text: vyaktaṃ hato dhṛto vāpi kacastāta bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Clearly, father, <s>Kaca</s> must have been killed or seized.

children.text: taṃ vinā naiva jīvāmi vacaḥ satyaṃ bravīmyaham ||
children.translated_text: Without him I will not live; I tell you the truth."
<s>Śukra</s> said:
"Then, with the words 'Come here, come here,' I shall bring the dead one back to life."
Then, applying the <s>saṃjīvanī</s> vidyā (life-restoring knowledge), he summoned <s>Kaca</s>.
When called, <s>Kaca</s> appeared, and he bowed to <s>Śukra</s>.
The son of <s>Dhiṣaṇā</s> reported, "I was killed by the Rākṣasas."
Again, at <s>Devayānī</s>'s request, when he happened to be gathering flowers,

children.text: vanaṃ yayau kaco vipraḥ paṭhanbrahma ca śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: the Brahmin <s>Kaca</s> went to the forest, reciting the eternal <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: vane puṣpāṇi cinvantaṃ dadṛśur dānavāśca tam
children.translated_text: The Dānavas saw him in the forest gathering flowers.

children.text: tato'dvitīyaṃ taṃ hatvā dagdhaṃ kṛtvā ca cūrṇavat
children.translated_text: Then, when he was alone, they killed him, burned him, and made him like powder.
At that time the Asuras gave him to the Brahmin himself in liquor.
Then once again <s>Devayānī</s> spoke a sentence to her father:
"Father, <s>Kaca</s>, who was sent to gather flowers, is not seen.

children.text: vyaktaṃ hato mṛto vāpi kacastāta bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Clearly, father, <s>Kaca</s> must have been killed and died.

children.text: taṃ vinā naiva jīvāmi vacaḥ satyaṃ bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: Without him I will not live; I tell you the truth."
<s>Śukra</s> said:

children.text: bṛhaspateḥ sutaḥ putri kacaḥ pretagatiṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: "Daughter, <s>Kaca</s>, the son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, has gone the way of the dead.
Even when brought to life by the vidyā he is killed in this way. What shall I do?

children.text: mainaṃ śuco mā ruda devayāni na tvādṛśī martyamanu praśocet
children.translated_text: Do not grieve for him, do not weep, <s>Devayānī</s>; one like you should not mourn for a mortal,

children.text: yasyāstava brahma ca brāhmaṇāśca sendrāśca devā vasavo'śvinau ca ||
children.translated_text: for your <s>brahman</s>, the Brahmins, the gods with <s>Indra</s>, the Vasus, and the Aśvins,
the enemies of the gods, and the whole world are at hand through the power of my tapas.

children.text: aśakyo'yaṃ jīvayituṃ dvijātiḥ saṃjīvito yo vadhyate caiva bhūyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This twice-born one is impossible to revive, since, after being brought to life, he is killed again."
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: yasyāṅgirā vṛddhatamaḥ pitāmaho bṛhaspatiścāpi pitā taponidhiḥ
children.translated_text: "His grandfather is <s>Aṅgiras</s>, eldest of all, and his father too is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, a treasury of tapas.

children.text: ṛṣeḥ suputraṃ tamathāpi pautraṃ kathaṃ na śoce yamahaṃ na rudyām ||
children.translated_text: How should I not mourn and not weep for that good son and grandson of a seer?

children.text: sa brahmacārī ca tapodhanaśca sadotthitaḥ karmasu caiva dakṣaḥ
children.translated_text: He is a celibate student, rich in tapas, always diligent and skillful in his duties.

children.text: kacasya mārgaṃ pratipatsye na bhokṣye priyo hi me tāta kaco'bhirūpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I will follow the path of <s>Kaca</s>; I will not eat. For handsome <s>Kaca</s> is dear to me, father."
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: sa tv evamukto devayānyā maharṣiḥ saṃrambheṇa vyājahārātha kāvyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Devayānī</s>, the great seer <s>Kāvya</s> then spoke in anger:

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ māmasurā dviṣanti ye me śiṣyānāgatānsūdayanti ||
children.translated_text: "Without doubt the Asuras hate me, since they slay my pupils when they come.

children.text: abrāhmaṇaṃ kartumicchanti raudrā ebhir vyarthaṃ prastuto dānavairhi
children.translated_text: The fierce ones wish to make me un-Brahmin; this undertaking by the Dānavas is futile.

children.text: tatkarmaṇāpyasya bhavedihāntaḥ kaṃ brahmahatyā na dahedapīndram ||
children.translated_text: Even by that act there would be an end for him here; whom would <s>brahmahatyā</s> (the killing of a Brahmin) not burn, even <s>Indra</s>?"

children.text: sa tenāpṛṣṭo vidyayā copahūtaḥ śanairvācaṃ jaṭhare vyājahāra
children.translated_text: Then, questioned by him and summoned by the vidyā, he slowly uttered speech from his belly.

children.text: tamabravītkena cehopanīto mamodare tiṣṭhasi brūhi vatsa ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, "By what means have you been brought here, and are you staying in my stomach? Tell me, child."
<s>Kaca</s> said:

children.text: bhavatprasādānna jahāti māṃ smṛtiḥ sarvaṃ smareyaṃ yacca yathā ca vṛttam
children.translated_text: "By your favor, memory does not leave me; I remember everything, what happened and how.

children.text: na tv evaṃ syāttapasaḥ kṣayo me tata kleśaṃ ghorataraṃ smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: Yet my tapas must not be lost in this way; father, I remember a far more terrible affliction.

children.text: asuraiḥ surāyāṃ bhavato 'smi datto hatvā dagdhvā cūrṇayitvā ca kāvya
children.translated_text: O <s>Kāvya</s>, after killing, burning, and pulverizing me, the Asuras gave me to you in liquor.

children.text: brāhmīṃ māyāṃ tv āsurī tv atra māyā tvayi sthite katham evābhibādhate ||
children.translated_text: How can Brahminical power, with Asuric power here, overcome you while I am within you?"
<s>Śukra</s> said:

children.text: kiṃ te priyaṃ karavāṇyadya vatse vinaiva me jīvitaṃ syātkacasya
children.translated_text: "What dear thing shall I do for you today, child? Apart from my life, <s>Kaca</s> may live.

children.text: nānyatra kukṣermama bhedanācca dṛśyet kaco madgato devayāni ||
children.translated_text: But, <s>Devayānī</s>, <s>Kaca</s>, who has entered me, cannot be seen except by splitting open my belly."
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: dvau māṃ śokāv agnikalpau dahetāṃ kacasya nāśastava caivopaghātaḥ
children.translated_text: "Two griefs, like fire, would burn me: the loss of <s>Kaca</s> and also injury to you.

children.text: kacasya nāśe mama nāsti śarma tavopaghāte jīvituṃ nāsmi śaktā ||
children.translated_text: At <s>Kaca</s>'s loss there is no happiness for me; at injury to you I am not able to live."
<s>Śukra</s> said:

children.text: saṃsiddharūpo'si bṛhaspateḥ suta yattvāṃ bhaktaṃ bhajate devayānī
children.translated_text: "You are accomplished in form, son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, since devoted <s>Devayānī</s> loves you.

children.text: vidyāmimāṃ prāpnuhi jīvanīṃ tvaṃ na cedindraḥ kacarūpī tvamadya ||
children.translated_text: Receive this life-giving vidyā, unless today you are <s>Indra</s> in the form of <s>Kaca</s>.
No other living person could come out again from my belly,
except a single Brahmin; therefore obtain the vidyā.

children.text: putro bhūtvā niṣkramasvodarānme bhittvā kukṣiṃ jīvaya māṃ ca tāta
children.translated_text: Become my son and come out from my belly, splitting my abdomen, and bring me back to life, child.

children.text: avekṣethā dharmavatīmavekṣāṃ guroḥ sakāśātprāpya vidyāṃ savidyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After receiving the vidyā from your teacher, being learned, you should show regard with a righteous regard."
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: guroḥ sakāśātsamavāpya vidyāṃ bhittvā kukṣiṃ nirvicakrāma vipraḥ
children.translated_text: Having obtained the vidyā from his teacher, the Brahmin split open his belly and came out.
It was like the moon at the coming of night on the full-moon day, breaking forth as the white peak of the snowy mountain.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ patitaṃ vedarāśimutthāpayāmāsa tataḥ kaco'pi
children.translated_text: Seeing him fallen, a mass of Veda, <s>Kaca</s> then raised him up too.

children.text: vidyāṃ siddhāṃ tāmavāpyābhivādya tataḥ kacastaṃ gurumityuvāca ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained that perfected vidyā and bowing, <s>Kaca</s> then said this to his teacher:

children.text: nidhiṃ nidhīnāṃ varadaṃ varāṇāṃ ye nādriyante gurumarcanīyam
children.translated_text: "Those who do not honor the teacher, the treasure of treasures, the giver of the best boons, who is worthy of worship,
go to sinful worlds without standing, though he is like the radiant forehead set on the snowy mountain."
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: surāpānād vañcanāt prāpayitvā saṃjñānāśaṃ cetasaścāpi ghoram
children.translated_text: Through drinking liquor and deception he had been brought to loss of consciousness and a terrible bewilderment of mind.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kacaṃ cāpi tathābhirūpaṃ pītaṃ tathā surayā mohitena ||
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Kaca</s>, so handsome, as having been drunk in that way with liquor by one who was deluded,
the great-souled <s>Uśanas</s> rose up angrily then, wishing to do what was beneficial for Brahmins.

children.text: kāvyaḥ svayaṃ vākyamidaṃ jagāda surāpānaṃ pratyasau jātaśaṅkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāvya</s> himself spoke these words, having become apprehensive about the drinking of surā.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
From today onward, whatever Brahmin here, dull-witted through delusion, shall drink surā,

children.text: apetadharmā brahmahā caiva sa syādasmiṃlloke garhitaḥ syātpare ca ||
children.translated_text: he shall be devoid of <s>dharma</s> (normative order) and indeed a slayer of a Brahmin; he shall be censured in this world and in the next.

children.text: mayā cemāṃ vipradharmoktasīmāṃ maryādāṃ vai sthāpitāṃ sarvaloke
children.translated_text: And by me this boundary, this rule declared as the dharma of Brahmins, has been established in all the world.

children.text: santo viprāḥ śuśruvāṃso gurūṇāṃ devā daityāścopaśṛṇvantu sarve ||
children.translated_text: Let virtuous Brahmins, obedient to their gurus, and all the gods and <s>Daityas</s> hear it.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: itīdamuktvā sa mahāprabhāvas taponidhīnāṃ nidhir aprameyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having said this, that one of great power, the immeasurable treasure of the treasures of tapas,
summoned those <s>Dānavas</s> of hidden intent and spoke these words to them.
<s>Śukra</s> said:

children.text: ācakṣe vo dānavā bāliśāḥ stha śiṣyaḥ kaco vatsyati matsamīpe
children.translated_text: I tell you, O <s>Dānavas</s>: you are childish. The disciple <s>Kaca</s> will remain near me.

children.text: saṃjīvanīṃ prāpya vidyāṃ mayāyaṃ tulyaprabhāvo brāhmaṇo brahmabhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained from me the <s>saṃjīvanī</s> vidyā (reviving knowledge), this Brahmin has become equal to me in power, as one formed of Brahman.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: guroruṣya sakāśe ca daśa varṣaśatāni saḥ
children.translated_text: After staying near his guru for a thousand years,
<s>Kaca</s>, given leave, wished to go to the abode of the thirty gods.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: samāpitavrataṃ taṃ tu visṛṣṭaṃ guruṇā tadā
children.translated_text: When he had completed his vow, had been released by his guru,
and had set out for the dwelling of the thirty gods, <s>Devayānī</s> spoke this to him.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
O grandson of the seer <s>Aṅgiras</s>, by conduct and by birth,

children.text: bhrājase vidyayā caiva tapasā ca damena ca ||
children.translated_text: and by knowledge, tapas, and self-restraint, you shine forth.
Just as the famous seer <s>Aṅgiras</s> is honored by my father,

children.text: tathā mānyaśca pūjyaśca mama bhūyo bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is still more honored and worshiped by me.
Knowing this, understand what I say, O treasure of tapas:
while you stood under vow and were furnished with observances, how I behaved toward you.

children.text: sa samāpitavidyo māṃ bhaktāṃ na tyaktumarhasi
children.translated_text: Now that your knowledge is complete, you ought not abandon me, devoted as I am to you.
Take my hand according to rule, preceded by the marriage mantras.
<s>Kaca</s> said:

children.text: pūjyo mānyaśca bhagavānyathā mama pitā tava
children.translated_text: As your blessed father is worshipful and honorable to me,
so you too, O faultless-limbed lady, are considered most worthy of worship.
You are dearer than his own life-breaths to the great-souled <s>Bhārgava</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ bhadre dharmataḥ pūjyā guruputrī sadā mama ||
children.translated_text: O gracious lady, by dharma you are always to be worshiped by me as my guru's daughter.

children.text: yathā mama gururnityaṃ mānyaḥ śukraḥ pitā tava
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Śukra</s>, your father, is always honorable to me as my guru,

children.text: devayāni tathaiva tvaṃ naivaṃ māṃ vaktumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: so too, <s>Devayānī</s>, are you; you should not speak to me in this way.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: guruputrasya putro me na tu tvamasi me pituḥ
children.translated_text: To me you are the son of a guru's son; you are not my father's son.
Therefore you too, O best of twice-born men, are honorable and worshipful to me.

children.text: asurairhanyamāne tu kace tvayi punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When you, <s>Kaca</s>, were being killed again and again by the <s>Asuras</s>,

children.text: tadāprabhṛti yā prītistāṃ tvameva smarasva me ||
children.translated_text: from that time onward, remember that affection which I had for you.

children.text: sauhārde cānurāge ca vettha me bhaktimuttamām
children.translated_text: You know my supreme devotion in friendship and in love.
O knower of dharma, you ought not abandon me, devoted and innocent as I am.
<s>Kaca</s> said:
You are appointing me to an appointment to which I should not be appointed, O lady of fair vows.

children.text: prasīda subhrūrmahyaṃ tvaṃ guror gurutarā śubhe ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious to me, O fair-browed, auspicious lady; you are more weighty than my guru.
Where you dwelt, O wide-eyed one, O moon-faced lady,
there I too dwelt, O gracious beauty, in the belly of <s>Kāvya</s>.

children.text: bhaginī dharmato me tvaṃ maivaṃ vocaḥ śubhānane
children.translated_text: By dharma you are my sister; do not speak thus, O fair-faced one.
I have dwelt happily here, O gracious lady; there is no anger in me.

children.text: āpṛcche tvāṃ gamiṣyāmi śivamastvatha me pathi
children.translated_text: I take leave of you and shall go; may there be welfare on my path.
Without conflict with dharma, remember me when the matter comes up again.
Careful and always intent, serve my guru.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
When you were killed by the <s>Daityas</s>, I protected you with the thought that you would be my husband.
If, though I seek dharma and love, you reject me on grounds of dharma,

children.text: tataḥ kaca na te vidyā siddhimeṣā gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: then, <s>Kaca</s>, this knowledge of yours shall not come to success.
<s>Kaca</s> said:
Because you are my guru's daughter, I reject you, not out of any fault.
And I have been permitted by my guru; curse me just as you wish.

children.text: ārṣaṃ dharmaṃ bruvāṇo'haṃ devayāni yathā tvayā
children.translated_text: I am speaking the dharma of the seers, <s>Devayānī</s>, as you know.

children.text: śaptuṃ nārho 'smi kalyāṇi kāmato'dya ca dharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: O auspicious lady, I do not deserve to be cursed today, either from desire or by dharma.

children.text: tasmādbhavatyā yaḥ kāmo na tathā sambhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Therefore the wish you have shall not come about in that way.

children.text: ṛṣiputro na te kaścijjātu pāṇiṃ grahīṣyati ||
children.translated_text: No son of a seer shall ever take your hand.
The knowledge will not bear fruit for me; and as for your word, so indeed it shall be.

children.text: adhyāpayiṣyāmi ca yaṃ tasya vidyā phaliṣyati ||
children.translated_text: But the knowledge will bear fruit for the one whom I teach.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Having spoken thus to <s>Devayānī</s> at that time, O best of kings,
<s>Kaca</s>, the best of twice-born men, quickly went to the abode of the lord of the thirty gods.
Seeing that he had arrived, the gods, with <s>Indra</s> at their head,
honored <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and, filled with joy, said this to <s>Kaca</s>.
The gods said:
O <s>Kaca</s>, you have done a great and wondrous deed for our welfare.

children.text: na te yaśaḥ praṇaśitā bhāgabhākca bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Your fame will not perish, and you shall be a sharer in the sacrificial portion.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
When learned <s>Kaca</s> had arrived, the dwellers in heaven were delighted in appearance.
Having learned that knowledge from <s>Kaca</s>, they had accomplished their purpose, O bull of the <s>Bharatas</s>.
Then all of them came together and spoke to <s>Śatakratu</s>:
'Now is the time for your prowess; slay your enemies, O <s>Puraṃdara</s>.'
Thus addressed then by those thirty gods, <s>Maghavan</s>
said, 'So be it,' and began; he saw women in the forest.
As the maidens were playing in a grove like <s>Caitraratha</s>,
he became a wind and mixed up all their garments.

children.text: tato jalāt samuttīrya tāḥ kanyāḥ sahitāstadā
children.translated_text: Then those maidens, coming up together out of the water,
took those garments in many ways according to how they lay.

children.text: tatra vāso devayānyāḥ śarmiṣṭhā jagṛhe tadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> took <s>Devayānī</s>'s garment there at that time,
the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s> not realizing that she was doing wrong.
Then a quarrel arose there between the two of them,
between <s>Devayānī</s> and <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, O king, because of that.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: kasmādgṛhṇāsi me vastraṃ śiṣyā bhūtvā mamāsuri
children.translated_text: Why do you take my garment, when you are my pupil, asura girl?
Since you are devoid of proper conduct, no good will come to you.
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:

children.text: āsīnaṃ ca śayānaṃ ca pitā te pitaraṃ mama
children.translated_text: Whether seated or lying down, your father praises my father
and constantly petitions him, standing lower, like one very humble.
And you are the daughter of one who begs, praises, and receives gifts;

children.text: sutāhaṃ stūyamānasya dadato na tu gṛhṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am the daughter of one who is praised and gives, not of one who receives.

children.text: anāyudhā sāyudhāyāḥ kiṃ tvaṃ kupyasi bhikṣuki
children.translated_text: Why are you angry, beggar woman, unarmed against one armed?

children.text: lapsyase pratiyoddhāraṃ na ca tvāṃ gaṇayāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: You will find someone to fight back, but I do not count you at all.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: sā vismayaṃ devayānīṃ gatāṃ saktāṃ ca vāsasi
children.translated_text: As <s>Devayānī</s> was caught in her garment and overcome with astonishment,
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> threw her into a well and then entered her own city.
Thinking, 'She has been killed,' <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, fixed on evil,
went away from that place without looking back, given over to the force of anger.
Then <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, came to that place,
his team weary, his body weary, desiring game and thirsty.

children.text: nāhuṣiḥ prekṣamāṇo hi sa nipāne gatodake
children.translated_text: The descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, looking about, came to a waterless watering-place,

children.text: dadarśa kanyāṃ tāṃ tatra dīptāmagniśikhām iva ||
children.translated_text: and there he saw that maiden, blazing like a tongue of fire.
Seeing that maiden, lovely as an immortal,
the best of kings questioned her after consoling her with very gentle words.
Who are you, beautiful-faced dark girl, with well-polished jeweled earrings?
Why do you ponder so deeply, and why do you sigh in distress?

children.text: kathaṃ ca patitā hy asminkūpe vīruttṛṇāvṛte
children.translated_text: And how have you fallen into this well covered with creepers and grass?

children.text: duhitā caiva kasya tvaṃ vada sarvaṃ sumadhyame ||
children.translated_text: Whose daughter are you? Tell me everything, slender-waisted one.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
He who by his knowledge raises up the daityas slain by the gods,

children.text: tasya śukrasya kanyāhaṃ tvaṃ māṃ nūnaṃ na budhyase ||
children.translated_text: I am the daughter of that <s>Śukra</s>; surely you do not know me.

children.text: eṣa me dakṣiṇo rājan pāṇis tāmranakhāṅguliḥ
children.translated_text: Here is my right hand, O king, with copper-colored nails and fingers.

children.text: samuddhara gṛhītvā māṃ kulīnastvaṃ hi me mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Take it and lift me out; I consider you to be of noble birth.

children.text: jānāmi tvāṃ ca saṃśāntaṃ vīryavantaṃ yaśasvinam
children.translated_text: I know you to be composed, powerful, and famous;
therefore you ought to lift me, fallen as I am, from this well.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: tāmatha brāhmaṇīṃ strīṃ ca vijñāya nahuṣātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, realizing that she was a brahmin woman, the son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>
took her by the right hand and lifted her from the pit.
After the king had quickly drawn her up from that well,
<s>Yayāti</s> took leave of the fair-hipped woman and went to his own city.
But when the descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s> had gone from there, <s>Devayānī</s>, disgraced,
spoke again, scorched by grief, to <s>Ghūrṇikā</s>, who had arrived.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: tvaritaṃ ghūrṇike gaccha sarvamācakṣva me pituḥ
children.translated_text: Go quickly, <s>Ghūrṇikā</s>, and tell my father everything.
I will not now enter the city of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: sā tu vai tvaritaṃ gatvā ghūrṇikāsuramandiram
children.translated_text: She, <s>Ghūrṇikā</s>, went quickly to the mansion of the asuras,
and, seeing <s>Kāvya</s>, said this, trembling and senseless with fear.

children.text: ācakhyau ca mahābhāgā devayānī vane hatā
children.translated_text: The noble woman reported, '<s>Devayānī</s> has been killed in the forest,
O very wise one, by <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.'
When <s>Kāvya</s> heard that his daughter had been killed by <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>,
he went out in haste and sorrow, searching for his daughter in the forest.
Seeing his daughter <s>Devayānī</s> in the ascetic grove, <s>Kāvya</s>
embraced her with both arms and, distressed, spoke these words:
All people obtain sorrow and happiness through their own faults.

children.text: manye duścaritaṃ te 'sti tasyeyaṃ niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: I think some misconduct of yours exists; this expiation has been made for it.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: niṣkṛtir vāstu vā māstu śṛṇuṣvāvahito mama
children.translated_text: Whether it is expiation or not, listen carefully to me,
to what I was told by <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.
Surely this is true, she said: I am the singer of the daityas.

children.text: evaṃ hi me kathayati śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, tells me.
With eyes reddened by anger, she spoke a sharp and harsh word,
'You are the daughter of one who praises, begs, and receives gifts.
I am the daughter of one who is praised and gives, not of one who receives.'
So <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, said to me,
her eyes reddened with anger and her face filled with pride.
If I am, father, the daughter of one who praises and receives gifts,

children.text: prasādayiṣye śarmiṣṭhām ityuktā hi sakhī mayā
children.translated_text: then I will go and appease <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>; that is what I told my friend.
<s>Śukra</s> said:

children.text: stuvato duhitā na tvaṃ bhadre na pratigṛhṇataḥ
children.translated_text: You are not, good lady, the daughter of one who praises or receives gifts.
Rather, <s>Devayānī</s>, you are the daughter of one who is praised.

children.text: vṛṣaparvaiva tadveda śakro rājā ca nāhuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s> himself knows that, as do <s>Śakra</s>, the king, and the descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s>.

children.text: acintyaṃ brahma nirdvaṃdvamaiśvaraṃ hi balaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: Inconceivable, free from duality, and sovereign indeed is my brahmanic power.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
The man who always endures the harsh speeches of others,
know, <s>Devayānī</s>, that by him all this has been conquered.

children.text: yaḥ samutpatitaṃ krodhaṃ nigṛhṇāti hayaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: He who restrains anger when it has arisen, as one restrains a horse,

children.text: sa yantetyucyate sadbhirna yo raśmiṣu lambate ||
children.translated_text: is called a true charioteer by the good, not one who merely hangs on to the reins.
He who restrains anger that has arisen by means of freedom from anger,
know, <s>Devayānī</s>, that by him all this has been conquered.
He who casts off anger by forbearance alone,

children.text: yathoragastvacaṃ jīrṇāṃ sa vai puruṣa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: as a snake casts off its old skin, he indeed is called a man.
But he who cultivates <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), who endures beyond measure...

children.text: yaśca tapto na tapati bhṛśaṃ so 'rthasya bhājanam ||
children.translated_text: And he who, though provoked, does not blaze up in anger is truly a fit recipient of prosperity.

children.text: yo yajedaśvamedhena māsi māsi śataṃ samāḥ
children.translated_text: One man might sacrifice with a horse-sacrifice month after month for a hundred years,
but one who does not become angry at anyone is the better of the two.
Boys and girls who are thoughtless may make enmity,
but a wise person would not do this; they do not know strength and weakness.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: vedāhaṃ tāta bālāpi kāryāṇāṃ tu gatāgatam
children.translated_text: Father, though I am young, I know the coming and going of affairs,
and, in anger or in excessive speech, I know the strength and weakness of the matter.
One who wishes to prosper should not tolerate undisciplined behavior in a pupil.
I take no pleasure in dwelling among those whose conduct is mixed with the wicked.
Those who do not honor a man for his conduct and lineage,
among such evil-minded people a wise person who seeks welfare should not dwell.
Those who recognize him by his conduct and lineage,

children.text: teṣu sādhuṣu vastavyaṃ sa vāsaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate ||
children.translated_text: among such good people one should dwell; that dwelling is called the best.
That word, harshly spoken, churns my heart
like fire in a fire-stick: the very dreadful word of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>'s daughter.

children.text: na hy ato duṣkaraṃ manye tāta lokeṣvapi triṣu
