children.translated_text: For I think nothing more difficult than this, father, even in the three worlds:
that one whose prosperity is low should attend upon the blazing prosperity of a rival.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Then <s>Kāvya</s>, the best of the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, came near in anger
to <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s> as he sat there, and spoke thus without hesitation:

children.text: nādharmaścarito rājan sadyaḥ phalati gaur iva
children.translated_text: Unrighteousness that has been practiced, O king, does not bear fruit at once like a cow.
But slowly turning back upon a man, it cuts away even his roots.

children.text: yadi nātmani putreṣu na cetpaśyati naptṛṣu
children.translated_text: If he does not see the sinful deed in himself or in his sons,
and if not in his grandsons, that deed passes beyond the three aims of life.
Thus sin surely bears fruit, like heavy food in the belly,
when you had the brahmin <s>Kaca</s>, descendant of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, killed.
He was of innocent character, knew <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), and delighted in service in my house.
Because of the killing of him, who did not deserve death, and because of the injury to my daughter,
understand this, <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>: I will abandon you together with your kinsmen.

children.text: sthātuṃ tvadviṣaye rājanna śaknomi tvayā saha ||
children.translated_text: I cannot remain in your realm, O king, together with you.
Today I know you as a <s>Daitya</s> who speaks falsely,
since you disregard your own daughter, swollen with arrogance.
<s>Vṛṣaparvan</s> said:

children.text: nāvadyaṃ na mṛṣāvādaṃ tvayi jānāmi bhārgava
children.translated_text: I know no fault and no falsehood in you, O <s>Bhārgava</s>.

children.text: tvayi satyaṃ ca dharmaśca tatprasīdatu māṃ bhavān ||
children.translated_text: Truth and <s>dharma</s> are in you; therefore let your honor be gracious to me.
If today you abandon us and go away from here, O <s>Bhārgava</s>,
I will enter the ocean; there is no other refuge.
<s>Śukra</s> said:

children.text: samudraṃ praviśadhvaṃ vo diśo vā vrajatāsurāḥ
children.translated_text: Enter the ocean, or go to the quarters, O asuras.

children.text: duhiturnāpriyaṃ soḍhuṃ śakto'haṃ dayitā hi me ||
children.translated_text: I am not able to endure what is displeasing to my daughter, for she is dear to me.

children.text: prasādyatāṃ devayānī jīvitaṃ yatra me sthitam
children.translated_text: Let <s>Devayānī</s> be appeased, for my life rests in her.
I am the maker of your welfare and security, as <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is for <s>Indra</s>.
<s>Vṛṣaparvan</s> said:
Whatever wealth of the asura lords exists, O <s>Bhārgava</s>,

children.text: bhuvi hastirathāśvaṃ vā tasya tvaṃ mama ceśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: on earth, whether elephants, chariots, or horses, you are lord of it and of me.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
Whatever wealth the lords of the <s>Daityas</s> have, O great asura,
I am its lord, if that is so; let <s>Devayānī</s> be appeased.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: tatastu tvaritaḥ śukrastena rājñā samaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śukra</s>, in haste, went together with that king
and said to her, 'Fair one, your word has been accepted.'
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
If you are lord of the king's wealth, father, O <s>Bhārgava</s>,

children.text: nābhijānāmi tatte'haṃ rājā vadatu māṃ svayam ||
children.translated_text: I do not recognize that from you; let the king himself tell me.
<s>Vṛṣaparvan</s> said:
Whatever desire you know to be yours, <s>Devayānī</s> of the bright smile,
I will grant it to you, even if it should be very hard to obtain.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
I desire <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> as my servant, together with a thousand maidens.

children.text: anuyāsyati māṃ tatra yatra dāsyati me pitā ||
children.translated_text: She shall follow me there, wherever my father gives me in marriage.
<s>Vṛṣaparvan</s> said:

children.text: uttiṣṭha dhātri gaccha tvaṃ śarmiṣṭhāṃ śīghramānaya
children.translated_text: Rise, nurse, go and bring <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> quickly.

children.text: yaṃ ca kāmayate kāmaṃ devayānī karotu tam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever desire <s>Devayānī</s> wishes, let her fulfill it here.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: tato dhātrī tatra gatvā śarmiṣṭhām idamabravīt
children.translated_text: Then the nurse went there and said this to <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>:
Rise, noble <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>; bring happiness to your kinsmen.
The brahmin, urged by <s>Devayānī</s>, is abandoning his pupils.

children.text: yaṃ sā kāmayate kāmaṃ sa kāryo'tra tvayānaghe
children.translated_text: Whatever desire she wishes must be done here by you, blameless one.
You have been appointed to servitude for <s>Devayānī</s>, beautiful one.
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:

children.text: yaṃ ca kāmayate kāmaṃ karavāṇyahamadya tam
children.translated_text: Whatever desire she wishes, I will do that today.

children.text: mā gānmanyuvaśaṃ śukro devayānī ca matkṛte ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Devayānī</s> not fall under the power of anger because of me.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Then, surrounded by a thousand maidens and carried in a palanquin,
she quickly went out from the excellent city at her father's command.
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:
I, together with a thousand maidens, am your slave and attendant.

children.text: dhruvaṃ tvāṃ tatra yāsyāmi yatra dāsyati te pitā ||
children.translated_text: Surely I will go with you wherever your father gives you in marriage.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
I am the daughter of one who praises, begs, and receives,
while you are the daughter of one who is praised; how will you become a slave?
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:
By whatever means one may bring happiness to distressed kinsmen,

children.text: anuyāsyāmyahaṃ tatra yatra dāsyati te pitā ||
children.translated_text: by that I will follow you wherever your father gives you in marriage.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
When servitude had been promised by the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>,
<s>Devayānī</s>, O best of kings, spoke these words to her father:
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
I will enter the city, father; I am satisfied, best of twice-born men.

children.text: amoghaṃ tava vijñānamasti vidyābalaṃ ca te ||
children.translated_text: Your knowledge is unfailing, and the power of your science too is real.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
When thus addressed by his daughter, the very renowned best of twice-born men
entered the city joyfully, honored by all the <s>Dānavas</s>.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Then, after a long time, O best of kings, <s>Devayānī</s>,
the beautiful lady, went out to that very forest for sport.
Then, together with that thousand of maidservants and with <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>,

children.text: tameva deśaṃ samprāptā yathākāmaṃ cacāra sā ||
children.translated_text: she reached that same region and roamed about as she pleased.
Accompanied by all those female friends, greatly delighted,
all of them were playing, enjoying themselves, and drinking the honey-wine of spring.
They were eating various foods and various fruits as well.
Then again the king descended from <s>Nahuṣa</s>, seeking game by chance,
came to that same place, very thirsty and desiring water.

children.text: dadarśa devayānīṃ ca śarmiṣṭhāṃ tāśca yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He saw <s>Devayānī</s>, <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, and those women.
He saw those maidens drinking, adorned with divine ornaments,
and he saw fair-smiling <s>Devayānī</s> seated there,
incomparable in beauty among those women, a lovely woman,
being served by <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> with foot-massage and the like.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
Two maidens, surrounded by two thousand maidens,

children.text: gotre ca nāmanī caiva dvayoḥ pṛcchāmyato hy aham ||
children.translated_text: I now ask the lineage and the names of you two.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
I shall tell you; receive my words, O ruler of men.

children.text: śuko nāmāsuraguruḥ sutāṃ jānīhi tasya mām ||
children.translated_text: The guru of the <s>Asuras</s> is named <s>Śukra</s>; know me as his daughter.

children.text: iyaṃ ca me sakhī dāsī yatrāhaṃ tatra gāminī
children.translated_text: And this friend of mine is my maidservant, one who goes wherever I go:
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, lord of the <s>Dānavas</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ tu te sakhī dāsī kanyeyaṃ varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: But how is this beautiful maiden your friend and maidservant,

children.text: asurendrasutā subhūḥ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me ||
children.translated_text: the fair daughter of the lord of the <s>Asuras</s>? This is a great curiosity to me.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
Everything, O tiger among men, follows ordinance.

children.text: vidhinā vihitaṃ jñātvā mā vicitraṃ manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing it as ordained by fate, do not let your mind be astonished.

children.text: rājavadrūpaveṣau te brāhmīṃ vācaṃ bibharṣi ca
children.translated_text: You have the appearance and dress of a king, and you bear Brahminical speech.

children.text: kiṃnāmā tvaṃ kutaścāsi kasya putraśca śaṃsa me ||
children.translated_text: What is your name? From where are you? Whose son are you? Tell me.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: brahmacaryeṇa vedo me kṛtsnaḥ śrutipathaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Through brahmacarya the whole Veda has entered the path of my hearing.
I am a king and a king's son, renowned as <s>Yayāti</s>.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: kena cārthena nṛpate hy enaṃ deśaṃ samāgataḥ
children.translated_text: For what purpose, O king, have you come to this region?
Was it in desire to take some water, or else in search of game?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
I am seeking game, O gracious lady, and I have come here for drinking water.
I have also been questioned in many ways; now you should permit me to depart.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
Together with two thousand maidens and with <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> as my maid,

children.text: tvadadhīnāsmi bhadraṃ te sakhe bhartā ca me bhava ||
children.translated_text: I am under your authority. Welfare to you, friend; be my husband.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: viddhyauśanasi bhadraṃ te na tvadarho 'smi bhāmini
children.translated_text: Know, O daughter of <s>Uśanas</s>, good fortune to you, that I am not worthy of you, fair lady.
We kings are not eligible bridegrooms for your father, O <s>Devayānī</s>.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭaṃ brahmaṇā kṣatraṃ kṣatraṃ brahmaṇi saṃśritam
children.translated_text: Brahmanhood has been joined with kṣatra, and kṣatra rests in brahmanhood.
You are a seer and a seer's son, O descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s>; choose me today.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
All four varṇas, O fair-faced one, arise from one body,

children.text: pṛthagdharmāḥ pṛthakchaucās teṣāṃ vai brāhmaṇo varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but their dharmas and purities are separate; among them the Brahmin is best.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: pāṇigraho nāhuṣāyaṃ na puṃbhiḥ sevitaḥ purā
children.translated_text: This taking of my hand, O descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, was not formerly practiced by men.
You took my hand first; therefore I choose you.

children.text: kathaṃ tu me manasvinyāḥ pāṇimanyaḥ pumānspṛśet
children.translated_text: How could another man touch the hand of me, a self-possessed woman,
when it has been taken by you, a seer's son, or indeed yourself a seer?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
More difficult to assail than an angry venomous serpent,
or than a fire facing everywhere, is a Brahmin for a man who understands.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
How do you say that a Brahmin is more difficult to assail
than a venomous serpent or a fire facing everywhere, O bull among men?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
A venomous serpent bites one person, and one person is killed by a weapon;

children.text: hanti vipraḥ sarāṣṭrāṇi purāṇyapi hi kopitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but an angered Brahmin destroys whole kingdoms, even cities.
Therefore, timid one, a Brahmin is in my view more difficult to assail;

children.text: ato'dattāṃ ca pitrā tvāṃ bhadre na vivahāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: therefore, gracious lady, I will not marry you when you have not been given by your father.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:

children.text: dattāṃ vahasva pitrā māṃ tvaṃ hi rājanvṛto mayā
children.translated_text: Marry me when I have been given by my father; for you, O king, have been chosen by me.

children.text: ayācato bhayaṃ nāsti dattāṃ ca pratigṛhṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no danger for one who does not ask and accepts what has been given.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Then a nurse, quickly sent by <s>Devayānī</s> to her own father,
reported everything to him exactly as it was.

children.text: śrutvaiva ca sa rājānaṃ darśayāmāsa bhārgavaḥ
children.translated_text: As soon as he heard, the <s>Bhārgava</s> showed himself to the king.
Seeing the Brahmin thus arrived, <s>Yayāti</s>, lord of the earth,

children.text: vavande brāhmaṇaṃ kāvyaṃ prāñjaliḥ praṇataḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: bowed to the Brahmin, <s>Kāvya</s>, and stood with folded hands, bent low.
And <s>Kāvya</s> too addressed him gently, in very charming words.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
Father, this king descended from <s>Nahuṣa</s> grasped my hand in a difficult place.

children.text: namaste dehi māmasmai loke nānyaṃ patiṃ vṛṇe ||
children.translated_text: Reverence to you; give me to him. In this world I choose no other husband.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
Hero, you have been chosen as husband by this beloved daughter of mine.
Take her, given by me, as your chief queen, O son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: adharmo māṃ spṛśedevaṃ pāpam asyāśca bhārgava
children.translated_text: May adharma not touch me in this way, nor sin from her, O <s>Bhārgava</s>,
through the mixture of varṇas, O Brahmin; for this I choose you as my recourse.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
I release you from adharma; choose the boon you desire.

children.text: asminvivāhe tvaṃ ślāghyo rahaḥ pāpaṃ nudāmi te ||
children.translated_text: In this marriage you are praiseworthy; I drive away the hidden sin for you.
Take as your wife, in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, <s>Devayānī</s> of pure smile.
Together with her, obtain incomparable affection and delight.

children.text: iyaṃ cāpi kumārī te śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī
children.translated_text: And this maiden too, <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, is in your care.

children.text: saṃpūjyā satataṃ rājanna caināṃ śayane hvaya ||
children.translated_text: She is always to be honored, O king, but do not summon her to your bed.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Thus addressed, <s>Yayāti</s>, having circumambulated <s>Śukra</s>,
went joyfully to his own city, permitted by that great-souled one.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
<s>Yayāti</s>, having reached his own city, which resembled the city of great <s>Indra</s>,
entered the inner apartments there and installed <s>Devayānī</s>.
With <s>Devayānī</s>'s consent, for that daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>
he made a house near the aśoka grove and settled her there.
He settled <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, the daughter of an Asura, surrounded by a thousand maidservants,
well provided and carefully protected, after allotting garments, food, and drink.

children.text: devayānyā tu sahitaḥ sa nṛpo nahuṣātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Devayānī</s>, that king, the son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>,
sported for many years, intensely delighted, like a god.
When her fertile season arrived, <s>Devayānī</s>, the lovely-limbed woman,
first conceived, and a son was born.
When a thousand years had passed, <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>,

children.text: dadarśa yauvanaṃ prāptā ṛtuṃ sā kamalekṣaṇā ||
children.translated_text: lotus-eyed and having attained youth, perceived that her fertile season had come.
The discerning woman, knowing <s>dharma</s>, reflected when her season had arrived:
'My fertile time has come, and no husband has been chosen by me.

children.text: kiṃ prāptaṃ kiṃca kartavyaṃ kathaṃ kṛtvā sukhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: What has happened? What is to be done? By doing what might happiness arise?
<s>Devayānī</s> has given birth, while I have reached youth in vain.

children.text: yathā tayā vṛto bhartā tathaivāhaṃ vṛṇomi tam
children.translated_text: Just as a husband was chosen by her, so I choose him.

children.text: rājñā putraphalaṃ deyam iti me niścitā matiḥ
children.translated_text: The fruit of a son must be given by the king; this is my settled thought.

children.text: apīdānīṃ sa dharmātmā raho me darśanaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Perhaps now that righteous man may come to see me in private.'
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Then that king, coming out at that time by chance,
reached <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> near the aśoka grove and was astonished.
Seeing him alone in private, <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> of charming smile
rose to meet him, made an añjali, and spoke these words to the king.
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:
Whether <s>Soma</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Yama</s>, or <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: tava vā nāhuṣa gṛhe kaḥ striyaṃ draṣṭumarhati ||
children.translated_text: or in your house, O son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, who is fit to look upon a woman?
By my beauty, birth, and character, O king, you always know me.

children.text: sā tvāṃ yāce prasādyeha rantumehi narādhipa ||
children.translated_text: So I entreat you here, having won your favor: come to make love with me, O lord of men.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
I know you, a flawless <s>Daitya</s> maiden, endowed with good character.

children.text: rūpaṃ tu te na paśyāmi sūcyagramapi ninditam ||
children.translated_text: And I do not see in your beauty even a needle-point of anything blameworthy.
But <s>Śukra</s> told me then, when I married <s>Devayānī</s>:
'This daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s> must not be summoned by you to the bed.'
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:

children.text: na narmayuktaṃ vacanaṃ hinasti na strīṣu rājan na vivāhakāle
children.translated_text: A word joined with jest does not harm, O king, nor one spoken among women, nor at the time of marriage.
At the risk of life or the loss of all wealth, they say five falsehoods are not sinful.

children.text: pṛṣṭāstu sākṣye pravadanti cānyathā bhavanti mithyāvacanā narendra te
children.translated_text: But when questioned as witnesses, people speak otherwise; they become speakers of falsehood, O lord of men.

children.text: ekārthatāyāṃ tu samāhitāyāṃ mithyā vadantaṃ hy anṛtaṃ hinasti ||
children.translated_text: When one purpose has been firmly established, falsehood indeed harms the person who speaks falsely.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: rājā pramāṇaṃ bhūtānāṃ sa vinaśyenmṛṣā vadan
children.translated_text: A king is the standard for living beings; he would perish if he spoke falsely.
Even if I come into difficulty over wealth, I cannot bring myself to falsehood.
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:

children.text: samāv etau matau rājanpatiḥ sakhyāśca yaḥ patiḥ
children.translated_text: These two are regarded as equal, O king: a husband and the husband of one's friend.

children.text: samaṃ vivāha ityāhuḥ sakhyā me 'si patiryataḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say marriage is shared, since you are the husband of my friend.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
'A gift must be given to one who asks': this has been laid down as my vow.

children.text: tvaṃ ca yācasi kāmaṃ māṃ brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi tat ||
children.translated_text: And you ask me, out of desire; tell me what I should do in this matter.
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:

children.text: adharmāttrāhi māṃ rājan dharmaṃ ca pratipādaya
children.translated_text: Protect me from <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), O king, and establish <s>dharma</s>.
Having offspring from you, I would practice the highest <s>dharma</s> in the world.

children.text: traya evādhanā rājan bhāryā dāsastathā sutaḥ
children.translated_text: Only three are without property, O king: a wife, a slave, and likewise a son.

children.text: yatte samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya taddhanam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever they acquire is the wealth of the one to whom they belong.

children.text: devayānyā bhujiṣyāsmi vaśyā ca tava bhārgavī
children.translated_text: I am <s>Devayānī</s>'s servant, and that <s>Bhārgavī</s> is subject to you.

children.text: sā cāhaṃ ca tvayā rājan bharaṇīyāṃ bhajasva mām ||
children.translated_text: She and I are both to be maintained by you, O king; therefore consort with me.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Thus addressed by her, the king acknowledged, 'This is true.'
He honored <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> and established <s>dharma</s>.
Having united with <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> and obtained what he desired,
and having honored one another, the two went back as they had come.
In that union, the fair-browed <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>,
first conceived from that best of kings.

children.text: prajajñe ca tataḥ kāle rājñī rājīvalocanā
children.translated_text: Then in due time the lotus-eyed queen gave birth
to a prince like a child of the gods, equal to the sun in splendor.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: śrutvā kumāraṃ jātaṃ sā devayānī śucismitā
children.translated_text: Hearing that a boy had been born, <s>Devayānī</s> of pure smile
became filled with anxious thought and afflicted by sorrow concerning <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, O <s>Bhārata</s>.
Then, approaching <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, <s>Devayānī</s> said this:

children.text: kimarthaṃ vṛjinaṃ subhrūḥ kṛtaṃ te kāmalubdhayā ||
children.translated_text: 'For what reason, fair-browed one, have you, greedy for desire, done this wrong?'
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:
A certain righteous seer, one who had gone beyond the Veda, came to me as a guest.

children.text: sa mayā tu varaḥ kāmaṃ yācito dharmasaṃhatam ||
children.translated_text: From him I asked for the boon I desired, one joined with <s>dharma</s>.
I do not practice desire unlawfully, O pure-smiling one.

children.text: tasmād ṛṣer mamāpatyamiti satyaṃ bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: My offspring is from that seer; I tell you the truth.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
If this is so, <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, then no anger of mine exists

children.text: apatyaṃ yadi te labdhaṃ jyeṣṭhācchreṣṭhācca vai dvijāt ||
children.translated_text: if you have obtained offspring from a twice-born man who is elder and superior.

children.text: śobhanaṃ bhīru satyaṃ cetkathaṃ sa jñāyate dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Beautiful timid one, if this is true, how is that twice-born man to be known?
I wish to hear of that twice-born man by his gotra, name, and family.
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:

children.text: ojasā tejasā caiva dīpyamānaṃ raviṃ yathā
children.translated_text: He was blazing with vigor and splendor, like the sun.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mama saṃpraṣṭuṃ śaktir nāsīcchucismite ||
children.translated_text: When I saw him, bright-smiling one, I had no power to question him.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: anyonyamevam uktvā ca samprahasya ca te mithaḥ
children.translated_text: After speaking thus to one another and laughing together among themselves,
the <s>Bhārgavī</s> went home, understanding, 'It is true.'
King <s>Yayāti</s> begot two sons on <s>Devayānī</s>, O king,

children.text: yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva śakraviṣṇū ivāparau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Turvasu</s>, like another <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
From that very royal sage, <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>,

children.text: druhyaṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca trīnkumārānajījanat ||
children.translated_text: gave birth to three boys: <s>Druhya</s>, <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Pūru</s>.
Then, at a certain time, <s>Devayānī</s> of the bright smile,
together with <s>Yayāti</s>, O king, went to a green forest.
There she then saw boys like gods,
playing freely; astonished, she said this:
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
Whose children are these, O king, handsome and like sons of gods?
In brilliance and in appearance they seem to be like you.
Having questioned the king in this way, she asked the boys in turn,

children.text: kiṃ nāmadheyagotre vaḥ putrakā brāhmaṇaḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: What are your names and gotras, children? Is your father a brahmin?

children.text: vibrūta me yathātathyaṃ śrotukāmāsmyato hy aham
children.translated_text: Tell me exactly, for I desire to hear about this.
They pointed with their forefingers to that very best of kings,

children.text: śarmiṣṭhāṃ mātaraṃ caiva tasyā ūcuḥ kumārakāḥ
children.translated_text: and the boys also said that <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> was their mother.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Having said this, they all approached the king together with him.
The king did not welcome them then in <s>Devayānī</s>'s presence.
Then the children, weeping, went to <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ tu bālānāṃ praṇayaṃ pārthivaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Seeing the affection of those children toward the king,
and understanding the matter truly, the lady said this to <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>:
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
While you were subject to me, why did you do what was displeasing to me?
Have you taken up that very conduct of the asuras, and are you not afraid?
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> said:
What was said, that he was a seer, was true, lovely-smiling one.

children.text: nyāyato dharmataścaiva carantī na bibhemi te ||
children.translated_text: Acting according to justice and <s>dharma</s> (right conduct), I do not fear you.

children.text: yadā tvayā vṛto rājā vṛta eva tadā mayā
children.translated_text: When the king was chosen by you, he was at that very time chosen by me as well.

children.text: sakhībhartā hi dharmeṇa bhartā bhavati śobhane ||
children.translated_text: For according to <s>dharma</s>, beautiful one, a friend's husband becomes a husband.

children.text: pūjyāsi mama mānyā ca śreṣṭhā jyeṣṭhā ca brāhmaṇī
children.translated_text: You are venerable to me, worthy of honor, superior and elder, a brahmin woman.

children.text: tvatto hi me pūjyataro rājarṣiḥ kiṃ na vetsi tat ||
children.translated_text: Yet this royal sage is more venerable to me than you; do you not know that?
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
After hearing her words, <s>Devayānī</s> then said this:

children.text: rājannādyeha vatsyāmi vipriyaṃ me tvayā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: O king, I will not live here today; what you have done is displeasing to me.
Seeing that dark woman suddenly spring up, her eyes filled with tears,
and set out quickly for <s>Kāvya</s>'s presence, he was distressed then.
The king, alarmed, followed behind her, consoling her,
but she, her eyes reddened with anger, did not turn back.
Speaking nothing to the king, with tearful eyes,
she very soon arrived near <s>Kāvya</s> <s>Uśanas</s>.
As soon as she saw her father, she bowed and stood before him.
Afterward <s>Yayāti</s> worshiped the <s>Bhārgava</s>.
<s>Devayānī</s> said:
<s>Dharma</s> has been conquered by <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness); the inferior has taken precedence over the superior.
<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, has transgressed the proper bounds.
Three sons have been begotten in her by this king <s>Yayāti</s>,

children.text: durbhagāyā mama dvau tu putrau tāta bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: while only two sons have been born to unlucky me, father; this I tell you.

children.text: dharmajña iti vikhyāta eṣa rājā bhṛgūdvaha
children.translated_text: This king is renowned as a knower of <s>dharma</s>, O scion of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
but he has overstepped the limit, O <s>Kāvya</s>; I tell you this.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
Though you know <s>dharma</s>, great king, you have committed <s>adharma</s> for pleasure.
Therefore unconquerable old age will soon overpower you.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: ṛtuṃ yo yācyamānāyā na dadāti pumānvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The chosen man who does not grant the fertile season to a woman asking for it,
is called a killer of embryos here by those who speak of <s>brahman</s>, O brahmin.

children.text: ṛtukāmāṃ striyaṃ yastu gamyāṃ rahasi yācitaḥ
children.translated_text: And he who, when asked in private, does not approach according to <s>dharma</s>

children.text: nopaiti yo hi dharmeṇa brahmahetyucyate budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: a woman fit to be approached and desiring her fertile season, is called a killer of a brahmin by the wise.
Considering these reasons, O scion of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
I approached <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, distressed by fear of <s>adharma</s>.
<s>Śukra</s> said:

children.text: na tv ahaṃ pratyavekṣyaste madadhīno'si pārthiva
children.translated_text: You should not have disregarded me; you are dependent on me, O king.
False conduct in matters of <s>dharma</s> is theft, O son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Cursed in anger by <s>Uśanas</s>, <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, then
gave up his former age and immediately entered into old age.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
I have not had my fill of youth with <s>Devayānī</s>, O scion of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: prasādaṃ kuru me brahmañjareyaṃ mā viśeta mām ||
children.translated_text: Grant me favor, O brahmin; may this old age not enter me.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
I do not speak falsely in this: you have reached old age, O lord of the earth.
But transfer this old age to another, if you wish.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
Let that son who gives me his youth have a share in the kingdom, O brahmin,
and also a share in merit and fame; may you approve this.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
You may transfer your old age as you wish, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>,
while keeping me truly in mind, and you will incur no sin.

children.text: vayo dāsyati te putro yaḥ sa rājā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: The son who gives you his youth will become king,
and he will be long-lived, famous, and have many descendants as well.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: jarāṃ prāpya yayātistu svapuraṃ prāpya caiva hi
children.translated_text: Having reached old age, and indeed having come to his own city,
he spoke to his eldest and best son, <s>Yadu</s>, O twice-born one.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: jarā valī ca māṃ tāta palitāni ca paryaguḥ
children.translated_text: Old age, wrinkles, and gray hairs have overtaken me, dear son,
because of the curse of <s>Kāvya Uśanas</s>, and I am not yet satisfied with youth.

children.text: tvaṃ yado pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha
children.translated_text: You, <s>Yadu</s>, take on the affliction together with old age;
with your youth I would enjoy the sense-objects.

children.text: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu tvadīyaṃ yauvanaṃ tv aham
children.translated_text: But when a thousand years are complete, I
will give back your youth and take on the affliction together with old age.
<s>Yadu</s> said:
Bearing a white beard, wretched, loosened by old age,
with limbs covered in wrinkles, ugly, weak, and thin,
unable to carry out duties, he is despised by young people
and also by those who live with him; I do not desire that old age.

children.text: santi te bahavaḥ putrā mattaḥ priyatarā nṛpa
children.translated_text: You have many sons dearer than I, O king;

children.text: jarāṃ grahītuṃ dharmajña putramanyaṃ vṛṇīṣva vai ||
children.translated_text: choose another son to take old age, O knower of dharma.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: yastvaṃ me hṛdayājjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi
children.translated_text: Since you, born from my heart, do not give your own age,
through sinful maternal connections your offspring will be wicked.
<s>Turvasu</s>, take on the affliction together with old age;
with your youth, my son, I would enjoy the sense-objects.
When a thousand years are complete, then I will return your youth,
and likewise I will take on the affliction together with old age.
<s>Turvasu</s> said:
I do not desire old age, father, which destroys enjoyments of desire,
which brings an end to strength and beauty and destroys intelligence and honor.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: yastvaṃ me hṛdayājjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi
children.translated_text: Since you, born from my heart, do not give your own age,
therefore your progeny, <s>Turvasu</s>, will go to extinction.
Confused, among those whose dharmas are thieving and who follow inverse practices,
among flesh-eating peoples, surely you will be king.
Among those attached to their elders' wives and delighting in animal wombs,
among sinful mlecchas who follow the conduct of beasts, you will have power.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ sa turvasuṃ śaptvā yayātiḥ sutamātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus cursed <s>Turvasu</s>, his own son, <s>Yayāti</s>
spoke these words to <s>Druhyu</s>, the eldest son of <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
<s>Druhyu</s>, take on old age, the destroyer of color and form,

children.text: jarāṃ varṣasahasraṃ me yauvanaṃ svaṃ prayacchatām ||
children.translated_text: for me for a thousand years, and give me your own youth.

children.text: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu te pradāsyāmi yauvanam
children.translated_text: When a thousand years are complete, I will give you your youth,

children.text: svaṃ cādāsyāmi bhūyo 'haṃ pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha ||
children.translated_text: and again I will take back my own affliction together with old age.
<s>Druhyu</s> said:

children.text: na rājyaṃ na rathaṃ nāśvaṃ jīrṇo bhuṅkte na ca striyam
children.translated_text: When old, one enjoys neither kingdom nor chariot nor horse, nor a woman;

children.text: na rāgaścāsya bhavati tajjarāṃ te na kāmaye ||
children.translated_text: nor does he have passion. I do not desire that old age of yours.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: yastvaṃ me hṛdayājjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi
children.translated_text: Since you, born from my heart, do not give your own age,

children.text: taddruhyo vai priyaḥ kāmo na te sampatsyate kvacit ||
children.translated_text: then, <s>Druhyu</s>, your dear desire shall never succeed for you.
Where travel will always be by boat over flooded waters,
there, together with your lineage, you will receive the designation of one who enjoys no kingdom.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: ano tvaṃ pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha
children.translated_text: <s>Anu</s>, take on the affliction together with old age;

children.text: ekaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu careyaṃ yauvanena te ||
children.translated_text: with your youth I would enjoy for one thousand years.
<s>Anu</s> said:
An old man takes food at the wrong time like a child, and is as if impure;

children.text: na juhoti ca kāle'gniṃ tāṃ jarāṃ nābhikāmaye ||
children.translated_text: and at the proper time he does not offer into the fire. I do not desire that old age.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: yastvaṃ me hṛdayājjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi
children.translated_text: Since you, born from my heart, do not give your own age,
because you have described the fault of old age, therefore you yourself shall take it on.

children.text: prajāśca yauvanaṃ prāptā vinaśyanti hy ano tava
children.translated_text: And your offspring, having attained youth, shall perish, O <s>Anu</s>;
and you too will become one who has lapsed in regard to the fire-offering.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: pūro tvaṃ pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha
children.translated_text: <s>Pūru</s>, take on the affliction together with old age;

children.text: tvaṃ me priyataraḥ putrastvaṃ varīyān bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: you are my dearer son; you will be the greater one.

children.text: jarā valī ca māṃ tāta palitāni ca paryaguḥ
children.translated_text: Old age, wrinkles, and gray hairs have overtaken me, dear son,
because of the curse of <s>Kāvya Uśanas</s>, and I am not yet satisfied with youth.
For a little while I would enjoy the sense-objects by means of your age.
But when a thousand years are complete, I will give back your youth,

children.text: svaṃ caiva pratipatsye'haṃ pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha ||
children.translated_text: and I will take back my own affliction together with old age.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Thus addressed, <s>Pūru</s> answered his father directly:

children.text: yathāttha tvaṃ mahārāja tatkariṣyāmi te vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As you say, great king, I will do that word of yours.
I will take on your affliction together with old age, O king;
take youth from me and enjoy pleasures as you wish.
Covered by old age, bearing your age and form,
having given youth to you, I will live as I choose.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: pūro prīto'smi te vatsa varaṃ cemaṃ dadāmi te
children.translated_text: <s>Pūru</s>, I am pleased with you, child, and I give you this boon:
your progeny shall have its purposes fulfilled with every desire.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: evamuktaḥ sa rājarṣiḥ kāvyaṃ smṛtvā mahāvratam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that royal seer, remembering <s>Kāvya</s>, the great-vowed one,
then transferred old age into that noble son.
Then with the age of the <s>Paurava</s>, <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>,
filled with delight, best of men, enjoyed the beloved sense-objects.
According to desire, according to energy, according to the time, and according to happiness,
that king of kings enjoyed only those things not opposed to dharma, as was proper.
He satisfied the gods with sacrifices, and the ancestors also with śrāddhas;
the distressed with favors, and the best twice-born men with desired gifts;
and guests with food and drink, and the common people by protection.
with compassion toward the Śūdras and with restraint of bandits,

children.text: dharmeṇa ca prajāḥ sarvā yathāvad anurañjayan
children.translated_text: and delighting all his subjects properly by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
<s>Yayāti</s> protected them like another <s>Indra</s> in person.
That king, advancing like a lion, young and moving within the range of the senses,
enjoyed the highest happiness without opposing <s>dharma</s>.
Having obtained auspicious pleasures, the earthly king became satisfied and weary,
and, at the end of a thousand years, the lord of men remembered the time.
Considering the time, and knowing its divisions into <s>kalā</s>s and <s>kāṣṭhā</s>s, the mighty one,

children.text: pūrṇam matvā tataḥ kālaṃ pūruṃ putramuvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: then thinking that the time was complete, spoke to his son <s>Pūru</s>.
Desire is never appeased by the enjoyment of desired objects;
like a fire's dark path by oblations, it only grows still more.
Whatever rice and barley, gold, cattle, and women there are on earth,
all that is not enough for one man; thinking thus, one should go to tranquility.
According to my pleasure, according to my energy, and according to my desire, O subduer of foes,

children.text: sevitā viṣayāḥ putra yauvanena mayā tava ||
children.translated_text: I have enjoyed sense-objects, my son, by means of your youth.

children.text: pūro prīto'smi bhadraṃ te gṛhāṇedaṃ svayauvanam
children.translated_text: O <s>Pūru</s>, I am pleased; welfare to you. Take back this youth of your own,

children.text: rājyaṃ caiva gṛhāṇedaṃ tvaṃ hi me priyakṛtsutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and take this kingdom as well, for you, my son, have done what is dear to me.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Then King <s>Yayāti</s>, descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, accepted old age,

children.text: yauvanaṃ pratipede sa pūruḥ svaṃ punarātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Pūru</s> again received his own youth for himself.

children.text: abhiṣektukāmaṃ ca nṛpaṃ pūruṃ putraṃ kanīyasam
children.translated_text: When the king wished to consecrate <s>Pūru</s>, his youngest son,
the social classes, headed by the Brahmins, spoke these words.

children.text: kathaṃ śukrasya dauhitraṃ devayānyāḥ sutaṃ prabho
children.translated_text: How, lord, will you pass over <s>Yadu</s>, the eldest, the grandson of <s>Śukra</s> and son of <s>Devayānī</s>,
and give the kingdom to <s>Pūru</s>?
Your eldest son is <s>Yadu</s>, and after him is <s>Turvasu</s>;

children.text: śarmiṣṭhāyāḥ suto druhyus tathānuḥ pūrureva ca ||
children.translated_text: the sons of <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> are <s>Druhyu</s>, then <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Pūru</s> too.
How can the younger deserve the kingdom when the eldest has been passed over?
We remind you of this; observe your own <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: brāhmaṇapramukhā varṇāḥ sarve śṛṇvantu me vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Let all the social classes headed by the Brahmins hear my word:

children.text: jyeṣṭhaṃ prati yato rājyaṃ na deyaṃ me kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: for my part, the kingdom is not to be given to the eldest in any way.
My command was not obeyed by my eldest, <s>Yadu</s>;

children.text: pratikūlaḥ pituryaśca na sa putraḥ satāṃ mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and one who is hostile to his father is not regarded by good people as a son.
A son who acts according to the words of his mother and father, who is beneficial and wholesome,
that one is truly a son, and he behaves as a son should toward father and mother.
I was despised by <s>Yadu</s>, and likewise by <s>Turvasu</s>;
by <s>Druhyu</s> and by <s>Anu</s> too such contempt was shown me greatly.

children.text: pūruṇā me kṛtaṃ vākyaṃ mānitaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: But my word was carried out by <s>Pūru</s>, and especially honored,

children.text: kanīyānmama dāyādo jarā yena dhṛtā mama ||
children.translated_text: the younger son who is my heir, by whom my old age was borne.

children.text: mama kāmaḥ sa ca kṛtaḥ pūruṇā putrarūpiṇā
children.translated_text: My desire was fulfilled by <s>Pūru</s>, who has the true form of a son;

children.text: śukreṇa ca varo dattaḥ kāvyenośanasā svayam ||
children.translated_text: and a boon was given by <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Kāvya</s> <s>Uśanas</s> himself:
'The son who follows you shall be king, lord of the earth.'
Let you all acknowledge this: let <s>Pūru</s> be consecrated in the kingdom.
The subjects said:
The son who is endowed with virtues and is always beneficial to mother and father,

children.text: sarvaṃ so 'rhati kalyāṇaṃ kanīyānapi sa prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: he deserves every good fortune; even if younger, he is the lord.

children.text: arhaṃ pūroridaṃ rājyaṃ yaḥ priyaḥ priyakṛt tava
children.translated_text: This kingdom is fitting for <s>Pūru</s>, who is dear to you and does what is dear to you;
because of the boon given by <s>Śukra</s>, no reply can be made.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Thus addressed then by the delighted citizens and country people, the descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s>,
after consecrating <s>Pūru</s>, his own son, in the kingdom,

children.text: dattvā ca pūrave rājyaṃ vanavāsāya dīkṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: and after giving the kingdom to <s>Pūru</s>, was initiated for forest-dwelling;
the king went forth from the city together with Brahmins and ascetics.
From <s>Yadu</s> were born the <s>Yādava</s>s, and from <s>Turvasu</s> the <s>Yavana</s>s as sons;
from <s>Druhyu</s> came the <s>Bhoja</s>s, and from <s>Anu</s> the peoples of the Mlecchas.

children.text: pūrostu pauravo vaṃśo yatra jāto'si pārthiva
children.translated_text: From <s>Pūru</s> came the <s>Paurava</s> lineage, in which you were born, O king;
and after a thousand years this kingdom came down to the family of <s>Kuru</s>.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ sa nāhuṣo rājā yayātiḥ putramīpsitam
children.translated_text: In this way King <s>Yayāti</s>, descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, having obtained the son he desired,
joyfully consecrated him in the kingdom and became a forest-dwelling sage.

children.text: uṣitvā vanavāsaṃ sa brāhmaṇaiḥ saha saṃśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Having lived in the forest-dwelling life, sheltered together with Brahmins,
self-controlled and feeding on fruits and roots, he went from here to heaven as was proper.

children.text: sa gataḥ svargavāsaṃ tu nyavasanmuditaḥ sukhī
children.translated_text: Having gone to a dwelling in heaven, he lived there joyful and happy,
but after no very long time he was cast down again by <s>Śakra</s>.
Helpless, fallen from heaven and not yet reaching the earth,

children.text: sthitaścāsīd antarikṣe sa tadeti śrutaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: he remained standing in midair; so I have heard.

children.text: tata eva punaścāpi gataḥ svargamiti śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: From there again he went back to heaven, so tradition says,
together with King <s>Vasumat</s> and with the mighty <s>Aṣṭaka</s>,
and after meeting, it is said, with <s>Pratardana</s> and <s>Śibi</s> in an assembly.
<s>Śatānīka</s> said:

children.text: karmaṇā kena sa divaṃ punaḥ prāpto mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: By what deed did that lord of the earth reach heaven again?
And how, venerable one, was he cast down to the earth by <s>Indra</s>?
I wish to hear all this in full, truly,
as it is being told by you, O Brahmin, in the presence of the hosts of divine seers.
For <s>Yayāti</s>, lord of the earth, was equal to the king of the gods,
the increaser of the <s>Kuru</s> lineage, with a brilliance like fire.
Of that great-souled one, whose fame was broad and whose renown was truthful,

children.text: śrotumicchāmi deveśa divi ceha ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear everything, O lord of gods, both in heaven and here.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Come then, I shall tell you the excellent story of <s>Yayāti</s>,
holy in its meaning both in heaven and here, and destructive of all sins.
King <s>Yayāti</s>, descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, after consecrating <s>Pūru</s>, his youngest son,
joyfully in the kingdom, went forth then to the forest.
Having installed his sons, with <s>Yadu</s> foremost, in the border regions,
that king, living on fruits and roots, dwelt for a long time in the forest.
Having conquered himself and conquered anger, satisfying the ancestors and the deities,
and offering oblations into the fires according to rule, in accordance with the ordinance for forest-dwellers,
continually honoring guests with forest-grown sacrificial food, the powerful one,
adopted the livelihood of gleaning and made his meal from the remaining food.
For a full thousand years, O king, such was his conduct.
And for three years he remained eating only water, with speech and mind restrained.
Then he became one who lived on air, tireless for a year;
and amid the five fires he again practiced austerity for a year.
He also stood on one foot for six months, subsisting on wind.
Then, of holy fame, he went to heaven, filling heaven and earth.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
When that best of kings had gone to heaven, he dwelt in the abode of the gods,
honored by the thirty gods, by the <s>Sādhyas</s>, and likewise by the <s>Maruts</s> and <s>Vasus</s>.
Passing from the world of the gods to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, that virtuous, self-mastered one
lived for a long time, the protector of the earth; so tradition says.
Once that best of kings, <s>Yayāti</s>, came to <s>Śakra</s>;

children.text: kathānte tatra śakreṇa pṛṣṭaḥ sa pṛthivīpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the end of a conversation there, that lord of the earth was asked by <s>Śakra</s>.
<s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: yadā sa pūrustava rūpeṇa rājañjarāṃ gṛhītvā pracacāra loke
children.translated_text: When <s>Pūru</s>, in your form, O king, took on old age and moved about in the world,

children.text: tadā rājyaṃ sampradāyaiva tasmai tvayā kimuktaḥ kathayeha satyam ||
children.translated_text: then, after handing the kingdom over to him, what was said by you? Tell the truth here.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
With the subjects' consent, having placed <s>Pūru</s> in the kingdom, I said this:
Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>, this whole realm is yours;
in the middle of the earth you are king, while your brothers are lords on the frontiers.

children.text: akrodhanaḥ krodhanebhyo viśiṣṭastathā titikṣur atitikṣor viśiṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: One free from anger is superior to the angry, and the patient man is likewise superior to the impatient.
A human being is chief among non-human beings, and in the same way the learned man is chief over the unlearned.
When reviled, one should not revile in return; one should endure anger itself.
He burns the reviler and obtains that person's merit.

children.text: nāruntudaḥ syānna nṛśaṃsavādī na hīnataḥ param abhyādadīta
children.translated_text: One should not wound another's vitals, nor speak cruel words, nor attack another as inferior.

children.text: yayāsya vācā para udvijeta na tāṃ vadedruśatīṃ pāpalaulyām ||
children.translated_text: One should not utter that harsh, sinful, greedy speech by which another person would be disturbed.

children.text: aruntudaṃ puruṣaṃ tīvravācaṃ vākkaṇṭakair vitudantaṃ manuṣyān
children.translated_text: A person who wounds the vitals, harsh in speech, piercing people with the thorns of words,

children.text: vidyād alakṣmīkatamaṃ janānāṃ mukhe nibaddhaṃ nirṛtiṃ vahantam ||
children.translated_text: should be known as the most unfortunate of people, carrying ruin bound in his mouth.

children.text: sadbhiḥ purastādabhipūjitaḥ syātsadbhistathā pṛṣṭhato rakṣitaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: One should be honored by the good in front and protected by the good from behind;

children.text: sadā satām ativādāṃstitikṣet satāṃ vṛttaṃ pālayansādhuvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should always endure the reproaches of the good, guarding the conduct of the good and being virtuous in conduct.

children.text: vāksāyakā vadanānniṣpatanti yair āhataḥ śocati vā tryahāni
children.translated_text: Verbal arrows fly from the mouth; struck by them, a person grieves for three days.

children.text: parasya no marmasu te patanti tānpaṇḍito nāvasṛjetpareṣu ||
children.translated_text: They fall upon another's vital points; a wise man should not release them against others.
There is no such means of winning people over anywhere in the three worlds

children.text: yathā maitrī ca lokeṣu dānaṃ ca madhurā ca vāk
children.translated_text: as friendship among people, giving, and sweet speech.

children.text: tasmātsāntvaṃ sadā vācyaṃ na vācyaṃ paruṣaṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: Therefore conciliatory speech should always be spoken; harsh speech should never be spoken.
One should fully honor those worthy of honor, should give, and should never curse.
<s>Indra</s> said:

children.text: sarvāṇi kāryāṇi samāpya rājan gṛhānparityajya vanaṃ gato'si
children.translated_text: Having completed all duties, O king, you abandoned your homes and went to the forest.

children.text: tattvāṃ pṛcchāmi nahuṣasya putra kenāpi tulyastapasā yayāte ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I ask you, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>: with whom are you equal in austerity, <s>Yayāti</s>?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
Among gods and human beings, nor among <s>Gandharvas</s> and great seers,
I do not see anyone equal to myself in austerity, O <s>Vāsava</s>.
<s>Indra</s> said:
Since, unaware of their power, you slighted those equal to you, those superior, and those inferior,

children.text: tasmāllokā hy antavantastaveme kṣīṇe puṇye patito'syadya rājan ||
children.translated_text: therefore these worlds of yours are finite; when your merit is exhausted, you have fallen today, O king.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
If my worlds of <s>Śakra</s> have come to an end because of contempt for gods, seers, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and men,

children.text: icchāmyahaṃ suralokādvihīnaḥ satāṃ madhye patituṃ devarāja ||
children.translated_text: then, bereft of the world of the gods, I wish to fall among the good, O king of gods.
<s>Indra</s> said:

children.text: satāṃ sakāśe patito'si rājaṃścyutaḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ yatra labdhāsi bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: You have fallen near the good, O king; having fallen there, you will again gain a foothold.

children.text: evaṃ viditvā tu punaryayāte na te 'vamānyāḥ sadṛśaḥ śreyase ca ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, <s>Yayāti</s>, henceforth those equal to you and those superior to you must not be slighted by you.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Then from the holy world enjoyed by the king of the immortals fell <s>Yayāti</s>; as he was falling,
seeing him, the best royal seer <s>Aṣṭaka</s>, guardian of the ordinances of true <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), spoke to him.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: kastvaṃ yuvā vāsavatulyarūpaḥ svatejasā dīpyamāno yathāgniḥ
children.translated_text: Who are you, young, with a form like <s>Vāsava</s>, blazing with your own splendor like fire,
falling with the brilliance of a great rain cloud, foremost among sky-goers in the sky like the sun?
Seeing you falling from the path of the sun, immeasurable in radiance like <s>Vaiśvānara</s> and the sun,

children.text: kiṃnusvid etat patatīva sarve vitarkayantaḥ parimohitāḥ smaḥ ||
children.translated_text: we are all bewildered, wondering, 'What indeed is this that seems to be falling?'
And seeing you established on the path of the gods, with majesty resembling <s>Śakra</s>, the sun, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: pratyudgatāstvāṃ vayamadya sarve tasmātpāte tava jijñāsamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: we all have come forward to meet you today, wishing to know the cause of your fall.

children.text: na cāpi tvāṃ dhṛṣṇavaḥ praṣṭumagre na ca tvamasmānpṛcchasi ke vayaṃ sma
children.translated_text: Yet we are not bold enough to question you first, and you do not ask us who we are.

children.text: tattvāṃ pṛcchāmi spṛhaṇīyarūpaṃ kasya tvaṃ vā kiṃnimittaṃ tvamāgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I ask you, desirable in form: whose are you, or for what reason have you come?

children.text: bhayaṃ tu te vyetu viṣādamohau tyajāśu devendrasamānarūpa
children.translated_text: Let your fear depart, and quickly abandon despondency and delusion, you whose form is like the lord of gods.

children.text: tvāṃ vartamānaṃ hi satāṃ sakāśe śakro na soḍhuṃ balahāpi śaktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For while you are present near the good, even <s>Śakra</s>, the slayer of <s>Bala</s>, is not able to withstand you.

children.text: santaḥ pratiṣṭhā hi sukhacyutānāṃ satāṃ sadaivāmararājakalpa
children.translated_text: The good are the foundation for those fallen from happiness; the good are always like the king of the immortals.

children.text: te saṃgatāḥ sthāvarajaṅgameśāḥ pratiṣṭhitastvaṃ sadṛśeṣu satsu ||
children.translated_text: Those lords of what is stationary and moving have gathered together; you are established among good people who are your equals.
Fire is lord in burning; earth is lord in receiving what is sown.

children.text: prabhuḥ sūryaḥ prakāśācca satāṃ cābhyāgataḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sun is lord because of illumination, and among good people an arriving guest is lord.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: ahaṃ yayātirnahuṣasya putraḥ pūroḥ pitā sarvabhūtāvamānāt
children.translated_text: I am <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, father of <s>Pūru</s>; because I showed contempt for all beings,
I have fallen from the world of gods and siddhas. Cast down, with little merit, I am falling.

children.text: ahaṃ hi pūrvo vayasā bhavadbhayastenābhivādaṃ bhavatāṃ na yuñje
children.translated_text: For I am older than you in age; therefore I do not properly offer reverence to you.

children.text: yo vidyayā tapasā janmanā vā vṛddhaḥ sa vai sambhavati dvijānām ||
children.translated_text: Among twice-born men, he who is elder through learning, ascetic practice, or birth is truly considered elder.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: avādīstvaṃ vayasāsmi pravṛddha iti vai rājann adhikaḥ kathaṃcit
children.translated_text: You said, 'I am advanced in age'; but, O king, how is one superior in any way merely by that?

children.text: yo vai vidvāṃstapasā sampravṛddhaḥ sa eva pūjyo bhavati dvijānām ||
children.translated_text: He who has truly grown through knowledge and ascetic practice is the one who deserves honor among twice-born men.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
They say that what is contrary to right actions is sin, and that the sinful world slopes downward for those who follow it.

children.text: santo'sato nānvavartanta te vai yadātmanaiṣāṃ pratikūlavādī ||
children.translated_text: The good do not follow the bad, since the bad man is, by his own nature, one who speaks against them.

children.text: abhūddhanaṃ me vipulaṃ mahadvai viceṣṭamāno'dhigantā tadasmi
children.translated_text: Great and abundant wealth once belonged to me; by striving, I became one who obtained it.

children.text: evaṃ pradhāryātmahite niviṣṭo yo vartate sa vijānāti dhīraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having thus made a firm judgment, the wise man who is intent on his own welfare understands.
In the world of living beings there are many different states, dependent on fate, with power over effort and action lost.

children.text: tattatprāpya na vihanyeta dhīro diṣṭaṃ balīya iti matvātmabuddhyā ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained each thing as it comes, the wise man should not be disturbed, thinking by his own understanding, 'Destiny is stronger.'

children.text: sukhaṃ hi janturyadi vāpi duḥkhaṃ daivādhīnaṃ vindati nātmaśaktyā
children.translated_text: A creature obtains happiness, or else suffering, as dependent on fate and not by its own power.
Therefore, regarding destiny as strong, one should never be fevered with grief and should never exult.

children.text: duḥkhe na tapyeta sukhe na hṛṣyetsamena varteta sadaiva dhīraḥ
children.translated_text: In suffering one should not be tormented, and in happiness one should not rejoice; the wise man should always conduct himself evenly.

children.text: diṣṭaṃ balīya iti manyamāno na saṃjvarennāpi hṛṣyet kadācit ||
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'Destiny is stronger,' one should never be fevered with grief and should never exult.

children.text: bhaye na muhyāmyaṣṭakāhaṃ kadācitsaṃtāpo me manaso nāsti kaścit
children.translated_text: I am never bewildered by fear, <s>Aṣṭaka</s>; there is no torment at all in my mind,

children.text: dhātā yathā māṃ vidadhāti loke dhruvaṃ tathāhaṃ bhaviteti matvā ||
children.translated_text: for I think, 'As the Ordainer disposes me in the world, surely so shall I become.'

children.text: saṃsvedajā hy aṇḍajā hy udbhidaśca sarīsṛpāḥ kṛmayo 'py apsu matsyāḥ
children.translated_text: Creatures born from sweat, born from eggs, and sprouting from the ground, reptiles, worms, and fish in the waters,

children.text: tathāśmānastṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ ca sarvaṃ diṣṭakṣaye svāṃ prakṛtiṃ bhajante ||
children.translated_text: and also stones, grass, and wood, all return to their own nature when destiny is exhausted.

children.text: anityatāṃ sukhaduḥkhasya buddhvā kasmāt saṃtāpamaṣṭakāhaṃ bhajeyam
children.translated_text: Knowing the impermanence of happiness and suffering, why should I, <s>Aṣṭaka</s>, resort to distress?

children.text: kiṃ kuryāṃ vai kiṃca kṛtvā na tapye tasmātsaṃtāpaṃ varjayāmyapramattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What should I do, and having done what should I not grieve? Therefore, vigilant, I avoid distress.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
As king <s>Yayāti</s> was speaking thus, <s>Aṣṭaka</s> again questioned

children.text: mātāmahaṃ sarvaguṇopapannaṃ yatra sthitaṃ svargaloke yathāvat ||
children.translated_text: his maternal grandfather, endowed with every virtue, about where he had properly stayed in the heavenly world.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: ye ye lokāḥ pārthivendra pradhānāstvayā bhuktā yaṃ ca kāle yathā ca
children.translated_text: O lord of kings, tell me exactly all those foremost worlds that you enjoyed, and at what time and in what manner,

children.text: tanme rājanbrūhi sarvaṃ yathāvatkṣetrajñavadbhāṣase tvaṃ hi dharmam ||
children.translated_text: for you speak of <s>dharma</s> like a knower of the field, O king.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: rājāhamāsaṃ tv iha sārvabhaumastato lokānmahataś cājaryaṃ vai
children.translated_text: I was once a universal sovereign king here; then I attained great, undecaying worlds.
There I lived for a thousand years; after that I reached still higher worlds.

children.text: tataḥ purīṃ puruhūtasya ramyāṃ sahasradvārāṃ śatayojanāntām
children.translated_text: Then I inhabited the lovely city of <s>Puruhūta</s>, with a thousand gates and extending a hundred yojanas,
for a thousand years; after that I reached still higher worlds.

children.text: tato divyamajaraṃ prāpya lokaṃ prajāpater lokapaterdurāpam
children.translated_text: Then, having reached the divine, undecaying world of <s>Prajāpati</s>, lord of creatures and lord of worlds, difficult to attain,
I lived there for a thousand years; after that I reached still higher worlds.

children.text: devasya devasya niveśane ca vijitya lokānnyavasaṃ yatheṣṭam
children.translated_text: And in the abode of the god of gods, having conquered worlds, I dwelt as I wished,
honored by all the thirty gods, equal in splendor and radiance to the lords.
So I lived in <s>Nandana</s>, able to assume forms at will, for hundreds of ten-thousands of years,
wandering with apsarases, seeing fragrant sacred trees that were blossoming and beautiful in form.

children.text: tatra sthitaṃ māṃ devasukheṣu saktaṃ kāle'tīte mahati tato'timātram
children.translated_text: When I was staying there, attached to divine pleasures, after a very great time had passed,
a frightful-looking messenger of the gods said loudly, three times in a drawn-out voice, 'Fall!'

children.text: etāvanme viditaṃ rājasiṃha tato bhraṣṭo'haṃ nandanātkṣīṇapuṇyaḥ
children.translated_text: This much is known to me, lion among kings. Then, my merit exhausted, I fell from <s>Nandana</s>.
And I heard the voices of the gods in the sky, grieving for me out of compassion, O lord of men:

children.text: akasmādvai kṣīṇapuṇyo yayātiḥ patatyasau puṇyakṛt puṇyakīrtiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Suddenly, his merit exhausted, <s>Yayāti</s> is falling, though he performed meritorious acts and has meritorious fame.'

children.text: tānabruvaṃ patamānastadāhaṃ satāṃ madhye nipateyaṃ kathaṃ nu ||
children.translated_text: Then, as I was falling, I said to them, 'How may I fall among the good?'
When they told me of your sacrificial ground, and when I saw it, I came here,

children.text: havirgandhair darśitāṃ yajñabhūmiṃ dhūmāpāṅgaṃ parigṛhya pratītām ||
children.translated_text: recognizing the sacrificial ground shown by the fragrances of oblations and marked by wreaths of smoke.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:
When you were living in <s>Nandana</s>, able to assume forms at will, for hundreds of ten-thousands of years,

children.text: kiṃkāraṇaṃ kārtayugapradhāna hitvā tadvai vasudhām anvapadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for what reason, O foremost one of the Kṛta age, did you leave that and descend to the earth?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: jñātiḥ suhṛtsvajano yo yatheha kṣīṇe vitte tyajyate mānavairhi
children.translated_text: Just as here a kinsman, friend, or relative is abandoned by men when his wealth is exhausted,

children.text: tathā svarge kṣīṇapuṇyaṃ manuṣyaṃ tyajanti sadyaḥ khecarā devasaṃghāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so in heaven the sky-going hosts of gods at once abandon a man whose merit is exhausted.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ tasminkṣīṇapuṇyā bhavanti saṃmuhyate me 'tra mano'timātram
children.translated_text: How do people in that world become those whose merit is exhausted? My mind is greatly confused about this.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ kasya dhāmopayānti tadvai brūhi kṣetravittvaṃ mato me ||
children.translated_text: What distinguished people go to whose abode? Tell me that, for I consider you a knower of the field.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: imaṃ bhaumaṃ narakaṃ te patanti lālapyamānā naradeva sarve
children.translated_text: All of them, lamenting, fall into this earthly hell, O king of men,

children.text: te kaṅkagomāyupalāśanārthaṃ kṣitau vivṛddhiṃ bahudhā prayānti ||
children.translated_text: and they go to repeated growth on the earth as food for herons, jackals, and owls.

children.text: tasmād evaṃ varjanīyaṃ narendra duṣṭaṃ loke garhaṇīyaṃ ca karma
children.translated_text: Therefore such an evil act, blameworthy in the world, is to be avoided, O lord of men.

children.text: ākhyātaṃ te pārthiva sarvametadbhūyaścedānīṃ vada kiṃ te vadāmi ||
children.translated_text: All this has been told to you, O king; now, if there is more, say what I should tell you.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: yadā tu tāṃs te vitudante vayāṃsi tathā gṛdhrāḥ śitikaṇṭhāḥ pataṃgāḥ
children.translated_text: When those birds tear at them, and likewise vultures, blue-necked birds, and flying creatures,

children.text: kathaṃ bhavanti kathamābhavanti tvatto bhaumaṃ narakamahaṃ śṛṇomi ||
children.translated_text: how do they come to be, and from what do they arise? I wish to hear from you about the earthly hell.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
After leaving the body, when karma has begun to unfold, they visibly move about upon the earth.

children.text: imaṃ bhaumaṃ narakaṃ te patanti nāvekṣante varṣapūgānanekān ||
children.translated_text: They fall into this earthly hell, and for many groups of years they do not behold release.

children.text: ṣaṣṭiṃ sahasrāṇi patanti vyomni tathāśītiṃ caiva tu vatsarāṇām
children.translated_text: For sixty thousand years, and also for eighty thousand years, they fall through the sky.

children.text: tānvai nudante prapatantaḥ prayātānbhīmā bhaumā rākṣasās tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As they fall and go downward, terrible earthly rākṣasas with sharp fangs drive them on.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:
When those terrible earthly rākṣasas with sharp fangs strike them as they fall,

children.text: kathaṃ bhavanti kathamābhavanti kathaṃbhūtā garbhabhūtā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: how do they come to be, from what do they arise, and of what sort do they become when they have entered the womb?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
Blood and semen, joined with menstrual fluid, at once follow what has been emitted by a man.

children.text: tava tarayā raja āpadyate ca sa garbhabhūtaḥ samupaiti tatra ||
children.translated_text: And when it reaches the woman's menstrual blood, there it comes forth as an embryo.

children.text: vanaspatīn oṣadhīṃścāviśanti apo vāyuṃ pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣam
children.translated_text: They enter trees and herbs, water, wind, earth, and the mid-region.

children.text: catuṣpadaṃ dvipadaṃ cāpi sarva evaṃbhūtā garbhabhūtā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: They also enter all four-footed and two-footed beings; becoming such, they become embryos.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:
Does the embryo here fashion another body, or does it go by its own will
as it enters this human birth? Tell me, as I ask from doubt.

children.text: śarīradehādisamucchrayaṃ ca cakṣuḥśrotre labhate kena saṃjñām
children.translated_text: By what does it obtain the growth consisting of body and frame, and the awareness of eye and ear?

children.text: etatsarvaṃ tāta ācakṣva pṛṣṭaḥ kṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ manyamānā hi sarve ||
children.translated_text: Tell me all this, father, since all regard you as one who knows the embodied self.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
In the proper season, the wind draws upward into the womb semen joined with menstrual fluid.

children.text: sa tatra tanmātrakṛtādhikāraḥ krameṇa saṃvardhayatīha garbham ||
children.translated_text: There, having an allotment made by the subtle elements, it gradually develops the embryo here.

children.text: sa jāyamāno'tha gṛhītamātraḥ saṃjñāmadhiṣṭhāya tato manuṣyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the human being, when born and just taken up, establishes awareness;

children.text: sa śrotrābhyāṃ vedayatīha śabdaṃ sa vai rūpaṃ paśyati cakṣuṣā ca ||
children.translated_text: with the two ears he perceives sound here, and with the eye he sees form.

children.text: ghrāṇena gandhaṃ jihvayātho rasaṃ ca tvacā sparśaṃ manasā devabhāvam
children.translated_text: With the nose he perceives smell, with the tongue taste, with the skin touch, and with the mind the divine state.

children.text: ityaṣṭakehopacitaṃ hi viddhi mahātmanaḥ prāṇabhṛtaḥ śarīre ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Aṣṭaka</s>, know this to have been accumulated in the body of the great-souled living being.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: yaḥ saṃsthitaḥ puruṣo dahyate vā nikhanyate vāpi nikṛṣyate vā
children.translated_text: When a man has died and is burned, buried, or dragged away,

children.text: abhāvabhūtaḥ sa vināśametya kenātmānaṃ cetayate purastāt ||
children.translated_text: and has become non-existent and gone to destruction, by what does he know himself thereafter?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: hitvā so 'sūn suptavanniṣṭhitatvāt purodhāya sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Having abandoned his vital breaths, like one asleep because he has come to rest, and placing before him both merit and demerit,

children.text: anyāṃ yoniṃ puṇyapāpānusārāṃ hitvā dehaṃ bhajate rājasiṃha ||
children.translated_text: after leaving the body he enters another womb according to his merit and sin, O lion among kings.

children.text: puṇyāṃ yoniṃ puṇyakṛto viśanti pāpāṃ yoniṃ pāpakṛto vrajanti
children.translated_text: Those who do merit enter a meritorious womb, and those who do evil go to an evil womb.

children.text: kīṭāḥ pataṃgāśca bhavanti pāpānna me vivakṣāsti mahānubhāva ||
children.translated_text: Because of sin they become worms and flying insects; I have no wish to elaborate, O great one.

children.text: catuṣpadā dvipadāḥ pakṣiṇaśca tathābhūtā garbhabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: They become four-footed beings, two-footed beings, and birds; in such forms they become embryos.

children.text: ākhyātametannikhilaṃ hi sarvaṃ bhūyastu kiṃ pṛcchasi rājasiṃha ||
children.translated_text: All this has been told in full; what more do you ask, O lion among kings?
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: kiṃ svitkṛtvā labhate tāta saṃjñāṃ martyaḥ śreṣṭhāṃ tapasā vidyayā vā
children.translated_text: By doing what, father, does a mortal obtain the best awareness, whether through austerity or knowledge?

children.text: tanme pṛṣṭaḥ śaṃsa sarvaṃ yathāvacchubhāṃllokān yena gacchet krameṇa ||
children.translated_text: Asked by me, tell me all that exactly, by which one may go in order to auspicious worlds.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: tapaśca dānaṃ ca śamo damaśca hrīr ārjavaṃ sarvabhūtānukampā
children.translated_text: Austerity, giving, tranquility, self-restraint, modesty, sincerity, and compassion for all beings:

children.text: svargasya lokasya vadanti santo dvārāṇi saptaiva mahānti puṃsām ||
children.translated_text: the good say these seven are the great gates of heaven's world for men.
And all these, as stated, though chiefly austerity,

children.text: naśyanti mānena tamo'bhibhūtāḥ puṃsaḥ sadaiveti vadanti santaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are destroyed by pride in a man overcome by darkness; so the good always say.

children.text: adhīyānaḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamāno yo vidyayā hanti yaśaḥ parasya
children.translated_text: One who studies and thinks himself learned, who by his learning destroys another's fame,

children.text: tasyāntavantaḥ puruṣasya lokā na cāsya tadbrahmaphalaṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: for that man the worlds have an end, and that learning does not grant him the fruit of brahman.
Four acts are terrifying, and when done improperly they produce fear:
an agnihotra performed with pride, silence practiced with pride, study done with pride, and sacrifice performed with pride.

children.text: na mānyamāno mudamādadīta na saṃtāpaṃ prāpnuyāccāvamānāt
children.translated_text: One should not take delight in being honored, nor should one feel distress from dishonor.

children.text: santaḥ sataḥ pūjayantīha loke nāsādhavaḥ sādhubuddhiṃ labhante ||
children.translated_text: The good honor the good here in the world; the wicked do not acquire the understanding of the good.
'One should give,' 'one should sacrifice,' and 'one should study': so I have heard.
These, they say, are fearless courses, and they are never to be avoided.

children.text: yenāśrayaṃ vedayante purāṇaṃ manīṣiṇo mānase mānayuktam
children.translated_text: By these, the wise come to know the ancient refuge, joined with reverence in the mind.

children.text: tanniḥśreyas tena saṃyogametya parāṃ śāntiṃ prāpnuyuḥ pretya ceha ||
children.translated_text: That is the highest good; having reached union with that, they attain supreme peace after death and here as well.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: carangṛhasthaḥ kathameti devānkathaṃ bhikṣuḥ katham ācāryakarmā
children.translated_text: How does a householder, while living his life, reach the gods? How does a mendicant, and how one engaged in the teacher's service?

children.text: vānaprasthaḥ satpathe saṃniviṣṭo bahūnyasmin samprati vedayanti ||
children.translated_text: How does a forest-dweller, established on the true path? Many teachings are now known on this matter.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: āhūtādhyāyī gurukarmasu codyataḥ pūrvotthāyī caramaṃ copaśāyī
children.translated_text: A brahmacārin who studies when called, is intent on service to the guru, rises first and lies down last,
who is gentle, restrained, firm, careful, and devoted to recitation, succeeds.

children.text: dharmāgataṃ prāpya dhanaṃ yajeta dadyāt sadaivātithīnbhojayecca
children.translated_text: Having obtained wealth that has come in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, one should sacrifice, give, and always feed guests;
and one should not take what has not been given by others. This is the ancient secret teaching of the householder.

children.text: svavīryajīvī vṛjinānnivṛtto dātā parebhyo na paropatāpī
children.translated_text: Living by his own strength, turned away from sin, a giver to others and not an oppressor of others,

children.text: tādṛṅmuniḥ siddhimupaiti mukhyāṃ vasann araṇye niyatāhāraceṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: such a sage attains the highest success, dwelling in the forest with his food and actions regulated.

children.text: aśilpajīvī vigṛhaśca nityaṃ jitendriyaḥ sarvato vipramuktaḥ
children.translated_text: Not living by crafts, always without possessions, with his senses conquered and wholly freed on every side,

children.text: anokaśāyī laghu lipsamānaś caran deśānekacaraḥ sa bhikṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: sleeping without a house, seeking little, wandering through many regions: he is a mendicant.

children.text: rātryā yayā cābhiratāśca lokā bhavanti kāmābhijitāḥ sukhena ca
children.translated_text: That night in which people delight, overcome by desires and at ease in pleasure,

children.text: tāmeva rātriṃ prayateta vidvānaraṇyasaṃstho bhavituṃ yatātmā ||
children.translated_text: that very night the wise man dwelling in the forest should strive to become self-controlled.
Ten ancestors and ten descendants, and also his own self as the twenty-first,

children.text: araṇyavāsī sukṛtaṃ dadhāti muktvā tv araṇye svaśarīradhātūn ||
children.translated_text: the forest-dweller establishes in merit, after leaving the constituents of his own body in the forest.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:
How many divine sages are there, and how many forms of silence also?
Tell that, for we wish to hear it.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: araṇye vasato yasya grāmo bhavati pṛṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: For one dwelling in the forest, if the village lies behind him,

children.text: grāme vā vasato 'raṇyaṃ sa muniḥ syājjanādhipa ||
children.translated_text: or for one dwelling in the village, if the forest lies behind him, he may be a sage, O lord of men.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:
How, when one dwells in the forest, does the village lie behind him?

children.text: grāme vā vasato'raṇyaṃ kathaṃ bhavati pṛṣṭhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when one dwells in the village, how does the forest lie behind him?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
One who would be a forest sage should not make use of village things;
in that way, while he dwells in the forest, the village lies behind him.
Without sacred fire and without a fixed dwelling, and also without attachment to clan or Vedic school, the sage
should desire clothing only so far as a loincloth and covering are needed.
He should desire food only so far as the maintenance of life requires;
then, while he dwells in the village, the forest lies behind him.
But the sage who has abandoned desires, given up ritual action, and conquered his senses,

children.text: ātiṣṭheta munir maunaṃ sa loke siddhimāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: if he practices silence, attains perfection in the world.
With teeth cleansed, nails cut, always bathed and adorned,
dark in body yet established in pure action, who would not be fit to honor him?
When, emaciated by austerity, thin, with flesh, bones, and blood wasted away,
the sage becomes free from the pairs of opposites, established in silence,

children.text: atha lokamimaṃ jitvā lokaṃ cāpi jayetparam
children.translated_text: then, having conquered this world, he may conquer the higher world as well.
And when the sage seeks food with his mouth like a cow,

children.text: athāsya lokaiḥ sarvo yaḥ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: then whatever whole world is his through those worlds becomes fit for immortality.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:
Which of these two first reaches likeness with the gods,
as both run on, O king, like the sun and the moon?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
Among those without homes and householders who follow desire, the restrained man,
though going as a mendicant in the village itself, has gone before those two.

children.text: aprāpyaṃ dīrghamāyuśca yaḥ prāpto vikṛtiṃ caret
children.translated_text: If one who has attained long life, difficult to obtain, should behave perversely,
and if, after doing that, he should repent and then practice fierce austerity,
what is cruel they call unwholesome; one who follows <s>dharma</s> with a mind set on harm

children.text: asāvanīśaḥ sa tathaiva rājaṃstadārjavaṃ sa samādhistadāryam ||
children.translated_text: is not master of himself in that way, O king. That straightforwardness, that concentration, that is noble conduct.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: kenādya tvaṃ tu prahito'si rājanyuvā sragvī darśanīyaḥ suvarcāḥ
children.translated_text: By whom have you been sent here today, O king, young, garlanded, handsome, and splendid?

children.text: kuta āgataḥ katamasyāṃ diśi tvamutāhosvitpārthivasthānam asti ||
children.translated_text: From where have you come, and in what direction are you going? Or is there perhaps a royal station for you?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: imaṃ bhaumaṃ narakaṃ kṣīṇapuṇyaḥ urvīṃ gaganādviprakīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: With my merit exhausted, scattered down from the sky toward the earth, toward this earthly hell,

children.text: uktvāhaṃ vaḥ prapatiṣyāmy ana tvarantvamī brahmaṇo lokapā ye ||
children.translated_text: having spoken to you, I shall fall. These guardians of the worlds of <s>Brahman</s> are not hurrying me.

children.text: satāṃ sakāśe tu vṛtaḥ prapātas sagatā guṇavantastu sarve
children.translated_text: My fall has been chosen in the presence of the good, and all who have come are virtuous;

children.text: śakrācca labdho hi varo mayaiṣa patiṣyatā bhūmitalaṃ narendra ||
children.translated_text: for this boon was obtained by me from <s>Śakra</s> as I was falling to the surface of the earth, O lord of men.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: pṛcchāmi tvāṃ prapatantaṃ prapātaṃ yadi lokāḥ pārthiva santi me'tra
children.translated_text: I ask you as you are falling in your fall: if there are worlds here belonging to me, O king,

children.text: yadyantarikṣe yadi vā divi śritāḥ kṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ tasya dharmasya manye ||
children.translated_text: whether they rest in the atmosphere or in heaven, I consider you a knower of that <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: yāvatpṛthivyāṃ vihitaṃ gavāśvaṃ sahāraṇyaiḥ paśubhiḥ pakṣibhiśca
children.translated_text: As many cattle and horses as are ordained on earth, together with forest animals and birds,

children.text: tāvallokā divi te saṃsthitā vai tathā vijānīhi narendrasiṃha ||
children.translated_text: so many worlds of yours are established in heaven. Know it so, lion among kings.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: tāṃste dadāmi mā prapata prapātaṃ ye me lokā divi rājendra santi
children.translated_text: I give them to you. Do not fall in your fall, O king of kings; those worlds of mine that are in heaven,
