children.text: yadyantarikṣe yadi vā divi śritāstānākrama kṣipramamitrahā'thasi ||
children.translated_text: whether they rest in the atmosphere or in heaven, enter them quickly, O slayer of enemies, if you are willing.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
One such as I, not a Brahmin though knowing <s>Brahman</s>, does not live by accepting gifts, O chief of kings.

children.text: yathā pradeyaṃ satataṃ dvijebhyastadā dade pūrvam ahaṃ narendra ||
children.translated_text: As gifts are always to be given to twice-born men, so I formerly gave, O lord of men.

children.text: nābrāhmaṇaḥ kṛpaṇo jātu jīvedyadyapi syādbrāhmaṇī vīrapatnī
children.translated_text: A non-Brahmin should never live as a wretched receiver, even if there were a Brahmin woman who was a hero's wife.

children.text: so'haṃ yadevākṛtapūrvaṃ careyaṃ vivitsamānaḥ kimu tatra sādhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If I, wishing to know, were to do what I have not done before, what good would there be in that?
<s>Pratardana</s> said:

children.text: pṛcchāmi tvāṃ spṛhaṇīyarūpa pratardano'haṃ yadi me santi lokāḥ
children.translated_text: I ask you, desirable in form: I am <s>Pratardana</s>. If there are worlds of mine,

children.text: yadyantarikṣe yadi vā divi śrutāḥ kṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ tasya dharmasya manye ||
children.translated_text: whether they are heard of in the atmosphere or in heaven, I consider you a knower of that <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: santi lokā bahavaste narendra apyekaikaṃ sapta śatānyahāni
children.translated_text: You have many worlds, O lord of men, each one lasting seven hundred days,
dripping honey, rich in ghee, free from sorrow; they wait for you, though they have an end.
<s>Pratardana</s> said:

children.text: tāṃste dadāmi patamānasya rājanye me lokāstava te vai bhavantu
children.translated_text: I give those worlds to you as you are falling, O king; let those worlds of mine indeed become yours.

children.text: yadyantarikṣe yadi vā divi śritās tānākrama kṣipramapetamohaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether they are set in midair or in heaven, quickly ascend to them, with delusion gone.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: nu tulyatejāḥ sukṛtaṃ hi kāmaye yogakṣemaṃ pārthivātpārthivaḥ san
children.translated_text: O equal in splendor, I seek the merit of good action and secure welfare; being myself a king, I do not seek it from another king.

children.text: daivādeśādāpadaṃ prāpya vidvāṃścarennṛśaṃsaṃ hi na jātu rājā ||
children.translated_text: Having met misfortune by divine command, a wise king should never act cruelly.

children.text: dharmyaṃ mārgaṃ cintayāno yaśasyaṃ kuryāttapo dharmamavekṣamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Reflecting on the righteous and fame-bringing path, he should practice austerity, keeping <s>dharma</s> in view.

children.text: na madvidho dharmabuddhirhi rājā hy evaṃ kuryātkṛpaṇaṃ māṃ yathāttha ||
children.translated_text: A king like me, whose understanding is set on <s>dharma</s>, would not do such a wretched thing as you tell me.

children.text: kuryāmapūrvaṃ na kṛtaṃ yadanyair vivitsamānaḥ kim u tatra sādhuḥ
children.translated_text: Should I do an unprecedented thing, not done by others, while trying to discern what is good in the matter?

children.text: bruvāṇamevaṃ nṛpatiṃ yayātiṃ nṛpottamo vasumānabravīt tam ||
children.translated_text: When King <s>Yayāti</s> had spoken in this way, the best of kings, <s>Vasumān</s>, said to him:
<s>Vasumān</s> said:

children.text: pṛcchāmyahaṃ vasumānauṣadaśviryadyasti loko divi mahyaṃ narendra
children.translated_text: I, <s>Vasumān</s>, son of <s>Auṣadaśva</s>, ask: if there is a world in heaven for me, O king of men,

children.text: yadyantarikṣe prathito mahātmankṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ tasya dharmasya manye ||
children.translated_text: or if one is renowned in midair, O great-souled one, I consider you an expert in that <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: yadantarikṣaṃ pṛthivī diśaśca yattejasā tapate bhānumāṃśca
children.translated_text: As far as midair, the earth, and the quarters extend, and as far as the radiant sun burns with light,

children.text: lokās tāvanto divi saṃsthitā vai te tvāṃ bhavantaṃ pratipālayanti ||
children.translated_text: so many worlds are established in heaven; they are waiting for your honored self.
<s>Vasumān</s> said:

children.text: tāṃs te dadāmi pata māṃ prapātaṃ ye me lokāstava te vai bhavantu
children.translated_text: I give those to you. Let me fall down into the abyss; let those worlds of mine become yours.
Buy them even for a blade of grass, O king, if receiving a gift is truly tainted for you.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: na mithyāhaṃ vikrayaṃ vai smarāmi mayā kṛtaṃ śiśubhāve'pi rājan
children.translated_text: I do not recall ever making a false sale, O king, even in childhood.

children.text: kuryāṃ na caivākṛtapūrvamanyair vivitsamāno vasumanna sādhu ||
children.translated_text: Nor would I do a thing not done before by others, O <s>Vasumān</s>, while seeking to know what is good.
<s>Vasumān</s> said:

children.text: tāṃs tvaṃ lokānpratipadyasva rājanmayā dattānyadi neṣṭaḥ krayaste
children.translated_text: Then accept those worlds, O king, as given by me, if purchase is not desired by you.

children.text: nāhaṃ tānvai pratigantā narendra sarve lokāstāvakā vai bhavantu ||
children.translated_text: I shall not go back to them, O lord of men; let all those worlds be yours.
<s>Śibi</s> said:

children.text: pṛcchāmi tvāṃ śibirauśīnaro'haṃ mamāpi lokā yadi santi tāta
children.translated_text: I, <s>Śibi</s> <s>Auśīnara</s>, ask you: if there are worlds for me too, dear sir,

children.text: yadyantarikṣe yadi vā divi śritāḥ kṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ tasya dharmasya manye ||
children.translated_text: whether they are set in midair or in heaven, I consider you an expert in that <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: na tvaṃ vācā hṛdayenāpi rājan parīpsamāno māvamaṃsthā narendra
children.translated_text: O king, O lord of men, you have never insulted me, even in speech or in your heart while striving for advantage.

children.text: tenānantā divi lokāḥ sthitā vai vidyudrūpāḥ svanavanto mahāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore boundless worlds are established in heaven for you, great, sounding, and formed like lightning.
<s>Śibi</s> said:

children.text: tāṃs tvaṃ lokānpratipadyasva rājanmayā dattānyadi neṣṭaḥ krayaste
children.translated_text: Then accept those worlds, O king, as given by me, if purchase is not desired by you.

children.text: na cāhaṃ tānpratipadya dattvā yatra tvaṃ tāta gantāsi lokān ||
children.translated_text: After giving them, I shall not accept them; I will go to the worlds to which you will go, dear sir.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
As you have a might like <s>Indra</s>, so too, O king of men, your worlds are boundless.

children.text: tathādya loke na rame'nyadatte tasmācchibe nābhinandāmi vācam ||
children.translated_text: Yet today I take no delight in what is given by another in this world; therefore, O <s>Śibi</s>, I do not welcome your words.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:
If you will not accept our worlds one by one, O king,

children.text: sarve pradāya tāṃllokān gantāro narakaṃ vayam ||
children.translated_text: then, after giving all those worlds, we shall go to hell.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
As good men who see truth and the rest, say what is worthy of you.

children.text: ahaṃ tu nābhigṛhṇāmi yatkṛtaṃ na mayā purā ||
children.translated_text: But I do not accept what I did not formerly earn by my own action.

children.text: alipsamānasya tu me yaduktaṃ na tattathāstīha narendrasiṃha
children.translated_text: What was said to me when I was not seeking it is not so here, O lion among kings.

children.text: asya pradānasya yadeva yuktaṃ tasyaiva cānantaphalaṃ bhaviṣyam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is proper in this giving, for that alone there will be endless fruit.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:
Whose are these five golden chariots that are seen here,
standing high and shining, blazing like flames of fire?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: bhavatāṃ mama caivaite rathā bhānti hiraṇmayāḥ
children.translated_text: These golden chariots shine for you and for me.
Mounting them, you and I together must go.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:
Take your place in the chariot, O king, and stride through the sky.
We too shall follow when the time comes.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: sarvairidānīṃ gantavyaṃ saha svargo jito yataḥ
children.translated_text: All must go now together, since heaven has been won.

children.text: eṣa vo virajāḥ panthā dṛśyate devasadmagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This stainless path of yours is seen, leading to the abode of the gods.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Having mounted the chariots, all those kings set out, O king.
As they climbed to heaven, they shone, enclosing heaven and earth with <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said:

children.text: ahaṃ manye pūrvameko'bhigantā sakhā cendraḥ sarvathā me mahātmā
children.translated_text: I thought that I would go first, alone, and that <s>Indra</s>, the great-souled one, was in every way my friend.
Why, then, has this <s>Śibi</s> <s>Auśīnara</s> alone gone beyond all the vehicles with speed?
<s>Yayāti</s> said:
This blameless son of <s>Uśīnara</s> gave all his wealth for the path to the gods.

children.text: uśīnarasya putro'yaṃ tasmācchreṣṭho hi vaḥ śibiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Śibi</s> is indeed the best among you.

children.text: dānaṃ śaucaṃ satyamatho hy ahiṃsā hrīḥ śrīstitikṣā samatānṛśaṃsyam
children.translated_text: Giving, purity, truth, nonviolence, modesty, splendor, patience, equality, and compassion:

children.text: rājantyetānyatha sarvāṇi rājñi śibau sthitānyapratime subuddhyā
children.translated_text: all these shine, O king, and are established in King <s>Śibi</s>, unmatched in his wisdom.

children.text: evaṃ vṛttaṃ hrīniṣevī bibharti tasmācchibir abhigantā rathena ||
children.translated_text: One of such conduct, devoted to modesty, bears them; therefore <s>Śibi</s> goes by chariot.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Then <s>Aṣṭaka</s>, moved by curiosity, again asked his grandfather, who was like <s>Indra</s>:

children.text: pṛcchāmi tvāṃ nṛpate brūhi satyaṃ kutaśca kaścāsi kathaṃ tvamāgāḥ
children.translated_text: I ask you, O king: tell the truth. From where and who are you, and how did you come?

children.text: kṛtaṃ tvayā yaddhi na tasya kartā loke tvadanyo brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vā ||
children.translated_text: For what you have done, no other Brahmin or Kshatriya in the world is the doer of it.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: yayātirasmi nahuṣasya putraḥ pūroḥ pitā sārvabhaumastvihāsam
children.translated_text: I am <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, father of <s>Pūru</s>, once universal sovereign here.

children.text: guhyaṃ mantraṃ māmakebhyo bravīmi mātāmaho bhavatāṃ suprakāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I speak a secret counsel to my own descendants; I am clearly your maternal grandfather.

children.text: sarvām imāṃ pṛthivīṃ nirjigāya ṛddhāṃ mahīmadadāṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having conquered all this earth, the prosperous land, I gave it to the Brahmins.
When many pure and handsome horses were given by me, then the gods became sharers in the merit.
I gave this praised earth, full of all kinds of food, to the brahmins,

children.text: gobhiḥ suvarṇaiśca dhanaiśca mukhyairaśvāḥ sanāgāḥ śataśastvarbudāni ||
children.translated_text: together with cows, gold, and excellent wealth, and with horses and elephants by the hundreds and by tens of millions.

children.text: satyena me dyauśca vasuṃdharā ca tathaivāgnirjvalate mānuṣeṣu
children.translated_text: By truth heaven and the earth are mine; likewise fire blazes among human beings.

children.text: na me vṛthā vyāhṛtameva vākyaṃ satyaṃ hi santaḥ pratipūjayanti ||
children.translated_text: No word uttered by me has been in vain, for the good honor truth.

children.text: sādhvaṣṭaka prabravīmīha satyaṃ pratardanaṃ vasumantaṃ śibiṃ ca
children.translated_text: O good <s>Aṣṭaka</s>, I proclaim the truth here: <s>Pratardana</s>, <s>Vasumat</s>, and <s>Śibi</s>,

children.text: sarve devā munayaśca lokāḥ satyena pūjyā iti me manogatam ||
children.translated_text: all the gods, sages, and worlds are honored through truth; this is what I think.

children.text: yo naḥ sarvajitaṃ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ nivedayet
children.translated_text: Whoever reports to us the whole all-conquering rite exactly as it occurred,
without envy toward the twice-born and the sacred fires, shall share our world.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ rājansa mahātmā yayātiḥ svadauhitraistārito mitravaryaiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, O king, the great-souled <s>Yayāti</s>, rescued by his own daughter's sons, those excellent friends,

children.text: tyaktvā mahīṃ paramodārakarmā svargaṃ gataḥ karmabhirvyāpya pṛthvīm ||
children.translated_text: abandoned the earth and, supremely noble in deeds, went to heaven after filling the earth with his acts.

children.text: evaṃ sarvaṃ vistarato yathāvadākhyātaṃ te caritaṃ nāhuṣasya
children.translated_text: Thus I have told you in full and exactly the conduct of <s>Nāhuṣa</s>,

children.text: vaṃśo yasya prathitaṃ pauraveyo yasmiñjātastvaṃ manujendrakalpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose Paurava lineage is renowned, and in which you were born, O lord of men.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard this from <s>Śaunaka</s>, King <s>Śatānīka</s>
became amazed and shone with supreme joy like the full moon.
Then the king honored <s>Śaunaka</s> according to rule
with jewels, cows, gold, and various garments.

children.text: pratigṛhya tataḥ sarvaṃ yadrājñā prahitaṃ dhanam
children.translated_text: Then, having accepted all the wealth that had been sent by the king,
and having given it to the brahmins, <s>Śaunaka</s> disappeared.
The sages said:
We wish to hear the lineage of <s>Yayāti</s>; tell it in detail,
as it was established in the world by his sons beginning with <s>Yadu</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall proclaim the lineage of <s>Yadu</s>, the eldest, of unsurpassed splendor;
listen to me as I speak of it in detail and in order.
<s>Yadu</s> indeed had five sons, like sons of gods,
great chariot-warriors and mighty archers; learn them by name.
<s>Sahasrajit</s> was the eldest, then <s>Kroṣṭu</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Antika</s>, and <s>Laghu</s>;
and the heir of <s>Sahasrajit</s> was the king named <s>Śatajit</s>.
The heirs of <s>Śatajit</s> too were three men of supreme fame:
<s>Haihaya</s>, <s>Haya</s>, and also <s>Veṇuhaya</s>.
The heir of <s>Haihaya</s> was the renowned <s>Dharmanetra</s>;
from <s>Dharmanetra</s> came <s>Kunti</s>, and his son was <s>Saṃhata</s>.
The heir of <s>Saṃhata</s> was the king named <s>Mahiṣmān</s>;
the mighty <s>Rudraśreṇya</s> was the son of <s>Mahiṣmān</s>.
He became king in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>; this has already been told before.
The son of <s>Rudraśreṇya</s> was the king named <s>Durdama</s>.
The wise and valiant <s>Kanaka</s> was <s>Durdama</s>'s son;
the heirs of <s>Kanaka</s> were four, famous in the world.
They were <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>, <s>Kṛtāgni</s>, and <s>Kṛtavarmā</s>,
and <s>Kṛtaujā</s> was the fourth; then from <s>Kṛtavīrya</s> came <s>Arjuna</s>.
Born with a thousand arms, he was a king ruling over the seven islands;
the lord of the earth performed difficult austerity for ten thousand years.
<s>Kārtavīrya</s> worshiped <s>Datta</s>, who was born from <s>Atri</s>;
by him four boons were given to him, O best of men.

children.text: pūrvaṃ bāhusahasraṃ tu sa vavre rājasattamaḥ
children.translated_text: First, O best of kings, he chose a thousand arms,
and also restraint by the good when he was acting in adharma.
After conquering the earth by war, he chose to protect it by dharma alone,
and, when he was engaged in battle, that his death should come only from one superior to him.
By him this whole earth, with its seven islands and mountains,
encircled by the seven oceans, was conquered according to the kṣatriya rule.
For that wise man, as he wished, a thousand arms indeed appeared;
his chariot and banner appeared as well: so we have heard.

children.text: daśa yajñasahasrāṇi rājñāṃ dvīpeṣu vai tadā
children.translated_text: At that time ten thousand sacrifices
are heard to have been performed unobstructed by that wise king on the islands.
All the sacrifices of that great king had abundant gifts,
and all had golden sacrificial posts and golden altars.
All were adorned by gods who had arrived together and were seated in aerial cars,
and they were always beautified by gandharvas and apsarases.

children.text: tasya yajñe jagau gāthāṃ gandharvo nāradastathā
children.translated_text: At his sacrifice the gandharva <s>Nārada</s> also sang a song,
after beholding the greatness of the royal seer <s>Kārtavīrya</s>.

children.text: na nūnaṃ kārtavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyanti kṣatriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Surely kṣatriyas will not attain the course of <s>Kārtavīrya</s>
through sacrifices, gifts, austerities, valor, and learning.

children.text: sa hi saptasu dvīpeṣu khaḍgī cakrī śarāsanī
children.translated_text: For across the seven islands he bore sword, discus, and bow;
a chariot-warrior roaming the islands, he saw thieves by virtue of being a yogin.
For eighty-five thousand years that lord of men,
possessed of every jewel, was a universal emperor.

children.text: sa eva paśupālo 'bhūt kṣetrapālaḥ sa eva hi
children.translated_text: He himself was protector of cattle, and he himself was protector of fields;
he himself, as <s>Arjuna</s>, became <s>Parjanya</s> with rain through his yogic power.
He, whose skin was hardened by bowstring-strikes on his thousand arms,
shines like the autumn sun with a thousand rays.
This great-radiant one, among men, in <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>,
having conquered the nāga, the son of <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, settled him there in the city.

children.text: eṣa vegaṃ samudrasya prāvṛṭkāle bhajeta vai
children.translated_text: This lord of the earth would take on the force of the ocean in the rainy season,
and, playing as if bursting with joy, he would go upstream against the current.
Sporting playfully, he wore a garland of opposing wreaths,
and the <s>Narmadā</s>, frightened by the frown of the waves, came trembling near.
Alone, with his thousand arms, he plunged into the great ocean,
and made the <s>Narmadā</s>, swollen and violent in the rainy season, turn back with an upsurging current.
When the great ocean was being churned by his thousand arms,
the great asuras dwelling in <s>Pātāla</s> became utterly motionless.
He crushed the great billows; the fish and mighty timis sank within them,
while masses of foam were struck by the wind and whirlpools made the ocean hard to endure.
Thus he churned the sea itself with his thousand arms,
and the great serpents, terrified as at the churning by <s>Mandara</s> and suspecting the production of nectar,
then held their heads motionless,
like clusters of plantains in the evening, still when there is no wind.
In this way, having bound the arrogant one to his bowstring with five arrows,

children.text: laṅkāyāṃ mohayitvā tu sabalaṃ rāvaṇaṃ balāt ||
children.translated_text: and having overpowered <s>Rāvaṇa</s> together with his army in <s>Laṅkā</s> by force,

children.text: nirjitya baddhvā cānīya māhiṣmatyāṃ babandha ca
children.translated_text: he defeated him, bound him, brought him to <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>, and kept him imprisoned.

children.text: tato gatvā pulastyastu hy arjunaṃ saṃprasādayan ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pulastya</s> went and appeased <s>Arjuna</s>;
and he released the <s>Paulastya</s> rakṣas, soothed here by <s>Pulastya</s>.
From his thousand arms there arose the sound of the bowstring,
like the crash of the thunderbolt among a thousand clouds at the end of an age.
Ah, indeed, such is the power of fate, that this <s>Bhārgava</s> cut off
that thousand of arms, like a forest of golden palm trees.
There, the mighty <s>Āpava</s>, angered, cursed <s>Arjuna</s>:

children.text: yasmādvanaṃ pradagdhaṃ vai viśrutaṃ mama haihaya
children.translated_text: "Because my famous forest has indeed been burned, O <s>Haihaya</s>,
therefore another mighty man will undo the difficult deed you have done.

children.text: chittvā bāhusahasraṃ te prathamaṃ tarasā balī
children.translated_text: First, after cutting off your thousand arms with force,

children.text: tapasvī brāhmaṇaśca tvāṃ sa vadhiṣyati bhārgava ||
children.translated_text: that ascetic Brahmin, the <s>Bhārgava</s>, will kill you."
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tasya rāmastadā tv āsīnmṛtyuḥ śāpena dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> became his death through the curse of the wise one,

children.text: varaścaiva tu rājarṣeḥ svayameva vṛtaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: and also through the boon formerly chosen by the royal seer himself.

children.text: tasya putraśataṃ tv āsītpañca tatra mahārathāḥ
children.translated_text: He had a hundred sons; among them five were great chariot-warriors,
trained in weapons, strong, heroic, righteous, and very powerful.
<s>Śūrasena</s>, <s>Śūra</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>, and likewise <s>Kroṣṭu</s>,
<s>Jayadhvaja</s>, <s>Vaikarta</s>, and <s>Avanti</s>, O lord of men.
The son of <s>Jayadhvaja</s> was <s>Tālajaṅgha</s>, very powerful;
his very hundred sons were known as the <s>Tālajaṅghas</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ pañca kulāḥ khyātā haihayānāṃ mahātmanām
children.translated_text: Among those noble <s>Haihaya</s> clans, five families are famed:
the <s>Vītihotras</s>, the <s>Śāryātas</s>, the <s>Bhojas</s>, and also the <s>Avantyas</s>,
the valiant <s>Kuṇḍikeras</s>, and likewise the <s>Tālajaṅghas</s>.
The son of <s>Vītihotra</s> too was a mighty man named <s>Ānarta</s>;
his son was <s>Durjeya</s>, a tormentor of enemies.
With honest purpose, O great king, he protected his subjects according to <s>dharma</s>.
There was a king named <s>Kārtavīrya Arjuna</s>, possessed of a thousand arms.
By his bow the earth, as far as the ocean's boundary, was conquered.
The man who rises at dawn and recites his name

children.text: na tasya vittanāśaḥ syānnaṣṭaṃ ca labhate punaḥ
children.translated_text: will not suffer loss of wealth, and what has been lost he obtains again.
Whoever here recounts the birth of wise <s>Kārtavīrya</s>
properly, with a soul purified by well-offered rites, is honored in the heavenly world.
The sages said:
Why was that forest of the great-souled <s>Āpava</s> burned?
Tell us truly, <s>Sūta</s>, how it was done by <s>Kārtavīrya</s> in his valor.

children.text: rakṣitā sa tu rājarṣiḥ prajānāmiti naḥ śrutam
children.translated_text: We have heard that that royal seer was a protector of his subjects.
How, being such a protector, did he burn that ascetic grove?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Āditya</s>, in the form of a Brahmin, approached <s>Kārtavīrya</s>.
"Grant me one satisfaction. I am <s>Āditya</s>, O lord of men."
The king said:
"Blessed one, by what is your satisfaction brought about, O maker of day?

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ bhojanaṃ dadmi hutvā tu vidadhāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: What kind of food shall I give, and how shall I provide it after offering oblation?"
<s>Āditya</s> said:

children.text: sthāvaraṃ dehi me sarvamāhāraṃ dadatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: "Give me all that is stationary as food, best of givers.

children.text: tena tṛpto bhaveyaṃ vai sā me tṛptirhi pārthiva ||
children.translated_text: By that I would be satisfied; that, O king, is my satisfaction."
<s>Kārtavīrya</s> said:

children.text: na śakyāḥ sthāvarāḥ sarve tejasā ca balena ca
children.translated_text: "All stationary things cannot be burned up by my brilliance and strength,

children.text: nirdagdhuṃ tapatāṃ śreṣṭha tena tvāṃ praṇamāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: O best of those who heat; therefore I bow to you."
<s>Āditya</s> said:
"Pleased with you, I give you inexhaustible arrows, facing in every direction.
When shot, they will blaze, endowed with my radiance.
Entered by my powers, they will dry up stationary things;
when dried, they will turn them to ash. By that, O lord of men, will come my satisfaction."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then <s>Āditya</s> gave those arrows to <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: tato dadāha samprāptān sthāvarān sarvameva ca ||
children.translated_text: Then he burned all the stationary things that came within reach.
Villages, hermitages, cowherd settlements, and cities,
pleasant ascetic groves, forests, and pleasure-groves;
thus he burned the whole eastern region, and after that the whole southern region.
The earth became without trees and without grass, struck by that terrible heat.
At that very time <s>Āpava</s> had resorted to the water;
for ten thousand years the great seer remained there.
When his vow was complete, the greatly radiant treasure of austerity rose up,
and that great sage saw his hermitage burned by <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: krodhācchaśāpa rājarṣiṃ kīrtitaṃ vo yathā mayā
children.translated_text: In anger he cursed the royal seer, as I have related to you.
Now hear the lineage of the royal seer <s>Kroṣṭu</s>, of unsurpassed prowess,
in whose line <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the upholder of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan, was born.
The son of <s>Kroṣṭu</s> was <s>Vṛjinīvān</s>, a great chariot-warrior.
And <s>Vṛjinīvat</s> had a son, named <s>Svāha</s>, mighty in strength.
O king, from <s>Svāha</s> was born <s>Ruṣaṅgu</s>, best of speakers.

children.text: sa tu prasūtimicchan vai ruṣaṅguḥ saumyamātmajam
children.translated_text: That <s>Ruṣaṅgu</s>, desiring progeny, obtained a gentle son.
His son was <s>Citra</s>, and also <s>Citraratha</s>, endowed with deeds.
Then the heroic descendant of <s>Citraratha</s> was born, lavish in sacrificial gifts.
Known as <s>Śaśabindu</s>, he became a universal emperor.
In this connection this ancestral verse was formerly sung about him:
The sons of <s>Śaśabindu</s> numbered a hundred hundreds.
They were intelligent and handsome, possessing abundant wealth and splendor.
Of those hundreds of chiefs, the great and mighty ones bore the name <s>Pṛthu</s>.
<s>Pṛthuśravas</s>, <s>Pṛthuyaśas</s>, <s>Pṛthudharmā</s>, <s>Pṛthuṃjaya</s>,
<s>Pṛthukīrti</s>, and <s>Pṛthumanas</s> were kings descended from <s>Śaśabindu</s>.
The knowers of the Purāṇas praise <s>Pṛthuśravas</s> as the foremost.
<s>Suyajña</s> was the son of <s>Antara</s>.
<s>Uśanā</s> was the son of <s>Suyajña</s>; while protecting this earth,
that supremely dharmic man performed a hundred horse sacrifices.
<s>Titikṣu</s>, son of <s>Uśanā</s>, was born, a scorcher of foes.
<s>Marutta</s>, his son, was the best of royal seers.
The sons of <s>Marutta</s> were <s>Vīra</s> and <s>Kambalabarhiṣa</s>.
The learned <s>Rukmakavaca</s> was the son of <s>Kambalabarhiṣa</s>.
Having slain enemy warriors wearing armor, <s>Rukmakavaca</s>
with various arrows from his bow, and having obtained this earth,
the king gave sacrificial gifts to the Brahmins at a horse sacrifice.
Then once, at a sacrifice, <s>Rukmakavaca</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,
had five sons born to him, of great valor and bearing bows:
<s>Rukmeṣu</s>, <s>Pṛthurukma</s>, <s>Jyāmagha</s>, <s>Parigha</s>, and <s>Hari</s>.
Their father established <s>Parigha</s> and <s>Hari</s> in <s>Videha</s>.
<s>Rukmeṣu</s> became king, and <s>Pṛthurukma</s> remained under his protection.
Then <s>Jyāmagha</s>, driven from the kingdom by them, stayed in that hermitage.
Peaceful and dwelling in the hermitage, he was instructed by a Brahmin.
Taking his bow, with banner and chariot, he went to another country.
The king went alone to the <s>Narmadā</s>, merely seeking a livelihood.
Having gone to Mount <s>Ṛkṣavat</s>, he settled where others had already dwelt.
<s>Jyāmagha</s> had a wife, <s>Caitrā</s>, a chaste woman advanced in age.
Childless, the king lived there and did not take another wife.
He won a victory in battle there, and obtained a maiden.
Out of fear he said to his wife, 'O bright-smiling one, this is your daughter-in-law.'
Being addressed in this way, she said to him, 'And whose daughter-in-law is she?'
The king said:
'The son who will be born to you: she will be his wife.'
Therefore, through fierce austerity, she gave birth because of that maiden.

children.text: putraṃ vidarbhaṃ subhagā caitrā pariṇatā satī
children.translated_text: The fortunate, chaste, mature <s>Caitrā</s> bore a son, <s>Vidarbha</s>.
And that wise man, with the princess who was his daughter-in-law, begot <s>Kratha</s> and <s>Kaiśika</s>,
and a third son, <s>Lomapāda</s>, exceedingly dharmic.
On her <s>Vidarbha</s> begot brave sons skilled in battle.
From <s>Lomapāda</s> came a son, <s>Manu</s>; his son was <s>Jñāti</s>.

children.text: kaiśikasya cidiḥ putras tasmāccaidyā nṛpāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Cidi</s> was the son of <s>Kaiśika</s>; from him the <s>Caidya</s> kings are remembered.
<s>Kratha</s> was the son of <s>Vidarbha</s>, and <s>Kunti</s> became his son.
From <s>Kunti</s> was born <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>, a powerful son bold in battle.
The son of <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s> was righteous <s>Nirvṛti</s>, slayer of enemy heroes.

children.text: tadeko nirvṛteḥ putro nāmnā sa tu vidūrathaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvṛti</s> had a single son, named <s>Vidūratha</s>.

children.text: daśārhastasya vai putro vyomastasya ca vai smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: His son was <s>Daśārha</s>, and his son is remembered as <s>Vyoma</s>.
From <s>Daśārha</s>, and then from <s>Vyoma</s>, the son is called <s>Jīmūta</s>.
The son of <s>Jīmūta</s> was <s>Vimala</s>; his son was <s>Bhīmaratha</s>.
The son of <s>Bhīmaratha</s> is remembered as <s>Navaratha</s>.
His son was <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>, and <s>Śakuni</s> was his son.
From him came <s>Karambha</s>; from <s>Karambha</s>, <s>Devarāta</s> was born.
The king <s>Devakṣatra</s>, descendant of <s>Devarāta</s>, was greatly renowned.
<s>Devagarbha</s>, equal to a god, was born, the delight of <s>Devanakṣatra</s>.
There was <s>Madhu</s> by name, very splendid, and from <s>Madhu</s> came <s>Puravas</s> likewise.
<s>Purudvān</s>, best of men, was the son of <s>Puravas</s>.
Then <s>Jantu</s> was born from <s>Purudvān</s> in the Vaidarbhī <s>Bhadrasenī</s>.
An Aikṣvākī woman became <s>Jantu</s>'s wife; from her was born
<s>Sātvata</s>, endowed with strength of being, increaser of the fame of the <s>Sātvatas</s>.
Having understood this descent of the great <s>Jyāmagha</s>,

children.text: prajāvān eti sāyujyaṃ rājñaḥ somasya dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: a man with offspring attains union with wise King <s>Soma</s>.
<s>Kauśalyā</s> bore sons to <s>Sātvata</s>, endowed with excellence:

children.text: bhajinaṃ bhajamānaṃ tu divyaṃ devāvṛdhaṃ nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhajin</s>, <s>Bhajamāna</s>, <s>Divya</s>, and <s>Devāvṛdha</s>, O king,

children.text: andhakaṃ ca mahābhojaṃ vṛṣṇiṃ ca yadunandanam
children.translated_text: and <s>Andhaka</s>, <s>Mahābhoja</s>, and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, delight of <s>Yadu</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu sargāś catvāro vistareṇaiva tacchṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: Their lines are four; hear that in full detail.
From <s>Bhajamāna</s>, in <s>Sṛñjayā</s> and in <s>Bāhyakā</s>, were born the <s>Bāhyakas</s>.

children.text: sṛñjayasya sute dve tu bāhyakāstu tadābhavan ||
children.translated_text: Those two were then the two daughters of <s>Sṛñjaya</s>, the <s>Bāhyakās</s>.

children.text: tasya bhārye bhaginyau dve suṣuvāte bahūnsutān
children.translated_text: His two wives, the two sisters, gave birth to many sons.

children.text: nimiṃ ca kṛmilaṃ caiva vṛṣṇiṃ parapuraṃjayam
children.translated_text: They were <s>Nimi</s>, <s>Kṛmila</s>, and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, conqueror of enemy cities.
They were born from <s>Bhajamāna</s> in <s>Bāhyakā</s> and <s>Sṛñjayā</s>.
At a sacrifice King <s>Devāvṛdha</s>, increaser of the friendship of his kinsmen,
was without a son; the king practiced supreme austerity,
longing, 'May a son endowed with every virtue be mine.'
Then, having joined the mantra, he touched the water of <s>Parṇāśā</s>.
Through that act of sipping the water, the river did what was pleasing to him.
Because of the king's auspiciousness, that best of rivers,
her mind surrounded by thought, then reached a decision.
I do not find a woman in whom such a son as this
would be born; therefore today I myself shall become manifold.

children.text: atha bhūtvā kumārī sā bibhratī paramaṃ vapuḥ
children.translated_text: Then she became a maiden, bearing a supreme beauty,
and made herself known to the king; the great-vowed one desired her.

children.text: atha sā navame māsi suṣuve saritāṃ varā
children.translated_text: Then, in the ninth month, that best of rivers gave birth
to a son endowed with every virtue, <s>Babhru</s>, from King <s>Devāvṛdha</s>.
It is traditionally heard that knowers of the Purāṇa sing in the lineage,
proclaiming also the virtues of the great-souled <s>Devāvṛdha</s>:
Just as we hear from afar, so we have seen from nearby:
<s>Babhru</s> is the best of men, and <s>Devāvṛdha</s> is equal to the gods.
Sixty former ancestors and seventy thousand more
attained immortality through <s>Babhru</s> and <s>Devāvṛdha</s>, O king.
He was a sacrificer, a lord of giving, heroic, devoted to Brahmins, and firm in vows,
handsome, very splendid, and likewise a bearer of learning and valor.

children.text: atha kaṅkasya duhitā suṣuve caturaḥ sutān
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of <s>Kaṅka</s> bore four sons:
<s>Kukura</s>, <s>Bhajamāna</s>, <s>Śaśi</s>, and <s>Kambalabarhiṣa</s>.
<s>Kukura</s>'s son was <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>'s son was <s>Dhṛti</s>.
Then <s>Kapotaromā</s> was his son, and <s>Taittiri</s> was his child.
His son was <s>Sarpa</s>; his learned son was said to be <s>Nala</s>.

children.text: khyāyate tasya nāmnā sa nandano daradundubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: His child, renowned by his name, was <s>Daradundubhi</s>.
When that extensive sacrifice was proceeding, <s>Punarvasu</s> was born.
That best of men undertook an <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) for the sake of a son.
In the midst of that <s>atirātra</s> rite, he rose up from the middle of the assembly.
Thus the learned <s>Punarvasu</s>, knowing ritual action, was a sacrificer and a giver.
He had a pair of children, said to be unconquered:
<s>Āhuka</s> and <s>Āhukī</s>, famous, O best of the intelligent.
Here they recite these verses concerning that <s>Āhuka</s>:
Of chariots with harnesses and draw-bars, with banners and protective gear,
sounding like clouds, there were exactly ten thousand.
No speaker of falsehood, no man without splendor, no non-sacrificer, no one who failed to give thousands,
no impure man, nor any unlearned man, was born among the <s>Bhojas</s>.
They had entered the service of <s>Āhuka</s>; this indeed is what is said of him.
<s>Āhuka</s> also gave his sister <s>Āhukī</s> among the <s>Avantīs</s>.
The daughter of <s>Kāśya</s> bore two sons to <s>Āhuka</s>:
<s>Devaka</s> and <s>Ugrasena</s>, both equal to divine children.
Heroic sons, like the thirty gods, were born to <s>Devaka</s>:
<s>Devavān</s>, <s>Upadeva</s>, <s>Sudeva</s>, and <s>Devarakṣita</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ svasāraḥ saptāsan vasudevāya tā dadau ||
children.translated_text: Their seven sisters he gave to <s>Vasudeva</s>.
<s>Devakī</s>, <s>Śrutadevī</s>, <s>Mitradevī</s>, <s>Yaśodharā</s>,

children.text: śrīdevī satyadevī ca sutāpī ceti saptamī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīdevī</s>, <s>Satyadevī</s>, and <s>Sutāpī</s> as the seventh.
<s>Ugrasena</s>'s sons were nine; <s>Kaṃsa</s> was the eldest of them.

children.text: nyagrodhaśca sunāmā ca kaṅkaḥ śaṅkuśca bhūyasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then came <s>Nyagrodha</s>, <s>Sunāman</s>, <s>Kaṅka</s>, and <s>Śaṅku</s>, besides others:
<s>Ajabhū</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, <s>Yuddhamuṣṭi</s>, and <s>Sumuṣṭida</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ svasāraḥ pañcāsan kaṃsā kaṃsavatī tathā ||
children.translated_text: Their sisters were five: <s>Kaṃsā</s>, <s>Kaṃsavatī</s>,

children.text: sutantū rāṣṭrapālī ca kaṅkā ceti varāṅganāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sutantū</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrapālī</s>, and <s>Kaṅkā</s>, women of excellent form.
<s>Ugrasena</s>, together with his offspring, has been explained as descended from <s>Kukura</s>.
Then the son of <s>Bhajamāna</s> was <s>Vidūratha</s>, foremost among chariot-fighters.
<s>Rājādhideva</s> and <s>Śūra</s> were sons of <s>Vidūratha</s>.
Two sons, equal to gods, were born to <s>Rājādhideva</s>:
<s>Śoṇāśva</s> and <s>Śvetavāhana</s>, eminent in discipline and vows.
<s>Śoṇāśva</s>'s sons were five heroes, skilled in battle:

children.text: śamī ca devaśarmā ca nikuntaḥ śakraśatrujit ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śamī</s>, <s>Devaśarmā</s>, <s>Nikunta</s>, and <s>Śakraśatrujit</s>.
<s>Śamī</s>'s son was <s>Pratikṣatra</s>, and <s>Pratikṣatra</s>'s son
was <s>Pratikṣetra</s>; his son was <s>Bhoja</s>, and <s>Hṛdīka</s> was his child.
<s>Hṛdīka</s> had ten sons of terrible prowess.
<s>Kṛtavarman</s> was the eldest among them, and <s>Śatadhanvan</s> the middle one.
There were also <s>Devārha</s>, <s>Nābha</s>, <s>Bhīṣaṇa</s>, and mighty <s>Mahābala</s>,
<s>Ajāta</s>, <s>Vanajāta</s>, <s>Kanīyaka</s>, and <s>Karambhaka</s>.
The learned <s>Kambalabarhiṣa</s> was born as the son of <s>Devārha</s>.
<s>Asāmañjā</s> was his son, and <s>Tamojāta</s> was his child.
The three sons of <s>Ajāta</s> were valiant and very famous:
<s>Sudaṃṣṭra</s>, <s>Sunābha</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; they are regarded as <s>Andhakas</s>.
A man who constantly recites this lineage of the <s>Andhakas</s>
obtains for himself an extensive lineage, rich in offspring.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: gāndhārī caiva mādrī ca vṛṣṇibhārye babhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gāndhārī</s> and <s>Mādrī</s> became the wives of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>.
<s>Gāndhārī</s> gave birth to <s>Sumitra</s>, who delighted his friends.

children.text: mādrī yudhājitaṃ putraṃ tato vai devamīḍhuṣam
children.translated_text: <s>Mādrī</s> bore as sons <s>Yudhājit</s>, then <s>Devamīḍhuṣa</s>,
<s>Anamitra</s>, <s>Śibi</s>, and the fifth, <s>Kṛtalakṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: anamitrasuto nighno nighnasyāpi tu dvau sutau
children.translated_text: <s>Anamitra</s>'s son was <s>Nighna</s>; <s>Nighna</s> also had two sons,
<s>Prasena</s>, of great valor, and <s>Śaktisena</s>, those two.
The <s>Syamantaka</s>, <s>Prasena</s>'s unsurpassed jewel-gem,
became, on earth, the king of all gems.

children.text: hṛdi kṛtvā tu bahuśo maṇiṃ tamabhiyācitaḥ
children.translated_text: Although he repeatedly longed for that gem in his heart,

children.text: govindo'pi na taṃ lebhe śakto'pi na jahāra saḥ ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Govinda</s> did not obtain it; though able, he did not seize it by force.
Once <s>Prasena</s>, adorned with it, went hunting.

children.text: yathāśabdaṃ sa śuśrāva bile sattvena pūrite ||
children.translated_text: Following the sound, he heard it in a cave filled with a living creature.

children.text: tataḥ praviśya sa bilaṃ praseno hy ṛkṣamaikṣata
children.translated_text: Then, entering the cave, <s>Prasena</s> saw a bear.

children.text: ṛkṣaḥ prasenaṃ ca tathā ṛkṣaṃ caiva prasenajit ||
children.translated_text: The bear saw <s>Prasena</s>, and likewise <s>Prasenajit</s> saw the bear.

children.text: hatvā ṛkṣaḥ prasenaṃ tu tatastaṃ maṇimādadāt
children.translated_text: After killing <s>Prasena</s>, the bear then took that jewel.
Unseen, he was killed by him then, after he had gone inside the cave.

children.text: prasenaṃ tu hataṃ jñātvā govindaḥ pariśaṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Govinda</s> knew that <s>Prasena</s> had been killed, he came under suspicion.
"Clearly <s>Prasena</s> was killed by <s>Govinda</s> because of the jewel."
<s>Prasena</s> had gone to the forest adorned with the jewel-gem.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa hatastena govindaḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Seeing him, he was killed by that one; then <s>Govinda</s> spoke in reply:

children.text: hanmi cainaṃ durācāraṃ śatrubhūtaṃ hi vṛṣṇiṣu ||
children.translated_text: "I shall kill this evil-doer, for he has become an enemy among the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>."

children.text: atha dīrgheṇa kālena mṛgayāṃ nirgataḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after a long time, he again went out hunting.
And by chance <s>Govinda</s> came near the cave.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu mahāśabdaṃ sa cakre ṛkṣarāḍbalī
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the mighty king of bears made a great noise.

children.text: śabdaṃ śrutvā tu govindaḥ khaḍgapāṇiḥ praviśya saḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the noise, <s>Govinda</s>, sword in hand, entered.
He saw <s>Jāmbavān</s>, that very mighty king of bears.
Then swiftly <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, straightaway,
seized <s>Jāmbavān</s>, the lord of bears, his eyes reddened with anger.
Then the bear praised him, the lord, through his deeds as <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Then the blessed lord, being pleased, favored him with a boon.
<s>Jāmbavān</s> said:
"I desire death from you, O lord, by the stroke of your discus.

children.text: kanyā ceyaṃ mama śubhā bhartāraṃ tvāmavāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: And may this auspicious daughter of mine obtain you as her husband.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ maṇiḥ prasenaṃ tu hatvā prāpto mayā prabho ||
children.translated_text: This jewel, O lord, is the one I obtained after <s>Prasena</s> was killed."

children.text: tataḥ sa jāmbavantaṃ taṃ hatvā cakreṇa vai prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the lord struck down that <s>Jāmbavān</s> with his discus.
Having accomplished his task, the mighty-armed one brought back the jewel together with the girl.
He gave it to <s>Satrājit</s> in the assembly of all the <s>Sātvatas</s>.
By that false accusation this <s>Janārdana</s> had been distressed.
Then all those <s>Yādavas</s> spoke to <s>Vāsudeva</s>:
"Our belief had indeed been that <s>Prasena</s> was killed by you."

children.text: kaikeyasya sutā bhāryā daśa satrājitaḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: The daughter of the <s>Kaikeya</s> was the wife of <s>Satrājit</s>; he had ten auspicious wives.
From them were born his sons, a famous hundred and one.
They were renowned and very heroic; <s>Bhaṅgakāra</s> was the eldest.
Then from <s>Vratavatī</s>, by <s>Bhaṅgakāra</s>, the firstborn,
were born three delicate girls, lotus-eyed.

children.text: satyabhāmā varā strīṇāṃ vratinī ca dṛḍhavratā
children.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, the best of women, <s>Vratinī</s>, firm in vows,

children.text: tathā padmāvatī caiva tāśca kṛṣṇāya so 'dadāt ||
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Padmāvatī</s>; he gave them to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
From <s>Anamitra</s> was born <s>Śini</s>, from the youngest, the delight of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.
<s>Satyaka</s> was his son, and <s>Sātyaki</s> was his son.
<s>Satyavān</s> and <s>Yuyudhāna</s> were mighty descendants of <s>Śini</s>.
<s>Asaṅga</s> was the son of <s>Yuyudhāna</s>, and <s>Dyumni</s> was his son.
From <s>Dyumni</s> came the son <s>Yugaṃdhara</s>; thus the <s>Śaineyas</s> are proclaimed.
This lineage of <s>Anamitra</s>, born in the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> race, has been explained.
To <s>Anamitra</s> was born on earth the heroic <s>Yudhājit</s>.

children.text: anyau tu tanayau vīrau vṛṣabhaḥ kṣatra eva ca ||
children.translated_text: And there were two other heroic sons, <s>Vṛṣabha</s> and <s>Kṣatra</s>.
<s>Vṛṣabha</s> obtained as wife the daughter of the king of <s>Kāśī</s>.
In <s>Jayantī</s>, the auspicious son <s>Jayanta</s> was born.
<s>Sadāyajña</s> was very heroic, learned, and fond of guests.
From <s>Sadāyajña</s> was born <s>Akrūra</s>, exceedingly generous.
<s>Ratnā</s> was the daughter of <s>Śaibya</s>; <s>Akrūra</s> obtained her.
He begot eleven very mighty sons.

children.text: upalambhaḥ sadālambho vṛkalo vīrya eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Upalambha</s>, <s>Sadālambha</s>, <s>Vṛkala</s>, and <s>Vīrya</s>,
<s>Savītara</s>, <s>Sadāpakṣa</s>, <s>Śatrughna</s>, and <s>Vārimejaya</s>,
<s>Dharmabhṛt</s> and <s>Dharmavarman</s>, and <s>Dhṛṣṭamāna</s> likewise:

children.text: sarve ca pratihotāro ratnāyāṃ jajñire ca te ||
children.translated_text: all these, sacrificial priests, were born from <s>Ratnā</s>.
From <s>Akrūra</s>, in <s>Ugrasenā</s>, two sons were born, increasers of the family:
<s>Devavān</s> and <s>Upadeva</s>, both resembling gods.

children.text: aśvinyāṃ ca tataḥ putrāḥ pṛthur vipṛthureva ca
children.translated_text: Then in <s>Aśvinī</s> sons were born: <s>Pṛthu</s> and <s>Vipṛthu</s>,
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, <s>Supārśvaka</s>, and <s>Gaveṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: vṛṣṭinemiḥ sudharmā ca tathā śaryātireva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣṭinemi</s>, <s>Sudharmā</s>, and likewise <s>Śaryāti</s>,
<s>Abhūmi</s>, <s>Varjabhūmi</s>, <s>Śramiṣṭha</s>, and <s>Śravaṇa</s> as well.
Whoever knows this false accusation as removed from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
is not to be cursed by any false curse at all.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
An <s>Aikṣvākī</s> woman bore <s>Śūra</s>, famous, wonderful, and bountiful.
From the manly <s>Śūra</s>, ten sons were born in <s>Bhojā</s>.
First came the mighty-armed <s>Vasudeva</s>, called <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>.
Then <s>Devamārga</s> was born, and after him <s>Devaśravas</s>.
<s>Anādhṛṣṭi</s> and <s>Śini</s>, <s>Nanda</s> together with <s>Sṛñjaya</s>,

children.text: śyāmaḥ śamīkaḥ saṃyūpaḥ pañca cāsya varāṅganāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śyāma</s>, <s>Śamīka</s>, and <s>Saṃyūpa</s>; and he had five excellent women.
<s>Śrutakīrti</s> and <s>Pṛthā</s>, <s>Śrutādevī</s>, <s>Śrutaśravas</s>,
and <s>Rājādhidevī</s> likewise: these five were mothers of heroes.

children.text: kṛtasya tu śrutādevī sugrīvaṃ suṣuve sutam
children.translated_text: <s>Śrutādevī</s>, wife of <s>Kṛta</s>, bore the son <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: kaikeyyāṃ śrutakīrtyāṃ tu jajñe so 'nuvrato nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Śrutakīrti</s>, the <s>Kaikeyī</s>, the king <s>Anuvrata</s> was born.
In <s>Śrutaśravas</s>, <s>Sunītha</s> of the <s>Caidya</s> came into being.
He became a frequent follower of <s>dharma</s> and a crusher of enemies.

children.text: atha sakhyena vṛddhe'sau kuntibhoje sutāṃ dadau
children.translated_text: Then, when friendship had grown, he gave the daughter to <s>Kuntibhoja</s>.
Thus <s>Kuntī</s>, <s>Pṛthā</s>, the sister of <s>Vasudeva</s>, has been described.

children.text: vasudevena sā dattā pāṇḍorbhāryā hy aninditā
children.translated_text: She, the blameless one, was given by <s>Vasudeva</s> as the wife of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
For the sake of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> she bore sons of the gods, great chariot-warriors.
From <s>Dharma</s> <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> was born; from <s>Vāyu</s> <s>Vṛkodara</s> was born.
And from <s>Indra</s> came <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor.
But in <s>Mādrī</s>, we have heard, two were born from the <s>Aśvins</s>.
<s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s>, endowed with beauty, conduct, and virtue.

children.text: rohiṇī pauravī nāma bhāryā hy ānakadundubheḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s>, named <s>Pauravī</s>, was the wife of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>.

children.text: lebhe jyeṣṭhaṃ sutaṃ rāmaṃ sāraṇaṃ ca sutaṃ priyam ||
children.translated_text: She obtained as her eldest son <s>Rāma</s>, and the beloved son <s>Sāraṇa</s>.
<s>Durdama</s>, <s>Damana</s>, <s>Subhru</s>, <s>Piṇḍāraka</s>, and <s>Mahāhanu</s>,

children.text: citrākṣyau dve kumāryau tu rohiṇyāṃ jajñire tadā ||
children.translated_text: and then two bright-eyed daughters were born to <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
In <s>Devakī</s> there were born to <s>Śauri</s> <s>Suṣeṇa</s> and also <s>Kīrtimān</s>,
<s>Udāsī</s>, <s>Bhadrasena</s>, and likewise <s>Ṛṣivāsa</s>,
and <s>Bhadravideha</s> as the sixth; <s>Kaṃsa</s> killed them all.

children.text: prathamā yā amāvāsyā vārṣikī tu bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: On the first new-moon day of the rainy season that was to come,

children.text: tasyāṃ jajñe mahābāhuḥ pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: on that day the mighty-armed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the former <s>Prajāpati</s>, was born.
His younger sister was dark <s>Subhadrā</s>, speaker of auspicious words.

children.text: devakyāṃ tu mahātejā jajñe śūro mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in <s>Devakī</s> the greatly radiant, very famous <s>Śūra</s> was born.
In <s>Tāmrā</s> was born <s>Sahadeva</s>, a <s>Śauri</s> and upholder of the family.
<s>Devarakṣitā</s> obtained a son, <s>Upāsaṅgadhara</s>.

children.text: ekāṃ kanyāṃ ca subhagāṃ kaṃsastām abhyaghātayat ||
children.translated_text: She also had one fortunate daughter; <s>Kaṃsa</s> struck her down.

children.text: vijayaṃ rocamānaṃ ca vardhamānaṃ tu devalam
children.translated_text: <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Rocamāna</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s>, and <s>Devala</s>,

children.text: ete sarve mahātmāno hy upadevyāṃ prajajñire ||
children.translated_text: all these great-souled ones were born to <s>Upadevī</s>.
And the great-souled <s>Avagāha</s> was born to <s>Vṛkadevī</s>.

children.text: vṛkadevyāṃ svayaṃ jajñe nandako nāma nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Vṛkadevī</s> herself was born one named <s>Nandaka</s>.
O king, <s>Devakī</s> bore <s>Madana</s> as her seventh son,
the greatly fortunate <s>Gaveṣaṇa</s>, unconquered in battles.

children.text: śraddhādevyā vihāre tu vane hi vicaranpurā
children.translated_text: Once, while wandering in the forest in <s>Śraddhādevī</s>'s pleasure-ground,
<s>Śauri</s> begot on a Vaiśyā a son, <s>Kauśika</s>, the eldest.
<s>Sutanū</s> and <s>Ratharājī</s> were wives of <s>Śauri</s>.
<s>Puṇḍra</s> and <s>Kapila</s> too were mighty sons of <s>Vasudeva</s>.
There was a Niṣāda named <s>Jarā</s>, the first, an archer.
And <s>Saubhadra</s> and <s>Bhava</s> became two beings of great strength.
The son of <s>Devabhāga</s> too is remembered by the name <s>Uddhava</s>.
They say that <s>Paṇḍita</s> was the foremost one born from <s>Devaśravas</s>.
The famous Ikṣvāku woman obtained offspring from <s>Anādhṛṣṭi</s>.
From him was born <s>Śrāddha</s>, with purified courage, a slayer of enemies.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, pleased, gave a son to childless <s>Karūṣā</s>,
the greatly fortunate <s>Sucandra</s>, vigorous and very strong.

children.text: jāmbavatyāḥ sutāv etau dvau ca satkṛtalakṣaṇau
children.translated_text: These two were sons of <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, both marked with noble signs,
<s>Cārudeṣṇa</s> and <s>Sāmba</s>, vigorous and very strong.
<s>Tantipāla</s> and <s>Tanti</s> were both sons of <s>Nandana</s>.
The four sons of <s>Śamīka</s> were bold and very powerful:
<s>Virāja</s>, <s>Dhanu</s>, <s>Śyāma</s>, and also <s>Sṛñjaya</s>.
<s>Śyāma</s> had no offspring, while <s>Śamīka</s> went to the forest.
Rejecting the state of a <s>Bhoja</s>, he attained the rank of a royal seer.
Whoever regularly celebrates the birth and rise of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
and whoever constantly hears it, that person is freed from all sins.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: atha devo mahādevaḥ pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the god, the great god, the ancient <s>Kṛṣṇa Prajāpati</s>,
that lord of gods, is born here among human beings for the sake of divine play.
Through the austerity of <s>Vasudeva</s>, the lotus-eyed one was born in <s>Devakī</s>,
four-armed then, of divine form, blazing with splendor.
Seeing the god marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and with divine signs,

children.text: uvāca vasudevastaṃ rūpaṃ saṃhara vai prabho ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vasudeva</s> said to him, 'Withdraw this form, O lord.'
'I am afraid, O god, of <s>Kaṃsa</s>; therefore I say this to you.
My elder sons, of terrible valor, have been killed by him.'
Hearing the words of <s>Vasudeva</s>, <s>Acyuta</s> withdrew his form.
Then <s>Śauri</s>, having received permission, took him to the house of <s>Nandagopa</s>.
Having given him to <s>Nandagopa</s>, he said, 'Let him be protected.'
'From this there will be every blessing for the <s>Yādavas</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ tu garbho devakyāṃ jātaḥ kaṃsaṃ haniṣyati ||
children.translated_text: This child born in <s>Devakī</s> will kill <s>Kaṃsa</s>.'
The sages said:

children.text: ka eṣa vasudevastu devakī ca yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: Who, then, is this <s>Vasudeva</s>, and who is famous <s>Devakī</s>?
Who is this <s>Nandagopa</s>, and who is <s>Yaśodā</s>, firm in her vow?

children.text: yo viṣṇuṃ janayāmāsa yaṃ ca tātetyabhāṣata
children.translated_text: Who begot <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and whom did he address as 'father'?

children.text: yā garbhaṃ janayāmāsa yā cainaṃ tv abhyavardhayat ||
children.translated_text: Who bore him in the womb, and who brought him up?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The <s>Puruṣa</s> was <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and <s>Aditi</s> is remembered as his beloved.
<s>Kaśyapa</s> was a portion of <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Aditi</s> likewise of the earth.
Then the mighty-armed one fulfilled the desires of <s>Devakī</s>,
those which she had always longed for concerning the unborn great-souled one.

children.text: so 'vatīrṇo mahīṃ devaḥ praviṣṭo mānuṣīṃ tanum
children.translated_text: That god descended to the earth and entered a human body,
bewildering all beings by <s>yogamāyā</s> (the power of yogic illusion), he whose self is yoga.

children.text: naṣṭe dharme tathā jajñe viṣṇurvṛṣṇikule prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>dharma</s> (normative order) had perished, lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> was born in the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> lineage,
to establish <s>dharma</s> (normative order) and to destroy the <s>asuras</s> (demons).

children.text: rukmiṇī satyabhāmā ca satyā nāgnajitī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, and <s>Satyā Nāgnajitī</s>,

children.text: subhāmā ca tathā śaibyā gāndhārī lakṣmaṇā tathā ||
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Subhāmā</s>, <s>Śaibyā</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>,

children.text: mitravindā ca kālindī devī jāmbavatī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Mitravindā</s>, <s>Kālindī</s>, and queen <s>Jāmbavatī</s>,

children.text: suśīlā ca tathā mādrī kauśalyā vijayā tathā
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Suśīlā</s>, <s>Mādrī</s>, <s>Kauśalyā</s>, and <s>Vijayā</s>,
and sixteen thousand queens beginning with these,
<s>Rukmiṇī</s> gave birth to sons skilled in battle.

children.text: cārudeṣṇaṃ raṇe śūraṃ pradyumnaṃ ca mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>, brave in battle, and mighty <s>Pradyumna</s>;

children.text: sucāruṃ bhadracāruṃ ca sudeṣṇaṃ bhadrameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Sucāru</s>, <s>Bhadracāru</s>, <s>Sudeṣṇa</s>, and <s>Bhadra</s> as well,
<s>Paraśu</s>, <s>Cārugupta</s>, <s>Cārubhadra</s>, and <s>Sucāruka</s>,

children.text: cāruhāsaṃ kaniṣṭhaṃ ca kanyāṃ cārumatīṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Cāruhāsa</s>, the youngest, and also a daughter, <s>Cārumatī</s>.
To <s>Satyabhāmā</s> were born <s>Bhānu</s>, whose eyes were like bees,
<s>Rohita</s>, <s>Dīptimān</s>, <s>Tāmra</s>, <s>Cakra</s>, and <s>Jalaṃdhama</s>.
Four younger sisters of theirs were born,
and <s>Jāmbavatī</s>'s son was born: <s>Sāmba</s>, splendid in battle.
<s>Mitravān</s>, <s>Mitravinda</s>, and <s>Mitravindā</s>, a beautiful woman,

children.text: mitrabāhuḥ sunīthaśca nāgnajityāḥ prajā hi sā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mitrabāhu</s> and <s>Sunītha</s>: these were the children of <s>Nāgnajitī</s>.
Learn that there were thousands of sons such as these,
one hundred times one hundred thousand sons of that wise one;
and eighty thousand sons of <s>Vāsudeva</s>,

children.text: lakṣamekaṃ tathā proktaṃ putrāṇāṃ ca dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and one lakh of sons is likewise declared, O best of twice-born men.

children.text: upasaṅgasya tu sutau vajraḥ saṃkṣipta eva ca
children.translated_text: The two sons of <s>Upasaṅga</s> were <s>Vajra</s> and <s>Saṃkṣipta</s>;
<s>Bhūrīndrasena</s> and <s>Bhūri</s> were both sons of <s>Gaveṣaṇa</s>.
The heir of <s>Pradyumna</s>, born from the Vidarbha princess, was supreme in intelligence:
<s>Aniruddha</s>, unrestrained in battle, was born to him, marked by the deer emblem.
From the daughter of <s>Supārśva</s>, a princess of <s>Kāśī</s>, mighty <s>Sāmba</s> obtained
five heroic sons, of true nature, who are celebrated as gods.
There were three crores of valiant, great-souled <s>Yādavas</s>,
and sixty hundred-thousands, heroic and very mighty.

children.text: devāṃśāḥ sarva eveha hy utpannāste mahaujasaḥ
children.translated_text: All of them, very powerful, were born here as portions of the gods;

children.text: devāsure hatā ye ca tv asurā ye mahābalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the mighty asuras who had been slain in the wars of gods and asuras,
being born here among human beings, oppressed all people.
For the sake of destroying them, he was born in the <s>Yādava</s> clan.
There was one hundred families of the great-souled <s>Yādavas</s>,
and this whole clan, as long as it exists, belongs to the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> lineage.

children.text: viṣṇusteṣāṃ praṇetā ca prabhutve ca vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is their leader and stands established in sovereignty;
all the <s>Yādavas</s> are said to abide by his command.
The seers said:
The Seven Seers, <s>Kubera</s>, and the yakṣa <s>Māṇicara</s>,
<s>Śālaki</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and the perfected <s>Dhanvantari</s>,
and the primordial god <s>Viṣṇu</s>: together with these divinities,

children.text: kimarthaṃ saṃghaśo bhūtāḥ smṛtāḥ sambhūtayaḥ kati ||
children.translated_text: for what purpose did beings arise in groups, and how many births are remembered?
How many other future manifestations of the great-souled one will there be?
When the Brahmins and Kṣatriyas have become pacified, for what purpose is he born here?
The purpose for which <s>Viṣṇu</s>, best of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Andhakas</s>, came into being here,
again and again among human beings: tell that to us who ask.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Abandoning his divine body, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is born here among human beings;

children.text: yuge tv atha parāvṛtte kāle praśithile prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the age has turned and time has become slack, the lord appears.
In the crushings of gods and asuras, <s>Hari</s>, the lord, is born.
When the daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> formerly ruled the three worlds,
and when, in former times, the three worlds were successively occupied by <s>Bali</s>,
there was the highest friendship of the gods with the asuras.
The world was exceedingly disturbed, full of asuras associated with the age;
and the gods and asuras alike stood under the command of those two.
A conflict, fierce and very terrible, grew for the crushing of <s>Bali</s>,
a great and dreadful destroyer of both gods and asuras.
To establish the order of <s>dharma</s>, he is born here among human beings,
then because of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s curse, in connection with the gods and asuras.
The sages said:
How, in connection with the gods and asuras, did he of himself undertake action?

children.text: devāsuraṃ yathā vṛttaṃ tannaḥ prabrūhi pṛcchatām ||
children.translated_text: Tell us, who ask, how the conflict of gods and asuras occurred.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Those most terrible battles were on account of their shares;

children.text: varāhādyā daśa dvau ca śaṇḍāmarkāntare smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: twelve, beginning with <s>Varāha</s>, are remembered in the interval of <s>Śaṇḍa</s> and <s>Amarka</s>.
Hear them by name, briefly, as I wish to state them:
the first was <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, and the second was <s>Vāmana</s>;
the third was <s>Varāha</s>, and the fourth the churning for nectar;
the fifth battle arose as the <s>Tārakāmaya</s>;
the sixth was called <s>Āḍībaka</s>, and the seventh the <s>Tripura</s> battle;
the eighth among them was called <s>Andhaka</s>, and the ninth was the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>;
and the tenth was that of <s>Dhātṛ</s>; after that, the <s>Hālāhala</s> is remembered,
and the twelfth among them was the famed and terrible <s>Kolāhala</s>.
The daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> was cast down by <s>Nārasiṃha</s>;
<s>Bali</s> was bound by <s>Vāmana</s> when he had once stridden over the three worlds.

children.text: hiraṇyākṣo hato dvaṃdve pratighāte tu daivataiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> was slain in combat, in the counterstroke by the gods;

children.text: daṃṣṭrayā tu varāheṇa samudrastu dvidhā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by <s>Varāha</s>'s tusk the ocean was split in two.
<s>Prahlāda</s> was defeated in battle by <s>Indra</s> at the churning for nectar;
<s>Virocana</s>, son of <s>Prahlāda</s>, was ever intent on killing <s>Indra</s>.
In the <s>Tārakāmaya</s>, <s>Indra</s> himself overcame him by valor and slew him;
he could not always endure the whole company of the gods.

children.text: nihatā dānavāḥ sarve trailokye tryambakeṇa tu
children.translated_text: All the <s>Dānavas</s> in the three worlds were slain by <s>Tryambaka</s>;
asuras, piśācas, and dānavas too in the battle with <s>Andhaka</s>
were slain on every side by gods, humans, and their own ancestors.
Terrible <s>Vṛtra</s>, joined with the dānavas, was slain in the <s>Hālāhala</s>.
Then, with <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s aid, he was driven back by great <s>Indra</s>;
skilled in yoga and concealed by magic, he was slain by great <s>Indra</s> at the banner,
after entering the banner-mark: <s>Vipracitti</s> together with his younger brother.
and the <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s>, restrained and indeed assembled together,
the mighty one, surrounded by the gods, conquered them all amid the tumult.
At the concluding bath of the sacrifice, <s>Śaṇḍa</s> and <s>Amarka</s> were seen by the divine beings.

children.text: ete devāsure vṛttāḥ saṃgrāmā dvādaśaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: These, then, were the twelve battles that occurred between gods and asuras.
They brought destruction upon gods and asuras, yet were for the welfare of creatures.
King <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> shone for an arbuda of years,
and for seventy-two further niyutas besides,
and eighty thousand years, having attained sovereignty over the three worlds.
In turn, <s>Bali</s> then became king for ten thousand years,
and for sixty thousand years, and twenty niyutas besides.
For as long as royal authority belonged to <s>Bali</s>,

children.text: tāvatkālaṃ tu prahlādo nivṛtto hy asuraiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: for just that long <s>Prahlāda</s> had withdrawn together with the asuras.
These three should be known as the <s>Indras</s> of the very powerful asuras.
All this realm belonged to the <s>Daityas</s> for ten yugas again.
This threefold world is calmly protected by great <s>Indra</s>.
All this was without rival for ten yugas again.
When that threefold world of <s>Prahlāda</s> had been destroyed through the turn of time,
and when, in turn, the three worlds had come into the possession of <s>Pākaśāsana</s>,
then <s>Śukra</s> abandoned the asuras and went to the gods.
When <s>Kāvya</s> had then gone to the gods at the sacrifice, the sons of <s>Diti</s> called to him:

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ no miṣatāṃ rājyaṃ tyaktvā yajñaṃ punargataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Why, while we look on, have you abandoned our kingdom and gone again to the sacrifice?

children.text: sthātuṃ na śaknumo hy atra praviśāmo rasātalam
children.translated_text: We cannot remain here; we shall enter <s>Rasātala</s>."
Thus addressed, he spoke to the despondent <s>Daityas</s>, consoling them with his words:

children.text: mā bhaiṣṭa dhārayiṣyāmi tejasā svena vo 'surāḥ
children.translated_text: "Do not be afraid, asuras. I shall sustain you by my own power.
Mantras, herbs, elixirs, wealth, and whatever is supreme,

children.text: kṛtsnāni mayi tiṣṭhanti pādasteṣāṃ sureṣu vai
children.translated_text: all these remain in me; only a quarter of them is among the gods.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ vaḥ pradāsyāmi yuṣmadarthe dhṛtā mayā ||
children.translated_text: All that I shall give to you, for I have held it for your sake."
Then the gods, seeing them protected by wise <s>Kāvya</s>,
consulted together, being fully aware and eager to seize them:

children.text: kāvyo hy eṣa idaṃ sarvaṃ vyāvartayati no balāt
children.translated_text: "This <s>Kāvya</s> is forcibly turning all this away from us.
Good; let us go quickly, before he teaches them.
Having slain them by force, let us send the survivors down to <s>Pātāla</s>."

children.text: tato devāstu saṃrabdhā dānavān upasṛtya ha ||
children.translated_text: Then the enraged gods approached the <s>Dānavas</s>.
And as they were being struck down, those asuras ran straight to <s>Kāvya</s>.

children.text: tataḥ kāvyastu tāndṛṣṭvā tūrṇaṃ devair abhidrutān ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kāvya</s>, seeing them being swiftly attacked by the gods,
withdrew the protection gathered by <s>Kāvya</s>; and the gods, though pressed by the asuras,
seeing <s>Kāvya</s> standing there, fearlessly struck down the asuras.
Then <s>Kāvya</s>, the Brahmin, after reflecting on beneficial speech,
then spoke to them, remembering what had happened before:

children.text: trailokyaṃ vo hṛtaṃ sarvaṃ vāmanena tribhiḥ kramaiḥ
children.translated_text: "All your three worlds were taken by <s>Vāmana</s> in three strides.
<s>Bali</s> was bound, <s>Jambha</s> was killed, and <s>Virocana</s> was slain.
The great asuras were killed by the gods in the twelve battles.
By those various means most of your leaders were destroyed.

children.text: kiṃcicchīṣṭāstu yūyaṃ vai yuddhaṃ māstviti me matam
children.translated_text: You who remain are only a few; my view is that there should be no battle.
Remain according to the turn of time, while I tell you the policy to follow.
I shall go to <s>Mahādeva</s> for mantras that bring victory.
Then, after receiving from the god <s>Maheśvara</s> mantras that cannot be opposed,
we shall fight the gods again, and then you shall indeed obtain victory."
Then, after they had made this agreement, the asuras spoke to the gods:
"We have all laid down our weapons; we are without armor and without chariots.
We shall practice austerity in the forest, covered with bark garments."

children.text: prahlādasya vacaḥ śrutvā satyābhivyāhṛtaṃ tu tat ||
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Prahlāda</s>'s words, which had truly been spoken,

children.text: tato devā nyavartanta vijvarā muditāśca te
children.translated_text: the gods then turned back, free from fever and delighted.
When the <s>Daityas</s> had laid down their weapons, the gods withdrew at that time.
Then <s>Kāvya</s> said to them, "Wait for some time,
free from arrogance and devoted to austerity, for a time that will accomplish the aim.
Staying in my father's hermitage, wait for me, <s>Dānavas</s>."
Having given this instruction to the asuras, <s>Kāvya</s> approached <s>Mahādeva</s>.
<s>Śukra</s> said:

children.text: mantrānicchāmyahaṃ deva ye na santi bṛhaspatau
children.translated_text: "I desire mantras, O god, which <s>Bṛhaspati</s> does not possess,
for the defeat of the gods and for the victory of the asuras."
Thus addressed, the god said, "Practice a vow, O <s>Bhārgava</s>.
For a full thousand years, with your head downward,

children.text: yadi pāsyasi bhadraṃ te tato mantrānavāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: if you drink smoke from husks, good fortune to you, then you will obtain the mantras."
Saying "So be it" and receiving permission, <s>Śukra</s>, the delight of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s line,
touched the god's feet and spoke the word, "Certainly."

children.text: vrataṃ carāmyahaṃ deva tvayādiṣṭo'dya vai prabho ||
children.translated_text: "I shall practice the vow, O god, exactly as you have commanded today, O lord."
Then <s>Kuṇḍadhāra</s>, assigned by the god, became his smoke-maker.

children.text: tadā tasmingate śukre hy asurāṇāṃ hitāya vai
children.translated_text: When <s>Śukra</s> had gone there for the welfare of the asuras,
he remained there before <s>Maheśvara</s>, practicing celibacy for the sake of the mantras.

children.text: tadbuddhvā nītipūrvaṃ tu rājye nyaste tadāsuraiḥ
children.translated_text: Learning that the asuras, with policy in mind, had laid aside their kingdom,
the gods, seizing that opening in anger, attacked them then,
all armored and armed, with <s>Bṛhaspati</s> at their head.
Seeing the gods once more with weapons raised, the host of asuras
suddenly leapt up, frightened, and spoke these words to them:
"When weapons had been laid down, when safety had been granted, and when our teacher had undertaken his vow,

children.text: dattvā bhavanto hy abhayaṃ samprāptā no jighāṃsayā ||
children.translated_text: you, after granting us safety, have now come intending to kill us."
We gods are without a teacher and stand here having laid aside our weapons,
wearing bark garments and black antelope skins, without rites and without possessions.

children.text: raṇe vijetuṃ devāṃśca na śakṣyāmaḥ kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: We shall not be able in any way to conquer the gods in battle.
Without fighting, we shall go for refuge to the mother of <s>Kāvya</s>.
Let us pass through this hardship until our guru comes back to us.

children.text: nivṛtte ca tathā śukre yotsyāmo daṃśitāyudhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when <s>Śukra</s> has returned, we shall fight, clad in armor and armed.
Having thus spoken to one another, they then sought refuge with the mother of <s>Kāvya</s>.
Then, frightened, they approached her, and she granted them freedom from fear.

children.text: na bhetavyaṃ na bhetavyaṃ bhayaṃ tyajata dānavāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Do not be afraid, do not be afraid; cast off your fear, O <s>dānavas</s> (demons).

children.text: matsaṃnidhau vartatāṃ vo na bhīr bhavitumarhati ||
children.translated_text: While you remain in my presence, there should be no fear for you.'
Then, seeing those asuras accepted by her, the gods
attacked them forcibly, without considering relative strength and weakness.
Then, seeing those asuras being harried at that time by the gods,
the goddess, angered, said to the gods, 'I shall make you bereft of <s>Indra</s>.'
Having gathered all the materials, she then performed an abhichāra rite against <s>Indra</s>.
The powerful goddess, rich in austerity and joined with yoga, paralyzed him.

children.text: tatastaṃ stambhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā indraṃ devāśca mūkavat
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Indra</s> paralyzed and the gods as if mute,

children.text: prādravanta tato bhītā indraṃ dṛṣṭvā vaśīkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: they fled away in fear when they saw <s>Indra</s> brought under control.
When the hosts of gods had gone, <s>Viṣṇu</s> addressed <s>Śakra</s>:

children.text: māṃ tvaṃ praviśa bhadraṃ te nayiṣye tvāṃ surottama ||
children.translated_text: 'Enter into me. Fortune be yours; I shall lead you away, O best of gods.'
Thus addressed, <s>Purandara</s> then entered into <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: viṣṇunā rakṣitaṃ dṛṣṭvā devī kruddhā vaco 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him protected by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the goddess, angered, spoke these words:

children.text: eṣā tvāṃ viṣṇunā sārdhaṃ dahāmi maghavanbalāt
children.translated_text: 'Now, together with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, I shall burn you by force, O <s>Maghavan</s>,
while all beings look on; let my power of austerity be seen.'
Overpowered by her, those two gods, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, were overcome.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> said to <s>Indra</s>, 'How shall we two together be released?'
<s>Indra</s> said, 'Strike her down, lord, before she burns us both.
I have been especially overpowered; strike her down quickly, for my sake, from within you.'

children.text: tataḥ samīkṣya viṣṇustāṃ strīvadhe kṛcchram āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, looking upon her, felt distress at the killing of a woman.
Then, after reflecting, he thought of the discus as the means of rescue from danger.
Then, moved by urgency, quick to act and filled with fear,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, knowing the cruel act that the goddess intended,
angrily took up his own weapon and cut off her head out of fear.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā strīvadhaṃ ghoraṃ cukrodha bhṛgurīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that terrible killing of a woman, lord <s>Bhṛgu</s> became enraged.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s> was cursed by <s>Bhṛgu</s> at that time for the killing of his wife:
'Because, though you knew <s>dharma</s> (normative order), a woman not to be killed was slain by you,
therefore you shall be born here seven times among human beings.'
Then, because of that curse of his, whenever <s>dharma</s> (normative order) perishes again and again,
for the welfare of the world he is born here among human beings.
Having thus addressed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he quickly took up the head,
joined it again to the body, and, taking hold of it, spoke these words:

children.text: eṣā tvaṃ viṣpunā devi hatā saṃjīvayāmyaham
children.translated_text: 'O goddess, you have been killed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>; I shall bring you back to life.'
Then, having joined her with her head, he said, 'Come back to life.'

children.text: yadi kṛtsno mayā dharmo jñāyate carito'pi vā
children.translated_text: 'If <s>dharma</s> (normative order) has been wholly known or practiced by me,

children.text: tena satyena jīvasva yadi satyaṃ vadāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: by that truth live, if I speak the truth.'
Then, sprinkling her with cool waters, he said, 'Live.'
And when he had spoken, the goddess was then restored to life.
Then, seeing her like one risen from sleep, all beings
cried out with their voices in every direction, 'Well done, well done!'

children.text: evaṃ pratyāhṛtā tena devī sā bhṛguṇā tadā
children.translated_text: Thus that goddess was brought back by <s>Bhṛgu</s> at that time,
and while the gods were looking on, it seemed like a marvel.
By the unconfused <s>Bhṛgu</s> his wife was made alive again.
Seeing this, <s>Indra</s> again found no peace, because of fear of <s>Kāvya</s>.
Then, at daybreak, <s>Indra</s> said this to <s>Jayantī</s>.

children.text: saṃcintya matimān vākyaṃ svāṃ kanyāṃ pākaśāsanaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise <s>Pākaśāsana</s>, having considered the matter, spoke to his own daughter:

children.text: eṣa kāvyo hyamitrāya vrataṃ carati dāruṇam
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Kāvya</s> is performing a terrible vow for the sake of my enemy.

children.text: tenāhaṃ vyākulaḥ putri kṛto matimatā bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: By that wise one, daughter, I have been made greatly troubled.
Go and bring him to success with auspicious removals of his weariness,
and with various services pleasing to his mind, tirelessly.
Propitiate this <s>Kāvya</s> so that the brahmin may be pleased.

children.text: gaccha tvaṃ tasya dattā'si prayatnaṃ kuru matkṛte ||
children.translated_text: Go; you have been given to him. Make every effort for my sake.'

children.text: evamuktā jayantī sā vacaḥ saṃgṛhya vai pituḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Jayantī</s> accepted her father's command

children.text: agacchadyatra ghoraṃ sa tapa ārabhya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: and went to where he stood, having undertaken terrible austerity.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu pibantaṃ sā kaṇadhūmam avāṅmukham
children.translated_text: She saw him drinking smoke particles, with his face turned downward,
and being caused to fall by a <s>yakṣa</s>, dropped by <s>Kuṇḍadhāra</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ pātyamānaṃ devī kāvyamavasthitam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Kāvya</s> standing there while he was being made to fall, the goddess
saw him calming his own form through meditation, weak, and covered with ashes.

children.text: pitrā yathoktaṃ vākyaṃ sā kāvye kṛtavatī tadā ||
children.translated_text: Then she did for <s>Kāvya</s> just what her father had instructed.
With favorable words she praised him, speaking sweetly,
and at the proper times serving him with massages of his limbs and pleasant touches.
With services suited to his observance of the vow, she dwelt there for many years.
When that terrible smoke-vow of a thousand years had been completed,
<s>Bhava</s>, then pleased, invited <s>Kāvya</s> to choose a boon.
<s>Mahādeva</s> said:
'This vow has been performed by you alone and by no one else.

children.text: tasmādvai tapasā buddhyā śrutena ca balena ca ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, by austerity, intelligence, learning, and strength...'
And by your splendor you alone will overpower all the gods.
And whatever has been desired by you, O <s>brahman</s>, O descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,

children.text: prapatsyase tu tatsarvaṃ nānuvācyaṃ tu kasyacit
children.translated_text: you will obtain all of that; but it must not be told to anyone.
Through that you will become one who overpowers all, O best of twice-born men.
Having given these boons to that <s>Bhārgava</s>, <s>Bhava</s> again
gave him lordship over creatures, lordship over wealth, and indeed invulnerability.
Having obtained these boons, <s>Kāvya</s> was thrilled, the hairs of his body standing on end.
From joy there arose in him a divine hymn to <s>Maheśvara</s>,
and, standing sideways as he was, he praised <s>Nīlalohita</s>.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
Homage to the blue-throated one, to the youngest one, to the one of fair splendor,
to the licking-flamed one, to <s>Kāvya</s>, to the year, to the lord of food.
Homage to the matted-haired one, the terrible one, the tawny-eyed one, and the boon-giver,
to the praised one, to the one of good sacred fords, to the god of gods, to the swift one.
Homage to the turbaned one, the fair-faced one, the many-formed one, the creator,
to the one whose seed is wealth, to <s>Rudra</s>, to austerity itself, to the one in variegated garments.
Homage to the short one, the loose-haired one, the commander, and the red one,
to the seer, to the royal tree, and to him whose plaything is <s>Takṣaka</s>.
Homage to the thousand-headed one, the thousand-eyed one, and the bountiful one,
to the excellent one, the one of auspicious form, the white one, and the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Homage to <s>Giriśa</s>, to the sun, to the strong one, and to the drinker of ghee,
to the well-satisfied one, the well-clad one, the bowman, and the <s>Bhārgava</s>.

children.text: niṣaṅgiṇe ca tārāya svakṣāya kṣapaṇāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to the quiver-bearing one, the deliverer, the fair-eyed one, and the destroyer,

children.text: tāmrāya caiva bhīmāya ugrāya ca śivāya ca ||
children.translated_text: to the copper-colored one, and also to the fearsome, fierce, and auspicious one.
Homage to <s>Mahādeva</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, and to the auspicious one whose form is the universe,
to the golden one, the best one, the eldest one, and the middle one.
Homage to <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, to <s>Pināka</s>, to liberation, and to the absolute one,
to the hunter of deer, the skillful one, <s>Sthāṇu</s>, and the terrifying one.
Homage to the many-eyed one, the leader, the three-eyed one, and the lord,

children.text: kapāline ca vīrāya mṛtyave tryambakāya ca ||
children.translated_text: to the skull-bearer, the hero, death, and <s>Tryambaka</s>.
Homage to the brown one, the tawny one, the reddish-yellow one, and the ruddy one,
to <s>Pinākin</s>, the arrow-bearing one, the variegated one, and the red one.
Homage to the drum-like one, the one-footed one, the unborn one, and the giver of understanding,
to the forest-dweller, the householder, the renunciant, and the celibate student.

children.text: sāṃkhyāya caiva yogāya vyāpine dīkṣitāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and to <s>Yoga</s>, to the all-pervading one and the consecrated one,
to the unstruck one, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Bhavyeśa</s>, and to <s>Yama</s>.
Homage to the restrainer, the knowing one, the one most devoted to brahman, and the great seer,
to the four-footed one, the ritually pure one, the protector, and the swift-going one.
Homage to the crested one, the terrible one, the fanged one, and the maker of the universe,
to the shining one, the renowned one, the brightly blazing one, and the wise one.
Homage to the cruel one, the unaltered one, the terrifying one, and the auspicious one,

children.text: saumyāya caiva mukhyāya dhārmikāya śubhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: and also to the gentle one, the foremost one, the righteous one, and the blessed one.
Homage to the invulnerable one, the immortal one, the eternal one, and the everlasting one,
