to the active one, the distinguished one, the bearer, and the witness.
Homage to welfare, to the enduring one, to truth, and to immortality,
to the maker, to the axe, to the trident-bearer, and to the divine-eyed one.
Homage to the drinker of Soma, the drinker of ghee, the drinker of smoke, and the drinker of heat,
to the pure one, the clothed one, <s>Sadyojāta</s>, and death.
Homage to the flesh-eater, to <s>Sarva</s>, to the cloud, and to lightning,
to the one who turns away, the best one, the full one, and the wild beast.
Homage to the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, to the sacred ford, to the straight one, and to the hairy one,
to the sharp-weaponed one, the expounder, the perfectly accomplished one, and <s>Pulastya</s>.
Homage to the shining one, the fierce one, the expanded one, and the bull,
to the vow-observing one, the one joined in discipline, the pure one, and the one whose seed is raised upward.
Homage to the slayer of <s>asuras</s>, the slayer of foes, the slayer of death, and the sacrificial one,
to fire, to the discerning one, to flame, and to the stainless one.
Homage to the slayer of <s>rakṣases</s>, the slayer of beasts, the unobstructed one, and the breathing one,
to the roving one, the great one, the ocean, and the hard-to-cross one.
Homage to the black one, the victorious one, and the lord of the worlds,
to the unsupported one, the knowable one, and the one established in equality.

children.text: hiraṇyabāhave caiva vyāptāya ca mahāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to the golden-armed one, and also to the all-pervading and great one,
to the doer of good works, the overpowering one, <s>Īśāna</s>, and the fair-eyed one.
Homage to the swift-arrowed one, the one with good horses, the auspicious one, and the giver of liberation,
to the tawny one, the reddish-brown one, <s>Mahādeva</s>, and the wise one.
Homage to the great-bodied one, the blazing one, the one who makes beings cry out, and the helper,
to the firm-bowed one, the armored one, the chariot-warrior, and the protected warrior.
Homage to the lord of the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, to <s>Śukra</s>, to the one dwelling in caves, and to the creator,
to the unfailing one, the tranquil one, the wise one, and the bull.
Homage to you, blessed lord, universal one, wearer of hides;

children.text: paśūnāṃ pataye tubhyaṃ bhūtānāṃ pataye namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: homage to you, lord of animals; homage to the lord of beings.

children.text: praṇave ṛgyajuḥsāmne svāhāya ca svadhāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Praṇava</s>, to the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, to <s>Svāhā</s> and <s>Svadhā</s>,
and homage to you whose self is the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>, to you whose self is mantra.

children.text: tvaṣṭre dhātre tathā kartre cakṣuḥśrotramayāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, to <s>Dhātṛ</s>, likewise to the maker, and to the one consisting of eye and ear,
to the lord of what has been, will be, and is; homage to you whose self is action.
Homage to the <s>Vasu</s>, the <s>Sādhya</s>, the <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Āditya</s>, and the <s>Sura</s>,
and also to poison and to the <s>Marut</s>; homage to you whose self is divine.
Homage to the knower of the rites of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, to the animal, the mantra, and the herb,
and indeed to the self-born, the unborn, the unprecedented first one.

children.text: prajānāṃ pataye caiva tubhyaṃ brahmātmane namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the lord of creatures, to you whose self is <s>Brahmā</s>.
Homage to the lord of the self, the self-mastered one, and the one surpassing all lords,
to the one whose limbs are the limbs of all beings; homage to you whose self is beings.
Homage to the qualityless one, the knower of the <s>guṇas</s>, the manifest one, and the immortal one.
Homage to you, the indescribable friend, whose nature is <s>Sāṃkhya</s> (enumerative wisdom).

children.text: pṛthivyai cāntarikṣāya divyāya ca mahāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to you as earth, as midspace, as the heavenly realm, and as the great one,
as <s>Janas</s>, <s>Tapas</s>, and <s>Satya</s>; homage to you, whose self is the worlds.
Homage to you as the unmanifest, as the great principle, as the source of beings, and as the senses,
as the knower of the self and as particularity; homage to you, whose self is all.
Homage to you as the eternal one, as the mark of the self, as the subtle, and also as the other,

children.text: buddhāya vibhave caiva tubhyaṃ mokṣātmane namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as intelligence and as sovereign power; homage to you, whose self is liberation.

children.text: namaste triṣu lokeṣu namaste paratas triṣu
children.translated_text: Homage to you in the three worlds; homage to you in the three beyond them.

children.text: satyānteṣu mahādyeṣu caturṣu ca namo'stu te ||
children.translated_text: Among the four beginning with the great one and ending in truth, homage be to you.

children.text: namaḥ stotre mayā hy asminyadi na vyāhṛtaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: If, in this hymn of praise, anything has not been uttered by me as salutation,
then, since I am your devotee, O lover of <s>brahman</s>, you should forgive all of it.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having addressed in this way the lord of gods, <s>Īśvara</s>, the blue-red one,
he bent low, bowed down to him, stood with joined palms, and became silent.
<s>Bhava</s>, pleased, touched <s>Kāvya</s>'s body with his hand,
and after granting him a full vision, he disappeared right there.
Then, when that lord of gods had disappeared, he saw an attendant woman
standing at his side, <s>Jayantī</s>, and said this to her:

children.text: kasya tvaṃ subhage kā vā duḥkhite mayi duḥkhitā
children.translated_text: Whose are you, fortunate one, or who are you, grieved when I am grieving?

children.text: mahatā tapasā yuktā kimarthaṃ māṃ niṣevase ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with great austerity, for what purpose do you attend on me?

children.text: anayā saṃstuto bhaktyā praśrayeṇa damena ca
children.translated_text: Praised by you with this devotion, humility, and self-restraint,
and also with affection, fair-hipped one, I am pleased, lovely woman.
What do you desire, fair lady? What wish of yours should be fulfilled?
I will accomplish that for you today, even if it should be very difficult.
Thus addressed, she said to him: By your austerity you ought to know

children.text: cikīrṣitaṃ hi me brahmaṃstvaṃ hi vettha yathātatham ||
children.translated_text: what I wish to do, O <s>brahman</s>, for you know it exactly as it is.
Thus addressed, he looked with divine sight and said to her:

children.text: mayā saha tvaṃ suśroṇi daśa varṣāṇi bhāmini ||
children.translated_text: Together with me, fair-hipped, radiant woman, for ten years
you desire union here, unseen by all beings.
O goddess, dark as a blue lotus, worthy of a boon, left-eyed beauty,

children.text: evaṃ vṛṇoṣi kāmaṃ tvaṃ matto vai valgubhāṣiṇi ||
children.translated_text: this is the wish you choose from me, sweet-speaking one.
So be it. Let us go to my house, O lovely shining one.
Then, coming to his own house and taking <s>Jayantī</s>'s hand in marriage,
<s>Bhārgava</s> lived with that goddess for ten years,
invisible to all beings, the lord covered by <s>māyā</s> (illusion).

children.text: kṛtārthamāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā kāvyaṃ sarve diteḥ sutāḥ
children.translated_text: When all the sons of <s>Diti</s> saw that <s>Kāvya</s> had returned successful,
they gladly went to his house, wishing to see him.

children.text: yadā gatā na paśyanti māyayā saṃvṛtaṃ gurum
children.translated_text: When, though they had gone, they did not see their guru, hidden by <s>māyā</s>,
they understood that sign of his and went back as they had come.

children.text: bṛhaspatistu saṃruddhaṃ kāvyaṃ jñātvā vareṇa tu
children.translated_text: But <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, knowing that <s>Kāvya</s> had been confined by the boon
for ten years, for <s>Jayantī</s>'s satisfaction and out of desire for her welfare,
and also understanding that interval, was urged on by <s>Indra</s> for the sake of the <s>Daityas</s>.
Taking on <s>Kāvya</s>'s form, he summoned the <s>asuras</s> (demons).
Then, seeing that they had come, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> said:

children.text: svāgataṃ mama yājyānāṃ prāpto'haṃ vo hitāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Welcome, my sacrificial clients. I have arrived for your welfare.

children.text: ahaṃ vo 'dhyāpayiṣyāmi vidyāḥ prāptāstu yā mayā
children.translated_text: I will teach you the sciences that I have obtained.
Then they, delighted in mind, approached him for the sake of knowledge.
When that ten-year period had then been completed for <s>Kāvya</s>,
at the end of the term <s>Devayānī</s> was born then, according to tradition.

children.text: buddhiṃ cakre tataḥ so 'tha yājyānāṃ pratyavekṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: After that, he formed the intention of looking after his sacrificial clients.
O goddess, I am going to see my clients, bright-smiling one,
virtuous lady of wandering glance, whose long eyes show three colors.
Thus addressed, she said to him: Favor your devotees, great-vowed one.

children.text: eṣa dharmaḥ satāṃ brahmanna dharmaṃ lopayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>dharma</s> (right order) of the good, O <s>brahman</s>; I do not obstruct your <s>dharma</s>.
Then, having gone and seen the <s>asuras</s> deceived by the wise teacher of the gods
through <s>Kāvya</s>'s form, <s>Kāvya</s> then said to them:

children.text: kāvyaṃ māṃ vo vijānīdhvaṃ toṣito giriśo vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: Know me to be your <s>Kāvya</s>. Mighty <s>Giriśa</s> has been pleased.

children.text: vañcitā bata yūyaṃ vai sarve śṛṇuta dānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alas, you have been deceived. All of you, listen, <s>Dānavas</s>.

children.text: śrutvā tathā bruvāṇaṃ taṃ saṃbhrāntāste tadābhavan
children.translated_text: Hearing him speak in that way, they became alarmed then,

children.text: prekṣantas tāv ubhau tatra sthitāsīnau suvismitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: gazing at both of them there as they sat, utterly astonished.

children.text: sampramūḍhās tataḥ sarve na prābudhyanta kiṃcana
children.translated_text: Then all of them, thoroughly bewildered, understood nothing at all.
While they were bewildered, <s>Kāvya</s> then said to those <s>asuras</s>:

children.text: ācāryo vo hy ahaṃ kāvyo devācāryo 'yamaṅgirāḥ
children.translated_text: I am your teacher, <s>Kāvya</s>; this is <s>Aṅgiras</s>, the teacher of the gods.
Follow me, <s>Daityas</s>; abandon this <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: ityuktā hy asurāstena tāv ubhau samavekṣya ca
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by him, the <s>asuras</s> looked at both of them,
and when they did not know any difference between the two of them,
<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, undisturbed, rich in austerity, said to them:
I am <s>Kāvya</s>, your guru, <s>Daityas</s>; this <s>Bṛhaspati</s> has my form.
By means of my form he is bewildering you, <s>asuras</s>.

children.text: śrutvā tasya tataste vai sametya tu tato'bruvan ||
children.translated_text: Hearing his words, they then gathered together and said:

children.text: ayaṃ no daśa varṣāṇi satataṃ śāsti vai prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: This lord has constantly instructed us for ten years.
He indeed is our guru; this twice-born man is seeking an opening among us.
Then all those <s>Dānavas</s>, bowing down and praising him,
accepted his statement, not bewildered because of their long practice.
All the <s>asuras</s> said to him, their eyes reddened with anger:

children.text: ayaṃ gurur hito'smākaṃ gaccha tvaṃ nāsi no guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: This one is our helpful guru. Go away. You are not our guru.

children.text: bhārgavo vāṅgirā vāpi bhagavāneṣa no guruḥ
children.translated_text: Whether he is <s>Bhārgava</s> or <s>Aṅgiras</s>, this blessed one is our guru.

children.text: sthitā vayaṃ nideśe'sya sādhu tvaṃ gaccha māciram ||
children.translated_text: We stand under his command. Good, go; do not delay.
Having spoken thus, all the Asuras resorted to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
when they did not accept the great benefit that had been stated by <s>Kāvya</s>.
Then the <s>Bhārgava</s> became angry at them because of that arrogance:

children.text: bodhitā hi mayā yasmānna māṃ bhajatha dānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Since, though awakened by me, you do not honor me, O Dānavas,
therefore, with your understanding destroyed, you shall meet defeat.'
Having said this to them, <s>Kāvya</s> then went away as he had come.
Knowing those Asuras to have been cursed by <s>Kāvya</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>

children.text: kṛtārthaḥ sa tadā hṛṣṭaḥ svarūpaṃ pratyapadyata ||
children.translated_text: had accomplished his purpose; then, delighted, he resumed his own form.
Knowing that the Asuras had been struck down by his intelligence, he disappeared, his aim accomplished.
Then, when he had vanished, the Dānavas became bewildered.
'Ah, we have been deceived,' they then said to one another.
They had been struck from behind and face to face by the descendant of <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.text: vañcitāḥ sopadhānena sve sve vastuni māyayā
children.translated_text: They had been deceived by a stratagem, by illusion, each in his own affairs.
Then, not content, they quickly went to that same one,
putting <s>Prahlāda</s> in front, once more following in <s>Kāvya</s>'s footsteps.
Then, having reached <s>Kāvya</s>, they stood before him with faces downcast.
Seeing his sacrificial clients assembled again, <s>Kāvya</s> addressed them:
'Since, though all of you were instructed by me, you did not welcome me,
therefore, because of that contempt, you have gone to defeat.'

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ śukraṃ tu bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā girā
children.translated_text: As <s>Śukra</s> was speaking in this way, <s>Prahlāda</s> then said to him

children.text: prahlādastaṃ tadovāca mā nastvaṃ tyaja bhārgava ||
children.translated_text: in a voice choked with tears, 'Do not abandon us, O <s>Bhārgava</s>.
Favor your own dependents who resort to you, your devotees, O <s>Bhārgava</s>.
When you were unseen, we were deluded by that teacher of the gods.
You ought to recognize your devotees with the eye made far-reaching by austerity.

children.text: yadi nastvaṃ na kuruṣe prasādaṃ bhṛgunandana
children.translated_text: If you do not grant us favor, O joy of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,

children.text: apadhyātās tvayā hy adya praviśāmo rasātalam ||
children.translated_text: then, cursed by you today, we shall enter <s>Rasātala</s>.'
Understanding the matter as it truly was, <s>Kāvya</s>, out of pity and compassion,

children.text: evaṃ pratyanunīto vai tataḥ kopaṃ niyamya saḥ
children.translated_text: when thus entreated in return, restrained his anger.
He said to them, 'You need not fear; you need not go to <s>Rasātala</s>.

children.text: avaśyaṃ bhāvino hy arthāḥ prāptavyā mayi jāgrati
children.translated_text: Events that are bound to happen must necessarily be reached while I am watchful.

children.text: na śakyamanyathā kartuṃ diṣṭaṃ hi balavattaram ||
children.translated_text: It cannot be made otherwise, for destiny is stronger.

children.text: saṃjñā pranaṣṭā yā vo 'dya tāmetāṃ pratipatsyatha
children.translated_text: The understanding of yours that has been destroyed today: you shall recover it.
After conquering the gods even once, you shall go to <s>Pātāla</s>.
And when the turn of time arrives, <s>Brahmā</s> declared it so:
'By my favor you have enjoyed the vigorous lordship of the three worlds.
For ten complete yuga-periods, after treading upon the heads of the gods,

children.text: etāvantaṃ ca kālaṃ vai brahmā rājyamabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: for just so long a time <s>Brahmā</s> proclaimed kingship.

children.text: rājyaṃ sāvarṇike tubhyaṃ punaḥ kila bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: In the time of <s>Sāvarṇi</s>, kingship will indeed again belong to you.
Your grandson <s>Bali</s> shall again become lord of the worlds.'

children.text: evaṃ kila mithaḥ proktaḥ pautraste viṣṇunā svayam
children.translated_text: Thus, it is said, your grandson was personally addressed by <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself.
When the worlds were taken away by a word, those words of his came to be.
Since his undertakings had been agreed upon in the presence of that one,
therefore, being pleased by his conduct, the Self-born gave this to you.
The Lord told me, '<s>Bali</s> is destined for the kingship of the gods.'
Therefore he remains invisible to beings, waiting upon time.
And another boon was granted to you by the pleased Self-born.
Therefore be free from anxiety, together with the Asuras, awaiting your turn.

children.text: na hi śakyaṃ mayā tubhyaṃ purastād viprabhāṣitum
children.translated_text: I am not able to speak falsely to you about what lies ahead,
for I have been forbidden by <s>Brahmā</s>, who knows the future, O lord.

children.text: imau ca śiṣyau dvau mahyaṃ samāv etau bṛhaspateḥ
children.translated_text: These two pupils of mine, these two equals of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
will sustain all of you when you are mingled with the deities.'
Thus addressed by <s>Kāvya</s>, whose deeds were unwearied, all the Asuras,
delighted, went away together with the great-souled <s>Prahlāda</s>.

children.text: avaśyaṃ bhāvyamarthaṃ tu śrutvā śukreṇa bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Having heard from <s>Śukra</s> the matter that must inevitably come to be,
and hoping for the victory once proclaimed by <s>Śukra</s>,
all of them, armored and armed, then challenged the gods.
When the gods saw the Asuras standing ready in battle,
all the gods, with their equipment gathered, fought against them.
While that battle between gods and Asuras was then continuing for a hundred years,
the Asuras defeated the gods; then the gods took counsel.
'We shall summon those two by means of a sacrifice; then we shall conquer the Asuras.'
Then the gods invited those two, <s>Śaṇḍa</s> and <s>Amarka</s>.

children.text: yajñe cāhūya tau proktau tyajetāmasurān dvijau
children.translated_text: Having summoned those two brahmins at the sacrifice, they said, 'Abandon the Asuras.

children.text: vayaṃ yuvāṃ bhajiṣyāmaḥ saha jitvā tu dānavān ||
children.translated_text: We shall honor you two, after conquering the Dānavas together.'
When those two, <s>Śaṇḍa</s> and <s>Amarka</s>, and likewise the gods had made this agreement,
then the gods obtained victory, and the Dānavas were defeated.
Abandoned by <s>Śaṇḍa</s> and <s>Amarka</s>, the Dānavas were powerless.
Thus in ancient times the Daityas were struck down by <s>Kāvya</s>'s curse.
Overpowered by <s>Kāvya</s>'s curse and wholly without support,
and being driven away by the gods, they entered <s>Rasātala</s>.

children.text: evaṃ nirudyamā devaiḥ kṛtāḥ kṛcchreṇa dānavāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the Dānavas, being repelled by the gods, were brought into distress.
From that time onward, because of the occasional curse of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
the lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> was born again and again whenever <s>dharma</s> was slackened,
establishing the order of <s>dharma</s> and bringing about the destruction of the Asuras.

children.text: prahlādasya nideśe tu na sthāsyantyasurāśca ye
children.translated_text: And those Asuras who will not stand under <s>Prahlāda</s>'s command
The lord said, "All these are to be slain by human beings, O <s>Brahmā</s>."
<s>Dharma</s>, a portion of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, was born in the interval of <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>.
In the interval of <s>Vaivasvata</s>, the gods set <s>Yajña</s> in motion.
At his manifestation, <s>Brahmā</s> indeed served as the priest.

children.text: yugākhyāyāṃ caturthyāṃ tu āpanneṣu sureṣu vai ||
children.translated_text: And in the fourth age so called, when the gods had fallen into distress,
he was born at the edge of the ocean for the slaying of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
In the second manifestation, called <s>Narasiṃha</s>, <s>Rudra</s> indeed served as the priest.
When the worlds were under <s>Bali</s>'s power, in the seventh <s>Tretā</s> age,
in the third manifestation, for the sake of <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Dharma</s> was the priest.

children.text: etās tisraḥ smṛtāstasya divyāḥ sambhūtayo dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: These three divine manifestations of his are remembered, O twice-born ones.
Now understand the seven others that were human and born from the curse.

children.text: tretāyuge tu prathame dattātreyo babhūva ha
children.translated_text: In the first <s>Tretā</s> yuga, <s>Dattātreya</s> was born.
When one fourth of <s>dharma</s> (normative order) had been lost, <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> stood at the head.

children.text: pañcamaḥ pañcadaśyāṃ ca tretāyāṃ saṃbabhūva ha
children.translated_text: As the fifth, in the fifteenth <s>Tretā</s>, he was born.
Then <s>Māndhātā</s>, the universal emperor, was born with <s>Uttaṅka</s> at the head.
In the nineteenth <s>Tretā</s>, the mighty destroyer of all kṣatriyas appeared.
The sixth was <s>Jāmadagnya</s>, likewise, with <s>Viśvāmitra</s> at the head.
In the twenty-fourth yuga, <s>Rāma</s> appeared with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> as priest.
The seventh, born for the sake of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, was the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.
In the eighth <s>Dvāpara</s>, the twenty-eighth age, <s>Viṣṇu</s> was born from <s>Parāśara</s>.
So too <s>Vedavyāsa</s> was born, with <s>Jātūkarṇya</s> at the head.
He appeared to establish the order of <s>dharma</s> and to destroy the asuras.
As the ninth, <s>Buddha</s>, lotus-eyed, was born through austerity,
in the form of <s>Devasundara</s>, with <s>Dvaipāyana</s> at the head.
When that very yuga has waned and only its twilight remains,
<s>Kalki</s>, son of <s>Viṣṇuyaśas</s>, will come with <s>Pārāśarya</s> at the head.
He will be the tenth future manifestation, with <s>Yājñavalkya</s> at the head.
All benighted beings and all heretics in every way,
surrounded by brahmins who have taken up weapons in hundreds of thousands,
then he will make the śūdra kings perish without remainder.
Having destroyed the enemies who hate brahman, he will also lay aside that body.
<s>Kalki</s>, standing in the twenty-fifth year, his aim accomplished and with his army,

children.text: śūdrān saṃśodhayitvā tu samudrāntaṃ ca vai svayam ||
children.translated_text: will himself purify the śūdras as far as the ocean's edge.
Powerful and with his wheel set in motion, he will carry out destruction.
He will overthrow those base and mostly unrighteous men.
Then that same <s>Kalki</s>, his aim accomplished and with his army,

children.text: prajāstaṃ sādhayitvā tu samṛddhāstena vai svayam ||
children.translated_text: after setting the subjects in order, they themselves prosperous through him,
will suddenly become angry with one another here, bewildered.
Driven by what is to come, they will destroy one another.

children.text: tataḥ kāle vyatīte tu sa devo'ntaradhīyata
children.translated_text: Then, when time has passed, that god will disappear.
And when the kings have perished, because the people have gathered together,
when protection has ceased, they will kill one another in battle.

children.text: parasparaṃ ca hatvā tu nirākrandāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having killed one another, with no one to cry out for them, they will be very miserable.
Abandoning cities and villages, reduced to equality and without possessions,
they will have lost the <s>dharma</s> of the āśramas and the order of varṇa and āśrama as well.
Fortified places will be bristling with spears, roads will be many-branched, and crossroads will have <s>Śiva</s>'s tridents.
At the end of the age, women will wear their hair like spikes.
They will have short bodies and short lives, and will dwell in the forests.
They will live by rivers and mountains, eating roots, leaves, and fruit.
Wearing bark, hides, and antelope skins, they will resort to a terrible social mixture.
Those people will suffer from portents, have little wealth, and be beset by many troubles.
Thus, when they have reached misery in the twilight portion of the age,

children.text: tataḥ kṣayaṃ gamiṣyanti sārdhaṃ kaliyugena tu ||
children.translated_text: they will then go to destruction together with the <s>Kali</s> yuga.
When that <s>Kali</s> yuga has waned, then the <s>Kṛta</s> age begins.
Thus the activity of gods and asuras has been properly recounted.
In connection with the lineage of <s>Yadu</s>, the fame of <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been briefly told.

children.text: turvasostu pravakṣyāmi pūror druhyostathā hy anoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now I shall tell of <s>Turvasu</s>, and likewise of <s>Pūru</s>, <s>Druhyu</s>, and <s>Anu</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The son of <s>Turvasu</s> was <s>Garbha</s>, and his son was <s>Gobhānu</s>.
The son of <s>Gobhānu</s> was the heroic, unconquered <s>Trisāri</s>.
<s>Karandhama</s> was the son of <s>Trisāri</s>, and <s>Bharata</s> was his son.

children.text: duṣyantaḥ pauravasyāpi tasya putro hy akalmaṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Duṣyanta</s>, of the Paurava line, was also his son, spotless in character.
Thus, long ago, because of <s>Yayāti</s>'s curse and the transfer of old age,

children.text: turvasoḥ pauravaṃ vaṃśaṃ praviveśa purā kila ||
children.translated_text: the Paurava lineage is said to have entered the line of <s>Turvasu</s>.

children.text: duṣyantasya tu dāyādo varūtho nāma pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: The heir of <s>Duṣyanta</s> was a king named <s>Varūtha</s>.
From <s>Varūtha</s> came <s>Āṇḍīra</s>, and <s>Saṃdhāna</s> was his son.
<s>Pāṇḍya</s>, <s>Kerala</s>, <s>Cola</s>, and <s>Karṇa</s> were likewise born.
Their flourishing peoples are the <s>Pāṇḍyas</s>, the <s>Colas</s>, and the <s>Keralas</s>.

children.text: druhyostu tanayau śūrau setuḥ ketustathaiva ca
children.translated_text: The two heroic sons of <s>Druhyu</s> were <s>Setu</s> and <s>Ketu</s>.
<s>Setu</s>'s son was <s>Śaradvān</s>, and <s>Gandhāra</s> was his son.
By his name that great country of <s>Gandhāra</s> is known.
The horses born in his <s>Āraṭṭa</s> country are the best of steeds.
The son of <s>Gandhāra</s> was <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Ghṛta</s> was his son.
From <s>Ghṛta</s> was born the wise <s>Vidus</s>, and <s>Pracetā</s> was his son.

children.text: pracetasaḥ putraśataṃ rājānaḥ sarva eva te
children.translated_text: <s>Pracetā</s> had a hundred sons, and all of them were kings.
All were rulers of mleccha realms, dwelling in the northern direction.
And <s>Anu</s>'s sons were three heroes, supremely devoted to <s>dharma</s>.
and <s>Sabhānara</s>, <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>, and likewise <s>Parameṣu</s>.
But <s>Sabhānara</s>'s son was the learned king <s>Kolāhala</s>;
the righteous son of <s>Kolāhala</s> was renowned by the name <s>Saṃjaya</s>.
The son of <s>Saṃjaya</s> was <s>Puraṃjaya</s>, named <s>Vīra</s>;
O great king, <s>Janamejaya</s> was the son of <s>Puraṃjaya</s>.
The royal sage <s>Janamejaya</s> had a son, <s>Mahāśāla</s>;
he was a king equal to <s>Indra</s>, and his fame was established.
<s>Mahāmanas</s>, the righteous son of that <s>Mahāśāla</s>,
was born as lord of the seven continents, a great-minded <s>cakravartin</s> (universal ruler).
Great-minded <s>Mahāmanas</s> begot two famous sons,

children.text: uśīnaraṃ ca dharmajñaṃ titikṣuṃ caiva tāv ubhau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uśīnara</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s> (right order), and <s>Titikṣu</s>; both were such.
<s>Uśīnara</s>'s wives were five, born from royal sages:

children.text: bhṛśā kṛśā navā darśā yā ca devī dṛṣadvatī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhṛśā</s>, <s>Kṛśā</s>, <s>Navā</s>, <s>Darśā</s>, and the lady <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>.
From them were born <s>Uśīnara</s>'s sons, upholders of the family,

children.text: tapasā te tu mahatā jātā vṛddhasya dhārmikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: righteous men born to the aged king through their great austerity.

children.text: bhṛśāyāstu nṛgaḥ putro navāyā nava eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Nṛga</s> was the son of <s>Bhṛśā</s>, and <s>Nava</s> indeed of <s>Navā</s>;
<s>Kṛśa</s> was born from <s>Kṛśā</s>, and <s>Suvrata</s> from <s>Darśā</s>;
and the king <s>Śibi Auśīnara</s> was also the son of <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>.
From <s>Śibi</s> came the <s>Śibis</s>, four sons renowned in the world:
<s>Pṛthudarbha</s>, <s>Suvīra</s>, <s>Kekaya</s>, and likewise <s>Bhadraka</s>.
Their flourishing realms were the <s>Kekayas</s> and the <s>Bhadrakas</s>,
and also the <s>Sauvīras</s> and <s>Pauras</s>; and likewise the <s>Kekayas</s> of <s>Nṛga</s>.
Likewise <s>Suvrata</s>'s people were the <s>Ambaṣṭhas</s>; <s>Kṛśa</s>'s city was <s>Vṛṣalā</s>.

children.text: navasya navarāṣṭraṃ tu titikṣostu prajāṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nava</s>'s realm was <s>Navarāṣṭra</s>; now hear the progeny of <s>Titikṣu</s>.
<s>Titikṣu</s> became a king famed in the eastern quarter;
his son was <s>Bṛhadratha</s>, and his son was <s>Sena</s>.
From <s>Sena</s> <s>Sutapas</s> was born; <s>Bali</s> was the son of <s>Sutapas</s>.

children.text: jāto mānuṣayonyāṃ tu kṣīṇe vaṃśe prajecchayā ||
children.translated_text: He was born in a human womb when the lineage had dwindled, out of desire for offspring.
That <s>Bali</s>, a great yogin, though bound with bonds by the great-souled one,
begot five royal sons, <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born) sons.

children.text: aṅgaṃ sa janayāmāsa vaṅgaṃ suhmaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: He begot <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Vaṅga</s>, and likewise <s>Suhma</s>,

children.text: puṇḍraṃ kaliṅgaṃ ca tathā bāleyaṃ kṣetramucyate
children.translated_text: and <s>Puṇḍra</s> and <s>Kaliṅga</s>; this is called the <s>Bāleya</s> field.
And the <s>Bāleya</s> brahmins, O lord, were continuers of his lineage.

children.text: baleśca brahmaṇā datto varaḥ prītena dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: And a boon was given to <s>Bali</s> by wise <s>Brahmā</s> when he was pleased:
the state of being a great yogin, and a lifespan measured by a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age),
invincibility in battle, and the highest understanding in <s>dharma</s> (right order),
vision of the three times, and preeminence in procreation,
unmatched victory in war, and insight into the true meaning of <s>dharma</s>.
He, the lord, would establish the four fixed <s>varṇas</s> (social classes).

children.text: teṣāṃ ca pañca dāyādā vaṅgāṅgāḥ suhmakāstathā
children.translated_text: Of them there are five heirs: the <s>Vaṅgas</s>, the <s>Aṅgas</s>, and the <s>Suhmakas</s>,

children.text: puṇḍrāḥ kaliṅgāśca tathā aṅgasya tu nibodhata ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the <s>Puṇḍras</s> and the <s>Kaliṅgas</s>. Now learn about <s>Aṅga</s>.
The sages said:

children.text: kathaṃ baleḥ sutā jātāḥ pañca tasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: How were the five sons of that great-souled <s>Bali</s> born?

children.text: kiṃnāmnī mahiṣī tasya janitā katama ṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: What was the name of his queen, and which sage begot them?
How were they produced by him? Tell that to us as we ask,

children.text: māhātmyaṃ ca prabhāvaṃ ca nikhilena vadasva tat ||
children.translated_text: and describe his greatness and power in full.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then, long ago, there was a learned sage famed as <s>Uśij</s>.

children.text: patnī vai mamatā nāma babhūvāsya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His wife was named <s>Mamatā</s>, the wife of that great-souled one.
The younger brother of <s>Uśij</s> desired his brother's wife;
the greatly radiant <s>Bṛhaspati</s> approached <s>Mamatā</s> out of passion.

children.text: uvāca mamatā taṃ tu devaraṃ varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: <s>Mamatā</s>, the lovely woman, said to him, her brother-in-law:
I am pregnant by your elder brother; you must desist.

children.text: ayaṃ tu me mahābhāga garbhaḥ kupyedbṛhaspate
children.translated_text: This fetus of mine, O blessed <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, may become angry;
he is an <s>Auśija</s>, born from your brother, reciting the <s>Veda</s> with its limbs.
Your seed too is unfailing, and you ought not enjoy me

children.text: asminn evaṃ gate kāle yathā vā manyase prabho ||
children.translated_text: at a time when matters stand thus, however you may think, O lord.
Although he was rightly addressed in this way, the greatly radiant <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: kāmātmā sa mahātmāpi na manaḥ so 'bhyavārayat ||
children.translated_text: being driven by desire, though great-souled, did not restrain his mind.
The righteous one lay with her even though she did not desire it.
As he was emitting that semen, the fetus spoke a word:
Sir, father, lord of speech, there is no room here for two;
your seed is unfailing, and I came here first.
Then, angered when thus addressed, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> cursed him,
the son of his elder brother, still in the womb, the blessed sage.
Because, though still in the womb, you obstruct me at such a time,
and have spoken to me in this way, therefore you shall enter long darkness.
Then, because of the curse, the seer was born with the name <s>Dīrghatamas</s>.
Thereafter he was born as a portion, of great fame, with power like <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Then that celibate one dwelt in his brother's hermitage.
He then heard the <s>Saurabheya</s> <s>dharmas</s> (teachings on order) from a bull.

children.text: tasya bhrātā pitṛvyo yaścakāra bharaṇaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: His father's brother then provided for his support.
While he was living there, by chance a bull
the son of <s>Surabhī</s>, grazed on the darbha grass brought for the sacrifice.
<s>Dīrghatamas</s> seized that four-footed one by the horns.
Restrained by him, it did not move a step from its place.

children.text: tato'bravīdvṛṣastaṃ vai muñca māṃ balināṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: Then the bull said to him: Release me, best of the strong.
Dear sir, I have never encountered anyone as strong as you anywhere;

children.text: mama cānyaḥ samo vāpi na hi me balasaṃkhyayā
children.translated_text: nor is there any other equal to me, nor anyone comparable to me in the reckoning of strength.

children.text: muñca tāteti ca punaḥ prītaste'haṃ varaṃ vṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: Release me, dear father; and again, I am pleased with you, choose a boon.
Thus addressed, he said to him: While I am alive, where will you go?

children.text: eṣa tvāṃ na vimokṣyāmi parasvādaṃ catuṣpadam ||
children.translated_text: I will not release you, a four-footed eater of another's property.
The bull said:

children.text: nāsmākaṃ vidyate tāta pātakaṃ steyameva ca
children.translated_text: Among us, dear father, there is no sin, nor any theft at all,

children.text: bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ tathā caiva peyāpeyaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: nor any distinction between edible and inedible, and likewise between drinkable and undrinkable.

children.text: dvipadāṃ bahavo hy ete dharma eṣa gavāṃ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For two-footed beings these distinctions are many; this is remembered as the <s>dharma</s> of cows.

children.text: kāryākārye na vāgamyāgamanaṃ ca tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: There is no distinction of what should or should not be done, nor likewise of what may or may not be approached.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: gavāṃ dharmaṃ tu vai śrutvā saṃbhrāntastu visṛjya tam
children.translated_text: Having heard the <s>dharma</s> of cows, he was bewildered, and released him.
Then, with gifts of food and drink according to his ability, he propitiated the lord of cows.
When he had been pleased and had gone away, the man devotedly
fixed the <s>dharma</s> of cows in his mind alone; he was intent on it, wholly given to it.
Then he approached the wife of <s>Gautama</s>'s younger son.

children.text: kṛtāvalepāṃ tāṃ matvā so 'naḍvāniva na kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thinking her to be proud, he, like a bull, was unable to restrain himself.

children.text: godharmaṃ tu paraṃ matvā snuṣāṃ tāmabhyapadyata
children.translated_text: Considering cow-<s>dharma</s> to be supreme, he approached that daughter-in-law.

children.text: nirbhartsya cainaṃ ruddhvā ca bāhubhyāṃ sampragṛhya ca ||
children.translated_text: She rebuked him, stopped him, and seized him firmly with both arms.

children.text: bhāvyamarthaṃ tu taṃ jñātvā māhātmyāttamuvāca sā
children.translated_text: Knowing, through her greatness, the matter that was to come about, she said to him:

children.text: viparyayaṃ tu tvaṃ labdhvā anaḍvāniva vartase ||
children.translated_text: You have fallen into reversal, and you behave like a bull.
You do not know who may or may not be approached, as you seek a daughter because of cow-<s>dharma</s>.

children.text: durvṛttaṃ tvāṃ tyajāmyadya gaccha tvaṃ svena karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: Wicked man, I abandon you today. Go, according to your own karma.
Putting him in a wooden chest, she cast him into the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
For you are blind and old, to be maintained, and difficult to manage.
As he was being carried along by the force of the current and had come near,

children.text: jagrāha taṃ sa dharmātmā balir vairocanistadā ||
children.translated_text: the righteous <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Virocana</s>, then seized him.
He protected him in the inner apartments, satisfying him with foods fit to be eaten and enjoyed.
And when he was pleased, he invited <s>Bali</s> to choose a boon.

children.text: tasmācca sa varaṃ vavre putrārthe dānavarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: From him the bull among <s>Dānavas</s> chose a boon for the sake of sons,
for the continuation of his line through my wife, O greatly fortunate giver of honor:
You should beget sons who know the truth of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>.
Thus addressed, the divine seer, the lord, said, So be it.

children.text: sa tasya rājā svāṃ bhāryāṃ sudeṣṇāṃ nāma prāhiṇot
children.translated_text: Then that king sent his own wife, named <s>Sudeṣṇā</s>, to him.

children.text: andhaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca taṃ jñātvā na sā devī jagāma ha ||
children.translated_text: But knowing him to be blind and old, that queen did not go.
Then she sent a śūdra nursemaid to that blind man.
In her, in a śūdra womb, the self-controlled seer begot <s>Kakṣīvat</s> and the others.
The righteous one begot śūdras, and so on.

children.text: uvāca taṃ balī rājā dṛṣṭvā kakṣīvadādikān ||
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Kakṣīvat</s> and the others, King <s>Bali</s> said to him:
The king said:
They are accomplished in the <s>dharma</s> of seers, powerful, proclaimers of <s>brahman</s>,
learned, directly perceptive of <s>dharma</s>, intelligent, well-conducted, and pure.

children.text: mamaiva ceti hovāca taṃ dīrghatamasaṃ baliḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bali</s> said to <s>Dīrghatamas</s>, Are they indeed mine?
The sage said No to him, and declared, They are mine alone.
They were born from a śūdra womb at your pleasure, O best of the gods.

children.text: andhaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca māṃ jñātvā sudeṣṇā mahiṣī tava
children.translated_text: Knowing me to be blind and old, <s>Sudeṣṇā</s>, your chief queen,
sent, in contempt of me, a śūdra nursemaid, O king.
Then <s>Bali</s> propitiated that best of seers.

children.text: baliḥ sudeṣṇāṃ tāṃ bhāryāṃ bhartsayāmāsa dānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bali</s>, the <s>Dānava</s>, rebuked that wife <s>Sudeṣṇā</s>.
Then, adorning her again, he handed her over to the seer.

children.text: tāṃ sa dīrghatamā devīṃ tathā kṛtavatīṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dīrghatamas</s> addressed that queen who had acted in that way:

children.text: dadhnā lavaṇamiśreṇa tv abhyaktaṃ madhukena tu
children.translated_text: Smeared with curds mixed with salt and with honey,
lick me, without disgust, from the soles of my feet up to my head.
Then, O queen, you will obtain the sons desired in your mind.

children.text: tasya sā tadvaco devī sarvaṃ kṛtavatī tadā
children.translated_text: The queen then did all of that speech of his.
But when she reached his anus, the queen then avoided it.

children.text: tāmuvāca tataḥ so 'tha yatte parihṛtaṃ śubhe
children.translated_text: Then he said to her: O auspicious one, because that was avoided by you,
you will give birth to a first-born boy without an anus.
<s>Sudeṣṇā</s> said:

children.text: nārhasi tvaṃ mahābhāga putraṃ me dātumīdṛśam
children.translated_text: O greatly fortunate one, you ought not give me such a son.

children.text: toṣitaśca yathāśakti prasādaṃ kuru me prabho ||
children.translated_text: You have been satisfied as far as my power allowed; show me favor, lord.
<s>Dīrghatamas</s> said:
Because of your offense, O queen, this will not be otherwise, auspicious one.

children.text: naiva dāsyati putraste pautrau vai dāsyate phalam ||
children.translated_text: Your son will not give the fruit, but his grandsons will indeed give the fruit.
And even without an anus, a proper condition will come about for him.
Then <s>Dīrghatamas</s>, touching her belly with his limbs, said this:
Whatever has been licked on my limbs, but not the generative organ, pure-smiling one,

children.text: tena tiṣṭhanti te garbhe paurṇamāsyām ivoḍurāṭ ||
children.translated_text: by that they remain in your womb like the lord of stars on the full-moon night.
Five boys, equal to sons of gods, will be born.
They will be brilliant, well-conducted, sacrificers, and righteous.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then the eldest son, a portion of him, was born to <s>Sudeṣṇā</s>.
<s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>Puṇḍra</s>, and likewise <s>Suhma</s>,
and King <s>Vaṅga</s>: these five were <s>Bali</s>'s sons, born on his field.
Thus these sons were given to <s>Bali</s> by <s>Dīrghatamas</s>.
For those who had attained standing, he then brought about brahminhood.

children.text: tato mānuṣayonyāṃ sa janayāmāsa vai prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, in a human womb, he begot offspring.
Then <s>Surabhi</s> said these words to <s>Dīrghatamas</s>:

children.text: vicārya yasmādgodharmaṃ pramāṇaṃ te kṛtaṃ vibho ||
children.translated_text: Because, after considering cow-<s>dharma</s>, you made it your authority, lord,
and because of your single-minded power toward us, I am pleased with you, sinless one.
Therefore, after smelling you, I remove your long darkness.
Likewise this <s>Bārhaspatya</s> sin indeed remains in you;
by smelling you I drive away your old age, death, and darkness.
At once, as soon as he had merely been smelled, <s>Asita</s>, that best of sages,
then became long-lived, handsome in form, and possessed of sight.
And because the darkness had been struck by cows, he then became <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: kākṣīvāṃstu tato gatvā saha pitrā girivrajam ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kākṣīvān</s>, going together with his father, went to <s>Girivraja</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā piturvai sa hy upaviṣṭaściraṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen and touched his father, he remained seated for a long time in austerity.

children.text: tataḥ kālena mahatā tapasā bhāvitastu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after a long time, he was matured by austerity.
Shaking off the body born from his mother, the powerful one attained brahminhood.
Then his father said to him, 'Through you I have become possessed of a son.
By a good son, knower of <s>dharma</s> (right order), by a glorious one, I have achieved my purpose.'
Then, freeing himself, he attained the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Having attained brahminhood, <s>Kākṣīvān</s> begot a thousand sons.
The <s>Kauṣmāṇḍas</s> and the <s>Gautamas</s> are remembered as the sons of <s>Kākṣīvān</s>.
Thus this meeting of <s>Dīrghatamas</s> and of <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Virocana</s>,
has been told to you, and so too the lineage of both of them.
<s>Bali</s>, praising them, spoke to those five stainless sons.
That righteous one too had achieved his purpose, himself covered by yogamāyā (yogic illusion).

children.text: adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ kālāpekṣaḥ sa vai prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Invisible to all beings, he, the lord, waited for the proper time.
There the heir of <s>Aṅga</s> was the king <s>Dadhivāhana</s>.
The son of <s>Dadhivāhana</s> is remembered as King <s>Diviratha</s>.
The offspring of <s>Diviratha</s> was the learned king <s>Dharmaratha</s>.

children.text: sa hi dharmarathaḥ śrīmāṃstena viṣṇupade girau
children.translated_text: That illustrious <s>Dharmaratha</s>, on the mountain called <s>Viṣṇupada</s>,

children.text: somaḥ śukreṇa vai rājñā saha pīto mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: drank <s>Soma</s> together with the great-souled king <s>Śukra</s>.
Then <s>Dharmaratha</s> had a son, indeed, named <s>Citraratha</s>.
His son was <s>Satyaratha</s>; from him, indeed, came <s>Daśaratha</s>.
He was famed as <s>Lomapāda</s>, and his daughter was <s>Śāntā</s>.
Then the heroic descendant of <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Caturaṅga</s>, of great fame,
was born by the grace of <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, increasing his own family.
The son of <s>Caturaṅga</s> is remembered as <s>Pṛthulākṣa</s>.
And the son of <s>Pṛthulākṣa</s> became one named <s>Campa</s>.

children.text: campasya tu purī campā pūrvaṃ yā mālinī bhavat ||
children.translated_text: The city of <s>Campa</s> was <s>Campā</s>, which formerly had been <s>Mālinī</s>.
By the favor of <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s>, his son was <s>Haryaṅga</s>.
At his sacrifice, <s>Vibhāṇḍaka</s> brought an elephant, a repeller of enemies,
down to the earth by mantras, an excellent mount.

children.text: haryaṅgasya tu dāyādo jāto bhadrarathaḥ kila ||
children.translated_text: The heir of <s>Haryaṅga</s> was born, indeed, as <s>Bhadraratha</s>.
Then <s>Bhadraratha</s> had <s>Bṛhatkarman</s>, lord of men.
His son was <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s>; from him a great-souled man was born.
King <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s>, best of kings, begot a son,
named <s>Jayadratha</s>; from him came King <s>Bṛhadratha</s>.
From <s>Bṛhadratha</s> were <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Janamejaya</s>.
His heir was <s>Aṅga</s>, and from him came King <s>Karṇa</s>.
The sons of <s>Karṇa</s> were <s>Vṛṣasena</s> and <s>Pṛthusena</s>.
All these sons of <s>Aṅga</s> have been proclaimed by me as kings.
Now listen, twice-born ones, in full and in order, to the line of <s>Pūru</s>.
The sages said:
How was <s>Karṇa</s> the son of a sūta, and how was he the son of <s>Aṅga</s>?
We wish to hear this, for you are exceedingly skillful.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The son of <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s> was born, a king named <s>Bṛhanmanas</s>.

children.text: tasya patnīdvayaṃ hy āsīcchaibyasya tanaye hy ubhe
children.translated_text: He had two wives, both daughters of <s>Śaibya</s>:

children.text: yaśodevī ca satyā ca tayorvaṃśaṃ ca me śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśodevī</s> and <s>Satyā</s>. Hear from me their lineages.

children.text: jayadrathaṃ tu rājānaṃ yaśodevī hy ajījanat
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśodevī</s> gave birth to King <s>Jayadratha</s>.

children.text: sā bṛhanmanasaḥ satyā vijayaṃ nāma viśrutam ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Satyā</s>, wife of <s>Bṛhanmanas</s>, bore the renowned <s>Vijaya</s>.
<s>Vijaya</s> had <s>Bṛhatputra</s>; his son was <s>Bṛhadratha</s>.
The son of <s>Bṛhadratha</s> was the high-minded <s>Satyakarman</s>.
From <s>Satyakarman</s> came <s>Adhiratha</s>; and <s>Adhiratha</s> is remembered as a sūta.

children.text: yaḥ karṇaṃ pratijagrāha tena karṇastu sūtajaḥ
children.translated_text: Because he accepted <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s> is therefore the son of a sūta.
This whole matter concerning <s>Karṇa</s> has been related just as it is told.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: pūroḥ putro mahātejā rājā sa janamejayaḥ
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Pūru</s> was the greatly splendid king <s>Janamejaya</s>.
His son was <s>Prācītvant</s>, who made the eastern quarter.
The son of <s>Prācītvant</s> was likewise <s>Manasyu</s>.
The son of <s>Manasyu</s> was a king named <s>Pītāyudha</s>.
His heir too was the earth-lord named <s>Dhundhu</s>.
<s>Dhundhu</s> had a son <s>Bahuvidha</s>, and his son was <s>Sampāti</s>.
From <s>Sampāti</s> came <s>Raṃhavarcā</s>, and his son was <s>Bhadrāśva</s>.
By <s>Dhṛtā</s>, the apsaras, <s>Bhadrāśva</s> had ten sons:
<s>Auceyu</s>, <s>Hṛṣeyu</s>, <s>Kakṣeyu</s>, and <s>Saneyuka</s>,
<s>Dhṛteyu</s>, <s>Vineyu</s>, and the excellent <s>Sthaleyu</s>,
<s>Dharmeyu</s>, <s>Saṃnateyu</s>, and <s>Puṇyeyu</s>; these were the ten.
<s>Jvalanā</s>, daughter of <s>Takṣaka</s>, was the wife of <s>Auceyu</s>.
In her he begot the earth-lord <s>Antināra</s>.
In <s>Manasvinī</s>, <s>Antināra</s> begot excellent, auspicious sons:
the heroic <s>Amūrtarayas</s> and the righteous <s>Trivana</s>,

children.text: gaurī kanyā tṛtīyā ca māndhāturjananī śubhā ||
children.translated_text: and a third, the maiden <s>Gaurī</s>, auspicious mother of <s>Māndhātṛ</s>.
And <s>Ilina</s> had a daughter of <s>Yama</s>, who bore sons
mighty in sacred discourse; and <s>Śubhadā</s> too belonged to <s>Ilina</s>.
<s>Upadānavī</s> obtained four sons, all born from <s>Ilina</s>.
And then came <s>Ṛṣyanta</s>, <s>Duṣyanta</s>, <s>Pravīra</s>, and likewise <s>Anadha</s>.
Thereafter, from <s>Duṣyanta</s> was born the universal ruler <s>Samitiṃjaya</s> in the sacrifice,

children.text: śakuntalāyāṃ bharato yasya nāmnā ca bhāratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, born of <s>Śakuntalā</s>, from whose name the <s>Bhāratas</s> are named.
An incorporeal voice spoke to the king concerning the daughter of <s>Duṣyanta</s>:

children.text: mātā bhastrā pituḥ putro yena jātaḥ sa eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The mother is but a vessel; the son belongs to the father from whom he is born.
Raise your son, <s>Duṣyanta</s>; do not despise <s>Śakuntalā</s>.
A son who receives the seed carries the dead man away from the abode of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ cāsya dhātā garbhasya satyamāha śakuntalā ||
children.translated_text: You are the begetter of this embryo; <s>Śakuntalā</s> has spoken the truth.'
Long ago, when <s>Bharata</s>'s sons had perished,

children.text: putrāṇāṃ mātṛkāt kopāt sumahān saṃkṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a very great destruction of sons was brought about through the anger of their mothers.

children.text: tato marudbhirānīya putraḥ sa tu bṛhaspateḥ
children.translated_text: Then a son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> was brought by the <s>Maruts</s>,
and <s>Bharadvāja</s> was transferred by the <s>Maruts</s> to <s>Bharata</s>.
The sages said:
How was the very powerful <s>Bharadvāja</s> transferred by the <s>Maruts</s>
for the purpose of being <s>Bharata</s>'s son? Tell us that exactly as it was.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
While the wife of <s>Uśij</s> had conceived and was staying on the earth,

children.text: bhrāturbhāryāṃ sa dṛṣṭvā tu bṛhaspatiruvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, seeing his brother's wife, addressed her.

children.text: upatiṣṭha svalaṃkṛtya maithunāya ca māṃ śubhe
children.translated_text: 'Adorn yourself and attend on me for intercourse, fair lady.'
Thus addressed, she herself spoke to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>:
'This embryo is now mature, and it utters sacred speech with its voice.
Your seed is unfailing, and this <s>dharma</s> is thus blameworthy.'
When she had spoken thus, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> himself said to her:
'Discipline is not to be taught to me by you, beautiful woman.'
Overpowering her by force, he began to approach her for intercourse.
Then the embryo spoke to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> as he was violating her:

children.text: saṃniviṣṭo hy ahaṃ pūrvamiha nāma bṛhaspate
children.translated_text: 'I have already settled here before, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
And your seed is unfailing; there is no room here for two.'

children.text: evamuktaḥ sa garbheṇa kupitaḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the embryo, he became angry and answered:
'Because at such a time, when it is desired by all beings,
you obstruct me, therefore you shall enter long darkness.'
Then, when <s>Bṛhaspati</s> had turned back his desire from her because of that obstruction,
that seed of his fell on the ground, and, though withdrawn, became a little child.

children.text: sadyojātaṃ kumāraṃ tu dṛṣṭvā taṃ mamatābravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing the boy born at once, <s>Mamatā</s> said to him:

children.text: gamiṣyāmi gṛhaṃ svaṃ vai bharasvainaṃ bṛhaspate ||
children.translated_text: 'I shall go to my own house; you must support this child, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.'

children.text: evamuktvā gatā sā tu gatāyāṃ so 'pi taṃ tyajat
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, she went away; when she had gone, he too abandoned him.

children.text: mātāpitṛbhyāṃ tyaktaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā taṃ marutaḥ śiśum
children.translated_text: Seeing the infant abandoned by both mother and father,
the <s>Maruts</s>, standing there out of compassion, took that <s>Bharadvāja</s>.
At that time the mighty <s>Bharata</s>, through many seasons,
performed sacrifices aimed at obtaining a son, desiring sons.
When that powerful sacrificer did not obtain a son,
he then undertook a <s>Marutsoma</s> rite for the sake of a son.
By that <s>Marutsoma</s>, those <s>Maruts</s> became pleased with him,
and they brought <s>Bharadvāja</s> to <s>Bharata</s> for the purpose of being a son.
He was heir to the son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, the natural son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
<s>Bharadvāja</s> was transferred by the <s>Maruts</s> to <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: bharatastu bharadvājaṃ putraṃ prāpya vibhur bravīt
children.translated_text: But <s>Bharata</s>, having obtained <s>Bharadvāja</s> as a son, said, mighty one:

children.text: ādāv ātmahitāya tvaṃ kṛtārtho 'haṃ tvayā vibho ||
children.translated_text: 'For my own welfare at the beginning, I have attained my purpose through you, lord.'

children.text: pūrvaṃ tu vitathe tasminkṛte vai putrajanmani
children.translated_text: Because formerly, in that matter, the birth of a son had been made fruitless,
thereafter <s>Bharadvāja</s> became the king named <s>Vitatha</s>.
From that <s>Bharadvāja</s> also, brahmins and kṣatriyas on earth
are remembered as born in two lineages and as twofold through their dual descent.

children.text: tato jāte hi vitathe bharataśca divaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: After <s>Vitatha</s> was born, <s>Bharata</s> went to heaven,

children.text: bharadvājo divaṃ yāto hy abhiṣicya sutamṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> also went to heaven after consecrating his son.
The heir of <s>Vitatha</s> was the very famous <s>Bhuvamanyu</s>.
The sons of <s>Bhuvamanyu</s> were four, comparable to great beings.
<s>Bṛhatkṣatra</s>, of great valor, <s>Nara</s>, and the valiant <s>Garga</s> were born.
<s>Nara</s>'s son was <s>Saṃkṛti</s>; his son was very famous.

children.text: gurudhī rantidevaśca satkṛtyāṃ tāv ubhau smṛtau
children.translated_text: <s>Gurudhī</s> and <s>Rantideva</s> are both remembered as born from <s>Satkṛtyā</s>.
And the heir of <s>Garga</s> was born as the learned <s>Śibi</s>.
From him the <s>Śaibyas</s> and then the <s>Gargas</s> are remembered as twice-born men endowed with kṣatriya status.
And the wise son of <s>Āhārya</s> was <s>Urukṣava</s>.

children.text: tasya bhāryā viśālā tu suṣuve putrakatrayam
children.translated_text: His wife <s>Viśālā</s> bore a triad of sons:

children.text: tryuṣaṇaṃ puṣkariṃ caiva kaviṃ caiva mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tryuṣaṇa</s>, <s>Puṣkarin</s>, and the very famous <s>Kavi</s>.

children.text: urukṣavāḥ smṛtā hy ete sarve brāhmaṇatāṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: These <s>Urukṣavas</s> are all remembered as having attained brahminhood.

children.text: kāvyānāṃ tu varā hy ete trayaḥ proktā maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These three great sages are said to be foremost among the <s>Kāvyas</s>.
The <s>Gargas</s>, the <s>Saṃkṛtis</s>, and the <s>Kāvyas</s> are twice-born men endowed with kṣatriya status.
The capable <s>Saṃbhṛtāṅgiras</s> was born; and <s>Kṣiti</s> was of <s>Bṛhatkṣatra</s>.
The heir of <s>Bṛhatkṣatra</s> became one named <s>Hastin</s>.

children.text: tenedaṃ nirmitaṃ pūrvaṃ puraṃ tu gajasāhvayam ||
children.translated_text: By him this city, formerly called <s>Gajasāhvaya</s>, was built.
And <s>Hastin</s>'s heirs were three, of supreme fame:
<s>Ajamīḍha</s>, <s>Dvimīḍha</s>, and likewise <s>Purumīḍha</s>.
<s>Ajamīḍha</s>'s wives, who carried on the <s>Kuru</s> line, were three:

children.text: nīlinī dhūminī caiva keśinī caiva viśrutā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nīlinī</s>, <s>Dhūminī</s>, and the renowned <s>Keśinī</s>.
Upon them he begot sons possessing the splendor of gods.
Those righteous sons of the aged, greatly radiant man were born at the end of his austerity.
By the favor of <s>Bharadvāja</s>, hear from me the detailed account concerning them.
In <s>Keśinī</s>, <s>Kaṇva</s> was indeed born as the son of <s>Ajamīḍha</s>.
<s>Medhātithi</s> was his son; from him came the <s>Kāṇvāyana</s> brahmins.
From <s>Ajamīḍha</s>, by <s>Bhūminī</s>, was born <s>Bṛhadanu</s>, O king.
From <s>Bṛhadanu</s> came <s>Bṛhanta</s>, and from <s>Bṛhanta</s> came <s>Bṛhanmanas</s>.
And the son of <s>Bṛhanmanas</s> is remembered as <s>Bṛhaddhanu</s>.
From <s>Bṛhaddhanu</s> came <s>Bṛhadiṣu</s>; his son was <s>Jayadratha</s>.
His son was <s>Aśvajit</s>, and <s>Senajit</s> was his son.
Then <s>Senajit</s> had four sons, renowned in the world:
<s>Rucirāśva</s>, <s>Kāvya</s>, king <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>,
and king <s>Vatsa Āvartaka</s>; these were his <s>Parivatsakas</s>.
The heir of <s>Rucirāśva</s> was the very famous <s>Pṛthusena</s>.
The son of <s>Pṛthusena</s> was <s>Paura</s>; from <s>Paura</s> then <s>Nīpa</s> was born.
<s>Nīpa</s> had a hundred sons of immeasurable vigor.

children.text: nīpā iti samākhyātā rājānaḥ sarva eva te
children.translated_text: All those kings were known by the name <s>Nīpas</s>.
The glorious maker of their lineage, increaser of the fame of the <s>Nīpas</s>,
from <s>Kāvya</s> was one named <s>Samara</s>, whose battles were well chosen.

children.text: samarasya pārasampārau sadaśva iti te trayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Samara</s>'s three sons were <s>Pāra</s>, <s>Saṃpāra</s>, and <s>Sadaśva</s>.

children.text: putrāḥ sarvaguṇopetā jātā vai viśrutā bhuvi
children.translated_text: They were born endowed with every virtue and were famed on earth.
The son of <s>Pāra</s> was <s>Pṛthu</s>; from <s>Pṛthu</s> came <s>Sukṛta</s>.
Endowed with every virtue, <s>Vibhrāja</s> was born as his son.
The heir of <s>Vibhrāja</s> was a powerful man named <s>Aṇuha</s>.
He became the son-in-law of <s>Śuka</s>, the husband of <s>Kṛtvī</s>, very famous.
The heir of <s>Aṇuha</s> was king <s>Brahmadatta</s>.
<s>Yugadatta</s> was his son, and <s>Viṣvaksena</s> was very famous.
<s>Vibhrāja</s> was born again here through meritorious action.
The son of <s>Viṣvaksena</s> was <s>Udaksena</s>.
His son was <s>Bhallāṭa</s>, and his son was <s>Janamejaya</s>.
For his sake all the <s>Nīpas</s> were destroyed by <s>Ugrāyudha</s>.
The sages said:

children.text: ugrāyudhaḥ kasya sutaḥ kasya vaṃśe sa kathyate
children.translated_text: Whose son was <s>Ugrāyudha</s>? In whose lineage is he said to belong?

children.text: kimarthaṃ tena te nīpāḥ sarve caiva praṇāśitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For what reason were all those <s>Nīpas</s> destroyed by him?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Ugrāyudha</s>, of the solar lineage, performed austerity in an excellent hermitage.
Standing like a post for eight thousand years, he was attended by <s>Janamejaya</s>.

children.text: tasya rājyaṃ pratiśrutya nīpān ājaghnivān prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Having promised him the kingdom, the lord struck down the <s>Nīpas</s>.

children.text: uvāca sāntvaṃ vividhaṃ jaghnuste vai hy ubhāv api ||
children.translated_text: He spoke many conciliatory words, yet they indeed struck both of them.
To those who had come while being slain he said, 'Because you do not heed my word,
for the sake of protecting those who have sought refuge, I therefore curse you in this way:

children.text: yadi me 'sti tapastaptaṃ sarvānnayatu vo yamaḥ
children.translated_text: if I have performed austerity, may <s>Yama</s> take you all away.'

children.text: tatastān kṛpyamāṇāṃstu yamena purataḥ sa tu ||
children.translated_text: Then, while they were being seized before him by <s>Yama</s>,
he was filled with supreme compassion and said to <s>Janamejaya</s>:
'You ought to protect these heroes, who have come to me, for my sake.'
<s>Janamejaya</s> said:
'Hey, wicked evildoers, will you become his servants?'
When they had said, 'So be it,' the king then fought with <s>Yama</s> for a long time.
Together with <s>Yama</s> and with terrible hellish diseases, he overcame them by force.
Having conquered them, he gave them to the sage; that was like a wonder.
Then <s>Yama</s>, pleased, gave him the supreme knowledge of liberation.
All of them, having done what was proper, went to imperishable <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: yeṣāṃ tu caritaṃ gṛhya hanyate nāpamṛtyubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever takes up their story is not slain by untimely deaths.
In this world and the next he enjoys inexhaustible happiness.
From <s>Ajamīḍha</s>, by <s>Dhūminī</s>, was born the learned <s>Yavīnara</s>.
His son was <s>Dhṛtimant</s>, and his son is remembered as <s>Satyadhṛti</s>.
Then the son of <s>Satyadhṛti</s> was the mighty <s>Dṛḍhanemi</s>.
And the son of <s>Dṛḍhanemi</s> was a king named <s>Sudharmā</s>.
The son of <s>Sudharmā</s> was the mighty <s>Sārvabhauma</s>.
Famed as <s>Sārvabhauma</s>, he shone on earth as sole ruler.
In his great lineage was the descendant of <s>Mahāpaurava</s>.
The son of <s>Mahāpaurava</s> is remembered as king <s>Rukmaratha</s>.
Then <s>Rukmaratha</s> had a king named <s>Supārśva</s>.
The son of <s>Supārśva</s> was also named <s>Sumati</s>, a righteous man.
From <s>Sumati</s> came the righteous king <s>Saṃnatimant</s>.
That <s>Saṃnatimant</s> had a great son named <s>Kṛta</s>.
He was the disciple of the great-souled <s>Hiraṇyanābha Kauśalya</s>.
By him the <s>Sāmasaṃhitās</s> were taught in twenty-four divisions.
They are remembered as the eastern Sāmans; here the Sāma-singers are named <s>Kārtas</s>.
That <s>Ugrāyudha</s> was <s>Kārti</s>, increaser of the <s>Mahāpaurava</s> line.

children.text: babhūva yena vikramya pṛthukasya pitā hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: By him, attacking with force, the father of <s>Pṛthuka</s> was killed.
There was a great king named <s>Nīla</s>, lord of the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, self-controlled.
The heir of <s>Ugrāyudha</s> was named <s>Kṣema</s>, very famous.
From <s>Kṣema</s> was born <s>Sunītha</s>; from <s>Sunītha</s>, <s>Nṛpaṃjaya</s>.
From <s>Nṛpaṃjaya</s> came <s>Viratha</s>; these <s>Pauravas</s> are praised.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
From <s>Ajamīḍha</s>, by <s>Nīlinī</s>, <s>Nīla</s> was born, O king.
By <s>Nīla</s>'s fierce austerity <s>Suśānti</s> was born.
From <s>Suśānti</s> came <s>Purujānu</s>, and from <s>Purujānu</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s>.
<s>Bhadrāśva</s> was <s>Pṛthu</s>'s heir; hear of the sons of <s>Bhadrāśva</s>.
<s>Mudgala</s>, <s>Jaya</s>, and king <s>Bṛhadiṣu</s>,
and the valiant <s>Javīnara</s>, with <s>Kapila</s> as the fifth.
From these five they know these peoples as the <s>Pañcālas</s>.

children.text: pañcālarakṣiṇo hy ete deśānāmiti naḥ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: For these were protectors of the <s>Pāñcāla</s> countries; so we have heard.
From <s>Mudgala</s> too came the <s>Maudgalyas</s>, twice-born men endowed with kṣatra.

children.text: ete hy aṅgirasaḥ pakṣaṃ saṃśritāḥ kāṇvamudgalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These <s>Kāṇvas</s> and <s>Mudgalas</s> indeed belonged to the <s>Aṅgirasa</s> branch.
A son of <s>Mudgala</s> was born, most devoted to Brahman and of very great fame;
his son was <s>Indrasena</s>, and <s>Vindhyāśva</s> was his son.
From <s>Vindhyāśva</s>, so it is heard, twins were born in <s>Menakā</s>:
<s>Divodāsa</s>, the royal seer, and the illustrious <s>Ahalyā</s>.
But <s>Ahalyā</s> bore an heir of <s>Śaradvat</s>,
<s>Śatānanda</s>, best of sages; and his too was a very austere
son named <s>Satyadhṛti</s>, who had mastered the <s>Dhanurveda</s> (science of archery).
The seed of that righteous <s>Satyadhṛti</s> was unfailing;
when <s>Satyadhṛti</s>'s semen was discharged on seeing an apsaras in the water,
twins were formed there, gathered in that lake.
Then, while passing by that lake,
King <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, who had gone hunting, saw them and took them up out of pity.

children.text: ete śaradvataḥ putrā ākhyātā gautamā varāḥ
children.translated_text: These excellent <s>Gautamas</s> have been declared to be the children of <s>Śaradvat</s>;

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi divodāsasya vai prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: from here onward I shall tell the offspring of <s>Divodāsa</s>.
The heir of <s>Divodāsa</s> was the most righteous king <s>Mitrayu</s>;
he was <s>Maitrāyaṇāvara</s>, and thereafter was remembered as <s>Maitreya</s>.

children.text: ete vaṃśyā yateḥ pakṣāḥ kṣatropetāstu bhārgavāḥ
children.translated_text: These descendants, branches of <s>Yati</s>, were <s>Bhārgavas</s> endowed with kṣatriya status;

children.text: rājā caidyavaro nāma maitreyasya sutaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a king named <s>Caidyavara</s> is remembered as the son of <s>Maitreya</s>.
Then from <s>Caidyavara</s> came the learned <s>Sudāsa</s>, and his son

children.text: ajamīḍhaḥ punarjātaḥ kṣīṇe vaṃśe tu somakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was <s>Ajamīḍha</s>, born again as <s>Somaka</s> when the line had dwindled.
<s>Somaka</s>'s son was <s>Jantu</s>; when he had been killed, there appeared a hundred
sons of great-souled <s>Somaka</s>, descendant of <s>Ajamīḍha</s>.
The queen of <s>Ajamīḍha</s>, <s>Dhūminī</s>, desiring the increase of sons,
when there was no son, performed hard austerity for a hundred years.
Having offered into the fire duly and properly, and having sanctified her food,
that woman of great vows slept according to the sequence of the <s>agnihotra</s> rite.
<s>Ajamīḍha</s> approached her, <s>Dhūminī</s>, who was smoke-colored;
she bore <s>Ṛkṣa</s>, smoke-colored and elder to a hundred sons.
From <s>Ṛkṣa</s> <s>Saṃvaraṇa</s> was born, and from <s>Saṃvaraṇa</s> <s>Kuru</s>,
who, passing beyond <s>Prayāga</s>, fashioned <s>Kurukṣetra</s>.
As the great king ploughed for many years,
<s>Śakra</s>, while it was being ploughed, out of fear granted him a boon.

children.text: puṇyaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ ca kurukṣetraṃ tu tatsmṛtam
children.translated_text: That <s>Kurukṣetra</s> is remembered as holy and lovely;
his lineage was very great, and by his name they are the <s>Kauravas</s>.

children.text: kurostu dayitāḥ putrāḥ sudhanvā jahnureva ca
children.translated_text: The beloved sons of <s>Kuru</s> were <s>Sudhanvan</s> and <s>Jahnu</s>,
and also mighty-radiant <s>Parīkṣit</s> and <s>Prajana</s>, crusher of enemies.
The heir of <s>Sudhanvan</s> was a son, best among the intelligent,
<s>Cyavana</s>; his son was a king who knew the truth of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>.
The son of <s>Cyavana</s> was <s>Kṛmi</s>; from <s>Ṛkṣa</s> a man of great austerity was born.
The son of <s>Kṛmi</s>, very heroic, was renowned, a lord equal to <s>Indra</s>;
he was the heroic <s>Caidyoparicara</s>, named <s>Vasu</s>, who moved through the sky.
From <s>Caidyoparicara</s>, <s>Girikā</s> bore seven sons.
The well-known <s>Bṛhadratha</s> was a great chariot-warrior and king of <s>Magadha</s>;
<s>Pratyaśravas</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, and the fourth, <s>Harivāhana</s>;

children.text: pañcamaśca yajuścaiva matsyaḥ kālī ca saptamī
children.translated_text: the fifth was <s>Yaju</s>, and also <s>Matsya</s>, and <s>Kālī</s> was the seventh.
The heir of <s>Bṛhadratha</s> was renowned by the name <s>Kuśāgra</s>;
and <s>Kuśāgra</s>'s son was named <s>Vṛṣabha</s>, mighty in valor.
The heir of <s>Vṛṣabha</s> was the earthly ruler named <s>Puṇyavān</s>;
from <s>Puṇyavat</s> came <s>Puṇya</s>, and then King <s>Satyadhṛti</s>.
His heir was <s>Dhanuṣa</s>, and from him <s>Sarva</s> was born.
The son of <s>Sarva</s> was <s>Sambhava</s>; from him came King <s>Bṛhadratha</s>.

children.text: dve tasya śakale jāte jarayā saṃdhitaś ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Two pieces of him were born, and he was joined by <s>Jarā</s>;
because he was joined by <s>Jarā</s>, he was therefore remembered as <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>.
<s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, very strong, was conqueror of all the kṣatriya power.
The son of <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s> was the majestic <s>Sahadeva</s>;
<s>Sahadeva</s>'s son was the splendid <s>Somavit</s>, a man of great austerity.
<s>Śrutaśravas</s> and the descendants of <s>Somādi</s> are proclaimed as the <s>Māgadhas</s>.
But <s>Jahnu</s> begot a son, an earthly ruler named <s>Suratha</s>.

children.text: surathasya tu dāyādo vīro rājā vidūrathaḥ
children.translated_text: The heir of <s>Suratha</s> was the heroic king <s>Vidūratha</s>;
and <s>Vidūratha</s>'s son is remembered as <s>Sārvabhauma</s>.
From <s>Sārvabhauma</s> came <s>Jayatsena</s>; his son was <s>Rucira</s>.
From <s>Rucira</s> came <s>Bhauma</s>, and then <s>Tvaritāyus</s> was born.
<s>Akrodhana</s> was the son of <s>Āyus</s>; from him <s>Devātithi</s> is remembered.

children.text: devātithestu dāyādo dakṣa eva babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: The heir of <s>Devātithi</s> was indeed <s>Dakṣa</s>.
From <s>Dakṣa</s> came <s>Bhīmasena</s>; <s>Dilīpa</s> was his son.

children.text: dilīpasya pratīpastu tasya putrās trayaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Dilīpa</s> was <s>Pratīpa</s>; three sons of his are remembered:
<s>Devāpi</s>, <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, and <s>Vāhlīka</s>, those three.

children.text: vāhlīkasya tu dāyādāḥ sapta vāhlīśvarā nṛpāḥ
children.translated_text: The heirs of <s>Vāhlīka</s> were seven kings, lords of <s>Vāhlī</s>.
But <s>Devāpi</s>, being disapproved by the subjects, became a sage.
The sages said:

children.text: prajābhistu kimarthaṃ vai hy apadhyāto janeśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: For what reason, O lord of men, was he disapproved by the subjects?
What fault of the prince was declared by the subjects?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The prince was affected with skin disease, a leper; they did not honor him.

children.text: kāryaṃ caiva tu devānāṃ kṣatraṃ prati dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: And there was also a purpose of the gods concerning the kṣatriya line, O best twice-born ones;
I shall tell the future of <s>Śaṃtanu</s>; listen.
<s>Śaṃtanu</s> became king, learned and indeed a great healer.
And in this connection they cite this verse concerning the great physician:

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ karābhyāṃ spṛśati jīrṇaṃ rogiṇameva ca
children.translated_text: Whomever he touches with his hands, whether aged or sick,

children.text: punaryuvā ca bhavati tasmāttaṃ śaṃtanuṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: becomes young again; therefore they know him as <s>Śaṃtanu</s>.
This indeed is his state of being <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, celebrated here among the people.
Then King <s>Śaṃtanu</s> chose <s>Jāhnavī</s> for the sake of marriage.
In her the lord begot a prince named <s>Devavrata</s>.
<s>Kālī</s>, the daughter of the fisherman, bore a son, <s>Vicitravīrya</s>.
For the beloved son of <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, tranquil in spirit and stainless,
the one named <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>, in <s>Vicitravīrya</s>'s field,

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ ca viduraṃ cāpyajījanat
children.translated_text: begot <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, and also <s>Vidura</s>.
But <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> begot a hundred sons in <s>Gāndhārī</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ duryodhanaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvakṣatrasya vai prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Of them <s>Duryodhana</s> was foremost, indeed the lord of all the kṣatra.

children.text: mādrī kuntī tathā caiva pāṇḍorbhārye babhūvatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mādrī</s> and <s>Kuntī</s> likewise became the wives of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
Five sons, given by gods, were born on behalf of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
From <s>Dharma</s> <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> was born, and from <s>Māruta</s> <s>Vṛkodara</s>.
And from <s>Indra</s> came <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, equal to <s>Indra</s> in valor.
<s>Mādrī</s> begot <s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s> from the <s>Aśvins</s>.
These five sons were born from the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> in <s>Draupadī</s>.
<s>Draupadī</s> bore the excellent <s>Prativindhya</s> from <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
She bore <s>Śrutasena</s> from <s>Bhīmasena</s>, and <s>Śrutakīrti</s> from <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
A fourth, <s>Śrutakarman</s>, was born from <s>Sahadeva</s>.
And <s>Śatānīka</s> from <s>Nakula</s>; these are proclaimed as the <s>Draupadeyas</s>.
Besides them there were six other <s>Pāṇḍaveyas</s>, great chariot-fighters.
From <s>Bhīmasena</s> a son, <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, was born of <s>Hiḍimbā</s>.
<s>Kāśī</s> bore a son, <s>Sarvaga</s>, from mighty <s>Bhīma</s>, the bearer of strength.
<s>Mādrī</s> bore a son, <s>Suhotra</s>, from <s>Sahadeva</s>.
And in <s>Kareṇumatī</s>, the <s>Caidya</s> princess, <s>Niramitra</s> was <s>Nakula</s>'s son.
In <s>Subhadrā</s>, <s>Abhimanyu</s>, a chariot-fighter, was born from <s>Pārtha</s>.

children.text: yaudheyaṃ devakī caiva putraṃ jajñe yudhiṣṭhirāt ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Devakī</s> bore a son, <s>Yaudheya</s>, from <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
But <s>Parīkṣit</s>, conqueror of enemy cities, was the son of <s>Abhimanyu</s>.
<s>Janamejaya</s>, son of <s>Parīkṣit</s>, was supremely righteous.
He appointed the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> as the brahman priest.
He, indeed, was cursed by the great sage <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>.
'Your word will not stand here on earth, evil-minded one.
As long as you remain in the world, only so long will it continue.'
Knowing from that time onward the victory of the kṣatra in every way,
they approached and stood by King <s>Janamejaya</s>.
From that time, because of the curse, for the kṣatriya who performs sacrifice,
the sacrificial priests in the sacrifice were ruined from that time onward in every way.
Some priests of the kṣatra, because of that great man's curse,
having sacrificed to <s>Prajāpati</s> with the full-moon oblation,
were then barred by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> himself as they entered.
That son of <s>Parīkṣit</s>, the <s>Paurava</s> <s>Janamejaya</s>,
having performed two horse-sacrifices, was a great <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>.
After setting all that in motion, the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> sage,
cursed in a dispute with brahmins, went to the forest.
From <s>Janamejaya</s> was born <s>Śatānīka</s>, that strong hero.
<s>Janamejaya</s> consecrated his son <s>Śatānīka</s> in the kingdom.
Then, from <s>Śatānīka</s>, through the horse-sacrifice, a powerful son
was born, named <s>Adhisomakṛṣṇa</s>, who is now very famous.
While he rules the realm, this has been undertaken by you,

children.text: durāpaṃ dīrghasattraṃ vai trīṇi varṣāṇi puṣkare
children.translated_text: a difficult-to-attain long <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session), for three years at <s>Puṣkara</s>,
and two years at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, at the <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>, best of twice-born men.
The sages said:
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s>, we wish to hear the future of the peoples.

children.text: purā kila yadetadvai vyatītaṃ kīrtitaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: You have indeed recounted what happened long ago and has passed away.

children.text: yeṣu vai sthāsyate kṣatramutpatsyante nṛpāśca ye
children.translated_text: The lines in which kṣatra will remain, and the kings who will arise,
their measure of life, and those kings by name,
the measure of the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>, and likewise of the <s>Tretā</s> and <s>Dvāpara</s>,
the measure of the <s>Kaliyuga</s>, the defect of the yuga, and the wasting away of the yuga,
the measure of happiness and suffering, and the fault of the people in the yuga:

children.text: etatsarvaṃ prasaṃkhyāya pṛcchatāṃ brūhi naḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: reckoning all this, tell it to us who ask, lord.
The <s>Sūta</s> said:
As it was formerly recounted to me by <s>Vyāsa</s>, whose deeds are unwearied,

children.text: bhāvyaṃ kaliyugaṃ caiva tathā manvantarāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: the future <s>Kaliyuga</s> and also the <s>manvantaras</s> (cosmic ages of Manus),
all the things still to come: listen as I speak.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi bhaviṣyā ye nṛpāstathā ||
children.translated_text: From here onward I shall declare the kings who will exist in the future,
in the <s>Aiḍa-Ikṣvāku</s> line and also in the <s>Paurava</s> line,
those in whom that auspicious <s>Aiḍa-Ikṣvāku</s> family will come to rest;
I shall name all those kings, as spoken of in the future.

children.text: tebhyo'pare'pi ye tv anye hy utpatsyante nṛpāḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: And the other kings besides them who will again arise,
kṣatriyas, pāraśavas, śūdras, and others who live outside,
<s>Andhas</s>, <s>Śakas</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, <s>Cūlikas</s>, and <s>Yavanas</s>,
<s>Kaivartas</s>, <s>Ābhīras</s>, <s>Śabaras</s>, and others born from mlecchas,
I shall declare those kings in order and by name.
Of these, King <s>Adhisomakṛṣṇa</s> is first at present.
In his lineage I shall tell of the kings spoken of in the future.
But <s>Adhisomakṛṣṇa</s>'s son <s>Vivakṣu</s> will become king, O ruler.
When that city called <s>Nāgasāhvaya</s> has been carried away by the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
<s>Vivakṣu</s>, abandoning the city, will dwell in <s>Kauśāmbī</s>.
He will have eight sons, of great strength and valor.
<s>Bhūri</s> will be his eldest son; his son is remembered as <s>Citraratha</s>.
From <s>Citraratha</s> came <s>Śucidrava</s>, and from <s>Śucidrava</s>, <s>Vṛṣṇimant</s>.
From <s>Vṛṣṇimant</s> will come <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, a pure king.
From that <s>Suṣeṇa</s> will come a ruler named <s>Sunītha</s>.
From king <s>Sunītha</s> will come <s>Nṛcakṣu</s>, of very great fame.
The heir of <s>Nṛcakṣu</s> will be <s>Sukhīvala</s>.
The son of <s>Sukhīvala</s> will also be the future king <s>Pariṣṇava</s>.
The son of <s>Pariṣṇava</s> will also be king <s>Sutapā</s>.

children.text: medhāvī tasya dāyādo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Medhāvī</s> will be his heir; there is no doubt.
And the son of <s>Medhāvī</s> will be <s>Puraṃjaya</s>.

children.text: urvo bhāvyaḥ sutastasya tigmātmā tasya cātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: His son will be <s>Urva</s>; <s>Tigmātman</s> will be his son.
From <s>Tigma</s> will come <s>Bṛhadratha</s>, and from <s>Bṛhadratha</s>, <s>Vasudāman</s>.
From <s>Vasudāman</s> will come <s>Śatānīka</s>, and after him <s>Udayana</s>.
And from <s>Udayana</s> there will be the king <s>Vahīnara</s>.
The son of <s>Vahīnara</s> will indeed be <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>.
From <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> will come <s>Niramitra</s>, and from <s>Niramitra</s>, <s>Kṣemaka</s>.
Here this lineage-verse was sung by ancient Brahmins:
The lineage which is the source of brahma and kṣatra, honored by divine seers,

children.text: kṣemakaṃ prāpya rājānaṃ saṃsthāsyati kalau yuge ||
children.translated_text: will, on reaching king <s>Kṣemaka</s>, come to an end in the Kali age.
Thus this <s>Paurava</s> lineage has been properly recounted here,
the lineage of the wise son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, the great-souled <s>Arjuna</s>.
The seers said:

children.text: ye pūjyāḥ syur dvijātīnāmagnayaḥ sūta sarvadā
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>, now tell us those fires that should always be honored by the twice-born,
and tell that lineage in order.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
That fire who is remembered as <s>Abhimānī</s> in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> interval
was the mind-born son of <s>Brahmā</s>; from him <s>Svāhā</s> gave birth

children.text: pāvakaṃ pavamānaṃ ca śuciragniśca yaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: to <s>Pāvaka</s>, <s>Pavamāna</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>, who is remembered as Agni.
<s>Pavamāna</s> is the fire produced by churning; the lightning-born fire is the son of <s>Pāvaka</s>.

children.text: śuciragniḥ smṛtaḥ sauraḥ sthāvarāścaiva te smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śuci</s> Agni is remembered as solar, and those are also remembered as stationary forms.
The son of <s>Pavamāna</s> is the fire called <s>Havyavāha</s>.
<s>Pāvaka</s> is joined with <s>Saharakṣa</s>, while <s>Śuci</s> has <s>Havyavāha</s> as foremost.
The gods' <s>Havyavāha</s> Agni was the first son of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: saharakṣaḥ surāṇāṃ tu trayāṇāṃ te trayo 'gnayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Saharakṣa</s> belongs to the gods; among those three, these are the three fires.
Their sons and grandsons are likewise forty.
I shall declare them by name, each separately according to its division.
