children.text: pāvano laukiko hy agniḥ prathamo brahmaṇaśca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pāvana</s>, the worldly fire, is the first one, belonging to <s>Brahmā</s>.
The <s>Brahmaudana</s> fire was his son, famed by the name <s>Bharata</s>.
<s>Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>Havyavāha</s>, died while carrying the oblation.
When he had died, <s>Puṣkarodadhi</s>, the son of <s>Atharvan</s>, was churned forth.

children.text: yo 'tharvā laukiko hy agnir dakṣiṇāgniḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: He who is <s>Atharvan</s>, the worldly fire, is called <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>.
<s>Atharvan</s> was born from <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s> is remembered as born from <s>Atharvan</s>.

children.text: tasya hy alaukiko hy agnirdakṣiṇāgniḥ sa vai smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His supernatural fire is indeed remembered as <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>.

children.text: atha yaḥ pavamānastu nirmathyo'gniḥ sa ucyate
children.translated_text: Now <s>Pavamāna</s> is called the fire produced by churning.

children.text: sa ca vai gārhapatyo'gniḥ prathamo brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And he is indeed the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, remembered as the first of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sabhyāvasathyau ca saṃśatyās tau sutāvubhau
children.translated_text: Then came <s>Sabhya</s> and <s>Āvasathya</s>; those two were both sons of <s>Saṃśati</s>.
Then <s>Havyavāhana</s> desired the sixteen rivers.
He is the one whom Brahmins remember as the personified <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.

children.text: kāverīṃ kṛṣṇaveṇīṃ ca narmadāṃ yamunāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kāverī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇī</s>, <s>Narmadā</s>, and likewise <s>Yamunā</s>,
<s>Godāvarī</s>, <s>Vitastā</s>, <s>Candrabhāgā</s>, and <s>Irāvatī</s>,

children.text: vipāśāṃ kauśikīṃ caiva śatadruṃ sarayūṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vipāśā</s> and <s>Kauśikī</s>, <s>Śatadru</s> and likewise <s>Sarayū</s>,

children.text: sītāṃ manasvinīṃ caiva hrādinīṃ pāvanāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Manasvinī</s>, <s>Hrādinī</s>, and likewise <s>Pāvanā</s>:
among them he divided himself sixteenfold, separately in each.

children.text: tadā tu viharaṃstāsu dhiṣṇyecchaḥ sa babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: Then, moving among them, he became one who desired the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> hearths.
The <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> stood under their own names, and the <s>dhiṣṇavas</s> were born among them.
Because they were born in the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s>, they are therefore remembered as <s>dhiṣṇavas</s>.
Thus these sons of the rivers entered into the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s>.
Hear which of them are to be approached in movement and attended upon.
<s>Vibhu</s>, <s>Pravāhaṇa</s>, and <s>Agnīdhra</s> are the other <s>dhiṣṇavas</s> stationed there.
He moves according to his proper place at the commencement of the auspicious day.
Hear the order of the fires that are not to be specified and not to be warded off.
<s>Vāsava</s> Agni, <s>Kṛśānu</s>, and the second <s>Uttaravedika</s>,
<s>Samrāḍ</s>, the son of Agni: Brahmins attend upon those eight.
<s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Pavamāna</s>, is seen as the second.
<s>Pāvaka</s>, <s>Uṣṇa</s>, and <s>Samūhya</s>; he is called the northern fire.

children.text: havyasūdo hy asaṃmṛjyaḥ śāmitraḥ sa vibhāvyate
children.translated_text: <s>Havyasūd</s>, <s>Asaṃmṛjya</s>, and <s>Śāmitra</s> are distinguished.
He is called <s>Śatadhāman</s>, <s>Sudhājyotis</s>, and <s>Raudraiśvarya</s>.
<s>Brahmajyotis</s> and <s>Vasudhāman</s> are called the one occupying <s>Brahmā</s>'s station.
<s>Ajaikapād</s> is to be attended upon; he is indeed <s>Śālāmukha</s>.
<s>Ahirbudhnya</s> is to be specified, and at the outer end are the two southern ones.

children.text: putrā hyete tu sarvasya upastheyā dvijaiḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are remembered as the sons of all, to be attended upon by Brahmins.
Next I shall tell those eight sons who are to be approached in movement.
The son of <s>Hautriya</s> is Agni, <s>Havyavāhana</s>, son of <s>Barhis</s>.
The fire <s>Praśaṃsya</s> is praised; <s>Pracetas</s> is the second, together with his assistants.
The son of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Viśvavedas</s>, is called the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>.

children.text: apāṃ yoniḥ smṛtaḥ svāmbhaḥ seturnāma vibhāvyate
children.translated_text: The source of the waters is remembered as <s>Svāmbha</s>; he is understood under the name <s>Setu</s>.

children.text: dhiṣṇya āharaṇā hyete somenejyanta vai dvijaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: These <s>dhiṣṇya</s> and <s>āharaṇa</s> fires were indeed worshipped with <s>Soma</s> by the twice-born.

children.text: tato yaḥ pāvako nāmnā yaḥ sadbhiryoga ucyate
children.translated_text: Then the one named <s>Pāvaka</s>, whom the good call <s>Yoga</s>,
that <s>Agni</s> should be known as the <s>Avabhṛtha</s>; he is worshipped together with <s>Varuṇa</s>.
The son of <s>Agni</s> of the heart is this one in the belly, cooking for human beings.
The wrathful belly-fire, <s>Jaṭhara</s>, is constantly remembered as <s>Viddhāgni</s>.
The fire arising from mutual contact here, powerful and burning beings,
is remembered as the terrible <s>Saṃvartaka</s>, son of wrathful <s>Agni</s>.
Drinking the waters, he dwells in the ocean at the mare's mouth.
The son of the ocean-dweller is understood as <s>Saharakṣa</s>.

children.text: saharakṣastu vai kāmāngṛhe sa vasate nṛṇām
children.translated_text: <s>Saharakṣa</s> indeed dwells in the homes of men, attending to their desires.
His son is the flesh-eating fire, which indeed eats dead men.
Thus these sons of <s>Pāvaka Agni</s> have been proclaimed by the twice-born.
Then his sons, through their great power, were carried off by Gandharvas and Asuras.
The fire that is churned in the fire-sticks obtained its kindling.

children.text: āyur nāmnā tu bhagavānpaśau yastu praṇīyate ||
children.translated_text: The blessed one named <s>Āyu</s> is the one that is led forward in the animal rite.
<s>Mahimān</s> was the son of <s>Āyu</s>; after him his son was <s>Dahana</s>.
Presiding over <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked-offering rites), he consumes the offered <s>havya</s> (oblations).
He who consumes <s>havya</s> and <s>kavya</s> from the whole world of the gods,
his son is <s>Agni Sahita</s>, the wondrous one of great fame.
Presiding over <s>prāyaścittas</s> (expiations), he consumes the offered <s>havya</s>.
The son of <s>Adbhuta</s> is the heroic <s>Devāṃśa</s>, remembered as great.
From him came <s>Vividhāgni</s>; his son was the great sage.
From <s>Arka</s>, son of <s>Vividhāgni</s>, eight fires are remembered as sons.
He who presides over desired <s>iṣṭis</s>, destroys demons, and brings prosperity,
<s>Surabhi</s>, <s>Vasumān</s>, <s>Nāda</s>, <s>Haryaśva</s>, and <s>Rukmavān</s>,
<s>Pravargya</s> and <s>Kṣemavān</s>: these eight are proclaimed.
This is the progeny of <s>Śucyagni</s>, and the fires are fourteen in number.

children.text: ityete hyagnayaḥ proktāḥ praṇītā ye hi cādhvare
children.translated_text: Thus these fires have been declared, those that are set forward in the <s>adhvara</s> (sacrifice).

children.text: samatīte tu sarge ye yāmaiḥ saha surottamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who, in the creation that has passed, were together with the excellent gods, the <s>Yāmas</s>,
in the former <s>Svāyambhuva</s> interval, were those presiding fires.
Here these, among moving and unmoving beings,
were formerly <s>Agnīdhras</s>, carriers of oblations, presiding over their stations.
Those fires of desired, occasional, and other rites were established in ritual actions.
In the former, elapsed <s>manvantara</s>, together with those bright <s>Yāmas</s>,
these were with the hosts of gods in the interval of the first <s>Manu</s>.
Thus these wombs of <s>Jātavedas</s>, called his stations, have been stated.
They should be known in the seven intervals from <s>Svārociṣa</s> through <s>Sāvarṇa</s>.
By them in this way the characteristic of <s>Jātavedas</s> has been enumerated here
in all the present and future <s>manvantaras</s>.
In all <s>manvantaras</s>, with manifold forms and purposes,
the fires continue together with the present <s>Yāma</s> gods.
And the future fires will dwell together with the future gods.
Thus this ordered series of fires has been spoken by me in sequence,
in detail and in proper order. What else do you wish to hear?
The sages said:
Now tell what <s>Viṣṇu</s>, when asked, declared as the supreme and highest matter;
tell that now in detail, the full extent of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus, in that single ocean, <s>Janārdana</s> in fish-form
told the entire extent of the primal creation and the re-creation,
the Self of the universe, to <s>Manu</s>, son of the Sun,
and also <s>karmayoga</s> and <s>sāṃkhya</s>, correctly and in full detail.
The sages said:
We wish to hear, O <s>Sūta</s>, the characteristic mark of <s>karmayoga</s>;
for there is nothing in the world unknown to you, O one of good vows.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain <s>karmayoga</s> as <s>Viṣṇu</s> described it.
For <s>karmayoga</s> is praised above a thousand <s>jñānayogas</s>.
Knowledge arises from <s>karmayoga</s>; from that comes the supreme state.
<s>Brahman</s> arises from action and knowledge, and there is no knowledge from inaction.
Therefore a self disciplined in action attains the eternal truth.
The whole <s>Veda</s> is the root of <s>dharma</s>, and so too is the conduct of those who know it.
In it eight qualities of the self are established as principal:

children.text: dayā sarveṣu bhūteṣu kṣāntī rakṣāturasya tu ||
children.translated_text: compassion toward all beings, forbearance, and protection of the afflicted;
also freedom from envy in the world, and purity within and without, O twice-borns;
ease in undertakings and the practice of auspicious conduct;

children.text: na ca dravyeṣu kārpaṇyam ārteṣūpārjiteṣu ca
children.translated_text: and no meanness regarding possessions, including what has been acquired for those in distress;
and likewise, always, lack of desire for another's property and for another's wife.
The eight qualities of the self have been stated by those skilled in the <s>Purāṇa</s>.
This very <s>kriyāyoga</s> (discipline of practice) is the means of accomplishing <s>jñānayoga</s>.

children.text: karmayogaṃ vinā jñānaṃ kasyacin neha dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Without <s>karmayoga</s>, no one's knowledge is seen here.
One should carefully attend to the <s>dharma</s> taught by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>.

children.text: devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca sarvadā
children.translated_text: For the deities, the ancestors, and human beings, always,
day by day one should perform satisfaction of beings and hosts of sages through <s>yajñas</s>.
With <s>svādhyāyas</s> let the learned man worship the seers, and with oblations according to rule;
the ancestors with <s>śrāddhas</s>, and beings with gifts of food and <s>bali</s> rites.
These five <s>yajñas</s> are prescribed for removing the five unavoidable household injuries.
The chopping block, the grinding stone, the hearth, the water-pot, and the broom:

children.text: pañca sūnā gṛhasthasya tena svargaṃ na gacchati
children.translated_text: these are the five slaughter-places of a householder; because of them he does not go to heaven.
For the destruction of that sin, these five sacrifices are proclaimed.
The twenty-two and also the eight rites of consecration that are proclaimed:
even one furnished with them is not fit for liberation if he is devoid of the virtues of the self.
Therefore, endowed with the virtues of the self, one should perform the rites taught by revelation.
With wealth for cows and Brāhmaṇas he should always perform what is auspicious.
With cows, land, gold, garments, perfumes, garlands, and water,
he should worship <s>Śiva</s>, whose nature is <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Sun, <s>Rudra</s>, and the <s>Vasus</s>.
He should do so with vows and fasts according to rule, with faith, and without envy.
He who is beyond the senses, tranquil, subtle, unmanifest, and eternal,
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, the form of the universe: these indeed are his manifestations.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the blessed <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, and the bull-bannered lord,
and likewise the eight <s>Vasus</s> and the eleven lords of hosts,
the guardians and rulers of the worlds, the fathers, and the mothers too:
these manifestations, together with the moving and unmoving world, have been declared.
The lord of the unmanifest is remembered as the root of the four beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: oṃ oṃ brahmaṇā cātha sūryeṇa viṣṇunātha śivena vā
children.translated_text: Oṃ, oṃ. By <s>Brahmā</s>, or then by the Sun, by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or by <s>Śiva</s>,
because there is no difference, when one is worshiped, all that moves and does not move is worshiped.
He is the supreme abode of those beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> and the very support of the three.
Therefore <s>Pūṣan</s>, in the form of the Veda, should be worshiped with care.
For that reason, making fire and Brāhmaṇas the mouths, a man should worship these deities
with gifts, vows, fasts, recitation, oblations, and the like.
For one devoted to the yoga of rites, fond of Vedānta, śāstra, and smṛti,

children.text: vikarmabhītasya sadā na kiṃcit prāptavyamastīha pare ca loke ||
children.translated_text: and always fearful of forbidden action, there is nothing left to be attained here or in the next world.
The sages said:
Tell us the number of the Purāṇas, O <s>Sūta</s>, in full and in order,
and also the entire dharma of giving, properly and in sequence.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In the Purāṇas, at that time, the ancient Person himself
spoke to <s>Manu</s>; hear what that soul of the universe said.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
The Purāṇa was first remembered by <s>Brahmā</s> as the foremost of all śāstras.
After that, the Vedas issued forth from his mouths.
At the end of a kalpa, O sinless one, there was just one Purāṇa,
holy, serving the three human goals, and extending to a hundred crores.

children.text: nirdagdheṣu ca lokeṣu vājirūpeṇa vai mayā
children.translated_text: When the worlds had been burned up, I, in the form of a horse,
took up the limbs, the four Vedas, the Purāṇa, and the extensive Nyāya,

children.text: mīmāṃsāṃ dharmaśāstraṃ ca parigṛhya mayā kṛtam
children.translated_text: as well as Mīmāṃsā and Dharmaśāstra; these were gathered together by me.
Then again, in the form of a fish at the beginning of the kalpa, in the ocean of waters,
all this was recounted by me while I was within the waters.
Having heard it, the four-faced one declared it to the sages and the gods.
Thereafter the activity of all śāstras arose from the Purāṇa.
Then, O king, seeing over time that the Purāṇa was no longer being fully grasped,
I assume the form of <s>Vyāsa</s> and condense it in every age,
always in each <s>Dvāpara</s>, to the measure of four hundred thousand.
Having made it eighteenfold, it is made manifest here in this earth-world.
Even now, in the world of the gods, it extends to a hundred crores.
Here its meaning has been placed in summary in four hundred thousand verses.
Now the eighteen Purāṇas are being described here.
I shall tell them by name; listen, best of sages,
in the measure in which they were formerly spoken by <s>Brahmā</s> to <s>Marīci</s>.
The <s>Brāhma</s> Purāṇa is proclaimed as thirteen thousand verses.
Whoever writes it out and gives it together with a water-cow,
on the full moon of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, is honored in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
When this very world became a golden lotus,
because it rests on the account of that event, the wise likewise call it the <s>Pādma</s>.
The <s>Pādma</s> is said here to be fifty-five thousand verses.
Whoever gives that Purāṇa together with a golden lotus,
in the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, along with sesame, obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice.
With reference to the account of the <s>Vārāha</s> kalpa, <s>Parāśara</s>
spoke all dharmas; furnished with that, it is known as the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> Purāṇa.
Whoever gives that in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, together with a ghee-cow,

children.text: paurṇamāsyāṃ vipūtātmā sa padaṃ yāti vāruṇam
children.translated_text: on the full-moon day, purified in self, goes to the realm of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
The wise know its measure to be twenty-three thousand verses.
In connection with the <s>Śveta</s> kalpa, <s>Vāyu</s> here proclaimed dharmas.
Where that text, joined with the greatness of <s>Rudra</s>, occurs, it is the <s>Vāyavīya</s>.
That Purāṇa is here said to be twenty-four thousand verses.
In the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, on the <s>Śrāvaṇī</s> day, together with a jaggery-cow,
whoever gives it, along with a bull, to a Brāhmaṇa householder,
that purified man dwells for one kalpa in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
Where, taking up the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the full extent of dharma is described,
together with the slaying of <s>Vṛtrāsura</s>, that is called the <s>Bhāgavata</s>.
In the middle of the <s>Sārasvata</s> kalpa, those excellent men who came to be,
from the account of them arising in the world, that too is called the <s>Bhāgavata</s>.
Whoever writes that out and gives it together with a golden lion,

children.text: paurṇamāsyāṃ prauṣṭhapadyāṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: on the full moon of <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s>, goes to the supreme goal.
That Purāṇa is declared to be eighteen thousand verses.
Where <s>Nārada</s> taught dharmas and matters based on the <s>Bṛhat</s> kalpa,
that is called the <s>Nāradīya</s>, twenty-five thousand verses.
On the fifteenth day of <s>Āśvina</s>, one should give it together with a cow.
He obtains supreme siddhi, from which return is hard to attain.
Where, with reference to the birds, the examination of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>
was explained, in answer to the sage's question, by sages who practiced <s>dharma</s>.
All that was related at length by <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>;
that <s>Purāṇa</s> of nine thousand verses is here called the <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>.
And whoever copies it and gives it together with a golden elephant,
on <s>Kārttikī</s>, becomes a sharer in the fruit of the <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> sacrifice.

children.text: yat tad īśānakaṃ kalpaṃ vṛttāntamadhikṛtya ca
children.translated_text: That which concerns the <s>Īśāna</s> kalpa and its events,
which <s>Agni</s> spoke to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, they call the <s>Āgneya</s>.
Whoever writes that and gives it, together with a golden lotus,
in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, according to rule, accompanied by a sesame-cow,
that text of sixteen thousand verses grants the fruit of all sacrifices.
The person who gives it is then honored in heaven.
Where the four-faced one, taking up the greatness of <s>Āditya</s>,
in connection with the events of the <s>Aghora</s> kalpa, described the stability of the world
and told <s>Manu</s> the characteristics of the multitude of beings,

children.text: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi tathā pañca śatāni ca
children.translated_text: that text, of fourteen thousand and also five hundred verses,
chiefly concerning future events, is here called the <s>Bhaviṣya</s>.
Whoever gives that in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, on the full-moon day, free from envy,
together with a jar of jaggery, obtains the fruit of an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice.
And concerning the events of the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> kalpa,
where <s>Sāvarṇi</s> told <s>Nārada</s> the supreme greatness of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
and where the account of <s>Brahmavarāha</s> is repeatedly described,
that text of eighteen thousand verses is called the <s>Brahmavaivarta</s>.
Whoever gives the <s>Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa</s> in the month of <s>Māgha</s>,
on the full-moon day, an auspicious day, is honored in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
Where the god <s>Maheśvara</s>, standing within a fiery liṅga, spoke,
for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, and liberation, with reference to the <s>Āgneya</s>,
that, at the end of the kalpa, was called the <s>Laiṅga Purāṇa</s> by <s>Brahmā</s> himself.
That text is eleven thousand verses; whoever gives it in <s>Phālguna</s>,
together with a sesame-cow, goes to equality with <s>Śiva</s>.
Again, concerning the greatness of the great <s>Varāha</s>,
that which was spoken by <s>Viṣṇu</s> to the Earth is here called the <s>Vārāha</s>.
In connection with the kalpa of <s>Manu</s>, O best of sages,
that <s>Purāṇa</s> is here said to have twenty-four thousand verses.
Having made a golden <s>Garuḍa</s>, together with a sesame-cow,
one should give it on the full-moon day in <s>Madhu</s> to a Brahmin householder.
By the grace of <s>Varāha</s>, he obtains the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> state.
Where <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>, taking up the <s>Māheśvara</s> dharmas,
described the events in the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> kalpa, amplified with narratives,
the <s>Purāṇa</s> named <s>Skānda</s> is said to be eighty-one
thousand verses and one hundred, so it is said among mortals.
Whoever copies it and gives it together with a golden trident
obtains the <s>Śaiva</s> state when the sun has entered <s>Mīna</s>.
Taking up the greatness of <s>Trivikrama</s>, the four-faced one
declared the three aims of life; that is celebrated as the <s>Vāmana</s>.
It is an auspicious <s>Purāṇa</s> of ten thousand verses, following the <s>Kūrma</s> kalpa.
Whoever gives it at the autumnal equinox goes to the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> state.
Where, in <s>Rasātala</s>, the greatness of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire,
and liberation was told by <s>Janārdana</s> in tortoise form,
to the sages, in the presence of <s>Śakra</s>, in connection with <s>Indradyumna</s>,
that text has eighteen thousand verses and is connected with the <s>Lakṣmī</s> kalpa.
Whoever gives the <s>Kūrma</s> at the solstice, together with a golden tortoise,
obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows.
Where, at the beginning of the kalpa, for the setting in motion of the Vedas, <s>Janārdana</s>
in fish form spoke to <s>Manu</s>, describing <s>Narasiṃha</s>,
and, taking that up, told the events of seven kalpas, O lords of sages,
know that as the <s>Mātsya</s>, of fourteen thousand verses.
At the equinox, together with a golden fish and also with a cow,

children.text: yo dadyātpṛthivī tena dattā bhavati cākhilā ||
children.translated_text: whoever gives it has thereby given the entire earth.
And when, in the <s>Gāruḍa</s> kalpa, from the cosmic egg came the birth of <s>Garuḍa</s>,
concerning which <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> spoke, that is here called the <s>Gāruḍa</s>.
That is recited here as eighteen thousand plus one thousand verses.
The man who gives it here together with a golden goose

children.text: sa siddhiṃ labhate mukhyāṃ śivaloke ca saṃsthitim ||
children.translated_text: obtains foremost siddhi and residence in <s>Śivaloka</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> again spoke concerning the greatness of the cosmic egg,
and that <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> is twelve thousand and two hundred verses.

children.text: bhaviṣyāṇāṃ ca kalpānāṃ śrūyate yatra vistaraḥ
children.translated_text: Where the expanse of future kalpas is heard,
that <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s> was declared by <s>Brahmā</s>.
Whoever gives that at the <s>Vyatīpāta</s>, together with a pair of yellow woolen garments,
that human obtains the fruit of a thousand <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifices.
And that, together with a golden cow, grants the fruit of <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
This has been declared as four hundred thousand verses by <s>Vyāsa</s> of wondrous deeds.

children.text: matpiturmama pitrā ca mayā tubhyaṃ niveditam ||
children.translated_text: It was imparted to you by my father, by my father's father, and by me.
For the welfare of the world here, it was abridged by the supreme seer.
Even today among the gods this text extends to a hundred crores.
I shall declare the subsidiary divisions that are established in the world.
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, where the description of <s>Narasiṃha</s> is stated,
that, consisting of eighteen thousand verses, is here called the <s>Nārasiṃha Purāṇa</s>.
Where the greatness of <s>Nandā</s> is described by <s>Kārttikeya</s>,
that is celebrated, called by people the <s>Nandīpurāṇa</s>.
Where a future narrative is told with <s>Sāmba</s> placed first,
that again, O sages firm in vows, is known in the world as the <s>Sāmba</s>.
The wise know the <s>Purāṇas</s> as belonging to the ancient <s>kalpa</s>.
The sequence of the <s>Purāṇas</s> is blessed, fame-giving, and life-giving;
and there too this is spoken of by the name <s>Āditya</s>.
But whatever <s>Purāṇa</s> is assigned separately apart from the eighteen,
know, best of twice-borns, that it has issued forth from these.
Among the <s>Purāṇas</s>, a narrative is remembered as one of the five limbs:
creation, re-creation, lineage, and the <s>manvantara</s> periods,
and also the accounts of dynastic descendants; a <s>Purāṇa</s> has these five marks.
The greatness of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Sun, and <s>Rudra</s>, and of the world,
together with dissolution and bestowal, is taught in the fivefold <s>Purāṇa</s>.
<s>Dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> are also proclaimed here,
and, in all the <s>Purāṇas</s>, whatever result is opposed to them.
In the sāttvika <s>Purāṇas</s>, the greatness of <s>Hari</s> is predominant;
in the rājasa ones, they know the greatness of <s>Brahmā</s> to be predominant.
Likewise in the tāmasa ones, the greatness of <s>Agni</s> and of <s>Śiva</s> is taught,
and in the mixed ones that of <s>Sarasvatī</s> and the ancestors is declared.
After composing the eighteen <s>Purāṇas</s>, the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>
made the entire narrative called the <s>Bhārata</s>, expanded by them,
which was spoken in one lakh verses, enriched with the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>.
And the excellent tale of <s>Rāma</s> that was spoken by <s>Vālmīki</s>,
and that which was declared by <s>Brahmā</s>, extending to a hundred crore verses,
having drawn it forth, he gave it thus to <s>Nārada</s>, and by him again to <s>Vālmīki</s>;
and by <s>Vālmīki</s> it was made known in the worlds as a means to <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s>.

children.text: evaṃ sapādāḥ pañcaite lakṣā martye prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus these five and a quarter lakhs are proclaimed among mortals.
The wise know the <s>Purāṇas</s> as belonging to the ancient <s>kalpa</s>.
The sequence of the <s>Purāṇas</s> is blessed, fame-giving, and life-giving;

children.text: yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: whoever reads or even hears it goes to the highest state.

children.text: idaṃ pavitraṃ yaśaso nidhānamidaṃ pitṝṇāmativallabhaṃ ca
children.translated_text: This is pure; this is a treasury of fame and is very dear to the ancestors;

children.text: idaṃ ca deveṣv amṛtāyitaṃ ca nityaṃ tvidaṃ pāpaharaṃ ca puṃsām ||
children.translated_text: and this is like nectar among the gods; this is always a remover of men's sins.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
After this I shall expound completely the <s>dharmas</s> of giving,
together with vows and fasts, as they have been stated here by <s>Matsya</s>.
In the dialogue of <s>Mahādeva</s> and wise <s>Nārada</s>,
I shall relate what occurred, accomplishing <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s>.
Once <s>Nārada</s> asked him as he sat on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>,
bowing respectfully to <s>Hara</s>, the enemy of <s>Anaṅga</s>, the destroyer of <s>Anaṅga</s>'s body.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Lord, lord of gods, ruler of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Indra</s>,
with splendid health, beauty, long life, fortune, auspiciousness, and prosperity,
how may a man, a devotee of yours or of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, become endowed?
Or how may a woman, even a widow, be endowed with every virtue and good fortune?
O god, please tell here of some vow that in due order bestows liberation.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
You have asked well, O <s>Brahman</s>, about what brings benefit to all worlds.
Hear, O <s>Nārada</s>, that vow which, when heard here, brings peace.
There is a vow named <s>Nakṣatrapuruṣa</s>, whose essence is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Beginning with the feet, one should perform it according to rule, reciting the names of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
One should worship the image of <s>Vāsudeva</s> in the lunar mansions beginning with <s>Mūla</s>,
when the month of <s>Caitra</s> has arrived, after having the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> recite.

children.text: mūle namo viśvadharāya pādau gulphāvanantāya ca rohiṇīṣu
children.translated_text: In <s>Mūla</s>: "Homage to <s>Viśvadhara</s>" for the feet; in <s>Rohiṇī</s>, to <s>Ananta</s> for the ankles.

children.text: jaṅghe'bhipūjye varadāya caiva dve jānunī vāśvikumāraṛkṣe ||
children.translated_text: The shanks are to be worshiped with "to <s>Varada</s>," and the two knees in the constellation of the <s>Aśvikumāras</s>.
In the pair <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> and <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, likewise, the thighs are to be worshiped with "Homage to <s>Śiva</s>."

children.text: pūrvottarāphalguniyugmake ca meḍhraṃ namaḥ pañcaśarāya pūjyam ||
children.translated_text: And in the pair <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s> and <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, the genitals are to be worshiped with "Homage to <s>Pañcaśara</s>."

children.text: kaṭiṃ namaḥ śārṅgadharāya viṣṇoḥ sampūjayennārada kṛttikāsu
children.translated_text: In <s>Kṛttikā</s>, O <s>Nārada</s>, one should worship the waist of <s>Viṣṇu</s> with "Homage to <s>Śārṅgadhara</s>."
Likewise, in the two <s>Bhādrapadās</s>, he should worship the sides with "Homage to <s>Keśiniṣūdana</s>."
The two bellies, O <s>Nārada</s>, are to be worshiped in <s>Revatī</s> with "to <s>Dāmodara</s>."
And in the constellation <s>Anurādhā</s>, the chest likewise is to be worshiped with "Homage to <s>Mādhava</s>."
The back is to be worshiped in <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> with that name, "destroyer of floods of sin."
And in <s>Viśākhā</s>, the arms are to be worshiped with "Homage to the lord of <s>Śrī</s>, bearer of conch, discus, sword, and mace."

children.text: haste tu hastā madhusūdanāya namo'bhipūjyā iti kaiṭabhāreḥ
children.translated_text: On <s>Hasta</s>, the hands are to be worshiped with "Homage to <s>Madhusūdana</s>," the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>.
In <s>Punarvasu</s>, the front parts of the fingers are to be worshiped with "Homage to the lord of the <s>Sāmans</s>."
On the day of the serpent constellation, one should worship the nails of him who bears the fish body.

children.text: kūrmasya pādau śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi jyeṣṭhāsu kaṇṭhe harirarcanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With "I take refuge in the feet of <s>Kūrma</s>," and in <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Hari</s> is to be worshiped at the throat.

children.text: śrotre varāhāya namo'bhipūjyā janārdanasya śravaṇena samyak
children.translated_text: The ears of <s>Janārdana</s> are to be properly worshiped in <s>Śravaṇa</s> with "Homage to <s>Varāha</s>."

children.text: puṣye mukhaṃ dānavasūdanāya namo nṛsiṃhāya ca pūjanīyam ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Puṣya</s>, the face is to be worshiped with "Homage to <s>Dānavasūdana</s>" and "Homage to <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>."
The teeth are to be worshiped with the formula "Homage, homage to <s>Kāraṇavāmana</s>," the crusher.

children.text: āsyaṃ harerbhārgavanandanāya saṃpūjanīyaṃ dvija vāruṇe tu ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vāruṇa</s> constellation, O twice-born, the mouth of <s>Hari</s> is to be worshiped with "to the son of <s>Bhārgava</s>."

children.text: namo'stu rāmāya maghāsu nāsā saṃpūjanīyā raghunandanasya
children.translated_text: In <s>Maghā</s>, the nose of <s>Raghunandana</s> is to be fully worshiped with "Homage to <s>Rāma</s>."

children.text: mṛgottamāṅge nayane'bhipūjye namo'stu te rāma vighūrṇitākṣa ||
children.translated_text: In the chief part of Mṛgaśiras the eyes are to be worshipped. Homage to you, O <s>Rāma</s>, whose eyes are rolling.

children.text: buddhāya śāntāya namo lalāṭaṃ citrāsu saṃpūjyatamaṃ murāreḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the awakened, peaceful one; the forehead of <s>Murāri</s> is most worthy of worship in Citrā.
Having worshipped the head of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the Bharaṇīs, homage to <s>Viśveśvara</s> in the form of <s>Kalki</s>.

children.text: ārdrāsu keśāḥ puruṣottamasya saṃpūjanīyā haraye namaste
children.translated_text: In the Ārdrās the hair of <s>Puruṣottama</s> is to be worshipped; homage to you, O <s>Hari</s>.
On the days of the lunar mansions, fasting and with devotion, excellent brahmins should be honored.

children.text: pūrṇe vrate sarvaguṇānvitāya vāgrūpaśīlāya ca sāmagāya
children.translated_text: When the vow is complete, to him who is endowed with every virtue, whose speech and character are refined, and who chants the <s>Sāman</s>,
one should give a golden image, broad, with long arm-staffs, set with pearls, moonstones, and diamonds,

children.text: jalasya pūrṇe kalaśe niviṣṭāmarcāṃ harervastragavā sahaiva
children.translated_text: an image of <s>Hari</s> placed in a water-filled pot, together with cloth and a cow,
and a bed furnished with accessories, vessels, and the like, to an excellent brahmin.
Whatever here there is to be given, whatever at all there is, one should give everything to the brahmin for one's own welfare.
Make our desires fruitful, O one whose forms are <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>.
One should give a golden <s>Puruṣottama</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>, to the brahmin along with his wife,
and also a bed, with the mantra, free from broken joints or knots.

children.text: yathā na viṣṇubhaktānāṃ vṛjinaṃ jāyate kvacit
children.translated_text: Just as sin never arises anywhere among the devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
so may beauty, health, and supreme devotion to <s>Keśava</s> be mine.

children.text: yathā na lakṣmyā śayanaṃ tava śūnyaṃ janārdana
children.translated_text: Just as your bed, O <s>Janārdana</s>, is not empty of <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
so may my bed also never be empty, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, birth after birth.
Having thus presented all that, the cloth, garlands, and unguent,
one should then send off the brahmin who knows the Nakṣatrapuruṣa.
Having fasted under all the lunar mansions, he should eat food without oil and salt,
and should provide a meal according to his ability, without deceit about his wealth.
Thus, having himself worshipped the Nakṣatrapuruṣa according to rule,
he obtains all desires and is honored in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Whatever sin such as brahmin-murder has been committed here or in the other world,
whether by oneself or by one's ancestors, all that comes to destruction.

children.text: iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vātibhaktyā puruṣavaro vratamaṅganātha kuryāt
children.translated_text: If an excellent man reads or hears this with great devotion, or if a woman, O lord, performs the vow,
it tears apart the impurity of the Kali age and grants men the fruit of every prosperity belonging to <s>Murāri</s>.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
For one who is unable to undertake fasts but desires that same fruit,
through lack of practice or because of illness, what excellent vow is considered best?
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
For those unable even to fast, eating at night is approved.
In the vow in which even that applies, hear now of this great, imperishable observance.
It is called Ādityaśayana, the proper worship of <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
which knowers of the <s>Purāṇa</s> proclaim for certain conjunctions of lunar mansions.
When the seventh lunar day, joined with Hasta, falls on the day of <s>Āditya</s>,
or when there is the Sun's saṃkrānti, that lunar day grants all desires.
One should worship the image of <s>Umāmaheśvara</s> with names of the Sun,
for one worships by performing worship of the Sun upon the <s>Śivaliṅga</s>.

children.text: umāpate ravervāpi na bhedo dṛśyate kvacit
children.translated_text: No distinction at all is seen between the lord of <s>Umā</s> and <s>Ravi</s>.
Therefore, O best of sages, one should worship <s>Śambhu</s> in the house.

children.text: haste ca sūryāya namo'stu pādāvarkāya citrāsu ca gulphadeśam
children.translated_text: In Hasta, homage to <s>Sūrya</s> for the feet; in Citrā, to <s>Arka</s> for the region of the ankles.

children.text: svātīṣu jaṅghe puruṣottamāya dhātre viśākhāsu ca jānudeśam ||
children.translated_text: In Svātī, the shanks are to be worshipped as <s>Puruṣottama</s>; in Viśākhā, the region of the knees as <s>Dhātṛ</s>.
Likewise in Anurādhā, homage is to be paid while worshipping the pair of thighs of the thousand-rayed one.

children.text: jyeṣṭhāsvanaṅgāya namo'stu guhyamindrāya somāya kaṭī ca mūle ||
children.translated_text: In Jyeṣṭhā, homage to <s>Anaṅga</s> for the secret part; in Mūla, the waist is worshipped as <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: pūrvottarāṣāḍhayuge ca nābhiṃ tvaṣṭre namaḥ saptataraṃgamāya
children.translated_text: In the pair Pūrvāṣāḍhā and Uttarāṣāḍhā, the navel is worshipped: homage to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, the seven-horsed one.

children.text: tīkṣṇāṃśave ca śravaṇe ca kukṣau pṛṣṭhaṃ dhaniṣṭhāsu vikartanāya ||
children.translated_text: In Śravaṇa, the belly is worshipped as the sharp-rayed one; in Dhaniṣṭhā, the back as <s>Vikartana</s>.
In the asterism of the lord of waters, the region of the eyes is to be worshipped as the destroyer of darkness.
In the two Bhādrapadās, the arms are to be worshipped with homage to the fierce-rayed one.

children.text: sāmnāmadhīśāya karadvayaṃ ca saṃpūjanīyaṃ dvija revatīṣu
children.translated_text: In Revatī, O brahmin, the two hands are to be worshipped as the lord of the <s>Sāmans</s>.
In the Aśvinīs the nails are to be worshipped: homage to the bearer of the team of seven horses.
In the Bharaṇīs the throat is to be worshipped as the harsh-rayed one, with the formula 'to <s>Divākara</s>'.
In the Fire-star the neck is worshipped, and in Rohiṇī the lower lip as the lord of lotuses, O <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: mṛgottamāṅge daśanā murāreḥ saṃpūjanīyā haraye namaste
children.translated_text: In the chief part of Mṛgaśiras, the teeth of <s>Murāri</s> are to be worshipped: homage to you, O <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: namaḥ savitre rasanāṃ śaṃkare ca nāsābhipūjyā ca punarvasau ca ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Savitṛ</s> for the tongue in <s>Śaṃkara</s>; and in Punarvasu the nose is to be worshipped.
In Puṣya, the forehead is worshipped as the beloved of the lotus; the locks as the bearer of the body of the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text: sārpe'tha mauliṃ vibudhapriyāya maghāsu karṇāviti gogaṇeśe ||
children.translated_text: Then in Āśleṣā the crown is worshipped as dear to the gods, and in Maghā the ears as the lord of the hosts of cows.
In the Pūrvās, the eyes of <s>Śambhu</s> are most worthy of worship as the one honored by cows and brahmins.

children.text: athottarāphalgunibhe bhruvau ca viśveśvarāyeti ca pūjanīye ||
children.translated_text: Then in the Uttarā Phalgunī asterism, the two brows are to be worshipped as <s>Viśveśvara</s>.
Homage to him who bears noose, goad, trident, lotus, skull, serpent, moon, and bow,
homage to <s>Śiva</s>, the root cause of the destruction of <s>Gajāsura</s>, <s>Anaṅga</s>, <s>Pura</s>, <s>Andhaka</s>, and others.

children.text: ityādi cāstrāṇi ca pūjya nityaṃ viśveśvarāyeti śivo'bhipūjyaḥ
children.translated_text: After worshipping the weapons and so on in this way each day, <s>Śiva</s> is to be worshipped as <s>Viśveśvara</s>.
Here one should eat in this manner: vegetables without oil, no meat, no alkaline seasoning, and nothing left over from another's meal.

children.text: ityevaṃ dvija naktāni kṛtvā dadyāt punarvasau
children.translated_text: Thus, O brahmin, after observing night-eating rites, one should give on Punarvasu
a prastha of śāli rice and ghee placed in a vessel made of udumbara wood.
Setting it in a vessel, one should present it to a brahmin together with gold.

children.text: saptame vastrayugmaṃ ca pāraṇe tvadhikaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: On the seventh day there should also be a pair of garments, and at the breaking of the fast something more.
But when the fourteenth day has arrived, at the yearly breaking of the fast, O <s>Nārada</s>...
He should feed Brahmins with devotion, with jaggery, milk, ghee, and the like.
Having made a golden lotus, with eight petals and with a pericarp,
pure, eight finger-breadths in size, and furnished with ruby petals,
and having made an exceptional bed, free from unsuitable knots,
with pillow, resting place, coverlet, and fans,
with vessels, sandals, parasol, yak-tail fan, seat, and mirror,
and also furnished with ornaments, fruits, garments, and unguents,
he should place that virtuous, adorned lotus upon it.
A tawny cow, supplied with cloth, gentle in character and rich in milk,
with silver hoofs, golden horns, with her calf, and with a bronze milking vessel,
he should give in the forenoon with a mantra, and he should not transgress against her.
"Just as your <s>Āditya</s>-bed is always unempty,

children.text: kāntyā dhṛtyā śriyā ratyā tathā me santu siddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so may my attainments be endowed with beauty, firmness, prosperity, and delight.

children.text: yathā na devāḥ śreyāṃsaṃ tvadanyamanaghaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: Just as the gods know no better, stainless one, than you,
so lift me up from the ocean of worldly existence filled with every suffering."
Then, having circumambulated and bowed down, he should dismiss her.
He should take the bed, cow, and all that to the house of the twice-born man.
This vow of the Moon-crested Lord is not to be disclosed to one of bad conduct, to a hypocrite, to one corrupted by false reasoning, or to a slanderer,
nor to one who engages in excessive blame.

children.text: bhaktāya dāntāya ca guhyametadākhyeyam ānandakaraṃ śivasya
children.translated_text: This secret of <s>Śiva</s>, bringing joy, should be told to a devoted and self-controlled person.

children.text: idaṃ mahāpātakabhin narāṇām apyakṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti ||
children.translated_text: Those who know the <s>Veda</s> say that even a syllable of this destroys the great sins of men.
One who performs it is not deprived of relatives, sons, wealth, or wives, and becomes a source of joy to the gods.

children.text: nābhyeti rogaṃ na ca śokaduḥkhaṃ yā vātha nārī kurute'tibhaktyā ||
children.translated_text: He does not encounter disease, grief, or suffering; and so too a woman who performs it with great devotion.

children.text: idaṃ vasiṣṭhena purārjunena kṛtaṃ kubereṇa puraṃdareṇa
children.translated_text: This was formerly performed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, by <s>Arjuna</s>, by <s>Kubera</s>, and by <s>Purandara</s>.
By merely proclaiming it, all sins come to destruction; there is no doubt.

children.text: iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya itthaṃ raviśayanaṃ puruhūtavallabhaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: Whoever thus reads or hears the <s>Raviśayana</s> becomes dear to <s>Puruhūta</s>.

children.text: api narakagatānpitṝn aśeṣānapi divamānayatīha yaḥ karoti ||
children.translated_text: And whoever performs it here brings even all his ancestors who have gone to hell up to heaven.
The Blessed Lord said:
Now I shall explain the <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī</s>, which destroys all sins.
Peace and liberation arise from it, and especially victory for men.
In <s>Mārgaśiras</s> one should worship <s>Śaṃkara</s>, and in <s>Pauṣa</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>;

children.text: māghe maheśvaraṃ devaṃ mahādevaṃ ca phālgune ||
children.translated_text: in <s>Māgha</s>, the god <s>Maheśvara</s>, and in <s>Phālguna</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>.
In <s>Caitra</s> a man should worship <s>Sthāṇu</s>, and likewise in <s>Vaiśākha</s>, <s>Śiva</s>;
in <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> he should worship <s>Paśupati</s>, and in <s>Āṣāḍha</s> he should worship <s>Ugra</s>.
In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> he should worship <s>Śarva</s>, and in <s>Nabhasya</s>, <s>Tryambaka</s>;
in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and likewise in <s>Kārttika</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>.
On all the dark eighth lunar days, according to his ability, he should fully worship Brahmins,
with cows, land, gold, and garments, after fasting, together with devotees of <s>Śiva</s>.
Cow urine, cow ghee, cow milk, sesame seeds, barley, water with <s>kuśa</s> grass,
water from a cow's horn, śirīṣa, arka, bilva leaves, and curds,
and also the five products of the cow: having sipped these, he should worship <s>Śaṃkara</s> at night.

children.text: aśvatthaṃ ca vaṭaṃ caivodumbaraṃ plakṣameva ca
children.translated_text: The aśvattha, the vaṭa, the udumbara, and the plakṣa,

children.text: palāśaṃ jambuvṛkṣaṃ ca viduḥ ṣaṣṭhaṃ maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the palāśa and jambu tree: the great seers know these as the six.
From the months of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> and <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, two by two in order,
he should use, one by one, a tooth-cleaning twig from these trees.

children.text: devāya dadyādarghyaṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃ gāṃ kṛṣṇavāsasam
children.translated_text: He should give an arghya to the god, and give a black cow clothed in black.
At the conclusion he should give rice with curds, a canopy, a banner, and a yak-tail fan,
and water pots for Brahmins, furnished with the five jewels.

children.text: gāvaḥ kṛṣṇāḥ suvarṇaṃ ca vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: He should give black cows, gold, and various garments.
But if he is unable, he should again give even a single cow, according to his means.
He should not act deceitfully with his wealth; doing so, he would incur fault.
Having fasted on <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī</s> for three hundred seven kalpas,
a man, honored by the gods, is magnified in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Tell me that vow by which a man becomes endowed with long life, health, and increase of family,
and, birth after birth, is repeatedly joined with royal houses, O Moon-crested Lord.
The Blessed Lord said:
This which you have asked is proper, and it has been declared to bring inexhaustible merit.
I shall tell you the secret which the knowers of the <s>Purāṇa</s> know.
There is here an excellent vow called <s>Rohiṇīcandraśayana</s>.
In it one should worship the image of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with the names of the Moon.
When, on a Monday, the bright fifteenth lunar day occurs at some time,
or when the Brahma asterism arises on the full-moon day,
then a man should bathe with the five products of the cow and with mustard seeds.
The learned man should then recite the mantra beginning "Āpyāyasva" eight hundred times.
Even a Śūdra, with supreme devotion and avoiding the talk of heretics,

children.text: somāya varadāyātha viṣṇave ca namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should say again and again, "Homage to <s>Soma</s>, the boon-giver, and to <s>Viṣṇu</s>."
Having completed the recitation and returned to his own house,
he should worship <s>Madhusūdana</s> with fruits and flowers, uttering the names of <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: somāya śāntāya namo'stu pādāvanantadhāmneti ca jānujaṅghe
children.translated_text: "Homage to <s>Soma</s>, to the peaceful one"; he should worship the feet, and with "to the one of endless abode," the knees and shanks.
He should fully worship the two thighs with the name <s>Jalodara</s>, and the genitals with <s>Anantabāhu</s>.

children.text: namo namaḥ kāmasukhapradāya kaṭiḥ śaśāṅkasya sadārcanīyā
children.translated_text: "Homage, homage to the giver of the pleasure of desire"; the waist of the Moon-marked one is always to be worshipped.
And likewise the belly with <s>Amṛtodara</s>; the navel is to be worshipped with homage to <s>Śaśāṅka</s>.

children.text: namo'stu candrāya mukhaṃ ca pūjyaṃ dantā dvijānāmadhipāya pūjyāḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Candra</s>; the face is to be worshipped, and the teeth are to be worshipped for the lord of the twice-born.
The smile is to be worshipped with “obeisance to <s>Candra</s>”; the lips, with “to him who loves the groves of night-lotuses.”

children.text: nāsā ca nāthāya vanauṣadhīnāmānandabhūtāya punarbhruvau ca
children.translated_text: And the nose is for the lord of forest herbs; then the two brows are for him whose nature is bliss.
The pair of eyes, lotus-like, belongs likewise to the Moon, to <s>Śauri</s>, whose rays are dark as blue lotuses.
Obeisance to him who is revered by all sacrifices; the two ears are for the destroyer of demons.
The forehead is for the Moon, dear to the ocean; the hairs are to be worshipped as belonging to the lord of the <s>Suṣumnā</s> ray.

children.text: śiraḥ śaśāṅkāya namo murārerviśveśvarāyeti namaḥ kirīṭine
children.translated_text: Obeisance to the moon-crested head of <s>Murāri</s>; obeisance to the lord of the universe, the crowned one.
O lover of lotuses, O <s>Rohiṇī</s>, named <s>Lakṣmī</s>, whose lovely body is the nectar of good fortune and happiness,
one should worship the goddess, the wife of <s>Indu</s>, with fragrant flowers, food-offerings, incense, and the rest.

children.text: suptvātha bhūmau punarutthitena snātvā ca viprāya haviṣyayuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having slept on the ground, risen again, and bathed, in the morning one should give to a Brahmin
a water-jar together with sacrificial food, gold, and water, saying, “Obeisance to the destroyer of sins.”
Having sipped cow urine, and having taken food without meat and without alkaline seasoning,
one should fast, eat twenty-eight morsels mixed with milk and ghee, and listen to an <s>Itihāsa</s> for a muhūrta.
<s>Kadamba</s>, blue lotus, <s>ketakā</s>, jasmine, lotus, and the hundred-petaled lotus,
the unfading and dwarf varieties, then <s>sinduvāra</s>, and again, O <s>Nārada</s>, the jasmine flower,

children.text: śubhraṃ ca viṣṇoḥ karavīrapuṣpaṃ śrīcampakaṃ candramasaḥ pradeyam ||
children.translated_text: a white flower and the karavīra flower for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and fine campaka are to be offered to <s>Candra</s>.
In the months beginning with <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, these are always to be offered in order.
In whichever month the vow begins, one should worship <s>Hari</s> with the flowers belonging to that month.
Thus, for as long as a year, a man should attend upon him according to rule.
At the end of the vow he should give a bed furnished with a mirror and accessories.
Then he should have a golden pair of <s>Rohiṇī</s> and <s>Candra</s> made.
<s>Candra</s> should be made six aṅgulas high, and <s>Rohiṇī</s> four aṅgulas high.
It should be furnished with eight pearls and covered with a white cloth for the eyes.
Again, on top of a milk-jar, in a bronze vessel furnished with unbroken rice,
he should give it in the forenoon with the mantra, together with rice, sugarcane, and fruit.
Then he should give a white cow with a golden face and silver hooves,

children.text: savastrabhājanāṃ dhenuṃ tathā śaṅkhaṃ ca śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: with cloth and vessels, and also a fine conch.
Having adorned with ornaments a virtuous Brahmin couple, endowed with good qualities,
he should imagine, “This is <s>Candra</s> in the form of a Brahmin, together with his wife.”

children.text: yathā na rohiṇī kṛṣṇa śayyāṃ saṃtyajya gacchati
children.translated_text: “Just as <s>Rohiṇī</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, does not abandon the bed and depart,
so, with prosperity, may there be no separation for me from you in your form as <s>Soma</s>.
Just as you alone are the giver of supreme bliss and liberation to all,
so may enjoyment, liberation, and devotion to you, O <s>Candra</s>, always be mine.”
Thus, O sinless one, for one afraid of saṃsāra and desiring liberation,
this is the unsurpassed means for producing beauty, health, and long life.

children.text: idameva pitṝṇāṃ ca sarvadā vallabhaṃ mune
children.translated_text: This very rite is always dear to the ancestors too, O sage.
Having become lord of the three worlds for three hundred and seven kalpas,
he attains <s>Candraloka</s>; then, becoming lightning-like, he is liberated.

children.text: nārī vā rohiṇī candraśayanaṃ yā samācaret
children.translated_text: And a woman who performs the <s>Rohiṇī</s>-<s>Candra</s> bed-rite
also obtains that fruit, from which return is hard to come by.

children.text: iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya itthaṃ madhumathanārcanam indukīrtanena
children.translated_text: Whoever thus reads or hears this worship of <s>Madhumathana</s>, accompanied by praise of <s>Indu</s>,

children.text: matimapi ca dadāti so'pi śaurerbhavanagataḥ paripūjyate'maraughaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who also gives his mind to it, he too, having gone to the abode of <s>Śauri</s>, is honored by hosts of immortals.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The son of <s>Ravi</s> spoke to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who was present in the water-reservoir:
“In reservoirs, groves, wells, stepwells, lotus ponds,
and temples of the gods, O lord of the gods, I ask about the rule.

children.text: ke tatra cartvijo nātha vedī vā kīdṛśī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Who should be the officiants there, O lord, and what should the altar be like?
What is the sacrificial fee, the sacred enclosure, the time, the place, and the teacher?
What substances are recommended? Tell me everything according to the truth.”
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu rājan mahābāho taḍāgādiṣu yo vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: Listen, O king, mighty-armed one, to the rule for reservoirs and the like.
This ancient account is recited in the <s>Purāṇas</s> by those who speak the Veda.
When an auspicious bright fortnight has arrived, and after the northern course has passed,
on a meritorious day declared by Brahmins, after causing Brahmins to recite,
on ground sloping eastward or northward, near the reservoir,
one should make an auspicious altar four hastas in size, square and four-sided.
Likewise the pavilion should be sixteen hastas in size and have four entrances.
Around the altar there should be pits, a ratni in measure, with three enclosing bands.

children.text: nava saptātha vā pañca nātiriktā nṛpātmaja
children.translated_text: There may be nine, seven, or five, O son of a king, but not more.
The yoni should be a span in measure and six or seven aṅgulas wide.
The pits there should be seven, with enclosing bands raised to three joints.
They should all be of the proper color and furnished with banners and standards.
From branches of aśvattha, udumbara, plakṣa, and vaṭa trees
one should make these doorways in each direction of the pavilion.
There should be eight auspicious hotṛ priests there, and likewise eight door-keepers.

children.text: aṣṭau tu jāpakāḥ kāryā brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Eight reciters should be appointed, Brahmins who have crossed to the far shore of the Veda.
The domestic priest should be a best of Brahmins, complete in all marks, knowing mantras, with senses subdued,
and endowed with good family and conduct.
At each pit there should be a water-pot and sacrificial implements,
a fan and two white chowries, set in broad copper vessels.
Then there should be many-colored caru offerings for each deity.
The skillful teacher should place them on the ground after consecrating them with permission.
The sacrificial post should measure three ratnis and be made from a kṣāra tree,
or else it should match the sacrificer’s height; it is to be set up by one who desires prosperity.
Twenty-five officiating priests, adorned with gold, should be appointed.
And golden earrings, armlets, and bracelets,
and likewise rings, purifying rings, and various garments:
he should honor all of them equally, and the teacher again with twice as much.
He should give something furnished with bedding, and also whatever is dear to himself.
A golden tortoise and makara, and a silver fish and drum,
a copper crab and frog, and a dolphin of iron:
having procured all that in this way at the very beginning, O lord of the people,
wearing white garlands and garments, and anointed with white fragrant paste,
he should there be bathed by masters of the Veda with water containing all herbs.
The sacrificer, together with his wife and accompanied by sons and grandsons,
should approach the western door and enter the sacrificial pavilion.
Then, with auspicious sounds and with the resounding of drums,
the knower of reality should at once make a maṇḍala with five colors.
Then he should make a wheel with sixteen spokes, lotus-centered and four-faced,

children.text: caturasraṃ ca parito vṛttaṃ madhye suśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: square all around and beautifully circular in the middle.
Having made that upon the altar, the skilled man should then place all the planets and the guardians of the worlds
in the respective directions, according to mantra.
He should place the tortoise and the others in the middle, relying on the <s>Vāruṇa</s> mantra.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ ca śivaṃ viṣṇuṃ tatraiva sthāpayedbudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the wise man should install <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> right there.
After installing <s>Vināyaka</s>, and likewise <s>Kamalā</s> and <s>Ambikā</s>,
he should then place the host of beings for the pacification of all worlds.
Having thus performed the <s>adhivāsana</s> (preliminary consecration), furnished with flowers, foods, and fruits,
he should wrap those water-filled pots with cloths.
Having adorned the door-guardians on every side with flowers and fragrances,
the teacher should say to them, "Recite," and should worship them.
Two <s>Bahvṛcas</s> should be stationed in the east, and two knowers of the <s>Yajurveda</s> in the south;
similarly, two singers of the <s>Sāmaveda</s> in the west, and two <s>Atharvans</s> in the north.
The sacrificer should sit on the southern side, facing north.
He should say to the officiants, once again, "Sacrifice."
To the chosen reciters of mantras he should say, "Stand by with mantra-recitation."
Having instructed them all in this way, he, knowing the mantras, should sprinkle the fire.
He should offer ghee and likewise fuel-sticks with <s>Vāruṇa</s> mantras.
And then the oblation should be offered by the priests everywhere with <s>Vāruṇa</s> mantras alone.
Having offered according to rule to the planets, and likewise to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>,
to the <s>Maruts</s>, to the guardians of the worlds, and according to rule to <s>Viśvakarman</s>,

children.text: rātrisūktaṃ ca raudraṃ ca pāvamānaṃ sumaṅgalam
children.translated_text: the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> in the east should separately recite the Rātrī hymn, the Raudra hymn, the Pāvamāna hymn, the auspicious one,

children.text: japeyuḥ pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ pūrvato bahvṛcaḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and the Puruṣa hymn.

children.text: śākraṃ raudraṃ ca saumyaṃ ca kūṣmāṇḍaṃ jātavedasam
children.translated_text: The knowers of the <s>Yajurveda</s> on the southern side should recite the Śākra, Raudra, Saumya, Kūṣmāṇḍa, and Jātavedas hymns,
and the Saura hymn as a mantra.
the Vairājya and Puruṣa hymns, the Sauvarṇa, the Rudrasaṃhitā,
the Śaiśava, the Pañcanidhana, the Gāyatra, and the Jyeṣṭhasāman,
the Vāmadevya, the Bṛhatsāman, the Raurava together with the Rathantara,

children.text: gavāṃ vrataṃ ca kāṇvaṃ ca rakṣoghnaṃ vayasastathā
children.translated_text: the Gavāṃ Vrata, the Kāṇva, the Rakṣoghna, and also the Vayas.
The <s>Sāmaveda</s> singers, O king, should sing them while stationed at the western door.
And the <s>Atharvans</s> on the northern side should recite the rites for peace and prosperity,
mentally resorting to the god, the lord <s>Varuṇa</s>.
On the previous day, at night, having performed the <s>adhivāsana</s> in this way,
he should take earth from an elephant-stable, a horse-stable, a road, an anthill, a confluence, a lake, a cow pen,
and likewise from a crossroads, and put it into the pots.

children.text: rocanāṃ ca sasiddhārthāṃ gandhaṃ guggulameva ca
children.translated_text: And rocanā with white mustard, fragrant substance, and guggulu:
the bathing of it should be performed together with the five products of the cow.

children.text: pratyekaṃ tu mahāmantrair eva kṛtvā vidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: Each one should be done separately with the great mantras, according to rule.
Having passed the night in this way with the prescribed rite,

children.text: tataḥ prabhāte vimale saṃjāte'tha śataṃ gavām
children.translated_text: then, when the clear morning has arisen, one hundred cows
should be given to Brahmins, or again sixty-eight,
or fifty, or thirty-six, or even twenty-five.
Then, at an auspicious and beautiful moment declared by the astrologer,
with the sounds of Veda, with celestial musicians, and again with various instruments,
he should adorn a cow with gold and make her descend into the water.

children.text: sāmagāya ca sā deyā brāhmaṇāya viśāṃ pate ||
children.translated_text: And she should be given to a <s>Sāmaveda</s>-singing Brahmin, O lord of the people.
Taking up a golden vessel furnished with the five jewels,
and then placing in it the makara, fish, and the rest, all together,
held by four Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
with water from a great river and with curds and unhusked rice,
he should place the north-facing cow in the middle of the water.
When she has been bathed by an <s>Atharvan</s> with the mantra beginning "punar mām etu"

children.text: āpo hi ṣṭheti mantreṇa kṣiptvāgatya ca maṇḍapam ||
children.translated_text: and with the mantra "āpo hi ṣṭhā," he should cast it in and then come to the pavilion.
Having worshipped the pond there, he should give bali-offerings on every side.
Again, oblations should be offered for four days, O best of sages.
The fourth-day rite should be performed, and there too a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) should be given according to ability,
O tiger among kings; then the appeasement of <s>Varuṇa</s> should be performed.
Having then prepared the sacrificial vessels and the sacrificial implements,
and having given them equally to the priests, he should divide up the pavilion again.

children.text: hemapātrīṃ ca śayyāṃ ca sthāpakāya nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: And he should present the golden vessel and the bed to the installing priest.
Then one thousand Brahmins, or else eight hundred,
or fifty, or twenty, should be fed according to his ability.
Thus this procedure for a pond is taught in the Purāṇas.
In all wells and reservoirs, and likewise in lotus ponds,

children.text: eṣa eva vidhirdṛṣṭaḥ pratiṣṭhāsu tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: this very same rule is observed, and so too in consecrations.
But there is a distinction in the mantras for temples and for garden grounds and the like.
This procedure, however, was prescribed by <s>Svayambhū</s> with reduction for those who lack the means.
For small works, people should perform it as if for a single sacred fire, but without deceitful stinginess over wealth.
If water remains during the rainy season, its fruit is remembered as that of an <s>agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice.
If it remains during autumn, it gives the fruit that has just been stated.
If it remains in the cold season and in winter, it is equal to a <s>vājapeya</s> and an <s>atirātra</s>.
If it remains in spring, they declare it equal to an <s>aśvamedha</s>.
And water that remains even in summer surpasses a <s>rājasūya</s>.
O great king, whoever performs these special <s>dharmas</s> with a mind purified by scripture

children.text: sa yāti rudrālayamāśu pūtaḥ kalpānanekāndivi modate ca ||
children.translated_text: quickly goes, purified, to the abode of <s>Rudra</s>, and rejoices in heaven for many kalpas.
Having enjoyed many worlds, beginning with the greatest ones, for two parārdhas together with women,

children.text: sahaiva viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ yatprāpnoti tadyāgaphalena bhūyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he again obtains that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> through the fruit of that sacrifice.
The sages said:
O <s>Sūta</s>, tell us fully and correctly the rule for trees.
By what rule should the learned perform the consecration of trees?

children.text: ye ca lokāḥ smṛtāsteṣāṃ tānidānīṃ vadasva naḥ
children.translated_text: And tell us now the worlds that are remembered for them.
You should tell us all the fruit that a person obtains after death.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain the rule for trees, and likewise for garden grounds.
Everything should be arranged according to the rule for a pond, O lord of the world.
The officiating priests, the pavilion, the ritual materials, and the ācārya should be of that same kind.
One should worship the Brahmins in the same way, with gold, garments, and unguents.
Having sprinkled the trees with water containing all herbs and adorned them with cakes of ground paste,
one should decorate them with garlands and wrap them in cloths.
The ear-piercing of all of them should be done with a golden needle.
Collyrium should also be applied in the same way with a golden rod.

children.text: phalāni sapta cāṣṭau vā kāladhautāni kārayet
children.translated_text: One should have seven or eight fruits made of refined silver prepared.
For each of all the trees, one should place those fruits on the altar for the overnight rite.
Here guggulu is the best incense, set in copper vessels.
After setting them on the seven grains, with cloths, perfumes, and unguents,
one should place jars at all the trees, O lord of men.
Having furnished all of them with gold, one should make the bali offering.
According to each one's place, for the guardians of the quarters, especially <s>Indra</s> and the others,
and for <s>Vanaspati</s>, the learned twice-born priests should perform the oblation.
Then, from among the trees, one should release a milk-giving cow facing north, wearing white cloth,
adorned with gold ornaments, with a bronze milking vessel and two golden horns, exceedingly fine,
a cow rich in milk, from the middle of the trees.
Then, with the abhiṣeka mantra, with auspicious instrumental music and songs,
and with <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> mantras, and with <s>Varuṇa</s> mantras all around,
the foremost Brahmin should perform the bathing with those same jars.
After bathing, the yajamāna, wearing white garments, should likewise worship
all those officiating priests with cows according to his means, with concentrated mind.
He should honor them with golden cords, with bracelets, rings, and pavitra-rings,
with garments, bedding, utensils, and sandals.
He should give them food prepared with milk for four days.
The oblation should be made with mustard seeds, barley, and black sesame seeds.
Fuel-sticks of palāśa are commended, and on the fourth day there should be a festival.
There also the gift for the priests should again be given according to one's ability.
Whatever is most desired, whatever it may be, he should give that without jealousy.
He should give twice as much to the ācārya, bow down, and dismiss him.
The learned man who performs a tree-festival by this rule
obtains all desires and enjoys endless fruit.
And, O king of kings, the man who establishes even a single tree
dwells in heaven, O king, for the span of thirty thousand <s>Indras</s>.
He saves past and future human beings equal in number to the trees,
and obtains supreme accomplishment, from which return is difficult.
The person who hears this daily, or causes it to be heard,
is honored by the gods and exalted in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Likewise I shall teach another rite, one that grants the fruit of all desires,
called <s>Saubhāgyaśayana</s>, which the knowers of the Purāṇas know.
Long ago, when the worlds, <s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svar</s>, <s>Mahaḥ</s>, and the others, had been burned,
the good fortune of all beings then became gathered in one place.
Having reached the heavenly <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, it remained on the chest of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tataḥ kālena mahatā punaḥ sargavidhau nṛpa
children.translated_text: Then, after a long time, at the renewed process of creation, O king,
when the world was covered by ahaṃkāra and possessed of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>,
and when rivalry had begun between <s>Kamalāsana</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
there arose something in the form of a liṅga, terrifying with flames of fire.
From the chest of <s>Hari</s>, scorched all around by it, that good fortune issued forth.
That good fortune, which had rested on the chest of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
then assumed the form of liquid until it reached the surface of the earth.
Raised up into the midair, it was drunk at once by the wise <s>Dakṣa</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
It produced beauty of form and loveliness.
Great strength and splendor arose in <s>Dakṣa</s>, the supreme lord.
What remained and fell upon the earth came into being in eight forms.
From it there arose for people seven bestowers of good fortune:
sugarcanes, the lords of sap, niṣpāva beans, cumin, and coriander.
And cow's milk with its derivative, safflower, and likewise saffron,
and salt as the eighth: that, my child, is called the <s>Saubhāgyāṣṭaka</s>.
Because that was drunk by the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, who again knew yogic knowledge,
she became his daughter, the one who is called <s>Satī</s>.
Because through her loveliness she surpassed the worlds, she is therefore called <s>Lalitā</s>.
The bearer of the bow <s>Pināka</s> married this most beautiful woman of the three worlds.
That goddess, consisting of good fortune, grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: tāmārādhya pumānbhaktyā nārī vā kiṃ na vindati ||
children.translated_text: When a man, or a woman, worships her with devotion, what does that person not obtain?
<s>Manu</s> said:
How is that nurse of the world to be worshipped, O <s>Janārdana</s>?

children.text: tadvidhānaṃ jagannātha tatsarvaṃ ca vadasva me ||
children.translated_text: O lord of the world, tell me that procedure, all of it.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
When the spring month has arrived, on the third lunar day, O beloved of the people,
in the forenoon of the bright fortnight, one should perform a bath with sesame seeds.

children.text: tasminnahani sā devī kila viśvātmanā satī
children.translated_text: For on that day, they say, that goddess <s>Satī</s>, the fair-limbed one,
was married by the universal Self with the mantras of taking the hand in marriage.
Then on the third lunar day one should worship the lord of gods together with her,
with fruits of many kinds, incense, lamps, and food offerings.
Having bathed the image with the five products of the cow and also with scented water,
one should worship <s>Gaurī</s> together with the moon-crested lord.

children.text: namo'stu pāṭalāyai tu pādau devyāḥ śivasya tu
children.translated_text: Saying, "Homage to <s>Pāṭalā</s>," one should worship the goddess's feet, and likewise <s>Śiva</s>'s,

children.text: śivāyeti ca saṃkīrya jayāyai gulphayor dvayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, uttering "to <s>Śiva</s>," one should worship the two ankles with "to <s>Jayā</s>."
With "to the three-formed one" for <s>Rudra</s>, and with "to <s>Bhavānī</s>," one should worship the pair of shanks.
Saying "to <s>Śivā</s>, to <s>Rudreśvarā</s>, and to <s>Vijayā</s>," one should worship the knees,
and, naming <s>Harikeśa</s>, one should worship the thighs; "Homage to the boon-giving one."

children.text: īśāyai ca kīṭaṃ devyāḥ śaṃkarāyeti śaṃkaram
children.translated_text: With "to <s>Īśā</s>" one should worship the goddess's waist, and with "to <s>Śaṃkara</s>" <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
and both flanks with "to <s>Koṭavī</s>," and with "to the trident-bearing <s>Śūlapāṇi</s>."
Saying, "Homage to you, <s>Maṅgalā</s>," one should reverently worship the belly,
and, with "homage to the all-souled one," <s>Rudra</s>; and with "to <s>Īśānī</s>," the two breasts.
Likewise one should worship <s>Śiva</s> with "to the essence of the Vedas," and the throat with "to <s>Rudrāṇī</s>."
With "to the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>" one should worship the lord of all, and with "to <s>Anantā</s>," the two hands.
With "to the three-eyed one" one should worship <s>Hara</s>, the arms, saying "O beloved of the fire of Time."
Saying "to the abode of good fortune," one should always worship the ornaments.
With "to <s>Svāhā</s> and <s>Svadhā</s>" one should worship the face, and with "to <s>Īśvara</s>," the trident-bearer.
With "to the one who dwells in aśoka and honey," the two lips, which grant prosperity, are to be worshipped.
Likewise with "to <s>Sthāṇu</s>" one should worship <s>Hara</s>, and the smile with "O moon-faced beloved."
With "homage to the destroyer who is lord of the half-woman form," one should worship the nose, saying "O dark-limbed one."
With "homage to the fierce one" one should worship the lord of the world, and then the brows with "to <s>Lalitā</s>."
With "to <s>Śarva</s>" one should worship the destroyer of cities, and likewise the curls with "to <s>Vāsavī</s>."
Saying "homage to the lady of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>," one should then worship the hair of <s>Śiva</s>.
With "to the one whose form is both terrible and fierce," one should worship the head; "homage to the all-souled one."
Having worshipped <s>Śiva</s> according to rule, one should place the <s>Saubhāgyāṣṭaka</s> in front:
ghee, niṣpāva beans, safflower, milk, and cumin,
also rasarāja, salt, and coriander: these are the eight.
Because good fortune is given from this, it is therefore called the <s>Saubhāgyāṣṭaka</s>.
Having thus offered all that in front of <s>Śiva</s> and his consort,
at night one should sip water from a horn and then sleep on the ground, O subduer of enemies.

children.text: punaḥ prabhāte tu tathā kṛtasnānajapaḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Again at dawn, having bathed, recited, and become pure,
one should honor a Brahmin couple with garments, garlands, and ornaments.
Together with the <s>Saubhāgyāṣṭaka</s>, one should offer a pair of golden feet
to a Brahmin, saying, "May <s>Lalitā</s> be pleased here."
In this way, for a whole year, always on the third lunar day, with one's mind intent,
it should be performed according to rule and with devotion by those who desire every kind of good fortune.

children.text: prāśane dānamantre ca viśeṣo'yaṃ nibodha me
children.translated_text: Now learn from me this distinction in the sipping, the gift, and the mantra:
in the month of <s>Caitra</s>, water from a horn; in <s>Vaiśākha</s>, cow dung again;
in <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, a mandāra flower; in <s>Śuci</s>, a bilva leaf is prescribed;

children.text: śrāvaṇe dadhi saṃprāśyaṃ nabhasye ca kuśodakam ||
children.translated_text: in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, curds should be sipped, and in <s>Nabhasya</s>, water with <s>kuśa</s> grass;
milk in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>; in <s>Kārttika</s>, spotted ghee;

children.text: mārge māse tu gomūtraṃ pauṣe saṃprāśayedghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: in the month of <s>Mārga</s>, cow urine; in <s>Pauṣa</s>, one should sip ghee;
in <s>Māgha</s>, black sesame seeds likewise, and in <s>Phālguna</s>, the five products of the cow.

children.text: lalitā vijayā bhadrā bhavānī kumudā śivā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Bhavānī</s>, <s>Kumudā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>,

children.text: vāsudevī tathā gaurī maṅgalā kamalā satī
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Vāsudevī</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Maṅgalā</s>, <s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Satī</s>,

children.text: umā ca dānakāle tu prīyatāmiti kīrtayet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Umā</s>: at the time of giving, one should recite each name with "may she be pleased."
Jasmine, aśoka, lotus, kadamba, blue lotus, and mālatī,
kubjaka, oleander, bāṇa, unfading saffron-flower,

children.text: sindhuvāraṃ ca sarveṣu māseṣu kramaśaḥ smṛtam
children.translated_text: and sindhuvāra are prescribed in order for all the months.
Hibiscus, safflower blossom, mālatī, and hundred-petaled lotus,
whatever is obtained, are praised; and oleander is always suitable.
Thus, for a whole year, after fasting according to rule, a man,

children.text: strī bhaktā vā kumārī vā śivamabhyarcya bhaktitaḥ
children.translated_text: or a devoted woman or maiden, should worship <s>Śiva</s> with devotion.
At the end of the vow one should give a bed furnished with all its accessories.

children.text: umāmaheśvaraṃ haimaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ ca gavā saha
children.translated_text: Having placed golden <s>Umā</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>, and a bull together with a cow,
upon the bed, one should then offer it to a Brahmin.
According to one's ability, one should also honor other couples with garments and the like,
with grain, ornaments, gifts of cows, and stores of wealth.
Free from deceit about his wealth, he should worship without arrogance.
Whoever properly performs this <s>Saubhāgyaśayana</s> vow in this way
obtains all desires and reaches the supreme state.
By renouncing the fruit of even a single thing, one should undertake this vow.
O king, whoever, while desiring it, obtains fame month by month...
With good fortune, health, beauty, long life, garments, ornaments, and adornments,
O king, he would not be separated from them for three hundred and nine arbudas of years.
But whoever for twelve years performs the vow of <s>Saubhāgyaśayana</s>,
or for seven or eight years, dwells in the abode of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, honored by the immortals,
properly, for three times ten thousand kalpas.

children.text: nārī vā kurute vāpi kumārī vā nareśvara
children.translated_text: Whether a woman performs it, or even a maiden, O lord of men,
she too obtains that fruit, cherished by the grace of the goddess.
And whoever even listens to this and then turns his mind toward it,

children.text: so'pi vidyādharo bhūtvā svargaloke ciraṃ vaset ||
children.translated_text: he too, becoming a <s>Vidyādhara</s>, dwells for a long time in heaven.

children.text: idamiha madanena pūrvamiṣṭaṃ śatadhanuṣā kṛtavīryasūnunā ca
children.translated_text: In former times this was sought here by <s>Madana</s>, by <s>Śatadhanus</s>, and by the son of <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>,

children.text: kṛtamatha varuṇena nandinā vā kim u jananātha tato yadudbhavaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: and then it was performed by <s>Varuṇa</s> or by <s>Nandin</s>; what need be said, O lord of men, of what result may arise from it?
<s>Nārada</s> said:
<s>Bhūrloka</s>, then <s>Bhuvarloka</s>, <s>Svarloka</s>, then <s>Maharloka</s> and <s>Janaloka</s>,

children.text: tapaḥ satyaṃ ca saptaite devalokāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tapoloka</s> and <s>Satyaloka</s>: these seven are declared to be the worlds of the gods.
How may sovereignty over all of them, one after another, come about?

children.text: iha loke śubhaṃ rūpamāyuḥ saubhāgyameva ca
children.translated_text: And in this world, how may auspicious beauty, long life, and good fortune,
as well as abundant prosperity, arise, O lord, O destroyer of <s>Pura</s>?
<s>Maheśvara</s> said:
Long ago <s>Hutāśana</s>, together with <s>Māruta</s>, was on earth
commanded by <s>Puruhūta</s> to destroy the enemies of the gods.
Then, when thousands of <s>Dānavas</s> had been burned by him,
<s>Tāraka</s>, <s>Kamalākṣa</s>, <s>Kāladaṃṣṭra</s>, <s>Parāvasu</s>,
and <s>Virocana</s> fled from the battle, O treasure of asceticism.
Entering the waters of the ocean, they made their dwelling there;
and, being impossible to reach, they were disregarded by <s>Agni</s> and <s>Māruta</s>.
From then on they oppressed the gods, human beings, and all moving creatures,
and all the sages too, and then they entered the water again.

children.text: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi vīrāḥ pañca ca sapta ca
children.translated_text: Thus for twelve thousand years those five heroes,
by the strength of their water-fortress, O brahman, afflicted the three worlds.
Thereafter, after a long time, the lord of the immortals commanded <s>Vahni</s> and <s>Māruta</s>:
"This ocean is to be dried up."
"Since this abode of <s>Varuṇa</s> is the refuge of our enemies,
therefore today it must be brought to destruction by you two."
Then the two of them said to <s>Śakra</s>, the destroyer of <s>Śambara</s>,
"O lord of the gods, this destruction of the ocean is unrighteousness.
For there would be the destruction of a vast multitude of living beings.
Therefore, O <s>Puraṃdara</s>, we two will not commit sin today.
Even within a single yojana of it, hundreds of crores of living beings
dwell, O best of the gods; how can it deserve destruction?"
Thus addressed, the lord of the gods, his eyes reddened with anger,
spoke these words in wrath, as if burning <s>Pāvaka</s> himself:
"The immortals never incur any connection with righteousness or unrighteousness,
and you two in particular stand in greatness.
Since my command has been transgressed by you together with <s>Māruta</s>,
