and since, O <s>Vibhāvasu</s>, you have acted after taking up considerations such as injury to a sage's vow,
toward an enemy, though the matter was beneficial according to the teachings of dharma and artha,
therefore, in one body, in the form of a sage, among human beings,

children.text: mārutena samaṃ loke tava janma bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: you will have birth in the world together with <s>Māruta</s>.
And when, even in human birth, the ocean will have been dried up by you as <s>Agastya</s>,
then, O <s>Vahni</s>, you will obtain divinity."
Fallen by <s>Indra</s>'s curse, at that very moment those two on earth
obtained birth in a single body from a jar, O treasure of asceticism.
From the seed of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, he became the younger brother of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>;
and the sage, fierce in asceticism, was born again under the name <s>Agastya</s>.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
How, having come into being, did that sage become the brother of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>?

children.text: kathaṃ ca mitrāvaruṇau pitarāvasya tau smṛtau
children.translated_text: And how are those two, <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, remembered as his fathers?
How could <s>Agastya</s>'s birth be from a jar, O destroyer of <s>Pura</s>?
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Long ago, once on <s>Gandhamādana</s>, the ancient Person,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, having become the son of <s>Dharma</s>, practiced great asceticism.
Frightened by his asceticism, <s>Śakra</s> sent those two for the sake of obstructing it,
<s>Mādhava</s> and <s>Anaṅga</s>, together with a host of apsarases.
When <s>Hari</s> was not disturbed toward sense-objects by song and music,
nor by cosmetics and the like, nor by <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>,
then the company of women belonging to <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Madhu</s> fell into dejection.
Then, to agitate them, the elder brother of <s>Nara</s>
created from the region of his own thigh a woman who bewitched the people of the three worlds.
The gods were stirred by her; and then those two best gods,
while the apsarases looked on, were addressed by <s>Hari</s> before the gods.
"The apsarases are common to the gods," <s>Hari</s> said to the gods,

children.text: urvaśīti ca nāmneyaṃ loke khyātiṃ gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "and this one, by the name <s>Urvaśī</s>, will become famous in the world."
Then <s>Mitra</s>, desiring her, summoned that <s>Urvaśī</s>

children.text: uktā māṃ ramayasveti bāḍham ityabravīttu sā ||
children.translated_text: and said, "Delight me." She replied, "Very well."
As the lotus-eyed woman was going a little way through the sky,
she was afterward seized by <s>Varuṇa</s>, but she did not take pleasure in <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: mitreṇāhaṃ vṛtā pūrvamadya bhāryā na te vibho
children.translated_text: "I was chosen first by <s>Mitra</s>; today I am not your wife, O lord."
<s>Varuṇa</s> said, "Set your mind on me, and then go."
When she had gone after saying, "Very well," <s>Mitra</s> then gave a curse
to her: "Go to the human world and resort to the son of the son of <s>Soma</s>,

children.text: bhajasveti yato veśyādharma eṣa tvayā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: because this conduct of a courtesan has been practiced by you."

children.text: jalakumbhe tato vīryaṃ mitreṇa varuṇena ca
children.translated_text: Then semen was placed in a water jar by <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.
Then, when it had been cast in, two excellent sages alone were born.
In ancient times a king named <s>Nimi</s> was playing at dice together with women.
In the meantime <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, born from <s>Brahmā</s>, arrived there.
Seeing the king not performing worship for him, that sage cursed him:
"Become bodiless." Then that sage too was cursed by him.
Because of their mutual curse, the minds of the two seemed to have departed.
They went to <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the world, for the destruction of the curse.
Then, by <s>Brahmā</s>'s command, <s>Nimi</s> settled in the eyes.
The blinking of people came to be for their rest, O <s>Nārada</s>.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> too came into that water-jar, as before.
Then, white, four-armed, with rosary and water-pot,
there arose the excellent sage <s>Agastya</s>, tranquil in spirit.
In one region of <s>Malaya</s>, according to the rule of the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>,
he, together with his wife and surrounded by Brahmins, performed very difficult austerity.
Then, after a long time, seeing the world greatly oppressed by <s>Tāraka</s>,
he angrily drank up the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>, the ocean.
Thereupon all the boon-givers, beginning with <s>Śaṃkara</s>, came to him.
<s>Brahmā</s> and the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> went to grant a boon.

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te yadabhīṣṭaṃ ca vai mune ||
children.translated_text: "Choose a boon, O sage; welfare to you. Choose whatever you desire."
<s>Agastya</s> said:
"For twenty-five crores of thousands of <s>Brahmā</s>s,
may I be one who has a celestial car on the path of the southern mountain.
Whoever performs worship for me at the rising of my celestial car
shall in turn become lord of the seven worlds."
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Saying to him, "So be it," the gods went back as they had come.
Therefore the wise should always give arghya (honor-offering) to <s>Agastya</s>.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: kathamarghapradānaṃ tu kartavyaṃ tasya vai vibho
children.translated_text: How, O lord, should the arghya-gift be made for him?
Tell me the procedure for worshipping <s>Agastya</s>.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
At early dawn, on the night of his rising, a learned householder should perform
bathing with white sesame seeds, and likewise should wear white garlands and garments.
He should set up an unblemished jar, adorned with garlands and cloths,
furnished with five jewels and accompanied by a vessel of ghee,
provided with various foods and fruits, and accompanied by a copper vessel.
He should place at the mouth of the jar a golden man the size of a thumb, with very long arm-staffs,
four-faced, together with seven grains and garments.
Together with a bronze vessel, unbroken rice, and a shell, he should give it with the mantra to the best of twice-born men,
lifting up the pot-bellied, long-armed figure, with undivided mind and facing the direction of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: śvetāṃ ca dadyādyadi śaktirasti raupyaiḥ khurair hemamukhīṃ savatsām
children.translated_text: If he has the means, he should also give a white milch cow, with silver hoofs, golden-faced, with her calf,

children.text: dhenuṃ naraḥ kṣīravatīṃ praṇamya savatsaghaṇṭābharaṇāṃ dvijāya ||
children.translated_text: after bowing, to a Brahmin: a milk-giving cow with her calf, bell, and ornaments.
A man should give all this for up to seven nights from his rising.

children.text: yāvatsamāḥ sapta daśāthavā syurathordhvamapyatra vadanti kecit ||
children.translated_text: This should be done for seven years, or ten; some say even longer in this matter.
"O one resembling a kāśa flower, born from fire and wind,
son of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, jar-born one, homage to you.
O reducer of <s>Vindhya</s>'s growth, remover of the poison in cloud-water,
lover of jewels, lord of gods, resident of <s>Laṅkā</s>, homage to you.

children.text: vātāpī bhakṣito yena samudraḥ śoṣitaḥ purā
children.translated_text: He by whom <s>Vātāpī</s> was eaten and the ocean was dried up in ancient times,
that glorious husband of <s>Lopāmudrā</s>: to him homage, homage.
O princess, greatly fortunate one, wife of the seer, fair-faced one,
<s>Lopāmudrā</s>, homage to you; may my arghya be accepted.
Doing this every year at the proper time, with renunciation of the fruit, he does not sink.
After performing the homa (fire-offering), a person should thereafter give up the fruit.
The man who presents arghya by this procedure
obtains this world, endowed with beauty and health.
By the second he obtains the <s>Bhuvarloka</s>, and then after that the world of heaven.
He who offers seven arghyas obtains the worlds.
And he who does it for the length of his life reaches the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: iha paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya etad yugalamuniprabhavārghyasampradānam
children.translated_text: Whoever reads or hears this presentation of arghya arising from the pair of sages,

children.text: matimapi ca dadāti so'pi viṣṇorbhavanagataḥ paripūjyate'maraughaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whoever even gives his assent to it, is honored by hosts of immortals after going to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s abode.
<s>Manu</s> said:
O god, tell me that which gives the fruit of good fortune and health and causes imperishable reward in the next world,
which grants enjoyment and liberation, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
I will now declare what the god, the destroyer of <s>Pura</s>, formerly said to <s>Umā</s>,
when, seated on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, he was questioned by the goddess.
When they had begun pleasant and righteous stories,
I will now tell that which grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Listen attentively, O goddess, to the unsurpassed worship
for men and for women, which produces endless merit.
In the month of <s>Nabhasya</s>, or in <s>Vaiśākha</s>, and in the holy month of <s>Mārgaśiras</s>,
on the third day of the bright fortnight, having bathed well with white mustard seeds,
one should place on the forehead a tilaka made of gorocanā, cow urine, warm cow dung,
and curds mixed with sandalwood paste.
Because it grants good fortune and health and is always dear to <s>Lalitā</s>.
On the third lunar days of each fortnight, a man should wear yellow garments.
If she is a restrained woman, she should then wear red garments.
A widow should wear garments dyed with red mineral pigment, and a maiden should wear white garments.

children.text: devīṃ tu pañcagavyena tataḥ kṣīreṇa kevalam
children.translated_text: But one should bathe the goddess with <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow), then with milk alone,
likewise with honey, and with water scented by flowers.
One should worship her with white flowers and also with fruits of many kinds,
with coriander, cumin, salt, jaggery, milk, and ghee.
One should always worship the goddess's image with white unbroken rice and sesame,
and every fortnight, O lovely-faced one, perform worship beginning with the feet.

children.text: varadāyai namaḥ pādau tathā gulphau namaḥ śriyai
children.translated_text: With 'homage to <s>Varadā</s>' one should worship the feet, and likewise the ankles with 'homage to <s>Śrī</s>.'

children.text: aśokāyai namo jaṅghe pārvatyai jānunī tathā ||
children.translated_text: With 'homage to <s>Aśokā</s>' the shanks, and likewise the knees with 'homage to <s>Pārvatī</s>.'
The thighs are for <s>Maṅgalakāriṇī</s>, and the waist likewise for <s>Vāmadevī</s>.
The belly is for <s>Padmodarā</s>; 'homage to <s>Kāmaśrī</s>' for the breast.
The hands are for <s>Saubhāgyadāyinī</s>, and the arms for <s>Haramukhaśrī</s>.
The face is for <s>Darpaṇavāsinī</s>; 'homage to <s>Smaradā</s>' for the smile.
Homage to <s>Gaurī</s> for the nose, and to <s>Utpalā</s> for the eyes.
The forehead is for <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, the curls for <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, and the head likewise.

children.text: namo gauryai namo dhiṣṇyai namaḥ kāntyai namaḥ śriyai
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Gaurī</s>, homage to <s>Dhiṣṇyā</s>, homage to <s>Kānti</s>, homage to <s>Śrī</s>;

children.text: rambhāyai lalitāyai ca vāsudevyai namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Rambhā</s>, to <s>Lalitā</s>, and to <s>Vāsudevī</s>, homage, homage.
Having thus worshipped according to rule, one should draw a lotus in front,
with twelve petals and a pericarp, using saffron.
In the east one should place <s>Gaurī</s>, and then <s>Aparṇā</s> next.

children.text: bhavānīṃ dakṣiṇe tadvadrudrāṇīṃ ca tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: In the south one should likewise place <s>Bhavānī</s>, and then <s>Rudrāṇī</s> next.
In the west one should place gentle <s>Saumyā</s>, always dwelling in love,
and in the northwest <s>Pāṭalā</s> and fierce <s>Ugrā</s>, and then <s>Umā</s> further within.

children.text: madhye yathāsvaṃ māṃsāṅgāṃ maṅgalāṃ kumudāṃ satīm
children.translated_text: In the middle, each in her proper place, one should place <s>Māṃsāṅgā</s>, <s>Maṅgalā</s>, <s>Kumudā</s>, and <s>Satī</s>.

children.text: rudraṃ ca madhye saṃsthāpya lalitāṃ karṇikopari
children.translated_text: Having also established <s>Rudra</s> in the middle, one should set <s>Lalitā</s> upon the pericarp.
One should place them with flowers, unbroken rice, water, and reverence.
Having had auspicious songs and sounds performed, one should honor married women,
worshipping them with red garments, red garlands, and red unguents,

children.text: sindūraṃ snānacūrṇaṃ ca tāsāṃ śirasi pātayet ||
children.translated_text: and should place vermilion and bathing powder upon their heads.
For a bathing with vermilion and saffron is especially dear.
Likewise one should carefully worship the guru, the teacher of the rite;
where the guru is not worshipped, all rites there are fruitless.
In <s>Nabhasya</s> one should always worship <s>Gaurī</s> with dark blue lotuses,
in <s>Āśvayuja</s> with bandhujīva flowers, and in <s>Kārttika</s> with hundred-petaled lotuses.
In <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> with jasmine flowers, and in <s>Pauṣa</s> with yellow kuraṇṭakas;
in <s>Māgha</s> one should worship the goddess with kunda and saffron flowers,
and in <s>Phālguna</s> one should worship <s>Umā</s> with sinduvāra or jasmine.
In <s>Caitra</s> with mallikā and aśoka flowers, in <s>Vaiśākha</s> with fragrant pāṭala blossoms,
in <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> with lotuses and mandāras, and in <s>Āṣāḍha</s> with fresh water-lotuses;
then in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> one should always worship with kadambas and mālatī.

children.text: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam
children.translated_text: Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curds, ghee, and water with <s>kuśa</s> grass,
a bilva leaf, an arka flower, barley, and water from a cow's horn,
<s>pañcagavya</s>, and bilva too: one should consume these then in sequence.
This sipping rite, beginning with <s>Bhādrapada</s>, has thus been declared.
Every fortnight, on the third lunar day, O lovely-faced one,
having worshipped a couple, one should honor them with devotion, with garments, garlands, and unguents.
For the man one should give yellow garments, and for the woman safflower-colored garments.
One should give her niṣpāva beans, cumin, salt, sugarcane stalk, and jaggery,
and give her fruit and a flower together with a golden lotus.

children.text: yathā na devi deveśastvāṃ parityajya gacchati
children.translated_text: 'Just as, O goddess, the lord of gods does not leave you and go away,
so rescue me from the entire ocean of the sorrows of worldly existence.'

children.text: kumudā vimalānantā bhavānī ca sudhā śivā
children.translated_text: <s>Kumudā</s>, <s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Anantā</s>, <s>Bhavānī</s>, <s>Sudhā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>,

children.text: lalitā kamalā gaurī satī rambhātha pārvatī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Satī</s>, <s>Rambhā</s>, and then <s>Pārvatī</s>:
in the months beginning with <s>Nabhasya</s>, one should recite, 'May she be pleased.'
At the end of the vow one should give a bed furnished with a golden lotus.

children.text: mithunāni caturviṃśad daśa dvo ca samarcayet
children.translated_text: One should worship twenty-four couples, or ten, or two,
or else eight or six; again, one may worship them month by month.
Having first made the gift to the guru, the wise person should worship the others too.
This <s>Anantatṛtīyā</s> has been taught; it always grants endless fruit.
O goddess, it removes all sins and increases good fortune and health.
One should never transgress it through deceit about one's wealth.

children.text: naro vā yadi vā nārī vittaśāṭhyāt patatyadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether a man or a woman, one falls downward through deceit about wealth.

children.text: garbhiṇī sūtikā naktaṃ kumārī vātha rogiṇī
children.translated_text: A pregnant woman, a woman recently delivered, one observing the night restriction, a maiden, or a sick woman,
if impure, should have another perform it, while she herself remains intent.
Whoever performs this third-day vow, which gives endless fruit,
is honored in <s>Śivaloka</s> for a hundred crores of <s>kalpas</s> and more.
Even one without wealth who performs it for three years with fasts,
using the rite of flowers and mantras, obtains that same fruit.

children.text: nārī vā kurute yā tu kumārī vidhavāthavā
children.translated_text: A woman who performs it, whether a maiden or a widow,
also obtains that fruit, cherished by the favor of <s>Gaurī</s>.

children.text: iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya itthaṃ giritanayāvratam indravāsasaṃsthaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever reads or hears in this way the vow of the mountain's daughter, and dwells in the abode of <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: matimapi ca dadāti so'pi devairamaravadhūjanakiṃnaraiśca pūjyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or even gives his mind to it, is worshipful to the gods, heavenly women, and kinnaras.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Now I shall also declare another third-day vow, a destroyer of sin.
Those who know the ancient ritual tradition know this one as <s>Rasakalyāṇinī</s>.
When the month of <s>Māgha</s> has arrived, on the third lunar day of the bright fortnight,
in the morning one should perform a bath with cow's milk and sesame seeds.
One should bathe the goddess with honey and likewise with sugarcane juice,
and again with scented water; then one should anoint her with saffron.
Having worshipped the limbs on the right side, then one should worship those on the left.

children.text: lalitāyai namo devyāḥ pādau gulphau tato 'rcayet
children.translated_text: With "homage to <s>Lalitā</s>," one should worship the goddess's feet and then her ankles.

children.text: jaṅghāṃ jānuṃ tathā śāntyai tathaivoruṃ śriyai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should worship the shank and knee with "to <s>Śānti</s>," and likewise the thigh with "homage to <s>Śrī</s>."
The waist is to be worshipped with "to <s>Madalasā</s>," and likewise the belly with "to <s>Amalā</s>."
The breasts are to be worshipped with "to <s>Madanavāsinī</s>," and the throat with "to <s>Kumudā</s>."
The arm and the hand are to be worshipped with "to <s>Mādhavī</s>," and the smiling face with "to <s>Kamalā</s>."
The brows and forehead are to be worshipped with "to <s>Rudrāṇī</s>," and the locks likewise with "to <s>Śaṃkarā</s>."
One should worship the crown with "to <s>Viśvavāsinī</s>," and the head with "to <s>Kānti</s>."
The forehead is to be worshipped with "to <s>Madanā</s>," and again the eyebrows with "to <s>Mohanā</s>."

children.text: netre candrārdhadhāriṇyai tuṣṭyai ca vadanaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: The eyes are to be worshipped with "to <s>Candrārdhadhāriṇī</s>," and the face again with "to <s>Tuṣṭi</s>."
Homage to <s>Utkaṇṭhinī</s> for the throat; homage to <s>Amṛtā</s> for the breasts.

children.text: rambhāyai vāmakukṣiṃ ca viśokāyai namaḥ kaṭim
children.translated_text: The left flank is to be worshipped with "to <s>Rambhā</s>," and the waist with "homage to <s>Viśokā</s>."
The heart is to be worshipped with "to <s>Manmathādhiṣṇī</s>," and likewise the belly with "to <s>Pāṭalā</s>."
The waist is to be worshipped with "to <s>Suratavāsinī</s>," and likewise the thighs with "to <s>Campakapriyā</s>."

children.text: jānujaṅghe namo gauryai gāyatryai ghuṭike namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Gaurī</s> for the knees and shanks; homage to <s>Gāyatrī</s> for the ankles.

children.text: dharādharāyai pādau tu viśvakāyai namaḥ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: The feet are to be worshipped with "to <s>Dharādharā</s>," and the head with "homage to <s>Viśvakā</s>."
Homage to <s>Bhavānī</s>, to <s>Kāminī</s>, to <s>Kāmadevī</s>, O beloved of the world.
Homage, homage to <s>Ānandā</s>, to <s>Sunandā</s>, and to <s>Subhadrā</s>.
Having worshipped in this way according to rule, one should worship a Brahmin couple.
Free from jealousy, one should feed them with sweet food and drink.
One should give a water-filled pot and a pair of white garments,
and, after giving a golden lotus, should honor them with perfumes and garlands.
"May <s>Kumudā</s> be pleased here; may she accept the <s>Lavaṇavrata</s> (salt vow)."

children.text: anena vidhinā devī māsi māsi sadārcayet ||
children.translated_text: By this procedure one should always worship the goddess month after month.

children.text: lavaṇaṃ varjayenmāghe phālgune ca guḍaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Māgha</s> one should avoid salt, and in <s>Phālguna</s> jaggery again.

children.text: tailaṃ rājiṃ tathā caitre varjyaṃ ca madhu mādhave ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Caitra</s> oil and mustard are to be avoided, and in <s>Mādhava</s> honey.

children.text: pānakaṃ jyeṣṭhamāse tu āṣāḍhe cātha jīrakam
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, sweet drink is to be avoided, and then in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, cumin.
In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> one should avoid milk, and likewise curds in <s>Bhādrapada</s>.
Ghee is to be avoided in <s>Āśvayuja</s>, and similarly bee-honey in <s>Ūrja</s>.

children.text: dhānyakaṃ mārgaśīrṣe tu pauṣe varjyā ca śarkarā ||
children.translated_text: Coriander is to be avoided in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, and sugar in <s>Pauṣa</s>.

children.text: vratānte karakaṃ pūrṇameteṣāṃ māsi māsi ca
children.translated_text: At the end of the vow, month after month, one should give a full <s>karaka</s> vessel of these substances,
at the time of the two daily observances, together with a full bowl.
White laḍḍuka sweets, saṃyāva, and then pūrikās,
ghārikās, apūpas, flour-cakes, and maṇḍakas,
milk, vegetables, curd-rice, iṇḍarīs, and aśoka-vartikās,
these, beginning with <s>Māgha</s> in order, one should give upon the <s>karaka</s> vessel.

children.text: kumudā mādhavī gaurī rambhā bhadrā jayā śivā
children.translated_text: <s>Kumudā</s>, <s>Mādhavī</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Rambhā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>,
<s>Umā</s>, <s>Rati</s>, <s>Satī</s>, likewise <s>Maṅgalā</s> and <s>Ratilālasā</s>:
beginning with <s>Māgha</s>, everywhere in order one should recite, "May she be pleased."
In every case, sipping <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow) is prescribed.
One should always be fasting; if unable, eating at night is allowed.
When <s>Māgha</s> comes again, one should place sugar on top of the <s>karaka</s> vessel,
and, having made a golden <s>Gaurī</s> furnished with five jewels,
golden, thumb-sized, with rosary and water-pot,
four-armed, marked with the moon, and wrapped in white cloth,
and likewise a white pair of cattle with golden faces and white garments,
one should give them, together with cloth and vessel, saying, "May <s>Bhavānī</s> be pleased."
Whoever performs the <s>Rasakalyāṇinīvrata</s> (vow of auspicious enjoyment) by this procedure
is freed from all sins at that very moment.

children.text: navārbudasahasraṃ tu na duḥkhī jāyate naraḥ
children.translated_text: For nine thousand arbudas he is not born as a suffering man.
A man who gives a golden lotus, O <s>Gaurī</s>, month after month
obtains the fruit that belongs to a thousand <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifices.

children.text: nārī vā kurute yā tu kumārī vā varānane
children.translated_text: And the woman who performs it, or a maiden, O fair-faced one,

children.text: vidhavā yā tathā nārī sāpi tatphalamāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: or a widow, that woman too obtains that fruit.
Endowed with good fortune and health, she is honored in the world of <s>Gaurī</s>.

children.text: iti paṭhati śṛṇoti śrāvayedyaḥ prasaṅgātkalikaluṣavimuktaḥ pārvatīlokameti
children.translated_text: Whoever reads this, hears it, or has it recited on an occasion goes to the world of <s>Pārvatī</s>, freed from the stain of the Kali age.

children.text: matimapi ca narāṇāṃ yo dadāti priyārthaṃ vibudhapativimāne nāyakaḥ syādamoghaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And whoever gives this instruction to people for the sake of something dear becomes an unfailing leader in the aerial car of the lord of the gods.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Likewise I shall teach another third-day observance that destroys sin,
this one known in the world by the name <s>Ārdrānandakarī</s>.
Whenever, on the bright third lunar day, the <s>Āṣāḍha</s> asterism occurs,

children.text: brahmarkṣaṃ vā mṛgarkṣaṃ vā hasto mūlamathāpi vā
children.translated_text: or the <s>Brahma</s> asterism, the <s>Mṛga</s> asterism, <s>Hasta</s>, or also <s>Mūla</s>,
then one should properly perform a bath with <s>darbha</s> grass, perfumes, and water.
Wearing white garlands and garments, and anointed with white perfume,
one should worship <s>Bhavānī</s> with devotion, using fragrant white flowers,
as she sits with <s>Mahādeva</s> upon a great seat.

children.text: vāsudevyai namaḥ pādau śaṃkarāya namo haram
children.translated_text: With "homage to <s>Vāsudevī</s>" one should worship her feet, and <s>Hara</s> with "homage to <s>Śaṃkara</s>."
Her shanks are to be worshipped with "to <s>Śokavināśinī</s>," and the Lord with "homage to <s>Ānanda</s>."
One should worship her thighs with "to <s>Rambhā</s>," and <s>Śiva</s>, the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>, with "to <s>Śivā</s>."

children.text: adityai ca kaṭiṃ devyāḥ śūlinaḥ śūlapāṇaye ||
children.translated_text: The goddess's waist is to be worshipped with "to <s>Aditi</s>," and the trident-bearing one with "to <s>Śūlapāṇi</s>."

children.text: mādhavyai ca tathā nābhimatha śambhorbhavāya ca
children.translated_text: Likewise her navel is to be worshipped with "to <s>Mādhavī</s>," and then <s>Śambhu</s> with "to <s>Bhava</s>."
Her breasts are to be worshipped with "to <s>Ānandakāriṇī</s>," and <s>Śaṃkara</s> with "to <s>Indudhārin</s>."

children.text: utkaṇṭhinyai namaḥ kaṇṭhaṃ nīlakaṇṭhāya vai haram
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Utkaṇṭhinī</s> for the throat, and <s>Hara</s> with "to <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>."
Her hands are to be worshipped with "to <s>Utpaladhāriṇī</s>," and <s>Rudra</s>, lord of the world, with homage.

children.text: bāhū ca parirambhiṇyai triśūlāya harasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Her arms are to be worshipped with "to <s>Parirambhiṇī</s>," and <s>Hara</s> with "to <s>Triśūla</s>."
The goddess's face is to be worshipped with "to <s>Vilāsinī</s>," and then the Lord's with "to <s>Vṛṣeśa</s>."
Her smile is to be worshipped with "to <s>Sasmeralīlā</s>," and the Lord's with "to <s>Viśvavaktra</s>."
the two eyes to <s>Madanavāsinī</s> and to <s>Viśvadhāman</s>, the trident-bearer,
but the two eyebrows to <s>Nṛtyapriyā</s> and to <s>Tāṇḍaveśa</s>, the bearer of the spear.
The forehead of the goddess is for <s>Indrāṇī</s>, and for <s>Havyavāha</s> of the lord,
the crown of the goddess for <s>Svāhā</s>, and of the lord for <s>Gaṅgādhara</s>.
I praise the two auspicious ones whose bodies are the universe, whose faces are the universe, and whose feet and hands are the universe,
<s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>, with gracious faces.
Having worshipped <s>Śiva</s> and his consort again in this way, according to rule, in front of them,
one should make lotuses and blue lotuses with powders of many colors.
One should make conches, disks, bracelets, svastikas, goads, and fly-whisks.
As many particles of powder as fall there upon the earth,
for that many thousands of years one is honored in <s>Śivaloka</s>.
According to one's ability, one should give four vessels of ghee together with gold,
and a water-pot supplied with water and food to a Brahmin.
For four months, fortnight by fortnight, one should offer this.
Then for four months, as before, upon the water-pot,
there should be four vessels of saktu (roasted meal), and after that vessels of sesame.
Scented water, flower-water, sandalwood water, and saffron water,

children.text: apakvaṃ dadhi dugdhaṃ ca gośṛṅgodakameva ca ||
children.translated_text: uncooked curds, milk, and water from a cow's horn,
flour-water, and again water mixed with powdered kuṣṭha,
likewise water of uśīra, and again water with barley flour,
and sesame-water: having sipped these, one should sleep in the months beginning with <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>.
The sipping is prescribed for the two fortnights of those months.
Everywhere white flowers are praised for constant worship,
and at every time of giving one should utter this mantra:
"May <s>Gaurī</s>, auspicious and destroyer of sin, always be pleased with me.
May <s>Lalitā</s> be for good fortune, and <s>Bhavānī</s> for every success."
At the end of the year, one should offer salt, a jar of molasses, sarjikā,
sandalwood, and an eye-bandage, together with a golden lotus.
One should also offer a golden <s>Umāmaheśvara</s>, likewise furnished with sugarcane and fruits,
and a bed with a cotton covering and a resting-place,
to a Brahmin together with his wife, saying, "May <s>Gaurī</s> be pleased with me."
This eternal tṛtīyā is known by the name <s>Ārdrānandakarī</s>,
and by fasting on it a man goes to the supreme state of <s>Śambhu</s>.
In this world he obtains lasting joy and wealth,
and with the attainment of long life and health no one suffers grief.

children.text: nārī vā kurute yā tu kumārī vidhavā ca yā
children.translated_text: And whatever woman performs it, whether a maiden or a widow,
she too obtains that fruit, cherished by the grace of the goddess.
Having fasted in this way each fortnight, knowing the rule of mantra and worship,
one reaches the world of <s>Rudrāṇī</s>, from which return is difficult.
The person who hears this regularly, or has it recited,
is worshipped by the gandharvas in <s>Śakra</s>'s world for three yugas.

children.text: ānandadāṃ sakaladuḥkhaharāṃ tṛtīyāṃ yā strī karotyavidhavā vidhavātha vāpi
children.translated_text: Whatever woman, whether not widowed or widowed, performs the tṛtīyā that gives joy and removes all sorrow,

children.text: sā sve gṛhe sukhaśatānyanubhūya bhūyo gaurīpadaṃ sadayitā dayitā prayāti ||
children.translated_text: after enjoying hundreds of pleasures in her own house, she goes again, beloved and with her beloved, to the feet of <s>Gaurī</s>.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Now I shall also describe another tṛtīyā, which grants every desire,

children.text: yasyāṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati cākṣayam ||
children.translated_text: on which whatever is given, offered in fire, or recited becomes imperishable.
Those who fast on the third lunar day in the bright fortnight of <s>Vaiśākha</s>
obtain an imperishable fruit from every good deed.
When that day is joined with <s>Kṛttikā</s>, it is especially well worshipped.
There whatever is given, offered in fire, or recited is said to be entirely imperishable.
His lineage is imperishable, and his merit on that day is imperishable.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is worshipped with akṣata grains; therefore that day too is remembered as Akṣayā.
Men, having bathed with akṣata grains and likewise given akṣatas to <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: vipreṣu dattvā tāneva tathā saktūn susaṃkṛtān
children.translated_text: and having given those same grains among Brahmins, and well-prepared saktus as well,
enjoy imperishable fruit, like a greatly fortunate eater of food.
A man who properly performs even one tṛtīyā in the manner described
receives the fruit of all these tṛtīyās.
Having worshipped <s>Janārdana</s> on the tṛtīyā while fasting,
he obtains the fruit of a rājasūya sacrifice and finds the highest course.
<s>Manu</s> said:
By what vrata, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>, does one obtain sweet speech,
and likewise good fortune among people and skill in higher branches of knowledge,
as well as unbroken harmony between husband and wife and with kinsmen?

children.text: āyuśca vipulaṃ puṃsāṃ tanme kathaya mādhava ||
children.translated_text: Tell me that by which men have abundant life, O <s>Mādhava</s>.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
You have asked rightly, O king. Hear the Sārasvata vrata,
by the very praise of which <s>Sarasvatī</s> is pleased here.
Whatever devoted man would perform this supreme vrata,
after worshipping at the beginning of that day, he should honor these Brahmins.
Or, on a Sunday, with favorable strength of planets and stars,
he should feed Brahmins with milk-rice after having Brahmins recite auspicious texts.
Having given white garments, together with gold according to his ability,
he should worship <s>Gāyatrī</s> with devotion, using white garlands and unguents:
"Just as, O goddess, the blessed <s>Pitāmaha</s> in <s>Brahmaloka</s>
does not remain after abandoning you, so be the giver of boons.

children.text: vedāḥ śāstrāṇi sarvāṇi gītanṛtyādikaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Just as the Vedas, all the śāstras, and whatever consists of song, dance, and the like

children.text: na vihīnaṃ tvayā devi tathā me santu siddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not without you, O goddess, so may accomplishments be mine.

children.text: lakṣmīrmedhā dharā puṣṭirgaurī tuṣṭiḥ prabhā matiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Dharā</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>, and <s>Mati</s>:
with these eight bodies protect me, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>."
Having thus worshipped <s>Gāyatrī</s>, who holds a vīṇā and rosary beads,
With white flowers and unbroken rice, with devotion, one should worship her as holding a water-pot and a book.
The knower of <s>dharma</s> should eat in the evening and in the morning, observing a vow of silence.
On the fifth lunar day and in each fortnight he should worship the one who dwells with <s>Brahman</s>.
Likewise he should offer a prastha of rice, together with a vessel of ghee,
milk and gold, saying, "May <s>Gāyatrī</s> be pleased."
At twilight too he should keep silence; doing this, he should carry out the observance.
He should not eat between those times until thirteen months have passed.
When the vow has ended, he should arrange a meal with white rice.
First he should give a meal to a Brahmin, together with a pair of garments.

children.text: devyā vitānaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ ca sitanetre payasvinīm
children.translated_text: He should give the goddess a canopy, a bell, and a white-eyed milk-giving cow,

children.text: candanaṃ vastrayugmaṃ ca dadyācca śikharaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as sandalwood, a pair of garments, and again a finial.
He should also devoutly honor the teacher who instructed him, the guru,
without deceit about his wealth, with garments, garlands, and unguents.
Whoever performs the Sārasvata vow by this rule
is born learned, endowed with wealth, and red-throated.
Through the favor of <s>Sarasvatī</s> he is honored in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: nārī vā kurute yā tu sāpi tatphalagāminī ||
children.translated_text: And whatever woman performs it also obtains that same fruit.
O king, she dwells in <s>Brahmaloka</s> for three ten-thousands of kalpas.

children.text: sārasvataṃ vrataṃ yastu śṛṇuyādapi yaḥ paṭhet
children.translated_text: Whoever even hears or recites this Sārasvata vow
dwells in the city of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> for three ten-thousands of kalpas.
I wish to hear about the bathing that is prescribed at an eclipse of the moon or the sun,
O knower of the rules concerning substances and mantras.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
When the disturbance of an eclipse occurs upon reaching a person's zodiac sign,
I shall explain his bathing according to the rules for mantras and herbs.
When a lunar eclipse has arrived, after having Brahmins recite auspicious words,
and after worshiping four Brahmins with white garlands and unguents,
before the eclipse itself he should gather herbs and the other materials.
He should set up four unblemished jars, saying that they are the oceans.
From an elephant's path, a horse-road, an anthill, a confluence, a lake, and a cow-pen,
and from the area of a royal gateway, he should bring earth and place it in them.
He should place in the jars the five products of the cow and pure pearls,
gorocanā, lotus, conch, and the five jewels.
He should add crystal, white sandalwood, water from a sacred ford, and mustard seed,
ivory, a white water-lily, and likewise uśīra and guggulu.
Having placed all this in the jars, he should invoke the gods into them.
"May all the oceans, rivers, sacred fords, clouds, streams, and rivers
come for the patron of the sacrifice, bringing about the destruction of sin.
May that god who bears the thunderbolt, regarded as lord of the <s>Ādityas</s>,
the thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s>, remove the affliction caused by the planet.
May <s>Agni</s>, the mouth of all the gods, seven-flamed and of immeasurable radiance,
remove the affliction arisen from the lunar eclipse.
May <s>Yama</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, who rides a buffalo and is witness of the deeds of beings,
remove my affliction arisen from the lunar eclipse.
May that lord of the hosts of rākṣasas himself, resembling the fire of dissolution,
intent on his sword and very terrifying, remove the affliction caused by rākṣasas.
May the god who holds the serpent-noose, who rides a makara in visible form,
that lord of waters, remove the affliction caused by the lunar eclipse.
May <s>Vāyu</s>, who as breath protects the worlds and is fond of the black antelope,
remove here the affliction arisen from the lunar eclipse.
May that god who is lord of treasures, bearing sword, spear, and mace,
<s>Dhanada</s>, remove for me the impurity of the lunar eclipse.
May that god who bears the moon, <s>Pinākī</s>, who rides the bull,
<s>Śaṃkara</s>, destroy the affliction born from the lunar eclipse.

children.text: trailokye yāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Whatever beings there are in the three worlds, stationary and moving,
together with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the Sun, may they burn away sin."
Having invoked them thus, and having been consecrated with those jars furnished with good qualities,
with mantras from the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, and with white garlands and unguents,
he should worship Brahmins and his chosen deities with gifts of garments and cows.
Then he should write these same mantras, accompanied by the small vessels,
on a strip of cloth or on a lotus, together with the five jewels.
Those best twice-born men should place them on the patron's head.
Then he should pass through the period that follows the eclipse.
Facing east, after worshiping and bowing to his chosen deity,
when the lunar eclipse has ended, with the auspicious gift of a cow performed,
he should present that cloth-strip to a Brahmin who has bathed.
Whoever performs the eclipse-bath by this rule

children.text: na tasya grahapīḍā syānna ca bandhujanakṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has no affliction from the planet, nor any loss of kinsmen.
He obtains the highest perfection, from which return is hard to attain.
At a solar eclipse one should always pronounce the name of the Sun in the mantras.

children.text: adhikāḥ padmarāgāḥ syuḥ kapilāṃ ca suśobhanām
children.translated_text: There should be more rubies, and also a beautiful tawny cow.
He should give it to the lord of night at eclipses of the moon and sun.
The person who constantly hears this or causes it to be heard
is freed from all sins and is honored in <s>Śakra</s>'s world.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
What is to be done when there is anxiety over a wondrous omen? By what is <s>Alakṣmī</s> destroyed?
And what is prescribed in rites such as the consecration for one whose children have died?
The blessed Lord said:
Formerly committed sins bear fruit in this life, O treasure of austerity,
in the form of disease and poverty, and likewise in the destruction of what is dear.
For the warding off of that, I shall explain what always produces welfare.
The rite called the <s>saptamī-snapana</s> (seventh-day bathing) destroys affliction among people.
Where the death of children who are still drinking milk is observed,
and likewise of the aged and the sick, and even of those who are in youth,
for pacification there I shall declare the consecration-bath for a woman whose children have died.
This very rite will also destroy agitation from portents and confusion of mind.
When, O treasure of austerity, the <s>Vārāha</s> kalpa is to come,
and when excellent <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s> will be there as well,
and when, in that very period, the twenty-fifth will occur,
then, in an age named <s>Kṛta</s>, an increaser of the <s>Haihaya</s> lineage
will be a heroic king, the powerful <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>.
He will rule the whole earth with its seven islands,
for seventy-seven thousand years, O <s>Nārada</s>.
And likewise his hundred sons, as soon as they are born,
will go to destruction through the curse of <s>Cyavana</s>.

children.text: sahasrabāhuśca yadā bhavitā tasya vai sutaḥ
children.translated_text: And when the thousand-armed one will be his son,
deer-eyed, splendid, and born with the marks of a king,
then <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>, after worshiping the thousand-rayed sun, the day-maker,
with fasts, divine vows, and Vedic hymns, O <s>Nārada</s>,
will obtain this bathing rite, sufficient for the life of his son.

children.text: kṛtavīryeṇa vai pṛṣṭa idaṃ vakṣyati bhāskaraḥ
children.translated_text: Asked by <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s> will declare this rite,
which pacifies all evil and always destroys defilement.
<s>Sūrya</s> said:
Enough of great hardship; your son, O lord of men,
will be long-lived. Yet I shall teach what destroys defilement.
I shall declare the <s>saptamī-snapana</s> for the welfare of all the worlds.
For a child born to a woman whose children have died, in the seventh month, O <s>Nārada</s>,
or on the bright seventh lunar day, all this is commended.
After securing the favorable strength of the planets and stars, and having Brahmins recite,
the wise man should avoid the child's birth-nakṣatra and that lunar date;
likewise, this should be done for the aged and the sick, and in other cases too.
On ground smeared with cow dung, then with a single sacred fire established,
with grains of red śāli rice, a <s>caru</s> (cooked oblation) mixed with cow's milk
should be offered to <s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Rudra</s> with their mantras, according to rule.
He should recite the seven-verse hymn sacred to <s>Sūrya</s> and offer oblations of ghee;
likewise, with the <s>Rudra-sūkta</s>, he should offer to <s>Rudra</s>, O <s>Nārada</s>.
Sacrificial sticks of <s>arka</s> and <s>palāśa</s> are also to be offered here,
and again a <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) with barley and black sesame should be performed eight hundred times.
Likewise, with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> and with ghee, another eight hundred offerings should be made.

children.text: hutvā snānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ maṅgalaṃ yena dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: After making the offerings, the intelligent man should perform the auspicious bath.
A Brahmin learned in the Veda, holding darbha grass, should duly perform it,
after placing four beautiful jars at the corners,
and again a fifth in the middle, adorned with curds and unbroken rice.
He should set down an uncracked jar, consecrated with the seven-verse hymn,
filled with sacred water, connected with the solar rite, and furnished with jewels.
All the jars should be joined with all herbs and furnished with <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five cow-products),
and he should wrap them with five jewels, fruits, flowers, and cloths.
Having brought purified earth from places of elephants and horses, from a road, an anthill, a confluence, a lake, and a cowpen,
he should place it in each and every one of the jars.
Among the four jars also, with jewels placed inside them, the middle one
the Brahmin should take there, and he should utter the solar mantras.
By seven women there, all with unimpaired limbs,
honored as far as possible with garlands, garments, and ornaments,
and accompanied by Brahmin women, the consecration-bath of the woman whose children have died is to be performed.
These are the consecration mantras:
May this boy have long life, and may the beautiful woman have living sons.
May <s>Āditya</s> and <s>Candramas</s>, together with the circles of planets and stars,
and the guardians of the worlds with <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: te te cānye ca devaughāḥ sadā pāntu kumārakam ||
children.translated_text: these and other hosts of gods always protect the little boy.

children.text: mitraḥ śanirvā hutabhugye ca bālagrahāḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: May <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Śani</s>, <s>Hutabhuj</s>, and whatever child-seizing spirits there may be

children.text: pīḍāṃ kurvantu bālasya mā māturjanakasya vai ||
children.translated_text: not cause affliction to the child, nor indeed to the mother or the father.
Then, wearing white garments and joined by her husband and child,
she should devoutly worship the group of seven women, and then the guru.
Then she should make a golden image placed upon a copper vessel,
and present that image of <s>Dharmarāja</s> to the guru.
With garments, gold, heaps of jewels, foods, and milk-rice mixed with ghee,
he should likewise worship the Brahmins, free from deceit over his wealth.

children.text: bhuktvā ca guruṇā ceyam uccāryā mantrasaṃtatiḥ
children.translated_text: After the guru has eaten, this sequence of mantras should be uttered:
May this boy be long-lived and happy for a hundred years.
Whatever evil there is for him, let it be cast into the submarine fire.

children.text: brahmā rudro vasuḥ skando viṣṇuḥ śakro hutāśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and <s>Hutāśana</s>

children.text: rakṣantu sarve duṣṭebhyo varadāḥ santu sarvadā
children.translated_text: protect him from all evil beings; may they always be grantors of boons.
He should honor the guru while he says these and similar words.
According to his ability, he should give a tawny cow, then bow and dismiss him.
Together with her son, after bowing to <s>Ravi</s> and <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
she should then eat the <s>caru</s>, the remnant of the offering, saying, "Homage to <s>Āditya</s>."
This very rite is commended for portents, anxieties, and bad dreams.
One should always perform the worship after avoiding the asterism of the performer's birthday,
and, doing this on the bright seventh lunar day for pacification, he does not sink into misfortune.
By this procedure, accompanied by gifts, a man became long-lived,
and ruled this earth for ten thousand years.
The seventh-day bathing rite is meritorious, purifying, and life-giving; <s>Ravi</s>
having described it, O best of twice-born men, disappeared right there.
All this has been fully explained: the excellent bathing rite of the seventh day,
which appeases every evil and is the highest benefit for children.
One should seek health from <s>Bhāskara</s>, wealth from <s>Hutāśana</s>,
knowledge from <s>Īśvara</s>, and liberation from <s>Janārdana</s>.
This would destroy great sins; it is supreme welfare and increases children.

children.text: śṛṇoti yaścainam ananyacetās tasyāpi siddhiṃ munayo vadanti ||
children.translated_text: The sages say that one who hears it with undivided mind also attains success.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Long ago, in the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> kalpa, when he was questioned by the great-souled one,
great <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Pinākī</s>, who dwelt on <s>Mandara</s>, was asked by <s>Brahmā</s> himself.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
How, O lord of the immortals, may men obtain health and endless sovereignty,
O god, through only a little austerity, or else liberation?
What is unknown to you, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, by your grace, O <s>Adhokṣaja</s>?
So now declare here the great fruit gained through slight austerity.
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ sa viśvātmā brahmaṇā lokabhāvanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus questioned by <s>Brahmā</s>, that soul of the universe, the creator of worlds,
<s>Umāpati</s> spoke these words, pleasing to the mind.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
When, after twenty-three from this <s>Rathaṃtara</s> kalpa,
the <s>Vārāha</s> kalpa will come, in its auspicious manvantara,
when the seventh, called <s>Vaivasvata</s>, maker of the seven worlds, has arisen,
they likewise call that age the twenty-eighth, named <s>Dvāpara</s>.
At its end that great god, <s>Vāsudeva</s> <s>Janārdana</s>,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, will become threefold for the sake of relieving the burden of the earth.
He will be the sage <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, likewise <s>Rauhiṇeya</s>, and then <s>Keśava</s>.
<s>Keśava</s>, destroyer of the pride of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and others, will remove afflictions.

children.text: purīṃ dvāravatīṃ nāma sāmprataṃ yā kuśasthalī
children.translated_text: The city now called <s>Kuśasthalī</s> will be named <s>Dvāravatī</s>;
endowed with divine power, it will be made for the residence of the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow.
At my command <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> will likewise make it for the lord of the world.
When, on some occasion, the slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, of immeasurable radiance, is seated there in the assembly,
with his wives, the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, and kings rich in sacrificial gifts,
with the <s>Kurus</s>, gods, and gandharvas all around,
while ancient tales connected with dharma are underway,
at the end of the discourse he, the mighty one, will be questioned by <s>Bhīmasena</s>,
and will reveal the distinction of this secret dharma about which you have asked.

children.text: bhavitā sa tadā brahmankartā caiva vṛkodaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vṛkodara</s> will be the doer of it,
and the mighty son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> will be the promulgator of this dharma.

children.text: yasya tīkṣṇo vṛko nāma jaṭhare havyavāhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Because a sharp fire named <s>Vṛka</s>, the eater of oblations,

children.text: mayā dattaḥ sa dharmātmā tena cāsau vṛkodaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: was placed by me in his belly, that righteous one is therefore <s>Vṛkodara</s>.
He will be wise, honorable, great, with the strength of ten thousand elephants,
unaging, prosperous, and beautiful in form like <s>Kandarpa</s>.
Because, though righteous, he will be unable to fast owing to the fierceness of his digestive fire,
this vow is superior to all vows without exception.
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, the soul of the universe and teacher of the world, will proclaim it,
as granting the fruit of all sacrifices and destroying every sin,
appeasing every evil and worshipped by all the gods,

children.text: pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ ca maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam
children.translated_text: the purifier of purifiers and the auspiciousness of auspicious things,
the future among future things, ancient among the purāṇas.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> said:
If, O <s>Bhārata</s>, on the eighth, fourteenth, or twelfth lunar days,
or even on other days and lunar asterisms, you are unable to fast,
then, having fasted on this holy lunar date, which destroys all sins,

children.text: upoṣya vidhinānena gaccha viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: by this rule go to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
When the tenth day of the bright fortnight occurs in the month of <s>Māgha</s>,
one should anoint oneself with ghee and perform a bath with sesame seeds.
Likewise, having worshipped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, saying 'Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> of the sky,'

children.text: kṛṣṇāya pādau sampūjya śiraḥ sarvātmane namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should worship the feet as belonging to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and the head with 'Homage to the soul of all.'
With '<s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>' one should worship the breast, as belonging to the bearer of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>,
and likewise, in order, the arms of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as conch-bearer, discus-bearer,
mace-bearer, and giver of boons.
With '<s>Dāmodara</s>' one should worship the belly, and the generative organ as belonging to the five-arrowed one;
the thighs as belonging to the lord of good fortune, and the knees as belonging to the bearer of beings.

children.text: namo nīlāya vai jaṅghe pādau viśvasṛje namaḥ
children.translated_text: With 'Homage to the dark-blue one' one should worship the shanks, and the feet with 'Homage to the creator of the universe.'

children.text: namo devyai namaḥ śāntyai namo lakṣmyai namaḥ śriyai ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the goddess, homage to peace, homage to <s>Lakṣmī</s>, homage to prosperity.

children.text: namaḥ puṣṭyai namastuṣṭyai dhṛṣṭyai hṛṣṭyai namo namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to nourishment, homage to contentment; homage again and again to boldness and gladness.
Homage to the lord of birds, the winged one swift as the wind;
one should always worship <s>Garuḍa</s>, the destroyer of poison.
Having thus worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Umāpati</s>, and <s>Vināyaka</s>,
with perfumes, garlands, incense, and various kinds of foods,
the wise person, keeping silence, should eat kṛsarā cooked in cow's milk,

children.text: sarpiṣā saha bhuktvā ca gatvā śatapadaṃ budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with ghee, and then go one hundred paces.
Taking a tooth-stick from a banyan tree, or else one of khadira wood,
the wise person should clean his teeth, sip water, and face east or north.
After performing the evening twilight rite when the sun has set, he should say,
'Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; I have gone to you for refuge.'
On the eleventh day, fasting from food and fully worshipping <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: rātriṃ ca sakalāṃ sthitvā snānaṃ ca payasā tathā ||
children.translated_text: having remained through the whole night, and then bathing likewise with milk,
and having offered oblations into the fire with ghee together with eminent brāhmaṇas,
O lotus-eyed one, on the twelfth day he should eat a meal of milk together with them.
With self-control, I shall perform it; may that be free from obstacles for me.
Having spoken thus, he should sleep on the ground, after again hearing a tale from the <s>Itihāsa</s>.

children.text: śrutvā prabhāte saṃjāte nadīṃ gatvā viśāṃ pate
children.translated_text: When morning has come, after going to a river, O lord of the people,
he should bathe and cleanse himself with clay in the same way, avoiding heretics.
Having worshiped at the twilight according to rule and made the offering to the ancestors,
and having bowed to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the sole lord of the seven worlds,
the wise man should, with devotion, have a pavilion made in front of his house.
He should make it ten <s>hastas</s> or eight <s>hastas</s> in measure, O lord of the people.
He should make an auspicious altar four <s>hastas</s> across, O slayer of enemies,
and there he should set up an archway four <s>hastas</s> in measure.
Having placed a water-jar there, he should then worship the guardians of the directions.
Then, seated on a black antelope skin, with a vessel filled with water and pierced with an opening,

children.text: tasya dhārāṃ ca śirasā dhārayetsakalāṃ niśām ||
children.translated_text: he should bear its stream upon his head for the whole night.
Likewise he should cause a stream of milk to fall upon the head of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
He should make a fire-pit there, an <s>aratni</s> in size, with three girdles.
After making it with a womb-shaped mouth, he should then, through Brahmins, offer barley and ghee,
and sesame, with mantras whose deity is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in the manner of a single sacred fire.
After properly offering a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> <s>caru</s> mixed with cow's milk,
he should pour a stream of ghee measuring half a <s>niṣpāva</s>.
O mighty one, after setting up thirteen water-jars,
provided with various kinds of eatables and adorned with white cloths,
furnished with <s>udumbara</s> vessels and supplied with five jewels,
a <s>homa</s> should be performed there by four <s>Ṛgveda</s>-knowers facing north.
A <s>Rudra</s> recitation should be made by four men devoted to the <s>Yajurveda</s>,
and four singers of the <s>Sāmaveda</s> should chant the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> <s>Sāmans</s>.
He should have them recited all around together with the apotropaic group.
Thus he should honor those twelve Brahmins with garments, garlands, and unguents,
and with rings, bracelets, and golden cords.
He should give clothes and beds, free from deceit about his wealth.
In this way the night should be passed with the sounds of songs and auspicious music.
For the preceptor, again, everything should be doubled.
Then, when the clear morning has come, he should rise and give thirteen
cows, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>, furnished with golden muzzles,
milch cows of good disposition, together with bronze milking vessels,
with silver hooves, clothed, and sprinkled with sandalwood.
Then, with devotion, after satisfying all those Brahmins with foods to be eaten and enjoyed,
and after feeding all the Brahmins with many kinds of food,
he himself should eat food without alkaline seasoning or salt, and then dismiss them.
Accompanying them for eight steps, together with his sons and wife,
he should say, "May <s>Keśava</s>, lord of gods and destroyer of affliction, be pleased here."
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is in the heart of <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> is in the heart of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: yathāntaraṃ na paśyāmi tathā me svasti cāyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As I see no difference between them, so may there be welfare and long life for me.
Having uttered this, the wise man should send those jars, the cows, and the beds,
and also the garments of them all, to their houses.
If many beds are not available, even one well-prepared
bed, furnished with all equipment, should be given to a twice-born man.
Having had the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s> recited, he should pass
that day, O tiger among men, if he desires abundant prosperity.
Therefore, taking hold of resolve, O <s>Bhīmasena</s>, free from envy,
perform this vow properly, which I have declared to you out of affection.
When it has been performed by you, O hero, it will be known by your name.
This indeed is the auspicious <s>Bhīmadvādaśī</s>, remover of all sins,

children.text: yā tu kalyāṇinī nāma purā kalpeṣu paṭhyate ||
children.translated_text: which in former ages is recited under the name <s>Kalyāṇinī</s>.
Become the first performer in this <s>Saukara</s> age, O great hero, foremost among excellent champions.
By remembering it, or even by praising it completely, one whose sins are destroyed becomes lord of the thirty gods.

children.text: kṛtvā ca yāmapsarasām adhīśā veśyā kṛtā hyanyabhavāntareṣu
children.translated_text: By performing it, the mistress of the <s>apsarases</s>, though made a courtesan in other births,
was, through great wonder, born as a cowherd girl; that very one is now <s>Urvaśī</s> on the height of heaven.
Or, though born in a Vaiśya family, she became the daughter of <s>Puloma</s>, the wife of <s>Puruhūta</s>;

children.text: tatrāpi tasyāḥ paricārikeyaṃ mama priyā samprati satyabhāmā ||
children.translated_text: and even there this attendant of hers is now my beloved <s>Satyabhāmā</s>.
In former times, after bathing, this shining orb likewise obtained a body made of the <s>Veda</s>,
on this auspicious lunar day, <s>Vivasvān</s>, the thousand-rayed one, by means of a thousand streams.
This very rite was performed by the chiefs such as <s>Mahendra</s>, by the <s>Vasus</s>, and by the gods, enemies of the demons.

children.text: phalamasya na śakyate'bhivaktuṃ yadi jihvāyutakoṭayo mukhe syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its fruit cannot be fully described, even if ten thousand million tongues were in the mouth.
The son of the lord of the <s>Yādavas</s> will proclaim it as endless, as the destroyer of the impurity of the Kali age.
Whoever performs it here is able to raise up all ancestors even if they have gone to hell.

children.text: ya idamaghavidāraṇaṃ śṛṇoti bhaktyā paripaṭhatīha paropakārahetoḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever hears this destroyer of sin, or devoutly recites it here for the sake of helping others,
that king, possessing all aims on this lunar day, O four-faced one, attains equality with you.

children.text: kalyāṇinī nāma purā babhūva yā dvādaśī māghadineṣu pūjyā
children.translated_text: The twelfth lunar day called <s>Kalyāṇinī</s>, which in former times was worshiped in the days of <s>Māgha</s>,
will, when performed by the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, be named after <s>Bhīma</s>, O sinless one, and will have endless merit.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
The origin of the social classes and life-stages has been heard by me in the <s>Purāṇas</s>.
O Blessed One, I have also heard the Dharmaśāstra determination of good conduct.
I wish to hear truly the good conduct of women who sell themselves.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
In that very age, O Brahman, there will be sixteen thousand
women of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O lotus-born one.
With them, in the springtime, when the place is filled with cuckoos and swarms of bees,
on the bank of a flowering lake whose kahlāra lotuses are opened by the wind,
while they are absorbed in lavish drinking parties, he will be adorned,
doe-eyed, splendid, and wearing a crest of mālatī flowers.
<s>Sāmba</s>, conqueror of enemy cities, passing along a nearby road,
like <s>Kandarpa</s> himself in beauty, adorned with every ornament,
will be gazed at with desire by them, tormented by the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s>.
Then their passion for him will grow strong within themselves.
At that time the Lord of the world, seeing this on every side with the eye of knowledge,

children.text: śāpaṃ vakṣyati tāḥ sarvā vo hariṣyanti dasyavaḥ
children.translated_text: will pronounce a curse: "Robbers will carry all of you away.
For, in my absence, such a thing has been done through the restlessness of desire."

children.text: tataḥ prasādito deva idaṃ vakṣyati śārṅgabhṛt
children.translated_text: Then, when the god, the bearer of Śārṅga, has been propitiated, he will say this
to them, scorched by the curse, the blessed maker of beings:
"Dear to Brahmins, the infinite-souled one will teach a means of crossing beyond the ocean of servitude,
one that will bring about future welfare.
The vow that the sage <s>Dālbhya</s> will explain to you
will itself be enough for deliverance, even in servitude."
Having spoken thus and embraced them, the lord of <s>Dvāravatī</s> departed.
Then, after a long time, when the burden of the earth had been removed,
when the Mausala destruction had likewise ended and <s>Keśava</s> had gone to heaven,
when the Yadu clan was empty and <s>Arjuna</s> had even been defeated by all the robbers,
when the wives of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had been seized and made objects of enjoyment for slaves by the sea,
and were remaining there, burned by misery, O Four-faced one,
there will come the great ascetic named <s>Dālbhya</s>, whose self is disciplined by yoga.
They will duly worship him with an arghya and bow again and again,
lamenting repeatedly, their eyes overwhelmed with tears.
Remembering their abundant pleasures, their divine garlands and unguents,
their husband, the lord of the worlds, the infinite and unconquered one,

children.text: divyabhāvāṃ tāṃ ca purīṃ nānāratnagṛhāṇi ca
children.translated_text: that divine city, its many jewel-filled houses,
and all the inhabitants of <s>Dvārakā</s>, the godlike youths,
they will stand facing the sage and ask this question:
The women said:
"Venerable sir, all of us have been violated by robbers by force.
In this fall from our own dharma, be our refuge.
Long ago, O Brahman, you were instructed by wise <s>Keśava</s>.
Why, after obtaining union with the Lord, have we come to the state of courtesans?

children.text: veśyānāmapi yo dharmastaṃ no brūhi tapodhana
children.translated_text: Tell us also the dharma of courtesans, O treasure of austerity."
Thereafter that <s>Dālbhya Caikitāyana</s> will speak to them.
<s>Dālbhya</s> said:
"Long ago, during water-sports and amusements in Lake <s>Mānasa</s>,
<s>Nārada</s> came near all of you.
Formerly all of you were apsarases, daughters of <s>Hutāśana</s>.
Without bowing, through arrogance, you questioned him, the knower of yoga:
'Teach us how <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> might become our husband.'
Therefore this granting of a boon and this curse came upon you in the past.
By giving a pair of beds in the months of Madhu and Mādhava,
and by presenting golden furnishings on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> will surely become your husband in another birth.
But because you questioned me without bowing, out of pride in beauty and good fortune,
for that reason separation will quickly befall you.
All of you will be carried off by thieves and will obtain the state of courtesans.
Thus, by the curse of <s>Nārada</s> and by the will of wise <s>Keśava</s>,
all of you, deluded by desire, have come to the state of courtesans.
Now listen, lovely women, to what I shall also say."
<s>Dālbhya</s> said:

children.text: purā devāsure yuddhe hateṣu śataśaḥ suraiḥ
children.translated_text: "Long ago, in the war between gods and asuras, when hundreds had been slain by the gods,
among the Dānavas, Asuras, Daityas, and Rākṣasas here and there,
the many thousands of bands of their women, and hundreds besides,
those who had been married and those who had indeed been enjoyed by force,

children.text: tāni sarvāṇi deveśaḥ provāca vadatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to all of them the lord of the gods, best of speakers, spoke.
<s>Indra</s> said:
"'Live now according to the dharma of courtesans in the palace of the king,
being devoted, O fair-hipped women, and likewise in the temples of the gods.

children.text: rājānaḥ svāminastulyāḥ sutā vāpi ca tatsamāḥ
children.translated_text: Kings are equivalent to your masters, and sons too are equal to them.
Good fortune will come to all of you, according to your capacity.
Whoever takes up the fee and always comes to your house
is to be received by you according to the arrangement, except for a hypocrite.
When an auspicious day for the gods and ancestors arises,
cows, land, gold, and grain should be given according to one's ability,
and the words of Brahmins, O fair-hipped women, should be carried out.
And whatever other vow I shall now teach correctly,
that too is to be performed by all of you without hesitation.
Those who know the Veda know that this is enough for crossing beyond saṃsāra.

children.text: yadā sūryadine hastaḥ puṣyo yātha punarvasuḥ ||
children.translated_text: When, on a Sunday, the asterism is Hasta, Puṣya, or Punarvasu,
then a woman should properly perform a bath with all herbs.
Then she will come into the very presence of <s>Pañcaśara</s>.
She should worship <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> with hymns naming <s>Anaṅga</s>.

children.text: kāmāya pādau sampūjya jaṅghe vai mohakāriṇe
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the feet as <s>Kāma</s>, and the shanks as <s>Mohakārin</s>,
she should worship the penis as <s>Kandarpanidhi</s>, and the uncertain kīṭa as <s>Prītimat</s>: homage.
The navel she should worship as <s>Saukhyasamudra</s>, and likewise the belly as <s>Vāma</s>.
The heart she should worship as <s>Hṛdayeśa</s>, and the breasts as <s>Āhlādakārin</s>."
With the formula 'to longing,' one should worship the mouth of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the maker of bliss;
the left side as belonging to <s>Puṣpacāpa</s>, and the right as belonging to <s>Puṣpabāṇa</s>.
With '<s>Mānasa</s>' one should worship the crest, and with '<s>Vilola</s>' the hair of the head;
and one should worship the whole body of the god of gods with 'Homage to the soul of all.'
Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, the peaceful one, and to the one who holds the noose and goad;
to the mace-bearer, the one clothed in yellow, and the bearer of conch and discus.
'Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'; homage to the one whose nature is <s>Kāmadeva</s>.

children.text: sarvaśāntyai namaḥ prītyai namo ratyai nama śriyai ||
children.translated_text: Homage to universal peace, homage to affection; homage to <s>Rati</s>, homage to <s>Śrī</s>.
Homage to <s>Puṣṭi</s>, homage to <s>Tuṣṭi</s>; homage to the attainment of every aim.
Having thus fully worshipped the lord of gods, the lord whose nature is <s>Anaṅga</s>,
the desirous woman should honor him with perfumes, garlands, incense, and food offerings.
Then she should summon a brāhmaṇa who knows <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty) and has mastered the Veda;
after honoring him, whose limbs are unimpaired, with offerings of perfume, flowers, and the like,
she should give him a prastha of śāli rice together with a vessel of ghee,
saying, 'May <s>Mādhava</s> be pleased,' to that brāhmaṇa.
She should provide that same best of twice-born men with whatever food he desires,
holding in her mind, 'For the sake of love, this man is <s>Kāmadeva</s>.'
Whatever the eminent brāhmaṇa desires, the charming woman should do that very thing;
speaking with a smile, she should offer herself to him with her whole being.
In this way she should perform all this on a Sunday,
and she should make the gift of a prastha of rice for thirteen months.
Then, when the thirteenth month has arrived, the lovely woman
should give that brāhmaṇa a special bed furnished with its accessories,
auspicious, with pillows and resting places, and with spreads and coverings,
together with a lamp, sandals, umbrella, shoes, and a seat.
Having adorned <s>Kāmadeva</s> together with his wife with gold thread and rings,
with fine garments, bracelets, incense, garlands, and unguents,
she should set <s>Kāmadeva</s> together with his wife upon a pot of molasses,
placed on a copper-vessel seat and covered with a golden cloth,
provided with bronze vessels and accompanied by a sugarcane stalk;
she should give this with the following mantra, and likewise one milk-giving cow.
'As I never see any difference between <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Keśava</s>,
so, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, may the attainment of every desire always be mine.

children.text: yathā na kamalā dehātprayāti tava keśava
children.translated_text: As <s>Kamalā</s> does not depart from your body, O <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: tathā mamāpi deveśa śarīre sve kuru prabho ||
children.translated_text: so too, O lord of gods, O master, make that true in my own body.'
And then, as the best of twice-born men accepts the golden image of the god,

children.text: ka idaṃ kasmā adāditi vaidikaṃ mantramīrayet ||
children.translated_text: he should pronounce the Vedic mantra, 'Who gave this, and to whom did he give it?'
Then, having circumambulated the eminent twice-born man and dismissed him,
she should have the bed, seat, and all the rest taken to the brāhmaṇa's house.

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti yo vipro ratyarthaṃ gṛhamāgataḥ
children.translated_text: From then onward, whatever brāhmaṇa comes to the house for the sake of pleasure

children.text: sa mānyaḥ sūryavāre ca sa mantavyo bhavettadā ||
children.translated_text: is to be honored on Sunday, and at that time he is to be regarded in that way.
Thus, for the full thirteen months, she should satisfy excellent twice-born men
as they desire; if one is away from home, she should perform the rite with another.
With his permission, whatever handsome visitor may come
should be treated, as far as there is no obstacle for herself, as dear and capable of producing conception.

children.text: daivaṃ vā mānuṣaṃ vā syādanurāgeṇa vā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Whether the matter is divine or human, or arises then through affection,
she should observe the fifty-eight practices with their proper conduct, according to her ability.
This has been explained correctly, especially for you women;
therefore this is not <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) for courtesans here at any time.
What was formerly spoken by <s>Puruhūta</s> among the Dānava women, by me,
all that now also applies to you.
It pacifies every sin and grants endless fruit;
it has been declared for auspicious women, so perform it, O fair-faced ones.
The auspicious woman who performs all this completely and without break comes to dwell in <s>Mādhava</s>'s world;

children.text: sā pūjitā devagaṇair aśeṣair ānandakṛtsthānam upaiti viṣṇoḥ ||
children.translated_text: worshipped by all the hosts of gods, she reaches <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s abode, which brings bliss.
The blessed Lord said:

children.text: tapodhanaḥ so'pyabhidhāya caivaṃ tadā ca tāsāṃ vratamaṅganānām
children.translated_text: After the ascetic had spoken thus at that time about the women's <s>vrata</s> (vow),

children.text: svasthānameṣyatyanu tāḥ samastaṃ vrataṃ kariṣyanti ca devayānaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he too will go to his own place, and those women will perform the whole vow and go by divine vehicles.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
If a man resorts to another's wife, whether from delusion or from intoxication,
tell me, O god, maker of compassion for all, the expiation even for him.
Blessed Lord, tell me also that by which, here, for a man and a woman,
separation and the grief, disease, fear, and suffering that follow it may not arise.
The blessed Lord said:
On the second lunar day of the dark fortnight of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>,
<s>Keśava</s>, together with his wife, always dwells in the Milk Ocean.
By worshipping <s>Govinda</s> on that day, one enjoys all desires;
the gifts of cows, land, gold, and the like accompany one for seven hundred kalpas.
That second lunar day is proclaimed by the name Aśūnyaśayana, 'the bed that is not empty';
on it one should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> according to rule with these mantras:
'O bearer of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, beloved of <s>Śrī</s>, abode of <s>Śrī</s>, imperishable lord of <s>Śrī</s>,

children.text: gārhasthyaṃ mā praṇāśaṃ me yātu dharmārthakāmadam ||
children.translated_text: may my household state, which grants <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and desire, not go to destruction.
May my sacred fires not perish, O <s>Puruṣottama</s>; may the deities not perish;
may the ancestors not perish, and may there be no division of the married pair.

children.text: lakṣmyā viyujyate deva na kadācidyathā bhavān
children.translated_text: As you, O god, are never separated from <s>Lakṣmī</s>,

children.text: tathā kalatrasambandho deva mā me viyujyatām ||
children.translated_text: so, O god, may my bond with my spouse not be severed.

children.text: lakṣmyā na śūnyo varada śayyāṃ tvaṃ śayanaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: O giver of boons, as you are not without <s>Lakṣmī</s> when you have gone to the bed to sleep,
so too, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>, may my bed not be empty.
One should praise the god of gods with the resounding of song and instruments.
For one who lacks the means, a bell should serve, since it comprises all musical instruments.
Having worshipped <s>Govinda</s> in this way, he should eat food free from oil,
at night, without alkali and without salt, until that fourfold observance is completed.
Then, when morning has come, he should give a special bed furnished with an image of <s>Lakṣmīpati</s>,
provided with lamps, food, and vessels,
together with sandals, shoes, a parasol, fly-whisks, and a seat,
supplied with desired accessories and covered with white flowers and garments,
with pillows and a resting place, provided with many kinds of fruits,
and also, according to his means, furnished with ornaments and grain.
It should be given to a brāhmaṇa whose limbs are unimpaired, a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, a householder,
one learned in the <s>Veda</s>, sincere in disposition, and not fallen.
Having seated the married couple there and adorned them according to rule,
he should give the wife a vessel filled with foods to be eaten and enjoyed.
And for the brāhmaṇa he should present a golden image of the god of gods,
provided with accessories and accompanied by a water-pot.
The man who performs this aśūnyaśayana rite of <s>Hari</s> in this way,
free from stinginess about wealth and devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: na tasya patnyā virahaḥ kadācidapi jāyate
children.translated_text: never experiences separation from his wife at any time;
nor does a woman become a widow, O <s>Brahmā</s>, as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.

children.text: na virūpau na śokārtau dampatī bhavataḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: The couple are never ugly and never afflicted by grief.
Sons, cattle, and jewels do not perish, O <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
For seven thousand kalpas and seven hundred kalpas,
while performing the aśūnyaśayana rite, he is honored in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Listen also to another future observance, one that bestows beauty and prosperity.
In that age, at the end of the <s>Dvāpara</s>, O <s>Pitāmaha</s>,
there will be a dialogue of <s>Pippalāda</s> with <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and the others.
At that time <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with dharma,
will approach the great sage <s>Pippalāda</s>, who is dwelling in <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>,
the treasure of austerity, and will ask him one question.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
How may there be health, lordly prosperity, intelligence fixed on dharma, and likewise a good path?
How may there be freedom from deformity, devotion to <s>Śiva</s>, or the state of being a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>?
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Hear, O <s>Brahmā</s>, this answer of wise <s>Pippalāda</s>,
which that righteous one will speak to the son of <s>Dharma</s>.
<s>Pippalāda</s> said:

children.text: sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā bhadra idānīṃ kathayāmi te
children.translated_text: You have asked well, noble one; now I shall tell you.
This is called the Aṅgāra-vrata, and he will declare it to the king.
Here too they cite this ancient history:
the dialogue of <s>Virocana</s> and wise <s>Bhārgava</s>.
Seeing the son of <s>Prahlāda</s>, sixteen years old,
incomparable in beauty and splendor, the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s> laughed.

children.text: sādhu sādhu mahābāho virocana śivaṃ tava
children.translated_text: 'Well done, well done, mighty-armed <s>Virocana</s>; may there be welfare for you.'
The slayer of the gods then asked him about that laugh of his:
'O <s>Brahman</s>, why did you suddenly laugh like this?
You said to me in this way, "Well done, well done"; tell me why.'
To him, who spoke thus, <s>Śukra</s>, best of speakers, said:
'I laughed from wonder at the greatness of the vow.
Long ago, when the trident-bearing one was enraged for the destruction of <s>Dakṣa</s>,
a drop of sweat born from the forehead of that terrible-faced one appeared.
Breaking through the seven netherworlds, it burned the seven oceans.
With many mouths and eyes, terrifying like blazing fire,
and furnished with countless hands and feet, he became famed as <s>Vīrabhadra</s>.
Having carried out the destruction of the sacrifice, he arose again on the surface of the earth,
and, again burning the three worlds, he was restrained by <s>Śiva</s>:
"You have accomplished the destruction of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice, O <s>Vīrabhadra</s>.
Now enough of this act of burning the worlds.
Become the foremost of the planets, the giver of peace to all.
People will look toward you, perform worship, and receive my boons.
You will become known as <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, O son of the earth,
and your form in the world of the gods will be without equal.

children.text: ye ca tvāṃ pūjayiṣyanti caturthyāṃ tvaddine narāḥ
children.translated_text: Those men who worship you on the fourth lunar day, on your day,
will have endless beauty, health, and prosperity."
Thus addressed, he who could assume any form became pacified at that time.
Born in that very moment, O king, he then attained the status of a planet.
Once you saw his excellent worship, offerings of arghya and the rest,
being performed by a Śūdra, while you were standing nearby.
By that you have been born beautiful, upholder of the family of the enemies of the gods,
and a manifold lovely radiance has arisen in you, because your brilliance spreads far.
Therefore the gods and Dānavas call you <s>Virocana</s>.
Seeing such beauty and prosperity in you from the sight
of the vow being performed by a Śūdra, I was astonished.
For that reason I said, "Well done, well done! Ah, the greatness is supreme.
Even one who sees it gains beauty and prosperity; how much more one who performs it!"
Because, through devotion to the son of the earth, the gift of cows and the like, even though disparaged,

children.text: ālokitaṃ tena surārigarbhe sambhūtireṣā tava daitya jātā ||
