children.translated_text: was seen by you, this birth of yours has arisen in the womb of the enemy of the gods, O Daitya.'
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Then, having heard that statement of the great-souled <s>Bhārgava</s>,
the heroic son of <s>Prahlāda</s>, astonished, asked again:
<s>Virocana</s> said:
Blessed sir, I wish to hear that vow properly and in truth.

children.text: dīyamānaṃ tu yaddānaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ bhavāntare ||
children.translated_text: Please tell me properly the greatness and the rule of that gift which I saw being given by me in a former existence.
You ought to describe its greatness and its procedure just as they are.

children.text: iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā punaḥ provāca vistarāt ||
children.translated_text: Having heard those words, he again spoke at length.
<s>Śukra</s> said:
O <s>Dānava</s>, when the fourth lunar day falls on a Tuesday,
then, adorned with ruby, one should perform a bath with clay.
Reciting the mantra beginning 'Agnir mūrdhā divaḥ,' he remains facing north.
But a śūdra, silently remembering <s>Bhauma</s>, remains without enjoyments.
Likewise, when the sun has set, he should smear the courtyard with cow-dung,
and all around with flower garlands and unbroken grains.
Having worshipped, he should draw an eight-petalled lotus with saffron.
If there is no saffron, red sandalwood is accepted.
Four jars are to be made, furnished with edible foods and cooked dishes,
together with red śāli rice and rubies.
Placing them in the four corners, and also various fruits,
he should offer all perfumes, garlands, and the rest in the same way.

children.text: suvarṇaśṛṅgīṃ kapilāmathārcya raupyaiḥ suraiḥ kāṃsyadohāṃ savatsām
children.translated_text: Then, having worshipped a tawny cow with golden horns, silver hoofs, a bronze milking vessel, and her calf,
a strong red bull, very gentle, and seven kinds of grain together with garments,
and likewise a golden man the size of a thumb, with very long arms,

children.text: caturbhujaṃ hemamaye niviṣṭaṃ pātre guḍasyopari sarpiyukte ||
children.translated_text: four-armed, placed in a golden vessel on top of jaggery mixed with ghee,
all this should be given to a worthy twice-born man, self-controlled, endowed with conduct and lineage, for the sake of all sacrifices,

children.text: dātavyametatsakalaṃ dvijāya kuṭumbine naiva tu dāmbhikāya
children.translated_text: to a householder Brahmin, not to a hypocrite.
With devotion and joined palms he should present it to an excellent Brahmin, first uttering the mantra:
O <s>Bhūmiputra</s>, greatly fortunate one, sweat-born son of <s>Pinākin</s>,

children.text: rūpārthī tvāṃ prapanno'haṃ gṛhāṇārghyaṃ namo'stu te ||
children.translated_text: desiring beauty, I have taken refuge in you; receive this <s>arghya</s> (honor-offering). Homage to you.
Having given the <s>arghya</s> with this mantra, using water scented with red sandalwood,
he should then worship the excellent Brahmin with red garlands, garments, and the like.
With that same mantra he should give an image of <s>Bhauma</s> together with a pair of cows,
and according to his ability he should give a bed furnished with all its accessories.
Whatever is most desired in the world, and whatever is dear to him in his house,
that very thing should be given to a virtuous man by one who wishes it to become inexhaustible.
Then, having circumambulated and dismissed the foremost Brahmin,
he should eat at night food without alkali or salt, mixed with ghee.
Now I shall tell you the merit of the one who devoutly performs this <s>Aṅgāraka</s> eightfold rite,

children.text: caturo vātha vā tasya yatpuṇyaṃ tadvadāmi te ||
children.translated_text: or four such rites.
In birth after birth he is endowed with beauty and good fortune.

children.text: viṣṇau vātha śive bhaktaḥ saptadvīpādhipo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Devoted either to <s>Viṣṇu</s> or to <s>Śiva</s>, he becomes lord of the seven continents.
For seven thousand kalpas he is honored in the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
Therefore you too, O lord of <s>Daityas</s>, should practice this vow.
<s>Pippalāda</s> said:

children.text: ityevamuktvā bhṛgunandano'pi jagāma daityaśca cakāra sarvam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s> departed, and the <s>Daitya</s> did everything.

children.text: tvaṃ cāpi rājankuru sarvametadyato'kṣayaṃ vedavido vadanti ||
children.translated_text: You too, O king, should perform all this, since those who know the Veda say that it is inexhaustible.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:

children.text: tatheti sampūjya sa pippalādaṃ vākyaṃ cakārādbhutavīryakarmā
children.translated_text: Saying 'So be it,' he honored <s>Pippalāda</s>; the man of wondrous valor and deeds carried out his instruction.

children.text: śṛṇoti yaścainam ananyacetās tasyāpi siddhiṃ bhagavānvidhatte ||
children.translated_text: And for one who hears this with undivided mind, the blessed Lord grants success.
<s>Pippalāda</s> said:
Now then, O king, listen to the rite for appeasing <s>Śukra</s>, on every Friday,
at the beginning and end of a journey, and here also at the rising of <s>Śukra</s>.
In a silver or golden vessel, or again in a bronze vessel,
filled with white rice and furnished with white flowers and garments,
having placed a silver image of <s>Śukra</s>, pure and accompanied by pearls,
he should offer all that to a singer of the <s>Sāman</s> with this mantra:
Homage to you, lord of all worlds; homage to you, descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.
O <s>Kavi</s>, for the accomplishment of every aim, receive this <s>arghya</s>. Homage to you.
Performing this at his rising, and at the start of journeys, O <s>Bhārata</s>,
one obtains all desires and is honored in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: yāvacchukrasya na hṛtā pūjā sā mālyakaiḥ śubhaiḥ
children.translated_text: So long as the worship of <s>Śukra</s> with auspicious garlands has not been completed,
with vaṭakas, pūrikās, wheat, and chickpeas too,
so long should he not eat food, for the sake of accomplishing the three aims of desire and wealth.
In the same way, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, I shall explain the worship of <s>Vācaspati</s>.
In a golden vessel he should place a golden image of the priest of the gods,
furnished with yellow flowers and garments; then, after bathing with mustard seeds,
with a mixture of palāśa and aśvattha and with water of the five products of the cow,
clothed in yellow garments and anointed with yellow unguent, he should cause an oblation of ghee to be offered.

children.text: praṇamya ca gavā sārdhaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: After bowing, he should present it, together with a cow, to a Brahmin.
Homage to you, lord of the descendants of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, lord of speech, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
To those afflicted by cruel planets you are like nectar; homage, homage to you.
At a saṃkrānti, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, on journeys, and on occasions of prosperity,
one who performs the worship of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> enjoys all desires.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Blessed Lord, maker of the crossing over the ocean of worldly existence,
teach some vow that grants heaven, health, and happiness.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
I shall explain the solar dharma called <s>Kalyāṇasaptamī</s>,
and likewise <s>Viśokasaptamī</s>, rich in fruit and destructive of sin,
the meritorious <s>Śarkarāsaptamī</s>, and likewise <s>Kamalasaptamī</s>,
and similarly <s>Mandārasaptamī</s> and the auspicious <s>Śubhasaptamī</s>.
All are said to have endless fruits, and all are honored by gods and seers.
I shall tell the rite for these, duly and in sequence.
When, on the bright seventh lunar day, it is the day of the Sun,

children.text: sā tu kalyāṇinī nāma vijayā ca nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>Kalyāṇinī</s>, and is also declared to be <s>Vijayā</s>.
On that day one should perform the morning bath with cow's milk.
Then, dressed in white garments, he should fashion a lotus with unbroken grains of rice.
Facing east, he should make it eight-petaled, and likewise with a round pericarp in the middle.
With flowers and unbroken grains he should install the lord of gods everywhere in due order.
In the eastern petal he should say, 'To <s>Tapana</s>,' and in the fire-corner, 'To <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>.'
In the southern petal, 'To <s>Divākara</s>,' and in the southwest, 'To <s>Vidhātṛ</s>.'
In the western petal, 'To <s>Varuṇa</s>,' and in the wind-corner, 'To <s>Bhāskara</s>.'
In the northern quarter, 'To <s>Vikartana</s>,' and in the eighth petal, 'To <s>Ravi</s>.'

children.text: ādāvante ca madhye ca namo'stu paramātmane
children.translated_text: At the beginning, at the end, and in the middle he should say, 'Homage to the supreme self.'
Having worshiped with these mantras, each made clear with a concluding salutation,
with white garments, fruits, foods, incense, garlands, and unguents,
he should worship on the altar with devotion, and with jaggery and salt.
Then, with the vyāhṛti-mantra, he should dismiss the foremost Brahmins.
According to his ability, he should honor them with devotion, with jaggery, milk, ghee, and the like.
He should present a vessel of sesame and gold to a Brahmin.
Having thus kept the rule and slept, a man should rise in the morning.
After bathing and reciting prayers, he should eat ghee-rice pudding together with Brahmins.
Then to a knower of the Veda, one free from the hypocritical 'cat-vow,'
he should present a vessel of ghee with gold, together with a water-pot.
May the blessed <s>Divākara</s>, the supreme self, be pleased by this.

children.text: anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi vrataṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: By this procedure he should observe the whole vow month after month.
Then, in the thirteenth month, he should give thirteen cows,
milk-giving cows adorned with garments and ornaments and with golden mouths.
Or, if he lacks wealth, he may give even one, without grudging.
He should not act deceitfully with his wealth, for through delusion one falls downward.
Whoever performs <s>Kalyāṇasaptamī</s> by this procedure
is freed from all sins and is honored in the world of the Sun.
Long life, health, and endless prosperity arise for him here.
It always removes all sin, is worshiped by all deities,
and always pacifies every evil: such is <s>Kalyāṇasaptamī</s>.
Whoever here hears or recites this <s>Kalyāṇasaptamī</s>,
which gives endless fruit, is released from all sins.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
In the same way, O foremost sage, I shall tell of <s>Viśokasaptamī</s>,
by fasting on which a man never experiences sorrow here.

children.text: māghe kṛṣṇatilaiḥ snātvā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vai śuklapakṣataḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Māgha</s>, on the sixth day of the bright fortnight, after bathing with black sesame seeds,
having taken a meal of kṛsara and first cleaned his teeth,
he should undertake the vow of fasting and remain celibate at night.
Then, rising at dawn, bathed, having recited prayers, and pure,

children.text: kṛtvā tu kāñcanaṃ padmamarkāyeti ca pūjayet
children.translated_text: he should make a golden lotus and worship it with the formula, 'To <s>Arka</s>.'
He should use red oleander and a pair of red garments.
'As the world is always free from sorrow through you alone, O <s>Āditya</s>,

children.text: tathā viśokatā me'stu tvadbhaktiḥ pratijanma ca ||
children.translated_text: so may freedom from sorrow be mine, and devotion to you in every birth.'

children.text: evaṃ sampūjya ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu bhaktyā sampūjayeddvijān
children.translated_text: Having worshiped in this way on the sixth day, he should devoutly honor the Brahmins.
After sleeping, sipping cow urine, rising, and completing his daily rites,
he should honor the Brahmins with food, together with a vessel of jaggery.
He should present that pair of garments and the lotus to a Brahmin.
On the seventh day, keeping silence, he should eat food without oil and salt.
Then one who desires prosperity should listen to a <s>Purāṇa</s>.
By this procedure he should do the whole rite in both fortnights
until the seventh day of the bright fortnight of <s>Māgha</s> comes again.
At the end of the vow he should give a water-jar furnished with a golden lotus.
He should give a bed with its accessories, and a tawny milk-giving cow.
Whoever, free from deceit over wealth,
performs <s>Viśokasaptamī</s> by this procedure goes to the highest state.
For a hundred crores and more of thousands of births,
he does not encounter sorrow, and is free from disease and misfortune.

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ prārthayate kāmaṃ taṃ tamāpnoti puṣkalam
children.translated_text: Whatever desire he asks for, that very desire he obtains in abundance.

children.text: niṣkāmaḥ kurute yastu sa paraṃ brahma gacchati ||
children.translated_text: But one who performs it without desire goes to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
Whoever recites or even hears the seventh-day vow called <s>Viśokā</s>
also obtains the world of <s>Indra</s> and is never born unhappy.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
I shall also teach another one, named <s>Phalasaptamī</s>,
by fasting on which a man, freed from sin, becomes a sharer in heaven.
In the auspicious month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, on the seventh day, one restrained in his vow,
should fast on that day and then have a golden lotus made.
He should give it, together with sugar, to a Brahmin who has a household.
The knower of dharma should make a golden <s>Ravi</s> of one pala in weight,
and give it at the two proper times, saying, 'May <s>Bhānu</s> be pleased with me.'
On the eighth day, after devoutly honoring the Brahmins, he should give a meal of milk.
He should perform the rite with fruit until the seventh day in the dark fortnight.
He should fast on that day too, according to rule, by this same sequence,
and likewise give a golden fruit furnished with a golden lotus,
together with a vessel of sugar and accompanied by garments and garlands.
For a year, by that same procedure, he should observe both seventh-day vows.
Having given the offerings successively, he should utter the solar mantra:

children.text: bhānurarko ravirbrahmā sūryaḥ śakro hariḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānu</s>, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Ravi</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Hari</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>.
May glorious <s>Vibhāvasu</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s> be pleased.
And on the seventh day of each month he should recite each name in turn.
Doing this, he should observe the renunciation of fruits in each fortnight.
At the end of the vow he should honor a Brahmin couple with garments and ornaments.
He should give a jar of sugar furnished with golden lotus petals.

children.text: yathā na viphalāḥ kāmāstvadbhaktānāṃ sadā rave
children.translated_text: As the wishes of your devotees, O <s>Ravi</s>, are never fruitless,
so may the attainment of endless fruit be mine through seven births.
Whoever performs this <s>Phalasaptamī</s>, which grants endless fruit,
with his self purified from every sin, is honored in the world of <s>Sūrya</s>.
Whatever act, such as drinking liquor, has been done here or in the next world,
all that comes to destruction for one who performs <s>Phalasaptamī</s>.
The man who constantly performs this seventh-day vow is free from disease,
and he delivers twenty-one men, past and future.
Whoever hears it or recites it also becomes a sharer in good fortune.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
I shall describe <s>Śarkarāsaptamī</s>, likewise destructive of sin,
by which endless life, health, and sovereignty arise.
On the seventh day of the bright fortnight of <s>Mādhava</s>, keeping his vow under restraint,
after bathing in the morning with white sesame seeds, wearing white garlands and unguents,
he should draw a lotus with its pericarp on a level altar with saffron.
There he should offer fragrance and incense, saying, 'Homage to <s>Savitṛ</s>.'
He should set down a water-jar together with a vessel of sugar.
Having adorned it with white garments, white garlands, and unguents,
and joined it with gold, he should worship it with this mantra:
Since you are composed of all the Vedas and are proclaimed as the speaker of the Veda,
and you are the very nectar of all, therefore grant me peace.
Then, having drunk <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow), he should sleep on the ground beside it.
He remains there remembering the solar hymn and listening to the Purāṇa.
When the day and night have passed, on the eighth day, after performing his daily rites,
he should present all that, in the same way, to a learned Brahmin.
According to his ability he should feed Brahmins with sugar, ghee, and milk-rice.
Then he himself should eat without oil or salt, while restrained in speech.

children.text: anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi samācaret
children.translated_text: By this procedure he should perform the whole rite month after month.
At the end of the year he should give a bed together with a jar of sugar,
equipped with all accessories, and likewise a milk-giving cow.
If he has the means, he should give a house furnished with every accessory.
Having made it with a thousand niṣkas, or with a hundred, he should give it,
or with ten niṣkas, or even with half of that, according to his ability.
A golden horse should be given, with recitation of the mantra as before.
He should not act deceitfully with his wealth; doing so, he incurs fault.
When <s>Sūrya</s> was drinking nectar, drops of nectar from his mouth
fell upon the earth; these are remembered as rice, mung beans, and sugarcane.
Sugar is superior among these, the essence of sugarcane and possessing the nature of nectar.
It is dear to <s>Ravi</s>; therefore sugar is holy in offerings to gods and ancestors.
This <s>Śarkarāsaptamī</s> grants the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
It pacifies every evil and increases sons and grandsons.

children.text: yaḥ kuryātparayā bhaktyā sa vai sadgatimāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: Whoever performs it with supreme devotion indeed obtains a good destiny.

children.text: kalpamekaṃ vasetsvarge tato yāti paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: He dwells in heaven for one kalpa; thereafter he goes to the supreme state.

children.text: idamanaghaṃ śṛṇoti yaḥ smaredvā paripaṭhatīha divākarasya loke
children.translated_text: Whoever hears this sinless rite, remembers it, or recites it here in the world of <s>Divākara</s>,
and whoever gives his mind to it, he too is worshiped by the gods with garlands from immortal women.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
After this I shall likewise proclaim <s>Kamalasaptamī</s>,
by the mere recitation of whose name <s>Divākara</s> is pleased here.
On the pure seventh day of spring, after bathing with white mustard seeds,

children.text: tilapātre ca sauvarṇe vidhāya kamalaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: having placed an auspicious lotus in a golden vessel filled with sesame,
and having covered it with a pair of garments, he should worship it with scents and flowers:
'Homage to the lotus-handed one; homage to you, sustainer of the universe.
Homage to you, O <s>Prabhākara</s>; homage be to you.'
Then, at the time of the two daily rites, together with a water-jar,
he should give it away after worshiping it with garments, garlands, and ornaments.
And according to his ability he should give a tawny cow, adorning it according to rule.
When the day and night have passed, on the eighth day he should feed twice-born men.
Then he himself should eat according to his ability, avoiding meat and oil.

children.text: anena vidhinā śuklasaptamyāṃ māsi māsi ca
children.translated_text: By this procedure, on the bright seventh day, month after month,
he should perform the whole rite with devotion, free from deceit in wealth.
At the end of the vow he should give a bed furnished with a golden lotus.

children.text: gāṃ ca dadyātsvaśaktyā tu suvarṇāḍhyāṃ payasvinīm ||
children.translated_text: And according to his ability he should give a milk-giving cow rich with gold.
He should give vessels, seats, lamps, and other desired accessories.
Whoever performs <s>Kamalasaptamī</s> by this procedure
attains endless prosperity and is honored in the world of <s>Sūrya</s>.
In kalpa after kalpa, after going separately to the seven worlds,
surrounded by apsarases, he then goes to the highest destiny.

children.text: yaḥ paśyatīdaṃ śṛṇuyācca martyaḥ paṭhecca bhaktyātha matiṃ dadāti
children.translated_text: The mortal who sees this, hears it, recites it with devotion, or gives his mind to it,
having gained firm prosperity here, becomes a sharer in the world of Gandharvas and Vidyādharas.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Now then I shall proclaim the lovely vow that destroys all sins,
that grants all desires, called <s>Mandārasaptamī</s>.
On the fifth day of the dark fortnight of <s>Māgha</s>, a wise man should eat lightly.
Then, after using a tooth-stick, he should fast on the sixth day.
But after honoring the Brahmins, he should partake of the <s>mandāra</s> at night.

children.text: tataḥ prabhāta utthāya kṛtvā snānaṃ punardvijān ||
children.translated_text: Then, rising at dawn and bathing, he should again honor the twice-born.
He should feed them according to his ability, having made eight <s>mandāra</s> flowers,
and likewise a beautiful golden figure of a man holding a lotus.
Having made an eight-petalled lotus of black sesame seeds in a copper vessel,
with golden <s>mandāra</s> flowers he should worship on the eastern side with the words, 'To <s>Bhāskara</s>.'
Likewise, with obeisance, on the southeastern petal he should worship with the words, 'To <s>Sūrya</s>.'
In the south likewise, 'To <s>Arka</s>,' and in the southwest, 'To <s>Aryaman</s>.'
In the west, 'To <s>Vedadhāman</s>,' and in the northwest, 'To <s>Caṇḍabhānu</s>.'
In the north he should worship with the words, 'To <s>Pūṣan</s>,' and after that, 'To <s>Ānanda</s>.'

children.text: karṇikāyāṃ ca puruṣaṃ sarvātmana iti nyaset
children.translated_text: In the pericarp he should place the figure of the man with the words, 'To <s>Sarvātman</s>.'
Having wrapped it in white cloths, with foods, garlands, fruits, and the like,
after worshiping all that in this way, he should then give it to one who knows the Veda.
The householder, restrained in speech and facing east, should eat food without oil and salt.

children.text: anena vidhinā sarvaṃ saptamyāṃ māsi māsi ca
children.translated_text: By this rule, on every <s>saptamī</s> in each month,
he should perform the observance for a year, free from deceit about his wealth.
At the end of the vow, placing this very thing on top of a water jar,
one who desires prosperity should give it together with cows, according to his means.
Homage to the lord of the <s>mandāra</s>, and to the one whose abode is the <s>mandāra</s>.
O <s>Ravi</s>, carry us across the ocean of fear that is worldly existence.
Whoever performs this <s>Mandārasaptamī</s> by this rule,

children.text: vipāpmā sa sukhī martyaḥ kalpaṃ ca divi modate ||
children.translated_text: that sinless, happy mortal rejoices in heaven for a kalpa.
Taking hold of this lamp against the terrifying darkness formed by masses of sin,
a man, while moving through worldly existence, obtains all his aims.
This <s>Mandārasaptamī</s> grants the fruit of desired objects.
Whoever recites it or even hears it is released from all sins.
The blessed Lord said:
Now I shall also declare another excellent and auspicious <s>Śubhasaptamī</s>,
by fasting for which a man is freed from disease, grief, and suffering.
In the meritorious month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>, having bathed, performed recitation, and become pure,
then, after causing Brahmins to recite, he should begin the <s>Śubhasaptamī</s>.
He should worship with devotion, using fragrances, garlands, and unguents.
I bow to you, born from <s>Sūrya</s>, abode of all the worlds,
to you whose body is auspicious and blessed, for the accomplishment of all aims.
Then, having prepared a prastha measure of sesame together with a copper vessel,
and likewise a golden bull, supplied with fragrance, garlands, and jaggery,
with various fruits, foods, ghee, and milk-rice,
he should give them at the two appointed times, saying, 'May <s>Aryaman</s> be pleased.'
After drinking <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow), he should sleep on the ground, free from envy.
Then, when morning has come, he should worship the Brahmins with devotion.

children.text: anena vidhinā dadyānmāsi māsi sadā naraḥ
children.translated_text: By this rule a man should always give, month after month,
a golden bull with a garment, and likewise a cow made of gold.
At the end of the year he should give a bed, furnished with sugarcane stalks and jaggery,
with a pillow and resting place, and supplied with vessels and a seat,
as well as a copper vessel, a prastha measure of sesame, and a golden bull.
He should give all of it to one who knows the Veda, saying, 'May <s>Viśvātman</s> be pleased.'
The wise man who performs the <s>Śubhasaptamī</s> by this rule
will have abundant prosperity and fame in birth after birth.
Honored by hosts of <s>Apsarases</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s> in the abode of the gods,
he dwells there as a lord of hosts until the dissolution of beings.
And when he descends at the beginning of a kalpa, he becomes lord of the seven continents.
For the destruction of a thousand killings of Brahmins and a hundred killings of embryos,
this holy <s>Śubhasaptamī</s>, when recited, is sufficient.
Whoever recites this, hears it for a moment, or even happens to see it being given,
that person too, his body here freed from all sin, attains leadership among the <s>Vidyādharas</s>.

children.text: yāvatsamāḥ sapta naraḥ karoti yaḥ saptamīṃ saptavidhānayuktām
children.translated_text: For as many as seven years as a man performs the <s>saptamī</s> endowed with sevenfold observance,

children.text: sa saptalokādhipatiḥ krameṇa bhūtvā padaṃ yāti paraṃ murāreḥ ||
children.translated_text: after becoming lord of the seven worlds in succession, he goes to the supreme abode of <s>Murāri</s>.
<s>Manu</s> said:
What fast or vow is sufficient to lift one out of the mass of grief caused by separation from what is desired,
to bring forth prosperity on this earth, and to destroy a man's fear of worldly existence?
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: paripṛṣṭamidaṃ jagatpriyaṃ te vibudhānāmapi durlabhaṃ mahattvāt
children.translated_text: This matter you have asked is dear to the world and, because of its greatness, hard even for the gods to obtain.
Nevertheless, since you are devoted, I shall teach you the vow that is secret among <s>Indra</s>, the demons, and human beings.
In the meritorious month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>, there is the vow of <s>Viśokadvādaśī</s>.
On the tenth day the learned man should begin it by rule, eating lightly.
Facing north or facing east, after first cleaning his teeth,
on the eleventh day he should fast, and after worshiping <s>Keśava</s>
or after duly worshiping <s>Śrī</s>, he should say, 'I shall eat on the following day.'
Having slept while observing this rule, the man should rise in the morning.
He should bathe with all herbs and with water mixed with <s>pañcagavya</s>.
Wearing white garlands and garments, he should worship <s>Śrīśa</s> with lotuses.

children.text: viśokāya namaḥ pādau jaṅghe ca varadāya vai
children.translated_text: He should worship the feet with 'Homage to <s>Viśoka</s>,' and the shanks with 'Homage to the boon-giver.'
Likewise the knees with 'Homage to <s>Śrīśa</s>,' and the thighs with 'Homage to the one who lies on the waters.'

children.text: kandarpāya namo guhyaṃ mādhavāya namaḥ kaṭim
children.translated_text: He should worship the private parts with 'Homage to <s>Kandarpa</s>,' and the waist with 'Homage to <s>Mādhava</s>.'
The belly with 'Homage to <s>Dāmodara</s>,' and the sides with 'Homage to <s>Vipula</s>.'

children.text: nābhiṃ ca padmanābhāya hṛdayaṃ manmathāya vai
children.translated_text: The navel with 'Homage to <s>Padmanābha</s>,' and the heart with 'Homage to <s>Manmatha</s>.'
The chest of the mighty one with 'Homage to <s>Śrīdhara</s>,' and the hands with 'Homage to <s>Madhujit</s>.'

children.text: cakriṇe vāmabāhuṃ ca dakṣiṇaṃ gadine namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the discus-bearer for the left arm, and homage to the mace-bearer for the right.
Homage to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> for the throat, and to him whose mouth is the sacrifice for the mouth.
For the nose, homage to the abode of freedom from sorrow; and for the two eyes, to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
For the forehead, one should say, 'to <s>Vāmana</s>'; and again for the two brows, to <s>Hari</s>.
For the locks, one should say, 'to <s>Mādhava</s>'; for the crown, to the one of universal form.
In the same way one should worship the head, saying, 'Homage to the self of all.'
Having thus worshipped <s>Govinda</s> with fruits, garlands, and unguents,
then he should make a maṇḍala and joyfully prepare a ritual altar.
It should be square on all sides, a cubit in measure, sloping toward the north,
smooth and pleasing, and surrounded all around by three embankments.
The embankments should be one finger high, and their breadth should be two fingers.
Above the ritual altar there should be a wall eight fingers high.
On a winnowing basket, with river sand, he should place an image of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
Having set the winnowing basket on the altar, the wise man should worship it as <s>Lakṣmī</s>.

children.text: namo devyai namaḥ śāntyai namo lakṣmyai namaḥ śriyai
children.translated_text: Homage to the goddess; homage to peace; homage to <s>Lakṣmī</s>; homage to <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: namaḥ puṣṭyai namastuṣṭyai vṛṣṭyai hṛṣṭyai namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to nourishment; homage to satisfaction; repeated homage to rain and gladness.
May <s>Viśokā</s>, free from sorrow, exist for the destruction of sorrow; may <s>Viśokā</s> be a giver of boons to me.
May <s>Viśokā</s> also exist for prosperity; may <s>Viśokā</s> exist for every success.
Then he should wrap the winnowing basket in white garments and worship it with fruits,
with various kinds of cloths, in the same way, and with a golden lotus.
During all the nights the wise man should drink water sanctified with darbha grass.
Then he should arrange singing, dancing, and the like for the whole night.
When three watches have passed, the man, after sleeping, should rise
and, approaching pairs of Brahmins, worship them then.
According to his ability, three pairs or one pair should be worshipped with garments, garlands, and unguents.
Those lying on a bed are to be honored, with the words: 'Homage to the one who lies upon the waters.'
Then, after a night vigil has been kept with song and instrumental music,

children.text: prabhāte ca tataḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā dāmpatyamarcayet ||
children.translated_text: at dawn, having bathed, he should worship the married couple.
Free from deceit about his wealth, he should feed them according to his ability.
Having eaten and listened to the Purāṇas, he should pass that day.

children.text: anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi samācaret
children.translated_text: By this procedure he should perform everything month after month.
At the end of the vow he should give a bed accompanied by a <s>guḍadhenu</s> (cow made of jaggery),
auspicious, with pillows and rest-supports, together with a cover and spread.

children.text: yathā na lakṣmīrdeveśa tvāṃ parityajya gacchati
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Lakṣmī</s>, O lord of gods, does not abandon you and go away,
so may beauty, health, and freedom from sorrow always be mine.

children.text: yathā devena rahitā na lakṣmīrjāyate kvacit
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Lakṣmī</s> never exists anywhere apart from the god,

children.text: tathā viśokatā me'stu bhaktiragryā ca keśave ||
children.translated_text: so may freedom from sorrow be mine, and foremost devotion to <s>Keśava</s>.
With this mantra, the bed accompanied by the <s>guḍadhenu</s>

children.text: śūrpaṃ ca lakṣmyā sahitaṃ dātavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā ||
children.translated_text: and the winnowing basket together with <s>Lakṣmī</s> should be given by one who desires prosperity.
Blue lotus, oleander, bāṇa, unfading saffron,
ketakī, sinduvāra, jasmine, fragrant pāṭalā,
kadamba, kubjaka, and jāti are always recommended.
<s>Manu</s> said:
Explain to me, O lord of the world, the rule for the <s>guḍadhenu</s>.
Tell here what form it has and with what mantra it should be given.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
I shall now declare the form and the fruit here of the rule for the <s>guḍadhenu</s>,
which destroys all sin.
He should place on the ground a black antelope skin four hastas long, with its neck toward the east,
on ground smeared with cow dung, after spreading darbha grass everywhere.
In the same way he should arrange a small antelope skin and also fashion the calf.
He should fashion the cow facing east, with its feet to the north, together with its calf.
The best <s>guḍadhenu</s> should always be four bhāras in weight.

children.text: vatsaṃ bhāreṇa kurvīta dvābhyāṃ vai madhyamā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: He should make the calf one bhāra; the middle grade is remembered as being two bhāras.
For that, the calf should be half a bhāra; but the lowest grade is one bhāraka.
For that, the calf should be one quarter, according to the wealth of the household.
The cow and calf should have mouths of ghee and be covered with fine white cloth.
They should have ears of oyster shell, feet of sugarcane, and eyes of pure pearls.
They should have heads marked with white thread and blankets made of white wool.
Their cheeks and backs should be of copper, and their hair of white chowries.
They should be provided with a pair of coral brows, and both should have breasts of fresh butter.
They should have tails of linen, bronze milking vessels, and pupils of sapphire.
They should be adorned with golden horns and furnished with silver hooves.
They should be joined with various fruits, and their noses should be boxes of fragrance.
Having fashioned the two in this way, he should then worship them with incense and lamps.

children.text: yā lakṣmīḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yā ca deveṣvavasthitā
children.translated_text: May that <s>Lakṣmī</s> who belongs to all beings, and who abides among the gods,

children.text: dhenurūpeṇa sā devī mama śāntiṃ prayacchatu ||
children.translated_text: as a goddess in the form of a cow, grant me peace.

children.text: dehasthā yā ca rudrāṇī śaṃkarasya sadā priyā
children.translated_text: May that <s>Rudrāṇī</s> who abides in the body and is always dear to <s>Śaṃkara</s>,

children.text: dhenurūpeṇa sā devī mama pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: as a goddess in the form of a cow, remove my sin.

children.text: viṣṇorvakṣasi yā lakṣmīḥ svāhā yā ca vibhāvasoḥ
children.translated_text: May that <s>Lakṣmī</s> who is on <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s breast, and <s>Svāhā</s> who belongs to <s>Vibhāvasu</s>,
and she who is the power of moon, sun, and <s>Śakra</s>, be in cow-form for my prosperity.
May the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of the four-faced one, and the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of the giver of wealth,
the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of the guardians of the worlds, be a boon-giving cow for me.

children.text: svadhā yā pitṛmukhyāṇāṃ svāhā yajñabhujāṃ ca yā
children.translated_text: May she who is <s>Svadhā</s> among the chief ancestors, and <s>Svāhā</s> among the eaters of sacrifice,
the cow that removes all sin, therefore grant me peace.
Having addressed that cow in this way, he should present it to a Brahmin.
This rule is recited for all cows.
Those ten cows that destroy sin are recited;

children.text: tāsāṃ svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi nāmāni ca narādhipa ||
children.translated_text: I shall describe their forms and names, O king.
The first should be the <s>guḍadhenu</s> (jaggery-cow), and another likewise the <s>ghṛtadhenu</s> (ghee-cow).
The third is the <s>tiladhenu</s> (sesame-cow), and the fourth is called the water-cow.
The milk-cow is well known, and another likewise is the honey-cow.
The seventh is the sugar-cow, and the eighth likewise the curd-cow.
The ninth is the juice-cow, and the tenth should be according to its own proper form.
For liquid-cows there should be pots; for the others, heaps.
Some Bhānavas here also desire a gold-cow.
Other great seers desire one made with fresh butter and jewels.
Such is this ordinance; those same items are remembered as the accessories.
Joined with mantra and invocation, always on each sacred occasion,
they should be given according to one's faith, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
In connection with the jaggery-cow, all of them have been stated by me to that extent.
All are auspicious, giving the fruit of every sacrifice and removing all sins.
Since the <s>Viśokadvādaśī</s> vow is the highest among vows,
the jaggery-cow is praised here as part of it.
At an ayana, at an auspicious equinox, at a vyatīpāta, or again
on eclipse and other sacred days, the jaggery-cow and the rest should be given.
This <s>Viśokadvādaśī</s> is meritorious, auspicious, and removing sin;

children.text: yāmupoṣya naro yāti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: having fasted on it, a man goes to that supreme station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
And in this world he obtains good fortune, long life, and health;
at death, remembering <s>Hari</s>, he reaches the city of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
For nine thousand arbudas and eighteen more, O knower of <s>dharma</s>,
no grief, pain, or misfortune arises for him, O king.

children.text: nārī vā kurute yā tu viśokadvādaśīvratam
children.translated_text: And whatever woman performs the <s>Viśokadvādaśī</s> vow,
though always devoted to dancing and singing, she too obtains that fruit.
Therefore continual singing, dancing, and instrumental music should be performed before <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: kartavyaṃ bhūtikāmena bhaktyā tu parayā nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: by one who desires prosperity, with highest devotion, O king.

children.text: iti paṭhati ya itthaṃ yaḥ śṛṇotīha samyaṅmadhumuranarakārer arcanaṃ yaśca paśyet
children.translated_text: Whoever reads thus, whoever here properly hears, and whoever sees the worship of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>, <s>Mura</s>, and <s>Naraka</s>,

children.text: matimāpa ca janānāṃ yo dadātīndraloke vasati sa vibudhaughaiḥ pūjyate kalpamekam ||
children.translated_text: and whoever gives understanding to people dwells in <s>Indraloka</s> and is honored by hosts of gods for one kalpa.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Blessed lord, I wish to hear the supreme greatness of giving,
which is imperishable in the next world and honored by hosts of divine seers.
<s>Umāpati</s> said:
I shall explain the gift of <s>Meru</s> in ten forms, O foremost sage,
by whose giving a man obtains worlds honored by the gods.
In the Purāṇas, in the Vedas, in sacrifices, and in temples,
one does not obtain here, through study or performance, the fruit that he obtains from that.
Therefore I shall explain the procedure for the mountains in order.
The first should be the grain-mountain, the second the salt-mountain.
The third is the jaggery-mountain, and the fourth the gold-mountain.
The fifth should be the sesame-mountain, and the sixth the cotton-mountain.
The seventh is the ghee-mountain, and the eighth likewise the jewel-mountain.
The ninth is of silver, and the tenth likewise is the sugar-mountain.
I shall explain their procedure properly and in sequence,
at an ayana, at an auspicious equinox, at a vyatīpāta, and at the end of a day,
on the third day of a bright fortnight, at an eclipse, and at the waning of the moon,
at wedding festivals and sacrifices, or again on the twelfth day,

children.text: śuklāyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ vā puṇyarkṣe vā vidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: or on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, or under an auspicious asterism, according to rule,
the grain-mountain and the others should be given by one who knows the śāstra.
At sacred fords, in temples, in a cowshed, or in the courtyard of a house,
he should devoutly have a square pavilion made, facing north,
sloping to the east and north, and likewise facing east, according to rule.
On ground smeared with cow dung, after spreading kuśa grass,
in its center he should make the mountain, furnished with supporting side-mountains.
Here the excellent mountain should be made with one thousand droṇas of grain;

children.text: madhyamaḥ pañcaśatikaḥ kaniṣṭhaḥ syāt tribhiḥ śataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the middle-sized one has five hundred, and the smallest should have three hundred.
The <s>Meru</s> in the middle should be made of great rice and furnished with three golden trees;
on the eastern side it should have pearls and diamonds, and on the southern side gomedaka and puṣparāga gems.
On the west it should have gārutmata and sapphire gems, and on the north vaidūrya and sarojarāga stones.
All around it should have pieces of sandalwood, coral, and creepers, and a floor of mother-of-pearl and stone.
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the blessed <s>Purāri</s>, and <s>Divākara</s> too should be golden there;
their placement on the summit should be arranged without stinginess, and again with many hosts of twice-born men.

children.text: catvāri śṛṅgāṇi ca rājatāni nitambabhāgeṣvapi rājataḥ syāt
children.translated_text: The four peaks should be silver, and the slopes should also be of silver;
its caves should be enclosed with sugarcane stalks, and there should be streams of ghee and water in the quarters.
In the east there should be white garments as rows of clouds, and yellow ones in the south;

children.text: vāsāṃsi paścādatha karburāṇi raktāni caivottarato ghanālī ||
children.translated_text: the garments in the west should be variegated, and red ones in the north as a bank of clouds.
Having installed in order eight silver world-protectors headed by <s>Mahendra</s>,

children.text: nānāphalālī ca samantataḥ syānmanoramaṃ mālyavilepanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: there should be rows of various fruits all around, and delightful garlands and unguents.

children.text: vitānakaṃ copari pañcavarṇam amlānapuṣpābharaṇaṃ sitaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Above there should be a five-colored canopy, and a white ornament of unfading flowers.
Having arranged thus the foremost mountain of the immortals, then the side-mountains of <s>Meru</s> in sequence,
he should establish them in the four directions at one-fourth the size, rich in flowers and unguents.
To the east, <s>Mandara</s> should be joined with rows of many fruits, made of barley and marked with golden bhadraka and kadamba trees.
He should fashion it shining with a golden <s>Kāma</s>, rich in flowers, garments, and unguents,

children.text: kṣīrāruṇodasarasātha vanena caivaṃ raupyeṇa śaktighaṭitena virājamānam ||
children.translated_text: and likewise with the milk and red-water lakes and with a forest, shining with silver and furnished with spears.
On the southern side <s>Gandhamādana</s> should be set up, made from a heap of wheat and joined with silver,

children.text: haimena yajñapatinā ghṛtamānasena vastraiśca rājatavanena ca saṃyutaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: with a golden lord of sacrifice, with a ghee-lake, and accompanied by garments and a silver forest.
Afterward he should fashion the sesame-mountain, with many fragrant flowers, golden pipal trees, and golden swans,
and likewise with a silver flower-forest, furnished with garments, and with lakes of curd and sugar-water in front.

children.text: saṃsthāpya taṃ vipulaśailamathottareṇa śailaṃ supārśvamapi māṣamayaṃ suvastram
children.translated_text: Having established that broad mountain, then to the north he should also make the mountain <s>Supārśva</s>, made of beans and well clothed.
With flowers and a golden banyan tree as its crest, he should fashion it shining with a golden cow.

children.text: mākṣīkabhadrasarasātha vanena tadvadraupyeṇa bhāsvaravatā ca yutaṃ vidhāya
children.translated_text: Likewise, having provided it with honey and auspicious lakes, with a forest, and with bright silver,
the homa should then be performed by four chief twice-born priests who know the Vedas and Purāṇas, are restrained, and are of blameless conduct and appearance.

children.text: pūrveṇa hastamitamatra vidhāya kuṇḍaṃ kāryastilairyavaghṛtena samitkuśaiśca
children.translated_text: On the eastern side a fire-pit of a cubit's measure should be made here; the rite is to be performed with sesame, barley, ghee, fuel-sticks, and kuśa grass.

children.text: rātrau ca jāgaramanuddhatagītatūryairāvāhanaṃ ca kathayāmi śiloccayānām ||
children.translated_text: At night there should be a vigil with modest songs and instruments; now I shall declare the invocation of the mountain-heaps.
O immortal mountain, you are the abode and treasure of all hosts of gods; quickly destroy what is hostile in our houses.

children.text: kṣemaṃ vidhatsva kuru śāntimanuttamāṃ naḥ sampūjitaḥ paramabhaktimatā mayā hi ||
children.translated_text: Grant us welfare, and bring us unsurpassed peace, for I have worshiped you with supreme devotion.
You yourself are the blessed Lord, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the Sun.
You are the eternal seed beyond the formed and the formless; therefore protect me.
Because you are the dwelling of the guardians of the worlds and of the universal form,
and of the <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, and <s>Vasus</s>, therefore grant me peace.
Because you are not empty of immortals, of divine women, and of <s>Śiva</s>,
therefore lift me out of the whole ocean of suffering and worldly existence.
Having worshiped that <s>Meru</s> in this way, he should worship <s>Mandara</s> as well:
Because, by reason of <s>Caitraratha</s> and <s>Bhadrāśva</s>,
you shine, O <s>Mandara</s>, quickly; therefore become a giver of satisfaction.
Because you are the crest-jewel in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, O <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
and possess the beauty of the forest of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, therefore may my fame be firm.
Because of <s>Ketumāla</s> and the <s>Vaibhrāja</s> forest,
you have a golden aśvattha as your crown; therefore may my nourishment be secure.
Because of the northern <s>Kurus</s> and the <s>Sāvitra</s> forest,
O <s>Supārśva</s>, you shine forever; therefore may there be protection of my prosperity.
Having addressed them all in this way, again at clear daybreak,
after bathing, he should give the excellent middle mountain to the guru.
He should give the surrounding mountains to the officiating priests in order, O sage.
He should also give twenty-four cows, or ten, O <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: nava sapta tathāṣṭau vā pañca dadyād aśaktimān ||
children.translated_text: or nine, seven, eight, or five, if he is unable.

children.text: ekāpi gurave deyā kapilā ca payasvinī
children.translated_text: Even one tawny, milk-giving cow should be given to the guru.
This same rule is remembered for all the mountains without exception.

children.text: ta eva pūjane mantrāsta evopaskarā matāḥ
children.translated_text: The same mantras are used in the worship, and the same accessories are prescribed
for the planets, the guardians of the worlds, and <s>Brahmā</s> and the others at all times.
For all the mountains, the homa is said to be performed with each one's own mantra.
One should always fast; for one who is unable, eating at night is allowed.
Hear in order, O <s>Nārada</s>, the procedure for all the mountains,

children.text: dānakāle ca ye mantrāḥ parvateṣu ca yatphalam ||
children.translated_text: and the mantras at the time of donation and the fruit that belongs to the mountains.

children.text: annaṃ brahma yataḥ proktamanne prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Food is declared to be <s>Brahman</s>, for lives are established in food.
Beings arise from food, and the world continues by food.
Food itself is <s>Lakṣmī</s>; food itself is <s>Janārdana</s>.
Therefore, in the form of a grain-mountain, protect me, O best of mountains.
Whoever by this rule gives a mountain made of grain
is honored in the world of the gods for a full hundred manvantaras and more.
In a splendid aerial car thronged with hosts of <s>Apsarases</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s>,
attended by them, he goes to the summit of heaven.
When <s>dharma</s> declines, he obtains royal sovereignty here; there is no doubt.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Now then I shall proclaim the excellent salt-mountain,
by the gift of which a man obtains worlds joined with <s>Śiva</s>.
An excellent salt-mountain should be made with sixteen droṇas;
a middling one is made with half of that, and the lowest is remembered as made with four.
A man lacking wealth should have one made according to his ability, but with more than a droṇa.
He should make the surrounding mountains separately with a fourth part.
He should perform the procedure as before, and always that of <s>Brahmā</s> and the others.
Likewise he should install all the golden guardians of the worlds.
Here too he should make the lakes and <s>Kāmadeva</s> and the others in the same way.
He should also keep a vigil; now learn the mantras for donation.
Since this salt savor arose from the lake of good fortune,
by virtue of making its gift, protect me, O best of mountains.
Because all the flavors of food are not strong without salt,

children.text: priyaṃ ca śivayornityaṃ tasmācchāntiṃ prayaccha me ||
children.translated_text: and because it is always dear to <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Umā</s>, therefore grant me peace.
Because, arisen from the body of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, it increases health,
therefore, in the form of a mountain, protect me from the ocean of worldly existence.
Whoever by this rule gives a salt-mountain

children.text: umāloke vasetkalpaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: dwells for a kalpa in the world of <s>Umā</s>, and afterward goes to the supreme goal.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
After this, I shall proclaim the excellent mountain of jaggery,
by the gift of which a man obtains heaven, honored by the gods.
The best is regarded as made with ten <s>bhāras</s>; the middling one with five.
The lowest should be with three <s>bhāras</s>; one of little wealth may make it with half of that.
Likewise the invitation, the worship, the golden tree, and the worship of the gods,
and likewise the supporting mountains, the lakes, and the forest deities,
the oblation, the night-vigil, and the installation of the <s>lokapālas</s> (world-protectors),
he should perform as in the case of the grain-mountain, and he should utter this mantra:
As among the gods this <s>Janārdana</s>, the soul of all, is foremost,
as the <s>Sāmaveda</s> is among the <s>Vedas</s>, and <s>Mahādeva</s> among yogins,
as the <s>praṇava</s> is among all mantras, and as <s>Pārvatī</s> is among women,
so sugarcane juice is always regarded as the foremost among juices.

children.text: mama tasmātparāṃ lakṣmīṃ guḍaparvata dehi vai
children.translated_text: Therefore, O mountain of jaggery, give me supreme prosperity.
Since you are the brother of the fortune-bestowing one, O mountain of jaggery,
and also the dwelling of <s>Pārvatī</s>, therefore grant me peace.
Whoever, by this rule, gives a mountain made of jaggery,
being honored by <s>Gandharvas</s>, is exalted in the world of <s>Gaurī</s>.
Then, at the end of a hundred kalpas, he becomes lord of the seven continents,
endowed with long life and health, and unconquered by enemies.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Now I shall describe the excellent golden mountain, remover of sin,
by whose gift a human being goes to the abode of <s>Vairiñca</s>.
The best is a thousand <s>palas</s>; the middling one is with five hundred.
The lowest is with half of that; similarly, even one of little wealth, according to ability,
should give more than a single <s>pala</s>, free from envy.
Everything should be arranged as for the grain-mountain, O best of sages,
and likewise he should assign the supporting mountains to the officiating priests.
Homage to you, seed of <s>Brahman</s>; homage to you, womb of <s>Brahman</s>.
Since you grant endless fruit, therefore protect me, O mountain-heap.
Since you are the offspring of fire, since you are holy, O lord of the world,
therefore, in the form of a golden mountain, protect me, O best of mountains.
Whoever, by this rule, gives a mountain of gold,
goes to the supreme <s>Brahmaloka</s>, which brings bliss.

children.text: tatra kalpaśataṃ tiṣṭhettato yāti parāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: There he remains for a hundred kalpas; after that he goes to the highest goal.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
After this, I shall duly proclaim the sesame mountain,
by whose gift a man goes to the eternal <s>Viṣṇuloka</s>.

children.text: uttamo daśabhir droṇair madhyamaḥ pañcabhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The best is with ten <s>droṇas</s>; the middling one is remembered as with five.
The lowest, O best of Brahmins, is with three; such is proclaimed as a sesame mountain.
As before, all the other supporting mountains should be placed around it,
and I shall proclaim the mantras for the gift exactly, O best of sages.
Since, at the slaying of <s>Madhu</s>, they arose from the bodily sweat of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
sesame seeds, <s>kuśa</s> grasses, and black gram, therefore may there be peace here.

children.text: havye kavye ca yasmācca tilā evābhirakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Since, in offerings to gods and ancestors, sesame seeds themselves are the protection,
lift me out of worldly existence, O lord of mountains; O sesame mountain, homage to you.
Having addressed it thus, whoever gives the unsurpassed sesame mountain,
goes to the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> abode, from which return is hard to obtain.
He obtains long life and rejoices with sons and grandsons.
Honored by ancestors, gods, and <s>Gandharvas</s>, he goes to heaven.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Now then, I shall proclaim the excellent cotton mountain,
by whose gift a man continually obtains the supreme state.
The cotton mountain likewise is best here with twenty <s>bhāras</s>.
The middling one is said to be with ten, and the lowest is remembered as with five.
A poor man should give it with one <s>bhāra</s>, free from deceit about his wealth.
Having prepared everything as for the grain-mountain, O best of sages,
he should give it in the morning after the night, uttering this:
Since you alone are always the covering of the worlds here,
O cotton mountain, homage to you; become the destroyer of the mass of sins.
Whoever gives the lordly cotton mountain in the presence of <s>Śarva</s>,
dwells in <s>Rudraloka</s> for a kalpa; after that he becomes a king here.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
After this, I shall proclaim the unsurpassed ghee mountain,
divine, made of splendor and ambrosia, and destructive of great sins.
The ghee mountain should be best with twenty jars of ghee.
The middling one is said to be with ten, and the lowest is remembered as with five.
Even a poor man who makes one here with two, according to the rule,
should likewise arrange the supporting mountains at one-fourth the measure.
He should place vessels of <s>śāli</s> rice grains above the jars,
and have them made compact and high, according to beauty and rule.
He should wrap it with white cloths, sugarcane stalks, fruits, and the like.
The remaining procedure is taught here as for the grain-mountain.
Consecration should come first, and likewise the oblation and the worship of the gods.

children.text: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ gurave taṃ nivedayet
children.translated_text: In the morning after the night, he should present it to the teacher,
and likewise the supporting mountains to the officiating priests, with a peaceful mind.
Since ghee arose from the union of ambrosia and splendor,
therefore may <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the universal soul with ghee as his flame, be pleased here.
Since the splendor-filled <s>Brahman</s> is known to be established in ghee,
therefore, in the form of a ghee mountain, protect us constantly.
By this rule he should give the unsurpassed ghee mountain.
Even one burdened with great sins attains the world of <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
In a celestial vehicle furnished with swans and cranes and garlanded with a net of tinkling bells,
surrounded by apsarases, siddhas, and vidyādharas,
he would roam together with his ancestors until the dissolution of beings.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Next I shall declare the unsurpassed jewel-mountain.
With a thousand pearls the mountain is the best.
The middle grade has five hundred, and the lowest is remembered as having three hundred.
The surrounding support-mountains on every side should be one quarter of it.
On the east, with diamonds and gomedas, and on the south, with sapphires,
<s>Gandhamādana</s> should be made by the learned, joined with rubies.
On the west, <s>Vimalācala</s> should be mixed with beryl and coral,
and on the north one should arrange it with rubies and gold.
Everything here too should be planned just as for the grain-mountain.
Likewise he should perform the invocation and make trees and gods of gold.
In the morning, free from ill-will, he should worship with flowers, fragrances, and the rest.
As before, he should recite these mantras for the guru and the officiating priests.
Since all the hosts of gods abide in all jewels,

children.text: tvaṃ ca ratnamayo nityaṃ namaste'stu sadācala ||
children.translated_text: and you are always made of jewels, homage to you, O steadfast mountain.
Since <s>Hari</s> is made pleased by the gift of jewels,
therefore, through the constant gift of jewels, protect us, O mountain.
Whoever gives a mountain made of jewels by this rule
goes to co-residence with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, worshiped by the lords of the immortals.
For a full hundred kalpas and more he would dwell there, O king;
endowed with beauty, health, and virtues, he would become lord of the seven continents.
Whatever sin beginning with brahmin-killing has been committed here or in the next world,
all that comes to destruction, like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Next I shall declare the unsurpassed silver-mountain,
by whose gift a man goes to the unsurpassed world of <s>Soma</s>.
A silver mountain of ten thousand palas is the best;
one of five thousand is called middling, and one of half that is remembered as the lowest.
If unable, then he should have it made above twenty palas, according to his capacity.
He should likewise prepare the support-mountains with a fourth part.
As before, making <s>Mandara</s> and the others of silver according to rule,
the wise man should likewise worship the world-lords made of refined silver.
Here the slope should be made golden and furnished with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the Sun.
Whatever is silver for the others is all gold here.
The rest, including the oblation, night-vigil, and so forth, he should perform as before.
Then in the morning he should give the silver mountain to the guru,
and the support-mountains to the officiating priests, with worship, garments, and ornaments.
Reciting this mantra, darbha grass in hand and free from ill-will, he should give it.
Since it is dear to the ancestors, to <s>Hari</s> and <s>Indra</s>, and to <s>Śiva</s>,
therefore you, O silver one, protect us from the ocean of sorrowful saṃsāra.
Having presented it thus, whoever gives the excellent silver mountain,
that person obtains the fruit of giving ten thousand cows.
In the world of <s>Soma</s>, with gandharvas and hosts of kinnaras and apsarases,
the wise man, being worshiped, would dwell until the dissolution of beings.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Now then I shall fully declare the excellent sugar-mountain,
by whose gift <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Sun, and <s>Rudra</s> are always pleased.
With eight bhāras of sugar the great mountain is the best;
with four it is called middling, and with two bhāras it is remembered as the lowest.
Or one of little wealth should make it with one bhāra or with half a bhāra.
A man should make the support-mountains with a fourth part.
Having prepared everything as with the grain-mountain, provided with nectar,
and likewise above <s>Meru</s>, three golden trees should be set.
<s>Mandāra</s>, <s>Pārijāta</s>, and, as the third, the <s>Kalpa</s> tree:
this triad of trees should be placed on the summit in every case.
<s>Haricandana</s> and <s>Saṃtāna</s> should be placed on the eastern and western sides,
on all the mountains, and especially on the sugar-mountain.
On <s>Mandara</s>, <s>Kāmadeva</s> should always face west,
and on the peak of <s>Gandhamādana</s>, <s>Dhanada</s> should face north.
On <s>Vipulācala</s>, the swan, embodiment of the Veda, should face east,
and on <s>Supārśva</s>, golden <s>Surabhi</s> should face south.
Having performed the whole procedure of invocation as with the grain-mountain,
he should give the middle, excellent mountain to the guru,
and the four mountains to the officiating priests, uttering these mantras.
This mountain joined with sugar is the essence of the nectar of good fortune;
therefore, O lord of mountains, be always a giver of joy.

children.text: amṛtaṃ pibatāṃ ye tu nipeturbhuvi śīkarāḥ
children.translated_text: The drops that fell to earth while the gods were drinking nectar,
from that substance of the gods you arose; protect us, O sugar-mountain.
Since sugar arose from the middle of <s>Manobhava</s>'s bow,
you consist of that, O great mountain; protect us from the ocean of saṃsāra.
The man who gives a sugar-mountain by this rule,

children.text: sarvapāpair vinirmuktaḥ sa yāti paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: freed from all sins, goes to the supreme state.
Mounting a vehicle shining like the moon, stars, and sun, together with his attendants,
he would take his place there, urged onward by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Then, at the end of a hundred kalpas, he would become lord of the seven continents,
endowed with long life and health for as many as three arbuda births.
He should arrange the meal according to his ability at all the mountain-gifts, free from envy.
Everywhere, with permission, he should eat food free from alkaline and salty ingredients.
He should bring all the implements for the mountains to the Brahmin's dwelling.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Formerly, in the great kalpa, there was a king named <s>Dharmamūrti</s>,
by whom thousands of <s>Daitya</s>s, the enemies of his friend <s>Śakra</s>, were slain.
The moon, the sun, and the others became bereft of brilliance through his splendor,
and by him hundreds of enemies were made unable to defeat him.
He could assume whatever form he wished, and though human he was unconquered.
His wife, named <s>Bhānumatī</s>, was beautiful in the three worlds,
and, with divine beauty like <s>Lakṣmī</s>, she surpassed the beauties of the immortals.
She was that king's chief queen, dearer even than his life-breaths.
Among ten thousand women she shone like <s>Śrī</s> herself.
The king would never part from her, not even for a thousand crores of kings.
Once, when he had gone to the assembly, he asked his household priest,
the excellent sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, while the king was filled with wonder.
The king said:
O blessed one, by what <s>dharma</s> is my prosperity unsurpassed,
and why is there always such abundant, supreme splendor in my body?
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said:
Formerly there was a courtesan named <s>Līlāvatī</s>, devoted to <s>Śiva</s>.
On the fourteenth lunar day she gave a salt-mountain to her guru,
together with golden trees and the other prescribed things, duly and according to rule.
At that time there was a <s>Śūdra</s> goldsmith named <s>Śauṇḍa</s>,
a servant in <s>Līlāvatī</s>'s house; by him, from gold, were fashioned
the trees and the chief gods, O king, with faith.
Having made them possessed of extraordinary beauty, without wages,
he knew it to be a work of <s>dharma</s> and would not accept payment in any way.
And the golden divine trees were polished brightly by his wife,

children.text: līlāvatī gireḥ pārśve paricaryāṃ ca pārthiva ||
children.translated_text: while <s>Līlāvatī</s>, O king, performed service beside the mountain.
After the two had sincerely performed attendance on the guru and the other services,

children.text: sā ca līlāvatī veśyākālena mahatāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: that courtesan <s>Līlāvatī</s>, even after a long time,
reached the law of time through the course of her deeds, O <s>Nārada</s>,
and, freed from all sins, went to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>.
That goldsmith, though poor, was exceedingly virtuous;
since he took no fee from the courtesan, he is now you here.
You have become lord of the seven islands, equal in splendor to ten thousand suns.
And she by whom the goldsmith's trees, made of gold,
were properly polished, his wife, is this <s>Bhānumatī</s> of yours.
From that polishing arose her radiant beauty and this sovereignty over the world,
because the service of the salt-mountain was done at night by those two without arrogance.
Therefore you have invincibility among the worlds, and prosperity joined with health and good fortune.
Therefore you too, here and according to rule, should make ten kinds of mountains, beginning with the grain-mountain.

children.text: tatheti satkṛtya sa dharmamūrtirvaco vasiṣṭhasya dadau ca sarvān
children.translated_text: Saying 'so be it,' <s>Dharmamūrti</s> honored <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s words and gave them all,
hundreds of grain-mountains and the rest, and went to the world of <s>Murāri</s>, honored by the immortals.
Even a poor man who sees these with great devotion, or touches them when they are being given by others,

children.text: śṛṇoti bhaktyātha matiṃ dadāti vikalmaṣaḥ so'pi divaṃ prayāti ||
children.translated_text: or hears of them with devotion and turns his mind to them, becomes free from stain and goes to heaven.
Bad dreams come to rest when men recite these chief mountains, which split apart the fear of worldly existence.
How much more, O best of sages, one who, calm in self, properly gives all the great mountains here?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago <s>Śaunaka</s> asked <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> as he was seated,
'How is the pacificatory and nourishing rite to be performed regularly for the attainment of all desires?'
<s>Vaiśampāyana</s> said:
One who desires prosperity or peace should undertake a graha-yajña (planetary sacrifice).
One who desires increase, long life, and nourishment should do the same, and again one performing an abhicāra (hostile rite).
By what rule this is done, O Brahmin, hear it as I tell you.
Having reviewed all the śāstras and condensed the extensive body of texts,
I shall teach the grahaśānti (pacification of the planets) enjoined by Purāṇa and Śruti.
On an auspicious day declared by Brahmins, after having Brahmins recite blessings,
he should establish the planets and their presiding deities and begin the homa (fire offering).
The graha-yajña is said by those skilled in Purāṇa and Śruti to be threefold.
The first is the ayuta-homa (ten-thousand-oblation offering); after that is the lakṣa-homa (hundred-thousand-oblation offering).
The third is the koṭi-homa (ten-million-oblation offering), which grants the fruits of all desires.
With ten thousand oblations it is remembered as the sacrifice to the nine planets.
I shall now state its rule as taught in Purāṇa and Śruti.
To the northeast of the pit he should make an altar two spans wide,
surrounded by two embankments and measuring a span in height,
square and facing north, for the installation of the gods.
After bringing forward the fire, he should invite the gods upon it.
Then the deities to be installed are thirty-two in number.
<s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Bhauma</s>, <s>Budha</s>, <s>Jīva</s>, <s>Sita</s>, and the son of the sun,
together with <s>Rāhu</s> and <s>Ketu</s>, are declared to be the planets that bring welfare to the world.

children.text: madhye tu bhāskaraṃ vidyāllohitaṃ dakṣiṇena tu
children.translated_text: He should know <s>Bhāskara</s> to be in the center, and <s>Lohita</s> to the south.
He should know <s>Guru</s> to be to the north, and <s>Budha</s> to the northeast.
He should know <s>Bhārgava</s> to be to the east, and <s>Soma</s> to the southeast.
He should know <s>Śani</s> to be to the west and <s>Rāhu</s> to the southwest,
and he should place <s>Ketu</s> to the northwest with white rice grains.
He should know <s>Īśvara</s> as the deity of <s>Bhāskara</s>, and likewise <s>Umā</s> as that of the moon.
and also <s>Skanda</s> for <s>Maṅgāraka</s>, and likewise <s>Hari</s> for <s>Budha</s>.
One should know <s>Brahmā</s> for <s>Guru</s>, and <s>Śacīpati</s> for <s>Śukra</s> too,

children.text: śanaiścarasya tu yamaṃ rāhoḥ kālaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> for <s>Śanaiścara</s>, and likewise <s>Kāla</s> for <s>Rāhu</s>.
And <s>Citragupta</s> for <s>Ketu</s>; these are the <s>adhidevatās</s> (presiding deities) of all.
<s>Agni</s>, the waters, the earth, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the goddess <s>Aindrī</s>,
as well as <s>Prajāpati</s>, the serpents, and <s>Brahmā</s>, are the <s>pratyadhidevatās</s> (counter-presiding deities).
He should invoke <s>Vināyaka</s>, and likewise <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Ākāśa</s>,
and also the two <s>Aśvin</s> princes, with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances).
He should visualize red <s>Āditya</s>, joined with <s>Maṅgāraka</s>.

children.text: somaśukrau tathā śveto budhajīvau ca piṅgalau
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> and <s>Śukra</s> are white, while <s>Budha</s> and <s>Jīva</s> are tawny.

children.text: mandarāhū tathā kṛṣṇau dhūmraṃ ketugaṇaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Manda</s> and <s>Rāhu</s> are black; they know the group of <s>Ketus</s> to be smoky-colored.
Garments and flowers should be given according to the colors of the planets.
Here the scent of incense should be fragrant, and above there should be a canopy.
A wise man should set up a beautiful one, furnished with fruits and flowers.
He should give molasses-rice to the Sun, and ghee-milk-rice to <s>Soma</s>.
To <s>Aṅgāraka</s> he should give <s>saṃyāva</s> (wheat porridge), and to <s>Budha</s> milk with <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice.

children.text: dadhyodanaṃ ca jīvāya śakrāya ca ghṛtaudanam
children.translated_text: He should give curd-rice to <s>Jīva</s>, and ghee-rice to <s>Śakra</s>.
To <s>Śanaiścara</s> he should give <s>kṛsarā</s> (rice-and-pulse gruel), and goat meat to <s>Rāhu</s>.
To the <s>Ketus</s> he should give variegated rice; then he should worship with every kind of food.
To the northeast of that, adorned with curds and unbroken rice,
covered with mango shoots and furnished with fruits and a pair of cloths,
provided with five jewels and supplied with five kinds of shoots,
he should set up an unbroken pot and install <s>Varuṇa</s> there.

children.text: gaṅgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ samudrāṃśca sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: All rivers beginning with <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and the oceans and lakes,
and earth from an elephant-place, a horse-place, a road, an anthill, a confluence, a pond, and a cow-station,
having brought it, O best of Brahmins, together with water containing all herbs,
the knower of <s>dharma</s> should place it there for the bathing of the yajamāna.

children.text: sarve samudrāḥ saritaḥ sarāṃsi ca nadāstathā
children.translated_text: May all oceans, rivers, lakes, and streams
come here for the yajamāna, causing the destruction of his misfortune.
Thus he should invoke these immortals, O best of sages.
He should begin the homa with ghee, barley, rice, sesame, and the like.
<s>Arka</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>khadira</s>, then <s>apāmārga</s> and <s>pippala</s>,

children.text: audumbaraḥ śamī dūrvā kuśāśca samidhaḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>audumbara</s>, <s>śamī</s>, <s>dūrvā</s>, and <s>kuśa</s> are the fuel-sticks in order.
For each one, one hundred and eight, or twenty-eight,
should be offered, combined with honey, ghee, and curd.
The wise man should prepare fuel-sticks a span long, without roots, without branches,
and without leaves, always, in all rites.
For all the gods too, the knower of the highest truth should offer silently;

children.text: svena svenaiva mantreṇa hotavyāḥ samidhaḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: the fuel-sticks should be offered separately with each one's own mantra.
And again, the <s>caru</s> (cooked oblation), food-offerings, and the like, anointed with ghee, should be offered.
Having offered ten oblations with mantras, he should then perform the homa with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>.
The foremost Brahmins should do it facing north or facing east.
The <s>carus</s> should be prepared with mantras for each deity.
Having properly offered those <s>carus</s>, he should then perform the homa.

children.text: ākṛṣṇeti ca sūryāya homaḥ kāryo dvijanmanā ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Sūrya</s>, the twice-born should perform the homa with the mantra beginning "ākṛṣṇeti".
For <s>Soma</s>, he should again offer with the mantra beginning "āpyāyasva".

children.text: agnirmūrdhā divo mantra iti bhaumāya kīrtayet ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Bhauma</s>, he should recite the mantra beginning "agnir mūrdhā divaḥ".
For the son of <s>Soma</s>, the mantra beginning "agne vivasvad uṣasaḥ" is prescribed.
For <s>Guru</s>, the accepted mantra is beginning "bṛhaspate paridīyā rathena".

children.text: śukraṃ te anyaditi ca śukrasyāpi nigadyate
children.translated_text: For <s>Śukra</s> too, the mantra beginning "śukraṃ te anyat" is stated.

children.text: śanaiścarāyeti punaḥ śaṃ no devīti homayet ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Śanaiścara</s>, again, he should offer with the mantra beginning "śaṃ no devīḥ".
The mantra beginning "kayā naś citra ā bhuvat" is declared for <s>Rāhu</s>.
For the pacification of the <s>Ketus</s> too, he should say the mantra beginning "ketuṃ kṛṇvan".

children.text: ā vo rājeti rudrasya balihomaṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: For <s>Rudra</s>, he should perform the bali-homa with the mantra beginning "ā vo rājā".
For <s>Umā</s> there is the mantra beginning "āpo hi ṣṭhā", and for the Lord likewise the one beginning "syonā".
For <s>Viṣṇu</s> there are the formulas beginning "viṣṇor idaṃ" and "viṣṇuḥ"; for <s>Svayambhū</s>, the one beginning "tam īśe".
Then he should offer to <s>Indra</s> with the mantra beginning "indram id devatātaye".

children.text: tathā yamasya cāyaṃ gauriti homaḥ prakīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, for <s>Yama</s>, the homa beginning "ayaṃ gauḥ" is proclaimed.
For <s>Kāla</s>, the mantra beginning "brahma jajñānam" is commended.
For <s>Citragupta</s>, those who know mantras know the one beginning "ajñātam".
For <s>Vahni</s>, the mantra beginning "agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe" is declared.

children.text: ud uttamaṃ varuṇamity apāṃ mantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: For the waters, the mantra beginning "ud uttamaṃ varuṇam" is proclaimed.
For the earth, the formula beginning "pṛthivy antarikṣam" is read in the Vedas.
For <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the mantra beginning "sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ" is declared.
For <s>Śakra</s>, the mantra beginning "indrāyendo marutvate" is praised.
For the goddess, he should perform the rite with the mantra beginning "uttānaparṇe subhage".
For <s>Prajāpati</s>, the homa is remembered with the mantra beginning "prajāpatiḥ".

children.text: namo'stu sarpebhya iti sarpāṇāṃ mantra ucyate
children.translated_text: For the serpents, the mantra beginning "namo'stu sarpebhyaḥ" is stated.

children.text: eṣa brahmā ya ṛtvigbhya iti brahmaṇyudāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Brahmā</s>, the mantra beginning "eṣa brahmā ya ṛtvigbhyaḥ" is declared.
For <s>Vināyaka</s>, the mantra beginning "anūnam" is remembered by the learned.
The mantra beginning "jātavedase sunavāma" is called the <s>Durgā</s> mantra.
For <s>Ākāśa</s>, the mantra beginning "ād it pratnasya retasaḥ" is declared.
For <s>Vāyu</s>, the mantra beginning "krāṇā śiśur mahīnām" is proclaimed.
For the <s>Aśvins</s>, the mantra beginning "eṣo uṣā apūrvyā" is stated.
For the full oblation, he should cast it in with the formula beginning "mūrdhānaṃ divaḥ".
Then, with the consecration mantra, with instruments and auspicious songs,
at the end of the homa, with that very full pot, while he faces east or north,
O Brahman, by four Brahmins of unblemished limbs, adorned with golden garlands and chains,
the bathing of the yajamāna should be performed.
May the gods, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>, consecrate you;
may <s>Vāsudeva</s>, lord of the world, and likewise the mighty <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>,
and <s>Pradyumna</s> and <s>Aniruddha</s> be for your victory.
May <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>, <s>Agni</s> the blessed one, <s>Yama</s>, and also <s>Nirṛti</s>,
<s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Pavana</s>, the lord of wealth, and likewise <s>Śiva</s>,
and <s>Śeṣa</s> together with <s>Brahmā</s>, the guardians of the directions, protect you.
Fame, fortune, steadfastness, intelligence, nourishment, faith, ritual action, and thought,
discernment, modesty, beauty, peace, contentment, and forbearance, the mothers,
these wives of <s>Dharma</s>, assembled together, should consecrate you.
May the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn,
the planets, together with <s>Rāhu</s> and <s>Ketu</s>, being satisfied, consecrate you.
Gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and serpents,

children.text: ṛṣayo munayo gāvo devamātara eva ca ||
children.translated_text: seers, sages, cows, and the mothers of the gods as well,
the wives of the gods, trees, Nāgas, Daityas, and hosts of Apsarases,
missile-weapons, all hand-weapons, kings, and vehicles,
herbs and jewels, and whatever are the divisions of time,
rivers, oceans, mountains, sacred fords, clouds, and streams,
let these consecrate you for the accomplishment of every desired aim.
Then, wearing white garments and anointed with white perfumes,
having been bathed by the best of twice-born men with all herbs and all fragrances,
the sacrificer, together with his wife, should honor the well-collected officiating priests
with <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fees), carefully and without bewilderment.
He should give a tawny cow to the Sun, and a conch likewise to the Moon;
to Mars he should give a red draught bull, a humped one.
To Mercury he should give gold, and to Jupiter a pair of yellow garments;
to the teacher of the Daityas a white horse, and to the son of the Sun a black cow.
To <s>Rāhu</s> he should give iron, and to <s>Ketu</s> an excellent goat;
the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should be made equal in gold by the sacrificer.
Or else cows adorned with gold should be given for all of them;
or he may give gold, or whatever satisfies the teacher.
All <s>dakṣiṇās</s> everywhere should be given with the proper mantra.
O tawny cow, O ruddy one, you are worthy of worship by all the gods;
since you consist of sacred fords and gods, therefore grant me peace.

children.text: puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṇyānāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam
children.translated_text: O conch, you are holy among holy things and the auspicious among auspicious things;

children.text: viṣṇunā vidhṛtaścāsi tataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me ||
children.translated_text: you are held by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and therefore grant me peace.
You are <s>Dharma</s> in the form of a bull, bringing joy to the world;
you are the seat of the eight-formed one, and therefore grant me peace.
You are born from the womb of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the golden seed of <s>Vibhāvasu</s>;
you bestow the fruit of endless merit; therefore grant me peace.
Since a pair of yellow garments is dear to <s>Vāsudeva</s>,

children.text: pradānāttasya me viṣṇo hyataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me ||
children.translated_text: by giving it to me, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, therefore grant me peace.
You are <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of a horse, since you arose from ambrosia;
you are always the vehicle of the Moon and Sun, and therefore grant me peace.
Since you are the whole earth, O cow, resembling <s>Keśava</s>,
always remover of every sin, therefore grant me peace.
Since laborious works are always dependent upon you,
the plough and other implements and weapons, therefore grant me peace.
Since you are established as a limb of all sacrifices,
and are always the vehicle of <s>Vibhāvasu</s>, therefore grant me peace.
In the limbs of cows stand the fourteen worlds;

children.text: yasmāttasmācchriye me syādiha loke paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: therefore may there be prosperity for me in this world and in the next.
