Since the couch of <s>Keśava</s> is never empty at any time,
may my own bed, once given, never be empty in birth after birth.

children.text: yathā ratneṣu sarveṣu sarve devāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as all the gods are established in every jewel,

children.text: tathā ratnāni yacchantu ratnadānena me surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so by the gift of jewels may the gods grant me jewels.
Just as other gifts do not deserve even a sixteenth part of the gift of land,
so through the gift of land may peace be mine here.
Thus he should worship with devotion, free from deceit about his wealth,
with masses of jewels, gold, and garments, with incense, garlands, and unguents.
Whoever performs worship of the planets according to this rule
obtains all desires and, after death, is honored in heaven.
But whatever planet is constantly troublesome, or so for a man of little wealth,
having worshiped that one carefully, the wise man should also honor the rest.
Planets, cows, kings, and especially Brahmins,
when honored, honor in return; when disrespected, they burn one up.
Just as armor is a warding-off of blows from arrows,
so <s>śānti</s> (pacification) is a warding-off of injuries caused by fate.
Therefore one who desires prosperity should not perform a rite lacking <s>dakṣiṇā</s>;
for even one god is satisfied by a complete <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.
This <s>ayutahoma</s> (ten-thousand oblation rite) is always established in a sacrifice to the nine planets,
in marriage festivals and sacrifices, and in rites such as consecration.
For the sake of freedom from obstacles, O best of sages, and likewise when marvels cause alarm,
this <s>ayutahoma</s> has been taught; now hear the <s>lakṣahoma</s>.
Because the wise know the <s>lakṣahoma</s> (hundred-thousand oblation rite) to bring the attainment of all desires,
dear to the ancestors directly and bestowing the fruits of enjoyment and liberation,
having obtained the favorable strength of planets and stars and having had Brahmins pronounce blessings,
the wise man should have a pavilion made to the northeast of the house,
or on the ground of a temple of <s>Rudra</s>, square and facing north.
Then, according to rule, he should make it ten cubits or eight cubits.
A wise man should carefully have the ground made sloping toward the east and north.
Having selected the northeastern area of the pavilion,
he should have an auspicious <s>kuṇḍa</s> (fire-pit) made, properly furnished with its prescribed marks.
It should be square on every side, with a yoni-shaped mouth and with a girdle.
The girdle is four finger-breadths wide and likewise four finger-breadths high.
It should slope toward the east and north and be evenly set on all sides.
The <s>navagrahamakha</s> (rite for the nine planets) is remembered as being for the pacification of all worlds.
A <s>kuṇḍa</s> deficient or excessive in measure would bring many dangers.
Therefore a fully correct pacificatory <s>kuṇḍa</s> is prescribed.
Compared with this, the <s>lakṣahoma</s> was declared tenfold by <s>Svayambhū</s>,
with respect to oblations, careful performance, and dakṣiṇās as well.
For it the <s>kuṇḍa</s> should again be two cubits broad and four cubits long;
in a <s>lakṣahoma</s> the <s>kuṇḍa</s> should have a yoni-shaped mouth and three girdles.
To its northeast, occupying three spans,
there should be a square structure on every side, sloping toward the east and north.
The <s>sthaṇḍila</s> (raised altar), said by <s>Viśvakarman</s>, is raised to half its diameter,
for the installation of the deities, and is enclosed by three embankments.

children.text: dvyaṅgulo hyucchrito vapraḥ prathamaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The first embankment is declared to be two finger-breadths high.
Then above it the two embankments are each furnished with a rise of one finger-breadth.

children.text: tryaṅgulasya ca vistāraḥ sarveṣāṃ kathyate budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: The breadth of all of them is said by the wise to be three finger-breadths.
On the <s>sthaṇḍila</s>, moreover, there should be a wall ten finger-breadths high.
On that one should invoke the deities as before, with flowers and rice-grains.
All of them, together with their presiding and counter-presiding deities, should face <s>Āditya</s> (the sun).
They are to be installed, O best of sages, not on the north side facing away.
There <s>Garutmān</s> should especially be worshipped by one who desires prosperity.
You whose body is the sound of the <s>Sāman</s>, the vehicle of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
you who always remove poison and sin: therefore grant me peace.
Having consecrated the pitcher as before, he should perform the homa in the same way.
Having offered a hundred thousand oblations, and again an additional number of fuel-sticks,
he should pour a <s>vasordhārā</s> (stream of ghee) from a ghee-pot over the fire.
Having made a ladle from fresh <s>audumbarī</s> wood, straight and free from hollows,
as long as an arm, then, over the two posts,
with it he should properly pour the stream of ghee over the fire.
He should recite the <s>Āgneya</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Raudra</s>, and <s>Aindava</s> hymns,
and have the <s>Mahāvaiśvānara</s> sāman and the <s>Jyeṣṭhasāman</s> chanted.
The bathing of the sacrificer and the recitation of blessings should be as before.
Dakṣiṇās should be given separately by the sacrificer as before.
With freedom from desire and anger, and with a peaceful mind, they should be given to the officiating priests.
For the <s>navagrahamakha</s>, four Brahmins learned in the Vedas are required.
Or else, for the pacificatory rite, only two officiants learned in śruti may be used.
In an <s>ayutahoma</s> (ten-thousand oblation rite) those two should be appointed; one should not become involved in excessive elaboration.

children.text: tadvacca daśa cāṣṭau ca lakṣahome tu ṛtvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, in a <s>lakṣahoma</s>, the officiating priests should be ten and eight, that is eighteen.
Or, according to one's ability, four may be appointed in the same way, without rivalry.
In the <s>lakṣahoma</s> everything is ten times beyond the <s>navagrahamakha</s>.
O best of sages, one should give foods and ornaments also, according to ability.
Beds with garments, and golden bracelets,
ear-ornaments, finger-rings, sacred ornaments, and necklaces should be given by one who is able.
A man should not perform it without dakṣiṇā through miserliness about his wealth.
If, from greed and delusion, he does not give, he incurs the destruction of his family.
Food-giving should be done according to one's ability by one who desires prosperity.
For when it is performed without food, it becomes productive of famine.
Without food it burns the kingdom; without mantra it burns the officiating priests.
Without dakṣiṇā it burns the sacrificer; there is no enemy equal to a sacrifice.
Nor should a man of little wealth ever perform a <s>lakṣahoma</s>,
because contention in a sacrifice is always oppressive.

children.text: tameva pūjayedbhaktyā dvau vā trīnvā yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: He should worship that one alone with devotion, or two or three according to rule.
He may worship even a single Brahmin who has reached the far shore of the Veda,
carefully with dakṣiṇās; a man of little wealth should not worship many.
A <s>lakṣahoma</s> should be performed according to one's wealth, when the wealth is abundant,
because, performing it according to rule, one obtains all desired objects.
And in <s>Śivaloka</s> he is honored by the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, and hosts of <s>Maruts</s>,
for eight hundred kalpas; then he attains liberation.
Whoever, having a desire, performs this <s>lakṣahoma</s> according to rule,
obtains that desire and enjoys an endless state.
One desiring sons obtains sons; one desiring wealth obtains wealth.

children.text: bhāryārthī śobhanāṃ bhāryāṃ kumārī ca śubhaṃ patim ||
children.translated_text: One desiring a wife obtains a beautiful wife, and a maiden obtains an auspicious husband.
One fallen from kingship likewise obtains a kingdom; one desiring prosperity obtains prosperity.

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ prārthayate kāmaṃ sa vai bhavati puṣkalaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever desire he longs for, that indeed becomes abundant.

children.text: niṣkāmaḥ kurute yastu sa paraṃ brahma gacchati ||
children.translated_text: But whoever performs it without desire goes to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
The <s>koṭihoma</s>, a hundred times greater than this, was declared by <s>Svayambhū</s>,
with respect to oblations, careful performance, dakṣiṇās, and the fruit.
As before are the invocation and dismissal of the planetary deities.

children.text: homamantrāsta evoktāḥ khāne dāne tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: The homa mantras are said to be the same, and likewise in the digging and in the giving.
Now learn from me this special distinction concerning the <s>kuṇḍa</s>, pavilion, and altar.
In a <s>koṭihoma</s>, the <s>kuṇḍa</s> is four cubits and square on every side,
provided with two yoni-shaped mouths; that too is said to have three girdles.
The first girdle should be made raised by two fingers, according to the learned;
likewise the second is said to be raised by three fingers.
And the third is four fingers in height and breadth;
the breadth of the former two is approved as two fingers.
The <s>yoni</s> should be a span in measure, six or seven fingers broad,
raised in the middle like a tortoise's back, and raised one finger at the sides.
Likewise it should be like an elephant's lip, elongated and furnished with an opening.
This is said to be the characteristic of the <s>yoni</s> in all <s>kuṇḍas</s>.
Everywhere above the girdle it should resemble the leaf of an <s>aśvattha</s> tree.
And for a <s>koṭihoma</s>, the <s>vedī</s> should measure four spans.
It should be square on every side and provided with three embankments.
The measure of the embankments and the height of the altars are as stated before.
Likewise the pavilion should be sixteen cubits across and four-faced.
At the eastern door one should install a <s>Bahvṛca</s>, one who has mastered the Veda.
At the southern door, likewise, a knower of the <s>Yajurveda</s>; at the western, a <s>Sāmavedin</s>.
In the same way the wise man should place a knower of the <s>Atharvaveda</s> in the north.
Eight homa-priests should be appointed, learned in the Veda and Vedāṅgas.
Thus there should be twelve Brahmins, with garments, garlands, and unguents;
as before, he should worship them with devotion, adorned with garments and ornaments.

children.text: rātrisūktaṃ ca raudraṃ ca pāvamānaṃ sumaṅgalam
children.translated_text: The <s>Rātrisūkta</s>, the <s>Raudra</s>, and the very auspicious <s>Pāvamāna</s>:
in the east the <s>Bahvṛca</s> sits facing north, reciting the <s>śānti</s> hymn.

children.text: śāktaṃ śākraṃ ca saumyaṃ ca kauṣmāṇḍaṃ śāntimeva ca
children.translated_text: The <s>Śākta</s>, <s>Śākra</s>, <s>Saumya</s>, <s>Kauṣmāṇḍa</s>, and also the <s>śānti</s> hymn:
he should have the excellent <s>Yajurvedin</s> recite these at the southern door.
The <s>Suparṇa</s>, then the <s>Vairāja</s>, the <s>Āgneya</s>, and the <s>Rudrasaṃhitā</s>,

children.text: jyeṣṭhamāsa tathā śāntiṃ chandogaḥ paścime japet ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the <s>Jyeṣṭhasāman</s> and the <s>śānti</s>: the <s>Chandoga</s> should mutter these in the west.

children.text: śāntisūktaṃ ca sauraṃ ca tathā śākunakaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: The <s>Śāntisūkta</s>, the <s>Saura</s>, and also the auspicious <s>Śākunaka</s>,
the <s>Pauṣṭika</s> and <s>Mahārājya</s>: in the north the knower of the <s>Atharvaveda</s> should recite them.
Here the homa should be performed with five or with seven, as before.

children.text: snāne dāne ca mantrāḥ syusta eva munisattama ||
children.translated_text: In bathing and giving, the mantras are the same, O best of sages.
And the rule for the <s>vasordhārā</s> is a special feature in the <s>lakṣahoma</s>.
Whoever performs a <s>koṭihoma</s> according to this rule
obtains all desires, and afterward goes to the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The man who reads or hears the threefold <s>grahayajña</s>
goes to the station of <s>Indra</s>, his self purified from every sin.
The fruit that a knower of dharma obtains by performing eighteen thousand <s>aśvamedhas</s>
he enjoys that fruit from the <s>koṭihoma</s>.
Thousands of Brahmin-killings and countless embryo-killings
are destroyed by the <s>koṭihoma</s>, as was properly declared by <s>Śiva</s>.
Acts of subjugation, sorcery, expulsion, and the like:
having performed the <s>navagrahamakha</s>, one should then undertake the desired rite.

children.text: anyathā phaladaṃ puṃsāṃ na kāmyaṃ jāyate kvacit
children.translated_text: Otherwise a desired rite never becomes fruitful for men.
Therefore one should first perform the procedure of the <s>ayutahoma</s>.

children.text: vṛttaṃ voccāṭane kuṇḍaṃ tathā ca vaśyakarmaṇi
children.translated_text: For expulsion, and also for the act of subjugation, the <s>kuṇḍa</s> should be round,
with three girdles, one mouth, and a width of one <s>aratni</s>.
<s>Palāśa</s> fuel-sticks are recommended, mixed with honey and <s>gorocanā</s>,
and likewise sprinkled with sandal, aloe-wood, and saffron.
He should offer bilva fruits and lotuses with honey and ghee.
Ten thousand oblations are stated by <s>Svayambhū</s> for every occasion.
For the subjugation rite, of bilva fruits and lotuses, O knower of dharma,

children.text: sumitriyā na āpa oṣadhaya iti homayet ||
children.translated_text: he should offer with the mantra beginning “May the waters and herbs be friendly to us.”

children.text: na cātra sthāpanaṃ kāryaṃ na ca kumbhābhiṣecanam
children.translated_text: Here no installation is to be performed, nor any consecration with pitchers.
Having bathed with all herbs, the householder should wear white flowers and garments.
He should honor the Brahmins with neck-cords accompanied by gold.
Fine garments should be given, and white cows together with gold.
He would bring under control even all hostile forces without fail.
Even enemies would become friends; this homa destroys sin.
For causing dissension and for sorcery, a triangular <s>kuṇḍa</s> is prescribed,
with two girdles, a mouth at the corner, and one cubit in every direction.
Then the Brahmins should perform the homa, wearing red garlands and unguents,
with red turbans put on and wearing red garments.
They should be furnished with three vessels filled with fresh crow's blood.
The fuel-sticks, with hawk-bones attached, are to be offered with the left hand
by men with loosened hair, meditating inauspiciousness against the enemy.

children.text: durmitriyās tasmai santu tathā huṃphaḍitīti ca
children.translated_text: The mantra should be, “Let there be hostile powers for him,” and likewise “huṃ phaṭ.”
Having consecrated a razor with the <s>śyena-abhicāra</s> mantra,
he should make an image of the enemy and cut it up with the razor.
Then he should cast the pieces of the enemy-form into the fire.
After the procedure of the <s>grahayajña</s>, whenever he again performs sorcery
or likewise causes dissension, he should follow this very procedure.
For men this gives fruit here in this world, but it is not auspicious in the next.
Therefore one who desires prosperity should perform here only the pacificatory rite.
The human being who performs the threefold <s>grahayajña</s> without desire
attains the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, from which return is difficult.
The person who listens to this daily or has it recited

children.text: na tasya grahapīḍā syānna ca bandhujanakṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has no affliction from planets and no destruction of relatives.
In the house where the written text of the threefold <s>grahayajña</s> remains,

children.text: na pīḍā tatra bālānāṃ na rogo na ca bandhanam ||
children.translated_text: there is no affliction of children, no disease, and no bondage.
It grants the fruit of all sacrifices and destroys every sin completely.
The wise know the <s>koṭihoma</s> to bestow both enjoyment and liberation.
The best of gods say that the <s>lakṣahoma</s> has the fruit of an <s>Aśvamedha</s>.
Likewise the twelve-day sacrifice and the <s>navagrahamakha</s> are remembered.
Thus has now been taught, for the joy of the festival, the consecration of the divine sacrifice, remover of every stain.

children.text: paripaṭhati ya itthaṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti prasaṅgādabhibhavati sa śatrūnāyurārogyayuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever recites it in this way, or whoever hears it by occasion, overcomes his enemies and is endowed with long life and health.
<s>Śiva</s> said:
<s>Ravi</s> should always be seated on a lotus, holding lotuses, with the brilliance of a lotus-womb.
He should have seven horses and seven reins, and should be two-armed.
The moon should be white, clothed in white garments, with white horses and a white vehicle.
<s>Śaśin</s> should be made mace in hand, two-armed, and granting boons.
The son of the earth should wear red garlands and garments and hold a spear, trident, and mace.
He should be four-armed, white-haired, and granting boons.
<s>Budha</s> should wear yellow garlands and garments and have the brilliance of the <s>karṇikāra</s> flower.
He should hold a sword, shield, and mace, be mounted on a lion, and grant boons.
In the same way the gurus of gods and demons should be yellow and white, and four-armed.
They should be made staff-bearing and boon-giving, with rosaries and water-pots.
The son of the Sun should have the brilliance of sapphire, hold a trident, grant boons, and have a vulture as his vehicle.
He should also be made holding arrows and a bow.
<s>Rāhu</s> is praised here as grim-faced, bearing sword, shield, and trident, and granting boons.
He should be seated on a blue lion-throne.
All the <s>Ketus</s> should be smoky-colored, two-armed, mace-bearing, and with distorted faces.
They should always be seated on vultures and should grant boons.
All the planets should be made crowned and bringing benefit to the world.
They should all always be one hundred and eight fingers high, measured by their own fingers.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Blessed lord, ruler of what has been and what will be, whatever else has been heard,
and is sufficient for the fruit of enjoyment and liberation, please tell that again.
Thus addressed, <s>Śambhu</s>, master of sacred speech, spoke.
O Brahman, by austerity he is equal to me and has mastered the broad extent of Purāṇa and Śruti.
This <s>dharma</s>, in the form of a bull, is named <s>Nandī</s>, lord of the hosts.
From now on, O <s>Nārada</s>, he will teach the <s>Māheśvara</s> dharmas.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Having said this, the god of gods disappeared right there.
And <s>Nārada</s>, wishing to hear, questioned <s>Nandikeśvara</s>:
You have been instructed here by <s>Śiva</s>; tell the <s>Māheśvara</s> vow.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Listen attentively, O Brahman; I shall teach the <s>Māheśvara</s> vow,
famous in the three worlds by the name <s>Śivacaturdaśī</s>.
On the bright thirteenth day of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, eating only once,
he should pray to the god of gods: I have gone to you for refuge.
On the fourteenth day, fasting and having properly worshiped <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
I shall give a golden bull and eat on the following day.
Having slept while observing this rule, a man should rise in the morning.
After bathing and recitation, he should then worship <s>Śaṃkara</s> together with <s>Umā</s>
with white lotuses, fragrances, garlands, and unguents.

children.text: pādau namaḥ śivāyeti śiraḥ sarvātmane namaḥ
children.translated_text: He should worship the feet with 'Homage to <s>Śiva</s>,' and the head with 'Homage to the Self of all.'
He should worship the eyes with 'To the three-eyed one,' and the forehead with 'Homage to <s>Hara</s>.'
He should worship the face with 'To the moon-faced one,' and the neck with 'To <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>.'

children.text: sadyojātāya karṇau tu vāmadevāya vai bhujau ||
children.translated_text: He should worship the ears with 'To <s>Sadyojāta</s>,' and the arms with 'To <s>Vāmadeva</s>.'
He should worship the heart with 'To the heart of <s>Aghora</s>.'
He should worship the breasts with 'To <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>,' and the belly with 'To <s>Īśāna</s>.'
He should worship the sides with 'To endless <s>dharma</s>,' and the waist with 'To the one whose nature is knowledge.'
He should worship the thighs with 'To the lion of endless detachment.'
The wise man should worship the knees with 'To the lord of endless sovereignty.'

children.text: pradhānāya namo jaṅghe gulphau vyomātmane namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should worship the shanks with 'Homage to the primal one,' and the ankles with 'Homage to the one whose self is space.'
He should worship the hair and back with 'To the one whose hair is space and whose form is the self.'

children.text: namaḥ puṣṭyai namastuṣṭyai pārvatīṃ cāpi pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should also worship <s>Pārvatī</s> with 'Homage to nourishment; homage to satisfaction.'
Then he should present a golden bull accompanied by a water-pot,
wearing white garlands and garments and furnished with five jewels,
together with various foods, to a Brahmin.
May the god of gods here, <s>Sadyojāta</s>, bearer of the <s>Pināka</s>, be pleased.
Then, having summoned auspicious Brahmins, he should satisfy them with devotion.
Having sipped <s>pṛṣadājya</s> (curds mixed with ghee), he should sleep on the ground facing north.
On the fifteenth day, having worshiped the Brahmins, he should eat while restraining his speech.
Likewise, on the dark fourteenth day, he should perform all this.
On all fourteenth days he should perform the worship as before.

children.text: ye tu māse viśeṣāḥ syustānnibodha kramādiha ||
children.translated_text: Now learn in order the special distinctions that apply in the months.
In the months beginning with <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, he should utter these in sequence:
Homage to <s>Śaṃkara</s>; homage to you, <s>Karavīraka</s>.
Homage to <s>Tryambaka</s>; thereafter, homage to <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: namaste'stu mahādeva sthāṇave ca tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Mahādeva</s>, and thereafter to <s>Sthāṇu</s>.

children.text: namaḥ paśupate nātha namaste śambhave punaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the lord <s>Paśupati</s>; again, homage to <s>Śambhu</s>.
Homage to <s>Paramānanda</s>; homage to the bearer of the half-moon.

children.text: namo bhīmāya ityevaṃ tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Bhīma</s>; thus: I have gone to you for refuge.

children.text: gomūtraṃ gomūyaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam ||
children.translated_text: Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curds, ghee, and water touched by kuśa grass,

children.text: pañcagavyaṃ tato bilvaṃ karpūraṃ cāguruṃ yavāḥ
children.translated_text: then <s>pañcagavya</s>, bilva, camphor, aguru, and barley,
and black sesame seeds are remembered as the ritual substances to be sipped in due order.
One such sipping is prescribed for each of the two fourteenth days in every month.
The worship should also be performed with <s>mandāra</s> and <s>mālatī</s> flowers, and likewise with <s>dhattūra</s> flowers,
with <s>sinduvāra</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, <s>mallikā</s>, and <s>pāṭala</s> flowers.
With arka flowers, kadamba flowers, śatapatrī blossoms, and likewise utpalas,
one should worship <s>Pārvatīpati</s> on each fourteenth lunar day with each of these.
Then again, when the month of <s>Kārttika</s> has arrived, he should satisfy the twice-born,
with various kinds of food, eatables, garments, garlands, and ornaments.
After performing the release of a dark bull according to the rule taught in śruti, a man

children.text: umāmaheśvaraṃ haimaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ ca gavā saha ||
children.translated_text: should give a golden image of <s>Umāmaheśvara</s>, and a bull together with a cow.
He should give a bed furnished with eight pearls and covered with a white cloth,
complete with all its accessories and accompanied by a water-pot.
Then, placing it above a copper vessel together with rice grains,
he should give it to a peaceful Brahmin devoted to Vedic vows.
It may be given to one who knows the <s>Jyeṣṭhasāman</s>, or to one observing the <s>navaka-vrata</s>;
he should give it to a discerning śrotriya, to an ācārya who knows reality,
whose limbs are without defect, who is gentle, and who always performs auspicious acts.
Having honored him together with his wife with garments, garlands, and ornaments,
if a guru is present, it should be given to the guru; in his absence, to a twice-born man.
He should not practise deceit with wealth; if he does, he falls downward because of that fault.
Whoever observes <s>Śiva-caturdaśī</s> by this rule,
that human being obtains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.
Whatever sin, such as Brahmin-murder, has been committed here or hereafter,
whether by ancestors or by brothers, all of that comes to destruction.
Here there is growth of long life, health, family, and food; hereafter there is inexhaustibility and four-armed form.
After dwelling in heaven as lord over the gaṇas for hundreds of crores of kalpas, he reaches the abode of <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: na bṛhaspatirapyanantamasyāḥ phalamindo na pitāmaho'pi vaktum
children.translated_text: Not even <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, nor the Moon, nor <s>Pitāmaha</s>, can state the boundless fruit of this observance;

children.text: na ca siddhagaṇo'pyalaṃ na cāhaṃ yadi jihvāyutakoṭayo'pi vaktre ||
children.translated_text: nor is even the host of siddhas able to do so, nor am I, even if there were crores of tongues in the mouth.

children.text: bhavatyamaravallabhaḥ paṭhati yaḥ smaredvā sadā śṛṇotyapi vimatsaraḥ sakalapāpanirmocanīm
children.translated_text: He who recites it, remembers it always, or hears it without envy becomes dear to the immortals, for it releases from all sin.

children.text: imāṃ śivacaturdaśīmamarakāminīkoṭayaḥ stuvanti tamaninditaṃ kimu samācaredyaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: Crores of heavenly women praise that blameless man for this <s>Śiva-caturdaśī</s>; how much more one who always performs it.

children.text: yā vātha nārī kurute'tibhaktyā bhartāramāpṛcchya sutāngurūnvā
children.translated_text: And any woman who performs it with deep devotion, after asking her husband, her sons, or her elders,

children.text: sāpi prasādātparameśvarasya paraṃ padaṃ yāti pinākapāṇeḥ ||
children.translated_text: she too, by the grace of the supreme lord, goes to the supreme state of <s>Pinākapāṇi</s>.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Hear, <s>Nārada</s>, the greatness that belongs to the renunciation of fruits,
which is imperishable, supreme in the world, and grants the fruits of all desires.

children.text: mārgaśīrṣe śubhe māsi tṛtīyāyāṃ mune vratam
children.translated_text: In the auspicious month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, on the third lunar day, O sage, this vow
or else on the twelfth, eighth, or even fourteenth lunar day,
should be begun in the bright fortnight, after inviting Brahmins to pronounce the rite.
In other holy months also, O best of sages,
one should feed twice-born men with milk-rice and dakṣiṇā, according to one's ability.
Among the eighteen grains, and also other fruits and roots,
one should give them up for one year, except for the sake of medicine.

children.text: savṛṣaṃ kāñcanaṃ rudraṃ dharmarājaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should have made a golden <s>Rudra</s> with a bull, and also <s>Dharmarāja</s>.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ mātuliṅgaṃ ca vārtākaṃ panasaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A kūṣmāṇḍa gourd, a mātuliṅga citron, a vārtāka eggplant, and likewise a panasa jackfruit,
an āmrātaka, kapittha fruits, a kaliṅga fruit, and then a vāluka fruit,
śrīphala, aśvattha, badara, jambīra, and kadalī fruit,
and kāśmara and pomegranate: according to ability he should have these sixteen made of kāladhauta metal.
Radish, āmalaka, jambu, tintiḍī, and karamardaka,
kaṅkola, elā, katuṇḍīra, karīra, kuṭaja, and śamī,
audumbara, coconut, grape, and the two bṛhatī plants:
according to ability he should have these sixteen fruits made in silver.
He should make in copper a palm fruit and an agasti fruit,
a piṇḍāra fruit, a kāśmarya fruit, and a sūraṇa tuber,
a red āluka tuber, a kanakāhva, and a cirbhiṭa,
a citravallī fruit, and likewise a fruit born from the kūṭa-śālmalī,
mango, niṣpāva bean, madhuka, vaṭa, mudga, and paṭola;
a man should have these sixteen made in copper, according to his ability.
He should prepare a pair of water-pots on top of grain, with cloths,
and then he should have a bed made, with fine garments, as described above.
It should be furnished with three vessels of eatables and accompanied by <s>Yama</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and a bull.
Then, together with a cow, he should present it to a peaceful Brahmin who is a householder,
honoring him together with his wife on an auspicious day.
As crores of immortals dwell in all fruits,
so, through the vow of renouncing all fruits, may I have devotion to <s>Śiva</s>.
As <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Dharma</s> are always givers of endless fruit,
so, by the gift of fruits joined with them, may those two become grantors of boons to me.
As fruits are endless forever among the devotees of <s>Śiva</s>,
so may the attainment of endless fruit be mine in birth after birth.
As I see no difference among <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Arka</s>, and <s>Padmaja</s>,

children.text: tathā mamāstu viśvātmā śaṃkaraḥ śaṃkaraḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: so may <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the soul of the universe, always be auspicious to me.

children.text: iti dattvā ca tatsarvamalaṃkṛtya ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus given all that and adorned it with ornaments,
if he is able, he should give a bed complete with all accessories.
But if he is unable, he should give only the fruits as prescribed according to rule,
and the two golden figures, <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Dharma</s>, together with water-pots.
After giving them to a Brahmin, he should eat silently, avoiding oil,
and he should feed other twice-born men too, according to his ability.
The knowers of the Veda know this, for Bhāgavatas, Sauras, Vaiṣṇavas, and Yogins,
as the auspicious vow of renouncing all fruits.
And it should be performed by women according to their ability, O foremost of twice-born men.
In this world and in the next, there is nothing higher than this,
O best of sages, no vow exists that grants such endless fruit.
As many atoms as there are in gold, silver, and copper
when they are being ground into powder, O best of sages,
for that many thousands of ages he is honored in <s>Rudraloka</s>.

children.text: etatsamastakaluṣāpaharaṃ janānāmājīvanāya manujeṣu ca sarvadā syāt
children.translated_text: This should always, among human beings, remove all people's impurities and conduce to lifelong welfare.

children.text: janmāntareṣvapi na putraviyogaduḥkhamāpnoti dhāma ca puraṃdaralokajuṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: Even in later births he does not obtain the sorrow of separation from a son, and he obtains the abode frequented by the city of <s>Purandara</s>.

children.text: yo vā śṛṇoti puruṣo 'lpadhanaḥ paṭhedvā devālayeṣu bhavaneṣu ca dhārmikāṇām
children.translated_text: Or if a man of little wealth hears it or recites it in temples or in the houses of righteous people,
he too, with a body freed from sins here, attains the joy-giving place, the city of <s>Murāri</s>, O lord of sages.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Tell me, O <s>Nandīśa</s>, that vow which brings health to men and grants endless fruit,

children.text: yacchāntaye ca martyānāṃ vada nandīśa tadvratam ||
children.translated_text: and which also brings peace to mortals.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
That abode of the Soul of the universe, the supreme, eternal <s>Brahman</s>,
stands in the world in three forms, as sun, fire, and moon.
Having worshiped that, a man, O Brahmin, always obtains welfare.
Therefore on Sunday he should always be one who eats at night.
When the day of <s>Āditya</s> is joined with <s>Hasta</s>,
then, on that day, free from envy, he should perform the corruptedly transmitted one-meal observance.
Having, on Sunday at night, fed the best of Brahmins,
he should draw a red-sandal lotus with twelve petals,
and, placing <s>Sūrya</s> there with a salutation first,
then <s>Divākara</s> in the southeast, and after that <s>Vivasvant</s>,

children.text: bhagaṃ tu nairṛte devaṃ varuṇaṃ paścime dale
children.translated_text: and the god <s>Bhaga</s> in the southwest, <s>Varuṇa</s> on the western petal,
similarly <s>Mahendra</s> in the northwest, and <s>Āditya</s> likewise in the north,
and peaceful <s>Īśāna</s> in the northeast, he should install them with salutations.
On the petal east of the pericarp he should place the horses of <s>Sūrya</s>.
On the southern petal he should place the one named <s>Aryaman</s>, and <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s> on the western petal.

children.text: uttare tu raviṃ devaṃ karṇikāyāṃ ca bhāskaram ||
children.translated_text: In the north he should place the god <s>Ravi</s>, and in the pericarp <s>Bhāskara</s>.
Then, on that lotus, he should give an <s>arghya</s> (honor-offering) with red flowers and water,
with sesame and red sandal, and should recite this mantra.
You are the self of time, the self of all beings, the self of the Vedas, facing in all directions;
since you have the forms of fire and <s>Indra</s>, therefore protect me, O <s>Divākara</s>.

children.text: agnim īḍe namastubhyam iṣetvorje ca bhāskara
children.translated_text: I praise fire; homage to you. For food and strength, O <s>Bhāskara</s>;

children.text: agna āyāhi varada namaste jyotiṣāṃ pate ||
children.translated_text: O fire, come here, bestower of boons; homage to you, lord of lights.
Having given the <s>arghya</s>, he should then dismiss him. At night, avoiding oil,
he should eat. At the end of the year he should have made an excellent golden lotus,
and also, according to his ability, a two-armed man-shaped figure.

children.text: suvarṇaśṛṅgīṃ kapilāṃ mahārghyāṃ raupyaiḥ khuraiḥ kāṃsyadohāṃ savatsām
children.translated_text: A costly tawny cow with golden horns, silver hooves, bronze milking vessel, and calf,

children.text: pūrṇe guḍasyopari tāmrapātre nidhāya padmaṃ puruṣaṃ ca dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: he should place, along with the lotus and the figure, upon a copper vessel full of molasses, and give them.
Having worshiped a Brahmin with red garments, garlands, incense, and then with red gifts and golden horns,
and having made the formal intention, he should give the figure together with the lotus to one who is fit to receive many vows and gifts,
to one of unblemished form, self-controlled, a householder, and not arrogant.
Homage, homage to the destroyer of sin, the Soul of the universe, the one with seven horses,
to the abode of the <s>Sāman</s>, <s>Ṛg</s>, and <s>Yajus</s>, to the creator, the boat across the ocean of becoming, the generator of the world.
Whatever human being in this world follows this procedure for one full year
ascends, with sin destroyed, to the abode of the Sun, where rows of yak-tail fans are shaken.
Having obtained the consummation of <s>dharma</s> (religious merit), he becomes a king free from sorrow, pain, fear, and disease,
lord of the seven islands again and again, embodied in armor and endowed with immeasurable splendor.
And whatever woman, devoted to husband, teacher, and deity, follows this day-and-night rite whose form is the Veda,

children.text: sāpi lokamamareśavanditā yāti nārada raverna saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: she too, O <s>Nārada</s>, goes to the world of <s>Ravi</s>, honored by the lords of the immortals; there is no doubt.

children.text: yaḥ paṭhedapi śṛṇoti mānavaḥ paṭhyamānamatha vānumodate
children.translated_text: A human being who recites it, hears it, or approves while it is being recited

children.text: so'pi śakrabhuvanasthito'maraiḥ pūjyate vasati cākṣayaṃ divi ||
children.translated_text: also, dwelling in the world of <s>Śakra</s>, is worshiped by the immortals and lives imperishably in heaven.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Now I shall also tell another fruit of completing the rite at a saṃkrānti,
which is imperishable in the other world and grants the fruit of every desire.
At an <s>ayana</s> (solstice) or at an equinox, he should observe the saṃkrānti vow.
On the preceding day, having first cleaned his teeth, he should eat only once.
On the day of saṃkrānti, in the morning, bathing with sesame is prescribed.
At the Sun's transition he should make on the ground, with sandalwood paste,
an eight-petaled lotus with a pericarp, and on it he should invoke <s>Ravi</s>.
In the pericarp he should place <s>Sūrya</s>, then <s>Āditya</s> in the east.

children.text: nama uṣṇārciṣe yāmye namo ṛṅmaṇḍalāya ca ||
children.translated_text: In the south, 'Homage to the one with hot rays,' and homage also to the circle of the <s>Ṛg</s>.

children.text: namaḥ savitre nairṛtye vāruṇe tapanaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: In the southwest, homage to <s>Savitṛ</s>; in the west again he should place <s>Tapana</s>.

children.text: vāyavye tu bhagaṃ nyasya punaḥ punarathārcayet ||
children.translated_text: In the northwest he should install <s>Bhaga</s>, and then worship again and again.
In the north he should place <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, and always <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the northeast.
Then he should worship on the altar with perfumes, garlands, fruits, and food offerings.
For a Brahmin he should have made a water-pot, a golden vessel of ghee,
and a lotus according to his ability, and should present them.
With sandal-water and flowers he should set an <s>arghya</s> on the ground for the god:
To the All, to the one whose form is all, to the abode of all, to the self-born one;
homage to the endless one, homage to the establisher, lord of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Yajus</s>.

children.text: anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi samācaret
children.translated_text: By this procedure he should perform everything month by month.
At the end of the year, or else, a man should perform the whole rite in twelve parts.
At the end of the year, having satisfied the fire and the foremost Brahmins with ghee and milk-rice,
he should again give twelve pots together with cows, furnished with jewels and golden lotuses.

children.text: payasvinīḥ śīlavatīśca dadyāddharmaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ raupyakhuraiśca yuktāḥ
children.translated_text: He should give milch cows, well-behaved, provided with suitable horns and silver hoofs.

children.text: gāvo'ṣṭa vā sapta sakāṃsyadohā mālyāmbarā vā caturo'pyaśaktaḥ
children.translated_text: Or he may give eight cows, or seven with bronze milking-vessels, garlands, and garments; if unable, even four.
If afflicted by poverty, he should present even a single tawny cow to an excellent Brahmin.

children.text: haimīṃ ca dadyātpṛthivīṃ saśeṣāmākārya rūpyāmatha vā ca tāmrīm
children.translated_text: He should also give a golden image of the earth, complete; or, after making one, a silver or copper one.

children.text: paiṣṭīmaśaktaḥ pratimāṃ vidhāya sauvarṇasūryeṇa samaṃ pradadyāt
children.translated_text: If unable, having fashioned an image from flour, he should give it together with a golden sun.

children.text: na vittaśāṭhyaṃ puruṣo'tra kuryātkurvannadho yāti na saṃśayo'tra ||
children.translated_text: A man should not act deceitfully with his wealth in this matter; if he does so, he goes downward. There is no doubt about this.
As long as the earth, with the seven oceans, stands here together with the great mountains headed by <s>Mahendra</s>,
so long is he honored by hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s>, O <s>Nārada</s>, on the summit of heaven.
Then, when his karma is exhausted, he becomes lord of the seven islands, endowed with noble family and conduct.
At the beginning of creation he has a flawless body, a wife, and feet honored by many sons and descendants.

children.text: iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vātha bhaktyā vidhimakhilaṃ ravisaṃkramasya puṇyam
children.translated_text: Whoever reads or hears with devotion the entire sacred procedure for the sun's transition,

children.text: matimapi ca dadāti so'pi devairamarapaterbhavane prapūjyate ca ||
children.translated_text: and whoever even sets his mind upon it, is also worshiped by the gods in the palace of the lord of the immortals.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Listen, O <s>Nārada</s>; I shall tell the unsurpassed vow of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
called <s>Vibhūtidvādaśī</s>, honored by all the gods.
In <s>Kārttika</s>, <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Vaiśākha</s>, <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, or <s>Phālguna</s>,

children.text: āṣāḍhe vā daśamyāṃ tu śuklāyāṃ laghubhuṅnaraḥ
children.translated_text: or in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, on the bright tenth lunar day, a man should eat lightly,
and, having performed the evening twilight rite, the wise man should undertake the observance.
On the eleventh day, fasting and having worshiped <s>Janārdana</s>,
he should say, 'On the twelfth day, together with Brahmins, I shall take food, O lord.

children.text: tadavighnena me yātu saphalaṃ syācca keśava
children.translated_text: May that proceed for me without obstruction, and may it be fruitful, O <s>Keśava</s>.'

children.text: namo nārāyaṇāyeti vācyaṃ ca svapatā niśi ||
children.translated_text: Then, saying 'Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,' he should sleep at night.
Then, rising in the morning, bathed, having performed japa, and pure,
he should worship <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> with white garlands and unguents.
With 'homage to <s>Vibhūti</s>,' he should worship the feet, and with 'to <s>Aśoka</s>,' the knees;

children.text: namaḥ śivāyetyūrū ca viśvamūrte namaḥ kaṭim ||
children.translated_text: with 'homage to <s>Śiva</s>,' the thighs, and with 'homage to <s>Viśvamūrti</s>,' the waist.
With 'homage to <s>Kandarpa</s>,' the genitals, and with 'homage to <s>Āditya</s>,' the hands;
with '<s>Dāmodara</s>,' the belly, and with '<s>Vāsudeva</s>,' the chest.
With '<s>Mādhava</s>,' he should worship the breast of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the neck with 'homage to <s>Utkaṇṭhin</s>.'
He should worship the face with '<s>Śrīdhara</s>' and the hair with '<s>Keśava</s>,' O <s>Nārada</s>.
The back is worshiped with 'to <s>Śārṅgadhara</s>,' and the ears, indeed, with 'to <s>Varada</s>.'
By his own name he should worship the one whose hands hold conch, discus, sword, mace, and lotus,
and the head with 'homage to <s>Sarvātman</s>': thus, O Brahmin, he should perform the worship.
Having made, according to his ability, a golden fish together with a lotus,
the wise man should set it in front together with a water-pot.
A vessel of molasses, mixed with sesame seeds and wrapped in white cloth,
he should use while keeping vigil at night with stories from the <s>Itihāsas</s> and the like.
When the night has become morning, to a Brahmin with a family,
he should present the god, together with a golden lotus and a water-pot.

children.text: yathā na mucyase deva sadā sarvavibhūtibhiḥ
children.translated_text: 'As you, O god, are never separated from all prosperities,
so lift me up from the mire of all suffering and <s>saṃsāra</s>.'
The forms of the ten avatāras, month by month in order, O sage,
and also <s>Dattātreya</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s>, each furnished with a lotus,
he should give in this way for a full year, avoiding heretics.
Having thus completed, according to his ability, the twelve twelfth-day observances,
at the end of the year, together with a mountain of salt,
he should give a bed to the guru, O best of sages, along with a cow.
If he has the means, he should give a village, or a field with a house,
after worshiping the guru according to rule with garments, ornaments, and decorations.
Having also fed other excellent Brahmins according to his ability,
he should satisfy them with gifts of garments and cows, with masses of jewels and heaps of wealth.
A man of little wealth should perform it according to his ability, little by little.
And whoever is extremely poor, but devoted to <s>Mādhava</s>,
should perform it for two years by the procedure of flower-worship.
Whoever performs the <s>Vibhūtidvādaśī</s> vow by this procedure,
being freed from sin, rescues a hundred of his ancestors.
For a hundred thousand births he does not become one who shares in the fruit of sorrow.

children.text: na ca vyādhirbhavettasya na dāridryaṃ na bandhanam
children.translated_text: Nor does disease arise for him, nor poverty, nor bondage.

children.text: vaiṣṇavo vātha śaivo vā bhavejjanmani janmani ||
children.translated_text: In birth after birth he becomes either a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> or a <s>Śaiva</s>.
For as long as one hundred and eight thousand yugas may last,
so long he dwells in heaven, O Brahmin, and then he again becomes a king.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Long ago, in the <s>Rathantara</s> kalpa, there was a king named <s>Puṣpavāhana</s>,
renowned by that name in the worlds and equal to the sun in splendor.
By the four-faced one, pleased with his austerity, O <s>Nārada</s>,
a golden lotus was given to him, moving wherever he wished, O sage.
Together with all the worlds and with the inhabitants of his city, the king
then wandered as he wished through the islands and the world of the gods.
At the beginning of the kalpa, the seventh island belonged to that dweller in <s>Puṣkara</s>;
and because it was honored in the world, it is called <s>Puṣkaradvīpa</s>.
Because a lotus vehicle had been given to him by the god <s>Brahmā</s>,
therefore gods and <s>Dānavas</s> call him <s>Puṣpavāhana</s>.
Nothing in the three worlds was unreachable for him, as he stood upon the lotus from <s>Brahmā</s>, by the power of his austerity.
And his wife, O lord of sages, was incomparable, praised on every side by thousands of women.

children.text: nāmnā ca lāvaṇyavatī babhūva sā pārvatīveṣṭatamā bhavasya ||
children.translated_text: Her name was <s>Lāvaṇyavatī</s>, and she was most dear to <s>Bhava</s>, like <s>Pārvatī</s>.
He had ten thousand sons, righteous in soul and foremost among bowmen.
Seeing all that belonged to him, the king was filled again and again with wonder.

children.text: so'bhyāgataṃ vīkṣya munipravīraṃ prācetasaṃ vākyamidaṃ babhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that the eminent sage <s>Prācetasa</s> had arrived, he spoke these words:
"How has this spotless prosperity arisen for me, worshiped by immortals and mortals, and how has there come to be a wife who surpasses all heavenly beauties?

children.text: bhāryā mamālpatapasā paritoṣitena dattaṃ mamāmbujagṛhaṃ ca munīndra dhātrā ||
children.translated_text: With only slight austerity having pleased him, O lord of sages, <s>Dhātṛ</s> has given me this wife and this lotus-house.
When even a hundred crores of kings enter it, surrounded by ministers, elephants, masses of chariots, and men,

children.text: no lakṣyate kva gatamambaramadhya industārāgaṇairiva gataḥ paritaḥ sphuradbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: no one sees where they have gone, like the moon in the midst of the sky surrounded by shining hosts of stars.
Therefore, in some other birth from another mother's womb, what dharma or other act was done by me that caused the attainment of all these fruits?

children.text: bhagavanmayātha tanayair athavānayāpi bhadraṃ yadetadakhilaṃ kathaya pracetaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or was it done by my sons, or by this woman? O blessed <s>Prācetasa</s>, tell me all of this clearly."
Then the sage, perceiving the king's former birth and the history that was the cause of this overpowering wonder, replied:

children.text: janmābhavattava tu lubdhakule'tighore jātastvamapyanudinaṃ kila pāpakārī ||
children.translated_text: "Your birth was in a very terrible family of hunters, and you too became a sinner day after day.
Your body was joined with human limbs, foul-smelling, and covered all around with creatures and snakes.

children.text: na ca te suhṛn na sutabandhujano na tātastvādṛksvasā na jananī ca tadābhiśastā ||
children.translated_text: At that time you had no friend, no son or kinsman, no father, no sister like yourself, and no mother; you were accursed.

children.text: abhisaṃgatā paramabhīṣṭatamā vimukhī mahīśa tava yoṣidiyam
children.translated_text: This woman of yours, O lord of the earth, was joined to you as your most desired wife, though she was turned away from you.
Once there came a drought, exceedingly terrible, for the sake of food in that place.
Then, afflicted by hunger, you obtained nothing at all: no grain, fruit, meat, or the like.
Then you saw a great lake rich with lotuses, its banks surrounded by mud.

children.text: padmānyathādāya tato bahūni gataḥ puraṃ vaidiśanāmadheyam ||
children.translated_text: Taking many lotuses from it, you went to the city named <s>Vaidisha</s>.

children.text: tanmaulyalābhāya puraṃ samastaṃ bhrāntaṃ tvayāśeṣam ahas tadāsīt
children.translated_text: For the sake of gaining their price you wandered through the entire city for the whole day.

children.text: kretā na kaścitkamaleṣu jātaḥ śrānto bhṛśaṃ kṣutparipīḍitaśca ||
children.translated_text: No buyer for the lotuses appeared, and you were greatly exhausted and oppressed by hunger.
Together with your wife you sat down in the courtyard of a certain house.
Then at night you heard a great auspicious sound.
Together with your wife you went there, where that auspicious sound was.
There, in the middle of a pavilion, you saw an image of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
A courtesan named <s>Anangavatī</s>, at the completion of the <s>Vibhūtidvādaśī</s> vow
in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, was presenting to her guru an excellent mountain of salt,
and also a bed furnished with its accessories.
She had adorned <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> and a golden celestial tree.

children.text: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tatastābhyāmidaṃ ca paricintitam
children.translated_text: Seeing her, the two of you then considered this:
'What use are these lotuses to us? Better that <s>Viṣṇu</s> be adorned.'
Thus devotion then arose in the married pair, O king.
On that occasion, after worshiping <s>Keśava</s> and the mountain of salt,

children.text: śayyā ca puṣpaprakaraiḥ pūjitā bhūśca sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the bed was honored with heaps of flowers, and so was the ground everywhere.
Then <s>Anangavatī</s>, pleased, ordered that three hundred pieces of wealth
be given to those two, and then three hundred pieces of refined silver.
But the two did not accept it, relying on their great resolve.
Again <s>Anangavatī</s> had four kinds of food brought for them,
and here she said, O king, 'Please eat.'

children.text: tābhyāṃ tu tadapi tyaktaṃ bhokṣyāvo vai varānane
children.translated_text: But the two refused that also, saying, 'We two shall eat, O fair-faced one;
today, through the chance of fasting for you, there is happiness for us.'
Though from birth you two were very sinful, evil-doers, O firm-vowed one,
through that occasion a small trace of dharma arose between the two of you, O sinless one.
Thus, through that occasion, the night-vigil was performed by the two of you.

children.text: prabhāte ca tadā dattā śayyā salavaṇācalā ||
children.translated_text: And in the morning the bed together with the mountain of salt was given away.

children.text: grāmāśca gurave bhaktyā vipreṣu dvādaśaiva tu
children.translated_text: With devotion villages were given to the guru, and to the Brahmins exactly twelve
cows, adorned with garments and ornaments and accompanied by water-pots.
Food was also given together with friends, companions, the poor, the blind, and the helpless.
And that hunter couple was honored and dismissed.

children.text: sa bhavāṁl lubdhako jātaḥ sapatnīko nṛpeśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: You, O lord of kings, were born as that hunter together with your wife.
Because of that heap of lotuses and the worship of <s>Keśava</s>,
all your sins were destroyed, and this lotus mansion became yours.
By the greatness of that goodness, with only slight austerity, O king,
you gained the power to go wherever you wished.
The four-faced lord, <s>Janārdana</s> in the form of <s>Brahmā</s>, was pleased with you, O king of kings.
That courtesan <s>Anangavatī</s> is now the wife of <s>Kāmadeva</s>,

children.text: patnī sapatnī saṃjātā ratyāḥ prītiriti śrutā
children.translated_text: having become the co-wife of <s>Rati</s>, known as <s>Prīti</s>;
she brings joy in the worlds and is worshiped by all the immortals.
Therefore, O king of kings, leave <s>Puṣkara</s> on the surface of the earth,
resort to the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and perform the <s>Vibhūtidvādaśī</s> vow.
O king of kings, you will certainly attain nirvāṇa."
Having spoken thus, that sage vanished right there, O Brahmin.
And King <s>Puṣpavāhana</s> again did exactly as he had been instructed.
For one who performs this, O Brahmin, the unbroken vow should be observed,
with lotuses, somehow or other, for twelve twelfth-days, O sage.
The rites should be done according to one's ability, O sinless one, and gifts should be given to Brahmins.

children.text: na vittaśāṭhyaṃ kurvīta bhaktyā tuṣyati keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should not practice deceit about wealth; <s>Keśava</s> is satisfied by devotion.

children.text: iti kaluṣatridāraṇaṃ janānāmapi paṭhatīha śṛṇoti cātha bhaktyā
children.translated_text: Thus this tears away the threefold impurity of people; whoever here reads it and also hears it with devotion,

children.text: matimapi ca dadāti devaloke vasati sa koṭiśatāni vatsarāṇām ||
children.translated_text: and who also grants understanding, dwells in the world of the gods for hundreds of crores of years.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Now therefore I shall proclaim the unsurpassed sixth set of vows,
divine, taught by <s>Rudra</s>, and destructive of great sins.

children.text: naktamabdaṃ caritvā tu gavā sārdhaṃ kuṭumbine
children.translated_text: Having lived on food at night for a year, then, together with a cow, for a Brahmin with a household,

children.text: haimaṃ cakraṃ triśūlaṃ ca dadyādviprāya vāsasī ||
children.translated_text: one should give a golden discus and trident, and two garments to the Brahmin.
Thereafter, having the form of <s>Śiva</s>, he rejoices with us in <s>Śiva</s>'s world.
This is named the <s>Devavrata</s>, the destroyer of great sins.
But whoever, eating once a day for a year, gives an image of <s>Śiva</s> together with a golden bull,

children.text: dhenuṃ tilamayīṃ dadyātsa padaṃ yāti śāṃkaram
children.translated_text: and a cow made of sesame, reaches the state of <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
This is named the <s>Rudravrata</s>, the destroyer of sin and grief.
Whoever gives a golden blue lotus together with a vessel of sugar,
eating at night on alternate days, and at the end of the year gives it together with a bull,

children.text: sa vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ yāti līlāvratamidaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: goes to the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> state; this is remembered as the <s>Līlāvrata</s>.
During the four months beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, a man should avoid anointing himself with oil.
He should give the utensils for a meal, and he goes to the abode of <s>Hari</s>.
It is called here the <s>Prītivrata</s>, which brings affection among people.
Whoever, in the month of <s>Madhu</s>, abstains from curds, milk, ghee, and sugarcane juice,
should give fine garments together with vessels of rich liquids.
Having worshiped a pair of Brahmins, saying, 'May <s>Gaurī</s> be pleased with me,'
this is named the <s>Gaurīvrata</s>, bestowing the world of <s>Bhavānī</s>.

children.text: puṣyādau yastrayodaśyāṃ kṛtvā naktaṃ madhau punaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever, beginning with <s>Puṣya</s>, on the thirteenth lunar day, observes a night fast, and again in <s>Madhu</s>,
should give a golden aśoka, ten fingers high, together with sugarcane,
to a Brahmin, together with garments, saying, 'May <s>Pradyumna</s> be pleased.'
Having remained for a kalpa in the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the man becomes free from sorrow again.
This is named the <s>Kāmavrata</s>, always destructive of sorrow.
Whoever, in the vow beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, abstains from cutting his nails,
and from eggplant for the four months, together with jars of honey and ghee,
should then, on the <s>Kārttikī</s> day, present that in gold to a Brahmin.
He obtains the world of <s>Rudra</s>; this is remembered as the <s>Śivavrata</s>.
Whoever abstains from flowers during the two seasons of <s>Hemanta</s> and <s>Śiśira</s>,

children.text: puṣpatrayaṃ ca phālgunyāṃ kṛtvā śaktyā ca kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: and on the <s>Phālgunī</s> day makes three flowers, and a golden one according to his ability,
should give them at the two daily times, saying, 'May <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Keśava</s> be pleased.'

children.text: dattvā paraṃ padaṃ yāti saumyavratamidaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Having given them, he reaches the supreme state; this is remembered as the <s>Saumyavrata</s>.
Whoever, from the third lunar day beginning in <s>Phālguna</s>, abstains from salt,
at the completion should give a bed and a house furnished with its equipment.
Having worshiped a pair of Brahmins, saying, 'May <s>Bhavānī</s> be pleased,'
he dwells for a kalpa in the world of <s>Gaurī</s>; this is called the <s>Saubhāgyavrata</s>.
Then, having practiced silence at twilight, at the end of the year he should offer a small pot of ghee,
a pair of garments, sesame seeds, and a bell to a Brahmin.
He goes to the <s>Sārasvata</s> state, from which return is difficult.
This is named the <s>Sārasvatavrata</s>, bestowing beauty and knowledge.
A man, having worshiped <s>Lakṣmī</s> on the fifth lunar day, should fast.
At the end of the year he should give a golden lotus together with a cow.
He goes to the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> state and is possessed of <s>Lakṣmī</s> in birth after birth.
This is named the <s>Sampadvrata</s>, always destructive of sin.
Having performed smearing before <s>Śambhu</s> and before <s>Keśava</s>,
for as long as a year, he should afterwards give a cow together with a water-pot.

children.text: janmāyutaṃ sa rājā syāttataḥ śivapuraṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: For ten thousand births he becomes a king; thereafter he goes to <s>Śiva</s>'s city.
This is named the <s>Āyurvrata</s>, bestowing all desires.
Having bowed in one place to the aśvattha tree, <s>Bhāskara</s>, and <s>Gaṅgā</s>, restrained in speech,
a man should eat one meal a day for one year, free from envy.
At the end of the vow, a pair of Brahmins should be worshiped together with three cows.
He should give a golden tree; he obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.
This is named the <s>Kīrtivrata</s>, bestowing the fruits of prosperity and fame.

children.text: ghṛtena snapanaṃ kuryācchambhor vā keśavasya ca
children.translated_text: One should perform a bathing rite with ghee for <s>Śambhu</s> or for <s>Keśava</s>,
having made a cow-dung maṇḍala with unbroken grains and excellent flowers.
At the end of the year, together with a sesame-cow, a golden lotus,
pure and eight fingers in measure, should be given; he is honored in <s>Śiva</s>'s world.
And this is for a singer of the <s>Sāman</s>; it is called here the <s>Sāmavrata</s>.
On the ninth lunar day, eating once a day, he should also honor maidens according to his ability.
Having fed them, he should give a seat, a golden bodice, and garments.

children.text: haimaṃ siṃhaṃ ca viprāya dattvā śivapadaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: Having given a golden lion to a Brahmin, he goes to the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
For a hundred million births he becomes handsome and unconquered by enemies.
This is named the <s>Vīravrata</s>, and it gives happiness to women.
Whoever observes a milk-vow on the fifteenth lunar day for a full year,
at the end of the year, after performing a śrāddha, should give five milk-giving cows,
and tawny garments together with water-pots.

children.text: sa yāti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tārayecchatam
children.translated_text: He goes to the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> world and rescues a hundred ancestors.

children.text: kalpānte rājarājaḥ syāt pitṛvratam idaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the kalpa he becomes a king of kings; this is remembered as the <s>Pitṛvrata</s>.
For the four months beginning with <s>Caitra</s>, one should give water unasked.
At the end of the vow, one should give a jewel together with food and garments,
and a vessel of sesame and gold; he is honored in <s>Brahmā</s>'s world.
At the end of a kalpa he certainly becomes a king; this is called the <s>Ānanda-vrata</s>.
Having performed the bathing of the Lord with <s>pañcāmṛta</s> for a year,
at the end of the year he should again give a cow, indeed, with <s>pañcāmṛta</s>.

children.text: viprāya dadyācchaṅkhaṃ ca sa padaṃ yāti śāṃkaram
children.translated_text: He should also give a conch to a Brahmin; he goes to the station of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
At the end of a kalpa he becomes a king; this is remembered as the <s>Dhṛti-vrata</s>.
A man, having avoided meat, should become a giver of a cow at the end of the year.
Likewise he should give a golden deer; he obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.
This is called the <s>Ahiṃsā-vrata</s>; at the end of a kalpa he becomes a king.
In the month of <s>Māgha</s>, after bathing at dawn, he should worship a married couple.
Having fed them according to his ability, he should honor them with garlands, garments, and ornaments.
He dwells in <s>Sūrya-loka</s> for a kalpa; this is remembered as the <s>Sūrya-vrata</s>.
Beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, for the four months, a man should bathe in the morning.
He should give food to Brahmins, and on the <s>Kārttikī</s> day he should be a giver of a cow.

children.text: sa vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ yāti viṣṇuvratamidaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: He goes to the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> station; this is the auspicious <s>Viṣṇu-vrata</s>.
From the beginning of one solar course until the next, he should avoid flowers and ghee.
At its end, he should give flower garlands together with a ghee-cow,
and, after giving ghee-rice pudding to a Brahmin, he goes to the station of <s>Śiva</s>.
This is named the <s>Śīla-vrata</s>, giving the fruit of good conduct and health.
Whoever gives lamps at twilight and avoids oil for a full year,
at the end of the year should give a lamp, and also a golden discus and trident.

children.text: vastrayugmaṃ ca viprāya tejasvī sa bhavediha
children.translated_text: He should give a pair of garments to a Brahmin; here he becomes radiant.
He obtains <s>Rudra-loka</s>; this is remembered as the <s>Dīpti-vrata</s>.
On the third lunar day beginning with <s>Kārttikī</s>, having eaten barley prepared with cow urine,
he should practice eating only at night for one year; at the end of the year he should be a giver of a cow.
He dwells in <s>Gaurī-loka</s> for a kalpa, and thereafter becomes a king here.
This is named the <s>Rudra-vrata</s>, always producing welfare.
And whoever, in the month of <s>Caitra</s>, avoids fragrant unguent,
after giving to a Brahmin a shell filled with perfume and two white garments,
obtains the station of <s>Varuṇa</s>; this is remembered as the <s>Dṛḍha-vrata</s>.
In <s>Vaiśākha</s>, after avoiding flowers and salt, he should then be a giver of a cow.

children.text: bhūtvā viṣāde kalpaṃ sthitvā rājā bhavediha
children.translated_text: Having remained for a kalpa in <s>Viṣāda</s> or in that unclear state, he becomes a king here.
This is named the <s>Kānti-vrata</s>, giving the fruit of beauty and fame.
Having made a golden cosmic egg, accompanied by a heap of sesame seeds,

children.text: tryahaṃ tilaprado bhūtvā vahniṃ saṃtarpya sadvijam ||
children.translated_text: having been a giver of sesame for three days, and having satisfied the fire and a good Brahmin,
he should worship a Brahmin couple with garlands, garments, and ornaments.
According to his ability, with more than three palas, he should say, 'May <s>Viśvātman</s> be pleased.'
On an auspicious day he should give it; he goes to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, from which there is no rebirth.
This is named the <s>Brahma-vrata</s>, bestowing the state of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
And whoever gives an <s>ubhayamukhī</s> cow, accompanied by abundant gold,
and remains for a day under a milk-vow, goes to the supreme station.
This is named the <s>Dhenu-vrata</s>, from which return is difficult.
Having remained under a milk-vow for three days, he should give a golden wish-fulfilling tree,
more than a pala in weight, according to his ability, and furnished with rice.
Having given it, he goes to the station of <s>Brahmā</s>; this is remembered as the <s>Kalpa-vrata</s>.
Whoever, fasting for a month, gives a beautiful cow to a Brahmin,

children.text: sa vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ yati bhīmavratamidaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: goes to the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> station; this is remembered as the <s>Bhīma-vrata</s>.

children.text: dadyād viṃśatpalādūrdhvaṃ mahīṃ kṛtvā tu kāñcanīm
children.translated_text: He should give a golden earth, made with more than twenty palas of gold.
Remaining for a day under a milk-vow, he is honored in <s>Rudra-loka</s>.
This is declared to be the <s>Dharā-vrata</s>, lasting for seven hundred kalpas.
In the month of <s>Māgha</s>, or else in <s>Caitra</s>, he should be a giver of a molasses-cow.
On the third lunar day, through the <s>Guḍa-vrata</s>, he is honored in <s>Gaurī-loka</s>.
This is named the <s>Mahā-vrata</s>, producing supreme bliss.
Whoever, fasting for a fortnight, gives a pair of tawny cows to a Brahmin,
obtains <s>Brahma-loka</s>, which is greatly honored by gods and asuras.
At the end of a kalpa he becomes a king of kings; this is remembered as the <s>Prabhā-vrata</s>.
Eating once a day for a year, he should give a water-pot together with food.
He dwells in <s>Śiva-loka</s> for a kalpa; this is remembered as the <s>Prāpti-vrata</s>.
He should eat at night on the eighth lunar days, and at the end of the year he should give a cow.
He goes to the city of <s>Purandara</s>; this is called the <s>Sugati-vrata</s>.
Whoever gives firewood to a Brahmin through the four seasons beginning with the rains,

children.text: ghṛtadhenuprado'nte ca sa paraṃ brahma gacchati
children.translated_text: and at the end gives a ghee-cow, goes to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
This is named the <s>Vaiśvānara-vrata</s>, destroying all sins.
And whoever, eating at night on the eleventh lunar day, presents a discus,

children.text: samānte vaiṣṇavaṃ haimaṃ sa viṣṇoḥ padamāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: at the end of the year, a golden <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> emblem; he obtains the station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
This is named the <s>Kṛṣṇa-vrata</s>; at the end of a kalpa he becomes a sharer in kingship.
Eating rice pudding, at the end of the year he should give a pair of cows to a Brahmin.
He obtains <s>Lakṣmī-loka</s>; this is remembered as the <s>Devī-vrata</s>.
On the seventh lunar day, eating at night, he should give a milk-giving cow at the end of the year.
He obtains <s>Sūrya-loka</s>; this is remembered as the <s>Bhānu-vrata</s>.
On the fourth lunar day, eating at night, he should give a golden elephant at the end of the year.
The vow is named the <s>Vaināyaka-vrata</s>, giving the fruit of <s>Śiva-loka</s>.
Having given up large fruits for four months, he should give to a twice-born man,
in <s>Kārttika</s>, golden ones together with a pair of cows.
This is named the <s>Phala-vrata</s>, giving the fruit of <s>Viṣṇu-loka</s>.
And whoever fasts on the seventh lunar day, at the end of the year should give a golden lotus,
and cows according to his ability, furnished with gold, food, and a pot.
This is named the <s>Saura-vrata</s>, giving the fruit of <s>Sūrya-loka</s>.
Whoever completes twelve twelfth lunar days with fasting as well...
A man should honor Brahmins with cows, garments, and gold according to his ability.
He obtains the supreme state; this is remembered as the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-vow.

children.text: kārttikyāṃ ca vṛṣotsargaṃ kṛtvā naktaṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: On the full moon of Kārttika, having released a bull, he should observe a night-fast.
He obtains the state of <s>Śiva</s>; this is remembered as the yearly vow.
At the end of a kṛcchra observance, the giver of a cow should provide food for Brahmins according to his ability.
He goes to the state of <s>Śaṅkara</s>; this vow is the <s>Prājāpatya</s>.
On the fourteenth lunar day he should eat only at night, and at the end of a year he should give a herd of cows.
He obtains the state of <s>Śiva</s>; this is the <s>Traiyambaka</s> vow.
Having fasted for seven nights, he should give a pot of ghee to a twice-born man.
They call this the ghee-vow, bestowing the fruit of <s>Brahmā</s>'s world.
During the rains he should sleep in the open air and give a milk-yielding cow with its calf.
He dwells always in <s>Śakra</s>'s world; this is remembered as the <s>Indra</s>-vow.

children.text: anagnipakkam aśnāti tṛtīyāyāṃ tu yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who on the third lunar day eats food not cooked by fire,
after giving a cow, reaches <s>Śiva</s>, from whom return is hard to obtain.
And here it brings joy to men; this is remembered as the vow of welfare.
He who gives, while fasting, a golden chariot weighing more than two palas and furnished with a pair of horses,
dwells in heaven for a hundred kalpas.
At the end of the kalpa he becomes a king of kings; this is remembered as the horse-vow.
In the same way a man should give a golden chariot joined with two elephants.
Then, O king, he dwells in <s>Satyaloka</s> for a thousand kalpas,
having first undertaken a fast; this is remembered as the elephant-vow.
Having completed a fast, at the end of the year he should become a giver of cows.
He obtains lordship over the yakṣas; this is remembered as the vow of happiness.

children.text: niśi kṛtvā jale vāsaṃ prabhāte goprado bhavet
children.translated_text: After spending the night dwelling in water, in the morning he should become a giver of cows.
He obtains the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>; this is called the <s>Varuṇa</s>-vow.

children.text: cāndrāyaṇaṃ ca yaḥ kuryāddhaimaṃ candraṃ nivedayet
children.translated_text: And he who performs the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> observance should offer a golden moon.
This is called the moon-vow, bestowing the fruit of the moon-world.
In Jyeṣṭha, one practicing the five fires should in the evening give a golden cow, on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days, and he goes to heaven.
This is remembered as the <s>Rudra</s>-vow.
Once, on the third lunar day, he should make a canopy in a temple of <s>Śiva</s>.
At the end of the year, giving a cow, he goes; this is called the <s>Bhavānī</s>-vow.
In Māgha, on the seventh lunar day, he should spend the night in wet garments and then give a cow.
Having dwelt in heaven for a kalpa, he becomes a king here; this is the wind-vow.
Having fasted for three nights, on the Phālgunī day he should give an auspicious house.
He obtains the world of <s>Āditya</s>; this is remembered as the dwelling-vow.
Fasting, he should worship the divine couple at the three twilights with ornaments.
Here, by the <s>Indra</s>-vow and the like, he obtains food, cows, and liberation.
On the bright second lunar day, having given to the moon a vessel of salt,
and at the end of the year having given a cow to a Brahmin, he goes to the temple of <s>Śiva</s>.
At the end of the kalpa he becomes a king of kings; this is remembered as the <s>Soma</s>-vow.
On the first lunar day, eating only once, at the end of the year he should give a tawny cow.
He goes to the state of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>; this is remembered as the <s>Śiva</s>-vow.
On the tenth lunar day, eating only once, at the end of the year he should give ten cows.
He should also give the directions with golden images; he becomes lord of the cosmic egg.
This is the vow called the <s>Viśva</s>-vow, destroying great sins.
Whoever recites or hears this unsurpassed set of sixty vows,
becomes lord of the gandharvas for a hundred manvantaras.
O <s>Nārada</s>, this meritorious set of sixty vows has been spoken to you as universally beneficial.

children.text: śrotuṃ tavecchā tadudīrayāmi priyeṣu kiṃ vākathanīyam asti ||
children.translated_text: If you wish to hear something else, I shall declare it; among dear ones, what is there that should not be told?
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:

children.text: nairmalyaṃ bhāvaśuddhiśca vinā snānaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: Purity and cleansing of intention do not exist without bathing.
Therefore bathing is first prescribed for the purification of the mind.
One should perform bathing with waters, whether drawn up or not drawn up.
The wise knower of mantras should also prepare a tīrtha (sacred bathing place) with the root-mantra.
'Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' is declared to be the root-mantra.
Holding darbha grass in his hand, having sipped water according to rule, restrained and pure,
the discerning man should prepare, on all sides, a square four hands in measure,
and should invoke <s>Gaṅgā</s> with these mantras.
'You are born from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s foot, a <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, having <s>Viṣṇu</s> as your deity.
Protect us from that sin which lasts from birth until death.
<s>Vāyu</s> has said that there are three crores and a half-crore of tīrthas,

children.text: divi bhuvyantarikṣe ca tāni te santi jāhnavi ||
children.translated_text: in heaven, on earth, and in the midspace; those, O <s>Jāhnavī</s>, are present in you.

children.text: nandinītyeva te nāma deveṣu nalinīti ca
children.translated_text: Among the gods your name is <s>Nandinī</s>, and also <s>Nalinī</s>.

children.text: dakṣā pṛthvī ca vihagā viśvakāyāmṛtā śivā ||
children.translated_text: You are <s>Dakṣā</s>, <s>Pṛthvī</s>, <s>Vihagā</s>, <s>Viśvakāyā</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, and <s>Śivā</s>.
You are <s>Vidyādharī</s>, <s>Supraśāntā</s>, and also <s>Viśvaprasādinī</s>.

children.text: kṣemā ca jāhnavī caiva śāntā śāntipradāyinī ||
children.translated_text: You are <s>Kṣemā</s> and <s>Jāhnavī</s>, and also <s>Śāntā</s>, giver of peace.
These holy names should be proclaimed at the time of bathing.
There the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, who goes in three paths, becomes present.
With the hollow of the hands joined, after reciting the mantra seven times,
he should again place water on the head three, four, five, or seven times.
In the same way he should bathe with clay, having addressed it according to rule.
'O earth crossed by horses, crossed by chariots, crossed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: mṛttike hara me pāpaṃ yanmayā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: O clay, remove my sin, whatever wrong deed has been done by me.
You were lifted up by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the form of the boar, the hundred-armed one.
O clay, you were given by <s>Brahmā</s> and consecrated by <s>Kāśyapa</s>.

children.text: āruhya mama gātrāṇi sarvaṃ pāpaṃ pracodaya ||
children.translated_text: Mounting my limbs, drive away all sin.

children.text: mṛttike dehi naḥ puṣṭiṃ tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: O clay, give us nourishment; everything is established in you.
Homage to you, source and lower fire-drill of all the worlds, O good-vowed one.'

children.text: evaṃ snātvā tataḥ paścādācamya ca vidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: Having bathed in this way, then afterward having sipped water according to rule,

children.text: utthāya vāsasī śukle śuddhe tu paridhāya vai
children.translated_text: and having risen, he should put on two clean white garments.
Then he should perform tarpaṇa, for the refreshment of the three worlds.
The gods, yakṣas, nāgas, gandharvas, apsarases, and asuras,

children.text: krūrāḥ sarpāḥ suparṇāśca taravo jambukāḥ khagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the fierce beings, serpents, suparṇas, trees, jackals, and birds,
those whose support is air, those whose support is water, and likewise those who move in the sky,

children.text: nirādhārāśca ye jīvā ye tu dharmaratāstathā ||
children.translated_text: those living beings who are without support, and those who are devoted to <s>dharma</s> as well:
for their refreshment this water is given by me.
Wearing the sacred thread in the upavīta manner, he should offer to the gods; then he should become nivītī.
With devotion he should satisfy human beings, and likewise the mind-born sons of <s>Brahmā</s>, the sages.
<s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sananda</s>, and the third, <s>Sanātana</s>,
and <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Āsuri</s>, <s>Voḍhu</s>, and <s>Pañcaśikha</s>:
may all of them always attain satisfaction through the water given by me.
He should satisfy <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Kratu</s>,

children.text: pracetasaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca bhṛguṃ nāradameva ca
children.translated_text: and <s>Pracetas</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Nārada</s> as well.
He should satisfy all the divine brahmarṣis with unbroken grains and water.

children.text: apasavyaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā savyaṃ jānvācya bhūtale
children.translated_text: Then, having placed the sacred thread over the right shoulder, and having put the left knee on the ground,
the ancestors called <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>, <s>Saumyas</s>, <s>Haviṣmants</s>, and also <s>Uṣmapās</s>,
the <s>Sukālīns</s>, <s>Barhiṣads</s>, and again the other <s>Vājyapās</s>,
the ancestors should be satisfied with devotion, using water with sesame and sandalwood.
Homage to <s>Yama</s>, to <s>Dharmarāja</s>, to <s>Mṛtyu</s>, and to <s>Antaka</s>,
to <s>Vaivasvata</s>, to <s>Kāla</s>, and to the destroyer of all beings,
to <s>Audumbara</s>, to <s>Dadhna</s>, to <s>Nīla</s>, and to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
to <s>Vṛkodara</s>, to <s>Citra</s>, and to <s>Citragupta</s> indeed.
A wise man, holding darbha grass in his hand, should satisfy the ancestors according to rule.
After satisfying his father and the others by name and lineage, and also his maternal grandfathers,
with devotion and according to rule, he should utter this mantra:
Those who are not my kinsmen, or who are my kinsmen, and those who were my kinsmen in another birth,
may they all attain complete satisfaction, as well as anyone who desires it from us.
Then, having sipped water according to rule, he should draw a lotus before him.
With unbroken grains and flowers, with water and red sandalwood,
he should carefully give an arghya and recite the names of the Sun.
Homage to you who have the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; homage indeed to you whose face is <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Homage always to you of a thousand rays; homage to you of all splendor.
Homage to you, <s>Śiva</s>, lord of all; homage to you, affectionate to all.
Homage to you, lord of the world, adorned with divine sandalwood.
Homage to you seated on a lotus, adorned with earrings and armlets.
Homage to you, lord of all worlds; you awaken the whole world.

children.text: sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ caiva sarvaṃ paśyasi sarvaga
children.translated_text: You see both good and evil, O omnipresent one.
Homage to you, true god; be gracious to me, O <s>Bhāskara</s>.
Homage to you, O <s>Divākara</s>; homage to you, O <s>Prabhākara</s>.

children.text: evaṃ sūryaṃ namaskṛtya triḥ kṛtvātha pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Having thus bowed to the Sun, and then having circumambulated three times,

children.text: dvijaṃ gāṃ kāñcanaṃ spṛṣṭvā tato viṣṇugṛhaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: he should touch a twice-born man, a cow, and gold, and then go to the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
After this I shall describe <s>Prayāga</s>,
as it was formerly told by <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> to the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.

children.text: bhārate tu yadā vṛtte prāptarājye pṛthāsute
children.translated_text: When the Bhārata war had taken place and the son of <s>Pṛthā</s> had obtained the kingdom,
at that time King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, son of <s>Kuntī</s>,
was tormented by grief for his brothers, reflecting again and again.
King <s>Suyodhana</s> had been the lord of eleven armies;

children.text: asmānsaṃtāpya bahuśaḥ sarve te nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: after tormenting us many times, all those men have gone to destruction.
Taking refuge in <s>Vāsudeva</s>, only the five <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> remain.

children.text: hatvā bhīṣmaṃ ca droṇaṃ ca karṇaṃ caiva mahābalam
