children.translated_text: Having killed <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and the mighty <s>Karṇa</s>,
and King <s>Duryodhana</s> together with his sons and brothers,

children.text: rājāno nihatāḥ sarve ye cānye śūramāninaḥ
children.translated_text: all the kings have been slain, and others too who considered themselves heroes.

children.text: kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogairjīvitena vā ||
children.translated_text: What use is kingdom to us, O <s>Govinda</s>? What use are enjoyments, or even life?
Thinking, "Alas, how painful!" the king became overcome with distress.
Motionless and without spirit, he remained for a while with his face cast down.

children.text: labdhasaṃjño yadā rājā cintayansa punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When the king regained consciousness, he reflected again and again:

children.text: kataro viniyogo vā niyamaṃ tīrthameva ca ||
children.translated_text: What application, or observance, or sacred ford is there
by which I may quickly be released from the guilt of great sin,
and where, having stayed, a man goes to the unsurpassed world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>?

children.text: kathaṃ pṛcchāmi vai kṛṣṇaṃ yenedaṃ kārito'smyaham
children.translated_text: How can I ask <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, by whom I have been made to do this?

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ kathaṃ pṛcche yasya putraśataṃ hatam ||
children.translated_text: How can I ask <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, whose hundred sons have been killed?

children.text: vyāsaṃ kathamahaṃ pṛcche yasya gotrakṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: How can I ask <s>Vyāsa</s>, whose lineage I have destroyed?
Thus <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the king of <s>dharma</s>, fell into distress.
All the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> wept, overwhelmed by grief for their brothers.

children.text: ye ca tatra mahātmānaḥ sametāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: And those great-souled ones there, known as the assembled <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>,

children.text: kuntī ca draupadī caiva ye ca tatra samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kuntī</s> and <s>Draupadī</s> too, and all who had gathered there,
all fell upon the ground, weeping on every side.
In <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> came to know of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,
that he had fallen into distress and was weeping in sorrow.
After only a short time, the great ascetic <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>
arrived at <s>Hastinapura</s> and stood at the royal gate.
The doorkeeper, seeing him, quickly told the king:

children.text: tvāṃ draṣṭukāmo mārkaṇḍeyo dvāri tiṣṭhatyasau muniḥ
children.translated_text: "The sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, wishing to see you, is standing there at the door."
Then the son of <s>Dharma</s> hurried to the gate.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:

children.text: svāgataṃ te mahābhāga svāgataṃ te mahāmune
children.translated_text: Welcome to you, greatly fortunate one; welcome to you, great sage.

children.text: adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me tāritaṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: Today my birth is fruitful; today my family has been carried across.
Today my ancestors are satisfied, now that you have been seen, O great sage.
Today I am one whose body is purified, because I have had an audience together with you.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Having seated him on a throne, with washing of the feet, worship, and the other rites,

children.text: yudhiṣṭhiro mahātmā vai pūjayāmāsa taṃ munim ||
children.translated_text: the great-souled <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> duly honored that sage.

children.text: tataḥ sa tuṣṭo mārkaṇḍaḥ pūjitaścāha taṃ nṛpam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, pleased and honored, said to that king:
'Tell me quickly, O king, for what reason you have wept.

children.text: kena vā viklavībhūtaḥ kā bādhā te kimapriyam ||
children.translated_text: By what have you become agitated? What trouble is yours, what unpleasant thing?'
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
'What has happened to us for the sake of the kingdom, O great sage,
knowing all this, I have fallen under the power of anxiety.'
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
'Listen, O king, mighty-armed one, to what is established as the <s>kṣatriya-dharma</s> (warrior's duty).

children.text: naiva dṛṣṭaṃ raṇe pāpaṃ yudhyamānasya dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: No sin at all is seen in battle for an intelligent man who is fighting.
How much less, then, for a kṣatriya in particular, when it is by the <s>rāja-dharma</s> (kingly duty).

children.text: tadevaṃ hṛdayaṃ kṛtvā tasmātpāpaṃ na cintayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made your heart thus firm, therefore you should not think of sin.'

children.text: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā praṇamya śirasā munim
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, bowing with his head to the sage,
asked, filled with humility, about that which destroys all sins.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
'I ask you, O very wise one, who always sees the three worlds:

children.text: kathaya tvaṃ samāsena yena mucyeta kilbiṣāt ||
children.translated_text: tell me briefly that by which one may be freed from guilt.'
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
'Listen, O king, mighty-armed one, to that which destroys all sins:
going to <s>Prayāga</s> is the best act for men whose deeds are meritorious.'
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
'Blessed lord, I wish to hear how, in an ancient kalpa, it was established,
as it was properly told by <s>Brahmā</s>, the chief of the gods, O sage.
How is the going to <s>Prayāga</s> for men there, and what is its nature?

children.text: mṛtānāṃ kā gatistatra snātānāṃ tatra kiṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: What is the destiny there of those who die, and what is the fruit there for those who bathe?

children.text: ye vasanti prayāge tu brūhi teṣāṃ ca kiṃ phalam
children.translated_text: And those who dwell at <s>Prayāga</s>, tell me what their fruit is.

children.text: etanme sarvamākhyāhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me ||
children.translated_text: Tell me all this; for my curiosity is supreme.'
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: kathayiṣyāmi te vatsa yacchreṣṭhaṃ tatra yatphalam
children.translated_text: 'I shall tell you, child, what is best there and what fruit there is.

children.text: purā hi sarvaviprāṇāṃ kathyamānaṃ mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Long ago I heard it being told among all the Brahmins.
From <s>Prayāga</s> and <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s> as far as the ancient pool of <s>Vāsuki</s>,
the nāgas <s>Kambala</s> and <s>Aśvatara</s>, and the nāga <s>Bahumūlaka</s>,
this is the field of <s>Prajāpati</s>, famed in the three worlds.

children.text: tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste'punarbhavāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who bathe there go to heaven; those who die there have no rebirth.

children.text: tato brahmādayo devā rakṣāṃ kurvanti saṃgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> gather and keep guard there.
There are also many other auspicious <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred bathing places), removers of all sin,
which cannot be described, O king, even in many hundreds of years.
I shall proclaim in brief the praise of <s>Prayāga</s>.
Sixty thousand bows' lengths guard the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.
<s>Savitṛ</s>, drawn by seven horses, always guards the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: prayāgaṃ tu viśeṣeṇa sadā rakṣati vāsavaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Vāsava</s> especially always guards <s>Prayāga</s>.
<s>Hari</s>, assembled with the deities, guards the circle.
<s>Maheśvara</s>, the trident-bearing lord, always guards that banyan tree.

children.text: sthānaṃ rakṣanti vai devāḥ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: The gods indeed guard that auspicious place which removes all sin.
The world, covered by unrighteousness, does not reach that state.
When even a small or very small sin is yours, O lord of men,
for one who remembers <s>Prayāga</s>, all of it comes to destruction.
By seeing that <s>tīrtha</s>, even by reciting its name,
or by touching its clay, a man is released from sin.

children.text: pañca kuṇḍāni rājendra teṣāṃ madhye tu jāhnavī
children.translated_text: There are five ponds, O king of kings; in their midst is the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.

children.text: prayāgasya praveśe tu pāpaṃ naśyati tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: At the entrance to <s>Prayāga</s>, sin perishes at that very moment.
From thousands of yojanas away, by remembering the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a man,

children.text: api duṣkṛtakarmā tu labhate paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: even one whose deeds are evil, obtains the supreme state.
By praising her he is freed from sin; seeing her, he sees auspicious things.

children.text: avagāhya ca pītvā tu punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: Plunging into her and drinking, he purifies his family up to the seventh generation.
Truth-speaking, with anger conquered, established in non-injury,
following <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), knowing reality, and devoted to the welfare of cows and Brahmins,
one who has bathed between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s> is freed from guilt.
Thinking upon his desires in his mind, he obtains them in great abundance.
Then, having gone to <s>Prayāga</s>, protected by all the gods,
he should dwell for a month as a celibate student and satisfy the ancestors and the gods.
Wherever he is born, he obtains the desires he has sought.

children.text: tapanasya sutā devī triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā
children.translated_text: The goddess daughter of <s>Tapana</s>, famed in the three worlds,
the greatly blessed river <s>Yamunā</s>, has come together there.
There the god <s>Maheśvara</s> himself is always present.

children.text: duṣprāpyaṃ mānuṣaiḥ puṇyaṃ prayāgaṃ tu yudhiṣṭhira
children.translated_text: Difficult for human beings to obtain is the merit of <s>Prayāga</s>, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
Gods, dānavas, gandharvas, seers, siddhas, and cāraṇas,
having touched it, O king of kings, dwell in the heavenly world.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen again, O king, to the greatness of <s>Prayāga</s>,
hearing which one is freed from all sins; of this there is no doubt.
For the afflicted, the poor, and those of fixed resolve,

children.text: sthānamuktaṃ prayāgaṃ tu nākhyeyaṃ tu kadācana ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prayāga</s> has been declared a place of liberation; it should never be left unspoken.

children.text: vyādhito yadi vā dīno vṛddho vāpi bhavennaraḥ
children.translated_text: If a man should be diseased, or wretched, or even old,
and should give up his life between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>,
then in aerial cars shining with the color of blazing gold, resembling the sun,
that man sports in heaven among gandharvas and apsarases.
He obtains the desires he has sought, so the foremost seers say.
With divine things made of every jewel, crowded with many banners,
filled with beautiful women and marked by auspicious signs, he rejoices.
While asleep he is awakened by the loud sounds of singing and instruments;
as long as he does not remember birth, so long he is honored in heaven.
Then, fallen away from heaven, his karma exhausted and dropped from the sky,
he is born in a prosperous family full of gold and jewels.
He remembers that very <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford), and by that remembrance he goes there.
Whether he is in his own country, in the forest, in a foreign land, or at home,
whoever, even while remembering <s>Prayāga</s>, gives up his breaths,
obtains the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, so the foremost sages say.
Where the trees bear the fruits of all desires and the earth is made of gold,

children.text: ṛṣayo munayaḥ siddhāstatra loke sa gacchati ||
children.translated_text: to that world he goes, where sages, seers, and perfected beings dwell.
On the fair, auspicious bank of the <s>Mandākinī</s>, surrounded by a thousand women,
he rejoices together with the sages through his meritorious deed here.
In heaven he is worshipped by perfected beings, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and deities;
then, fallen away from heaven, he becomes lord of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.

children.text: tataḥ śubhāni karmāṇi cintayānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, thinking again and again of auspicious deeds,
he becomes virtuous and endowed with wealth here; there is no doubt.
With deed, mind, and speech established in <s>dharma</s> (normative order) and truth,
whoever gives a cow between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>,
or gold, jewels, pearls, or any other possession,
whether for his own purpose, for an ancestral rite, or for the worship of deities,
for him that <s>tīrtha</s> is fruitful, and he obtains merit properly.
Thus one should not accept anything at a <s>tīrtha</s> or in holy shrines,
and on all such occasions, a twice-born man should be vigilant.
Whoever gives a tawny cow of reddish color,
with golden horns, silver hooves, a bronze milking vessel, and rich in milk,
at <s>Prayāga</s>, having caused a worthy learned Brahmin to receive it according to rule,
clad in white garments, peaceful, knowing <s>dharma</s>, and versed in the <s>Veda</s>,
that cow should be given to him at the confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: along with very valuable garments and various jewels.

children.text: yāvadromāṇi tasyā goḥ santi gātreṣu sattama
children.translated_text: As many hairs as that cow has on her limbs, O best one,
for so many thousands of years he is honored in the world of heaven.
Wherever he obtains birth, that cow is born for him there.

children.text: na ca paśyati taṃ ghoraṃ narakaṃ tena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: By that deed he does not see that dreadful hell,
and, reaching the northern <s>Kurus</s>, he rejoices for an imperishable time.
Rather than hundreds of thousands of cows, one should give a single milk-giving cow;
one cow carries across sons, wives, and servants alike.
Therefore, among all gifts, the gift of a cow is especially distinguished.
In a difficult, uneven, terrible place, when great sins have arisen,
the cow alone gives protection; therefore it should be given to an excellent twice-born man.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:

children.text: yathā yathā prayāgasya māhātmyaṃ kathyate tvayā
children.translated_text: As the greatness of <s>Prayāga</s> is being told by you,
so I am being released from all sins; there is no doubt.
Blessed one, by what rule should those firm in <s>dharma</s> go there?

children.text: prayāge yo vidhiḥ proktastanme brūhi mahāmune ||
children.translated_text: Tell me the rule that is prescribed at <s>Prayāga</s>, O great sage.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
I shall tell you, O king, the ordered procedure of <s>tīrtha</s>-pilgrimage,
according to this ancient rule, as it has been seen and as it has been heard.
Listen also to the result for the man who, desiring pilgrimage to the <s>Prayāga</s> <s>tīrtha</s>,
sets out somewhere mounted on a bull.

children.text: narake vasate ghore gavāṃ kroṣṭā hi dāruṇe
children.translated_text: He dwells in a dreadful hell, for he is a cruel tormentor of cows,

children.text: salilaṃ na ca gṛhṇanti pitarastasya dehinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the ancestors of that embodied man do not accept water.
But he who has sons and children bathed and likewise gives them drink,

children.text: yathātmanā tathā sarvaṃ dānaṃ vipreṣu dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: and, as for himself, has every gift given to Brahmins,
or the man who goes by vehicle through desire, greed, or delusion of wealth,
all that of his is fruitless; therefore one should avoid a vehicle.
Whoever gives a maiden between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>,
in the ancient form of marriage, according to his available means,

children.text: na sa paśyati taṃ ghoraṃ narakaṃ tena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: by that deed he does not see that dreadful hell.
Having gone to the northern <s>Kurus</s>, he rejoices for an imperishable time,
and he obtains sons and wives who are righteous and endowed with beauty.
There a gift should be made according to the extent of one's means;

children.text: tena tīrthaphalaṃ caiva vardhate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: by that, the fruit of the <s>tīrtha</s> increases; there is no doubt about this.
O king of kings, he remains in heaven until the dissolution of created beings.
Whoever reaches the root of the banyan tree and gives up his breaths there,
passes beyond all worlds and goes to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
There those twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, abiding in <s>Rudra</s>, shine with heat;
they burn the whole world, but the root of the banyan is not burned.
When the moon, sun, and worlds have disappeared and the universe is one ocean,

children.text: sthīyate tatra vai viṣṇuryajamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the sacrificer again and again, remains there.
Gods, demons, <s>Gandharvas</s>, sages, perfected beings, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>
always attend that <s>tīrtha</s>, the confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: tato gaccheta rājendra prayāgaṃ saṃstuvaṃśca yat
children.translated_text: From there one should go, O king of kings, praising <s>Prayāga</s>,
where the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, the sages, perfected beings, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
the world-protectors, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, and the ancestors honored by the world,
as well as the supreme sages headed by <s>Sanatkumāra</s>,
and other brahmarṣis headed by <s>Aṅgiras</s>, are present.

children.text: tathā nāgāḥ suparṇāśca siddhāśca khecarāśca ye ||
children.translated_text: Likewise the nāgas, the suparṇas, the siddhas, and those who move through the sky,

children.text: sāgarāḥ saritaḥ śailā nāgā vidyādharāśca ye
children.translated_text: the oceans, rivers, mountains, nāgas, and vidyādharas, whoever they are,
and the blessed <s>Hari</s> dwell there, with <s>Prajāpati</s> at their head.
Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s> is remembered as the loins of the earth.
<s>Prayāga</s>, O tiger among kings, is renowned in the three worlds.

children.text: tataḥ puṇyatamaṃ nāsti triṣu lokeṣu bhārata ||
children.translated_text: There is nothing more holy than that in the three worlds, O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>.
By hearing of that tīrtha (sacred place), even by reciting its name,
or even by touching its clay, a man is released from sin.
Whoever performs ablution there at the confluence, with his vow duly praised and observed,
obtains a fruit equal to that of the rājasūya and aśvamedha sacrifices.
Not because of the words of gods, dear one, nor likewise because of the words of people,
should your resolve be made to turn away from going to <s>Prayāga</s>.
Ten thousand tīrthas, and also another sixty crores,
have their presence right here; therefore go, O delight of the <s>Kurus</s>.
The goal that belongs to a wise man joined with yoga and established in truth,
that same goal belongs to one who gives up his life at the confluence of <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: na te jīvanti loke'smiṃstatra tatra yudhiṣṭhira
children.translated_text: They do not truly live in this world, here and there, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,

children.text: ye prayāgaṃ na samprāptās triṣu lokeṣu vañcitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who have not reached <s>Prayāga</s>; they are deprived in the three worlds.

children.text: evaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu tattīrthaṃ prayāgaṃ paramaṃ padam
children.translated_text: Having thus seen that tīrtha, <s>Prayāga</s>, the supreme abode,
one is released from all sins, like the moon from <s>Rāhu</s>.
The nāgas <s>Kambala</s> and <s>Aśvatara</s> are on the broad bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: Bathing there and drinking there, one is released from all sins.

children.text: tatra gatvā ca saṃsthānaṃ mahādevasya viśrutam
children.translated_text: And having gone there to the famous abode of <s>Mahādeva</s>,
a man carries across all of them, ten ancestors before him and ten descendants after him.
By performing ablution there, a man obtains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice,
and reaches the world of heaven for as long as the dissolution of beings has not come.

children.text: pūrvapārśve tu gaṅgāyās triṣu lokeṣu bhārata
children.translated_text: On the eastern side of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>, renowned in the three worlds,

children.text: kūpaṃ caiva tu sāmudraṃ pratiṣṭhānaṃ ca viśrutam ||
children.translated_text: are the oceanic well and the famous <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>.
If a celibate man, with anger conquered, stays there for three nights,
his self purified of all sins, he obtains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice.
North of <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s> and east of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>,
there is a tīrtha called <s>Haṃsaprapatana</s>, renowned in the three worlds.
In that place, O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>, by bathing alone one gains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice,
and as long as the moon and the sun endure, one is honored in heaven.
At holy <s>Urvaśīramaṇa</s>, broad and white like a goose,
listen to the fruit also for one who gives up his life there.
For sixty thousand years and sixty hundreds of years,
he is served together with the ancestors in the world of heaven, O lord of men.
He always sees <s>Urvaśī</s> in the world of heaven, O best of men,
and is constantly honored, son, by sages, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras.
Then, fallen from heaven when his karma is exhausted and descended from the sky,
he obtains a hundred maidens resembling <s>Urvaśī</s>.
Among many thousands of women he becomes the husband,
and, O king, he becomes the enjoyer of ten thousand villages.
He is awakened from sleep by the sound of girdles and anklets,

children.text: bhuktvā tu vipulān bhogāṃstattīrthaṃ bhajate punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and after enjoying abundant pleasures, he seeks that tīrtha again.
Always wearing white garments, disciplined, and with his senses restrained,

children.text: ekaṃ kālaṃ tu bhuñjāno māsaṃ bhūmipatirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: eating only once a day for a month, he becomes a lord of the earth.
He obtains a hundred women adorned with gold,
and becomes a great lord of the earth as far as the ocean.
He is endowed with wealth and grain, and is always a giver.
After enjoying abundant pleasures, he again obtains that tīrtha.
Then at lovely <s>Saṃdhyāvaṭa</s>, a celibate man with his senses conquered,
fasting and pure, observing the twilight rite, reaches <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
Whoever reaches <s>Koṭitīrtha</s> and gives up his life there,
is honored in the world of heaven for crores of thousands of years.
Then, fallen from heaven when his karma is exhausted and descended from the sky,
he is born handsome in a family rich in gold, jewels, and pearls.
Then, going to <s>Bhogavatī</s>, north of <s>Vāsuki</s>,
there is another tīrtha there called <s>Daśāśvamedhaka</s>.
A man who has performed ablution there obtains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice,
and becomes wealthy, handsome, capable, generous, and righteous.
Whatever merit is found in the four Vedas, whatever merit is found among truth-speakers,

children.text: ahiṃsāyāṃ tu yo dharmo gamanādeva tatphalam ||
children.translated_text: and whatever dharma (religious merit) is in nonviolence, that fruit comes merely from going there.
The <s>Gaṅgā</s> is equal to <s>Kurukṣetra</s> wherever one bathes in it,
and is ten times greater than <s>Kurukṣetra</s> where it meets the <s>Vindhya</s>.
Where the greatly blessed <s>Gaṅgā</s>, rich in many tīrthas and rich in austerity, flows,

children.text: siddhakṣetraṃ hi tajjñeyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: that should be known as a field of siddhas; no deliberation is needed here.
On earth she carries mortals across; below she carries the nāgas across,
and in heaven she carries the gods across; therefore she is remembered as <s>Tripathagā</s>, the one going by three paths.
As long as the bones of an embodied being remain in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
for that many thousands of years he is honored in the world of heaven.
Then, fallen from heaven, he becomes lord of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.

children.text: tīrthānāṃ tu paraṃ tīrthaṃ nadīnāṃ tu mahānadī
children.translated_text: Of tīrthas she is the supreme tīrtha, and of rivers the great river,
giving liberation to all beings, even to those guilty of great sins.

children.text: sarvatra sulabhā gaṅgā triṣu sthāneṣu durlabhā
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaṅgā</s> is easy to find everywhere, but hard to find in three places:
at <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>, at <s>Prayāga</s>, and at the confluence of <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the ocean.

children.text: tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste'punarbhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having bathed there, those who die go to heaven; they are not born again.
For all beings whose minds are struck down by sin,
and who are seeking a path, there is no path equal to the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ ca maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam
children.translated_text: She is the purifier of purifiers and the auspiciousness of auspicious things,
fallen from the head of <s>Maheśvara</s>, blessed, remover of all sin.

children.text: kṛte tu naimiṣaṃ kṣetraṃ tretāyāṃ puṣkaraṃ param
children.translated_text: In the Kṛta age the sacred field is <s>Naimiṣa</s>; in the Tretā, supreme <s>Puṣkara</s>;

children.text: dvāpare tu kurukṣetraṃ kalau gaṅgā viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: in the Dvāpara it is <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, but in the Kali age the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is preeminent.
One should resort to the <s>Gaṅgā</s> alone, and especially to <s>Prayāga</s>;
in the terrible Kali age, O king, no other remedy is known.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen again, O king, to the greatness of <s>Prayāga</s>,
by hearing which one is released from all sins; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: mānasaṃ nāma tattīrthaṃ gaṅgāyā uttare taṭe
children.translated_text: That sacred ford on the northern bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is called <s>Mānasa</s>;
having fasted for three nights, one obtains all desires there.
The fruit that a man would obtain by gifts of cows, land, and gold,
he obtains that same fruit when he remembers that sacred ford again.

children.text: akāmo vā sakāmo vā gaṅgāyāṃ yo'bhipadyate
children.translated_text: Whether without desire or with desire, whoever enters the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: mṛtastu labhate svargaṃ narakaṃ ca na paśyati ||
children.translated_text: if he dies, obtains heaven and does not see hell.
He is awakened from sleep by songs of groups of apsarases;
he goes in a celestial vehicle furnished with haṃsas and sārasa cranes,
and for many thousands of years, O best of kings, he enjoys heaven.
Then, fallen from heaven, his karma exhausted and dropped from the celestial world,
he is born in a great family rich in gold, jewels, and pearls.
Sixty thousand sacred fords and sixty crores of rivers likewise
will go in the month of <s>Māgha</s> to the confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>.
The fruit of a hundred thousand cows properly given
is that same fruit from bathing for three days at <s>Prayāga</s> in the month of <s>Māgha</s>.
Whoever performs the <s>karṣāgni</s> observance between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>,
with limbs unimpaired, free from illness, and endowed with the five senses,
for as many hair-pores as there are on that embodied person's limbs,
for that many thousands of years he is honored in the world of heaven.
Then, fallen from heaven, he becomes lord of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>;
after enjoying abundant pleasures, he remembers that sacred ford again.
Whoever performs entry into the water at the world-renowned confluence,
when the moon is seized by <s>Rāhu</s>, is freed from all sins.
He obtains the world of <s>Soma</s> and rejoices together with <s>Soma</s>;
for sixty thousand years he is honored in the world of heaven.
In heaven, in this world of <s>Śakra</s>, attended by sages and gandharvas,
and when he has fallen from it, O best of kings, he is born in a prosperous family.
The man who, with head downward and feet upward, drinks the flame,
is honored in the world of heaven for a hundred thousand years.
And when he has fallen from it, O best of kings, that man becomes an <s>agnihotrin</s> (maintainer of the sacred fire);
after enjoying abundant pleasures, he resorts to that sacred ford again.

children.text: yaḥ svadehaṃ tu kartitvā śakunibhyaḥ prayacchati
children.translated_text: Whoever cuts up his own body and gives it to birds,
listen also to the fruit for him whose body is consumed by the birds.
For a hundred thousand years he is honored in the world of <s>Soma</s>;
and even after falling from that, he becomes a righteous king.
He is virtuous, endowed with beauty, learned, and pleasant-spoken;
after enjoying abundant pleasures, he resorts to that sacred ford again.

children.text: yāmune cottare kūle prayāgasya tu dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: On the northern bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> and to the south of <s>Prayāga</s>,
that supreme sacred ford is remembered as <s>Ṛṇapramocana</s>, 'Release from Debt.'
Having stayed one night and bathed there, one is released from all debts;
he obtains the world of heaven and is always free from debt.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
Having heard this account of <s>Prayāga</s> that you have proclaimed,

children.text: viśuddhaṃ me'dya hṛdayaṃ prayāgasya tu kīrtanāt ||
children.translated_text: my heart has today become purified by the praise of <s>Prayāga</s>.
Tell me, blessed one, what the fruit of <s>anāśaka</s> (fasting to death) is there,
and what world one obtains when purified from all sins.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen, O king, O lord, to the fruit of <s>anāśaka</s> at <s>Prayāga</s>,
which a wise man, faithful and self-controlled, obtains.
Though his limbs are unimpaired, he is free from disease and endowed with the five senses;
as he goes, at every step there is for him the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
He carries across ten families before him and ten after him, O king;
he is released from all sins and goes to the supreme state.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:

children.text: mahābhāgyaṃ hi dharmasya yattvaṃ vadasi me prabho
children.translated_text: Great indeed is the fortune of <s>dharma</s> that you tell me of, O lord,
for with very little effort one obtains many acts of <s>dharma</s>.
Here it is attained by many horse sacrifices and by those of excellent vows;

children.text: imaṃ me saṃśayaṃ chinddhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me ||
children.translated_text: cut away this doubt of mine, for my curiosity is great.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen, O king, great hero, to what was said by the womb-born of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ saṃnidhau pūrvaṃ kathyamānaṃ mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: which I heard being recounted formerly in the presence of the sages.
The district of <s>Prayāga</s> extends for five yojanas;
as soon as one has entered that ground, there is a horse sacrifice at every step.
Seven ancestors who have passed away and fourteen future descendants,
a man who gives up his life there carries all of them across.

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā tu rājendra sadā sevāparo bhavet
children.translated_text: Knowing this, O best of kings, one should always be devoted to service there.
Men without faith, whose minds are struck down by sin,
do not reach that place, <s>Prayāga</s>, guarded by the gods.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:

children.text: snehādvā dravyalobhādvā ye tu kāmavaśaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who, whether from affection or greed for wealth, have come under the control of desire

children.text: kathaṃ tīrthaphalaṃ teṣāṃ kathaṃ puṇyaphalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: How would the fruit of a <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford) belong to them, and how would the fruit of merit come about?
For one who, not knowing what should and should not be done, sells all kinds of goods,

children.text: prayāge kā gatistasya tanme brūhi pitāmaha ||
children.translated_text: what is his destiny at <s>Prayāga</s>? Tell me that, Grandfather.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen, O king, to a great secret, destructive of all sins.
Whoever bathes for one month at <s>Prayāga</s>, with his senses restrained,
is released from all sins and goes to the supreme state.
Now hear what fruit at <s>Prayāga</s> belongs to those who betray trust.
He should bathe at the three times and should live on begged food.

children.text: tribhirmāsaiḥ sa mucyeta prayāge tu na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In three months he would be released at <s>Prayāga</s>; there is no doubt.
If here, through ignorance, someone's pilgrimage and the like should take place,
he becomes endowed with the fulfillment of all desires and is honored in the heavenly world,
and he obtains an eternal abode filled with wealth and grain.

children.text: evaṃ jñānena sampūrṇaḥ sadā bhavati bhogavān
children.translated_text: Thus, being complete in knowledge, he is always possessed of enjoyments,
and by him his fathers and great-grandfathers have been carried across from hell.
O follower of <s>dharma</s> (normative order), knower of truth, as you ask again and again,
for the sake of pleasing you I have fully declared this eternal secret.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:

children.text: adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me tāritaṃ kulam
children.translated_text: Today my birth is fruitful; today my family has been carried across.
I am pleased; I have been favored merely by the sight of you, O sage.
Through seeing you, O righteous one, today I am freed from guilt,
and now, blessed one, I know myself as one whose defilement has departed.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: diṣṭyā te saphalaṃ janma diṣṭyā te tāritaṃ kulam
children.translated_text: By good fortune your birth is fruitful; by good fortune your family has been carried across.
By recitation merit increases; from hearing it there is destruction of sin.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:

children.text: yamunāyāṃ tu kiṃ puṇyaṃ kiṃ phalaṃ tu mahāmune
children.translated_text: What merit is there in the <s>Yamunā</s>, and what fruit, O great sage?
Tell me all this, as it has been seen and as it has been heard.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: tapanasya sutā devī triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā
children.translated_text: The goddess, daughter of <s>Tapana</s>, is renowned in the three worlds.
She is proclaimed there as the greatly fortunate <s>Yamunā</s>, the river flowing downward.

children.text: yenaiva niḥsṛtā gaṅgā tenaiva yamunā gatā
children.translated_text: By the very way by which the <s>Gaṅgā</s> issued forth, by that same way the <s>Yamunā</s> went.
Over thousands of yojanas she destroys sin by the utterance of her name.

children.text: tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca yamunāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira
children.translated_text: Having bathed there and drunk in the <s>Yamunā</s>, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,
one obtains merit by recitation, and, having seen her, one sees auspicious things.

children.text: avagāhya ca pītvā ca punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam
children.translated_text: Having plunged in and drunk, one purifies one's family up to the seventh generation.

children.text: prāṇāṃstyajati yastatra sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: Whoever gives up his breaths there goes to the highest destination.
On the southern bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> is the famous <s>Agnitīrtha</s>,

children.text: paścime dharmarājasya tīrthaṃ tu narakaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and to the west is the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Dharmarāja</s>, remembered as <s>Naraka</s>.

children.text: tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste'punarbhavāḥ
children.translated_text: Having bathed there, they go to heaven; those who die there are not born again.
Thus there are thousands of <s>tīrthas</s> on the southern bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
On the northern side I shall describe the <s>tīrtha</s> of the great-souled <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: tīrthaṃ nirañjanaṃ nāma yatra devāḥ savāsavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is the stainless <s>tīrtha</s> named <s>Nirañjana</s>, where the gods, together with <s>Vāsava</s>,

children.text: upāsate sma saṃdhyāṃ ye trikālaṃ hi yudhiṣṭhira
children.translated_text: used to worship the twilight rite at the three times, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.

children.text: devāḥ sevanti tattīrthaṃ ye cānye vibudhā janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods serve that <s>tīrtha</s>, and so do other wise divine beings.
Having become intent upon faith, perform ablution at the <s>tīrthas</s>.
And many other <s>tīrthas</s> are remembered as removers of all sin.

children.text: teṣu snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste'punarbhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having bathed in them, they go to heaven; those who die there are not born again.

children.text: gaṅgā ca yamunā caiva ubhe tulyaphale smṛte
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s> are both remembered as equal in fruit.
Only because of seniority is the <s>Gaṅgā</s> honored everywhere.
Thus perform ablution at all the <s>tīrthas</s>, O <s>Kaunteya</s>.
The sin committed throughout one's life is destroyed at that very moment.

children.text: yastvimaṃ kalya utthāya paṭhate ca śṛṇoti ca
children.translated_text: But whoever, having risen in the morning, recites and hears this,
is released from all sins and goes to the heavenly world.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: śrutaṃ me brahmaṇā proktaṃ purāṇe brahmasambhave
children.translated_text: I have heard this, spoken by <s>Brahmā</s> in the ancient <s>purāṇa</s> born of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tīrthānāṃ tu sahasrāṇi śatāni niyutāni ca
children.translated_text: There are thousands of <s>tīrthas</s>, hundreds and tens of thousands,

children.text: sarve puṇyāḥ pavitrāśca gatiśca paramā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: and all are meritorious and purifying; their destination is remembered as supreme.
The <s>Somatīrtha</s> is very holy and destroys great sins.
By bathing alone, O king of kings, it would carry across a hundred men.
Therefore one should, with every effort, perform bathing there.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
On earth <s>Naimiṣa</s> is holy, and in the mid-space <s>Puṣkara</s> is holy;
among all three worlds <s>Kurukṣetra</s> is distinguished.
Abandoning all those, how do you praise one alone?
What is said there is without measure, unbelievable, and unsurpassed.

children.text: gatiṃ ca paramāṃ divyāṃ bhogāṃścaiva yathepsitān
children.translated_text: The supreme divine destination and enjoyments just as one desires are promised;
for what reason do you praise much <s>dharma</s> (religious merit) with slight practice?
Tell me this doubt, as it has been seen and as it has been heard.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Something unbelievable should not be spoken, even if it has been directly perceived,
to a man without faith, whose mind is afflicted by sin.
For one without faith, impure, foolish, and bereft of auspiciousness,

children.text: ete pātakinaḥ sarve tenedaṃ bhāṣitaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: all these are sinners; therefore this has been said by you.
Hear the greatness of <s>Prayāga</s>, as it has been seen and as it has been heard,

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ ca parokṣaṃ ca yathānyastaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: both directly and indirectly, as it will be set forth.
Just as something else may be unseen, and just as it may be seen and heard,

children.text: śāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ kṛtvā ca yujyate yogamātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having made scripture the authority, one is joined to the yoga of oneself.
Another suffers there and does not attain yoga at all.
After thousands of other births, yoga may be obtained by human beings.
Just as, through a thousand yogas, yoga may be obtained by human beings,
but whoever gives all jewels to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>

children.text: tena dānena dattena yogaṃ nābhyeti mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: By that gift, once given, a man does not attain yoga;

children.text: prayāge tu mṛtasyedaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: but for one who has died at <s>Prayāga</s>, all this comes about, and not otherwise.
I shall tell you the principal reason; have faith, O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: yathā sarveṣu bhūteṣu brahma sarvatra dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Brahman</s> is seen everywhere among all beings,

children.text: brāhmaṇe vāsti yatkiṃcid abrāhmam iti vocyate
children.translated_text: and whatever exists in a brāhmaṇa is spoken of as not separate from <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: evaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu brahma sarvatra pūjyate ||
children.translated_text: so too <s>Brahman</s> is worshiped everywhere among all beings.
In the same way, among all worlds, the wise man should worship <s>Prayāga</s>.
The king of tīrthas is indeed worshiped; this is the truth, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
Even <s>Brahmā</s> constantly remembers <s>Prayāga</s>, the supreme tīrtha.
Having reached the king of tīrthas, one needs nothing else at all.
For who, after reaching divinity, would wish to become human?
By this very comparison you will understand, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,

children.text: yathā puṇyatamaṃ cāsti tathaiva kathitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: that it is the most meritorious place, just as I have told you.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:

children.text: śrutaṃ cedaṃ tvayā proktaṃ vismito'haṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: I have heard this spoken by you, and I am astonished again and again.
How is that attainment through yoga, while residence in heaven comes through karma?

children.text: dātā vai labhate bhogān gāṃ ca yatkarmaṇaḥ phalam
children.translated_text: A giver surely obtains enjoyments, and also a cow, as the fruit of whatever action he performs.

children.text: tāni karmāṇi pṛcchāmi punastaiḥ prāpyate mahī ||
children.translated_text: I ask about those actions again, by which the earth is obtained through them.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen, O mighty-armed king, to the attainment of the earth through conduct as it has been stated.

children.text: gāmagniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ śāstraṃ kāñcanaṃ salilaṃ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Cow, fire, brāhmaṇa, scripture, gold, water, women,

children.text: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva ye nindanti narādhamāḥ
children.translated_text: mother, and father: those lowest of men who revile these
have no upward going; <s>Prajāpati</s> has declared this.
Thus the place for attaining yoga is exceedingly hard to gain.

children.text: gacchanti narakaṃ ghoraṃ ye narāḥ pāpakarmiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those men who perform sinful deeds go to a terrible hell.
Whoever secretly steals an elephant, a horse, a cow, a bull, jewels, pearls, and gold,
and afterward makes a gift,

children.text: na te gacchanti vai svargaṃ dātāro yatra bhoginaḥ
children.translated_text: those donors do not go to heaven, where the enjoyers dwell.
Joined with that karma, they are cooked again in hell.

children.text: evaṃ yogaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca dātāraṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, concerning yoga, dharma, and the giver,

children.text: yathā satyamasatyaṃ vā asti nāstīti yatphalam
children.translated_text: and whatever result there is in truth or falsehood, in being or nonbeing,
I shall explain the derivation, just as <s>Aṃśumān</s> himself said.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen again, O king, to the greatness of <s>Prayāga</s>.
<s>Naimiṣa</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Gotīrtha</s>, and the <s>Sindhusāgara</s>,

children.text: gayā ca caitrakaṃ caiva gaṅgāsāgarameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Gayā</s>, <s>Caitraka</s>, and <s>Gaṅgāsāgara</s>,

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavo ye ca puṇyāḥ śiloccayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these and many others, and whatever holy rocky heights there are,
ten thousand tīrthas, and furthermore thirty crores,
are always situated at <s>Prayāga</s>; so the wise say.

children.text: trīṇi cāpyagnikuṇḍāni yeṣāṃ madhye tu jāhnavī
children.translated_text: There are also three fire-pits, in the midst of which is the <s>Jāhnavī</s>,
issued forth from <s>Prayāga</s> and honored by all tīrthas.

children.text: tapanasya sutā devī triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā
children.translated_text: The goddess daughter of the Sun, renowned in the three worlds,
<s>Yamunā</s>, together with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, is a benefactor of the worlds.
Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s> is remembered as the loins of the earth.
<s>Prayāga</s>, O tiger among kings, is not equaled by even a sixteenth part.
Three crores and a half-crore of tīrthas, <s>Vāyu</s> said,

children.text: divi bhuvyantarikṣe ca tatsarvaṃ jāhnavī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: in heaven, on earth, and in the atmosphere: all that is remembered as the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.
<s>Prayāga</s> is the abiding place, and so are both <s>Kambala</s> and <s>Aśvatara</s>;
and this <s>Bhogavatī</s> is the altar of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
There the Vedas and sacrifices, embodied in form, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,
attend upon <s>Prajāpati</s>, along with sages rich in austerity.
There the gods sacrifice with rites, as do kings who bear the discus.

children.text: tataḥ puṇyatamaṃ nāsti triṣu lokeṣu bhārata ||
children.translated_text: Therefore there is nothing more meritorious in the three worlds, O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>.
By its power, O lord, it surpasses all tīrthas in greatness:
ten thousand tīrthas, and furthermore three crores.
Where the greatly blessed <s>Gaṅgā</s> is, that region is a treasure of austerity.
It should be known as a field of siddhas, joined with the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
One should know this to be true for good people and for oneself,
and should whisper it in the ear of a friend and of a devoted disciple.
This is blessed; this leads to heaven; this is true; this is happiness.
This is meritorious; this accords with dharma; it is purifying and the highest dharma.
This is the secret of the great seers, the destroyer of all sins.
Even a twice-born man, after studying this, becomes stainless and reaches heaven.

children.text: ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ tīrthaṃ puṇyaṃ sadā śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever, always pure, hears this holy tīrtha every day
obtains memory of former births and rejoices on the summit of heaven.
Those tīrthas are reached by good people who follow the learned and disciplined.

children.text: snāhi tīrtheṣu kauravya na ca vakramatirbhava ||
children.translated_text: Bathe in the tīrthas, O <s>Kauravya</s>, and do not be crooked in mind.

children.text: tvayā ca samyakpṛṣṭena kathitaṃ vai mayā vibho
children.translated_text: Since you have asked properly, O lord, I have told it to you.
All the ancestors are carried across, and likewise the grandfathers.

children.text: vrataṃ dānaṃ tapastīrthaṃ yāgāḥ sarve sadakṣiṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Vows, gifts, austerity, tīrthas, and all sacrifices with proper fees,

children.text: yogāḥ sāṃkhyaṃ sadācāro ye cānye jñānahetavaḥ
children.translated_text: yogas, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, good conduct, and whatever other causes of knowledge there are,

children.text: prayāgasya tu sarve te kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ||
children.translated_text: all these do not equal even a sixteenth part of <s>Prayāga</s>.

children.text: evaṃ jñānaṃ ca yogaśca tīrthaṃ caiva yudhiṣṭhira
children.translated_text: Thus knowledge, yoga, and tīrtha, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,

children.text: bahukleśena yujyante tena yānti parāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: are attained with much hardship; through that people go to the supreme goal.
Knowledge of the three times arises, and one will go to the world of heaven.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
How has all this been declared about <s>Prayāga</s>, great sage?

children.text: etannaḥ sarvamākhyāhi yathā hi mama tārayet ||
children.translated_text: Tell us all this, by which it may carry me across.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu rājanprayāge tu proktaṃ sarvamidaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Listen, O king: at <s>Prayāga</s> this whole world has been declared to be present,
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and likewise <s>Īśāna</s>, the deities, the imperishable lord.

children.text: brahmā sṛjati bhūtāni sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> creates beings, whatever is stationary and moving;

children.text: tānyetāni paraṃ loke viṣṇuḥ saṃvardhate prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the other world <s>Viṣṇu</s> sustains all these creatures.

children.text: kalpānte tatsamagraṃ hi rudraḥ saṃharate jagat
children.translated_text: At the end of a kalpa <s>Rudra</s> gathers back that entire world;
but then the tīrtha (sacred crossing-place) of <s>Prayāga</s> never perishes.

children.text: īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
children.translated_text: The one who sees <s>Īśvara</s> as lord of all beings truly sees.

children.text: yatnenānena tiṣṭhanti te yānti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: Those who remain there with this effort go to the supreme state.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:

children.text: ākhyāhi me yathātathyaṃ yathaiṣā tiṣṭhati śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: Tell me exactly how this sacred tradition stands,
or for what reason the best beings of the worlds remain there.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
At <s>Prayāga</s> dwell these three: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
I shall explain that reason; listen to the truth, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
The circuit of <s>Prayāga</s> extends for five yojanas.
They remain here for its protection, to ward off sinful deeds.
North of <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> remains in a concealed form,
and the blessed one remains there in the form of <s>Veṇīmādhava</s>.
The supreme lord remains as <s>Māheśvara</s>, having become the banyan tree.
Therefore the gods, together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the supreme seers,
continually protect that circuit, to ward off sinful deeds.

children.text: yasmiñjuhvansvakaṃ pāpaṃ narakaṃ ca na paśyati
children.translated_text: A man who offers up his own sin there does not behold hell.

children.text: evaṃ brahmā ca viṣṇuśca prayāge sa maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and that <s>Maheśvara</s> are at <s>Prayāga</s>.
The seven islands, the oceans, and the mountains on the surface of the earth
remain under protection until the dissolution of all beings.

children.text: ye cānye bahavaḥ sarve tiṣṭhanti ca yudhiṣṭhira
children.translated_text: And all the many others, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, remain there too,

children.text: yat pṛthivī tatsamāśritya nirmitā daivatais tribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the earth was fashioned by the three deities by taking refuge in it.
This is the field of <s>Prajāpati</s>, renowned as <s>Prayāga</s>.

children.text: etatpuṇyaṃ pavitraṃ vai prayāgaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira
children.translated_text: This <s>Prayāga</s> is holy and purifying, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
Rule your own kingdom, O king of kings, together with your brothers, sinless one.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Together with all his brothers and with <s>Draupadī</s> his wife,
he bowed to the brahmins and satisfied his elders and the gods.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> also arrived there at that very time in an instant;
<s>Mādhava</s> was honored by all the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> together.
Again, together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and all those great-souled men,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, was consecrated in his own kingdom.
Just then the great sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>,
after saying, 'May it be well,' went in an instant to his hermitage.
And righteous <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> lived there together with his brothers.
Then the noble-minded son of <s>Dharma</s> gave a great gift.

children.text: yastvidaṃ kalya utthāya māhātmyaṃ paṭhate naraḥ
children.translated_text: A man who, rising in the morning, recites this māhātmya (glorification)

children.text: prayāgaṃ smarate nityaṃ sa yāti paramaṃ padam
children.translated_text: and continually remembers <s>Prayāga</s> goes to the supreme abode.
He is freed from all sins and goes to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> said:

children.text: mama vākyaṃ ca kartavyaṃ mahārāja bravīmyaham
children.translated_text: My instruction is to be carried out, great king; I speak it now.
Always perform japa and oblations at <s>Prayāga</s>, free from distress.
Remember <s>Prayāga</s> constantly, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, together with us.

children.text: svayaṃ prāpsyasi rājendra svargalokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You yourself, O king of kings, will attain the world of heaven; there is no doubt.
A man who goes after <s>Prayāga</s>, or who dwells there,
with his self purified of all sins, goes to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
One who has turned away from accepting gifts, is content, restrained, and pure,
and has abandoned egoism, obtains the fruit of a tīrtha.
One who is free from anger, truthful, a speaker of truth, and firm in his vow,
and who regards beings as like himself, obtains the fruit of a tīrtha.
Sacrifices have been taught by the seers and also, in due order, by the gods;

children.text: na hi śakyā daridreṇa yajñāḥ prāptuṃ mahīpate ||
children.translated_text: but sacrifices cannot be obtained by a poor man, O lord of the earth.
Sacrifices require many implements and extensive preparations of various kinds;
they are sometimes attained by prosperous kings and wealthy men.

children.text: yo daridrairapi vidhiḥ śakyaḥ prāptuṃ nareśvara
children.translated_text: But learn, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the rite that can be attained even by the poor, O lord of men,
and that is equal to the holy fruits of sacrifices.
This is the supreme secret of the seers, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>:
the holy following of tīrthas is superior even to sacrifices.
Ten thousand tīrthas and likewise thirty million rivers
will go to the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, O bull of the <s>Bhāratas</s>.
Be at ease, great king, and enjoy your kingdom free from thorns.
You will see me again, O king of kings, especially when you are sacrificing.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Having spoken thus, that greatly blessed <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, rich in austerity,
vanished there before King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
Then the king, together with his retinue, bathed his limbs there,
and by the prescribed rite attained supreme contentment.
So you too, divine seer, turn your face toward <s>Prayāga</s>.
Having performed the consecrating bath today, you will have accomplished your purpose.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having spoken thus, <s>Nandīśa</s> vanished there at once,
and <s>Nārada</s> too quickly went toward <s>Prayāga</s>.

children.text: tatra snātvā ca japtvā ca vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: There, having bathed and recited japa according to the rule laid down,

children.text: dānaṃ dattvā dvijāgryebhyo gataḥ svabhavanaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: and having given gifts to the foremost twice-born men, he then went to his own abode.
The sages said:

children.text: kati dvīpāḥ samudrā vā parvatā vā kati prabho
children.translated_text: How many islands, oceans, and mountains are there, lord?

children.text: kiyanti caiva varṣāṇi teṣu nadyaśca kāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And how many <s>varṣas</s> (regions) are there, and what rivers are remembered in them?
Also tell the measure of the great earth, and likewise <s>Lokāloka</s>,
its extent and measurement, and likewise the course of the moon and the sun.
Tell us all this in detail, since you know reality as it is.
We wish to hear all this in its entirety as spoken by you.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The divisions of the <s>dvīpas</s> are thousands, and seven are contained within them.

children.text: na śakyante krameṇeha vaktuṃ vai sakalaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: It is not possible here to describe the whole world in order.
But I shall describe just the seven, together with the moon, sun, and planets;
their measures are declared according to human reasoning.

children.text: acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvāstāṃstu tarkeṇa sādhayet
children.translated_text: Those realities that are truly inconceivable should not be established by reasoning;
and whatever is beyond the prakṛtis, that is the mark of the inconceivable.
I shall describe the seven <s>varṣas</s> and <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> according to its form;
hear its extent and circular measure in <s>yojanas</s>.
The extent of the <s>dvīpa</s> is one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>,
filled with many countries and with various auspicious cities.
It is thronged with siddhas and cāraṇas and adorned with mountains,
bound with all kinds of minerals and rising up in masses of rock.
On every side it has rivers that spring from the mountains.
These six <s>varṣa</s>-mountains are extended eastward and have great flanks.
On both sides they enter the eastern and western oceans.
<s>Himavān</s> is mostly snowy, and <s>Hemakūṭa</s> is golden.
The great mountain <s>Niṣadha</s> is pleasant on every side.
<s>Meru</s>, golden and connected with the four varṇas, is remembered as made of the primal covering.
It extends twenty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> in each of the four directions.
In measured form it is circular, yet square and firmly set,
equal on its sides with many colors and endowed with the qualities of Prajāpati.
It was born from the navel-bond of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth is unmanifest.

children.text: pūrvataḥ śvetavarṇastu brāhmaṇyaṃ tasya tena vai ||
children.translated_text: On the east it is white in color; by that, indeed, its brāhmaṇa nature is known.
On the south it is yellow, and by that its vaiśya nature is accepted.
On the west it is endowed with the hue of a black bee's wing,
and by that its śūdra nature is established, from the name, meaning, and function of <s>Meru</s>.
Its northern side is naturally red in color;
by that it has a kṣatra nature. Thus the varṇas are proclaimed.
<s>Nīla</s> is made of vaiḍūrya; <s>Śveta</s> is white; <s>Pīta</s> is golden.
And the one colored like a peacock's tail, <s>Śṛṅgavān</s>, is made of śātakumbha gold.
These kings of mountains are served by siddhas and cāraṇas.
The intervening span between them is said to be nine thousand <s>yojanas</s>.
In the middle, all around great <s>Meru</s>, lies the region named <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.
It is equally twenty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth.
In its middle stands great <s>Meru</s>, like a smokeless fire.
The southern half of <s>Meru</s> is like one half of an altar, and the northern half likewise forms the other.

children.text: varṣāṇi yāni saptātra teṣāṃ vai varṣaparvatāḥ
children.translated_text: The seven <s>varṣas</s> here have their <s>varṣa</s>-mountains;
each is two thousand <s>yojanas</s> broad from south to north.
Their length is said to be the breadth of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.

children.text: nīlaśca niṣadhaścaiva teṣāṃ hīnāśca ye pare ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s> and <s>Niṣadha</s>, and the others that are smaller than them,
<s>Śveta</s>, <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, <s>Himavān</s>, and <s>Śṛṅgavān</s>,
are declared according to the measure of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, O bull among sages.
From that, <s>Hemakūṭa</s> too is smaller by a twelfth part;
<s>Himavān</s> is smaller than that by a twentieth part.
<s>Hemakūṭa</s>, the great mountain, is eighty-eight thousand <s>yojanas</s> long.
<s>Himavān</s> mountain is eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> long from east to west.
Because the <s>dvīpa</s> has a circular form, decrease and increase are proclaimed.
So too, successively, according to the divisions of the <s>varṣas</s> and mountains.

children.text: teṣāṃ madhye janapadāstāni varṣāṇi sapta vai ||
children.translated_text: In the midst of them are inhabited lands; those indeed are the seven <s>varṣas</s>.
They are enclosed by those mountains, difficult with precipices,
and the seven are mutually inaccessible because of the divisions made by rivers.
Beings of many different kinds live in them everywhere.

children.text: imaṃ haimavataṃ varṣaṃ bhārataṃ nāma viśrutam ||
children.translated_text: This snowy <s>varṣa</s> is famous by the name <s>Bhārata</s>.
Beyond <s>Hemakūṭa</s> from that is the one remembered by the name <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>.
From <s>Hemakūṭa</s> up to <s>Niṣadha</s>, that is called <s>Harivarṣa</s>.
Beyond <s>Harivarṣa</s>, around <s>Meru</s>, is that <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.
Beyond <s>Ilāvṛta</s>, past <s>Nīla</s>, the region named <s>Ramyaka</s> is famous.
Beyond <s>Ramyaka</s>, past <s>Śveta</s>, that famous region is <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>.
Beyond <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, the region <s>Śṛṅgaśākaṃkura</s> is remembered.
They should be understood as bow-shaped to the south and north, O divine seer.
Four of them are long, and the middle one is <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.
East of <s>Niṣadha</s>, this southern half is remembered as half an altar;
beyond, after <s>Ilāvṛta</s>, that northern half is likewise half an altar.
Between those two, <s>Meru</s> should be known to stand where <s>Ilāvṛta</s> lies,
to the south of <s>Nīla</s> and to the north of <s>Niṣadha</s>.
Extending northward is the great mountain named <s>Mālyavān</s>;
for thirty-two thousand <s>yojanas</s> it follows the ocean in the west.
<s>Mālyavān</s> is one thousand <s>yojanas</s> wide, stretching as far as <s>Nīla</s> and <s>Niṣadha</s>.
The mountain <s>Gandhamādana</s> too is said in the same way to be thirty-two thousand <s>yojanas</s> long.
In the middle of the two circular regions stands <s>Meru</s>, the golden mountain,
equal to the four varṇas in its colors, square, and rising high.

children.text: nānāvarṇaḥ sa pārśveṣu pūrvānte śveta ucyate
children.translated_text: It is many-colored on its sides; at the eastern end it is said to be white.

children.text: pītaṃ tu dakṣiṇaṃ tasya bhṛṅgipattranibhaṃ param
children.translated_text: Its southern side was yellow, exceedingly like the wing of a bee,

children.text: uttaraṃ tasya raktaṃ vai iti varṇasamanvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and its northern side was indeed red: thus it was endowed with colors.

children.text: merustu śuśubhe divyo rājavatsa tu veṣṭitaḥ
children.translated_text: The divine <s>Meru</s>, encircled like a king, shone beautifully,
with the radiance of the young sun, like a smokeless fire.
It rose eighty-four thousand yojanas high,
entered sixteen thousand below, and was twenty-eight thousand wide.
Its circumference on every side was twice its breadth.
That mountain was very divine and furnished with divine herbs.
It was surrounded by all the worlds, adorned with gold.
There the hosts of gods, and also <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
rejoice on the king of mountains, everywhere with groups of <s>Apsarases</s>.
That <s>Meru</s> was surrounded by worlds that sustain living beings,
and these four regions of it stand on its various sides:

children.text: bhadrāśvaṃ bhārataṃ caiva ketumālaṃ ca paścime
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadrāśva</s> and <s>Bhārata</s>, and <s>Ketumāla</s> in the west,
and the northern <s>Kurus</s>, the refuge of those who have done meritorious deeds.
Likewise the supporting mountains are <s>Mandara</s>, <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
<s>Vipula</s>, and <s>Supārśva</s>, adorned with every jewel.
<s>Aruṇoda</s>, <s>Mānasa</s>, <s>Sitoda</s>, and that called <s>Bhadra</s>:

children.text: teṣāmupari catvāri sarāṃsi ca vanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: above them are four lakes and forests.
So too the <s>Bhadrakadamba</s> tree is on Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
the <s>Jambū</s> tree, then the <s>Aśvattha</s> on <s>Vipula</s>, and the supreme banyan.
On the western side of <s>Gandhamādana</s> is <s>Amaragaṇḍika</s>,
thirty-two thousand yojanas, equal on every side.
There those people famed as <s>Ketumālas</s> are of auspicious deeds.
There all are <s>Kālānalas</s>, great in being and great in strength.
The women are beautiful, lovely to behold, and have the appearance of blue lotuses.
There is a divine great tree, a jackfruit tree shining with leaves.
Having drunk the juice of its fruit, they live for ten thousand years.

children.text: tasya mālyavataḥ pārśve pūrve pūrvā tu gaṇḍikā
children.translated_text: On the eastern side of that <s>Mālyavat</s> is the eastern <s>Gaṇḍikā</s>,
and there too thirty-two thousand and a hundred are said.
There <s>Bhadrāśva</s> should be known, always joyful in mind.
There is the <s>Bhadramāla</s> forest and the great <s>Kālāmra</s> tree.

children.text: tatra te puruṣāḥ śvetā mahāsattvā mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: There the men are white, great in being and great in strength.
The women have the appearance of white lotuses, beautiful and lovely to behold.
They have the brilliance of the moon, the color of the moon, and faces like the full moon.
The women have limbs cool as the moon and the fragrance of blue lotuses.
Their life, free from disease, is ten thousand years.

children.text: kālāmrasya rasaṃ pītvā te sarve sthirayauvanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having drunk the juice of the <s>Kālāmra</s>, they all remain firm in youth.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus <s>Brahmā</s>, who had formerly shown favor to me, spoke to the sages
about the regions according to their nature. What more shall I describe to you?
Having heard this speech, all those sages of strict vows,
filled with curiosity, replied, endowed with joy.
The sages said:

children.text: pūrvāparau samākhyātau yau deśau tau tvayā mune
children.translated_text: The eastern and western regions, those two lands, have been described by you, O sage,

children.text: uttarāṇāṃ ca varṣāṇāṃ parvatānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also all the northern regions and the mountains in every respect.

children.text: ākhyāhi no yathātathyaṃ ye ca parvatavāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: Tell us accurately who the mountain-dwellers are.
Thus addressed by the sages, he again told them.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇudhvaṃ yāni varṣāṇi pūrvoktāni ca vai mayā
children.translated_text: Listen to the regions that were indeed previously mentioned by me,
south of <s>Nīla</s> and north of <s>Niṣadha</s>.

children.text: varṣaṃ ramaṇakaṃ nāma jāyante yatra vai prajāḥ
children.translated_text: There is a region named <s>Ramaṇaka</s>, where creatures are born.
There humans are born pure and devoted chiefly to pleasure,
endowed with a fair lineage, all of them lovely to behold.

children.text: tatrāpi ca mahāvṛkṣo nyagrodho rohiṇo mahān
children.translated_text: There too is a great tree, a great red banyan,

children.text: tasyāpi te phalarasaṃ pibanto vartayanti hi ||
children.translated_text: and they sustain themselves by drinking the juice of its fruit.
For ten thousand years and ten hundred years

children.text: jīvanti te mahābhāgāḥ sadā hṛṣṭā narottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those greatly fortunate best of men live, always joyful.

children.text: uttareṇa tu śvetasya pārśve śṛṅgasya dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: North of <s>Śveta</s> and on the southern side of <s>Śṛṅga</s>

children.text: varṣaṃ hiraṇvataṃ nāma yatra hairaṇvatī nadī ||
children.translated_text: is the region named <s>Hiraṇvata</s>, where the <s>Hairaṇvatī</s> river is.
They are very strong, great in being, and always joyful in mind,
endowed with a fair lineage, and all lovely to behold.
Those best of men live for eleven thousand years

children.text: āyuṣpramāṇaṃ jīvanti śatāni daśa pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: and fifteen hundred more as the measure of their lifespan.
In that region is a great <s>Lakuca</s> tree, sheltered by leaves.

children.text: tasya pītvā phalarasaṃ tatra jīvanti mānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having drunk the juice of its fruit, the humans live there.

children.text: śṛṅgasāhvasya śṛṅgāṇi trīṇi tāni mahānti vai
children.translated_text: There are three great peaks of the one called <s>Śṛṅga</s>.

children.text: ekaṃ maṇiyutaṃ tatra ekaṃ tu kanakānvitam
children.translated_text: One there is set with jewels, one is furnished with gold,
and one is made of every jewel and beautified by worlds.

children.text: uttare cāsya śṛṅgasya samudrānte ca dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: North of this <s>Śṛṅga</s>, and south of the end of the ocean,
there are the <s>Kurus</s>, that excellent holy land frequented by siddhas.
There the trees have honeyed fruits, and the rivers are made of divine nectar.
They bring forth garments, and from their fruits ornaments as well.
Some delightful trees grant every desire.
Other delightful trees there are called milk-bearing,

children.text: ye rakṣanti sadā kṣīraṃ ṣaḍrasaṃ cāmṛtopamam ||
children.translated_text: which always preserve milk of six flavors, like nectar.
All the ground is made of jewels, fine with golden sand.
Everywhere the auspicious winds are pleasant to the touch and silent.
There auspicious humans are born, fallen from the world of the gods,
endowed with a fair lineage, and all of them firm in youth.
Pairs are born, and the women are like <s>apsarases</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ te kṣīriṇāṃ kṣīraṃ pibanti hyamṛtopamam ||
children.translated_text: Indeed they drink the milk of those milk-bearing ones, like nectar.
In a single day a pair is born, and it grows in equal measure.

children.text: samaṃ rūpaṃ ca śīlaṃ ca samaṃ caiva mriyanti vai ||
children.translated_text: Their form is the same, their character is the same, and they die at the same time.
Each is attached to the other, unfailingly, like a <s>cakravāka</s> bird.
They are free from disease and from sorrow, always joyful in mind.
For ten thousand years and ten hundreds of years

children.text: jīvanti ca mahāsattvā na cānyā strī pravartate ||
children.translated_text: those great beings live, and no other woman comes forth.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evameva nisargo vai varṣāṇāṃ bhārate yuge
children.translated_text: Just so is the natural order of the regions seen in the <s>Bhārata</s> age.

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ paramadharmajñāḥ kiṃ bhūyaḥ kathayāmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O supreme knowers of <s>dharma</s>, what more shall I tell you?
When this had thus been explained to the sages by the wise son of <s>Sūta</s>,
desiring to hear the sequel again, they asked the son of <s>Sūta</s>.
The sages said:
This <s>Bhārata</s> region, in which the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> and the others,
the fourteen <s>Manus</s>, brought forth the creation of living beings:
we wish to know this from you, O excellent votary.
Tell us the sequel again, O best of speakers.
Having heard this from the sages, <s>Laumaharṣaṇi</s>,
the <s>Sūta</s> and reciter of the Purāṇas, then addressed those sages of disciplined selves.

children.text: buddhyā vicārya bahudhā vimṛśya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After considering it with his intellect in many ways and reflecting again and again,
he then told them that sequel.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Now I shall describe the peoples in this region of <s>Bhārata</s>.
Because he sustains and brings forth people, <s>Manu</s> is called <s>Bharata</s>.
And by etymological statements that region is remembered as <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: yataḥ svargaśca mokṣaśca madhyamaścāpi hi smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because heaven, liberation, and also the middle state are remembered from it.

children.text: na khalvanyatra martyānāṃ bhūmau karmavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For mortals, the rule of action is not remembered elsewhere on earth.
Learn the nine divisions of this region of <s>Bhārata</s>.
<s>Indradvīpa</s>, <s>Kaśeru</s>, <s>Tāmraparṇa</s>, and <s>Gabhastimān</s>,
then <s>Nāgadvīpa</s>, <s>Saumya</s>, <s>Gandharva</s>, and then <s>Vāruṇa</s>.
This is the ninth island among them, surrounded by the ocean.
This island extends a thousand <s>yojanas</s> from south to north.
It stretches from <s>Kumārī</s> up to the current of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: tiryagūrdhvaṃ tu vistīrṇaḥ sahasrāṇi daśaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: and crosswise and upward it is ten thousand <s>yojanas</s> broad.
This island is settled on every side at its edges by <s>mlecchas</s>.
The <s>Yavanas</s> and <s>Kirātas</s> are at its eastern and western boundaries.

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā madhye śūdrāśca bhāgaśaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>vaiśyas</s>, and the <s>śūdras</s> in the middle, stand in their respective divisions,
carrying on sacrifice, commerce, and the like.

children.text: teṣāṃ sa vyavahāro'yaṃ vartanaṃ tu parasparam
children.translated_text: This is their usage, their mutual way of living,
joined with <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and desire, while the <s>varṇas</s> perform their own duties.
For the <s>āśramas</s>, with resolve as the fifth, according to rule,
here among human beings there is activity for the sake of heaven and liberation.
This human island is proclaimed to extend crosswise.

children.text: ya enaṃ jayate kṛtsnaṃ sa samrāḍiti kīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The one who conquers it entire is called a <s>samrāṭ</s>.
This world is remembered as the realm of the <s>samrāṭ</s>, for those who conquer the midspace.
That world is remembered as the <s>svarāṭ</s>; I shall speak again in detail.
In this great region seven famous family-mountains are known:
<s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, <s>Sahya</s>, <s>Śuktimān</s>, and also <s>Ṛkṣavān</s>,
<s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Pāriyātra</s>; these are the family-mountains.
Near them there are thousands of other mountains.
Some are well known, vast, and with variegated slopes;
others, apart from them, are known as low, sustaining those who live on low ground.
Mixed among them are settled lands everywhere, of <s>Āryas</s> and <s>mlecchas</s>.

children.text: pibanti bahulā nadyo gaṅgā sindhuḥ sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: Many rivers give them drink: the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>;
the <s>Śatadru</s>, <s>Candrabhāgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, and likewise <s>Sarayū</s>;

children.text: airāvatī vitastā ca viśālā devikā kuhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Airāvatī</s>, <s>Vitastā</s>, <s>Viśālā</s>, <s>Devikā</s>, and <s>Kuhū</s>;

children.text: gomatī dhautapāpā ca bāhudā ca dṛṣadvatī
children.translated_text: the <s>Gomatī</s>, <s>Dhautapāpā</s>, <s>Bāhudā</s>, and <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>;

children.text: kauśikī tu tṛtīyā ca niścalā gaṇḍakī tathā ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Kauśikī</s>, and the third, <s>Tṛtīyā</s>, and likewise <s>Niścalā</s> and <s>Gaṇḍakī</s>;
<s>Ikṣu</s> and <s>Lauhita</s>: these issue from the side of <s>Himavat</s>.
<s>Vedasmṛti</s>, <s>Vetravatī</s>, <s>Vṛtraghnī</s>, and <s>Sindhu</s> too,

children.text: parṇāśā narmadā caiva kāverī mahatī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Parṇāśā</s>, <s>Narmadā</s>, <s>Kāverī</s>, and likewise <s>Mahatī</s>;
<s>Pārā</s>, <s>Dhanvatīrūpā</s>, <s>Viduṣā</s>, and also <s>Veṇumatī</s>;

children.text: śiprā hyavantī kuntī ca pāriyātrāśritāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śiprā</s>, <s>Avantī</s>, and <s>Kuntī</s> are remembered as depending on <s>Pāriyātra</s>.
<s>Śoṇa</s>, <s>Mahānada</s>, <s>Nandanā</s>, <s>Sukṛśā</s>, and <s>Kṣamā</s>;

children.text: mandākinī daśārṇā ca citrakūṭā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Mandākinī</s>, <s>Daśārṇā</s>, and likewise <s>Citrakūṭā</s>;

children.text: tamasā pippalī śyenī tathā citrotpalāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tamasā</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Śyenī</s>, and also <s>Citrotpalā</s>;

children.text: vimalā cañcalā caiva tathā ca dhūtavāhinī
children.translated_text: <s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Cañcalā</s>, and likewise <s>Dhūtavāhinī</s>;

children.text: śuktimantī śunī lajjā mukuṭā hrādikāpi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Śuktimantī</s>, <s>Śunī</s>, <s>Lajjā</s>, <s>Mukuṭā</s>, and also <s>Hrādikā</s>:
those rivers, born from <s>Ṛṣyavant</s>, have pure waters and are auspicious.

children.text: tāpī payoṣṇī nirvindhyā kṣiprā ca ṛṣabhā nadī
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpī</s>, <s>Payoṣṇī</s>, <s>Nirvindhyā</s>, <s>Kṣiprā</s>, and the river <s>Ṛṣabhā</s>;
<s>Veṇā</s>, <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, <s>Viśvamālā</s>, and <s>Kumudvatī</s>;

children.text: toyā caiva mahāgaurī durgamā tu śilā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Toyā</s>, <s>Mahāgaurī</s>, <s>Durgamā</s>, and likewise <s>Śilā</s>:
those, all with cool waters and auspicious, are born from the foot of <s>Vindhya</s>.
<s>Godāvarī</s>, <s>Bhīmarathī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇī</s>, and <s>Vañjulā</s>;

children.text: tuṅgabhadrā suprayogā vāhyā kāverī caiva tu
children.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgabhadrā</s>, <s>Suprayogā</s>, <s>Vāhyā</s>, and <s>Kāverī</s> too:
those rivers of the southern path issue from the foot of <s>Sahya</s>.
<s>Kṛtamālā</s>, <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, <s>Puṣpajā</s>, and <s>Utpalāvatī</s>;
those rivers born from <s>Malaya</s> all have cool and auspicious waters.
<s>Tribhāgā</s>, <s>Ṛṣikulyā</s>, <s>Ikṣudā</s>, and <s>Tridivācalā</s>.

children.text: tāmraparṇī tathā mūlī śaravā vimalā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, likewise <s>Mūlī</s>, <s>Śaravā</s>, and also <s>Vimalā</s>,
all daughters of <s>Mahendra</s>, are famous and flow auspiciously.
<s>Kāśikā</s>, <s>Sukumārī</s>, <s>Mandagā</s>, and <s>Mandavāhinī</s>,

children.text: kṛpā ca pāśinī caiva śuktimantātmajās tu tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Kṛpā</s> and <s>Pāśinī</s>: those indeed are daughters of <s>Śuktimat</s>.
All are holy, with sacred waters; they go everywhere and flow to the ocean.
All are mothers of the world, auspicious removers of every sin.
Their rivers and tributaries are by the hundreds and thousands.
Among them are these <s>Kuru-Pāñcālas</s>, the <s>Śālvas</s>, and those with the <s>Jāṅgalas</s>;
the <s>Śūrasenas</s>, <s>Bhadrakāras</s>, the outer peoples together with the <s>Paṭaccaras</s>,
the <s>Matsyas</s>, <s>Kirātas</s>, <s>Kulyas</s>, <s>Kuntalas</s>, and the <s>Kāśi-Kośalas</s>;
the <s>Āvantas</s>, <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, and <s>Mūkas</s>, together with the <s>Andhakas</s>;
these are mostly proclaimed as the janapadas of the middle country.
Immediately after <s>Sahya</s> are these; there is the river <s>Godāvarī</s>.
Even upon the whole earth, that region is delightful.
There are <s>Govardhana</s> by name, <s>Mandara</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
and heavenly trees and divine herbs, for the sake of pleasing <s>Rāma</s>,
were brought down by the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> for that beloved purpose.
Then, through them, that flower-excellent country became lovely.
The <s>Vāhlīkas</s>, <s>Vāṭadhānas</s>, <s>Ābhīras</s>, and <s>Kālatoyakas</s>,
the <s>Puraṃdhras</s>, the <s>Śūdras</s>, the <s>Pallavas</s>, and the <s>Āttakhaṇḍikas</s>,
the <s>Gāndhāras</s>, <s>Yavanas</s>, <s>Sindhus</s>, <s>Sauvīras</s>, and <s>Madrakas</s>,
the <s>Śakas</s>, <s>Druhyas</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, <s>Pāradas</s>, and <s>Hāramūrtikas</s>,
the <s>Rāmaṭhas</s>, <s>Kaṇṭakāras</s>, <s>Kaikeyas</s>, and <s>Daśanāmakas</s>,
settlements of kṣatriyas, and clans of vaiśyas and śūdras,
the <s>Atrayas</s>, then the <s>Bharadvājas</s>, the <s>Prasthalas</s>, and the <s>Sadaserakas</s>,
the <s>Lampakas</s>, <s>Talagānas</s>, and <s>Sainikas</s>, together with the <s>Jāṅgalas</s>:
these are the northern countries; now learn the eastern countries.
The <s>Aṅgas</s>, <s>Vaṅgas</s>, <s>Madgurakas</s>, <s>Antargiris</s>, and <s>Bahirgiris</s>,
then the <s>Plavaṃgas</s>, <s>Mātaṃgas</s>, <s>Yamakas</s>, and <s>Mallavarṇakas</s>,
the northern <s>Suhmas</s>, the <s>Pravijayas</s>, <s>Mārgavas</s>, and <s>Geyamālavas</s>,
the <s>Prāgjyotiṣas</s>, <s>Puṇḍras</s>, <s>Videhas</s>, and <s>Tāmraliptakas</s>,
the <s>Śālvas</s>, <s>Māgadhas</s>, and <s>Gonardas</s> are remembered as eastern janapadas.
Beyond them are the janapadas dwelling in the <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>.
The <s>Pāṇḍyas</s>, <s>Keralas</s>, <s>Colas</s>, and likewise the <s>Kulyas</s>,
the <s>Setukas</s>, <s>Sūtikas</s>, <s>Kupathas</s>, and <s>Vājivāsikas</s>,
the <s>Navarāṣṭras</s>, <s>Māhiṣikas</s>, and the <s>Kaliṅgas</s> in every part,
the <s>Kārūṣas</s> together with the <s>Aiṣīkas</s>, the forest peoples, and the <s>Śabaras</s>,
the <s>Pulindas</s>, <s>Vindhyapuṣikas</s>, and <s>Vaidarbhas</s>, together with the <s>Daṇḍakas</s>,
the <s>Kulīyas</s>, <s>Sirālas</s>, and <s>Rūpasas</s>, together with the ascetics,
and likewise the <s>Taittirikas</s>, and all the <s>Kāraskaras</s> as well,
the <s>Vāsikyas</s> and whatever others there are, and those within the <s>Narmadā</s> region,
the <s>Bhārukacchas</s> and <s>Samāheyas</s>, together with the <s>Sārasvatas</s>,
the <s>Kācchīkas</s>, <s>Saurāṣṭras</s>, and <s>Ānartas</s>, together with the <s>Arbudas</s>:
these are the western peoples; hear now of those who dwell in the <s>Vindhya</s>.
