The <s>Mālavas</s>, <s>Karūṣas</s>, <s>Mekalas</s>, together with the <s>Utkalas</s>,

children.text: auṇḍrā māṣā daśārṇāśca bhojāḥ kiṣkindhakaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Auṇḍras</s>, <s>Māṣas</s>, <s>Daśārṇas</s>, and <s>Bhojas</s>, together with the <s>Kiṣkindhakas</s>,
the <s>Stośalas</s>, <s>Kosalas</s>, <s>Traipuras</s>, and likewise the <s>Vaidiśas</s>,
the <s>Tumuras</s>, <s>Tumbaras</s>, and <s>Padgamas</s>, together with the <s>Naiṣadhas</s>,
the <s>Arūpas</s>, <s>Śauṇḍikeras</s>, <s>Vītihotras</s>, and <s>Avantayas</s>:
these are the famous janapadas dwelling on the back of the <s>Vindhya</s>.
Now I shall declare the countries that depend upon the mountains:
the <s>Nirāhāras</s>, <s>Sarvagas</s>, and the <s>Kupathas</s>, and likewise the <s>Apathas</s>,
the <s>Kuthaprāvaraṇas</s>, <s>Ūrṇādavas</s>, and <s>Samudgakas</s>,
the <s>Trigartas</s> and <s>Maṇḍalas</s>, and the <s>Kirātas</s> together with the <s>Cāmaras</s>.
The sages have spoken of four yugas in <s>Bhārata-varṣa</s>:

children.text: kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliśceti caturyugam
children.translated_text: the <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s>; this is the fourfold yuga.
I shall describe their natural character later, in full.
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: etacchrutvā tu ṛṣaya uttaraṃ punareva te
children.translated_text: When the seers had heard this, wishing to hear further,
they again spoke at length to that son of <s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s>.
The seers said:

children.text: yacca kimpuruṣaṃ varṣaṃ harivarṣaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: The land of <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>, and likewise <s>Harivarṣa</s>:

children.text: ācakṣva no yathātattvaṃ kīrtitaṃ bhārataṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: tell us about them according to reality, now that <s>Bhārata</s> has been described by you.
Tell us the extent of <s>Jambūkhaṇḍa</s>, O best of the learned,

children.text: dvīpānāṃ vāsināṃ teṣāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ prabravīhi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also about the other dvīpas, their inhabitants, and their trees.
Thus questioned then by the brāhmaṇas, according to each question in particular,
he spoke what had been seen by the seers and was accepted by the Purāṇa.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Since you wish to hear, O brāhmaṇas, listen without weariness.
The <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s> varṣa in <s>Jambū</s> is very great, like <s>Nandana</s>.
A lifespan of ten thousand years is remembered in <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>.
Human beings are born there with the brilliance of well-refined gold.

children.text: varṣe kimpuruṣe puṇye plakṣo madhuvahaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: In the holy <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s> varṣa, a plakṣa tree flowing with honey is remembered.
All the <s>Kiṃpuruṣas</s>, drinking its excellent sap,
are free from disease and grief, always joyful in mind.
The men are golden in color, and the women are remembered as apsarases.
Beyond <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>, they call the next land <s>Harivarṣa</s>,
where human beings are born with the appearance of great silver.
All have fallen from the world of the gods, and they are manifold in form in every way.
In <s>Harivarṣa</s>, all the people drink auspicious sugarcane juice.

children.text: na jarā bādhate tatra tena jīvanti te ciram
children.translated_text: Old age does not afflict them there; therefore they live for a long time.
Their lifespan is proclaimed to be eleven thousand years.
I have described the middle region; by name it is the <s>varṣa</s> called <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.

children.text: na tatra sūryastapati na ca jānanti mānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the sun does not burn, and men do not perceive
the moon and sun together with the stars, for they are without radiance in <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.
They have the radiance of lotuses, the color of lotuses, and eyes like lotus petals;

children.text: padmagandhāśca jāyante tatra sarve ca mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: and all the people there are born with the fragrance of lotuses.
They feed on the juice of <s>jambū</s> fruits, are free from agitation, and are fragrant.
All have fallen from the world of the gods and wear splendid silver garments.
Those best of men live for thirteen thousand

children.text: āyuṣpramāṇaṃ jīvanti ye tu varṣa ilāvṛte
children.translated_text: years as the measure of their life, those who are in the <s>varṣa</s> <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.
On the southern side of <s>Meru</s>, or north of <s>Niṣadha</s>,
there is a great, eternal <s>jambū</s> tree named <s>Sudarśana</s>.
It is always furnished with flowers and fruit, and is attended by siddhas and cāraṇas.
From the name of that forest-lord, <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> is so called.

children.text: yojanānāṃ sahasraṃ ca śatadhā ca mahānpunaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is a thousand <s>yojanas</s> multiplied by a hundred, immense indeed;
such is the height of that king of trees, and it stands covering heaven.
The juice of its <s>jambū</s> fruits becomes a river and flows forth.
Having circumambulated <s>Meru</s>, it returns again to the root of the <s>jambū</s> tree.
The joyful inhabitants of <s>Ilāvṛta</s> always drink that <s>jambū</s> juice.

children.text: jambūphalarasaṃ pītvā na jarā bādhate'pi tān
children.translated_text: After drinking the juice of the <s>jambū</s> fruit, old age does not afflict them.

children.text: na kṣudhā na klamo vāpi na duḥkhaṃ ca tathāvidham ||
children.translated_text: Nor do hunger, fatigue, or any such sorrow afflict them.
There is produced gold called <s>jāmbūnada</s>, an ornament of the gods,
bright and resembling the <s>indragopaka</s> insect.
That auspicious fruit-juice of all the <s>varṣa</s>-trees,

children.text: skannaṃ tu kāñcanaṃ śubhraṃ jāyate devabhūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: when spilled, becomes pure gold, an ornament of the gods.

children.text: teṣāṃ mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā dikṣvaṣṭāsu ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Their urine or excrement, everywhere in the eight directions,
and also their dead, the earth consumes through the grace of the Lord.
Rākṣasas, piśācas, and yakṣas are all in the <s>Haimavata</s> region.
On <s>Hemakūṭa</s> are to be known the gandharvas together with the hosts of apsarases.
All the nāgas, <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s>, resort there.
On great <s>Meru</s> the thirty-three auspicious gods, worthy of sacrifice, sport.
On this mountain joined with blue beryl dwelt siddhas and brahmarṣis.

children.text: daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca śvetaḥ parvata ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The white mountain is said to belong to the daityas and dānavas.
<s>Śṛṅgavān</s>, the best of mountains, is the resort of the ancestors.
Thus these nine <s>varṣas</s> in <s>Bhārata</s> have been told by me.
They are inhabited even by beings, and they are enduring.
Their manifold increase is seen among gods and men.
It is impossible to enumerate, and should be accepted on faith by one who desires prosperity.
<s>Manu</s> said:
O <s>Janārdana</s>, I have heard the career of the son of <s>Budha</s>.
I have heard the holy rite of śrāddha, which destroys all sins.

children.text: dhenvāḥ prasūyamānāyāḥ phalaṃ dānasya me śrutam
children.translated_text: I have heard the fruit of giving a cow that is calving,
as well as the gift of a black antelope skin and the release of a bull.
O <s>Keśava</s>, after hearing of the form of the king, the son of <s>Budha</s>,
curiosity has arisen in me; tell that to me as I ask.

children.text: kena karmavipākena sa tu rājā purūravāḥ
children.translated_text: By the ripening of what deed did that king <s>Purūravāḥ</s>
obtain such beauty and also supreme good fortune?
Leaving the gods, the best in the three worlds, and the charming gandharvas,

children.text: urvaśī saṃmatā tyaktvā sarvabhāvena taṃ nṛpam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Urvaśī</s> gave herself with her whole being to that king.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Hear by the ripening of what deed King <s>Purūravāḥ</s>
obtained such beauty and also supreme good fortune.

children.text: atīte janmani purā yo'yaṃ rājā purūravāḥ
children.translated_text: In a former birth long ago, this king <s>Purūravāḥ</s>,

children.text: purūravā iti khyāto madradeśādhipo hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: well known as <s>Purūravāḥ</s>, was lord of the <s>Madra</s> country.
He was a king in the lineage of <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>, in the interval of <s>Cākṣuṣa Manu</s>.
He was endowed with royal virtues, but was lacking only in beauty.
The sages said:
By what deed was <s>Purūravāḥ</s>, lord of <s>Madra</s>, a king,
and by what deed did he become handsome as well, O son of <s>Sūta</s>?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In a village of brahmins there was an excellent brahmin named <s>Purūravāḥ</s>.
On the bank of a river, O great king, he lived in a former birth, O king.

children.text: sa tu madrapatī rājā yastu nāmnā purūravāḥ
children.translated_text: That king, the lord of <s>Madra</s>, who was named <s>Purūravāḥ</s>,
in that birth was this brahmin; on the twelfth lunar day, O sinless one,
after fasting, he worshiped <s>Janārdana</s>, desiring kingship.
And while fasting he performed a bath preceded by an oil-anointing.
From the fruit of the fast he obtained an unopposed kingdom among the <s>Madras</s>.
But because he was fasting and yet had an oil-anointing, he was born without beauty.
Therefore, by men who are fasting, a bath preceded by oil-anointing
should be carefully avoided, O king; that is supremely destructive of beauty.
All this has been told to you, what occurred in his former birth.
Now hear the account of his becoming lord of <s>Madra</s>, O lord of the earth.
Although that king was furnished with all royal virtues,
there was no affection from the people for him, because he was without beauty.
Desiring beauty, that lord of <s>Madra</s> firmly resolved on austerity.
Having placed the kingdom in the hands of his ministers, he went to the <s>Himālaya</s> mountain.
With resolve as his only companion, the greatly renowned one went on foot,

children.text: draṣṭuṃ sa tīrthasadanaṃ viṣayānte svake nadīm ||
children.translated_text: to see a place of pilgrimage, a river at the edge of his own territory.
He saw the exceedingly lovely river famed as <s>Airāvatī</s>.
It was born from the snowy mountain, swift with a great flood, and its water was as cool as moonbeams.
The king, whose fame was like snow, saw the river, a mass of snowy, golden color.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: sa dadarśa nadīṃ puṇyāṃ divyāṃ haimavatīṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: He saw the holy river, divine, auspicious, and born of the <s>Himālaya</s>,
crowded with <s>gandharvas</s> and always frequented by <s>Śakra</s>.
It shone all around, sprinkled with the rut-fluid of the elephants of the gods,
and through its middle it had the appearance of <s>Śakra</s>'s bow on that day, as ever.
It was furnished with hermit refuges and served by great brāhmaṇas;
the great king <s>Purūravas</s> saw it, shining like refined gold.
It was covered with rows of white swans and adorned with kāśa grasses like chowries;
seeing it as if consecrated for the good, he went to supreme delight.
It was holy, very cool, pleasing, and increased the gladness of the mind;
lovely, possessed of waning and increase, it was like another embodied <s>Soma</s>.
Its water was very cool, swift, and drinkable, and it was frequented by hosts of birds;
it was the best daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, adorned with trembling waves.
Its water tasted like nectar, and it was beautified by ascetics;
it was a ladder for ascent to heaven and a destroyer of every stain.
It was foremost, the ocean's queen, and served by bands of great seers;
it aroused wonder in the whole world and was exceedingly charming.
It was beneficial to all the world and gave the path to heaven;
its banks were crowded with herds of cattle, and it was lovely and free of moss.
It resounded with swans and cranes and was adorned with water-born flowers;
deep with eddies as its navel, it had islands as its broad hips and loins.
It had the beauty of blue lotuses for eyes and blossoming lotuses for a face;
its garment was foam white as snow, and cakravāka birds were its lips.
Rows of cranes were its teeth, and lines of moving fish were its eyebrows.
Its lovely jar-like breasts were the temples of elephants born from its own waters;
it rang with swans as anklets and had rows of lotus-stalks for bracelets.
In it, intoxicated by pride in their beauty and always followed by <s>gandharvas</s>,
groups of <s>apsarases</s> play at midday, O king.
It carried auspicious kuṅkuma cast off by the <s>apsarases</s>,
fragrant and many-colored, produced from the trees on its own banks.
It was hard to look upon because the disk of the sun passed into masses of waves;
it was adorned on both banks by blows made by the elephants of the gods.
With the waters from <s>Śakra</s>'s elephants' temples and with sandal from the breasts of heavenly women,
its water, thus joined together, was frequented by bees.
The trees growing on its banks were adorned with fragrant flowers,
and were noisy with the humming of bees, bewildered as they were drawn away.

children.text: yasyāstīre ratiṃ yānti sadā kāmavaśā mṛgāḥ
children.translated_text: On its bank deer, always under the sway of desire, take delight,
as do ascetic groves and seers, and likewise gods together with <s>apsarases</s>.
There, with purified bodies and honored by the gods, they obtain
heavenly women in abundance, whose faces resemble lotuses and the moon.
It always bears water untroubled even by hosts of gods,
untroubled by <s>Pulindas</s>, by throngs of kings, and by packs of tigers.
The king saw that river, its water clear and fit to drink, spotless as a starry sky;
seeing it, the king went on, for it grants the desired wishes of the good.
The kāśa grasses growing on its bank, full and resembling rays of the moon,
made its lovely bank shine with great trees of many forms.
It is always frequented by various brāhmaṇas and also by gods.

children.text: yā ca sadā sakalaughavināśaṃ bhaktajanasya karotyacireṇa
children.translated_text: It always quickly destroys every flood of sin for devoted people;

children.text: yānugatā saritāṃ hi kadambairyānugatā satataṃ hi munīndraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is followed by clusters of rivers and constantly followed by the chief sages.

children.text: yā hi sutāniva pāti manuṣyānyā ca yutā satataṃ himasaṃghaiḥ
children.translated_text: It protects human beings like its own sons and is always joined with masses of snow;

children.text: yā ca yutā satataṃ suravṛndairyā ca janaiḥ svahitāya śritā vai ||
children.translated_text: it is always joined with hosts of gods, and people resort to it for their own welfare.

children.text: prayuktā ca kesarigaṇaiḥ karivṛndajuṣṭā saṃtānayuktasalilāpi suvarṇayuktā
children.translated_text: It is frequented by troops of lions and enjoyed by herds of elephants; though its water is continuous, it is also filled with gold.
The king, whose fame was like the moon, saw it, its coolness increased by the spreading heat of the sun's rays.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
As he looked upon the holy river, his weariness carried away by its breeze,
while going onward he saw <s>Himavān</s>, the great mountain.
It was surrounded by many pale peaks that seemed to scratch the sky,
an auspicious place with no passage even for birds, but with the path of siddhas.
On every side it was filled with great sounds born from the streams of rivers,
so that no other sound was heard; it was charming and possessed of cool waters.
The lord of men saw the auspicious mountain, wearing blue deodar forests as a lower garment
and clouds as its upper robe.
In places it had a turban made of white clouds and a crown of moon and sun;
its whole body was smeared with snow, and elsewhere it was mixed with minerals.
It was as though its limbs had been smeared with sandal and marked with five-fingered handprints;
it gave coolness even in summer, and was rugged and difficult because of its rocks.
In places it was stamped by the lac-red feet of <s>apsarases</s>.
In places it was touched by the rays of the sun, and in places covered by darkness;
in places, through terrifying cave-mouths, it seemed to drink great waters.
In places it was adorned by bands of <s>vidyādharas</s> at play,

children.text: upagītaṃ tathā mukhyaiḥ kiṃnarāṇāṃ gaṇaiḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: and in places it was sung over by the foremost troops of <s>kiṃnaras</s>.
In places, on drinking grounds of <s>gandharvas</s> and <s>apsarases</s>,
it was beautified by fallen divine flowers of santānaka and other trees.
In places it was strewn with flower-beds from which sleepers had risen,
and with crushed ones as well, delightful to the <s>gandharvas</s>.
It had places where the wind was blocked and that were adorned with blue turf.
in places filled with flowers, exceedingly lovely and auspicious;
a mountain that is a refuge for ascetics and very hard for pleasure-seekers to reach;
roamed by deer, with great trees broken by elephants;
where, at the roar of lions, the dreadful cry of the terrified is heard,

children.text: dṛśyate na ca saṃśrāntaṃ gajānāmākulaṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: and the confused herd of elephants is seen no longer at ease;
where the banks, adorned with thickets, are occupied by ascetics,
and by the jewels produced from it the three worlds are adorned;
always an unfailing refuge, frequented by people who are not base,
the man who is not base beholds that mountain, not lacking in the wealth of jewels;

children.text: alpena tapasā yatra siddhiṃ prāpsyanti tāpasāḥ
children.translated_text: where ascetics will attain perfection with only slight austerity,
and by the mere sight of which every stain is destroyed;
with waters belonging to the falls from great cataracts, cascades, precipices, and the like,
carried by the wind and constantly refreshing places here and there;
with peaks here and there made wet with gathered water and rising high,
with regions hard to approach and made harsh by the constant heat of the sun;
with uninterrupted masses of branches from great deodar trees,
adorned by places shaped like forests of bamboo pillars;
with great peaks like snow-white parasols and with hundreds of falling streams,
with rough places where water is found by sound, and with caverns blocked by snow;

children.text: dṛṣṭvaiva taṃ cārunitambabhūmiṃ mahānubhāvaḥ sa tu madranāthaḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen that mountain, with its lovely slopes and ground, the mighty <s>Madranātha</s>

children.text: babhrāma tatraiva mudā sametaḥ sthānaṃ tadā kiṃcidathāsasāda ||
children.translated_text: wandered there filled with joy, and then came upon a certain place.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
A very charming region of that very lord of mountains,
inaccessible to other human beings, was reached by him through divine chance.
The best of rivers, <s>Airāvatī</s>, issued from that region,
and that cloud-dark region was thick in many ways with clusters of trees:
with śāla, tāla, tamāla, and dark karṇikāra trees,
and with nyagrodha, aśvattha, śirīṣa, and śiṃśapā trees;
with śleṣmātaka, āmalaka, harītaka, and vibhītaka,
with bhūrja, muñjaka, and bāṇa plants, and with saptacchada trees;
with great nimba trees and nimba trees, with nirguṇḍī and hari trees,
with great deodar trees and likewise with kāleyaka trees;
with padmaka, sandalwood, bilva, kapittha, and red sandalwood,
with mātāmra, riṣṭaka, walnut, abdaka, and likewise arjuna trees;
with hastikarṇa, sumanas, and fully flowering kovidāra trees,
and also with old āmalaka trees, dhanaka, and marāṭaka;
with date-palms and coconut-palms, with priyāla, āmrātaka, and iṅguda,
with tantumāla, splendid dhava trees, and kāśmīrīparṇī plants;
with nutmeg, areca-nut, kaṭphala, and elāvalī fruit,
with mandāra, kovidāra, and kiṃśuka trees, their flowers like bright garments;
with yavāsa, śamīparṇa, vetasa, and water-vetasa,
with red atiraṅga and nāraṅga, with hiṅgu and priyaṅgu;
with red aśoka trees and other aśokas, with ākalla and avicāraka,
with mucukunda and kunda, with āṭarūṣa and parūṣaka;
with kirāta, kiṅkirāta, ketaka, and white ketaka,
with śobhāñjana and añjana, with sukaliṅga and nikoṭaka;
with excellent asana trees, charming as if clothed in gold,
and with delightful sahakāra mangoes shaped like the arrows of <s>Manmatha</s>;
with yellow yūthikā and also with white yūthikā,
with jātī and campaka-jātī, and with tumbara and atumbara;
with moca and loca, with lakuca, sesame-flower plants, and lotuses,
and with cavyaka, beloved of lovers, covered with excellent flowers;
with bakula trees bearing flower-buds, and with pāribhadra and haridrā trees,
with dhārā-kadamba, kuṭaja, kadamba, and mountain-kuṭaja;
with ādityamustaka, kumbha, saffron, and kāmavallabha plants,
with kaṭphala, badara, and nīpa trees, brightly blazing like lamps;
with red and white pālīvana trees, with pomegranates and campaka trees,
with bandhūka and fine bandhūka, and with varieties of kuñjaka;
with blossoms, pāṭalā trees, jasmine, and oleander,
with kurabaka, himavara, jambu, and royal jambu trees;
with citron trees and camphor trees, with guru and aguru trees,
with bimba and pratibimba, and with spreading saṃtānaka and vitānaka creepers;
and with guggulu trees, hintāla palms, and white sugarcane,
with grassless karavīra, aśoka, and cakramardana;
crowded with pīlu, dhātakī, and ciribilva,
with tamarind, lodhra, viḍaṅga, and kṣīrikā trees;
with aśmantaka, kāla, jambīra, and śvaitaka trees,
with bhallātaka, indrayava, and valguja, which bring about siddhi;
with nāgakesara trees, charming with beautiful filaments,
with karamarda, kāsamarda, ariṣṭaka, and variṣṭaka,
with rudrākṣa, grape-born vines, saptāhva, and putrajīvaka;
with kaṅkola, cloves, cinnamon trees, and pārijātaka,
and with tendrils of long pepper and nāgavalī in separate places;
with thickets of black pepper and likewise with navamallikā,
with chief bowers of grape-vines and bowers of atimuktaka;
with cucumbers and with auspicious, fruit-bearing tendrils of nartikā plants.
with spreading vines of <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> gourds and, here and there, of bottle-gourds as well;
with spreading growths of <s>cirbhiṭa</s>, and with <s>paṭolī</s> and <s>kāravellaka</s> vines;
with canopies of <s>karkoṭakī</s>, and with eggplants and large <s>bṛhatī</s> fruits;
with thorny plants, radishes, roots, and various root-vegetables too;
with <s>kahlāra</s> flowers, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>rurūṭa</s>, and sweet-thorn plants;
with <s>bhāṇḍīra</s>, <s>vidūsāra</s>, royal rose-apples, and sandy growths;
with all kinds of <s>suvarcalā</s> herbs and likewise with mustard plants;
with <s>kākolī</s> and <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, with <s>chattrā</s> and <s>aticchattrā</s>;
with <s>kāsamardī</s>, with other bright growths, and with bulbs and stalks;
and likewise with milk-vegetables and also dark greens;
with pulse-grains and with every kind of grain, without exception;
with diverse medicinal plants, shining brightly indeed;
with herbs that promote long life, fame, and strength, O king;
with plants that remove fear of old age and death, and likewise those that remove fear of hunger;
and with many kinds of plants that bring good fortune and repel what is contemptible;
there also with bamboo creepers, and likewise with hollow <s>kīcaka</s> bamboos;
with <s>kāśa</s> reeds, moon-white <s>kāśa</s>, and thickets of reeds as well;
with lovely clumps of <s>kuśa</s> grass and delightful clumps of sugarcane;
with a rare and auspicious class of cotton and jasmine plants;
and also with excellent, charming groves of plantains;
and likewise with regions green like emeralds and covered with fresh turf;
with places filled with <s>irā</s> flowers and, in parts, with saffron;
with <s>tagara</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, and knots of fragrant herbs;
with golden flowers, and likewise with earth-flowers and other kinds too;
with citron trees, ground grasses, juicy growths, and shoots as well;
with ginger, celery-seed plants, <s>kuberaka</s>, and <s>priyālaka</s>;
and with fragrant aquatic plants and other water-born growths;
some shining like the rising sun, and likewise others resembling the sun and moon;
some the color of refined gold, and some resembling flax blossoms;
others like reed-leaves, and, in places, with land-leaves too;
strewn with five-colored and many-colored flowers alike;
with lotuses pleasing and joyful to the eye of the beholder, and with water-lilies like the moon;
and with auspicious elephant-faced lotuses shaped like tongues of fire;
with blue lotuses and <s>kahlāras</s>, with <s>guñjātaka</s> and <s>kaseruka</s>;
with water-chestnuts, lotus-fibers, <s>karaṭa</s> plants, and silver lotuses;
with aquatic and terrestrial roots, and especially with fruits and flowers;
and with many kinds of wild rice fit for sages to eat, O king;

children.text: na taddhānyaṃ na tatsasyaṃ na tacchākaṃ na tatphalam
children.translated_text: there was no grain, no crop, no vegetable, no fruit,

children.text: na tanmūlaṃ na tatkandaṃ na tatpuṣpaṃ narādhipa ||
children.translated_text: no root, no tuber, and no flower, O king,
whether divine, produced in <s>Nāgaloka</s>, or born in the human world,

children.text: anūpotthaṃ vanotthaṃ ca tatra yannāsti pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether arising in marshland or in the forest, that was not there, O ruler of the earth;
everything always had flowers and fruit, undecaying, according to the proper season;
the lord of <s>Madra</s> saw it through his austerity and intense yogic power;

children.text: dadṛśe ca tathā tatra nānārūpān patatriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: and there he also saw birds of many forms there:
peacocks, <s>śatapattra</s> birds, <s>kalaviṅkas</s>, and cuckoos;
as well as <s>kādambakas</s>, swans, <s>koyaṣṭis</s>, and wagtails;
ospreys, <s>kālakūṭas</s>, <s>khaṭvāṅgas</s>, and <s>lubdhakas</s> too;
<s>gokṣveḍakas</s>, <s>kumbhas</s>, <s>dhārtarāṣṭras</s>, parrots, and herons;
<s>ghātukas</s>, ruddy geese, <s>kaṭukas</s>, plovers, and <s>bhaṭas</s>;
<s>putrapriyas</s>, <s>lohapṛṣṭhas</s>, <s>gocarmas</s>, and <s>girivartakas</s>;
pigeons, <s>kamalas</s>, mynahs, and <s>jīvajīvakas</s>;
quails, partridges, <s>vārtākas</s>, <s>raktavartmans</s>, and <s>prabhadrakas</s>;
red-crested and golden-crested birds, fowl, and wood-fowl;
francolins, <s>kalaviṅkas</s>, and also saffron-crested birds;
<s>bhṛṅgarājas</s>, <s>sīrapādas</s>, <s>bhūliṅgas</s>, and new <s>ḍiṇḍimas</s>;
<s>mañjulītakas</s>, <s>dātyūhas</s>, <s>bhāradvājas</s>, and <s>caṣas</s>;
these and many other delightful flocks of birds;
wild beasts of various forms, deer, and great deer as well;
tigers, maned lions, lions, panthers, <s>śarabhas</s>, and wolves;
bears, <s>tarakṣus</s>, and many langurs and monkeys;
<s>śaśalomans</s>, with <s>kādambas</s>, and cats swift as the wind;
mice, mongooses, crows, lions, and creatures charming among the trees;

children.text: tathā mattāṃśca mātaṃgān mahiṣān gavayān vṛṣān
children.translated_text: and likewise rutting elephants, buffaloes, wild oxen, and bulls;
yaks and <s>sṛmaras</s>, and likewise gaurs and wild asses;
rams, sheep, spotted deer, and then dogs;
blue antelopes, great <s>nālas</s>, fierce beasts, and mothering deer;
fang-bearing creatures, forest <s>śarabhas</s>, and <s>śambaras</s> shaped like cranes;
fierce ones, <s>kṛtamālas</s>, black-tailed animals, and <s>toraṇas</s>;
tusked beasts, rhinoceroses, boars, horses, and asses and donkeys;
these, hostile and mutually opposed by nature, the lord of <s>Madra</s>
saw in the forest without hostility, and he reached supreme wonder;
and that holy hermitage had formerly belonged to <s>Atri</s>, O king;
through his favor it was endowed with radiance, with both stationary and moving beings;

children.text: hiṃsanti hi na cānyonyaṃ hiṃsakāstu parasparam ||
children.translated_text: for the violent creatures there did not injure one another at all;
all the flesh-eating animals there fed on milk and fruit;
they had been created there in great abundance by the very great-souled <s>Atri</s>;
and the king himself dwelt on the slopes and lower flanks of the mountains.
They exude divine milk, sweet as nectar to the throat.
In some places, O king, there are she-buffaloes, and in other places goats everywhere;

children.text: śilāḥ kṣīreṇa sampūrṇā dadhnā cānyatra vā bahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: rocks are filled with milk, and elsewhere also with curds outside.
Seeing this, the lord of the earth obtained supreme delight.
There were divine lakes there, and rivers with clear water,
as well as channels, warm and cold in separate parts,

children.text: kandarāṇi ca śailasya susevyāni pade pade ||
children.translated_text: and caves of the mountain, pleasant to resort to at every step.
For five yojanas all around there is no fall of snow there.
There is no valley beneath the summit of that fine mountain.
There, O king, is a pale summit of the lord of mountains,

children.text: himapātaṃ ghanā yatra kurvanti sahitāḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: where dense clouds, gathered together, always produce snowfall.

children.text: tatrāsti cāparaṃ śṛṅgaṃ yatra toyaghanā ghanāḥ
children.translated_text: And there is another peak there, where dense rain-clouds
constantly shower the excellent summit with hailstones.
That hermitage is charming, where the earth bears what is desired,
and, because it is useful to the chief gods, the fruit-trees are rich with fruit.
It is supreme, always sung around by bees and served by heavenly women,
destroying every sin like a striking power of the mountain itself.
There, O lord of men, monkeys play from place to place,
and heaps of snow shine with the brilliance of the disk of the moon.
That hermitage, on every side, has caves blocked by snow
and is surrounded by mountain enclosures, always inaccessible to human beings.
That great king <s>Purūravas</s>, whose devotion had been cultivated before,
reached the site of that hermitage through the grace of the god of gods.
That king saw the charming hermitage that dispelled weariness, adorned with hundreds of lovely flowers,

children.text: kṛtaṃ svayaṃ ruciramathātriṇā śubhaṃ śubhāvahaṃ ca hi dadṛśe sa madrarāṭ ||
children.translated_text: made beautiful and auspicious by <s>Atri</s> himself, and bringing auspiciousness.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tatra yau tau mahāśṛṅgau mahāvarṇau mahāhimau
children.translated_text: There were those two great peaks there, great in color and great in snow;
between the two of them was a third peak, exceedingly high.
It consisted of rocks always heated by the sun and was always free from clouds.
Below it, among a group of trees, in the western quarter,
there was a fair-looking opening surrounded by jasmine creepers.
As soon as he saw it, the king, filled with curiosity, entered it.
It was exceedingly dense with darkness, only a nalva in length, and very narrow.
After he had passed beyond that nalva's length, it shone with the ornament of its own light.
Then he saw that very lofty, exceedingly deep, and circular place.

children.text: na tatra sūryastapati na virājati candramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the sun does not burn, nor does the moon shine,
yet a daylight-like radiance is there day and night.
It extended for more than a krośa and was resplendent with a lake.
Around that lake was a terrace attached to the mountain,
adorned with trees of gold, silver, and coral.
It was bright with flowers of many kinds of jewels, shining like brilliant ornaments.
In that lake were lotuses whose petals were rubies,
furnished with networks of diamond filaments and fragrant as well,
with leaves of emerald, blue stones, and vaiḍūrya, O lord of the earth.
Their seed-vessels, too, O king, were made of gold.
The ground in that lake, O king, was not merely crowded with diamonds;
it was furnished with many kinds of jewels and served as a refuge for aquatic creatures,
for cowries, oysters, and conches, O lord of the earth,

children.text: makarāṇāṃ ca matsyānāṃ caṇḍānāṃ kacchapaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: and for makaras, fish, fierce creatures, and turtles as well.
There were fragments of emerald and diamonds by the thousands,
rubies, sapphires, and great sapphires, O king,
all kinds of topaz, and karkoṭaka stones as well,

children.text: tutthakasya tu khaṇḍāni tathā śeṣasya bhāgaśaḥ
children.translated_text: fragments of tuttha, and portions also of śeṣa stone,
chief rājāvarta stones and also rucirākṣa gems,
sun-stones and moon-stones, and the blue stone of finest color,
beautiful jyotīrasa stones and syamantaka stones in portions,
suroraga and valakṣa stones, and likewise crystal,
gomedaka and pittaka stones, and powdered emerald,
vaiḍūrya and saugandhika stones, and the royal gem, O king,
the foremost diamond itself, and also the brahma-jewel.
There were pearls from pearl-oysters, bearing the forms of stars.
That water was pleasantly warm; by bathing in it one destroyed cold.
In the middle of that lake was a beautiful slab of vaiḍūrya.

children.text: pramāṇena tathā sā ca dve ca rājandhanuḥśate
children.translated_text: Its measure, O king, was two hundred bows,
and it was square, lovely, and fashioned by <s>Atri</s>'s austerity.
Wherever there was a place like the mouth of the cavern, it was golden,

children.text: pradeśaḥ sa tu rājendra dvīpe tasminmanohare ||
children.translated_text: that spot, O king of kings, on that charming island.
There was also a lovely lotus-pool there, O king, on that stone surface,
with very cool, clear drinking-water, and shining with aquatic flowers.
It was like the sky, O king, square and charming.
Its water was sweet, light, cool, and fragrant.

children.text: na kṣiṇoti yathā kaṇṭhaṃ kukṣiṃ nāpūrayatyapi
children.translated_text: It did not parch the throat, nor did it fill the belly;

children.text: tṛptiṃ vidhatte paramāṃ śarīre ca mahatsukham ||
children.translated_text: it produced supreme satisfaction and great pleasure in the body.

children.text: madhye tu tasyāḥ prāsādaṃ nirmitaṃ tapasātriṇā
children.translated_text: In its middle was a palace built by <s>Atri</s> through austerity,
auspicious, made entirely of jewels, and entered by a golden bridge.
It was a silver palace, beneficial and resembling the rays of the moon,
with beautiful vaiḍūrya stairways and pure coral beams,
with great sapphire pillars and a terrace set with emeralds.
It was lovely, sparkling with nets of diamond rays, delightful to the sight.
In that palace was the blessed God of gods, <s>Janārdana</s>,
asleep upon a row of serpent coils and adorned with every ornament.
One leg of the God of gods, the discus-bearer, was bent at the knee,
and the second foot likewise rested upon the serpent-lord, O sinless one.
The foot of him who reclined on the coils of <s>Śeṣa</s> lay in <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s lap,
and his arm, adorned with armlets, was placed upon the coils of the serpent-lord.
One arm of the God of gods held his divine head, which rested on the backs of his fingers,

children.text: ekaṃ vai devadevasya dvitīyaṃ tu prasāritam ||
children.translated_text: while the second was stretched out.
It shone with its wrist resting on the fully bent knee,
slightly bent as well, with the hand placed near the region of the navel.

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ tu bhujaṃ tasya caturthaṃ tu tathā śṛṇu
children.translated_text: Now hear of his third arm, and likewise of the fourth.
It held a santānaka flower and moved toward the region of his nose.
His foot was being massaged by <s>Lakṣmī</s> with hands like lotus petals,
and he wore a crown of santānaka garlands, adorned with necklaces and armlets.
The god was likewise adorned with bracelets and rings,
and he blazed with the lovely jeweled crest set upon the hood of the serpent-lord.
Unknowable in his true being and deeds, he had then been installed there by <s>Atri</s>.
He was continually worshipped by siddhas and honored with santānaka flowers.
His limbs were anointed with divine fragrances and perfumed with divine incense,
and siddhas always brought him delicious, excellent, and pleasing fruits.
The king looked straight ahead at that god, <s>Utpalaśīrṣaka</s>, whose excellent sides were adorned,

children.text: tataḥ sammukham udvīkṣya vavande sa narādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then he bowed to him.

children.text: jānubhyāṃ śirasā caiva gatvā bhūmiṃ yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Going down to the ground with his knees and head in the prescribed manner,
he then praised <s>Madhusūdana</s> with the thousand names.

children.text: pradakṣiṇamatho cakre sa tūtthāya punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After that he rose and circumambulated him again and again.
Having seen the lovely sanctuary, he again stayed there in the hermitage.
Taking shelter in a certain very charming cave outside the cavern,
he practiced austerity right there, worshipping <s>Madhusūdana</s>.
He worshipped with various kinds of flowers, with fruits, roots, and milk preparations,
bathing three times each day and devoted to the worship of fire.
The lord of men constantly sustained his life with water from the divine pool,
having abandoned every kind of food.
The king passed his time sleeping in an uncovered cave.
Having also given up the act of eating, O king, he lived on water alone,

children.text: na tasya glānimāyāti śarīraṃ ca tadadbhutam ||
children.translated_text: and his body did not come to exhaustion; that was astonishing.

children.text: evaṃ sa rājā tapasi prasaktaḥ sampūjayandevavaraṃ sadaiva
children.translated_text: Thus that king, intent on austerity and always worshipping the best of gods,
lived for some time in that heaven-like hermitage, finding no suffering there.
In that lovely hermitage-ground, having given up food and possessions,
he watched the play and amusement of the <s>gandharvas</s> together with the <s>apsarases</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā puṣpoccayaṃ bhūri granthayitvā tathā srajaḥ
children.translated_text: He gathered many flowers and likewise strung garlands;
after first presenting the foremost portion to the god, he then gave them to the <s>gandharvas</s>.
Although he saw those absorbed in gathering flowers and playing as they pleased,
and their gestures of many different forms, he saw them as if he did not see them.
One woman, intent on gathering flowers, was wrapped in a net of creepers,
abandoned by her circle of friends and left behind by her lover.
Another, fragrant like a lotus, had her face swarmed over by bees
drawn by the wind of her breath, until she was freed by her lover.
One woman had her eyes invaded by masses of pollen,
and by the wind of her lover's breath her eyes were made free of dust.

children.text: kācid uccīya puṣpāṇi dadau kāntasya bhāminī
children.translated_text: One lovely woman picked flowers and gave them to her beloved,
and she shone with a head-wreath made from flowers strung by her beloved.
After picking and stringing them herself, she was given a head-wreath by her beloved,
and, increasing the power of love, she considered herself as if she had accomplished her purpose.
'In this dense bower let there be a creeper with especially fine flowers'--
saying so, one woman was led aside in private by her lover, who desired to make love.
One woman, gathering flowers from a creeper bent down by her beloved,
considered herself superior to all the others in every virtue.
Some lovely divine women saw the king, each in a separate lotus pond,
as they played with the <s>gandharvas</s>.
One pure-smiling woman splashed her beloved with water,
and another, being splashed by her beloved, attained delight.
A lovely-limbed woman, grown weary, struck her beloved as well,
and the fair-hipped one appeared with her breasts dancing from her breath.
The binding of her mass of hair had been loosened by her lover's splashing of water,
and with her face disordered by her hair she shone like a lotus plant surrounded by bees.
In a lotus pond covered with flowers resembling her own eyes,
one woman, hidden there, was found after a long time by her beloved, who searched carefully.
One woman, after bathing, spoke urgently on the pretext of being cold,
and she received the embrace of her lover that her heart had long desired.
Wearing a fine garment, wet with water and clinging to her limbs,

children.text: dhārayantī janaṃ cakre kācit tatra samanmatham ||
children.translated_text: one pure-smiling woman there made the people full of passion.
One woman, being pulled in the water by her beloved by the strands of her neck-garland,
laughed for a long time at her lover when the garland-string broke and he fell.
One woman, bent over, with nail-scratches near the knee supported by a friend,
and another, confused and long submerged, went to her beloved for refuge.
One woman, with the sun behind her, was squeezing the water from her hair;
standing on a slab of stone, she was seen by her husband with eyes afflicted by desire.
Her garland was cut, she was disheveled, and the saffron from her breasts had been transferred.
It shone with that lake-water, like a beloved woman after the play of love.
And by a company of gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, and divine women who had bathed well,
he saw <s>Janārdana</s>, the god of gods, being worshipped.

children.text: kvacic ca dadṛśe rājā latāgṛhagatāḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: And in places the king saw women who had gone into bowers of vines,
adorning their own bodies, their minds laid upon their beloveds.
One, holding a mirror, was intent on hearing from the mouth of a messenger
the words of her beloved, and she shone all the more in that state.
Another, hurried by her messenger, was putting her ornaments in the wrong places
and, her mind possessed by <s>Manmatha</s>, did not even notice it.
In a place adorned with a mass of exceedingly fragrant flowers driven by the wind,
he saw one woman drinking maireya wine on the blue turf.
One lovely woman herself made her lover drink,
and another fair-hipped woman drank what had been offered by her lover's hand.
Another, after drinking water joined with the blue lotuses of her own restless eyes,

children.text: pītvā papraccha ramaṇaṃ kva gate te mamotpale ||
children.translated_text: asked her lover, 'Where have my lotuses gone?'

children.text: tvayaiva pītau tau nūnamityuktā ramaṇena sā
children.translated_text: When her lover said, 'Surely those two were drunk by you yourself,'
she understood it so and, from innocence, became deeply ashamed.
One beautiful-browed woman drank a drink offered by her beloved,
left over after her beloved had drunk it, especially flavorful and increasing desire.
Likewise, at the drinking gatherings of those women, that bull among men
heard varied song mixed with the sound of stringed instruments.
At twilight those women, O king, always dance before
<s>Janārdana</s>, the god of gods, preceded by many kinds of instruments.
When a watch of the night had passed, having come out from the cave-mouth,
they dwelt, joined with their lovers, in a cave fashioned with supreme splendor,
covered with vines of many fragrances, fragrant with many scents,
with many variegated beds and adorned with heaps of flowers.
Thus seeing the sports of the <s>apsarases</s> on the mountain,
O great king, he practiced austerity, his mind offered to <s>Keśava</s>.
The companies of <s>gandharvas</s> and <s>apsarases</s> went to the king and said:
'O king, subduer of enemies, you have reached this region resembling heaven.

children.text: vayaṃ hi te pradāsyāmo manasaḥ kāṅkṣitānvarān
children.translated_text: For we shall grant you the boons desired by your mind;

children.text: tānādāya gṛhaṃ gaccha tiṣṭheha yadi vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: take them and go home, or else remain here again.'
The king said:
'All of you are of unfailing sight, and you are mighty in splendor.
Grant this boon today itself: favor from <s>Madhusūdana</s>.'
When they had said, 'So be it,' that king <s>Purūravāḥ</s>
dwelt there happily for a month, worshipping <s>Janārdana</s>.
The king was always dear to the <s>gandharvas</s> and <s>apsarases</s>,
and that people was pleased by the king's conduct, free from greed.

children.text: māsasya madhye sa nṛpaḥ praviṣṭastadāśramaṃ ratnasahasracitram
children.translated_text: In the middle of the month the king entered that hermitage, variegated with thousands of jewels;

children.text: toyāśanastatra hyuvāsa māsaṃ yāvatsitānto nṛpa phālgunasya ||
children.translated_text: living on water there, he stayed for a month, O king, until the bright close of <s>Phālguna</s>.
At the end of the bright fortnight of <s>Phālguna</s>, King <s>Purūravāḥ</s>, in a dream,
heard the auspicious utterance of that same god of gods.
'When this night has passed, you will meet <s>Atri</s>;
having met with him, O king, you will become one whose purpose is fulfilled.'
Having seen such a dream, that royal seer, equal to <s>Indra</s> in valor,
at daybreak bathed according to rule, with his senses controlled.
Having fulfilled his duty as he wished and having worshipped <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: dadarśātriṃ muniṃ rājā pratyakṣaṃ tapasāṃ nidhim ||
children.translated_text: the king saw the sage <s>Atri</s> directly, a treasure of austerities.
The righteous one reported the dream of the god of gods,
and then he heard the speech uttered by the deities:
'This is so, O protector of the earth; no deliberation should be made about it.
You have thus obtained favor from <s>Janārdana</s>, the god of gods.'
The king, having performed worship of the gods and having offered oblations into the fire,
obtained all desires through the gift of a boon from <s>Keśava</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
North of that hermitage, frequented by <s>Tripurāri</s>,
with peaks made of many jewels and furnished with wish-fulfilling trees,

children.text: madhye himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe kailāso nāma parvataḥ
children.translated_text: on the middle ridge of <s>Himavat</s> is a mountain named <s>Kailāsa</s>;
on it the glorious <s>Kubera</s> dwells together with the <s>Guhyakas</s>.
The lord of <s>Alakā</s>, a king guarded by <s>apsarases</s>, delights there.
Born from the foot of <s>Kailāsa</s> is a holy, auspicious lake with cool water;
it is called <s>Mandodaka</s>, and its water resembles curds.

children.text: tasmāt pravahate divyā nadī mandākinī śubhā ||
children.translated_text: From it flows the divine, auspicious river <s>Mandākinī</s>.

children.text: divyaṃ ca nandanaṃ tatra tasyāstīre mahadvanam
children.translated_text: There on its bank is the divine <s>Nandana</s>, a great forest.
To the northeast of <s>Kailāsa</s> is the divine mountain <s>Saugandhika</s>;
toward the divine <s>Suvela</s> mountain, made of every mineral,

children.text: candraprabho nāma giriḥ yaḥ śubhro ratnasaṃnibhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is a mountain named <s>Candraprabha</s>, white and resembling a jewel.
Near it is a divine lake, famed by the name <s>Acchoda</s>;
from it arises the divine, auspicious river <s>Acchodakā</s>.
On its bank is the divine and great auspicious forest <s>Caitraratha</s>.
On that mountain dwells <s>Maṇibhadra</s> with his retinue,
a fierce commander of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, surrounded by <s>Guhyakas</s>.

children.text: puṇyā mandākinī nāma nadī hyacchodakā śubhā ||
children.translated_text: Holy is the river named <s>Mandākinī</s>, and auspicious too is <s>Acchodakā</s>.
In the middle of the circle of the earth they enter the great ocean.
Southeast of <s>Kailāsa</s> is the auspicious mountain of all herbs;
toward the divine <s>Suvela</s> mountain, made of realgar,
is the great mountain <s>Lohita</s>, sun-bright and with golden peaks.

children.text: tasya pāde mahaddivyaṃ lohitaṃ sumahat saraḥ
children.translated_text: At its foot is a great divine lake, very vast and red.
From that arises the sacred <s>Lauhitya</s>, the great river.

children.text: divyāraṇyaṃ viśokaṃ ca tasya tīre mahadvanam
children.translated_text: On its bank is a great forest, divine and free from sorrow.
On that mountain dwells the yakṣa <s>Maṇidhara</s>, self-controlled.
He is surrounded by gentle and very righteous <s>Guhyakas</s>.
To the west and north of <s>Kailāsa</s> is <s>Kakudmān</s>, the mountain of medicinal herbs.
There too is <s>Kakudmatī</s>, and there was the origin of <s>Rudra</s> <s>Kakudmin</s>.
Then there is <s>Añjana</s>, the three-peaked <s>Traikakuda</s>, facing the mountain <s>Trikakuda</s>.
There is the very great <s>Vaidyuta</s> mountain, made of every kind of mineral.
At its foot is the great divine lake <s>Mānasa</s>, frequented by siddhas.
From it arises the sacred <s>Sarayū</s>, purifier of the worlds.

children.text: yasyāstīre vanaṃ divyaṃ vaibhrājaṃ nāma viśrutam ||
children.translated_text: On its bank is the divine forest well known as <s>Vaibhrāja</s>.
There, as an attendant of <s>Kubera</s>, dwells the self-controlled son of <s>Praheti</s>,
the rākṣasa <s>Brahmadhātā</s>, of limitless valor.
In the western quarter from <s>Kailāsa</s> is a divine mountain of every medicinal herb.
It is <s>Varuṇa</s>, best of mountains, adorned with veins of gold ore.
Beloved of <s>Bhava</s>, splendid, it is a mountain resembling gold.
It is covered with masses of divine rocks made of fine gold.
With a hundred golden peaks it seems to scrape the sky.
<s>Śṛṅgavān</s> is a very great, divine, inaccessible, and lofty mountain.
On that mountain dwells <s>Giriśa</s>, the smoke-red lord.
From its foot springs the lake called <s>Śailoda</s>.
From it arises the sacred and auspicious river <s>Śailodakā</s>.
That river, between the two <s>Cakṣuṣī</s> courses, entered the western ocean.
North of <s>Kailāsa</s> there is the auspicious mountain <s>Sarvauṣadha</s>.
It faces the excellent white mountain, made of yellow orpiment.
The great mountain <s>Hiraṇyaśṛṅga</s> is made of divine medicinal herbs.
At its foot is a great divine lake with golden sand.

children.text: ramyaṃ bindusaro nāma yatra rājā bhagīrathaḥ
children.translated_text: It is the lovely lake called <s>Bindusaras</s>, where king <s>Bhagīratha</s>

children.text: gaṅgārthe sa tu rājarṣiruvāsa bahulāḥ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the royal sage stayed for many years for the sake of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
'May my ancestors, their bones washed by the water of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, go to heaven.'

children.text: tatra tripathagā devī prathamaṃ tu pratiṣṭhitā ||
children.translated_text: There the goddess <s>Tripathagā</s> was first established.
Born from the foot of <s>Soma</s>, she is divided sevenfold.
There are sacrificial posts made of jewels and aerial palaces made of gold.

children.text: tatreṣṭvā kratubhiḥ siddhaḥ śakraḥ suragaṇaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: There <s>Śakra</s>, together with the hosts of gods, attained success after sacrificing with rituals.
There the divine path of light, the circle of the stars,

children.text: dṛśyate bhāsurā rātrau devī tripathagā tu sā
children.translated_text: is seen shining at night, and that goddess <s>Tripathagā</s>

children.text: antarikṣaṃ divaṃ caiva bhāvayitvā bhuvaṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: after filling the atmosphere and heaven, came down to the earth.
She fell upon the head of <s>Bhava</s> and was restrained by his yogic power.

children.text: tasyā ye bindavaḥ kecitkruddhāyāḥ patitā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: Some drops of her, as she was angry, fell upon the earth.
By those many lakes were formed; therefore it is remembered as <s>Bindusaras</s>.
Then, when she had suddenly been restrained by <s>Bhava</s> in anger,
he understood the cruel intention that the goddess wished to carry out:

children.text: bhittvā viśāmi pātālaṃ srotasā gṛhya śaṃkaram ||
children.translated_text: 'Breaking through, I shall enter <s>Pātāla</s>, carrying <s>Śaṃkara</s> along with my current.'

children.text: athāvalepaṃ taṃ jñātvā tasyāḥ kruddhastu śaṃkaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śaṃkara</s>, angered, understood that arrogance of hers.
His intention was to make that river disappear within his limbs.
At that very time, however, he saw the king before him,
emaciated, his veins standing out, his senses distressed by hunger.
'I was already pleased by this man before for the sake of the river.'

children.text: buddhvā'sya varadānaṃ tu tataḥ kopaṃ nyayacchata ||
children.translated_text: Recognizing the boon granted to him, he then restrained his anger.
Hearing the word of <s>Brahmā</s>, and holding the river as he had been told,
he then released her, though she had been restrained by his own power.
For the sake of <s>Bhagīratha</s>, pleased by his fierce austerity, he released the river.
Then he released the seven streams of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Three faced east, and likewise three faced west.
The streams of <s>Tripathā</s> became sevenfold.

children.text: nalinī hlādinī caiva pāvanī caiva prācyagā
children.translated_text: <s>Nalinī</s>, <s>Hlādinī</s>, and <s>Pāvanī</s> went eastward.

children.text: sītā cakṣuśca sindhuśca tisrastā vai pratīcyagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Cakṣu</s>, and <s>Sindhu</s>, those three, went westward.
The seventh of them followed <s>Bhagīratha</s> to the south.
Therefore she is indeed <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, and she entered the southern ocean.

children.text: sapta caitāḥ plāvayanti varṣaṃ tu himasāhvayam
children.translated_text: These seven flood the region called <s>Himavat</s>.
The seven auspicious rivers were born from <s>Bindusaras</s>.
They flooded those lands everywhere, mostly inhabited by mlecchas.
They flooded mountain lands, the <s>Kukuras</s>, <s>Raudhras</s>, <s>Barbaras</s>, <s>Yavanas</s>, and <s>Khasas</s>,
the <s>Pulikas</s>, <s>Kulatthas</s>, <s>Aṅgalokyas</s>, and the other excellent peoples there.
Having split <s>Himavat</s> in two, she entered the southern ocean.
Then she flooded the <s>Vīramarūs</s>, the <s>Kālikas</s>, and the <s>Śūlikas</s>,
the <s>Tukaras</s>, the <s>Barbarākāras</s>, the <s>Pahlavas</s>, the <s>Pāradas</s>, and the <s>Śakas</s>.
Having flooded these peoples, <s>Cakṣu</s> went to the ocean.
The <s>Daradas</s>, <s>Orjaguḍas</s>, <s>Gāndhāras</s>, <s>Aurasas</s>, and <s>Kuhūs</s>,
the <s>Śivapauras</s>, <s>Indramarūs</s>, <s>Vasatīs</s>, and <s>Samatejasas</s>,
the <s>Saindhavas</s>, <s>Urvasas</s>, <s>Barbas</s>, <s>Kupathas</s>, and <s>Bhīmaromakas</s>,
the <s>Śunāmukhas</s> and <s>Ordamarūs</s>: <s>Sindhu</s> reaches these lands.
She also serves the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rakṣasas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and serpents,
the villages of <s>Kalāpa</s>, and likewise <s>Kimpuruṣas</s> and human beings,
the <s>Kirātas</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, <s>Kurus</s>, and also the <s>Bhāratas</s>,
the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, <s>Kauśikas</s>, <s>Matsyas</s>, <s>Māgadhas</s>, and <s>Aṅgas</s> as well.
and the <s>Brahmottara</s>s, the <s>Vaṅga</s>s, and likewise the <s>Tāmralipta</s>s.
The auspicious <s>Gaṅgā</s> nourishes these Aryan regions.
Then, checked at <s>Vindhya</s>, she entered the southern ocean.
After that the holy <s>Hlādinī</s> went facing the east,
flooding the <s>Upaka</s>s and also all the <s>Niṣāda</s>s in every way.
She flooded the <s>Dhīvara</s>s and the <s>Ṛṣika</s>s, and likewise the <s>Nalimukha</s>s,
the <s>Kekara</s>s, the <s>Ekakarṇa</s>s, and indeed the <s>Kirāta</s>s as well,
the <s>Kālañjara</s>s, the <s>Vikarṇa</s>s, the <s>Kuśika</s>s, and the <s>Svargabhaumaka</s>s.

children.text: sā maṇḍale samudrasya tīre bhūtvā tu sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: She then came everywhere to the shore in the circle of the ocean.

children.text: tatastu nalinī cāpi prācīmeva diśaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: After that <s>Nalinī</s> too went toward the eastern direction.
She flooded the <s>Kupatha</s>s and even the lakes of <s>Indradyumna</s>,
as well as the lands of the <s>Kharapatha</s>s and the <s>Vetraśaṅkupatha</s>s.
Through the middle she went to the <s>Ujjānaka</s>s, the <s>Maru</s>s, and the <s>Kuthaprāvaraṇa</s>s.
Near <s>Indradvīpa</s> she entered the salt ocean.

children.text: tatastu pāvanī prāyāt prācīmāśāṃ javena tu ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pāvanī</s> went swiftly toward the eastern quarter.
She flooded the <s>Tomara</s>s, the <s>Haṃsamārga</s>s, and the <s>Samūhaka</s>s.

children.text: pūrvāndeśāṃśca sevantī bhittvā sā bahudhā girim
children.translated_text: Serving the eastern lands, she split the mountain in many ways,
and, reaching the <s>Karṇaprāvaraṇa</s>s, she went also to the <s>Aśvamukha</s>s.
Having moistened Mount <s>Meru</s>, she went also to the <s>Vidyādhara</s>s.
She then entered the great lake called <s>Śaimimaṇḍalakoṣṭha</s>.
Other rivers and subsidiary rivers of these are by the hundreds and thousands.

children.text: upagacchanti tā nadyo yato varṣati vāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those rivers go to the places where <s>Vāsava</s> sends rain.
On the bank of the <s>Vaṃśaukasārā</s> is that forest named <s>Surabhi</s>.
There dwells <s>Hiraṇyaśṛṅga</s>, learned, a follower of <s>Kubera</s>, and self-controlled.
He is great, removed from sacrifice, of immeasurable power, and very valorous.
There he is surrounded by <s>Agastya</s>s and learned <s>Brahmarākṣasa</s>s.
These four attendants of <s>Kubera</s> indeed have resorted to that place.
In just this way the success of those who dwell on mountains should be understood.
In relation to one another it is doubled in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>kāma</s> (pleasure), and <s>artha</s> (prosperity).

children.text: hemakūṭasya pṛṣṭhe tu sarpāṇāṃ tatsaraḥ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: On the back of <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, that lake is remembered as belonging to the serpents.
From it arises <s>Sarasvatī</s>, she who is also <s>Jyotiṣmatī</s>,
having plunged on both sides into the eastern and western oceans.
On the excellent mountain <s>Niṣadha</s> is a lake named <s>Viṣṇupada</s>,
from which she first arises; and those waters are favorable to the <s>Gandharva</s>s.
From the side of <s>Meru</s> arises the great lake <s>Candraprabha</s>,

children.text: jambūścaiva nadī puṇyā yasyāṃ jāmbūnadaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and the holy river <s>Jambū</s>, in which <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold is remembered.

children.text: payodastu hrado nīlaḥ sa śubhraḥ puṇḍarīkavān
children.translated_text: The lake <s>Payoda</s> is dark blue, clear, and filled with white lotuses.
From <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> and from <s>Payoda</s> those two rivers are born.
Among lakes, this lake is remembered as <s>Uttaramānasa</s>.

children.text: mṛgyā ca mṛgakāntā ca tasmād dve samprasūyatām ||
children.translated_text: From it two rivers are born, <s>Mṛgyā</s> and <s>Mṛgakāntā</s>.
In the <s>Kuru</s>s there are famous lakes, crowded with lotuses and schools of fish.

children.text: nāmnā te vai jayā nāma dvādaśodadhisaṃnibhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those twelve, resembling oceans, are known by the name <s>Jayā</s>.

children.text: tebhyaḥ śāntī ca madhvī ca dve nadyau samprasūyatām
children.translated_text: From them two rivers are born, <s>Śāntī</s> and <s>Madhvī</s>.

children.text: kimpuruṣādyāni yānyaṣṭau teṣu devo na varṣati ||
children.translated_text: In the eight regions beginning with <s>Kimpuruṣa</s>, the god does not rain.
There waters springing from the ground flow as excellent rivers.

children.text: balāhakaśca ṛṣabho cakro maināka eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Balāhaka</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Cakra</s>, and <s>Maināka</s>
are set in the several directions and sink into the salt ocean.
<s>Candrakānta</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and the very great mass of rock
stretch northward in the northern quarter and plunge into the great ocean.
<s>Cakra</s>, <s>Badhiraka</s>, and also Mount <s>Nārada</s>
extend westward and are established in the great ocean.
<s>Jīmūta</s>, <s>Drāvaṇa</s>, <s>Maināka</s>, and Mount <s>Candra</s>
are those great mountains extending toward the southern ocean.
Between <s>Cakra</s> and <s>Maināka</s>, in the southern path of the sky,

children.text: tatra saṃvartako nāma so'gniḥ pibati tajjalam
children.translated_text: there the fire named <s>Saṃvartaka</s> drinks that water.
That fire dwelling in the ocean is <s>Aurva</s>, the mare-mouthed fire.
Thus these four mountain ranges enter the salt ocean.

children.text: chidyamāneṣu pakṣeṣu purā indrasya vai bhayāt ||
children.translated_text: Long ago, when their wings were being cut off through fear of <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: teṣāṃ tu dṛśyate candre śukle kṛṣṇe samāplutiḥ
children.translated_text: their inundation is seen with the moon in its bright and dark fortnights.

children.text: te bhāratasya varṣasya bhedā yena prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those divisions of <s>Bhārata-varṣa</s> have been proclaimed by this means.
Some are seen as stated here, while others are stated elsewhere.
Each succeeding <s>varṣa</s> among these surpasses the previous one in qualities,
in health, length of life, and measure, and in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>kāma</s> (pleasure), and <s>artha</s> (prosperity).
The beings in those <s>varṣa</s>s are endowed with these in their several portions.

children.text: vasanti nānājātīni teṣu sarveṣu tāni vai
children.translated_text: Those beings, of many kinds, live in all those regions.
Bearing all this, the earth, this world, stands firm.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall now describe here, exactly and with certainty, <s>Śākadvīpa</s>.

children.text: kathyamānaṃ nibodha tvaṃ śākaṃ dvīpaṃ dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Listen, best of twice-born men, as <s>Śākadvīpa</s> is being related.
Its extent is twice the extent of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.
Its circumference all around is three times its breadth.
This ocean, the salt ocean, is surrounded by that island.
There the peoples are meritorious, and a person dies only after a long time.
How indeed could there be famine here among those endowed with forbearance and vigor?
There too are seven bright mountains, adorned with jewels.

children.text: śākadvīpādiṣu tveṣu sapta sapta nagās triṣu
children.translated_text: In these three islands beginning with <s>Śākadvīpa</s> there are seven mountains each.
They are straight, extend in every direction, and are established as <s>varṣa</s>-mountains.
Named <s>Ratnākara</s> and so on, they have summits and are greatly heaped up.
They rise evenly in every direction according to the measure of the island's extent.
And the salt ocean and the milk ocean are entered on both sides.
But in <s>Śākadvīpa</s> I shall describe the seven divine great mountains.
The first, joined with gods, seers, and gandharvas, is called <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: prāgāyataḥ sa sauvarṇa udayo nāma parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Extending eastward, that golden mountain is named <s>Udaya</s>.
There the clouds arise for the sake of rain, and then depart.
To the west of it is the very great mountain <s>Jaladhāra</s>.
It is also known as <s>Candra</s>, endowed with every medicinal herb.
From it <s>Vāsava</s> always takes the supreme water.
There is also said to be a great, difficult mountain called <s>Nārada</s>, piled high.
There, in ancient times, two immovable mountains arose, the <s>Nārada</s> mountains.
To the west of it is the very great mountain named <s>Śyāma</s>.
There, it is said, these peoples formerly acquired their dark color.
That very one is also named <s>Dundubhi</s>, resembling the <s>Śyāma</s> mountain.
In ancient times, when a kettle-drum was beaten there by the gods, death came through sound.
<s>Śālmala</s>, made within of strings of jewels, forms the intervening space.
To the west of it the great silver mountain <s>Asta</s> is remembered.

children.text: sa vai somaka ityukto devairyatrāmṛtaṃ purā
children.translated_text: It is called <s>Somaka</s> by the gods; there in ancient times the nectar was gathered

children.text: saṃbhṛtaṃ ca hṛtaṃ caiva māturarthe garutmatā ||
children.translated_text: and then carried away by <s>Garutmat</s> for the sake of his mother.
To the west of it is <s>Āmbikeya</s>; it too is remembered as <s>Sumanas</s>.
On that mountain <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> was slain by <s>Varāha</s>.
Beyond <s>Āmbikeya</s> is the lovely mountain frequented by all medicinal herbs.
It is called <s>Vibhrāja</s>, a great mountain made of crystal.
Because fire shines forth from it, it is remembered as <s>Vibhrāja</s>.

children.text: saiveha keśavetyukto yato vāyuḥ pravāti ca ||
children.translated_text: It is also called <s>Keśava</s> here, because the wind blows from it.
I shall tell the varṣas (regions) of those mountains, O best of twice-born ones.
Listen to their names properly and in order.
The varṣas have two names, just as the mountains do.
The varṣa of <s>Udaya</s> is called <s>Udaya</s> and is famed as <s>Jaladhārā</s>.

children.text: nāmnā gatabhayaṃ nāma varṣaṃ tatprathamaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: The first varṣa is remembered by name as <s>Gatabhaya</s>.
The second, belonging to <s>Jaladhāra</s>, is remembered as <s>Sukumāra</s>.
That same varṣa is proclaimed under the name <s>Śaiśira</s>.

children.text: nāradasya ca kaumāraṃ tadeva ca sukhodayam ||
children.translated_text: That of <s>Nārada</s> is <s>Kaumāra</s>, and that same one is also <s>Sukhodaya</s>.
The varṣa of <s>Śyāma</s> mountain is remembered as <s>Anīcaka</s>.
The sages call that same auspicious one <s>Ānandaka</s>.
The auspicious varṣa of <s>Somaka</s> should be known as <s>Kusumotkara</s>.
That same varṣa, connected with <s>Somaka</s>, is called <s>Asita</s>.
That of <s>Āmbikeya</s> is made <s>Maināka</s> and also <s>Kṣemaka</s>.
And that of the <s>Kesari</s> mountain is remembered as <s>Mahādruma</s>.
That same varṣa, connected with <s>Vibhrāja</s>, is called <s>Dhava</s>.
The circumference of the dvīpa (island-continent), and likewise its shortness and length,
are reckoned by <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>; in its middle is a forest-tree.
There is a great tree named <s>Śāka</s>, and the people are great followers of it.
In these regions gods and gandharvas, and siddhas together with cāraṇas,

children.text: viharanti ramante ca dṛśyamānāśca taiḥ saha
children.translated_text: wander and take delight, visible together with them.
There are holy countries there, furnished with the four social classes.
In them there are exactly seven rivers in each varṣa, flowing to the ocean.

children.text: dvināmnā caiva tāḥ sarvā gaṅgāḥ saptavidhāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All those seven kinds of <s>Gaṅgās</s> are remembered as having two names.
The first <s>Gaṅgā</s>, auspicious and with blessed water, is <s>Sukumārī</s>.
This river is also proclaimed by the name <s>Munitaptā</s>.
The second, by name, is the true <s>Sukumārī</s>, perfected by austerity.

children.text: nandā ca pāvanī caiva tṛtīyā parikīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: The third is proclaimed as <s>Nandā</s> and also <s>Pāvanī</s>.

children.text: śibikā ca caturthī syāddvividhā ca punaḥ smṛtā
children.translated_text: The fourth is <s>Śibikā</s>, and it is again remembered in two forms.

children.text: ikṣuśca pañcamī jñeyā tathaiva ca punaḥ kuhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fifth should be known as <s>Ikṣu</s>, and likewise again as <s>Kuhū</s>.
The sixth is proclaimed as <s>Veṇukā</s> and also <s>Amṛtā</s>.

children.text: sukṛtā ca gabhastī ca saptamī parikīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: The seventh is proclaimed as <s>Sukṛtā</s> and <s>Gabhastī</s>.
These seven highly blessed rivers, with auspicious waters in each varṣa,
nourish all the people dwelling in <s>Śākadvīpa</s>.

children.text: abhigacchanti tāścānyā nadā nadyaḥ sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: And other rivers, streams, and lakes also flow into them,
with abundant outpourings of water, because <s>Vāsava</s> rains there.

children.text: tāsāṃ tu nāmadheyāni parimāṇaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: But their names, and likewise their measure,
cannot be fully enumerated; those excellent rivers are holy.

children.text: tāḥ pibanti sadā hṛṣṭā nadīrjanapadāstu te
children.translated_text: Those peoples of the countries always drink from those rivers, joyful.

children.text: ete śāntabhayāḥ proktāḥ pramodā ye ca vai śivāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are said to be free from fear, delighted, and indeed blessed.
They are joyful and happy, secure together with their kin.
Those seven countries are famed as endowed with the practices of the social classes and life-stages.
They are healthy and strong, and all are free from death.

children.text: avasarpiṇī na teṣvasti ta tathaivotsarpiṇī punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no descending age among them, nor likewise any ascending age.
There is nowhere among them a condition of ages made by the four yugas.
There time proceeds there as if equal to the Tretā age.
This should be understood in every way for the five beginning with <s>Śākadvīpa</s>.

children.text: deśasya tu vicāreṇa kālaḥ svābhāvikaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In consideration of the country, time is remembered as natural.
Among them there is no mixture at all caused by social classes or life-stages.
Because <s>dharma</s> (right order) does not deviate, the people are wholly happy.

children.text: na teṣu māyā lobho vā īrṣyāsūyā bhayaṃ kutaḥ
children.translated_text: Among them there is no deceit, nor greed, nor envy, nor malice; how could there be fear?

children.text: viparyayo na teṣvasti tadvai svābhāvikaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: There is no reversal among them; that indeed is remembered as natural.

children.text: kālo naiva ca teṣvasti na daṇḍo na ca dāṇḍikaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor is there time in the ordinary sense among them; there is no punishment and no punisher.
Knowing <s>dharma</s>, they protect one another by their own <s>dharma</s>.
The very great circular dvīpa is called <s>Kuśa</s>.
It is surrounded by river waters, and by mountains resembling clouds.
It is varied with every mineral and adorned with gems and coral,
and also with other delightful inhabited lands of diverse forms.
With trees endowed with flowers and fruits, it is everywhere rich in wealth and grain,
always furnished with flowers and fruits and covered with every jewel.
It is covered everywhere with all kinds of domestic and wild animals.
Hear, in brief and in order, about <s>Kuśadvīpa</s>.

children.text: atha tṛtīyaṃ vakṣyāmi kuśadvīpaṃ ca kṛtsnaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Now I shall describe the third, <s>Kuśadvīpa</s>, in its entirety.
The ocean of milk is surrounded on all sides by <s>Kuśadvīpa</s>.
It is endowed with twice the extent of <s>Śākadvīpa</s>.
There too seven mountains are to be known as sources of jewels.
The rivers too are jewel-bearing; hear their names from me.

children.text: dvināmānaśca te sarve śākadvīpe yathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: All of them also have two names, just as in <s>Śākadvīpa</s>.
The first mountain, bright like the sun, is named <s>Kumuda</s>.

children.text: vidrumoccaya ityuktaḥ sa eva ca mahīdharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That same earth-bearing mountain is called <s>Vidrumoccaya</s>.
It has peaks made of every mineral and is furnished with masses of rock.
The second mountain there is celebrated by the name <s>Unnata</s>.

children.text: hemaparvata ityuktaḥ sa eva ca mahīdharaḥ
children.translated_text: That same earth-bearing mountain is called <s>Hemaparvata</s>.
With peaks made of orpiment, it surrounds the island completely.
The third is <s>Balāhaka</s>, a mountain made of native collyrium.

children.text: dyutimānnāmataḥ proktaḥ sa eva ca mahīdharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That same earth-bearing mountain is proclaimed by the name <s>Dyutimān</s>.
The fourth mountain is <s>Droṇa</s>, on whose great mountain the herbs grow,
namely <s>Viśalyakaraṇī</s> and likewise <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s>.
That same very great, heaped-up mountain is called <s>Puṣpavān</s>.
The fifth among them is <s>Kaṅka</s>, a mountain by name and rich in substance.

children.text: kuśeśaya iti proktaḥ punaḥ sa pṛthivīdharaḥ
children.translated_text: That same earth-supporting mountain is again called <s>Kuśeśaya</s>.
It is endowed with divine flowers and fruits and furnished with divine plants.
The sixth mountain there is <s>Mahiṣa</s>, resembling a cloud.

children.text: sa eva tu punaḥ prokto harirityabhiviśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That very one is again called <s>Hari</s> and is widely known.
On it dwells that fire born in the waters, named <s>Mahiṣa</s>.
The seventh mountain there is said to be <s>Kakudmān</s>.
It should be known as <s>Mandara</s>, auspicious and made of every mineral.
The element called <s>manda</s> is understood as indicating water.
And because it splits the waters, it is called <s>Mandara</s>.
There <s>Vāsava</s> himself guards many jewels,
taking <s>Prajāpati</s> with him and himself distributing them to creatures.
The interval between them is said to be twice as great.
Thus these seven mountains have been declared in <s>Kuśadvīpa</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ varṣāṇi vakṣyāmi saptaiva tu vibhāgaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall describe their seven <s>varṣas</s> (regions), according to their divisions.

children.text: kumudasya smṛtaḥ śveta unnataśceva sa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śveta</s> is remembered as belonging to <s>Kumuda</s>, and <s>Unnata</s> too is so remembered.
For <s>Unnata</s>, the <s>varṣa</s> (region) is to be known by the name <s>Lohita</s>.
And <s>Veṇumaṇḍalaka</s> too is likewise celebrated.
For <s>Balāhaka</s> it is <s>Jīmūta</s>, and also <s>Svairathākāra</s>.

children.text: droṇasya harikaṃ nāma lavaṇaṃ ca punaḥ smṛtam
children.translated_text: For <s>Droṇa</s>, the name is <s>Harika</s>, and again <s>Lavaṇa</s> is remembered.
For <s>Kaṅka</s> too, the name is <s>Kakun</s>; it is also remembered as <s>Dhṛtimat</s>.
For <s>Mahiṣa</s> too, it is <s>Mahiṣa</s>, and again <s>Prabhākara</s>.
The <s>varṣa</s> (region) of <s>Kakudmin</s> is famed by the name <s>Kapila</s>.
These too, distinguished, are seven and seven, each separately:
the <s>varṣas</s> (regions) and the mountains; now learn the rivers among them.

children.text: tatrāpi nadyaḥ saptaiva prativarṣaṃ hi tāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: There too the rivers are just seven, remembered in each <s>varṣa</s> (region).
All of them have two names, and all are remembered as having holy waters.

children.text: dhūtapāpā nadī nāma yoniścaiva punaḥ smṛtā
children.translated_text: The river named <s>Dhūtapāpā</s> is again remembered as <s>Yoni</s>.

children.text: sītā dvitīyā vijñeyā sā caiva hi niśā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> is to be known as the second; she too is remembered as <s>Niśā</s>.

children.text: pavitrā tṛtīyā vijñeyā vitṛṣṇāpi ca yā punaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pavitrā</s> is to be known as the third, and also again <s>Vitṛṣṇā</s>.

children.text: caturthī hlādinītyuktā candrabhā iti ca smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: The fourth is called <s>Hlādinī</s>, and is remembered as <s>Candrabhā</s>.

children.text: vidyucca pañcamī proktā śuklā caiva vibhāvyate
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyut</s> is declared the fifth, and <s>Śuklā</s> too is understood.

children.text: puṇḍrā ṣaṣṭhī tu vijñeyā punaścaiva vibhāvarī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puṇḍrā</s> is to be known as the sixth, and again also <s>Vibhāvarī</s>.

children.text: mahatī saptamī proktā punaścaiṣā dhṛtiḥ smṛtā
children.translated_text: <s>Mahatī</s> is declared the seventh; again she is remembered as <s>Dhṛti</s>.
From them other rivers too have arisen, by hundreds and then by thousands.

children.text: abhigacchanti tā nadyo yato varṣati vāsavaḥ
children.translated_text: Those rivers go wherever <s>Vāsava</s> rains.
Thus this arrangement of <s>Kuśadvīpa</s> has been described to you.
Its ancient extent has been stated in relation to <s>Śākadvīpa</s>.
<s>Kuśadvīpa</s> is surrounded by an ocean whose water is clarified butter,
a very great island, encircled on all sides like the moon.
In extent and circumference it is regarded as twice the ocean of milk.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi krauñcadvīpaṃ yathā tathā
children.translated_text: After that I shall describe <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s> as it truly is.
Its extent is twice the extent of <s>Kuśadvīpa</s>.
The ocean of ghee-water is enclosed by <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s>.
It is surrounded everywhere in a circle, like the rim of a wheel.
On that island the excellent mountains are spoken of; the mountain is called <s>Devana</s>.
Beyond <s>Devana</s> there is also a mountain named <s>Govinda</s>.
Beyond <s>Govinda</s> too, <s>Krauñca</s> is the first mountain.
Beyond <s>Krauñca</s> is <s>Pāvanaka</s>; beyond <s>Pāvana</s> is <s>Andhakāraka</s>.
Beyond <s>Andhakāra</s> too is a mountain named <s>Devāvṛt</s>.
Beyond <s>Devāvṛta</s> too is the great mountain <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>.
These are the seven jewel-made mountains of <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s>.
The breadth of each <s>varṣa</s> (region) and mountain is twice that of the preceding one.
I shall describe its <s>varṣas</s> (regions); learn them by name.
The region of <s>Krauñca</s> is <s>Kuśala</s>; that of <s>Vāmana</s> is <s>Manonuga</s>, pleasing to the mind.
Beyond <s>Manonuga</s> are the <s>Uṣṇas</s>; that is also called the third.
Beyond <s>Uṣṇa</s> is <s>Pāvanaka</s>; after <s>Pāvana</s> is <s>Andhakāraka</s>.
Beyond the land of <s>Andhakāraka</s>, moreover, is the land of the sages.
And beyond the land of the sages is said to be <s>Dundubhisvana</s>.
It is thronged with <s>siddhas</s> and <s>cāraṇas</s>; the people are mostly fair and pure.
There, in those very places, the auspicious rivers that go through each <s>varṣa</s> are traditionally heard of.
<s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Kumudvatī</s>, <s>Saṃdhyā</s>, <s>Rātri</s>, and <s>Manojavā</s>,

children.text: khyātī ca puṇḍarīkā ca gaṅgā saptavidhā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>Khyātī</s> and <s>Puṇḍarīkā</s>: <s>Gaṅgā</s> is remembered as sevenfold.
And thousands of other rivers belonging to their neighboring regions
flow into those rivers, abundant and rich in water.
The natural character of all those regions, in proper sequence,
cannot be described in detail, even in hundreds of years.

children.text: sargo yaśca prajānāṃ tu saṃhāro yaśca teṣu vai
children.translated_text: The creation of the beings there, and likewise their dissolution,
I shall describe from this point onward; listen to the account of <s>Śālmala</s>.
<s>Śālmala</s> is an island-continent twice the extent of <s>Krauñca</s>.
It stands encircling an ocean whose water is the creamy part of curds.
There the inhabited lands are holy, and people die only after a long time.

children.text: kuta eva tu durbhikṣaṃ kṣamātejoyutā hi te ||
children.translated_text: How indeed could there be famine there? For they are endowed with forbearance and splendor.
The first mountain, named <s>Sumanā</s>, has the appearance of the sun.
The middle one was yellow; next came the mountain made like a jar.
Named <s>Sarvasukha</s>, it is furnished with divine herbs.
The third mountain is golden, resembling the wing of a bee.

children.text: sumahān rohito nāma divyo girivaro hi saḥ
children.translated_text: It is named <s>Rohita</s>, very great, divine, and the best of mountains.
<s>Sumanā</s> is the <s>Kuśala</s> region, with happiness as its result and happiness as its rise.
The third, which is <s>Rohita</s>, is famed by the name <s>Rohiṇa</s>.
There <s>Vāsava</s> himself guards many jewels.
Taking <s>Prajāpati</s> as his support, he himself, well pleased, arranges it.

children.text: na tatra meghā varṣanti śītoṣṇaṃ ca na tadvidham ||
children.translated_text: There clouds do not rain, nor are cold and heat of that kind.

children.text: varṇāśramāṇāṃ vārttā vā triṣu dvīpeṣu vidyate
children.translated_text: Nor is there concern with the orders of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s> in the three island-continents.

children.text: na graho na ca candro'sti īrṣyāsūyā bhayaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: There is no planet and no moon there, and likewise no envy, resentment, or fear.
Here there are waters springing up from the ground and streams flowing from the mountains.
Food of the six flavors presents itself to them of its own accord.

children.text: adhamottamaṃ na teṣvasti na lobho na parigrahaḥ
