children.translated_text: Among them there is no low or high, no greed, and no taking possession.
The people are healthy and strong, and wholly happy.
They abide in mental perfection for thirty thousand years.

children.text: sukhamāyuśca rūpaṃ ca dharmaiśvaryaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Happiness, lifespan, beauty, <s>dharma</s>, and sovereignty as well
are to be understood everywhere in the three island-continents up to <s>Śālmala</s>.

children.text: vyākhyātaḥ śālmalāntānāṃ dvīpānāṃ tu vidhiḥ śubhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The auspicious rule of the island-continents up to <s>Śālmala</s> has thus been explained.
The island-continent is circular, encircled like a wheel,
and is joined to an ocean of wine twice as large.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall describe <s>Gomedaka</s>, the sixth island-continent, O rich in austerity.
The ocean of wine-water is surrounded by <s>Gomeda</s>.
Its extent is twice the extent of <s>Śālmala</s>.

children.text: tasmindvīpe tu vijñeyau parvatau dvau samāhitau ||
children.translated_text: On that island-continent two mountains should be known, standing firmly.
The first mountain is named <s>Sumanā</s>, made of native antimony.
The second, named <s>Kumuda</s>, is furnished with every herb.
It is glorious, made of refined gold, and should be known as very greatly piled up.
That <s>Gomedaka</s> is surrounded by an ocean of sugarcane juice.
It is encircled by the sixth ocean, twice as large as the wine-ocean.
<s>Dhātakī</s> and <s>Kumuda</s>, the sons of <s>Havya</s>, are very extensive.
The first <s>varṣa</s>, <s>Saumana</s>, is called <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s>.

children.text: dhātakinaḥ smṛtaṃ tadvai prathamaṃ prathamasya tu ||
children.translated_text: That first one of the first mountain is remembered as belonging to <s>Dhātakin</s>.

children.text: gomedaṃ yatsmṛtaṃ varṣaṃ nāmnā sarvasukhaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: The <s>varṣa</s> remembered as <s>Gomeda</s> is by name <s>Sarvasukha</s>.
Then, belonging to <s>Kumuda</s>, the second mountain, the second <s>varṣa</s> is <s>Kumuda</s>.

children.text: etau dvau parvatau vṛttau śeṣau sarvasamucchritau
children.translated_text: These two mountains are round, and both are wholly elevated.

children.text: pūrveṇa tasya dvīpasya sumanāḥ parvataḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the eastern part of that island-continent stands Mount <s>Sumanā</s>.
It stands extending to the ocean with slopes stretching east and west.
In its western half <s>Kumuda</s> stands in just the same way.

children.text: etaiḥ parvatapādaistu sa deśo vai dvidhākṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: By the slopes of these mountains that region is divided into two.
The southern half of the island-continent is called <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s>.
To its north is <s>Kumuda</s>, the excellent second <s>varṣa</s>.

children.text: etau janapadau dvau tu gomedasya tu vistṛtau ||
children.translated_text: These two inhabited lands of <s>Gomedaka</s> are extensive.
After this I shall describe the seventh, excellent island-continent.
And the ocean of sugarcane juice is twice as large as <s>Gomeda</s>.
The island-continent <s>Puṣkara</s>, covered with lotuses, stands enclosing it.
Within <s>Puṣkara</s> is the glorious great mountain <s>Citrasānu</s>.
It has variegated peaks made of jewels, arising from masses of stone.

children.text: dvīpasyaiva tu pūrvārdhe citrasānuḥ sthito mahān ||
children.translated_text: The great <s>Citrasānu</s> stands in the eastern half of the island-continent.
It extends for twenty-seven thousand circular measures.
Upward it rises twenty-four <s>yojanas</s>, mighty as it is.
In the west, the mountain <s>Mānasa</s> encircles half of the island-continent.
It stands near the shore, risen like the moon in the east.
It is fifty and a half thousand <s>yojanas</s> high.
Its son, <s>Mahāvīta</s>, is the protector of the western half.

children.text: pūrvārdhe parvatasyāpi dvidhā deśastu sa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And in the eastern half of the mountain the region is remembered as divided in two.
<s>Puṣkara</s> is surrounded by an ocean of sweet water.
In extent and circumference it is twice as great as <s>Gomeda</s>.
Human beings live in them for thirty thousand years.
There is no reversal among them; this is remembered as their natural condition.
They possess health, abundance of happiness, and mental perfection.

children.text: sukhamāyuśca rūpaṃ ca triṣu dvīpeṣu sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Happiness, lifespan, and beauty exist in every way in the three dvīpas (island-continents).
Among them there are neither inferior nor superior people; they are equal in strength and form.

children.text: na tatra vadhyavadhakau nerṣyāsūyā bhayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: There are no slain or slayers there, nor envy, jealousy, or fear.

children.text: na lobho na ca dambho vā na ca dveṣaḥ parigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no greed, no hypocrisy, no hatred, and no possessiveness.

children.text: satyānṛte na teṣvāstāṃ dharmādharmau tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Among them there are neither truth and falsehood, nor likewise <s>dharma</s> (right order) and <s>adharma</s> (wrongdoing).
Nor is there any mention of the social classes and life-stages, cattle-keeping, trade, or agriculture.

children.text: trayīvidyā daṇḍanītiḥ śuśrūṣā daṇḍa eva ca
children.translated_text: There is no threefold Vedic knowledge, no science of punishment, no service, and no punishment itself.

children.text: na tatra varṣaṃ nadyo vā śītoṣṇaṃ ca na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: There is no rain there, nor rivers; neither cold nor heat exists.
There are waters that spring up from plants, and streams from the mountains.
The time there is always equal to that of the <s>Uttarakurus</s>.
Everywhere that is a season of happiness, free from the affliction of old age.
The creation in <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s> and likewise in <s>Mahāvīta</s> is the same.
Thus the seven dvīpas are encircled by seven oceans.
Whatever ocean comes immediately after a dvīpa is equal to that dvīpa.
Thus the mutual increase of dvīpas and oceans should be understood.
Because of the great overflowing of waters, it is called a samudra (ocean).
There, in the varṣas (regions), the fourfold peoples dwell.
Because of this, they are indeed called varṣas there, as places of great delight.

children.text: udayatīndau pūrve tu samudraḥ pūryate sadā
children.translated_text: When the moon rises in the east, the ocean is always filled.
When it wanes in the dark fortnight and when it sets, the ocean diminishes.
Being filled, the sea is filled from within itself.

children.text: tato vai kṣīyamāṇe tu svātmanyeva hy apāṃ kṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when it diminishes, the decrease of the waters occurs within itself.

children.text: udayātpayasāṃ yogāt puṣpanty āpo yathā svayam
children.translated_text: Just as waters swell of themselves at the rising, through conjunction with watery power,

children.text: tathā sa tu samudro'pi vardhate śaśinodaye ||
children.translated_text: so that ocean too increases at the rising of the moon.
Without becoming deficient or excessive in itself, the waters increase and decrease.
This happens at the rising and setting of the moon, and in the bright and dark fortnights.
The decrease and increase of the ocean correspond likewise to the increase and decrease of the moon.
They say that the measure is five hundred and ten aṅgulas.

children.text: apāṃ vṛddhiḥ kṣayo dṛṣṭaḥ samudrāṇāṃ tu parvasu
children.translated_text: At the lunar junctures, the increase and decrease of the waters of the oceans is observed.
It is remembered as a dvīpa because it has water on both sides, and as an udadhi because it holds water.
Mountains are called giris because they are swallowed up, and parvatas because of their joints or ridges.

children.text: śākadvīpe tu vai śākaḥ parvatastena cocyate ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Śākadvīpa</s> there is <s>Śāka</s>, a mountain; therefore it is so called.
In <s>Kuśadvīpa</s> there is a clump of kuśa grass in the middle of the inhabited land.
In <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s> there is the mountain <s>Krauñca</s>; it is named after that.
In <s>Śālmaladvīpa</s> that great śālmali tree is worshiped.
In <s>Gomedaka</s> there is <s>Gomeda</s>, a mountain; therefore it is so called.
In <s>Puṣkaradvīpa</s> there is a banyan tree; because it is lotus-like, it is so remembered.
That great one is worshiped by gods, a portion of <s>Brahmā</s>, born from the unmanifest.

children.text: tasminsa vasati brahmā sādhyaiḥ sārdhaṃ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: There <s>Brahmā</s>, the Prajāpati, dwells together with the <s>Sādhyas</s>.
There the gods attend upon him, together with thirty-three great seers.
There that god is worshiped by the gods and by the best of the great seers.
And from <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> various kinds of jewels proceed.

children.text: dvīpeṣu teṣu sarveṣu prajānāṃ kramaśastu vai
children.translated_text: Among all those dvīpas, for the peoples in successive order,
through uprightness, celibacy, truth, and self-restraint,
health and the measure of lifespan become doubled and doubled thereafter.

children.text: dvīpeṣu teṣu sarveṣu yathoktaṃ varṣakeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: In all those dvīpas, and in the varṣas as described,
the people there are protected by all those who are innately wise.
Food always presents itself of its own accord, without effort.

children.text: ṣaḍrasaṃ tanmahāvīryaṃ tatra te bhuñjate janāḥ
children.translated_text: There the people eat that food of six tastes and great potency.
Then beyond <s>Puṣkara</s>, surrounding it, there is a great
ocean of sweet water, which encircles it on every side.
Around the sweet-water ocean there is a mountain, circular in shape.
It is bright and unbright, and is called <s>Lokāloka</s>.
On this side of it there is light; beyond it there is no light.
Outside, there is half the earth, equal in extent to the inhabited world.
It is cut off on every side, vast, and covered with water.
Waters ten times greater than the earth enclose the earth on every side.
Fire ten times greater than the waters supports the waters everywhere.
Wind ten times greater than fire is established, supporting the light.
The wind, extending crosswise in a circle, envelops and supports the elements.
Likewise space, ten times greater than wind, supports the elements.
The source of the elements supports space, and is ten times greater than it.
The great principle, ten times greater than the source of the elements, supports the elements.
The <s>mahat-tattva</s> (great principle) is supported by the infinite unmanifest.
These transformations of the transformable things stand in the relation of support and supported.
Earth and the others are those transformations, each bounded in relation to the next.
They are also greater than one another and have entered into one another.
Thus produced from one another, they are also supported by one another.
Because they have entered into one another, therefore they have attained stability.
They were undifferentiated, and they became differentiated through mutual entry.
Earth and the rest, up to wind, are bounded there.

children.text: bhūtebhyaḥ paratas tebhyo hyalokaḥ sarvataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beyond those elements, darkness beyond the world is remembered on every side.
For in the space of light all things are bounded in every way.

children.text: pātre mahati pātrāṇi yathā hyantargatāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Just as vessels are contained within a great vessel,
and, though distinct from one another, exist through mutual dependence,
so too, in the luminous expanse of space, distinctions have entered and are contained within it.
These <s>tattvas</s> (principles) have thus been made, each exceeding another.
As far as these <s>tattvas</s> extend, so far is origination spoken of.
Here the formation of living beings occurs among the elements that are contained within one another.
If the elements are rejected here, there is no origination of an effect.
Therefore the distinctions are remembered as limited and as having the nature of effects.
And the distinctions beginning with <s>mahat</s> would also have the nature of causes.
Thus this arrangement, occupied by the earth part by part,
of the seven island-continents and oceans has been stated by me according to the truth.
By extent, by circumference, and by enumeration,
it is the manifold form of <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), possessing only a partial measure.
This much of the arrangement has been properly made clear by me.
Only this much is to be heard concerning the arrangement, O king.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
After this I shall describe the course of the sun and moon.
For as long as these two, the sun and the moon, shine,
so far the extent of the island-continents among the seven island-continents and oceans is illuminated.
Outside that, half the extent of the earth lies beyond.
The moon and sun illuminate the measure of their circuit.
From the measure of that circuit, heaven is remembered by the wise as equal to it.
The sun goes without delay in common toward the three worlds.
Because he quickly illumines and because he protects, he is remembered as <s>Ravi</s>.
Again and again I shall state the measure of the moon and the sun.
Because of greatness, the word 'great' is used in this sense.
The disk of <s>Bhāskara</s> is equal in breadth to the diameter of this <s>Bhāratavarṣa</s>.
Now learn its measure in <s>yojanas</s>.
The breadth of the disk is nine thousand <s>yojanas</s>.
Here, in the disk, the circumference is three times the breadth.
The moon is twice <s>Bhāskara</s> in diameter and in disk.

children.text: ataḥ pṛthivyā vakṣyāmi pramāṇaṃ yojanaiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall again state the measure of the earth in <s>yojanas</s>.
The extent of the disk of the earth with its seven island-continents and oceans
has thus been enumerated here in the <s>Purāṇa</s> according to measure.
I shall now state it, having calculated it, together with the presiding powers.
For the presiding powers who have passed away are equal here to the present ones.
The gods of the past have passed away from the gods only in forms and names.
Therefore I shall describe the surface of the earth through the present gods.
The arrangement of the divine realm is, in its entirety, through the present ones.
The whole earth is remembered as fifty crores in extent.
And half of its measure, taking <s>Meru</s> as the middle, is successively toward every direction.

children.text: merormadhye pratidiśaṃ koṭirekā tu sā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: From the middle of <s>Meru</s>, in each direction, that is remembered as one crore.
Likewise there are again eighty-nine hundred-thousands,
and fifty thousand: this is the extent of half the earth.
Having set out the extent of the earth, learn it in <s>yojanas</s>.
Three crores are counted as the extent in the four directions.
Likewise seventy-nine hundred-thousands are stated.
That is the extent of the earth with its seven island-continents and oceans.
The inner circle of the earth is three times the extent.
The reckoning in <s>yojanas</s> is remembered as eleven crores,
and those include thirty-seven hundred-thousands.
Thus the inner circle of the earth has been enumerated.
Whatever circle in heaven belongs to the arrangement of the stars,
that same circle belongs to the earth with its complete arrangement.
And the measure of heaven's circuit is remembered as equal to that of the earth.
On the summit of <s>Mānasottara</s>, in the eastern direction from <s>Meru</s>,
is the holy <s>Māhendrī</s> city, of one solid substance and adorned with gold.
South of <s>Meru</s>, again, on the slope of <s>Mānasottara</s>,
<s>Vaivasvata</s> <s>Yama</s> dwells in the city <s>Saṃyamana</s>.
In the western direction from <s>Meru</s>, on the summit of <s>Mānasottara</s>,

children.text: suṣā nāma purī ramyā varuṇasyāpi dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: is the delightful city named <s>Suṣā</s>, belonging to wise <s>Varuṇa</s>.
In the northern direction from <s>Meru</s>, on the summit of <s>Mānasottara</s>,
is <s>Vibhāvarī</s>, the city of <s>Soma</s>, equal even to <s>Mahendra</s>'s city.
On the slopes of <s>Mānasottara</s>, the guardians of the worlds stand in the four directions,
for the establishment of <s>dharma</s> (order) and for the protection of the worlds.
Above the guardians of the worlds, everywhere in the southern course,
learn there the motion of the sun when it has reached its limit.
At the commencement of the southern course, the sun glides like a released arrow.
Taking along the circle of the luminaries, he continually goes around.
When <s>Bhāskara</s> is in the middle of <s>Amarāvatī</s>,
the rising sun is seen in <s>Vaivasvata</s>'s <s>Saṃyamana</s>.
It is midnight in <s>Suṣā</s>, and he sets in <s>Vibhāvarī</s>.
When <s>Ravi</s> is at midday in <s>Vaivasvata</s>'s <s>Saṃyamana</s>,
then he is seen rising in <s>Suṣā</s>, the city of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
It is midnight in <s>Vibhāvarī</s>, and he sets in <s>Māhendrī</s>.
When <s>Ravi</s> is at midday in <s>Suṣā</s>, the city of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
<s>Vibhāvasu</s> rises in <s>Vibhāvarī</s>, the city of <s>Soma</s>.
The maker of day rises in <s>Mahendra</s>'s <s>Amarāvatī</s>.
It is midnight in <s>Saṃyamana</s>, and he sets in the city of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
It very quickly goes around like the circle of a whirling firebrand.
The sun moves, revolving, among the asterisms that are themselves revolving.
Thus on the four sides it creeps along the southern extremities.
At rising and at setting it rises again and again.

children.text: pūrvāhṇe cāparāhṇe ca dvau dvau devālayau tu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the forenoon and in the afternoon it has two divine stations each.

children.text: patatyekaṃ tu madhyāhne bhābhireva ca raśmibhiḥ
children.translated_text: At midday it falls upon one of them with its lights and rays.
When risen, the sun burns at midday with rays that are increasing.
After that it goes to setting with rays that are diminishing.

children.text: udayāstamayābhyāṃ ca smṛte pūrvāpare tu vai ||
children.translated_text: From rising and setting the eastern and western directions are remembered.
As it shines in front, so also behind and on the two sides.

children.text: yatrodayastu dṛśyeta teṣāṃ sa udayaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where its rising is seen, that is remembered as rising for those people.

children.text: praṇāśaṃ gacchate yatra teṣāmastaḥ sa ucyate
children.translated_text: Where it goes to disappearance, that is called setting for them.
For all beings <s>Meru</s> is to the north, and it is to the south of <s>Lokāloka</s>.
Because the sun, having gone, is far away from the earth,

children.text: śrayante raśmayo yasmāttena rātrau na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: and because the rays resort there, it is not seen at night.
The hundred-thousand-rayed one stands above and is seen there.

children.text: evaṃ puṣkaramadhye tu yadā bhavati bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when the light-maker is in the middle of <s>Puṣkara</s>,

children.text: triṃśadbhāgaṃ ca medinyā muhūrtena sa gacchati
children.translated_text: it traverses a thirtieth part of the earth in a <s>muhūrta</s>.
Hear this enumeration in thousands of <s>yojanas</s>.
It is remembered as thirty-one full hundred-thousands,
and fifty thousand, with still more besides.
This is prescribed as the sun's motion in one <s>muhūrta</s>.

children.text: etena kramayogeṇa yadā kāṣṭhāṃ tu dakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: By this orderly sequence, when that sun goes to the southern limit,
it reaches that limit in a month from the northern day.
Then, in the southern course, it circles through the middle of <s>Puṣkara</s>.
The interval between <s>Mānasottara</s> and <s>Meru</s> is remembered as threefold.
Now understand it on every side at the southern limit.
The circumference is reckoned as nine crores in <s>yojanas</s>,
and likewise forty-five hundred-thousands.
This is prescribed as the bird-like sun's course in a day and night.
When that sun, having turned back from the southern direction, stands at the equinox,
it moves in the direction north even of the ocean of milk.
Hear also that equinoctial circle in <s>yojanas</s>.
The circle of the equinox is three complete crores,
and also twenty-one hundred-thousands.
When in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> the bright-rayed one is at the northern limit,

children.text: gomedasya paradvīpe uttarāṃ ca diśaṃ caran ||
children.translated_text: moving in the northern direction on the further island-continent of <s>Gomeda</s>,

children.text: uttarāyāḥ pramāṇaṃ tu kāṣṭhāyā maṇḍalasya tu
children.translated_text: then the measure of the circle of the northern limit
should be known in order as southern, northern, and middle.
The station <s>Jaradgava</s> is in the middle, and <s>Airāvata</s> is the highest.
<s>Vaiśvānara</s> is indicated here truly as lying to the south.
The northern path is the <s>Nāgavīthī</s>, while the southern path is the <s>Ajavīthī</s>.
The two <s>Āṣāḍhās</s> and <s>Mūla</s> are the three beginning with <s>Ajavīthī</s>.
Beginning with <s>Abhijit</s> and ending with <s>Svāti</s> are the three northern <s>Nāgavīthīs</s>.

children.text: aśvinī kṛttikā yāmyā nāgavīthyas trayaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Kṛttikā</s>, and the southern one are remembered as three <s>Nāgavīthīs</s>.
<s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, and <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> are remembered as the <s>Nāgavīthī</s>.
The path of <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, and <s>Punarvasu</s> is remembered as <s>Airāvatī</s>.

children.text: tisrastu vīthayo hyetā uttaro mārga ucyate
children.translated_text: These three paths are called the northern road.

children.text: pūrvottarā ca phalgunyau maghā caivārṣabhī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The two <s>Phalgunīs</s>, former and latter, together with <s>Maghā</s>, are <s>Ārṣabhī</s>.
The two <s>Proṣṭhapadas</s>, former and latter, and <s>Revatī</s> are remembered as <s>Govīthī</s>.

children.text: śravaṇaṃ ca dhaniṣṭhā ca vāruṇaṃ ca jaradgavam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Vāruṇa</s> are <s>Jaradgava</s>.

children.text: etāstu vīthayas tisro madhyamo mārga ucyate
children.translated_text: These three paths are called the middle road.
<s>Hasta</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, and <s>Svāti</s> are remembered as <s>Ajavīthī</s>.

children.text: jyeṣṭhā viśākhā maitraṃ ca mṛgavīthī tathocyate
children.translated_text: <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and <s>Maitra</s> are also called the <s>Mṛgavīthī</s>.
<s>Mūla</s> and the former and latter <s>Āṣāḍhās</s> constitute the <s>Vaiśvānarī</s> path.

children.text: smṛtāstisrastu vīthyastā mārge vai dakṣiṇe punaḥ
children.translated_text: Those three paths are remembered again on the southern road.
The interval between the two limits will now be stated in <s>yojanas</s>.
This is remembered as thirty-one hundred-thousands,
and three hundred more, and likewise thirty-three.
This interval between the two limits is proclaimed in <s>yojanas</s>.
As for the two limits and the two lines in the southern and northern courses,
I shall state them by enumeration; understand them in <s>yojanas</s>.
Each interval is likewise joined with these seven.
It exceeds a thousand, and after that there are another twenty-five.
Moving along the outer and inner lines and limits,
in the northern course it goes around the inner circles.
But outside, to the south, is always the solar circle.
Moving northward, that sun traverses one hundred and eighty circles.

children.text: abhyantaraṃ sa paryeti kramate maṇḍalāni tu ||
children.translated_text: It goes around inside, stepping through the circles.
Understand also the measure of the circle in <s>yojanas</s>.

children.text: yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi daśa cāṣṭau tathā smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: It is remembered as eighteen thousand <s>yojanas</s>,
with fifty-eight <s>yojanas</s> in addition.
This is prescribed as the breadth of the circle across.

children.text: ahastu carate nābheḥ sūryo vai maṇḍalaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: By day the sun moves from the nave, traversing the circle in order.
As at the rim of a potter's wheel, so move the moon and the sun.
On the southern side the sun turns back swiftly, like a wheel.
Therefore it crosses a very extended stretch of earth in a short time.
In the southern course, the sun swiftly, in twelve <s>muhūrtas</s>,
moves in its circle through the midst of thirteen and a half <s>ṛkṣas</s>.
Moving through those <s>ṛkṣas</s> at night in eighteen <s>muhūrtas</s>,
it advances slowly, as though placed at the center of a potter's wheel.
So too, in the northern course, the sun creeps on with slow progress;
therefore over a long time it passes over only a small portion of the earth.
In the northern course, the sun, during the day, in eighteen <s>muhūrtas</s>,

children.text: trayodaśānāṃ madhye tu ṛkṣāṇāṃ carate raviḥ
children.translated_text: moves, as <s>Ravi</s>, through the midst of thirteen <s>ṛkṣas</s>;
at night it moves through those <s>ṛkṣas</s> in twelve <s>muhūrtas</s>.

children.text: tato mandataraṃ tābhyāṃ cakraṃ tu bhramate punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, between those two, the wheel turns again still more slowly;
and <s>Dhruva</s> too turns there, as a lump of clay placed in the middle.
Circling the earth through thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, day and night,
the constellational circles revolve between the two extremities.
When the sun moves northward, its motion by day is remembered as slow;

children.text: tasyaiva tu punarnaktaṃ śīghrā sūryasya vai gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but at night the very same sun's motion is swift.
And when it proceeds southward, its motion by day is prescribed as swift;

children.text: gatiḥ sūryasya vai naktaṃ mandā cāpi vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: while the sun's motion at night is prescribed as slow.
Thus, by this distinction in motion, dividing nights and days,
on the southern <s>Aja-vīthī</s>, north of <s>Lokāloka</s>,
outside the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> path, from the continuity of the world,
as far as the solar radiance at dawn proceeds from <s>Puṣkara</s>,
so far outward from its sides stands <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain.
That mountain rises upward ten thousand <s>yojanas</s>.
The circular mountain is both illumination and non-illumination.
The constellations, the moon, the sun, the planets, and the hosts of stars
shine within <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain.
Only this much is the world; beyond it is without light.
<s>Loka</s> is from the root meaning 'to see'; absence of illumination is <s>alokatā</s>.
Because the sun, as it revolves, joins together <s>loka</s> and <s>aloka</s>,
therefore they call that interval <s>sandhyā</s>, between <s>uṣā</s> and <s>vyuṣṭi</s>.

children.text: uṣā rātriḥ smṛtā viprairvyuṣṭiścāpi ahaḥ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The learned remember <s>uṣā</s> as night, and <s>vyuṣṭi</s> as day.

children.text: triṃśatkalo muhūrtastu ahaste daśa pañca ca
children.translated_text: A <s>muhūrta</s> consists of thirty <s>kalās</s>; in the day there are fifteen.
The decrease and increase of days occur according to the portions of daylight,
except for those decreases and increases that belong to the measure of the twilight <s>muhūrta</s>.
Beginning with the line of light, when the sun has gone three <s>muhūrtas</s>,

children.text: prātaḥ smṛtastataḥ kālo bhāgāṃścāhuśca pañca ca
children.translated_text: that time is remembered as morning, and they also call it five parts.
From that time called morning, the three <s>muhūrtas</s> are <s>saṃgava</s>.
The midday period is three <s>muhūrtas</s>; immediately after that time,
from that midday period, the time is remembered as afternoon.

children.text: traya eva muhūrtāstu kāla eṣa smṛto budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: There are just three <s>muhūrtas</s>; this period is so remembered by the wise.
After the afternoon has passed, that time is called evening.

children.text: daśa pañca muhūrtāhno muhūrtās traya eva ca
children.translated_text: The day has fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, and the periods are of three <s>muhūrtas</s> each.
At the equinox, the day is remembered as consisting of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>.
From that point it increases and decreases in the southern and northern courses.

children.text: ahastu grasate rātriṃ rātristu grasate ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The day swallows the night, and the night swallows the day.
The middle point of autumn and spring is prescribed as the equinox.
The world is remembered as ending with illumination; what is beyond the world is called non-light.
The guardians of the world stand there, in the middle of <s>Lokāloka</s>.
Those four great-souled ones remain until the dissolution of beings.
<s>Sudhāman Vairāja</s> and <s>Kardama Prajāpati</s>,
<s>Hiraṇyaroman Parjanya</s>, and <s>Ketumān Rājasa</s> as well;
free from pairs of opposites, free from pride, sleepless, and without possessions,
these guardians of the world stand at <s>Lokāloka</s> in the four directions.
The peak north of <s>Agastya</s>, frequented by divine seers,
is remembered as the path of the ancestors, outside the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> path.
There dwell the seers who desire offspring and maintain the <s>agnihotra</s>.
Standing on the path of the ancestors, they sustain the continuity of the world.
O lord of men, they undertake action that begins living beings, and blessings too;
desiring the world, they begin them. That path of theirs is the southern one.

children.text: calitaṃ te punardharmaṃ sthāpayanti yuge yuge
children.translated_text: Age after age they restore <s>dharma</s> when it has slipped away,
by intense austerity, by ordinances, and by sacred learning.

children.text: jāyamānāstu pūrve vai paścimānāṃ gṛheṣu te
children.translated_text: The earlier ones are born in the houses of the later ones,
and the later ones are born here at the deaths of the earlier ones.
Thus revolving, they continue until the dissolution of beings:
eighty-eight thousand householder seers.
Having taken refuge in the southern path of <s>Savitṛ</s>, they remain until the dissolution of beings.
This is the enumeration of those engaged in rites, those who resorted to the cremation grounds.
For the sake of worldly activity, and through action that begins living beings,
because of attachment to desire and aversion, and because of resorting to sexual union,
and likewise because of acts done from desire here and the enjoyment of sense-objects,
for these reasons the accomplished ones resorted to the cremation grounds in this world.
The seven seers of <s>Prajauṣaṇi</s> were born here in the <s>Dvāpara</s> ages.
They abhor progeny; therefore death was conquered by them.
For those celibate ones too there are eighty-eight thousand,
having taken the northern path, without end, until the dissolution of beings.
Through avoiding intercourse with the world and sexual coupling,
through the cessation of envy and hatred, and through refraining from beginning living beings,
and then through seeing the defect in contact with other desires, sounds, and the like...
By these pure causes they indeed attained immortality.
Their immortality is understood to last until the dissolution of beings.
For it lasts for the period of the three worlds' stability; they do not go again on the path of death.
It is beyond things resembling sins and merits such as embryo-killing and the horse-sacrifice.
But at the end of the dissolution of beings, even the <s>ūrdhvaretas</s> are exhausted.
Above the higher seers is the place where <s>Dhruva</s> is established.
That is the divine, radiant third step of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in heaven.

children.text: yatra gatvā na śocanti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
children.translated_text: Having gone there, they do not grieve; that is the supreme station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: dharme dhruvasya tiṣṭhanti ye tu lokasya kāṅkṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who desire that world abide in the <s>dharma</s> of <s>Dhruva</s>.
Having heard this divine account, they spoke to <s>Laumaharṣaṇi</s>.
They asked about the course of the sun and moon, and of all the planets in every respect.
The seers said:
How do these luminaries revolve in the circle of the sun?
How do they all move without disarray and without mutual confusion?

children.text: kaśca bhrāmayate tāni bhramanti yadi vā svayam
children.translated_text: Who causes them to revolve, or do they revolve by themselves?
We wish to know this; therefore tell us, best of men.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Listen to this, which bewilders beings, as I explain it.
Although it is a visible thing directly perceived, it surely confounds creatures.
That <s>Śiśumāra</s> which is established among the fourteen constellations
is that son of <s>Uttānapāda</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, who has become the pivot-post in heaven.
As he revolves, he causes the moon and sun to revolve along with the planets.
As he revolves, the lunar mansions follow him like a wheel.

children.text: dhruvasya manasā yo vai bhramate jyotiṣāṃ gaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The whole host of lights revolves by the will of <s>Dhruva</s>.
Bound to <s>Dhruva</s> by bonds made of masses of wind, it moves onward.

children.text: teṣāṃ bhedaśca yogaśca tathā kālasya niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: Their separation and conjunction, and likewise the determination of time,
their risings and settings, portents, and the southern and northern courses,
the equinox and the colors of the planets: all this is impelled by <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: jīmūtā nāma te meghā yadebhyo jīvasambhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those clouds are named <s>Jīmūta</s>, because life arises from them.
The second wind is <s>Āvaha</s>; those clouds depend upon it.
From here, at about a <s>yojana</s>'s measure, though altered by half again,
their discharge of rain and the streaming downpour are likewise proclaimed.
The clouds called <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> are those born from wings.
For the wings of the mountains were cut off by mighty <s>Śakra</s>,
when they were powerful, moving at will, and intent on the destruction of beings.
Those wings, called <s>Puṣkara</s>, were great and water-bearing.
For that reason they are called <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> here.
They assume many forms, and their sounds are very terrible.
They bring the rain at the end of a <s>kalpa</s> and restrain the fire at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>.
Supported by wind, carrying ambrosial water, they move as sustainers of the <s>kalpa</s>.
Those natural things which came into being when this egg was split at that time,
when the four-faced, self-born lord arose,
those very shells of the egg are all proclaimed to be clouds.
Smoke is the nourishment of all of them, especially.
Their chief is <s>Parjanya</s>, and there are also the four elephants of the quarters.

children.text: gajānāṃ parvatānāṃ ca meghānāṃ bhogibhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Of elephants, mountains, clouds, and serpents together,

children.text: kulamekaṃ dvidhā bhūtaṃ yonirekā jalaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the family, though divided in two, is one; water is remembered as their single womb.
<s>Parjanya</s> and the elephants of the quarters, in winter, produce what is born of cold.
They pour frost-rain, strengthened for the increase of food.
The sixth wind, named <s>Parivaha</s>, is their support.
It is the venerable one that bears the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, moving through the sky,
divine, holy, with immortal waters, renowned as the three-pathed river.

children.text: tasyā vispanditaṃ toyaṃ diggajāḥ pṛthubhiḥ karaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the water stirred by her, the elephants of the quarters, with their broad trunks,

children.text: śīkarān sampramuñcanti nīhāra iti sa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: release sprays of drops; that is known as mist.
The mountain to the south which is remembered as <s>Hemakūṭa</s>,
north of <s>Himavat</s> mountain and again to the south,
is called <s>Puṇḍra</s>, for the proper increase of rain.
There the rain begins, and it is born from frost.
Then the wind from <s>Himavat</s> brings the snow produced there,
by its own force, sprinkling the great mountain.
After crossing <s>Himavat</s>, the remaining rain thereafter
then, afterward, in the region called <s>Ibhāsya</s>, is for the increase of beings.
A pair of rainfalls has been declared for the proper increase of rain.
The clouds and their nourishment too: all this has been proclaimed.

children.text: sūrya eva tu vṛṣṭīnāṃ sraṣṭā samupadiśyate ||
children.translated_text: But the sun itself is taught to be the creator of rains.

children.text: varṣaṃ gharmaṃ himaṃ rātriṃ saṃdhye caiva dinaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Rain, heat, snow, night, the two twilights, and day as well,
and auspicious and inauspicious results here all proceed from <s>Dhruva</s>.
The sun takes hold of the waters that are presided over by <s>Dhruva</s>.
And whatever waters are lodged in the bodies of all beings,
when those very moving and unmoving beings are heated,
those waters, becoming smoke, go forth here in every way.
By that the clouds are born; their place is remembered as cloud-formed.
By its heat, with its rays, the sun takes water from all the worlds.
From the ocean, in conjunction with wind, the rays carry the waters.
Then, in due season and under the control of the seasons, the day-maker turns.
With white rays it releases the clear waters from the clouds.
The waters situated in the clouds fall, impelled by the wind.
Then it rains for six months for the growth of all beings.
Thunder is produced by the winds, and lightning is remembered as born of fire.

children.text: mehanācca miher dhātor meghatvaṃ vyañjayanti ca
children.translated_text: And from raining, from the verbal root <s>mih</s>, they indicate the state of being a cloud.

children.text: na bhraśyante tato hyāpastasmādabhrasya vai sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: For the waters do not fall away from it; therefore the condition of the cloud is established.
This <s>Ravi</s>, governed by <s>Dhruva</s>, is the creator of the sending forth of rain.
The wind, governed by <s>Dhruva</s>, again draws the rain back.
And by the withdrawal of the grasping, it moves from the sun through the circle of the constellations.
At the end of its course it enters <s>Arka</s>, who is firmly governed by <s>Dhruva</s>.
Therefore they describe also the arrangement of the chariot of the sun.
It stands with a single wheel, with five spokes, and with three naves.
It is golden, subtle, with eight wheels and a single rim.
With that shining, advancing chariot-wheel, <s>Sūrya</s> moves forth.
Its breadth and length are said to be one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>.
The pole-shaft, in measure, is twice the size of the chariot-platform.

children.text: sa tasya brahmaṇā sṛṣṭo ratho hyarthavaśena tu
children.translated_text: That chariot of his was created by <s>Brahmā</s> for the sake of its purpose.
It is unattached, golden, divine, and yoked with horses that move by wind.
Those horses are the Vedic meters in horse-form, stationed according to the wheel.
And here it is similar in its characteristics to the chariot of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
By means of it <s>Bhāsvān</s> moves each day through the sky in heaven.

children.text: athāṅgāni tu sūryasya pratyaṅgāni rathasya ca
children.translated_text: Now the limbs of <s>Sūrya</s> and the subordinate parts of the chariot
are arranged in sequence from the constituent parts of the year.
Day is remembered as the nave of the one-wheeled <s>Sūrya</s>.
Its spokes are the years, and its rims are remembered as the six seasons.
Night is its covering, and <s>dharma</s> stands upright as its banner.
The yugas are at the ends of its axle, and the season-bearing portions are remembered as its parts.

children.text: tasya kāṣṭhā smṛtā ghoṇā dantapaṅktiḥ kṣaṇāstu vai
children.translated_text: Its <s>kāṣṭhās</s> are remembered as its snout, while the <s>kṣaṇas</s> are its row of teeth.
The <s>nimeṣa</s> is its rear-draft, and its <s>kalā</s> is remembered as its pole.
The two yoke-and-axle ends of it are remembered as <s>artha</s> and <s>kāma</s> together.
The meters, having the form of seven horses, draw it with the speed of wind.
They are <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, <s>Jagatī</s>, and also <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>,

children.text: paṅktiśca bṛhatī caiva uṣṇigeva tu saptamam ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>Paṅkti</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Uṣṇih</s> as the seventh.

children.text: cakramakṣe nibaddhaṃ tu dhruve cākṣaḥ samarpitaḥ
children.translated_text: The wheel is fastened to the axle, and the axle is fixed in <s>Dhruva</s>.
The axle turns together with the wheel, and <s>Dhruva</s> turns together with the axle.
That axle, along with the wheel, turns, impelled by <s>Dhruva</s>.
Thus, according to its purpose, is the arrangement of that chariot.

children.text: tathā saṃyogabhāgena siddho vai bhāskaro rathaḥ
children.translated_text: And by that mode of conjunction the chariot of <s>Bhāskara</s> is indeed established.
By it that god <s>Taraṇi</s> glides through the heaven of the sky.

children.text: yugākṣakoṭī te tasya dakṣiṇe syandanasya tu
children.translated_text: Those two yoke-and-axle ends of his are on the right side of the chariot.

children.text: bhramato bhramato raśmī tau cakrayugayostu vai ||
children.translated_text: As it turns and turns, those two reins of the wheel and yoke also turn.
The circles of this sky-going chariot turn round.
Like the turning of a potter's wheel, its circle moves in every direction.

children.text: yugākṣakoṭī te tasya vātormī syandanasya tu
children.translated_text: Those two yoke-and-axle ends of his chariot are wind-waves.
They move across the fixed great circle in every direction.
As it turns in the circle of the northern course, those two reins of his
increase here in the southern circles as the chariot turns through the circles.
The two reins of the chariot are fastened to the yoke-and-axle ends.

children.text: dhruveṇa pragṛhītau tau rathau yau vanato ravim ||
children.translated_text: Held by <s>Dhruva</s>, those two draw the chariots that bend toward <s>Ravi</s>.

children.text: ākṛṣyete yadā te tu dhruveṇa samadhiṣṭhite
children.translated_text: When those two, governed by <s>Dhruva</s>, are drawn inward,

children.text: tadā so'bhyantare sūryo bhramate maṇḍalāni tu ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Sūrya</s> turns within the circles.
Moving through one hundred and eighty circles at both limits,
and again being released by <s>Dhruva</s> with the pair of reins,

children.text: tathaiva bāhyataḥ sūryo bhramate maṇḍalāni tu
children.translated_text: <s>Sūrya</s> likewise turns through the circles on the outside.
Unwinding the circles with speed, he goes through the circles.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
That chariot, presided over by deities month by month in due order,
then carries <s>Āditya</s> together with many sages,
with gandharvas, apsarases, serpents, grāmaṇīs, and rākṣasas.

children.text: ete vasanti vai sūrye māsau dvau dvau krameṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: These dwell in <s>Sūrya</s> two months at a time, in sequence.
<s>Dhātā</s> and <s>Aryamā</s>, and the two prajāpatis <s>Pulastya</s> and <s>Pulaha</s>,
and the two serpents, <s>Vāsuki</s> and <s>Saṃkīrṇa</s>, those two together,
and <s>Tumburu</s> and <s>Nārada</s>, the two gandharvas, best of singers,
and the apsaras <s>Kṛtasthalā</s>, and she who is <s>Puñjikasthalā</s>,
and the two grāmaṇīs, <s>Rathakṛt</s> and <s>Rathaujā</s>,
and the rākṣasas <s>Heti</s> and <s>Praheti</s>, both yātudhānas in that season,
this group dwells in <s>Bhāskara</s> during the months <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>.

children.text: vasangrīṣme tu dvau māsau mitraśca varuṇaśca vai ||
children.translated_text: But dwelling during the two summer months are <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.
The sages are <s>Atri</s> and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; the two nāgas are <s>Takṣaka</s> and <s>Rambhaka</s>.

children.text: menakā sahajanyā ca hāhā hūhūśca gāyakau ||
children.translated_text: There are <s>Menakā</s> and <s>Sahajanyā</s>, and <s>Hāhā</s> and <s>Hūhū</s> are the singers.
<s>Rathantara</s> and <s>Rathakṛt</s> are remembered as the two grāmaṇīs.

children.text: puruṣādo vadhaścaiva yātudhānau tu tau smṛtau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣāda</s> and <s>Vadha</s> are remembered as those two yātudhānas.

children.text: ete vasanti vai sūrye māsayoḥ śuciśukrayoḥ
children.translated_text: These dwell in <s>Sūrya</s> during the months <s>Śuci</s> and <s>Śukra</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sūrye punaścānyā nivasanti sma devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then again other deities used to dwell in <s>Sūrya</s>.
They are <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vivasvān</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s> and <s>Bhṛgu</s> as well.
There is the serpent <s>Elāpattra</s>, and the pannaga <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>.
There are <s>Viśvāvasu</s> and <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and also <s>Prāta</s> and <s>Ratha</s>.
The apsarases are <s>Pramlocā</s> and <s>Nimrocantī</s>, those two.
And the yātudhānas are <s>Heti</s> and <s>Vyāghra</s>, those two.
With these they dwell in <s>Divākara</s> during the months <s>Nabhasya</s> and <s>Nabhas</s>.

children.text: māsau dvau devatāḥ sūrye vasanti ca śaradṛtau
children.translated_text: For two months the deities dwell in the sun in the autumn season,
<s>Parjanya</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>, and <s>Bharadvāja</s> together with <s>Gautama</s>.
And <s>Citrasena</s> the Gandharva, and also he who is <s>Suruci</s>,

children.text: viśvācī ca ghṛtācī ca ubhe te puṇyalakṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Viśvācī</s> and <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, those two of auspicious marks.
And the Nāga <s>Airāvata</s>, and the renowned <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
and <s>Senajit</s> and <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, commanders and leaders likewise.
<s>Cāra</s> and <s>Vāta</s>, these two, are both remembered as Yātudhānas.

children.text: vasantyete ca vai sūrye māsayośca tviṣorjayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: These indeed dwell in the sun in the two months <s>Tviṣa</s> and <s>Ūrja</s>.

children.text: haimantikau ca dvau māsau nivasanti divākare
children.translated_text: And during the two winter months they dwell in the day-maker.

children.text: aṃśo bhagaśca dvāvetau kaśyapaśca kratuśca tau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṃśa</s> and <s>Bhaga</s>, those two, and <s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Kratu</s>, those two,
and the serpent <s>Mahāpadma</s>, and likewise the serpent <s>Karkoṭaka</s>,
and <s>Citrasena</s> the Gandharva and <s>Pūrṇāyu</s>, those two singers,

children.text: apsarāḥ pūrvacittiśca gandharvā hyurvaśī ca yā
children.translated_text: and the Apsarases <s>Pūrvacitti</s> and <s>Urvaśī</s>,
and <s>Tārkṣya</s> and <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, those two commanders and leaders.

children.text: vidyutsūryaśca tāvugrau yātudhānau tu tau smṛtau
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyut</s> and <s>Sūrya</s> are remembered as those two fierce Yātudhānas.

children.text: sahe caiva sahasye ca vasantyete divākare ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Saha</s> and <s>Sahasya</s> these dwell in the sun.
Then, too, in the cold season they dwell in those two months:
<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s>, and likewise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
and the two Kādraveya Nāgas, <s>Kambala</s> and <s>Aśvatara</s>,
and the two Gandharvas <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and <s>Sūryavarcā</s>,
and the Apsaras <s>Tilottamā</s> and the lovely goddess <s>Rambhā</s>,
and the leaders <s>Ṛtajit</s> and <s>Satyajit</s>, mighty in strength,
and the Rākṣasa <s>Brahmopeta</s>, and likewise <s>Yajñopeta</s>.

children.text: ityete nivasanti sma dvau dvau māsau divākare ||
children.translated_text: Thus these dwell in the sun, two months by two months.
These are the twelve septads of groups that preside over their stations.
By their splendor they bring the sun to supreme brilliance.
With woven words the seers praise <s>Ravi</s>,
and the Gandharvas and Apsarases attend him with song and dance.
The Yakṣas, the Vidyās and Grāmaṇīs, draw together the reins.

children.text: sarpāḥ sarpanti vai sūrye yātudhānānuyānti ca ||
children.translated_text: The serpents glide in the sun, and the Yātudhānas follow along.
The <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, surrounding <s>Ravi</s>, lead him from rising to setting.
According to the very power and austerity of these gods,
according to discipline, according to dharma, according to reality, and according to strength,
so that sun shines, kindled by their splendor.
By his own radiance he drives away all inauspiciousness from beings.
By these auspicious ones, indeed, the evil of human beings is removed.
Here and there they drive away the sin of those whose conduct is auspicious.

children.text: ete sahaiva sūryeṇa bhramanti sānugā divi ||
children.translated_text: Together with the sun, and with their followers, these wander in heaven,
heating, reciting, and gladdening the creatures.
They protect beings and act out of compassion.
This indeed is the station, through the Manvantaras, of those who preside over stations,

children.text: atītānāgatānāṃ ca vartante sāmprataṃ ca ye ||
children.translated_text: of those past and future, and of those who exist at present.

children.text: evaṃ vasanti vai sūrye saptakāste caturdaśa
children.translated_text: Thus the fourteen septads dwell in the sun.
These groups function through the fourteen Manvantaras.

children.text: grīṣme hime ca varṣāsu muñcamānā yathākramam
children.translated_text: In summer, in the cold season, and in the rains, releasing in due order

children.text: dharmaṃ himaṃ ca varṣaṃ ca yathākramamaharniśam ||
children.translated_text: heat, cold, and rain respectively, day and night,
that sun goes day by day, turning his rays, fully satisfying gods, ancestors, and humans.

children.text: śukle ca kṛṣṇe tadahaḥkrameṇa kālakṣaye caiva surāḥ pibanti ||
children.translated_text: In the bright and dark fortnights, according to the order of the days, and at the waning of time, the gods drink.

children.text: māsena taccāmṛtamasya mṛṣṭaṃ suvṛṣṭaye raśmiṣu rakṣitaṃ tu
children.translated_text: Within a month that sweet nectar of his is preserved in the rays for good rain,

children.text: sarve'mṛtaṃ tatpitaraḥ pibanti devāśca saumyāśca tathaiva kāvyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all the ancestors drink that nectar, as do the gods, the Saumyas, and the Kāvyas.

children.text: sūryeṇa gobhirhi vivardhitābhir adbhiḥ punaścaiva samucchritābhiḥ
children.translated_text: By waters increased by the sun's rays and then raised up again,
and by plants rained upon by rain, mortals then overcome hunger with food.

children.text: tṛptiśca tenārdhamāsaṃ surāṇāṃ māsaṃ sudhābhiḥ svadhayā pitṝṇām
children.translated_text: By that there is satisfaction for the gods for a half-month, and for the ancestors for a month through nectar and <s>svadhā</s>.

children.text: annena jīvantyaniśaṃ manuṣyāḥ sūryaḥ śritaṃ taddhi bibharti gobhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Humans live constantly by food; the sun indeed bears all that depends on him with his rays.
Thus this sun moves swiftly with a single wheel.
There, with those unwearied horses, he proceeds at the end of the day.

children.text: harir haridbhir hriyate turaṃgamaiḥ pibatyathāpo haribhiḥ sahasradhā
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> is borne by tawny horses; with his tawny rays he drinks the waters in a thousand ways.

children.text: punaḥ pramuñcatyatha tāśca yo hariḥ sa muhyamāno haribhisturaṃgamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Hari</s> releases those waters again, moved along by the tawny horses.
By day and night he revolves on that one-wheeled chariot,
swiftly traversing the seven island-continents and oceans with seven and seven horses.
Yoked to those horses whose forms are the Vedic metres, the wheel then has its appointed course.
Once yoked, they take forms at will, go where they will, and are swift as thought.
They are tawny, tireless, powerful, and praised by knowers of Brahman.
According to the sequence of days, he traverses the outer and inner circle.
Yoked at the beginning of the kalpa, they carry him until the dissolution of beings.
Surrounded by the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, he revolves through nights and days,
praised by great seers with their own woven words,
and served with song and dance by hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases.
The lord of day is made to revolve by flying, bird-like horses.
Likewise the moon travels through the lunar mansions that lie along its path.
Its waning and waxing, and likewise its rays, are remembered as like those of the sun.
The moon's chariot should be known as three-wheeled and as having horses on both sides.
The chariot was born from the womb of the waters, with horses and charioteer,
equipped with those harnesses and three wheels, and with excellent white horses.
With ten divine steeds, unattached and swift as the mind,
once yoked to that chariot, they carry it until the end of the age.
On that chariot are gathered <s>Śveta</s> and <s>Cakṣuḥśravas</s>;
those horses are of one color and bear him with the radiance of a conch.

children.text: ajaśca tripathaścaiva vṛṣo vājī naro hayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Aja</s>, <s>Tripatha</s>, <s>Vṛṣa</s>, <s>Vājī</s>, <s>Nara</s>, and <s>Haya</s>,
<s>Aṃśumān</s>, <s>Saptadhātu</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>, and <s>Vyomamṛga</s> likewise:
these, by name, are the ten horses of the moon,
and in this way they carry the god <s>Candramas</s> until the end of the age.

children.text: devaiḥ parivṛtaḥ somaḥ pitṛbhiḥ saha gacchati
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s>, surrounded by the gods, goes together with the Pitṛs.
At the beginning of <s>Soma</s>'s bright fortnight, when <s>Bhāskara</s> stands beyond him,

children.text: āpūryate paro bhāgaḥ somasya tu ahaḥkramāt
children.translated_text: the farther portion of <s>Soma</s> is filled up in the sequence of days.
Then <s>Ravi</s>, approaching the <s>Soma</s> that had been diminished by drinking, pervades it.
For fifteen days <s>Bhāskara</s>, with a single ray, fills up what has been drunk,
and thereby gives him portion after portion in the order of days.
As he is being filled by <s>Suṣumṇā</s>, his digits increase in the bright fortnight;

children.text: tasmāddhrasanti vai kṛṣṇe śukle hyāpyāyayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: therefore they diminish in the dark fortnight, while in the bright fortnight they are replenished.
Thus, by the power of the sun, the body of the moon is filled up.
At the full moon he appears white, with a complete disk.
In this way <s>Soma</s> is filled up in the bright fortnights, day by day.
Then, beginning with the second day of the dark fortnight up to the fourteenth,
the gods drink from <s>Indu</s>, who is made of the essence of the waters and consists only of sap,
the water-formed, honey-like, gentle nectar.
That nectar, gathered during the half-month by the heat of the sun,
is attended by them at the full moon, when <s>Soma</s> has come for their consumption.
For one night the gods, together with the Pitṛs and the seers, drink.
At the beginning of <s>Soma</s>'s dark fortnight, when he faces <s>Bhāskara</s>,
his farther self is diminished according to the succession of the digits being drunk.
Thirty-three, and three hundred and thirty besides,
and thirty-three thousand gods drink <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: ityevaṃ pīyamānasya kṛṣṇe vardhanti tāḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, while he is being drunk, those dark digits increase in the dark fortnight,

children.text: kṣīyante ca tāḥ śuklāḥ kṛṣṇā hyāpyāyayanti ca
children.translated_text: and the bright ones diminish, while the dark ones are replenished.
Thus, when the night-maker has been drunk day by day by the gods,
those gods, after drinking for a half-month, depart at the new moon.
And the Pitṛs attend the moon at the new moon.
Then, when a little remains in the fifteenth part of the night-maker,
the Pitṛs, in the afternoon on that last day,

children.text: pibanti dvikalaṃ kālaṃ śiṣṭāstāstu kalāstu yāḥ
children.translated_text: drink for the time of two digits the remaining digits that are left.
At the new moon that nectar is released from the rays;
having drunk that nectar at the completion of the half-month, they depart.
The <s>Saumyas</s>, the <s>Barhiṣads</s>, and those remembered as <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>,

children.text: kāvyāścaiva tu ye proktāḥ pitaraḥ sarva eva te
children.translated_text: and those who are called <s>Kāvyas</s>: all these are Pitṛs.

children.text: saṃvatsarāśca ye kāvyāḥ pañcābdā vai dvijāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Saṃvatsaras</s> who are <s>Kāvyas</s> are remembered, O twice-born ones, as the five-year groups.
The <s>Saumyas</s> should be known as <s>Sutapas</s>, and the <s>Saumyas</s> likewise as <s>Barhiṣads</s>.
And the three <s>Agniṣvāttas</s> are established in the creation of the Pitṛs, O twice-born ones.

children.text: pitṛbhiḥ pīyamānāyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ tu vai kalām
children.translated_text: When the fifteenth digit is being drunk by the Pitṛs,
as far as it is diminished, that indeed is the fifteenth portion.

children.text: amāvāsyāṃ tathā tasya antarā pūryate paraḥ
children.translated_text: At the new moon, meanwhile, his farther portion is filled again.

children.text: vṛddhikṣayau vai pakṣādau ṣoḍaśyāṃ śaśinaḥ mṛtau
children.translated_text: At the beginning of the fortnights there are the waxing and waning of the moon, and at the sixteenth digit its death.
Thus, because of the sun, these wanings and waxings occur in the night-maker.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall now describe the chariot of <s>Svarbhānu</s> among the stars and planets.

children.text: atha tejomayaḥ śubhraḥ somaputrasya vai rathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the radiant, bright chariot of the son of <s>Soma</s>
is yoked with ten tawny horses, swift as the wind.

children.text: śvetaḥ piśaṅgaḥ sāraṅgo nīlaḥ śyāmo vilohitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: White, tawny, dappled, blue, dark, and blood-red,
and white, green, spotted, and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> as well:
with these ten greatly fortunate, excellent horses, born of the wind,
then the chariot of <s>Bhauma</s> too is remembered as golden and eight-limbed.
With eight red horses, bearing banners and born of fire,
that <s>Kumāra</s> proceeds, moving straight, retrograde, and obliquely retrograde.
Then the learned <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, son of <s>Aṅgiras</s> and teacher of the gods,
moves along in a golden chariot with pale horses.
Yoked with eight horses and with banners, born from fire,

children.text: abdaṃ vasati yo rāśau svadiśaṃ tena gacchati ||
children.translated_text: he dwells for a year in a zodiacal sign and by that goes in his own direction.
Yoked with eight horses, with banners and like fire,
the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s> travels in that swiftly moving chariot.
Then <s>Śanaiścara</s> too, with strong horses swift as the wind,
mounts an iron chariot and goes forth; that is <s>Śani</s>.
As for <s>Svarbhānu</s>, his eight horses are black and swift as the wind;

children.text: rathaṃ tamomayaṃ tasya vahanti sma sudaṃśitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: well-armored, they carry his chariot, which is made of darkness.
<s>Rāhu</s>, whose station is with the sun, goes to the moon at the lunar junctures;
and from the moon he approaches the sun at the junctures at the ends of darkness.
Then the horses of <s>Ketumat</s> are eight, swift as the wind;
they have the appearance and color of straw-smoke, with emaciated bodies, very terrible.

children.text: ete vāhā grahāṇāṃ vai mayā proktā rathaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: These, together with their chariots, are the vehicles of the grahas, as I have described them.
All of them are fastened to <s>Dhruva</s>, bound with wind-cords.

children.text: ete vai bhrāmyamāṇāste yathāyogaṃ vahanti vai
children.translated_text: These, revolving, carry them according to their proper order,
by the invisible wind-reins with which they are bound by the wind.
Bound by those, the moon, the sun, and the planets revolve in heaven,
as long as the whole host of lights follows that <s>Dhruva</s> around.
Just as something in the water of a river is carried along together with the water,
so the houses of the gods are carried along by the force of the wind;
therefore those that are grasped in the sky are called houses of the gods.
And as many stars as there are, so many are its rays;
all of them, bound to <s>Dhruva</s>, revolve and cause others to revolve.

children.text: tailapīḍaṃ yathā cakraṃ bhramate bhrāmayanti vai
children.translated_text: Just as the wheel of an oil-press turns and makes things turn,
so all the luminaries revolve, bound in every way by the wind.
They move like the circle of a firebrand, driven by the wheel of wind;
because it makes them move onward, it is therefore remembered as <s>Pravaha</s>.

children.text: evaṃ dhruve niyukto'sau bhramate jyotiṣāṃ gaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus this host of luminaries, fastened to <s>Dhruva</s>, revolves;

children.text: eṣa tārāmayaḥ proktaḥ śiśumāre dhruvo divi ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Dhruva</s> in heaven is declared to be in the starry <s>Śiśumāra</s>.

children.text: yadahnā kurute pāpaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā niśi muñcati
children.translated_text: Whatever sin a person commits by day, after seeing him at night he is released from it.
As many stars as are situated in the body of the <s>Śiśumāra</s>,
after seeing them, one lives that many more years.
Having understood the form of the <s>Śiśumāra</s> in all its divisions,
one should know <s>Uttānapāda</s> as its upper jaw, facing north;
<s>Yajña</s> should be known as the lower one, and <s>Dharma</s> rests upon the head.
In its heart is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; the <s>Sādhyas</s> and the <s>Aśvins</s> are in the forefeet.
<s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Aryaman</s> are its two hind thighs.
The year is to be known in its generative organ, and <s>Mitra</s> is situated in the lower vital passage.
In the tail are <s>Agni</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: eṣa tārāmayaḥ stambho nāstameti na vodayam
children.translated_text: This pillar made of stars has neither setting nor rising.
The lunar mansions, the moon, the sun, and the planets, together with the hosts of stars,
all stand in heaven as a wheel, facing toward its mouth.
Presided over by <s>Dhruva</s>, they go around <s>Dhruva</s> alone, keeping him to the right,
around the excellent god <s>Dhruva</s> in heaven, who has become the central post.

children.text: āgnīdhrakāśyapānāṃ tu teṣāṃ sa paramo dhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the descendants of <s>Āgnīdhra</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s>, he is that supreme <s>Dhruva</s>.
This one alone revolves above the central summit of <s>Meru</s>,
drawing along the wheel of luminaries, with its face turned downward,
and, while gazing upon <s>Meru</s>, it proceeds clockwise.
The sages said:
We have heard completely and without remainder what has been spoken by you.
How can they be houses of the gods? Describe the luminaries again.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain all this, the movement of the sun and the moon,
and how the houses of the gods belong in the same way to the sun and moon.
When fire shone forth in the night, through <s>Brahmā</s>, the unmanifest source,
this world was unmanifest, covered by the darkness of night.
In this world, when only the four elements remained and <s>Brahmā</s> presided over it,
the blessed self-born one, intent on accomplishing the truth of the worlds,
moving in the form of a firefly, considered manifestation.

children.text: jñātvāgniṃ kalpakālādāv apaḥ pṛthvīṃ ca saṃśritā ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning of the kalpa, he understood that fire had entered the waters and the earth.
Having gathered it for the sake of illumination, he again became threefold in equal measure.
That which cooks in this earthly world is called fire.

children.text: yaścāsau tapate sūrye śuciragniśca sa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And that which heats in the sun is remembered as pure fire.
There is electric fire, digestive fire, lunar fire, and also electric fire without fuel.
Among these fiery forms, one has fuel and another is without fuel.
The fire fueled by wood, produced by friction, is the fire that is quenched by waters.
The flaming cooking fire is fire; the one without brightness has a lunar character.

children.text: yaścāsau maṇḍale śukle nirūṣmā na prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: And that which is in the white orb, without heat, does not shine forth.

children.text: prabhā saurī tu pādena astaṃ yāti divākare
children.translated_text: A quarter of the solar radiance goes to setting with the sun;
at night it enters fire, and therefore fire shines.

children.text: udite tu punaḥ sūrye ūṣmāgnestu samāviśat
children.translated_text: When the sun rises again, heat from the fire enters it;
through a quarter of the fire's brilliance, therefore it gives heat by day.

children.text: prākāśyaṃ ca tathauṣṇyaṃ ca sauryāgneye tu tejasī
children.translated_text: Luminosity and heat are the solar and fiery radiances respectively;
through mutual interpenetration they are nourished day and night.

children.text: uttare caiva bhūmyardhe tathā hyasmiṃstu dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: In the northern half of the earth, and likewise here in the southern half,

children.text: uttiṣṭhati punaḥ sūrye rātrirāviśate hy apaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the sun rises again, night enters the waters.
Therefore the waters become copper-colored, because day and night enter them.

children.text: astaṃ gate punaḥ sūrye aharvai praviśaty apaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the sun has set again, day enters the waters.

children.text: tasmānnaktaṃ punaḥ śuklā hyāpo dṛśyanti bhāsurāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore at night the waters are again seen as bright and white.
By this ordered sequence, in the southern and northern halves of the earth,
at sunrise and sunset here, day and night enter the waters.

children.text: yaścāsau tapate sūryaḥ so 'paḥ pibati raśmibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that sun which gives heat drinks the waters with his rays.
This fire is thousand-footed; it is like a red jar.

children.text: ādatte sa tu nāḍīnāṃ sahasreṇa samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: With a thousand channels it draws up water on every side,
from rivers and oceans, and also from lakes and wells.
Through its thousand rays there is an outpouring of cold, rain, and heat.
Of those, four hundred channels, varied in form, send down rain;
they are <s>Candanā</s>, <s>Medhyā</s>, <s>Ketanā</s>, and likewise <s>Cetanā</s>.
All are immortal, life-giving rays that produce rain.
The rays born of snow, mutually connected, are remembered as thirty.
The rays of <s>Bhānu</s> are drunk by the moon, the stars, and all the planets.
These middle ones, and others too, are gladdening rays that produce snow.
The white ones, the <s>Kakubhas</s>, the <s>Gāvas</s>, and those that are <s>Viśvasṛts</s>,
all these are named <s>Śuklās</s>; the thirty are producers of heat.

children.text: saṃbibhrati hi tāḥ sarvā manuṣyāndevatāḥ pitṝn ||
children.translated_text: For all of them sustain human beings, gods, and ancestors.
They sustain human beings with plants, and the ancestors also with <s>svadhā</s> (ancestral oblation),
and they continually satisfy all the gods with <s>amṛta</s> (nectar).

children.text: vasante caiva grīṣme ca śanaiḥ saṃtapate tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: In spring and summer he heats gently with three [rays],
and in the rainy season and autumn, in the same way, he rains with four.

children.text: hemante śiśire caiva himotsargas tribhiḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: In winter and the cool season, again, there is an emission of frost by three [rays].

children.text: oṣadhīṣu balaṃ dhatte sudhāṃ ca svadhayā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He places strength in the plants, and again nectar together with <s>svadhā</s>.
The sun sets immortality in the nectar, threefold among the three.
Thus the thousand solar rays accomplish the welfare of the worlds.
On reaching the seasons, that thousand divides again in many ways.
Thus the white, radiant disk is known by the name 'world',
and is the foundation and source of the nakṣatras, planets, and moon.
The moon, the lunar mansions, and all the planets should be understood as born from the sun.
The solar ray called <s>Suṣumnā</s> makes the waned moon increase.
In the east is <s>Harikeśa</s>, which indeed makes the source of the nakṣatras.
To the south is <s>Viśvakarman</s>, the ray that nourishes <s>Budha</s>.
That which is behind, <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, is remembered as the source of <s>Śukra</s>.

children.text: saṃvardhanastu yo raśmiḥ sa yonirlohitasya ca
children.translated_text: The ray called <s>Saṃvardhana</s> is the source of the red one, <s>Lohita</s>.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhastu hyaśvabhū raśmiryoniḥ sa hi bṛhaspateḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sixth ray, <s>Aśvabhū</s>, is indeed the source of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Again the ray <s>Surāṭ</s> nourishes <s>Śanaiścara</s>.
Because those do not perish, therefore their state as nakṣatras is remembered.
These fields indeed fall upon the sun by means of his beams.
The sun receives their fields; from that comes their state as nakṣatras.
For virtuous souls who have crossed from this world to that world,
these are stars because they carry one across, and bright ones because of their whiteness.

children.text: divyānāṃ pārthivānāṃ ca vaṃśānāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Of all divine and earthly lineages, in every respect,
because the heater is joined with radiance, he is called <s>Āditya</s>.
The root <s>srav</s> is stated in the sense of flowing.
Because of the flowing forth of his radiance, therefore he is remembered as <s>Savitṛ</s>.
This word <s>canda</s> is said to be principal and rich in meanings,

children.text: śuklatve hyamṛtatve ca śītatve hlādane'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: in whiteness, immortality, coolness, and also in gladdening.
The two divine, radiant, sky-moving disks of the sun and moon,
white, auspicious, made of water and fire, and resembling round jars,
are inhabited by the karma-gods; these are all stations,
for seers, suns, planets, and the rest in all the Manvantaras.

children.text: tāni devagṛhāṇi syuḥ sthānākhyāni bhavanti hi
children.translated_text: They are houses of the gods, and indeed they become what are called stations.
The sun entered the solar station, and the moon likewise the lunar one.
<s>Śukra</s> entered the station of <s>Śukra</s>, brilliant and having sixteen spokes.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s> entered the great station, and <s>Lohita</s> the red one.
<s>Śanaiścara</s> entered his station; thus likewise there is the station of <s>Śanaiścara</s>.

children.text: budho'pi vai budhasthānaṃ bhānuṃ svarbhānureva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Budha</s> too entered the station of <s>Budha</s>, and <s>Svarbhānu</s> the station of <s>Bhānu</s>.
And all the nakṣatras enter the nakṣatra stations.

children.text: jyotīṃṣi sukṛtām ete jñeyā devagṛhāstu vai ||
children.translated_text: These lights of the meritorious should be known as houses of the gods.
These stations remain until the dissolution of beings,
through all Manvantaras; indeed they are stations of the gods.

children.text: abhimānena tiṣṭhanti tāni devāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: The gods occupy them again and again through identification with them.
The past ones exist with past gods, and the future ones with future gods,

children.text: vartante vartamānaiśca suraiḥ sārdhaṃ tu sthāninaḥ
children.translated_text: while the present station-holders exist together with present gods.
The god <s>Sūrya</s> is <s>Vivasvant</s>, the eighth son of <s>Aditi</s>.
The bright god <s>Soma</s>, joined with dharma, is remembered as a <s>Vasu</s>.
<s>Śukra</s> should be known as a Daitya, a Bhārgava, and the priest of the Asuras.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, of great splendor, is the preceptor of the gods, the son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>.
<s>Budha</s> is charming, and he is remembered as the son of the moon.
<s>Śanaiścara</s> is misshapen and the son of <s>Saṃjñā</s> and <s>Vivasvat</s>.
Fire was born in <s>Vikeśī</s>; that young one is the lord of <s>Lohita</s>.
The daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s>, named after the nakṣatras, are remembered in the fields.
<s>Svarbhānu</s>, son of <s>Siṃhikā</s>, is an Asura who subdues beings.
He is proclaimed as presiding over the moon, sun, planets, and nakṣatras.
These stations have been described, and also the deities who occupy the stations.
The divine white station of thousand-rayed <s>Vivasvat</s> is equal to fire.
The station of him whose light has a thousand rays is watery and also fiery.
The charming one's station, resting in the house of the sun's rays, is a station of the quarters.
<s>Śukra</s>, the god who is made of waters, has sixteen rays.

children.text: lohito navaraśmistu sthānamāpyaṃ tu tasya vai
children.translated_text: The red one has nine rays; his station is indeed watery.
The great station of the creator has twelve rays and the color of turmeric.
That of eight-rayed <s>Śani</s> is black, old, and made of iron.
The iron station of <s>Svarbhānu</s> is an abode for afflicting beings.
The stars are refuges of the meritorious; their rays are golden.
Because they carry one across they are stars, and because of whiteness they are also stars.
The diameter of <s>Savitṛ</s> is remembered as nine thousand yojanas.

children.text: maṇḍalaṃ triguṇaṃ cāsya vistāro bhāskarasya tu ||
children.translated_text: The disk of <s>Bhāskara</s> is three times that as its extent.
The extent of the moon is remembered as twice the extent of the sun.
Because of the moon's breadth, its disk is remembered as three times that.
The disks of the stars are set forth above all.
But other groups beyond them measure half a yojana.
Then <s>Svarbhānu</s>, becoming equal, moves below it,
having raised up the earthly shadow, fashioned in the shape of a circle.

children.text: brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ sthānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu tamomayam
children.translated_text: That third station, made by <s>Brahmā</s>, is composed of darkness.

children.text: ādityātsa tu niṣkramya somaṃ gacchati parvasu ||
children.translated_text: Coming forth from the <s>Āditya</s>, he goes to <s>Soma</s> at the lunar junctures.
And from <s>Soma</s> he returns to the <s>Āditya</s> at the solar junctures.
Because <s>Svarbhānu</s> strikes with his own radiance, he is remembered by that name.
For <s>Bhārgava</s> a sixteenth part of the moon is prescribed,
in diameter and also in disk, measured in yojanas, so it is remembered.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s> should be known as a quarter less than <s>Bhārgava</s>.
<s>Ketu</s> and <s>Vakra</s> are both remembered as a quarter less than <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
In breadth and disk <s>Budha</s> is a quarter less than those two.
Those embodied forms here which are stars and lunar mansions,
are equal to <s>Budha</s> in breadth and disk.
The forms of stars and lunar mansions are smaller in relation to one another.

children.text: śatāni pañca catvāri trīṇi dve caikameva ca
children.translated_text: Five, four, three, two, and one hundred respectively
are the disks of the stars, set above everything else.
They measure half a yojana; nothing smaller than them exists.

children.text: upariṣṭāttu ye teṣāṃ grahā ye krūrasāttvikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Above them are those planets which are fierce and benign.
<s>Saura</s>, <s>Aṅgirasa</s>, and <s>Vakra</s> should be known as slow-moving.
Below them again are four other great planets.
<s>Soma</s>, the sun, <s>Budha</s>, and <s>Bhārgava</s> are the swift-moving ones.
As many lunar mansions as there are, so many crores of stars there are.
The sun moves below all the planets.

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tasyordhvaṃ carate śaśī ||
children.translated_text: Having formed a broad disk, the moon moves above him.
The circle of the lunar mansions also moves above <s>Soma</s>.
Above the lunar mansions is <s>Budha</s>, and above <s>Budha</s> is <s>Bhārgava</s>.

children.text: vakrastu bhārgavād ūrdhvaṃ vakrād ūrdhvaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vakra</s> is above <s>Bhārgava</s>, and above <s>Vakra</s> is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Above him is <s>Śanaiścara</s>, stationed above the teacher of the gods.
And above <s>Śanaiścara</s> should be known the circle of the <s>Saptarṣis</s>.
Above the <s>Saptarṣis</s> is <s>Dhruva</s>; the whole heaven is fixed in <s>Dhruva</s>.
In doubled thousands and in hundreds of yojanas
is each interval between planets upward from the circle of the lunar mansions.
The intervals between stars and planets are established higher and higher.

children.text: grahāśca candrasūryau ca divi divyena tejasā ||
children.translated_text: The planets, and the moon and sun, with divine radiance in heaven,
are joined with the lunar mansions as they move according to a fixed order.
The moon, sun, planets, and lunar mansions occupy low and high houses.

children.text: samāgame ca bhede ca paśyanti yugapatprajāḥ
children.translated_text: At conjunction and at separation, people see them all at once.

children.text: parasparaṃ sthitā hyevaṃ yujyante ca parasparam ||
children.translated_text: Thus they stand in relation to one another and are joined with one another.
Their conjunction should be understood by the wise without confusion.

children.text: ityevaṃ saṃniveśo vai pṛthivyā jyotiṣāṃ ca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this is the arrangement of the earth and of the luminaries,
and likewise of the island-continents, oceans, and mountains,

children.text: varṣāṇāṃ ca nadīnāṃ ca ye ca teṣu vasanti vai ||
children.translated_text: of the lands and rivers, and of those who dwell in them.
Thus this arrangement of the luminaries is governed by the sun alone.

children.text: āvartaḥ sāntaro madhye saṃkṣiptaśca dhruvāttu sa ||
children.translated_text: It is a revolving circuit with an interval in the middle, and it narrows from <s>Dhruva</s>.
It is spread out on all sides among them, rising as if circular in shape.
It was created by the Lord for the sake of worldly activity.
At the beginning of the kalpa it was deliberately established by <s>Svayambhū</s>.
Thus this is the arrangement of everything that consists of light.
It is remembered as the <s>Vaiśvarūpa</s> transformation of primal matter.

children.text: teṣāṃ śakyaṃ na saṃkhyātuṃ yāthātathyena kenacit
children.translated_text: No one is able to enumerate them according to reality,
the coming and going of the luminaries, by means of a human eye of flesh.
The seers said:
How did the blessed <s>Maheśvara</s> formerly become the enemy of the cities?

children.text: dadāha ca kathaṃ devastanno vistarato vada ||
children.translated_text: And how did the god burn them? Tell us that in detail.
We all ask you again and again out of great respect.
Tell us how that <s>Tripura</s>, difficult to assail and made by the magical power of <s>Maya</s>,

children.text: devenaikeṣuṇā dagdhaṃ tathā no vada mānada ||
children.translated_text: was burned by the god with a single arrow, O giver of honor.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇudhvaṃ tripuraṃ devo yathā dāritavān bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Listen to how the god <s>Bhava</s> split <s>Tripura</s> apart.
There was an Asura named <s>Maya</s>, a great master of magic, the source of magical powers.

children.text: nirjitaḥ sa tu saṃgrāme tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Defeated in battle, he performed supreme austerity.
While he was practicing austerity, O brahmins, two other Daityas, by his favor,
performed supreme austerity, intent upon his very purpose.
The strong <s>Vidyunmālī</s> and the heroic one named <s>Tāraka</s>,
filled with <s>Maya</s>'s power and staying at <s>Maya</s>'s side, practiced austerity.

children.text: lokā iva yathā mūrtās trayas traya ivāgnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like the worlds embodied, like three fires,
those Dānavas practiced austerity, heating the three worlds.
In winter they lay on beds of water, and in summer amid the five fires.
