In the rainy season they remained in the open air, wasting away their dear bodies.

children.text: sevānāḥ phalamūlāni puṣpāṇi ca jalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: They subsisted on fruits, roots, flowers, and water.
At other times they followed different diets, wearing bark garments smeared with mud.
They were sunk in mossy mud, both pure and impure.
Then they became fleshless, emaciated, and covered with veins.
Through the power of their austerity, as though its brilliance had been shaken away,
the whole world became without radiance and appeared only dim.
As the worlds were being burned by those three Dānava-fires,
<s>Pitāmaha</s>, the friend of the world, appeared before them.
Then the Daityas, doers of bold deeds, spoke to their own grandsire, who had suddenly arrived.

children.text: svakaṃ pitāmahaṃ daityāstaṃ vai tuṣṭuvureva ca
children.translated_text: Those Daityas also praised him.
Then <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to those Dānavas, whose radiance blazed through austerity,
his eyes full of joy and his face full of joy at that time:
"I am a giver of boons to you, children. Pleased by your austerity, I have come.
Choose what you desire; let whatever you long for be spoken."
When they were thus addressed and had accepted the grandsire,
<s>Maya</s>, the <s>Viśvakarman</s>, spoke, his eyes opening wide with delight:

children.text: deva daityāḥ purā devaiḥ saṃgrāme tārakāmaye ||
children.translated_text: "O god, long ago in the battle connected with <s>Tāraka</s>, the Daityas were defeated by the gods,
beaten down and even slain by weapons.
Because the enmity with the gods continued, we fled trembling with fear;

children.text: śaraṇaṃ naiva jānīmaḥ śarma vā śaraṇārthinaḥ
children.translated_text: we who seek refuge know neither refuge nor safety.

children.text: so'haṃ tapaḥprabhāvena tava bhaktyā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the power of austerity and likewise by devotion to you,
I wish to make that fortress which even the gods would find hard to cross.

children.text: tasmiṃśca tripure durge matkṛte kṛtināṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: "And in that fortress, <s>Tripura</s>, made by me, O best of craftsmen,
against beings of earth and water, against curses and the fiery power of sages,
and against the weapons of the gods and the gods themselves, O <s>Prajāpati</s>,

children.text: alaṅghanīyaṃ bhavatu tripuraṃ yadi te priyam
children.translated_text: let <s>Tripura</s> be unassailable, if it is pleasing to you."
When the <s>Viśvakarman</s> had spoken thus, he then, addressed by that <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
said with a smile to <s>Maya</s>, lord of the hosts of Daityas:
"Complete immortality does not exist for one whose conduct is unrighteous, O Dānava.
Therefore let the construction of the fortress be carried out, even in a moment."
Hearing the words of the grandsire, the Dānava <s>Maya</s> at once
again addressed <s>Brahmā</s>, the lotus-born, with joined palms:
"Whoever should burn the fortress with one arrow, released only once,

children.text: samaṃ sa saṃyuge hanyādavadhyaṃ śeṣato bhavet
children.translated_text: let him kill it all at once in battle; otherwise let it remain invulnerable."
Having said, "So be it," the god, the grandsire, to <s>Maya</s>,

children.text: svapne labdho yathārtho vai tatraivādarśanaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: as if the desired object had been obtained in a dream, vanished right there.
When the grandsire had gone, the Daityas, shining with a splendor like that of <s>Maya</s> and the sun,
became brilliant through the granting of the boon and very powerful through austerity.
But that Dānava <s>Maya</s>, very wise and best among bulls,
resolved to make the fortress and then thought as follows:

children.text: kathaṃ nāma bhaveddurgaṃ tanmayā tripuraṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: "How indeed should that fortress be, the <s>Tripura</s> made by me?

children.text: vatsyate tatpuraṃ divyaṃ matto nānyairna saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: That divine city will be inhabited by me and by no others; there is no doubt.

children.text: yathācaikeṣuṇā tena tatpuraṃ na hi hanyate ||
children.translated_text: And as that city must not be destroyed by that one arrow,
I must devise such an arrangement against the gods through deliberation.
The extent of each city should be one hundred yojanas,
and the breadth of each of them should be one hundred yojanas.
Their construction will take place under the conjunction of <s>Puṣya</s>, and the cities will endure from ancient times;
under the conjunction of <s>Puṣya</s> they will come together in the sky.
Whoever reaches those cities when they are joined under the conjunction of <s>Puṣya</s>,
will destroy the cities, even hundreds of them, with a single blow.

children.text: āyasaṃ tu kṣititale rājataṃ tu nabhastale ||
children.translated_text: One city will be iron on the surface of the earth, and one silver in the sky;
above the silver one there will be a golden city.
Thus that <s>Tripura</s> will be furnished with three cities,
hard to approach, with intervals a hundred yojanas broad.
With upper chambers, hundreds of engines, and devices that hurl stones, wheels, and spears,
with gateways like great <s>Mandara</s> and <s>Meru</s>, it will shine with peaks of ramparts.

children.text: satārakākhyena mayena guptaṃ svasthaṃ ca guptaṃ taḍinmālināpi
children.translated_text: Guarded by <s>Maya</s>, called <s>Tāraka</s>, and securely guarded also by <s>Taḍinmālin</s>,

children.text: ko nāma hantuṃ tripuraṃ samartho muktvā trinetraṃ bhagavantamekam ||
children.translated_text: who could be able to destroy <s>Tripura</s>, apart from the one blessed <s>Trinetra</s>?"
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus filled with thought, the Daitya, by the power of divine means,
made the fortress <s>Tripura</s>, moving according to the motion of the mind.
"Let the rampart be by this path; let the gateway be here or there.
Here let there be a tower-gate, and here a towered gateway.
Let the royal road from here also be broad.

children.text: rathyoparathyāḥ sattrikā iha catvara eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Let streets, side-streets, covered ways, and crossroads be here.
This is the place of the inner palace, and here is the shrine of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: savaṭāni taḍāgāni hyatra vāpyaḥ sarāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: Here are ponds with banyan trees, tanks, reservoirs, and lakes.
Here are parks and assembly halls, and gardens here or there.
Here is a charming exit for the Dānavas."
In this way the knower of city-planning mentally arranged it there.

children.text: mayena tatpuraṃ sṛṣṭaṃ tripuraṃ tviti naḥ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: That city was created by <s>Maya</s>; we have heard that it was indeed <s>Tripura</s>.
The city made by <s>Maya</s> that was formed of black iron
was inhabited there by the ruler called <s>Tāraka</s>, who was appointed lord of that place.
The city that was built of silver, resembling the full moon,
had <s>Vidyunmālī</s> as its lord there, like a lightning-wreathed cloud.
And the city made by <s>Maya</s> that was fashioned with gold,
there <s>Maya</s> himself went as its lord and ruler.
There <s>Tāraka</s>'s city was at an interval of one hundred yojanas,
and <s>Vidyunmālī</s>'s city also was at an interval of one hundred yojanas.
The great city of <s>Maya</s> too was like Mount <s>Meru</s>.
In time, through the mere conjunction with <s>Puṣya</s>, long ago that <s>Maya</s>,
the Daitya, made <s>Tripura</s>, just as <s>Trinetra</s> made the <s>Puṣpaka</s>.

children.text: yena yena mayo yāti prakurvāṇaḥ puraṃ purāt ||
children.translated_text: Wherever <s>Maya</s> went, making city after city,
there, in those places, excellent mansions appeared by themselves in the western quarter.
Hundreds and thousands of cities of gold, silver, and iron,
adorned with jewels, shone for the enemies of the immortals.
They were furnished with hundreds of palaces and crowded with lofty mansions.
For all of them they could go wherever desire led, and they could pass beyond every world.
They had gardens, reservoirs, wells, and lotus-filled lakes.
They had become groves of aśoka trees and were filled with the cries of cuckoos.
They had spacious picture galleries and excellent four-courtyard houses.
They had seven, eight, and ten storeys, and had been honored by <s>Maya</s>.
They had many banners and flags and were adorned with garlands and wreaths.
They rang with the sound of networks of little bells; they were fragrant and vast.
They were well joined together and well plastered, and were supplied with flowers and food offerings.
They were darkened by the smoke of sacrifices and furnished with full jars.
They seemed to cover the sky and were like rows of swans.
Arranged in lines, the houses shone in the city of <s>Tripura</s>.
With strings of pearls hanging down, they seemed to laugh at the splendor of the moon.
They were perfumed with jasmine, jāti blossoms, and other flowers, and with fragrant incense.
They constantly gave delight to the five senses, like good men who are impartial.
The ramparts in that <s>Tripura</s> were marked with gold, silver, iron, jewels, gems, and collyrium.
They were like the enclosing walls of mountains.
In each city there were a hundred upon a hundred gateways.
With flags and banners, they appeared like mountain peaks.
Even those cities in <s>Tripura</s> were charming with the sounds of anklets.
There too were maidens' quarters whose splendor surpassed heaven.
With parks, pleasure grounds, ponds, banyan trees, and crossroads,
and with lakes, rivers, forests, and groves as well,
the approaches to <s>Tripura</s> were filled with divine enjoyments and pleasures, and possessed many jewels.
They were lovely with masses of flowers.
Moats a hundredfold deep were made there, with devices to ward off magic.
Hearing of that excellent arrangement of the fortress, made by <s>Maya</s>, whose valor and deeds were marvelous,
the sons of <s>Diti</s>, enemies of the king of the gods, came there by the thousands, men of boundless prowess.
Then <s>Tripura</s> was filled with Asuras, crushers of arrogant enemies, tormentors of men, resembling mountains and lordly elephants,

children.text: babhūva pūrṇaṃ tripuraṃ tathā purā yathāmbaraṃ bhūrijalair jalapradaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as the sky in former times is filled with abundant waters by rain clouds.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When the fortress of <s>Tripura</s> had been built by <s>Maya</s>, the architect of the Asuras,
that fortress became hard to approach for the gods and Asuras whose enmities were bound fast.
With wives and sons, bearing weapons and equal to Death,
they entered the houses assigned by <s>Maya</s>, and they were delighted.
Many entered like lions entering a forest, like makaras entering the ocean,
and with their angers and extreme harshness they were like passions gathered in a body.
In that same way, that city was occupied by the mighty enemies of the gods.
<s>Tripura</s> became crowded, thronged with hundreds of crores of Daityas.
Coming up even from <s>Sutala</s> and from the Pātāla abode of the Dānavas,
those cloud-like beings, and those who lived in the mountains, attended there.
Whatever desire anyone sought, once he had reached the refuge of <s>Tripura</s>,

children.text: tasya tasya mayastatra māyayā vidadhāti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: for each of them <s>Maya</s> provided it there by his magic.
On evenings accompanied by the moon, in lakes filled with lotuses,
in parks with mango trees and in the groves of ascetics,
the Dānavas, handsome and with limbs smeared with sandalwood, like rutting elephants,
wearing fine ornaments and garments, and fine garlands and unguents,
with beloved women of charming gait, born of amorous gestures and expressions,
constantly sported with women, and the Dānavas were joyful.
Rejoicing in the place built by <s>Maya</s>, the great Asuras

children.text: arthe dharme ca kāme ca nidadhuste matīḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: set their minds of their own accord on wealth, <s>dharma</s> (religious duty), and pleasure.
For those enemies of the Thirty gods who were joined with <s>Tripura</s> and lived in <s>Tripura</s>,

children.text: vrajati sma sukhaṃ kālaḥ svargasthānāṃ yathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: time passed happily, just as it does for those dwelling in heaven.
Sons served their fathers, and wives likewise served their husbands.
They were freed from quarrels, and affections became abundant.
Even powerful <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) did not trouble those who stayed in <s>Tripura</s>,
while the sons of <s>Diti</s> worshiped <s>Hara</s> in the sanctuary of <s>Tripura</s>.
Cries of 'an auspicious day!' arose, together with blessings and Vedic chants,
mixed with the sounds of their own anklets and the notes of flutes and vīṇās.
The laughter of excellent women, which unsettled the mind,
was always heard in <s>Tripura</s> as the lordly Dānavas took their pleasure.
As they worshiped the gods and honored the brahmins,
a long time passed for them in deliberations concerning <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and pleasure.
Then misfortune, envy, thirst, and hunger,
and Kali and quarrel as well, entered <s>Tripura</s> together.
Those fearsome beings entered <s>Tripura</s> at twilight,
and, terrible ones, they took possession of bodies alike, just as diseases do.
As all these were entering the interior of <s>Tripura</s> by means of <s>Maya</s>,
they were seen in dreams as terrifying, entering the Dānavas.
When the thousand-rayed sun had risen, the maker of auspicious light,
<s>Maya</s> entered the assembly, like a cloud attended by two suns.
On a beautiful seat like a peak of <s>Meru</s>, adorned with gold,
they sat like rain clouds on the summit of a golden mountain.
At his two sides were the Dānavas named <s>Tāraka</s> and <s>Vidyunmālī</s>.
They sat near <s>Maya</s> like two elephant calves beside an elephant.
Then all the enemies of the gods, wholly enraged for the field of battle,
the Dānavas, foes of the gods, sat down, firmly pierced by anger.
When all of them had taken their seats and were seated comfortably,
<s>Maya</s>, the begetter of magic, spoke thus to the Dānavas:
'Sky-goers, whose cries are those of sky-goers, ho! ho! sons of <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>,'
Listen: this terrifying dream was seen by me.
There were four women there, and three terrifying mortals,
their faces blazing with the fire of anger, entering as destroyers of <s>Tripura</s>.
Having entered, those furious ones of incomparable valor entered the cities,
and, becoming many-bodied, entered our bodies.
And this city, <s>Tripura</s>, was established in darkness,
and, together with its houses and with you, was sunk in the ocean-water.

children.text: ulūkaṃ rucirā nārī nagnārūḍhā kharaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A beautiful woman, naked, had mounted an owl, and also a donkey;

children.text: saha strībhirhasantī ca cumbane pramadā yathā
children.translated_text: laughing together with women, she was like an amorous woman in kissing.
There was a man with a vermilion mark, four-footed and three-eyed.

children.text: yena sā pramadā nunnā ahaṃ caiva vibodhitaḥ
children.translated_text: By him that woman was driven away, and I myself was awakened.
Such a very terrifying woman was seen by me.

children.text: eṣa īdṛśakaḥ svapno dṛṣṭo vai ditinandanāḥ
children.translated_text: Such is the dream that I saw, O sons of <s>Diti</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ kathaṃ hi kaṣṭāya asurāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When such a thing has been seen, how could it not become calamity for the Asuras?

children.text: yadi vo'haṃ kṣamo rājā yadidaṃ vettha ceddhitam
children.translated_text: If I am acceptable to you as king, and if you recognize this as beneficial,
then understand it, with good minds, and you must not resent it.

children.text: kāmaṃ cerṣyāṃ ca kopaṃ ca asūyāṃ saṃvihāya ca
children.translated_text: Set aside desire, jealousy, anger, and spite,

children.text: satye dame ca dharme ca munivāde ca tiṣṭhata ||
children.translated_text: and stand firm in truth, self-restraint, <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), and the teaching of the sages.
Let rites of appeasement be performed, and let <s>Maheśvara</s> be worshiped,

children.text: yadi nāmāsya svapnasya hyevaṃ coparamo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if perhaps in this way there may be a cessation of this dream.
Surely <s>Rudra</s>, the three-eyed god of gods, is angry with us,
for omens of the future are being seen by us Asuras in <s>Tripura</s>.
Avoiding quarrel and cultivating straightforwardness,
await the arising of the dream, and likewise the arising of its appointed time.
Having heard this speech of <s>Maya</s>, the sons of <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>
appeared filled with states of anger and jealousy and headed toward destruction.
Seeing destruction near at hand, the Asuras, possessed by their prosperity,
looked at one another right there with eyes filled with anger.
Then the Dānavas dwelling in <s>Tripura</s>, ruined by fate,

children.text: hitvā satyaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca akāryāṇyupacakramuḥ ||
children.translated_text: abandoned truth and <s>dharma</s> and began to undertake improper deeds.
They hated holy Brāhmaṇas and did not worship the deities.

children.text: guruṃ caiva na manyante hyanyonyaṃ cāpi cukrudhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They did not honor the teacher either, and they became angry with one another.

children.text: kalaheṣu ca sajjante svadharmeṣu hasanti ca
children.translated_text: They attached themselves to quarrels and laughed at their own duties.
They reviled one another, each saying only, "I!"
They spoke loudly to their elders and did not answer when they were honored.
For no reason they became tearful-eyed and agitated.
Curds, parched flour, milk, and wood-apples
they ate at night, and they lay down while unclean with leftovers and wrapped up.
After urinating they sipped water without washing their feet,
and they lay down on beds, devoid of proper purity and conduct.
They shrank from fear, like mice before cats.

children.text: bhāryāṃ gatvā na śudhyanti rahovṛttiṣu nistrapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After going to their wives they did not purify themselves, shameless in private acts.
Though formerly well-conducted, they had come to misconduct.
The dwellers in <s>Tripura</s> oppressed the gods and the ascetics rich in austerity.
Although they were restrained by <s>Maya</s>, they stood close to destruction,
doing only displeasing acts against Brāhmaṇas and seeking quarrels.

children.text: vaibhrājaṃ nandanaṃ caiva tathā caitrarathaṃ vanam
children.translated_text: <s>Vaibhrāja</s>, <s>Nandana</s>, and also the <s>Caitraratha</s> forest,
<s>Aśoka</s>, <s>Varāśoka</s>, and likewise <s>Sarvartuka</s>,
heaven, the dwelling-place of the gods, and the places once subject to the former gods,
they destroyed in anger, along with the groves of the ascetics rich in austerity.
With shrines of the gods and hermitages destroyed, and with worshipers of gods and twice-borns shattered,
the world, overrun by the wicked enemies of the king of the immortals, became like crops attacked by swarms of insects.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When the Dānavas of evil nature had become ill-conducted and corrupt,
when the worlds were being ravaged, and the groves of the ascetics as well,
when living beings were frightened by those sky-goers with their lion-roars,
and when the three worlds were bewildered by fear and had entered dense darkness,

children.text: ādityā vasavaḥ sādhyāḥ pitaro marutāṃ gaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the Fathers, and the hosts of the <s>Maruts</s>,
afraid, came for refuge to <s>Brahmā</s>, the great-grandfather.
They approached <s>Brahmā</s> as he sat on a golden lotus,
bowed, and together spoke to the five-mouthed, four-faced one:
The Dānavas dwelling in <s>Tripura</s>, protected here by your boon,
oppress us like servants; therefore command them, O sinless one.
As swans at the coming of the clouds, or as deer from fear of a lion,
so, from fear of the Dānavas, we wander about, O Grandfather.
The names of our sons, and likewise of our wives,
have been forgotten by us as we are being driven about by the Dānavas, O sinless one.
The breaking of the gods' houses and the destruction of hermitages
are being done by the Dānavas, blinded by delusion, as they wander about.

children.text: yadi na trāyase lokaṃ dānavairvidrutaṃ drutam
children.translated_text: If you do not quickly protect the world, routed by the Dānavas,
through this violence the world will be without gods, without men, and without hermitages.
Thus addressed by the Thirty Gods, <s>Brahmā</s>, the lotus-born Grandfather,
the lord with a moon-like face, replied to the Thirty Gods together with <s>Indra</s>:

children.text: bhayasya yo varo datto mayā matimatāṃ varāḥ
children.translated_text: The boon concerning fearlessness that was given by me, O best of the wise,

children.text: tasyānta eṣa samprāpto yaḥ purokto mayā surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: has now reached the end that I formerly declared, O gods.
And that stronghold of theirs, <s>Tripura</s>, O bulls among the Thirty Gods,
is to be destroyed by the release of a single arrow, not by showers of arrows.

children.text: bhavatāṃ ca na paśyāmi kamapyatra surarṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: And among you, O best of the gods, I do not see anyone here
who could destroy the city together with its Dānavas in a single blow.

children.text: tripuraṃ nālpavīryeṇa śakyaṃ hantuṃ śareṇa tu
children.translated_text: <s>Tripura</s> cannot be destroyed with an arrow by one of slight strength,
apart from <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Maheśāna</s>, the lord of creatures.

children.text: te yūyaṃ yadi anye ca kratuvidhvaṃsakaṃ haram
children.translated_text: Therefore, if you and the others agree, let us together beseech <s>Hara</s>, the destroyer of sacrifices;

children.text: yācāmaḥ sahitā devaṃ tripuraṃ sa haniṣyati ||
children.translated_text: that god will destroy <s>Tripura</s>.

children.text: kṛtaḥ purāṇāṃ viṣkambho yojamānāṃ śataṃ śatam
children.translated_text: The width of the cities was made a hundred yojanas by a hundred,

children.text: yathā caikaprahāreṇa hate vai bhavena tu
children.translated_text: so that they might indeed be struck down by <s>Bhava</s> with a single blow,
when, joined with the conjunction of <s>Puṣya</s>, they come together in a single moment.

children.text: tato devaiśca samprokto yāsyāma iti duḥkhitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the distressed gods, being addressed, said, 'We shall go,'
and the grandsire, together with them, came to the assembly of <s>Bhava</s>.
They saw that <s>Bhava</s>, lord of beings past and future, <s>Giriśa</s>, the trident-bearer,

children.text: paśyanti comayā sārdhaṃ nandinā ca mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>Umā</s> and with the great-souled <s>Nandin</s>.
He was fire-colored, the unborn god, with eyes like fire-pits,
shining like a thousand fires and suns, adorned with fire-colored ornaments,
marked with a portion of the moon, with a face gentler than the moon.
Having approached that unborn god, that <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
they praised <s>Śambhu</s>, the lord of beings, the boon-giver, the husband of <s>Pārvatī</s>.
The gods said:

children.text: namo bhavāya śarvāya rudrāya varadāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Bhava</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Rudra</s>, and to the boon-giver;
ever to the lord of beasts, to the fierce one, and to the matted-haired one.
To <s>Mahādeva</s>, to the terrible one, to the three-eyed one, and to the peaceful one;
to <s>Īśāna</s>, remover of fear; homage to the slayer of <s>Andhaka</s>.
To the blue-necked, terrible creator, praised by the creator;
to the destroyer of <s>Kumāra</s>'s enemy and to the father of <s>Kumāra</s>.
To the very red one, the smoky one, the excellent one, and the crusher;
always to the blue-crested one, the trident-bearer, the one who reclines divinely.
To the serpent-formed one, the three-eyed one, whose seed is golden treasure;
to the inconceivable one, husband of <s>Ambikā</s>, praised by all the gods.
To him whose banner bears the bull, to the shaven-headed one, the matted-haired one, the celibate;
to him performing austerity in the water, devoted to Brahman, unconquered;
to the self of the universe, creator of the universe, who stands enveloping the universe;
homage to the one of divine form, to the source, to divine <s>Śambhu</s>.
To the approachable one, the desirable one, the one always worthy of praise and worship;
to him who is always compassionate to devotees and grants what is in their mind.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The god <s>Maheśvara</s>, being praised by the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>,
said this to <s>Prajāpati</s>: 'Where is the great fear of the gods?

children.text: bho devāḥ svāgataṃ vo'stu brūta yadvo manogatam
children.translated_text: O gods, welcome to you. Speak what is in your mind.

children.text: tāvadeva prayacchāmi nāstyadeyaṃ mayā hi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I will grant it at once; indeed there is nothing that I cannot give you.

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ nitarāṃ śaṃ vai kartāhaṃ vibudharṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: I will bring about exceeding welfare for you, O best of the wise gods,
for I practice great and very fierce austerity, even the supreme one.

children.text: vidviṣṭā vo mama dviṣṭāḥ kaṣṭāḥ kaṣṭaparākramāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are hated by you are hated by me: harmful foes of harsh valor.

children.text: teṣāmabhāvaḥ saṃpādyo yuṣmākaṃ bhava eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Their nonexistence must be accomplished, and your well-being as well.'
Thus addressed affectionately by the god, the gods together with <s>Brahmā</s>
spoke to the greatly fortunate <s>Rudra</s>, all of them entitled to their sacrificial shares:
'Blessed lord, fierce austerity has been practiced by those Asuras of fierce valor;

children.text: asurairvadhyamānāḥ sma vayaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: being afflicted by the Asuras, we have come to you for refuge.
A son of <s>Diti</s> named <s>Maya</s>, O three-eyed one, fond of strife,
made that inaccessible <s>Tripura</s>, with white towers.
Taking shelter in that inaccessible city, the Dānavas, fearless because of their boon,
harass us, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, as one harasses a servant who has no master.

children.text: udyānāni ca bhagnāni nandanādīni yāni ca
children.translated_text: The gardens, including <s>Nandana</s> and the others, have been broken down,
and all the excellent Apsarases, beginning with <s>Rambhā</s>, have been carried off by the Danujas.
The riding elephants of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Añjana</s>, and <s>Vāmana</s>,
including <s>Airāvata</s>, have been seized from the deities, O <s>Maheśvara</s>.
And the tawny steeds, foremost those of <s>Indra</s>'s chariot, have been carried off by the Asuras;
they have become the chariot-yoked horses of the Dānavas.

children.text: ye rathā ye gajāścaiva yāḥ striyo vasu yacca naḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever chariots, elephants, women, and wealth were ours,

children.text: tanno vyapahṛtaṃ daityaiḥ saṃśayo jīvite punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all that has been taken from us by the Daityas, and now there is doubt about our very lives.'
The three-eyed one, thus addressed by the gods with <s>Śakra</s> at their head,
the god of gods, the boon-giver, the bull-mounted lord, said to the gods:
'Let your great fear born of the Dānavas depart, O gods.

children.text: tadahaṃ tripuraṃ dhakṣye kriyatāṃ yadbravīmi tat ||
children.translated_text: I shall burn that <s>Tripura</s>; let what I say be done.
If you wish that city, together with its people, to be burned by me,
prepare a suitable chariot for me. Why are you sitting still?'
Thus addressed by the sky-clad one, the gods together with the grandsire
said 'So be it' to <s>Mahādeva</s> and made a supreme chariot.
They made the earth the support, and the two pole-pieces were both attendants at <s>Rudra</s>'s side;

children.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ śiro merorakṣo mandara eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the base was the summit of <s>Meru</s>, and the axle was <s>Mandara</s> itself.

children.text: cakruścandraṃ ca sūryaṃ ca cakre kāñcanarājate
children.translated_text: They made the moon and the sun the two wheels, one golden and one silver,
and the dark fortnight and the bright fortnight, both fortnights, O lords,
the gods headed by <s>Brahmā</s> made into the two rims of the chariot.
These deities also made the paired starting-parts and the mechanism of the fortnights as the apparatus.
It was bound around by the two Nāgas <s>Kambala</s> and <s>Aśvatara</s>.
<s>Bhārgava</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Budha</s> and <s>Aṅgāraka</s>,
and likewise <s>Śanaiścara</s> there - all those best of the gods -
made the sky the beautiful enclosure of that chariot.
They made it two-tongued and many-eyed, with three bamboo-poles, and golden,
and covered with jewels, pearls, and sapphires, attended by eight-faced gods.
The <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the <s>Sindhu</s>, the <s>Śatadru</s>, the <s>Candrabhāgā</s>, the <s>Irāvatī</s>,

children.text: vitastā ca vipāśā ca yamunā gaṇḍakī tathā ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>Vitastā</s>, the <s>Vipāśā</s>, the <s>Yamunā</s>, and likewise the <s>Gaṇḍakī</s>,

children.text: sarasvatī devikā ca tathā ca sarayūrapi
children.translated_text: the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the <s>Devikā</s>, and also the <s>Sarayū</s>,

children.text: etāḥ saridvarāḥ sarvā veṇusaṃjñā kṛtā rathe ||
children.translated_text: all these best rivers were made, on the chariot, into the parts called <s>veṇu</s>.

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭrāśca ye nāgāste ca veśyātmakāḥ kṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: The nāgas called <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭras</s> were made into binding elements,

children.text: vāsukeḥ kulajā ye ca ye ca raivatavaṃśajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those born in <s>Vāsuki</s>'s family and those of the line of <s>Raivata</s>,
those serpents, filled with pride and not deficient in the bow-cases and quivers,
stood there as arrows, with auspicious faces of many kinds.
<s>Surasā</s>, <s>Saramā</s>, <s>Kadrū</s>, <s>Vinatā</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>,
and thirst, hunger, all terrible powers, death, and likewise the all-subduer,
the slaying of a brahmin, the slaying of a cow, the slaying of a child, and terrors to creatures,
became maces and spears, and then approached the chariot of the gods.
Here the yoke was the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>; the rites employing the four hotṛ-priests,
and the four varṇas, graceful and wearing golden earrings, came into being.
That yoke, resembling an age of the world, was set upon the head of the chariot,
bound firmly by the mighty great nāga <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>.
The <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and further the <s>Yajurveda</s>,
these very four Vedas became the four horses.
Whatever gifts there are, headed by the gift of food,
those became, by the thousands, the ornaments of those steeds.
The two <s>Padmas</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
these nāgas became the fastenings for the horses' tails.
Those rites born from the <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the mantras, sacrifices, kratus, and ritual acts,
the remedies for troubles, and the animal-binding iṣṭis as well,
these were the sacrificial fittings on that auspicious chariot of the world,
adorned by the thousands with jewels, pearls, and coral.
The goad was the <s>Oṃkāra</s> itself, and its tip was the utterance <s>Vaṣaṭ</s>.

children.text: sinīvālī kuhū rākā tathā cānumatiḥ śubhā
children.translated_text: <s>Sinīvālī</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>, <s>Rākā</s>, and likewise auspicious <s>Anumati</s>
became the harnesses of the horses, taking forms that held them back and guided them.
Then black, yellow, white, and madder-red,
and bright banners came into being, driven by the wind.
A bow was made from the six seasons, and the year became its bow,
while <s>Ajarā</s>, also called <s>Sāmbikā</s>, became the firm bowstring of that bow.

children.text: kālo hi bhagavānrudrastaṃ ca saṃvatsaraṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: For blessed <s>Rudra</s> is Time, and they know that year as him;
therefore <s>Umā</s>, as <s>Kālarātri</s>, became the ageless bowstring of the bow.
The arrow with which the three-eyed god burned <s>Tripura</s> together with what it contained
was made of the three deities <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Agni</s>.
Its mouth was <s>Agni</s>, and its barb was <s>Soma</s>, dispeller of darkness;
then the holder of the discus was the gathered energy and splendor of that arrow.
And for the increase of its power, <s>Vāsuki</s>, king of nāgas,
released exceedingly poisonous poison, so that splendor might dwell in it.

children.text: kṛtvā devā rathaṃ cāpi divyaṃ divyaprabhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus made the chariot, divine through divine power, the gods
approached the lord of the worlds and spoke these words:
"This chariot has been prepared by us for you, O conqueror of the Dānava enemies;
it is a rescue from danger for the gods, with <s>Indra</s> at their head."
<s>Śaṃkara</s> praised that best chariot of the three worlds, shaped like the peak of <s>Meru</s>,
and, saying "Good, good" to the gods, looked upon the chariot.
Again and again he looked at the chariot and repeatedly said, "Good, good,"
and the lord of the immortals himself spoke to the immortals together with <s>Indra</s>:
"Since this chariot has been prepared for me in such a form by you, O excellent ones,
let a driver equal to such a chariot and its equipment be appointed quickly."
When the god of gods had spoken thus, the gods, as if pierced by arrows,
fell into great anxiety, saying, "How is this to be done?"

children.text: mahādevasya devo'nyaḥ ko nāma sadṛśo bhavet
children.translated_text: "What other god could be equal to <s>Mahādeva</s>
apart from the god who bears the discus? Yet he too has taken refuge in this arrow."

children.text: dhuri yuktā ivokṣāṇo ghaṭanta iva parvataiḥ
children.translated_text: Like bulls yoked to a pole, as if struggling with mountains,
all the gods sighed and said, "How can this be?"
Among the gods the god of gods addressed those who had gone to the pole of the lord of the world:
"I am the charioteer," he said; then the first-born took hold of the horses.
Then a great lion-roar was made by the gods together with the gandharvas,
when they saw <s>Brahmā</s>, goad in hand, having become the charioteer.
And when the grandsire was standing on the chariot, the blessed lord of all,

children.text: sadṛśaḥ sūta ityuktvā cāruroha rathaṃ haraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s>, saying, "The charioteer is fitting," mounted the chariot.
As the god mounted the chariot, the horses, distressed by <s>Hara</s>'s weight,
fell to the ground on their knees and swallowed mouthfuls of dust.
Then the god saw those Vedas, who as fierce horses were overcome with fear,
and, grieved, lifted up those distressed fathers like a good son.
Then again there arose a lion-roar, terrible like the chariot itself,
and the gods' cry of victory came forth, like the ocean.
Then the boon-giving lord, the self-born one, took the goad made of <s>Oṃkāra</s>
and set the horses in motion as swiftly as he could, after instructing them.
As if devouring the sky and as if stealing away the earth,
they released breaths from their mouths like exhaling serpents.
Urged on by the self-born one and driven by the matted-haired god,
those swift horses went like the winds at the time of destruction.
For the raising and fashioning of the banner, the peerless banner-staff
was mounted by <s>Nandī</s>, the bull, who stood upon it by <s>Śiva</s>'s will.
The two gods <s>Bhārgava</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>, staffs in hand and radiant like the sun,
But the two, desiring what was dear to <s>Rudra</s>, guarded the wheels of the chariot.
And <s>Śeṣa</s>, the blessed serpent, <s>Ananta</s>, destroyer of enemies,
with arrow in hand, then guarded the chariot, the couch of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Yama</s> swiftly mounted his very terrible buffalo,
the lord of wealth mounted a serpent, and the lord of the gods mounted an elephant.

children.text: mayūraṃ śatacandraṃ ca kūjantaṃ kiṃnaraṃ yathā
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s>, the boon-giver, mounted the peacock marked with a hundred moonlike spots,
crying out like a <s>Kiṃnara</s>, and the age-ending chariot of his father.
And blessed <s>Nandīśvara</s>, blazing, took up his trident,
behind and on both sides, like one who brings about the destruction of the world.
The <s>Pramathas</s>, with the appearance of fire-colored forms, like immovable flames with fire,

children.text: anujagmū rathaṃ śārvaṃ nakrā iva mahārṇavam ||
children.translated_text: followed <s>Śarva</s>'s chariot, like crocodiles following the great ocean.
<s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, rich in austerity,
and blessed <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, then <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and the great seers headed by <s>Parāśara</s> and <s>Agastya</s>,
praised <s>Hara</s>, the unconquered and unborn one, with special utterances adorned in varied ways.
The chariot, together with the golden mountain, went toward <s>Tripura</s>, like a winged mountain in the sky.
The hosts of <s>Pramathas</s>, resembling elephants, mountains, suns, and clouds, roaring with the sound of rainclouds filled with water,

children.text: pramathagaṇāḥ parivārya devaguptaṃ rathamabhitaḥ prayayuḥ svadarpayuktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: surrounded the god-protected chariot and went forth on every side, filled with their own pride.
Like the ocean greatly swollen at the dissolution, surrounded by makaras, timis, and timiṅgilas,
the excellent chariot, exceedingly radiant, went on with the sound of thunderbolts falling and clouds resounding.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
While that chariot was being honored by the worlds and the god stood upon the chariot,
while the <s>Pramathas</s> roared fiercely and cried out, 'Well done!',
while the great bull bellowed with the sound of <s>Īśvara</s>'s voice,

children.text: jayatsu vipreṣu tathā garjatsu turageṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: while the brahmins shouted victory and the horses thundered,
the divine seer, lordly <s>Nārada</s>, rose up from the battlefield,
and, like the moon in radiance, quickly came to the city <s>Tripura</s>.

children.text: autpātikaṃ tu daityānāṃ tripure vartate dhruvam
children.translated_text: Surely a portentous sign was occurring among the Daityas in <s>Tripura</s>,
for blessed <s>Nārada</s>, rich in austerity, had appeared there.
When the cloud-like one had arrived, all the Dānavas assembled,
and, seeing <s>Nārada</s>, rose up, speaking words of greeting.
With arghya, water for the feet, and the madhuparka, the lords
honored <s>Nārada</s> as <s>Vāsava</s> would honor <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ sa pūjāṃ pūjārhaḥ pratigṛhya tapodhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having accepted their worship, he who was worthy of worship, rich in austerity,
<s>Nārada</s> sat comfortably on a supreme golden seat.
When <s>Nārada</s>, of <s>Nārada</s>'s line, was seated at ease, <s>Maya</s>,
the lord of the Dānavas, sat with the Dānavas according to rank.
Then, seeing <s>Nārada</s> seated, <s>Maya</s>, the great Asura,
pleased, with hair bristling and eyes delighted, spoke these words:
'In our city a portent exists such as nowhere else,

children.text: vartate vartamānajña vada tvaṃ hi ca nārada ||
children.translated_text: O knower of what is present; tell us, <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: dṛśyante bhayadāḥ svapnā bhajyante ca dhvajāḥ param
children.translated_text: Frightening dreams are seen, and the standards are badly broken;

children.text: vinā ca vāyunā ketuḥ patate ca tathā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: and without wind a banner likewise falls to the ground.
Watchtowers dance, together with their banners and gateway towers,

children.text: hiṃsa hiṃseti śrūyante giraśca bhayadāḥ pure ||
children.translated_text: and frightening voices are heard in the city, saying, Strike! Strike!
I do not fear the gods, even with <s>Indra</s>, <s>Nārada</s>,
except for the single boon-giving <s>Sthāṇu</s>, <s>Hara</s>, who grants safety to his devotees.
Blessed one, nothing about portents is unknown to you, sinless one.
You know truly both what is yet to come and what has passed.
Therefore tell us, best of sages, this source of fear,
made known by the portents, for one who has taken refuge, <s>Nārada</s>.'
Thus addressed by <s>Maya</s>, who was free from affliction, <s>Nārada</s> replied.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
'Listen, Dānava, in truth, how portentous signs come to be.
The verbal root dhṛ is taught in the sense of supporting and also in the sense of greatness;
because it supports and because of its greatness, this is called <s>dharma</s>.
Teachers teach that <s>dharma</s> brings about the attainment of what is desired;
the other, whose fruit is undesired, is not taught by teachers.
If one should come from a wrong path to the path, and again from the path to a false way,
the knowers of the Veda know that his destruction is thereby indicated.
You, mounted on the chariot of <s>adharma</s>, together with these intoxicated Dānavas,
are giving aid to those who do harm to the gods.
Therefore these and similar signs, announced by portents,
are seen as destructive for the Dānavas likewise.
This <s>Rudra</s>, having mounted the great chariot made of the worlds,
is coming to destroy <s>Tripura</s>, <s>Maya</s>, and you Asuras too.

children.text: sa tvaṃ mahaujasaṃ nityaṃ prapadyasva maheśvaram
children.translated_text: Therefore always take refuge in mighty <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: yāsyase saha putreṇa dānavaiḥ saha mānada ||
children.translated_text: Then, giver of honor, you will go on with your son and with the Dānavas.
Having thus announced the great danger that had come upon the Dānavas,
the divine one then went back to the place of the lord of gods.

children.text: nārade tu munau yāte mayo dānavanāyakaḥ
children.translated_text: When the sage <s>Nārada</s> had gone, <s>Maya</s>, leader of the Dānavas,
the Dānava, spoke to the Dānavas: 'This alone is what heroes approve.

children.text: śūrāḥ stha jātaputrāḥ stha kṛtakṛtyāḥ stha dānavāḥ
children.translated_text: You are heroes, you have sons born, you have accomplished what had to be done, Dānavas.

children.text: yudhyadhvaṃ daivataiḥ sārdhaṃ kartavyaṃ cāpi no bhayam ||
children.translated_text: Fight with the gods; fear must not be ours.
After conquering, we shall all become members of the assembly of the immortals;
having slain the gods together with <s>Indra</s>, we Asuras shall enjoy the worlds.
And so stand on the watchtowers, weapons in hand;
armored, arrayed for battle, stand with weapons raised.'
O Dānavas, remain in your proper stations in these three cities;
for the cities may become vulnerable to being crossed and attacked.

children.text: namogatāstathā śūrā devatā viditā hi vaḥ
children.translated_text: The sky-going deities, brave ones, are indeed known to you;
they must be carefully warded off and pierced with arrows.
Having thus spoken these words to the sons of <s>Danu</s> about warding off the hosts of gods,
King <s>Maya</s> suddenly entered that city of <s>Tripura</s>, where the minds of the young women were dejected.
Then, with a disposition purified like silver, he worshiped <s>Bhava</s>, the sky-clad lord, with excellent praises,
and went for refuge to the god of gods, the destroyer of <s>Madana</s>, <s>Andhaka</s>, and the sacrifice's body.

children.text: mayamabhayapadaiṣiṇaṃ prapannaṃ na kila bubodha tṛtīyadīptanetraḥ
children.translated_text: The three-eyed blazing one did indeed recognize <s>Maya</s>, who had come seeking the gift of fearlessness;

children.text: tadabhimatamadāttataḥ śaśāṅkī sa ca kila nirbhaya eva dānavo'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: then the moon-crested lord granted what he desired, and that Dānava became fearless indeed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then <s>Nārada</s> again approached the army of the gods in battle;
and, having come from <s>Tripura</s>, he himself stood in the assembly.
That broad and extended region is known as <s>Ilāvṛta</s>,

children.text: yatra yajño balervṛtto baliryatra ca saṃyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: where <s>Bali</s>'s sacrifice took place and where <s>Bali</s> was restrained.
It is famed in the three worlds as the birthplace of the gods,
where their marriages, sacrifices, birth-rites, and other ceremonies were performed.

children.text: devānāṃ yatra vṛttāni kanyādānāni yāni ca
children.translated_text: There the rites of the gods took place, and the gifts of maidens that were made;

children.text: reme nityaṃ bhavo yatra sahāyaiḥ pārṣadairgaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: there <s>Bhava</s> always delighted with his attendants, servants, and gaṇas.
There the guardians of the worlds always stood, as on Mount <s>Meru</s>.
Then <s>Maheśvara</s>, with honey-brown eyes and adorned with the moon as an ornament,
spoke to the lord of the gods and to the chiefs of the gaṇas:
O <s>Vāsava</s>, this <s>Tripura</s> of your enemies is visible,
adorned with aerial cars, banners, and standards.
This event has arisen, this renowned city, intensely scorching like fire;
and these people, mountain-like, wear earrings and crowns.
The Dānavas stand on the ramparts, gateways, towers, and inner courts;
and these sons of <s>Danu</s>, cloud-like and deformed in face,
come out before the city, armed and eager for victory.

children.text: sa tvaṃ suraśataiḥ sārdhaṃ sasahāyo varāyudhaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore you, together with hundreds of gods, with allies and excellent weapons,
and with my own attendants who support you, must slay the great Asuras.
And I, standing firm like an unmoving mountain on my excellent chariot,

children.text: puraḥ purasya randhrārthī sthāsyāmi vijayāya vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: shall stand before the city, seeking an opening in it, for your victory.

children.text: yadā tu puṣyayogeṇa ekatvaṃ sthāsyate puram
children.translated_text: But when, under the conjunction with <s>Puṣya</s>, the city becomes one,
then I shall burn it up with a single arrow, O <s>Vāsava</s>.
Thus addressed here by the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of the gods

children.text: yayau tattripuraṃ jetuṃ tena sainyena saṃvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went to conquer that <s>Tripura</s>, surrounded by that army.
They set forth with terrible chariots, together with the gods and the hosts of attendants,
filled with lion-roars, like clouds rising upward.
At that roar the Dānavas, eager for battle, sprang up from <s>Tripura</s>;
armed, they rushed and moved through the sky against the lords of the gaṇas.
Some, roaring like rain-clouds, became equal to rain-clouds;
the haughty ones sounded their instruments with lion-roars.
The lion-roar of the gods and the great sound of all the musical instruments
were swallowed up by the noises of the Daityas, as the moon is swallowed by rain-clouds.
As the ocean swells on the full-moon day, produced by the moonrise,
so <s>Tripura</s> swelled with great Asuras of terrible form.
There in the city, on the ramparts, and elsewhere on the gateways,
some climbed the towers and cried out in agitation.
Heroes wearing golden garlands, their hands and garments shining,
some Danujas roared like water-drunk clouds.
Some, with garments tossed up, ran here and there;
taking shelter in their houses, they asked one another, What is this?
I do not know what this is; my understanding has vanished.
You will know soon, for the time is vast and unfolding.
That one there too, solid as the essence of earth and lion-like, has mounted a chariot
and stands oppressing <s>Tripura</s> like a disease risen up in the body.

children.text: ya eṣo'sti sa eṣo'stu kā cintā sambhrame sati
children.translated_text: Whoever he is, let him be; what worry is there when alarm has arisen?

children.text: ehi āyudham ādāya kva me pṛcchā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Come, take up a weapon; where will there be any questioning by me?
Thus, agitated among themselves and each replying after another,
the Dānavas dwelling in <s>Tripura</s> approached and questioned one another then.
The Daityas in the city called <s>Tārakākhyapura</s>, with <s>Tārakākṣa</s> at their head,
came out quickly in anger, like great serpents from a hole.
As those Daityas rushed out, they were checked by the troop-leaders of the Pramatha lords,
as lordly elephants are checked by troops of lions.
Then, of those proud ones, like proud fires,
their forms blazed like fires being blown.
Then, drawing great bows that sounded terribly everywhere,
they struck one another with arrows that fed on life.
Seeing again and again the attendants, with dreadful faces like cats and wild beasts and with deformed features,
the Dānavas laughed loudly at the richness of their appearance.
The arrows, released from bows drawn by arms shaped like iron clubs,
entered the warriors' armor like birds into ponds.

children.text: mṛtāḥ stha kva nu yāsyadhvaṃ haniṣyāmo nivartatām
children.translated_text: You are dead! Where indeed will you go? Turn back; we shall kill you.
Having spoken such harsh words to the bull-like attendants, the Dānavas
split them with sharp arrows, as the sun's rays split clouds.
The Pramathas too, lion-eyed and moving with lion-like stride,
With fragments of rock, stones, and trees they split apart the Daityas and Dānavas.
Like the sky crowded with clouds, or crowded with swans,
that whole city shone, utterly crowded with Dānavas.
The lords of the Daityas, their bows drawn, created a dreadful autumn day,
like rain-clouds making bad weather with rainbows marked upon their breasts.
Struck by arrows again and again, those lords of the gaṇas
poured out the essence of their bodies, like mountains yielding golden ore.
And with trees, stones, thunderbolts, spears, lances, and axes,
the Daityas, when struck, were crushed like glass struck by a hammer.
As the ocean swells at the rising of the moon on the full-moon night,
so <s>Tripura</s> swelled forth with great Asuras of terrible form.
"This <s>Tārakākhya</s> is victorious!" the Daityas cried out;
and the lords of the gaṇas cried in turn, "<s>Indra</s> is victorious, and <s>Rudra</s> too!"
In that ocean of forces, warriors checked and torn open by arrows
roared like clouds heavy with water in the rainy season.
With severed hands, heads, standards, and pale parasols,
the battlefield became dreadful, filled with flesh and blood.
Leaping suddenly into the sky to the height of a palm tree, with excellent weapons,
Dānavas and Pramathas alike, firmly struck, fell down again.
The Siddhas, Apsarases, and Cāraṇas, moving in the sky,
delighted by the heavy blows, cried, "Good! Good!"
And the divine drums in the air, though not struck,
sounded with the roar of clouds, like enraged śarabhas.
In that <s>Tripura</s>, the Daityas, like rivers into the lord of streams,
entered with angry faces, like serpents entering an anthill.
In that city of <s>Tārakākhya</s>, brave gods from every side,

children.text: saśastrā nipatanti sma sapakṣā iva bhūdharāḥ ||
children.translated_text: armed with weapons, fell upon it like mountains with wings.
The lords of the gaṇas fought in the three divisions of <s>Tripura</s>,
while <s>Vidyunmālī</s> and <s>Maya</s> were plunged in battle like trees in flood.
That Daitya lord <s>Vidyunmālī</s>, with a splendor like the king of mountains,
took up a terrible iron club and struck <s>Nandin</s>.
That <s>Nandin</s>, struck hard by the Dānava lord with the iron club,

children.text: bhramate madhunā vyaktaḥ purā nārāyaṇo yathā ||
children.translated_text: reeled plainly, as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> once did from <s>Madhu</s>.
When <s>Nandīśvara</s> had fallen into that state, the chiefs of the gaṇas, famous for valor,
rushed forward, stirred to fury, against the Asura <s>Vidyunmālī</s>.
<s>Ghaṇṭākarṇa</s>, <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>, and <s>Mahākāla</s>, attendants of the lord,
then all the gaṇa-chiefs, the gaṇas and their leaders, with arrows
he pierced again and again, those greatest lords of the gaṇas.
Having pierced them again and again, he roared loudly like a cloud in the sky.
At the sound begun by him, <s>Nandin</s>, radiant as the sun,
regained consciousness, and then he too rushed at <s>Vidyunmālī</s>.
Then the blazing thunderbolt given by <s>Rudra</s>, bright as flaming fire,
he hurled at the Dānava whose limbs were like adamant.
Released from <s>Nandin</s>'s arm and adorned with pearls,

children.text: papāta vakṣasi tadā vajraṃ daityasya bhīṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: that dreadful thunderbolt then fell upon the Daitya's chest.
The Daitya, struck by the thunderbolt, though like one made of adamant,
fell as a mountain falls when struck by <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt.
Seeing the lord of the Daityas slain by <s>Nandin</s>, delight of his clan,
the Dānavas cried out, and the chiefs of the gaṇas rushed forward.
Afflicted with grief, resentment, and anger when <s>Vidyunmālī</s> had fallen,
they poured down a great rain of trees and mountains, as clouds pour water.
The lords of the gaṇas, oppressed by heavy mountains and rocks,

children.text: kartavyaṃ na viduḥ kiṃcid vandyamādhārmikā iva ||
children.translated_text: did not know at all what should be done, like irreligious men being reproved.
Then the glorious Asura chief, the powerful one named <s>Tārakākhya</s>,
appeared equal in form to mountains together with their trees.
The gaṇa-chiefs, their heads split and their faces marked by broken feet,
shone like serpents being restrained by spells, in whatever way they could.
The lords of the gaṇas, being struck by <s>Maya</s> through the power of illusion,
wandered about in great confusion, like birds in a cage.
Then the glorious Asura chief, the powerful one named <s>Tārakākhya</s>,
burned the whole army like fire burning dry fuel.
At that time the gaṇas were checked by showers of arrows from <s>Tārakākhya</s>.
Struck down by <s>Maya</s>'s magic and by <s>Tārakākhya</s>'s arrows,

children.text: gaṇeśā vidhurā jātā jīrṇamūlā yathā drumāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lords of the gaṇas became distressed, like trees with aged roots.
Again fire, planets, crocodiles, serpents,
great mountains, lions, tigers, trees, and beasts of tawny hue came rushing down.
Śarabhas with eight legs, waters, and wind as well,
<s>Maya</s>, by the power of magic alone, kept casting down upon his enemies.

children.text: te tārakākhyena mayena māyayā saṃmuhyamānā vivaśā gaṇeśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: Bewildered by <s>Tārakākhya</s> and by <s>Maya</s>'s illusion, those helpless lords of the gaṇas
could not stir even in thought, like the objects of the senses restrained by a sage.
Assailed by great waters, fire, and the rest, together with elephants and serpents, and by mighty lions, tigers, bears, hyenas, and Rākṣasas,
and deluded by darkness, they longed for footing as men would in the midst of the sea.
While the lords of the gaṇas were being crushed and the enemies of the gods were roaring,

children.text: tataḥ surāṇāṃ pravarābhirakṣituṃ riporbalaṃ saṃviviśuḥ sahāyudhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, to protect the foremost of the gods, they entered the enemy's army with their weapons.
<s>Yama</s>, armed with his mace, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, and likewise <s>Kumāra</s>, accompanied by ten million immortals,

children.text: svayaṃ ca śakraḥ sitanāgavāhanaḥ kulīśapāṇiḥ suralokapuṃgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Śakra</s> himself, riding a white elephant, thunderbolt in hand, foremost of the world of gods,

children.text: sa coḍunāthaḥ sasuto divākaraḥ sa sāntakas tryakṣapatir mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: and the lord of the stars, the Sun with his son, and the greatly radiant three-eyed lord together with <s>Antaka</s>,

children.text: ete ripūṇāṃ prabalābhirakṣitaṃ tadā balaṃ saṃviviśurmadoddhatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these, exultant with pride, then entered that army, though it was powerfully guarded by enemies.

children.text: yathā vanaṃ darpitakuñjarādhipā yathā nabhaḥ sāmbudharaṃ divākaraḥ
children.translated_text: As proud lordly elephants enter a forest, as the Sun enters the sky covered with clouds,

children.text: yathā ca siṃhairvijaneṣu gokulaṃ tathā balaṃ tattridaśair abhidrutam ||
children.translated_text: and as a herd of cattle in lonely places is attacked by lions, so that army was assailed by the thirty gods.
Then the attendants broke that army of Dānavas, which was wretched and distressed from the blows it had received,

children.text: svarjyotiṣāṃ jyotir ivoṣmavān harir yathā tamo ghorataraṃ narāṇām ||
children.translated_text: as the hot-rayed light among the heavenly lights dispels a darkness most terrible for men,

children.text: viśāntayāmāsa yathā sadaiva niśākaraḥ saṃcitaśārvaraṃ tamaḥ
children.translated_text: and as the moon always brings to rest the accumulated darkness of night.

children.text: tato'pakṛṣṭe ca tamaḥprabhāve astraprabhāve ca vivardhamāne ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the power of darkness had been drawn away and the power of the weapons was increasing,
a great lion-roar was raised for a moment by the guardians of the quarters and worlds and by the leaders of the gaṇas.
In the battle, the distorted ones were broken, maimed, with their best heads cut off and their limbs filled with arrows.

children.text: devetarā devavarairvibhinnāḥ sīdanti paṅkeṣu yathā gajendrāḥ
children.translated_text: The enemies of the gods, split apart by the best of the gods, sank like mighty elephants in mud.

children.text: vajreṇa bhīmena ca vajrapāṇiḥ śaktyā ca śaktyā ca mayūraketuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt-handed one struck with a dreadful thunderbolt, and the peacock-bannered one with his spear,

children.text: daṇḍena cogreṇa ca dharmarājaḥ pāśena cogreṇa ca vārigoptā
children.translated_text: and <s>Dharmarāja</s> with his fierce staff, and the guardian of the waters with his fierce noose.

children.text: śūlena kālena ca yakṣarājo vīryeṇa tejasvitayā sukeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The lord of the yakṣas attacked with a trident and with deathly force, and <s>Sukeśa</s> with valor and brilliance.
Those lords of the gaṇas, resembling the gods and shining like fire sprinkled with full oblations,
were destroying the hosts of Danu's sons just like falling thunderbolts of <s>Indra</s>.
But <s>Maya</s>, striking with an arrow <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Umā</s>'s son, the best of gods and protector of the gods,

children.text: śareṇa bhittvā sa hi tārakāsutaṃ sa tārakākhyāsuram ābabhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: pierced that son of <s>Tāraka</s>; then he addressed the Asura called <s>Tāraka</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā prahāraṃ praviśāmi vīraṃ puraṃ hi daityendrabalena yuktaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Having delivered a blow, O hero, I shall enter the city, accompanied by the force of the Daitya lord.
After gaining rest, which restores vigor, I shall again make war on those who have attacked us.
For our bodies are torn and wounded by weapon cuts; our weapons, banners, armor, and mounts are shattered.
Your lords of the gaṇas, seeking victory and shining with victory, are rulers favored by the best of the worlds.'
Hearing the words of <s>Maya</s> in the sky, the one called <s>Tāraka</s>, his eyes like blood, desiring battle,

children.text: viveśa tūrṇaṃ tripuraṃ diteḥ sutaiḥ sutairadityā yudhi vṛddhaharṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: swiftly entered <s>Tripura</s> with the sons of <s>Diti</s>, while the sons of <s>Aditi</s> grew joyful in battle.
Then <s>Hara</s>'s army, terrible with conches, kettledrums, and bherī-drums, and with lion-roars, appeared resplendent,
following <s>Maya</s>, dreadful, deep, and cavernous, as if filled with the roar of lions.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: mayaḥ prahāraṃ kṛtvā tu māyāvī dānavarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: After making his attack, <s>Maya</s>, the master of magic and bull among Dānavas,
swiftly entered <s>Tripura</s>, like a dark cloud entering the sky.
He sighed long and hot, and, looking at the Dānavas gathered in the middle,

children.text: dadhyau lokakṣaye prāpte kālaṃ kāla ivāparaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he pondered, when the destruction of the worlds had arrived, like another <s>Kāla</s> himself.
'<s>Indra</s> too fears him when he stands in front, eager for battle;

children.text: sa cāpi nidhanaṃ prāpto vidyunmālī mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and even the greatly renowned <s>Vidyunmālī</s> has met his death.

children.text: durgaṃ vai tripurasyāsya na samaṃ vidyate puram
children.translated_text: There is no city equal to this fortress of <s>Tripura</s>,

children.text: tasyāpyeṣo'nayaḥ prāpto na durgaṃ kāraṇaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: yet disaster has come even upon it; a fortress is never the cause of safety.

children.text: kālasyaiva vaśe sarvaṃ durgaṃ durgataraṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Everything, even what is fortified and still more difficult to assail, is under the power of Time.

children.text: kāle kruddhe kathaṃ kālāttrāṇaṃ no'dya bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When Time is angered, how will there now be protection for us from Time?
Whatever power exists in the three worlds and among all beings,
all of that is under the control of Time: such is the ordinance of <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
What strategy could prevail against this immeasurable one who cannot be withstood?

children.text: laṅghane kaḥ samarthaḥ syādṛte devaṃ maheśvaram ||
children.translated_text: Who would be able to overstep him, except the god <s>Maheśvara</s>?
I do not fear <s>Indra</s>, nor <s>Yama</s>, nor <s>Varuṇa</s>, nor the lord of wealth.

children.text: svāmī caiṣāṃ tu devānāṃ durjayaḥ sa maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the master of these gods, that unconquerable <s>Maheśvara</s>, is to be feared.
The fruit of lordship and the fruit of sovereignty, whatever it is,
that I shall show today, while heroes stand on every side.
I shall create a reservoir filled with nectar-water and excellent herbs.
Then the Daityas will live again by means of the best life-restoring herbs.'
Having so reflected, mighty <s>Maya</s>, best of magicians,
by his magic created a reservoir, as <s>Pitāmaha</s> once created <s>Rambhā</s>.
It was two yojanas long and a full yojana wide,
provided with ascents and crossings, and variegated in form like a painted tale.
With smooth water, scented like nectar and resembling the rays of the moon,
it was filled with supreme water, like a woman filled with virtues.
It was covered with blue lotuses, white lotuses, red lotuses, and flocks of kādamba birds,
and enclosed by formidable embankments shining with the colors of the moon and sun.
It was filled with birds of sweet cries and lovely golden radiance,
as though thronged with seekers of pleasure, like a fire-drill for living beings.

children.text: tāṃ vāpīṃ sṛjya sa mayo gaṅgāmiva maheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having created that reservoir, <s>Maya</s>, like <s>Maheśvara</s> creating the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
first washed <s>Vidyunmālin</s> in it.

children.text: sa vāpyāṃ majjito daityo devaśatrur mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: That Daitya, mighty enemy of the gods, when plunged in the reservoir,
rose at once like a sacrificial fire kindled by fuel.
Making a respectful añjali to <s>Maya</s>, the one called <s>Tāraka</s> offered reverence;
and <s>Vidyunmālī</s>, rising up, spoke these words to <s>Maya</s>:

children.text: kva nandī saha rudreṇa vṛtaḥ pramathajambukaiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Where is <s>Nandī</s> with <s>Rudra</s>, surrounded by the <s>Pramathas</s> and jambuka-like attendants?

children.text: yudhyāmo 'rīn viniṣpīḍya dayā deheṣu kā hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let us fight the enemies and crush them. What compassion should we have for bodies?
After confronting <s>Rudra</s> himself, we shall become powerful.'
or, slain by them in battle, we shall become food for <s>Yama</s>.
Hearing this forceful speech of <s>Vidyunmālin</s>, <s>Maya</s>
embraced him, and with moist eyes the great Asura said this:
'<s>Vidyunmālin</s>, I do not desire my kingdom, nor life itself,
without you, mighty-armed great Asura; what use is anything else?
This pool, truly made of great amṛta, lord of māyā,
has been created by illusion for the Dānavas and Daityas, increasing the life of those who have been slain.

children.text: diṣṭyā tvāṃ daitya paśyāmi yamalokād ihāgatam
children.translated_text: By good fortune I see you, Daitya, come here from <s>Yama</s>'s world.
Today, after being seized by calamity's ruin, we shall enjoy a great treasure.'

children.text: dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ vāpīṃ māyayā mayanirmitām
children.translated_text: Seeing again and again that pool made by <s>Maya</s> through māyā,
the lords of the Daityas, with delighted faces and eyes, spoke these words:
'Let the Dānavas now fight fearlessly with the pramathas.
The pool made by <s>Maya</s> will bring the slain back to life.'

children.text: tataḥ kṣubdhāmbudhinibhā bherī sā tu bhayaṃkarī
children.translated_text: Then that terrifying war-drum, like the agitated ocean,

children.text: vādyamānā nanādoccai rauravī sā punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: being beaten, roared loudly, again and again with a hellish sound.
Hearing the dreadful roar of the drum, like the onset of clouds,
the Asuras swiftly rushed down from <s>Tripura</s>, eager for battle.
With armlets of iron, silver, and gold, adorned with jewels,
with earrings, necklaces, and lofty crowns put on,
smoking without cease, as if they were blazing fires,
taking up weapons, shining and firm in valor,

children.text: nṛtyamānā iva naṭā garjanta iva toyadāḥ
children.translated_text: like actors dancing, like clouds roaring,

children.text: karocchrayā iva gajāḥ siṃhā iva ca nirbhayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: like elephants with raised trunks, and like fearless lions,

children.text: hradā iva ca gambhīrāḥ sūryā iva pratāpitāḥ
children.translated_text: deep as lakes, scorching as suns,

children.text: drumā iva ca daityendrāstrāsayanto balaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: and like trees, the Daitya lords frightened that great army.
The pramathas too, full of zeal, swooping down like <s>Garuḍa</s> in attack,
eager to fight, rushed against the Dānavas, enemies of the Dānavas.
The pramathas under <s>Nandīśvara</s>, and the Dānavas under one named <s>Tāraka</s>,

children.text: cakruḥ saṃhatya saṃgrāmaṃ codyamānā balena ca ||
children.translated_text: joined together and made battle, urged on by force.
With swords shining like the moon, with tridents tawny like fire,
and with arrows firmly released, they struck one another.
The forms of the arrows being loosed and of the swords being hurled
were like great firebrands falling from the sky.
With hearts split by spears, fallen as if by pitiless ones,
the pramathas and Asuras shrieked as though sunk in hells.
Heads furnished with golden earrings and bearing lofty crowns
fell to the earth like mountain peaks at the end of time.
Cut down by axes, spears, swords, and iron clubs,
those warriors, like great elephants, fell upon the surface of the earth.
The pramathas, suddenly exultant, roared with terrible roars;
other Siddhas performed a wondrous battle-music of the Gandharvas.
'You seem strong, pramatha; you seem proud, Dānava,'
thus uttering words, the warriors bore the burden of battle.
Some followers of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, struck by the Dānavas with iron clubs,
vomited blood from their mouths like mountains pouring forth golden ore.
The Asuras, enemies of the gods, were also struck hard in battle by the pramathas
with iron arrows, trees, and mountain peaks.
Then other foremost Dānavas, urged on by <s>Maya</s> the Dānava,
lifted up those slain Daityas and hurled them into the pool.
And they too, with radiant bodies, like immortals in heaven,
rose up on reaching the pool, with their proper forms, ornaments, and garments restored.
Then some Dānavas, regaining their lives by being thrown into the pool,
slapped their arms, made a lion-roar, and then the Asuras charged.
'Dānavas, advance upon these pramathas! Why are you standing still?
For even if you are slain, the pool will bring you back to life again.'
Hearing this, <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>, like a fierce seizer in speech,
quickly came to the lord of gods and spoke these words:
'Slain, slain by the pramathas, god, these Asuras
rise again, terrible, like crops sprinkled with water.
In this city, it is said, there is a pool filled with the water of amṛta-juice;

children.text: nihatā nihatā yatra kṣiptā jīvanti dānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the slain Dānavas are thrown there, they live.'
While <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> was thus informing the god <s>Maheśvara</s>,
very terrible portents occurred in the army of the Dānavas.
<s>Tāraka</s>, with very dreadful eyes and a gaping mouth, like <s>Hari</s>,
rushed in great anger toward the chariot of <s>Mahādeva</s>.
In <s>Tripura</s> a great and terrible sound of drums and conches arose,
when the Dānavas saw the god on the chariot of the god of gods.
There was an earthquake there, and the great chariot sank into the earth;
seeing the disturbance, <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Svayambhū</s>, the grandsire, were troubled.
Accompanied by those two best of gods, that supreme chariot,
reaching a place without support, sank like a virtuous man without a refuge.
Like a body when its elements are exhausted, or like a little water in summer,

children.text: śaithilyaṃ yāti sa rathaḥ sneho viprakṛto yathā ||
children.translated_text: the chariot grew slack, like affection that has been wronged.
Then <s>Ātmabhū</s>, leaping from the chariot, with great strength
raised up the sinking supreme chariot, which had the three worlds as its form.
Then, springing forth from the arrow, yellow-robed <s>Janārdana</s>,
taking on the form of a great bull, seized the chariot that was hard to hold.
With his two horns the great chariot-warrior grasped that chariot, the three worlds itself,
and bore it up, ready, as a bearer of a family bears his family.
The Daitya lord called <s>Tāraka</s> too, like a winged lord of mountains,
then charged at the god <s>Brahmā</s> and struck him.
Struck by the one called <s>Tāraka</s>, he set the goad down upon the yoke-pole,
and <s>Brahmā</s> blazed up again and again, sending breath out from his mouth.
There a great and terrifying roar was raised by the Daityas and by the Dānavas,
like a thundercloud, in honor of the one called <s>Tāraka</s>.
Then in the great battle <s>Keśava</s>, with the chariot-wheel in hand, in the form of a bull and honored by the lord of bulls,

children.text: dititanayabalaṃ vimardya sarvaṃ tripurapuraṃ praviveśa keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: crushed the whole army of <s>Diti</s>'s sons and entered the city of <s>Tripura</s>.
He drank that whole reservoir, adorned as if with rain-clouds and rich with blooming white lotuses, blue lotuses, and lotuses,
that nectar-like water, as the sun drinks up the dense blind darkness gathered in the night.
Having drunk the reservoir of the Asura lords, yellow-robed <s>Janārdana</s>,
the mighty-armed one, roaring, then entered the arrow.
Then the Asuras, struck by the fearsome lords of hosts, with rivers of blood swollen by blows,

children.text: parāṅmukhā bhīmamukhaiḥ kṛtā raṇe yathā nayābhyudyatatatparairnaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: were turned away in battle by the grim-faced ones, as by men intent upon an advancing stratagem.

children.text: sa tārakākhyas taḍinmālireva ca mayena sārdhaṃ pramathairabhidrutāḥ
children.translated_text: That one called <s>Tāraka</s>, <s>Taḍinmālin</s> as well, and <s>Maya</s> with them, were assailed by the Pramathas;

children.text: puraṃ parāvṛtya nu te śarārditā yathā śarīraṃ pavanodaye gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: pierced by arrows, they turned back toward the city, as toward a body when the wind rises.
The lords of hosts, shining with uplifted pride, <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Nandīśvara</s>, and <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> in battle,
roared loudly and laughed in their arrogance: 'Together with <s>Candra</s> and the guardians of the quarters, we shall conquer.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Broken in battle by the Pramathas, those enemies of the gods, the Tripura demons,
entered the city in fear, its gate-towers shattered by the Pramathas.

children.text: śīrṇadaṃṣṭrā yathā nāgā bhagnaśṛṅgā yathā vṛṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Like serpents whose fangs are broken, like bulls whose horns are broken,

children.text: yathā vipakṣāḥ śakunā nadyaḥ kṣīṇodakā yathā ||
children.translated_text: like birds without wings, like rivers whose water is exhausted,
so the Daityas were almost dead, their faces distorted by the deities,
and they became dejected, saying, 'What is to be done?'
Then lotus-faced <s>Maya</s>, seeing them dejected in mind at that time,
that Daitya, the supreme lord of the Daityas, spoke to the Daityas.

children.text: kṛtvā yuddhāni ghorāṇi pramathaiḥ saha sāmaraiḥ
children.translated_text: 'After you had fought terrible battles with the Pramathas and the immortals,
and likewise had satisfied the Pramathas in battle together with the immortals,
the fact that you Daityas first fought, but afterward, oppressed by force,
entered the city from fear, being violently crushed by the Pramathas,
plainly means that something unwelcome is being done by the gods; there is no doubt about this,
when, indeed, such greatly fortunate ones enter the forest of the mountain.

children.text: aho hi kālasya balamaho kālo hi durjayaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, the power of Time! Ah, Time is truly hard to conquer,
since the siege of such a fortress has come down upon us.'
As <s>Maya</s> was speaking, roaring like a cloud,
the Daityas became without splendor, like planets at the rising of the moon.
Then the guards of the reservoir came near, like clouds in the sky at the season's turn,
and stood with joined hands as they spoke to <s>Maya</s>, who was like <s>Yama</s>:

children.text: yā sāmṛtarasā gūḍhā vāpī vai nirmitā tvayā
children.translated_text: 'That hidden reservoir, filled with the essence of nectar, which was made by you,
with its lotus-beds stirred up and its lotuses crowded with fish,
has been drunk by someone in the form of a bull, O leader of the Daityas.

children.text: vāpī sā sāmprataṃ dṛṣṭā mṛtasaṃjñā ivāṅganā ||
children.translated_text: That reservoir is now seen like a lifeless woman.'
Hearing the words of the reservoir-guards, that <s>Maya</s>, lord of the Dānavas,
said again and again, 'Alas!' and spoke this to <s>Diti</s>'s sons:

children.text: mayā māyābalakṛtā vāpī pītā tviyaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: 'If this reservoir made by the power of my māyā has been drunk,

children.text: vinaṣṭāḥ sma na saṃdehastripuraṃ dānavā gatam ||
children.translated_text: we are destroyed; there is no doubt, Dānavas, that <s>Tripura</s> is gone.
It used to revive the Daityas slain again and again by the deities;

children.text: pītā vā yadi vā vāpī pītā vai pītavāsasā ||
children.translated_text: if indeed the reservoir has been drunk, then it has surely been drunk by the yellow-robed one.
Who else, apart from unconquered <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the mace-bearer,
could drink the reservoir of nectar-water protected by my māyā?
Even the most secret thing of the Daityas is not unknown to him on earth,

children.text: yatra madvarakauśalyaṃ vijñātaṃ na vṛtaṃ budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: since the skill bound up with my boon has been discovered, though it was not grasped by the wise.
This region is level and pleasant, treeless, with treeless hills;
when it is filled with fresh water, the hosts of Maruts will harass us.
So if you think, 'Stationed upon the ocean's surface,
we shall withstand the great speed of the Pramathas, which is like the wind;
and the undertakings of these foes, in that flooding of the ocean,
will become dispirited, their chariot-road obstructed;
while they fight and strike down enemies, and while the frightened flee,
the ocean, like the sky, will become our refuge,'
having spoken thus, that Daitya <s>Maya</s>, lord of the Daityas, at that time
went quickly with <s>Tripura</s> to the ocean, kinsman of rivers.
In the ocean, deep with water, the excellent city rose up,
and the cities themselves, with their gateway ornaments, came to rest there.
But when <s>Tripura</s> had withdrawn, three-eyed <s>Hara</s>, the enemy of <s>Tripura</s>,
spoke this to the Grandfather, skilled in the doctrine of the Veda:

children.text: pitāmaha dṛḍhaṃ bhītā bhagavandānavā hi naḥ
children.translated_text: 'Grandfather, blessed one, the Dānavas are indeed deeply afraid of us;

children.text: vipulaṃ sāgaraṃ te tu dānavāḥ samupāśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those Dānavas have taken refuge in the vast ocean.

children.text: yata eva hi te yātāstripureṇa tu dānavāḥ
children.translated_text: By the very path by which those Dānavas went with <s>Tripura</s>,

children.text: tata eva rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ prāpayasva pitāmaha ||
children.translated_text: bring the chariot quickly by that same path, Grandfather.'

children.text: siṃhanādaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā devā devarathaṃ ca tam
children.translated_text: Then, making a lion-roar, the gods surrounded that divine chariot,
and, delighted and armed, went to the western ocean.
Then the immortals, surrounding <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Hara</s>, the preceptor of the immortals,
went quickly, roaring, to the ocean, the abode of the Dānavas.
Then, seeing <s>Tripura</s> adorned with beautiful banners, booming with kettledrums and resounding with conches,
the gods, with their various forces, roared like clouds.
Even in the excellent city of the immortals there was a dreadful sound, cavernous with the roar of clouds and drums,
mingled with the cries of the sons of <s>Danu</s>, like an ocean thrown into confusion by answering echoes.
Then the lord of the worlds, the refuge of the gods, whose purpose was well resolved, gave the order for the hunt against the enemy.

children.text: tridaśagaṇapatirhyuvāca śakraṃ tripuragataṃ sahasā nirīkṣya śatrum ||
children.translated_text: For the lord of the hosts of the gods spoke to <s>Śakra</s>, suddenly seeing the enemy stationed in <s>Tripura</s>:
O lord of the hosts of the gods, mark this: the <s>Dānavas</s> have entered the dwelling of <s>Tripura</s>.
Together with <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>, and the lords of the gaṇas, I shall strike it down at once.

children.text: vihitaparabalābhighātabhūtaṃ vraja jaladhestu yataḥ purāṇi tasthuḥ
children.translated_text: Go to the ocean, becoming the force appointed to crush the enemy host, for from there the cities stand.

children.text: sa rathavaragato bhavaḥ samartho hyudadhimagāttripuraṃ punarnihantum ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Bhava</s>, mounted on his excellent chariot and fully capable, went to the ocean to destroy <s>Tripura</s> again.
As the sons of <s>Diti</s> were reckoning thus, they stood above the salt ocean,
attacking <s>Tripura</s>, together with its lord of <s>Dānavas</s>, with showers of arrows, clubs, and thunderbolt-like weapons.
I too, mounted on the best of chariots, O best of the excellent gods, would be at your rear.
For the comfort of you, sinless one, I shall give support to those who have risen up to slay the best of the Asuras.
Urged on by this speech of <s>Bhava</s>, the thousand-eyed one, his body ready for action,
<s>Hari</s>, lotus-eyed and blooming, set out, wishing to destroy the city of <s>Tripura</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then <s>Maghavan</s>, lord of the immortals, went to kill those Asuras,
and all the guardians of the worlds and every leader of the gaṇas went as well.
All the lords, rejoicing, flew up then into the sky.
Moving through the air, they shone like mountains furnished with wings.
They advanced to destroy that city, like diseases advancing against a body.
With the din of conches and great drums, and with small drums and kettledrums too,
