the gods sounded them before the city and were seen by the inhabitants of <s>Tripura</s>.
Saying, '<s>Hara</s> has arrived,' those powerful great Asuras
fell into supreme agitation, like oceans at the time of dissolution.
Hearing the sound of the gods' instruments, the <s>Dānavas</s>, terrible to behold,
roared and repeatedly sounded many kinds of instruments.
Their valor stirred up still more, they committed offenses against one another,
the former gods and the gods striking one another down.
Even amid shouting that seemed alike on both sides, the cutting apart of their bodies
began as an incomparable battle, with a roar made by blows.
They seemed like suns falling, like fires blazing,

children.text: śaṃsanta iva nāgendrā bhramanta eva pakṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: like great serpents hissing, like birds wheeling about,

children.text: girīndrā iva kampanto garjanta iva toyadāḥ ||
children.translated_text: like chief mountains trembling, like rain-clouds thundering.

children.text: jṛmbhanta iva śārdūlāḥ garjanta iva toyadāḥ
children.translated_text: They seemed like tigers stretching themselves, like rain-clouds thundering,
like oceans growing rough with masses of swelling waves.
The great heroic <s>Pramathas</s> and the very mighty <s>Dānavas</s>
fought after becoming immovable, like thunderbolts against great mountains.
Terrible sounds arose from the bows as they were drawn,
as from clouds following upon the end-time, driven by wind in the sky.

children.text: āhuśca yuddhe mā bhaiṣīḥ kva yāsyasi mṛto hyasi
children.translated_text: In the battle they cried, 'Do not be afraid! Where will you go? You are dead indeed.
Strike quickly! I stand here. Come, show your manhood!'

children.text: gṛhāṇa chinddhi bhinddhīti khāda māraya dāraya
children.translated_text: 'Seize! Cut! Split!' and 'Eat! Kill! Tear apart!'
Thus crying out to one another, they went to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Some were cast aside by swords; some were cut down by axes.
Some were crushed by hammers, and some were struck by arms.
Some were slain by spears; some were split open by tridents.
The <s>Dānavas</s>, resembling flowers made of arrows, like mountains with groves,
fell into the ocean water, terrible with crocodiles and timingilas.
As the lifeless opponents of the gods fell, their limbs tightly bound,
a sound arose in the ocean like the roar of rain-filled clouds.
By that sound, the makaras, crocodiles, timis, and timingilas,
intoxicated by the smell of blood, churned the great ocean.
Quarrelling with one another, those beings of dreadful form
wandered about, devouring the <s>Dānavas</s> and their blood.
The timis swallowed the <s>Daityas</s>, together with their chariots, weapons, horses,
and coverings of garments and ornaments, driving the other water-creatures away.
Just as battle was taking place between the Asuras and the <s>Pramathas</s>,
so too the water-creatures made war in the sky and in the water.

children.text: yathā bhramanti pramathāḥ sadaityāstathā bhramante timayaḥ sanakrāḥ
children.translated_text: As the <s>Pramathas</s> and <s>Daityas</s> whirled about, so the timis and crocodiles whirled about.

children.text: yathaiva chindanti parasparaṃ tu tathaiva krandanti vibhinnadehāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as they cut one another apart, so too those with split bodies cried out.
With the gods, Asuras, crocodiles, and timingilas, their wound-mouths streaming the fluid of their limbs,
the region of the sea was made, in a moment, full of bloody water and heaving water.

children.text: pūrvaṃ mahāmbhodharaparvatābhaṃ dvāraṃ mahāntaṃ tripurasya śakraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> pressed hard against the great gate of <s>Tripura</s>, which first appeared like a mountain of great rain-clouds,

children.text: nipīḍya tasthau mahatā balena yukto'marāṇāṃ mahatā balena ||
children.translated_text: and stood there, joined with the great strength of the immortals and with his own great force.
Likewise at the northern gate stood that son born from the body of <s>Hara</s>, colored like the young sun and jambu-gold.
<s>Skanda</s> then mounted the city gate, like the aged sun falling upon the peak of the western mountain.
And <s>Yama</s>, and the god who is lord of wealth, armed with his staff, and the one whose excellent weapon is the noose,

children.text: devāriṇastasya purasya dvāraṃ tābhyāṃ tu tatpaścimato niruddham ||
children.translated_text: But the western gate of that city of the enemies of the gods was blocked by those two.
The god <s>Rudra</s>, enemy of <s>Dakṣa</s>, shining like ten thousand suns, with a radiant divine chariot,
blocked the southern gate of the enemy's city and stood there, the blessed three-eyed lord.
The lofty houses, furnished with gate-towers, golden, and shining like <s>Kailāsa</s> and the moon,

children.text: prahlādarūpāḥ pramathāvaruddhā jyotīṃṣi meghā iva cāśmavarṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: were hemmed in by the pramathas of fearful form, like lights by clouds that rain stones.
Uprooting and again uprooting their houses, with their ranges of hills and terraces,

children.text: prakṣipya prakṣipya samudramadhye kālāmbudābhāḥ pramathā vineduḥ ||
children.translated_text: and hurling them again and again into the middle of the ocean, the pramathas, dark like clouds of destruction, roared.
Those houses were blood-red, joined with whole groves, with clumps of aśoka trees and with cuckoos,

children.text: gṛhāṇi he nātha pitaḥ suteti bhrāteti kānteti priyeti cāpi
children.translated_text: and as the houses were being uprooted, the women cried, 'O lord! O father! O son!' and also 'O brother! O beloved! O dear one!',
uttering many kinds of un-Aryan cries.
When wives and sons were being destroyed and lives lost, and the battle raged fiercely in that city,
the great Asuras, with speed like the ocean, advanced against the lords of the gaṇas, who were wrapped in anger.
There, with axes and stone missiles, and with tridents, thunderbolts, and excellent clubs,
a very dreadful battle began, destroying the dwelling of the body and bound fast by deep enmity.

children.text: anyonyamuddiśya vimardatāṃ ca pradhāvatāṃ caiva vinighnatāṃ ca
children.translated_text: As they crushed one another, rushed forward, and struck each other down,
the sound of the gods and Dānavas arose like that of oceans at the end of an age.

children.text: vraṇairajasraṃ kṣatajaṃ vamantaḥ kopoparaktā bahudhā nadantaḥ
children.translated_text: Vomiting blood ceaselessly from their wounds, reddened by fury, and roaring in many ways,
the lords of the gaṇas and those foremost Asuras fought, sending forth a mighty noise.
The roads in the city, streaked with bloody mud and variegated with broken gold bricks and crystal,

children.text: kṛtā muhūrtena sukhena gantuṃ chinnottamāṅgāṅghrikarāḥ karālāḥ ||
children.translated_text: were made in a moment terrible with severed heads, feet, and hands, though once easy to travel on.

children.text: kopāvṛtākṣaḥ sa tu tārakākhyaḥ saṃkhye savṛkṣaḥ sagirir nilīnaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Tāraka</s>, his eyes covered with anger, hidden in battle with trees and mountains about him,
at that moment wished to guard the best gate, which had been blocked by <s>Bhava</s> of wondrous valor.
There, striking down the beings who had reached the rampart, he, a being of great and wondrous strength,
moved about, proud in the arrogance of his mastered senses; coming out of the city, he roared terribly.

children.text: tataḥ sa daityottamaparvatābho yathāñjasā nāga ivābhimattaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that best of Daityas, mountain-like, as direct as a rutting elephant,
when checked, sought to seize <s>Rudra</s>'s chariot and surged onward like an ocean beyond its shore.

children.text: śeṣaḥ sudhanvā giriśaśca devaścaturmukho yaḥ sa trilocanaśca
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Sudhanvan</s>, the god <s>Giriśa</s>, the four-faced one, and that three-eyed lord

children.text: te tārakākhyābhigatā gatājau kṣobhaṃ yathā vāyuvaśātsamudrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: were shaken in battle when <s>Tāraka</s> came upon them, like oceans under the power of the wind.

children.text: śeṣo girīśaḥ sapitāmaheśaś cotkṣubhyamāṇaḥ sa rathe'mbarasthaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Girīśa</s>, and the lord with the grandsire were thrown into agitation on the chariot standing in the sky;

children.text: bibheda saṃdhīṣu balābhipannaḥ kūjanninādāṃśca karoti ghorān ||
children.translated_text: pressed by force, it split at the joints and made terrible creaking sounds.

children.text: ekaṃ tu ṛgvedaturaṃgamasya pṛṣṭhe padaṃ nyasya vṛṣasya caikam
children.translated_text: Placing one foot on the back of the horse that was the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, and one on the bull,
<s>Bhava</s> stood with bow and arrow raised, watching for the conjunction of that city.
Then, because <s>Bhava</s> set his feet upon the horse and the bull,
their teats and teeth fell out, for they had been pressed by the wielder of the trident.

children.text: tataḥprabhṛti cāśvānāṃ stanā dantā gavāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: From that time onward, the teats of horses and likewise the teeth of cows
became hidden because of that and passed out of sight.
But <s>Tāraka</s>, with dreadful eyes and glances red within with fury,
was tightly hemmed in near <s>Rudra</s> by <s>Nandin</s>, the joy of his lineage.
With a sharp axe, that <s>Nandin</s> carved away at the lord of the Dānavas,

children.text: takṣayāmāsa vai takṣā candanaṃ gandhado yathā ||
children.translated_text: as a carpenter carves fragrant sandalwood.
Struck by the axe, the hero <s>Tāraka</s> rushed, like a śarabha, against <s>Śailādi</s>;
drawing his sword, <s>Tāraka</s> ran at the lord of the gaṇas.

children.text: yajñopavītam ādāya cicheda ca nanāda ca
children.translated_text: He seized the sacred thread, cut it, and roared.
Then a terrible lion-roar and a fearsome sound of conches
were made there by the lords of the gaṇas when <s>Tāraka</s> had been struck down.
Hearing the roar of the pramathas and also the sound of instruments,
<s>Maya</s>, standing nearby, spoke to broad-sided <s>Vidyunmālin</s>.

children.text: bahuvadanavatāṃ kimeṣa śabdo nadatāṃ śrūyate bhinnasāgarābhaḥ
children.translated_text: 'What is this sound of many-mouthed ones roaring, heard like a split ocean?

children.text: vada vacanaṃ taḍinmālin kiṃ kimetadgaṇapālā yuyudhuryayurgajendrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, O <s>Taḍinmālin</s>: what is this? Have the guardians of the gaṇas fought, and have the elephant-lords charged?'
Thus goaded by <s>Maya</s>'s words as by an elephant-hook, that <s>Taḍinmālin</s>, ray-garlanded like the sun,
came to the forefront of the gods' battle and, with great joy, spoke this to the subduer of foes:
'Your <s>Tāraka</s>, firm one, a storehouse of your fame and mighty as <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: sakalasamaraśīrṣaparvatendro yuddhvā yastapati hi tārako gaṇendraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Tāraka</s>, lordly mountain at the head of every battle, is being hard pressed after fighting with the chiefs of the gaṇas.'
Hearing that <s>Tāraka</s>, whose wide eyes were terrible like sun-bright fire, had been crushed,
the pramathas, with all their eyes, hairs, and bodies thrilled with joy, roared like rainclouds.

children.text: iti suhṛdo vacanaṃ niśamya tattvaṃ taḍimāleḥ sa mayaḥ suvarṇamālī
children.translated_text: Hearing the true words of his friend <s>Taḍinmālin</s>, that golden-garlanded <s>Maya</s>,
dark like a mountain of black collyrium at the head of battle, spoke this sentence to <s>Navendumālin</s>:
'<s>Vidyunmālin</s>, this is not the time for us to act with contemptuous ease;
by valor I shall make this city free from misfortune.'
Then angry <s>Vidyunmālin</s> and <s>Maya</s>, lord of <s>Tripura</s>,
together with those great Asuras, very tall and powerful, struck the gaṇas.

children.text: yena yena tato vidyunmālī yāti mayaśca saḥ
children.translated_text: Then wherever <s>Vidyunmālin</s> went, and <s>Maya</s> too...

children.text: tena tena puraṃ śūnyaṃ pramathaiḥ prahṛtaiḥ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: By those pramathas striking in many ways, the city was made empty.
Then, with the booming of yama-drums, varuṇa-drums, and mṛdaṅgas, and with the resounding of paṇavas, ḍiṇḍimas, and bowstrings,
and with clapping hands and lion-roars, the gods worshiped <s>Bhava</s> and then stood in attendance.
The all-pervading lord, worshiped by great sons of <s>Diti</s>, whose splendor was like that of the thousand-rayed sun,
and praised by truth-devoted treasures of tapas, was like the sun when it has reached the peak of the western mountain.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When <s>Tāraka</s> had been slain in battle, <s>Maya</s>, having driven off the pramathas,

children.text: uvāca dānavān bhūyo bhūyaḥ sa tu bhayāvṛtān ||
children.translated_text: again and again spoke further to the Dānavas, who were overcome with fear:
"O lords of the Asuras, now all of you listen to what I say,
to what must be done by me and by you, mighty ones.
At the proper time the Moon will enter <s>Puṣya</s>, O moon-faced ones;
then all of <s>Tripura</s> will become one city for a single instant.
Act fearlessly at that time, and according to the sign announced by the cuckoo.

children.text: sa kālaḥ puṣyayogasya purasya ca mayā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That time of the <s>Puṣya</s> conjunction and of the city has been arranged by me.
At that time, whoever in the city brings about the conjunction,
that powerful god will grind it to powder with a single arrow.

children.text: yo vaḥ prāṇo balaṃ yacca yā ca vo vairitāsurāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever is your life, whatever your strength, and whatever enmity you have, O Asuras,
placing that in your heart, protect this city.
With every breath, turn away completely the one dreadful chariot of <s>Maheśvara</s>,
so that he does not release the arrow.
When we have thus secured the protection even of <s>Tripura</s>,
the heaven-dwellers, helpless, will wait for the <s>Puṣya</s> conjunction.
Hearing this speech of <s>Maya</s>, the Dānavas who dwelt in <s>Tripura</s>
made lion-roars again and again and, like <s>Yama</s>, spoke to <s>Maya</s>:
"With effort we shall all do what you have declared.

children.text: tathā kurmo yathā rudro na mokṣyati pure śaram ||
children.translated_text: We shall act so that <s>Rudra</s> will not release the arrow against the city.
Today we shall go to battle, desiring to kill that <s>Rudra</s>,"
said the sons of <s>Diti</s>, delighted, with the hairs of their bodies standing on end.

children.text: kalpaṃ sthāsyati vā khasthaṃ tripuraṃ śāśvataṃ dhruvam
children.translated_text: "Either <s>Tripura</s>, standing in the sky, will remain for a kalpa, eternal and firm,
or <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s three strides will become devoid of Dānavas.

children.text: vayaṃ na dharmaṃ hāsyāmo yasminyokṣyasi no bhavān
children.translated_text: We shall not abandon the dharma in which you, sir, will yoke us.

children.text: adaivatam adaityaṃ vā lokaṃ drakṣyanti mānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Men will see a world either without gods or without Daityas."
Having thus conferred, those enemies of the gods, delighted within the city,
became joyful at evening and engaged in the conduct of love.
The great jewel, the blessed Moon, wandering at the summit of its rising and repeatedly released into view,
dispelling the darkness, expanded through the sky.
Like a haṃsa in a broad lake adorned with water-lilies,
or like a great lion seated on a peak of beryl,
or like a necklace resting on the broad chest of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
so the Moon, born from the eye of <s>Atri</s>, sank deep into the sky
and shone, making the worlds shine and powerfully pouring forth the essence of moonlight.
When the cool-rayed Moon had risen and the city was filled with moonlight, the Asuras
at evening adorned their houses and themselves gracefully.
In the streets, royal roads, palaces, and houses
lamps shone like campaka flowers, kindled with abundant oil.

children.text: tadā maṭheṣu te dīpāḥ snehapūrṇāḥ pradīpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then in their halls those lamps, full of oil, were lit;
and their wealthy houses, made of every jewel,
as they blazed, made the lamps shine, like planets at moonrise.
With moonbeams gleaming and inner lamps brightly lit,
the darkness in <s>Tripura</s> was consumed, like a family by calamities.
In that city, in the fresh evening, while the Moon laughed aloud in the fresh evening,

children.text: ratyarthino vai danujā gṛheṣu sahāṅganābhiḥ suciraṃ viremuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Danujas, desiring love, sported for a long time in their houses with women.

children.text: vinoditā ye tu vṛṣadhvajasya pañceṣavaste makaradhvajena
children.translated_text: Those five arrows of the bull-bannered god, set in play by the makara-bannered <s>Kāma</s>,
among the Asuras, the foremost Asuras, made their own limbs and their women sweat.

children.text: kalapralāpeṣu ca dānavīnāṃ vīṇāpralāpeṣu ca mūrchiteṣu
children.translated_text: In the sweet prattling of Dānava women, in the swooning strains of vīṇās,

children.text: mattapralāpeṣu ca kokilānāṃ sacāpabāṇo madano mamantha ||
children.translated_text: and in the drunken cries of cuckoos, <s>Madana</s>, holding bow and arrows, churned them.

children.text: tamāṃsi naiśāni drutaṃ nihatya jyotsnāvitānena jagadvitatya
children.translated_text: Swiftly destroying the darkness of night and spreading the world with a canopy of moonlight,

children.text: khe rohiṇīṃ tāṃ ca priyāṃ sametya candraḥ prabhābhiḥ kurute'dhirājyam ||
children.translated_text: the Moon, having met <s>Rohiṇī</s>, his beloved, in the sky, exercised sovereignty with his rays.

children.text: sthitvaiva kāntasya tu pādamūle kācidvarastrī svakapolamūle
children.translated_text: Standing at her lover's feet, one lovely woman, at the base of her cheek,

children.text: viśeṣakaṃ cārutaraṃ karoti tenānanaṃ svaṃ samalaṃkaroti ||
children.translated_text: applied a still more charming ornamental mark, and with it adorned her face.

children.text: dṛṣṭvānanaṃ maṇḍaladarpaṇasthaṃ mahāprabhā me mukhajeti japtvā
children.translated_text: Seeing her face in a round jeweled mirror and murmuring, "This great radiance is born from my face,"

children.text: smṛtvā varāṅgī ramaṇeritāni tenaiva bhāvena ratīmavāpa ||
children.translated_text: that beautiful-limbed woman, remembering the words spoken by her lover, attained passion in that very mood.
Other women, their fine limbs bristling, from passion for love-play with young men and lovers,

children.text: svayaṃ drutaṃ yānti madābhibhūtāḥ kṣapā yathā cārkadināvasāne ||
children.translated_text: went swiftly of themselves, overcome by intoxication, as night comes at the end of the sun's day.

children.text: pepīyate cātirasānuviddhā vimārgitānyā ca priyaṃ prasannā
children.translated_text: One, pierced through by excessive passion, drank deeply; another, pleased, sought her beloved;
and another, long delighted with her lover, became fully delighted in his amorous talk.
With gośīrṣa sandal and yellow sandal, the excellent Asurī women, their eyes marked with paste,
became lovely and beautiful, like golden jars filled with complete nectar.

children.text: kṣatādharoṣṭhā drutadoṣaraktā lalanti daityā dayitāsu raktāḥ
children.translated_text: The Daityas, their lower lips wounded and quickly reddened by passion, sported, attached to their beloveds.
In <s>Tripura</s> they delighted in the murmuring of strings, but again were indifferent to the chatter of women.

children.text: kvacitpravṛttaṃ madhurābhigānaṃ kāmasya bāṇaiḥ sukṛtaṃ nidhānam
children.translated_text: Here and there sweet singing had begun, a well-fashioned treasury of the arrows of <s>Kāma</s>;

children.text: āpānabhūmīṣu sukhaprameyaṃ geyaṃ pravṛttaṃ tvatha sādhayanti ||
children.translated_text: and in the drinking grounds they then performed songs that could be measured by pleasure.

children.text: geyaṃ pravṛttaṃ tvatha śodhayanti kecitpriyāṃ tatra ca sādhayanti
children.translated_text: Some then refined the singing that had begun, and some there won over a beloved woman;

children.text: kecitpriyāṃ samprati bodhayanti saṃbudhya saṃbudhya ca rāmayanti ||
children.translated_text: some now awakened their beloveds, and, awakening them again and again, delighted them.

children.text: dhūtaprasūnaprabhavaḥ subandhaḥ sūrye gate vai tripure babhūva
children.translated_text: When the sun had gone down, a pleasant breeze born from shaken blossoms arose in <s>Tripura</s>,
and the rustling sound of anklets and girdles crowded out the voices of the cuckoos.
One woman, closely embraced by her lover and clasped by her beloved, though the hair on her body had risen,
was like the earth newly sprinkled with water, with lovely sprouts and leaf-buds in the form of tears.
In the excellent palaces of the beautiful women, adorned by the rays of the moon,
the great sounds of their ornaments, transformed into sweetness, became equal to sounds in the abodes of <s>Madana</s>.

children.text: pānena khinnā dayitātivelaṃ kapolamājighrasi kiṃ mamedam
children.translated_text: "Wearied by drinking, beloved, why do you smell this cheek of mine for so long?

children.text: āroha me śroṇimimāṃ viśālāṃ pīnonnatāṃ kāñcanamekhalāḍhyām ||
children.translated_text: Mount this broad hip of mine, full and high, rich with a golden girdle."
In the streets brightened by the rising moon and on the broad roads like the path of the gods,

children.text: daityāṅganā yūthagatā vibhānti tārā yathā candramaso divānte ||
children.translated_text: the Daitya women, gathered in troops, shone like stars beside the moon at the end of day.

children.text: aṭṭāṭṭahāseṣu ca cāmareṣu preṅkhāsu cānyā madalolabhāvāt
children.translated_text: Amid loud bursts of laughter, fans, and swings, other women, wavering with intoxication,
were swung to and fro with melodious laughter, while the girdle spoke with the subtle sound of its strings.
This was the season of joyful beauties adorned with unfading garlands;

children.text: śrūyanti vācaḥ kaladhautakalpā vāpīṣu cānye kalahaṃsaśabdāḥ ||
children.translated_text: voices like refined silver were heard, and elsewhere, at the tanks, the cries of kalahaṃsas.
The bands of their girdles, together with body-paint, and the moods produced on the swings by that passion
cut open, for those Asura women, the paths to their lovers by means of <s>Manmatha</s>'s arrows.
The variegated garments and loosened masses of hair of the Asura women, swaying to and fro, shone
with beautiful dress and ornaments, like the moon surrounded by clusters of stars.
From the swinging, as they breathed deeply, threads snapped; when girdles slipped, pearls were scattered abroad.
The swing-ground, variegated with them, shone like the regions beside the moon, varied with stars.

children.text: sacandrike sopavane pradoṣe ruteṣu vṛndeṣu ca kokilānām
children.translated_text: At evening, moonlit and with groves nearby, while flocks of cuckoos were calling,
<s>Madana</s>, having found his targets in the city of the Asuras, wandered with his arrows exhausted.

children.text: iti tatra pure'maradviṣāṇāṃ sapadi hi paścimakaumudī tadāsīt
children.translated_text: Thus in that city of the enemies of the immortals there at once came that western moonlight,

children.text: raṇaśirasi parābhaviṣyatāṃ vai bhavaturagaiḥ kṛtasaṃkṣayā arīṇām ||
children.translated_text: as the enemies, soon to be defeated at the front of battle, were brought to destruction by the horses of <s>Bhava</s>.
Then the moon, colored like jasmine flowers and pearl necklaces, lacking its spread of moonlight and cloud-like in hue,

children.text: vichāyatāṃ hi samupetya na bhāti tadvadbhāgyakṣaye dhanapatiśca naro vivarṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became pale and did not shine; in the same way, when his fortune is destroyed, a wealthy man becomes colorless.
The moon's radiance was overcome by the sun, whose charioteer is <s>Aruṇa</s>, whose disk resembled a heated golden chariot-wheel;

children.text: sthitvodayāgramukuṭe bahureva sūryo bhātyambare timiratoyavahāṃ tariṣyan ||
children.translated_text: standing on the crest of the eastern mountain, the great sun shone in the sky, as if about to cross the river of dark waters.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: udite tu sahasrāṃśau merau bhāsākare ravau
children.translated_text: When the thousand-rayed sun, the maker of light, had risen on <s>Meru</s>,
the whole army of the gods roared like the ocean at the end of an age.
Then <s>Hara</s> went toward <s>Tripura</s> together with the thousand-eyed god <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Purandara</s>,
together with <s>Vittada</s> and with <s>Varuṇa</s>.
Those pramathas, of many different forms and exceedingly destructive,
advanced with terrible lion-roars and with the noise of musical instruments too.
Then, with instruments resounding, with parasols and great trees,

children.text: babhūva tadbalaṃ divyaṃ vanaṃ pracalitaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: that divine army became like a forest set in motion.
Seeing that great, terrible army of <s>Rudra</s> rushing forward,
a disturbance among the lords of the Dānavas appeared like the ocean.
They grasped swords, paṭṭiśas, spears, tridents, clubs, and axes,
bows, thunderbolts, and heavy pestles as well.
With eyes reddened by anger, like mountains furnished with wings,
they struck at the mountain-slayer like clouds at the end of the hot season.
Those sons of <s>Diti</s>, together with <s>Vidyunmālin</s>,
the enemies of the gods, rejoicing, came near the gods of gods.
For those whose minds had resolved on death and whose hearts were uncertain about victory,
the army of the powerless was like the limbs of powerless men.
Roaring like clouds, with a brilliance like clouds,
skilled in battle, they fought, each having injured the other.
Smoking and blazing with moon-bright weapons,
whether from anger or from greed for battle, they battered one another.
Some, struck by thunderbolts, fell; others were split by arrows;
others, split apart by discus-weapons, fell into the water of the ocean.
With wreath-strings and necklaces cut away, with garments and ornaments swept off,
pramathas and gods fell among the shoals of timis and makaras.
From maces, pestles, javelins, and axes,
from the falls of thunderbolts, tridents, ṛṣṭis, and paṭṭiśas on every side,
and from mountain peaks and stones hurled by the very wrathful,
from swift Dānavas, smoky and sun-bright,
a great flood of weapons fell even into the flood of the ocean.
There, by those weapons of increased speed, hurled by the hands of gods and Asuras...
A great destruction was being wrought by weapons, while even the stars were terrified.
As destruction befalls small creatures in a battle between two elephants,
so there was destruction of timis and crocodiles amid the hosts of gods and Asuras.
And <s>Vidyunmāli</s>, moving swiftly, like a cloud wreathed with lightning,
with a roar like a dense thundercloud wreathed in lightning, rushed upon <s>Nandīśvara</s>.
Roaring, he, whose face was like darkness, that best of speakers,
the <s>Dānava</s> with the sound of the ocean, spoke to <s>Śailādi</s> in battle:
"I, strong <s>Vidyunmāli</s>, desiring battle, have come.
If now, <s>Nandikeśvara</s>, you escape alive from me,
then, <s>Dānava</s>, the slaying of <s>Vidyunmāli</s> in battle is not accomplished by words."
To that <s>Daitya</s> who spoke thus, <s>Nandīśa</s>, best of the mighty,
spoke there as he struck, skilled in the adornment of speech:
"O <s>Dānava</s>, this is no occasion for those who desire <s>dharma</s>.
Are you able to kill yourself, or do you swell with pride because of the fault of your birth?
If indeed you were previously struck down by me like a beast,

children.text: idānīṃ vā kathaṃ nāma na hiṃsye kratudūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: how now should I not kill one who defiles the sacrifice?
Even one who could cross the ocean with his arms and cast down the sun
would still not be able to look at me with his eyes."
As <s>Nandin</s>, equal to him in strength, was speaking thus there,
the <s>Daitya</s> split him with a single arrow, as the sun splits a cloud with its ray.
That arrow drank the excellent blood from his chest,
as the sun, by its own power, drinks the water of rivers and oceans.
By that well-aimed blow he was first greatly enraged,
and, uprooting a tree with his hand, hurled it like a lordly elephant.

children.text: vāyununnaḥ sa ca taruḥ śīrṇapuṣpo mahāravaḥ
children.translated_text: That tree, driven by the wind, with its flowers scattered and making a great roar,
was cut apart by <s>Vidyunmāli</s>'s arrows and fell like the lord of birds.
Seeing that tree cut apart by the <s>Dānava</s> with excellent arrows,
<s>Nandīśvara</s>, strong in body, summoned up fierce anger.
Raising his arm with a roar, shining like the rays of the sun and of <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: dudrāva hantuṃ sa krūraṃ mahiṣaṃ gajarāḍiva ||
children.translated_text: he ran to kill the cruel one, like a lordly elephant against a buffalo.
As he rushed on swiftly, the swift <s>Vidyunmāli</s>, by force and violence,
filled <s>Nandin</s> with hundreds of arrows.
Then <s>Śailādi</s>, his limbs bristling with arrows,

children.text: arergṛhya rathaṃ tasya mahataḥ prayayau javāt ||
children.translated_text: seized the chariot of that great enemy and sped away swiftly.
Its horses checked, headless, and whirled about in battle, the chariot
fell, like the sun's chariot with <s>Āditya</s>, under a sage's curse.
Then that son of <s>Diti</s>, coming out from within by illusion,
struck <s>Śailādi</s>, who stood firm, with a spear.
Drawing out that very spear, adorned with blood,
the foremost of the <s>Pramathas</s> hurled it at <s>Vidyunmāli</s>.
With his armor split by it and his heart also pierced,
<s>Vidyunmāli</s> fell to the ground like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.
When <s>Vidyunmāli</s> had been slain, the Siddhas, Cāraṇas, and Kiṃnaras,

children.text: sādhu sādhviti coktvā te pūjayanta umāpatim ||
children.translated_text: saying, "Good! Good!" honored <s>Umāpati</s>.

children.text: nandinā sādite daitye vidyunmālau hate mayaḥ
children.translated_text: When the <s>Daitya</s> <s>Vidyunmāli</s> had been brought down by <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Maya</s>,
burned the army of <s>Pramathas</s> like a blazing fire burning a forest.
With their chests torn open by tridents, their heads crushed by maces,
and deeply pierced by arrows, they fell into the ocean of <s>Pramathas</s>.

children.text: atha vajradharo yamo'rthadaḥ sa ca nandī sa ca ṣaṇmukho guhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the bearer of the thunderbolt, <s>Yama</s>, the giver of wealth, <s>Nandin</s>, and six-faced <s>Guha</s>,
having slain their enemies, shook <s>Maya</s>, who had entered upon the valor of an Asura hero, with their finest weapons.

children.text: nāgaṃ tu nāgādhipateḥ śatākṣaṃ mayo vidāryeṣuvareṇa tūrṇam
children.translated_text: But <s>Maya</s> quickly split the elephant of the lord of elephants, the hundred-eyed one, with an excellent arrow,

children.text: yamaṃ ca vittādhipatiṃ ca viddhvā rarāsa mattāmbudavattadānīm ||
children.translated_text: and, piercing <s>Yama</s> and the lord of wealth, roared then like an intoxicated rain-cloud.
Then the <s>Dānavas</s>, struck hard by arrows and by the hosts of <s>Pramathas</s>, and possessing supreme speed and valor,
were, after being deeply pierced, driven into <s>Tripura</s>, as if <s>Śiva</s> himself had been driven in battle by the discus-bearer.
Then conches, kettledrums, war-drums, and mardalas, together with lion-roars, marking the rout of the sons of <s>Danu</s>,

children.text: kapardisainye prababhuḥ samantato nipātyamānā yudhi vajrasaṃnibhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: resounded everywhere in the army of the matted-haired lord, as those thunderbolt-like warriors were being struck down in battle.
Then, when the destruction of the <s>Daitya</s> city was near, the conjunction with <s>Puṣya</s> occurred.
And through that conjunction the three cities also became joined together.
Then the three-eyed <s>Hara</s>, lord of the three paths, quickly released against <s>Tripura</s>
an arrow, threefold and made of the three deities.
By that released arrow, which had a brilliance like the flower of the bāṇa tree,
the sky, golden in appearance, was made as if tinted by the sun.
Having released the triple-divine arrow against <s>Tripura</s>, the god

children.text: dhigdhiṅ māmiti cakranda kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭamiti bruvan ||
children.translated_text: cried out, saying, "Shame on me, shame! Alas, alas!"
Seeing the deity in distress, <s>Śailādi</s> approached like an elephant
and asked <s>Maheśvara</s>, the trident-bearer, "What is this?"
Then the crescent-crested, matted-haired lord, exceedingly pained,

children.text: uvāca nandinaṃ bhaktaḥ sa mayo 'dya vinaṅkṣyati ||
children.translated_text: spoke to <s>Nandin</s>: "He is devoted to me; that <s>Maya</s> will perish today."
Then mighty <s>Nandīśvara</s>, swift as mind and wind,
entered <s>Tripura</s> as the arrow was approaching <s>Tripura</s>.

children.text: sa mayaṃ prekṣya gaṇapaḥ prāha kāñcanasaṃnibhaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Maya</s>, the golden-hued lord of the gaṇas said:
"The terrible destruction of this <s>Tripura</s> has arrived, <s>Maya</s>.
Depart with this very house. I tell you this."
Hearing that word of <s>Nandin</s>, and being firmly devoted to <s>Maheśvara</s>,
he withdrew from <s>Tripura</s> with that very chief house.
That arrow too, like a packet of leaves, burned those three cities,
and the Fire, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> likewise were as if divided threefold.
O best of twice-born men, the cities, surrounded by the heat of the arrow,
burned just as families burn upward because of the fault of a bad son.
Like <s>Meru</s> and <s>Kailāsa</s>, resembling the peaks of <s>Mandara</s>,
with doors and windows, and adorned with offerings,
with lovely mansions and lofty upper chambers,
with waters, renowned halls, and lookout windows,
with fixed banners and flags, and made of gold and silver,
the houses of the <s>Dānavas</s> in that <s>Tripura</s>, in the calamity,
burned by the thousands in the fire, appearing like fire itself.
On the tops of lovely mansions, in woods and pleasure groves,
and others standing at windows and on the levels of the sky,
embraced by their lovers and sporting together with their lovers,
those women of the lords of the <s>Dānavas</s> were indeed burned by the fire.
One woman, unable to go elsewhere after abandoning her beloved,
met destruction and death before her beloved in the mouth of the fire.
Lotus-eyed and tear-eyed, with joined palms, she said:
O carrier of oblations, O scorcher of enemies, I am another man's wife.
As witness of <s>dharma</s> in the three worlds, you ought not touch me here.

children.text: śāyitaṃ ca mayā deva śivayā ca śivaprabha
children.translated_text: I have lain here, O god, in auspiciousness, O auspiciously radiant one;

children.text: pareṇa praihi muktvedaṃ gṛhaṃ ca dayitaṃ hi me ||
children.translated_text: go on to another place, leaving me and this house, for it is dear to me.
One <s>Dānava</s> woman, taking up her young little son,
stood near the fire and spoke thus to the fire:
O <s>Pāvaka</s>, this boy, my little son, was obtained by me through suffering.
You ought not take away this dear one, O you who are dear to <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>.
Some <s>Dānava</s> women, distressed, abandoned their beloveds
and fell into the ocean water, their ornaments jingling.

children.text: tāta putreti māteti mātuleti ca vihvalam
children.translated_text: Crying in confusion, 'Father! Son!' and 'Mother! Maternal uncle!'
the women in <s>Tripura</s> wailed, shaken by the flames of fire.
Just as a mountain fire burns a water-born lotus pond full of lotuses,
so the fire in <s>Tripura</s> burned the lotus-faces of the women.
Just as a mass of frost burns the lotuses of lotus ponds in the cold,
so that very fire burned the face-lotuses and eye-lotuses of the women of <s>Tripura</s>.
From the fall of the arrow-fire, the very delicate women there fled in terror,
and there arose a deeply mingled sound of their girdle-strings, anklets, and cries.
Burned, with their crescent ornaments and platforms, their mansions shattered, with their gateways,

children.text: dagdhāni dagdhāni gṛhāṇi tatra patanti rakṣārthamivārṇavaughe ||
children.translated_text: the burned houses there fell, as if for protection, into the mass of the ocean.
Because of the falling houses, licked by lines of flame, the water in the ocean became heated,

children.text: kuputradoṣaiḥ prahatānuviddhaṃ yathā kulaṃ yāti dhanānvitasya ||
children.translated_text: just as the family of a wealthy man, struck and pierced by the faults of bad sons, comes to ruin.
The ocean water, boiled on every side by the heat of the houses, with its force stirred up,
terrified the timis with the crocodiles, the timingilas, and others likewise, as they were being boiled.
Then that excellent rampart in <s>Tripura</s>, with towers and like the foot of <s>Mandara</s>,

children.text: taireva sārdhaṃ bhavanaiḥ papāta śabdaṃ mahāntaṃ janayansamudre ||
children.translated_text: fell together with those very buildings, producing a great sound in the ocean.

children.text: sahasraśṛṅgair bhavanair yadāsīt sahasraśṛṅgaḥ sa ivācaleśaḥ
children.translated_text: When, because of its thousand-peaked buildings, <s>Tripura</s> had seemed like that thousand-peaked lord of mountains,
it became only a name, assigned as an oblation and food for the fire.

children.text: pradahyamānena pureṇa tena jagat sapātāladivaṃ prataptam
children.translated_text: As that city burned, the world together with <s>Pātāla</s> and heaven was scorched,
and the great, excellent palace of <s>Maya</s> there, after reaching great distress, sank into the water.
Having heard that speech, the lord of the gods, <s>Indra</s>, bearer of the thunderbolt, then
cursed that house of <s>Maya</s>, O son of <s>Aditi</s>.
The house of <s>Maya</s> will be unapproachable, without a secure foundation,
and always surrounded by fear, like fire itself.

children.text: yasya yasya tu deśasya bhaviṣyati parābhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Whichever region is destined for defeat,

children.text: drakṣyanti tripuraṃ khaṇḍaṃ tatredaṃ nāśagā janāḥ
children.translated_text: there people doomed to destruction will see a fragment of <s>Tripura</s>.
That house of <s>Maya</s>, even today, is devoid of <s>Maya</s>.
The sages said:
Blessed sir, tell us the course of <s>Maya</s>,
by means of which house <s>Maya</s> fled, O bowl-born one.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Wherever <s>Dhruva</s> is seen, there the abode of <s>Maya</s> is surely seen.

children.text: devadviṭ tu mayaścātaḥ sa tadā khinnamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Maya</s>, hater of the gods, then with a distressed mind,
having fallen from there into this other world, made it for protection.
There too there are deities, the excellent gods called <s>Āptoryāmas</s>;

children.text: tatrāśaktaṃ tato gantuṃ taṃ caikaṃ puramuttamam ||
children.translated_text: therefore, being unable to go to that one excellent city,
<s>Śiva</s> created a house and gave it to <s>Maya</s> himself, who desired a house.
The thousand-eyed one desisted and worshipped <s>Īśvara</s>.
And all praised <s>Īśvara</s>, the lord of beings, as he was being worshipped.

children.text: sampūjyamānaṃ tridaśaiḥ samīkṣya gaṇairgaṇeśādhipatiṃ tu mukhyam
children.translated_text: Seeing the lord of hosts, the foremost lord of <s>Gaṇeśas</s>, being fully worshipped by the thirty gods and by the hosts,

children.text: harṣād vavalgur jahasuśca devā jagmurnanardustu viṣaktahastāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the gods leapt for joy, laughed, went forth, and roared, their hands joined together.

children.text: pitāmahaṃ vandya tato maheśaṃ pragṛhya cāpaṃ pravimṛjya bhūtān
children.translated_text: Then, having bowed to <s>Pitāmaha</s> and <s>Maheśa</s>, taking up the bow and comforting the beings,

children.text: rathācca saṃpatya hareṣudagdhaṃ kṣiptaṃ puraṃ tanmakarālaye ca ||
children.translated_text: and having leapt down from the chariot, they saw that city burned by <s>Hara</s>'s arrow and cast into the abode of makaras.
Whoever reads this victory of <s>Rudra</s>, which brings victory,
<s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s> grants him victory in his undertakings.

children.text: pitṝṇāṃ vāpi śrāddheṣu ya imaṃ śrāvayiṣyati
children.translated_text: And whoever causes this to be recited at śrāddhas for the ancestors
Its merit would be endless, bestowing the fruit of all sacrifices.
This is an auspicious rite; this is holy; this is a great <s>puṃsavana</s>.

children.text: idaṃ śrutvā paṭhitvā ca yānti rudrasalokatām ||
children.translated_text: Having heard and recited this, they go to the same world as <s>Rudra</s>.
The sages said:

children.text: kathaṃ gacchatyamāvāsyāṃ māsi māsi divaṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: How does the king go to heaven on each new-moon day, month after month?

children.text: ailaḥ purūravāḥ sūta tarpayeta kathaṃ pitṝn
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>, how did <s>Aila Purūravāḥ</s> satisfy the Fathers?
We wish to hear this, the power of that wise one.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: etadeva tu papraccha manuḥ sa madhusūdanam
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s> himself asked <s>Madhusūdana</s> just this,
and he told it to the son of the Sun; understand it from me as it was.
The Fish said:

children.text: tasya cāhaṃ pravakṣyāmi prabhāvaṃ vistareṇa tu
children.translated_text: I shall now declare his power at length,

children.text: ailasya divi saṃyogaṃ somena saha dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: and the heavenly meeting of the <s>Aila</s> with wise <s>Soma</s>.
From <s>Soma</s> came the obtaining of nectar and also the satisfaction of the Fathers,
the Saumyās, the Barhiṣads, the Kāvyas, and the Agniṣvāttas likewise.
When the Moon and the Sun meet among the constellations,
on the new-moon day they dwell in one and the same orb.
Then, on every new moon, he goes to see the maker of day and the maker of night,
his maternal grandfather and paternal grandfather.

children.text: abhivādya tu tau tatra kālāpekṣaḥ sa tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Having greeted those two there, he remains awaiting the proper time.
Then, having honored <s>Soma</s> with effort, he moved onward.
The learned <s>Aila Purūravāḥ</s>, wishing to perform a monthly <s>śrāddha</s>,

children.text: tataḥ sa divi somaṃ vai hyupatasthe pitṝnapi ||
children.translated_text: then attended in heaven upon <s>Soma</s> and also upon the Fathers.

children.text: dvilavaṃ kuhūmātraṃ ca tāvubhau tu nidhāya saḥ
children.translated_text: Setting aside two <s>lavas</s> and a mere measure of <s>Kuhū</s> for those two,
when the observance begins, with a measure of <s>Sinīvālī</s> and a small measure of <s>Kuhū</s>,
knowing the <s>Kuhū</s>-measure as intended for the Fathers, they attend upon <s>Kuhū</s>.
Having attended upon her, he then waits for <s>Soma</s>, expecting the lunar digit.

children.text: svadhāmṛtaṃ tu somādvai vasaṃsteṣāṃ ca tṛptaye
children.translated_text: The <s>svadhā</s>-nectar from <s>Soma</s>, as he dwelt there, was for their satisfaction.
With ten and with five streams of <s>svadhā</s>-nectar,
the delight of those who partake in the dark fortnight is strengthened by the highest rays.

children.text: sadyo'bhikṣaratā tena saumyena madhunā ca saḥ
children.translated_text: At once he, streaming forth with that Soma-born honey,

children.text: nivāpeṣvatha datteṣu pitryeṇa vidhinā tu vai ||
children.translated_text: when the libations had been given according to the ancestral rite,
satisfied the Fathers with the Soma-born <s>svadhā</s>-nectar,
the Saumyās, the Barhiṣads, the Kāvyas, and the Agniṣvāttas likewise.
Fire is remembered by the learned as the season; they know the season as the year.
The seasons were born from him, and from the seasons arose the seasonal divisions.
The Fathers are the seasons; the half-months are to be understood as sons of the seasons.
The grandfathers, however, are the seasons, sons of the new-moon years.

children.text: prapitāmahāḥ smṛtā devāḥ pañcābdā brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The great-grandfathers are remembered as gods, the five-year cycles, sons of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: saumyā barhiṣadaḥ kāvyā agniṣvāttā iti tridhā
children.translated_text: They are remembered as threefold: the Saumya Barhiṣads, the Kāvyas, and the Agniṣvāttas.

children.text: gṛhasthā ye tu yajvāno haviryajñārtavāśca ye
children.translated_text: Those householders who are sacrificers, and those connected with oblation-sacrifices and the seasons,

children.text: smṛtā barhiṣadaste vai purāṇe niścayaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are remembered as those Barhiṣads in the Purāṇa; this is the settled conclusion.
Householders and sacrificers are remembered as the seasonal Agniṣvāttas.
The lords of the Aṣṭakās are the Kāvyas; now understand the five years.
Among them the <s>saṃvatsara</s> is Fire, and the <s>parivatsara</s> is the Sun.
The <s>iḍvatsara</s> is <s>Soma</s>, and the <s>anuvatsara</s> is Wind.
<s>Rudra</s> is their <s>vatsara</s>; these are the five years that have the nature of a yuga.
Established in them by Time, the Moon lets the nectar flow.
These are remembered as connected with divine rites, the drinkers of Soma and the drinkers of heat.
<s>Purūravāḥ</s> satisfied them with that for as long as he lived.
Because <s>Soma</s> is produced especially month after month,
therefore that, laden with <s>svadhā</s>, belongs to the Soma-drinking Fathers.
This is that nectar, <s>Soma</s>, and indeed the honey that he obtained.
Then the Sun, with a single ray,
nourishes <s>Soma</s>, who has drunk the nectar, by means of <s>Suṣumnā</s>, the Soma drunk by the Soma-drinkers.

children.text: niḥśeṣā vai kalāḥ pūrvā yugapad vyāpayan purā
children.translated_text: Formerly all the earlier lunar digits, without remainder, pervaded at once,
portion by portion, day by day, the share of the one being filled by <s>Suṣumnā</s>.

children.text: kalāḥ kṣīyanti kṛṣṇāstāḥ śuklā hyāpyāyayanti ca
children.translated_text: Those dark digits wane, while the bright ones make him increase.
Thus the body of the Moon is nourished by the power of the Sun.
On the full-moon day he is seen bright, with a complete disk.
Thus <s>Soma</s> is nourished in the bright fortnight, day by day.
First the gods drink <s>Soma</s>, whose nectar has been drunk; afterward the Sun drinks him.
For fifteen days the maker of light drinks him with one ray,
while he nourishes him by <s>Suṣumnā</s>, portion by portion, day by day.
When he is being nourished by <s>Suṣumnā</s>, the bright digits increase.

children.text: tasmāddhrasanti vai kṛṣṇāḥ śuklā hyāpyāyayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the dark ones diminish, while the bright ones make him grow full.

children.text: evamāpyāyate somaḥ kṣayite ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Soma</s> is nourished again and again when he has waned.
In this way <s>Soma</s>'s prosperity occurs in the two fortnights, bright and dark.
Thus this <s>Soma</s>, possessing the Fathers, is remembered as having that nourishing essence.
He is beautiful, together with fifteen streams bearing nectar.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi parvaṇāṃ saṃdhayaśca yāḥ
children.translated_text: After this I shall declare the junctions of the lunar phases,
how the phases are tied together, like recurring joints in sugarcane and bamboo.

children.text: tathābdamāsāḥ pakṣāśca śuklāḥ kṛṣṇāstu vai smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: So the year, the months, and the fortnights, bright and dark, are remembered.
The distinctions of the full-moon days are likewise knots and junctions.
The joints of the half-month begin with the second lunar day and the rest.
Because the rites of establishing the sacred fire are conducted at the junctions of the phases,
therefore, at the beginning of a phase, at the junctions beginning with the first lunar day,

children.text: sāyāhne anumatyāśca dvau lavau kāla ucyate
children.translated_text: in the evening the time of <s>Anumatī</s> is said to be two <s>lavas</s>.
The time of <s>Rākā</s> too should be known as just two <s>lavas</s> in the afternoon.
The natural state of the dark fortnight, when the afternoon time has passed,
at evening, on the pratipad, is this time belonging to the full-moon rite.
When the sun stands in vyatipata above the line, there is the interval between yugas;
and when the moon, risen at the yuga-interval, stands above the line,
when one sees the full moon and the vyatipata facing one another,
then those two are situated at that time up to the pratipad.
Fixing on the sun at that time, after observing it, you should calculate it.
That indeed is the proper time for rites; it is called the sixth time.
The full moon, the purnima, is in the bright fortnight at the junctions of night;
therefore on the full-moon night the night-maker becomes full at night.
When, at the junction, one observes by day a full-moon time joined with the other body,
and the moon and sun in the afternoon, it is remembered as Purnima because of fullness.
Because the ancestors approve it together with the gods,
therefore it is named Anumati; because of fullness it is remembered as Purnima.
Because the night-maker shines exceedingly on the full-moon day,
and because of the moon's brightening, poets know it as Raka.
When the moon and the day-maker dwell together in one asterism,
that single fifteenth night is therefore remembered as Amavasya.
When, with that amavasya in view, the two have come together for the darsa,
the moon and sun see one another; because of seeing it is called Darsa.

children.text: dvau dvau lavāvamāvāsyāṃ sa kālaḥ parvasaṃdhiṣu
children.translated_text: Two lavas and two lavas on amavasya: that is the time at the junctions of the parvan;
having two syllables and measuring only a Kuhu, it is remembered as the parvan-time.
But an amavasya whose moon is visible here begins from midday onward;

children.text: divā tadūrdhvaṃ rātryāṃ tu sūrye prāpte tu candramāḥ
children.translated_text: by day above that, but at night, when the sun has arrived, the moon
would rise suddenly together with the sun; therefore it belongs to the morning time.
Coming together for two lavas, as the sun descends from midday,
the moon, as the pratipad of the bright fortnight, comes forth from the solar orb.
Between those two orbs as they are being released,

children.text: sa tadānvāhuteḥ kālo darśasya ca vaṣaṭkriyāḥ
children.translated_text: that is then the time of the anvahuti and the vasat rites of the Darsa;
this parvan at amavasya should be known as the mouth of the season.

children.text: divā parva tvamāvāsyāṃ kṣīṇendau dhavale tu vai
children.translated_text: By day the parvan is amavasya when the moon is waned and pale;
therefore on amavasya by day that sun is taken as the marker.
Because, when the time is completed, it is uttered by the cuckoo as 'kuhu',
this amavasya, designated by that time, is remembered as Kuhu.
When the night-maker is only a waning remnant, of the measure of Sinivali,
and amavasya enters the sun, then it is remembered as Sinivali.
Anumati and Raka, and Sinivali and Kuhu likewise:

children.text: etāsāṃ dvilavaḥ kālaḥ kuhūmātrā kuhūḥ smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: for these the time is two lavas; Kuhu is remembered as having the measure of Kuhu.

children.text: ityeṣa parvasaṃdhīnāṃ kālo vai dvilavaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus this time of the parvan-junctions is remembered as two lavas;
the parvans have equal time, and their oblation and vasat rites are equal.
When the lunar fullness and vyatipata are equal, both full moons are indeed equal;
the parvan-time, when the pratipad has begun, has two measures.
The time of Kuhu and Sinivali, when properly set forth, is remembered as two lavas;
when the moon is within the solar disk, the parvan-time is remembered by kalas.

children.text: yasmād āpūryate somaḥ pañcadaśyāṃ tu pūrṇimā
children.translated_text: Because Soma is filled on the fifteenth day, there is the full moon,
with ten and five kalas, in the sequence of days.

children.text: tasmātpañcadaśe some kalā vai nāsti ṣoḍaśī
children.translated_text: Therefore, on the fifteenth Soma there is no sixteenth kala;
therefore the waning of Soma on the fifteenth has been declared by me to you, O Brahmin.
Thus these ancestors are gods, soma-drinkers, increasers of Soma;
the seasonal periods, the seasons, and then the years are gods, and they foster them.
Hereafter I shall declare the ancestors who eat sraddha offerings,

children.text: teṣāṃ gatiṃ ca sattatvaṃ prāptiṃ śrāddhasya caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: and also their course, their true nature, and the attainment of sraddha.

children.text: na mṛtānāṃ gatiḥ śakyā jñātuṃ vā punarāgatiḥ
children.translated_text: The course of the dead, or their return, cannot be known,
even by perfected tapas; how much less by eyes of flesh.
Here these worldly ancestors are remembered as both gods and ancestors;
by the power of their dharma, Brahmins remember them as attaining union with them.
Or, through the dharma of the asramas, among those established in knowledge,
others here also become pleased by rites performed with faith.
Through chastity, tapas, sacrifice, progeny on earth,
sraddha, knowledge, and the gift of food, in seven ways,

children.text: karmasveteṣu ye saktā vartanty ā dehapātanāt
children.translated_text: those who are attached to these acts and continue until the fall of the body,
together with the gods and ancestors, with the steam-drinkers and the soma-drinkers,
having gone to heaven, rejoice in heaven and attend upon those who possess ancestors.

children.text: prajāvatāṃ prasiddhaiṣā uktā śrāddhakṛtāṃ ca vai
children.translated_text: This has been declared as belonging to men with offspring and to performers of sraddha;

children.text: teṣāṃ nivāpe dattaṃ hi tatkulīnaistu bāndhavaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the offering given for them at the nivapa is indeed given by kinsmen of their family.
Eating the monthly sraddha, these are the Soma-worldly ones beyond those;
these human ancestors are indeed eaters of the monthly sraddha.

children.text: tebhyo'pare tu ye tvanye saṃkīrṇāḥ karmayoniṣu
children.translated_text: But beyond them, those others who are mixed among wombs born of karma,
fallen from the dharmas of the asramas and deprived of svadha and svaha,
after the body is broken, falling into misery, become pretas in <s>Yama</s>'s abode;
lamenting their own deeds, they have come to the place of torment.
Long-limbed, exceedingly dried up, bearded, and without clothing,
overcome by hunger and thirst, they run about here and there,
toward rivers, lakes, ponds, and lotus-pools everywhere,
desiring others' food, being driven about here and there.

children.text: sthāneṣu pātyamānā ye yātanāstheṣu teṣu vai
children.translated_text: Those who are made to fall in those places of torment,
in <s>Salmalī</s>, in <s>Vaitarani</s>, and in <s>Kumbhipaka</s>, and in burning sands.
And in the forest of sword-leaves, being cast down by their own deeds,

children.text: tatrasthānāṃ tu teṣāṃ vai duḥkhitānām aśāyinām ||
children.translated_text: for those who remain there, suffering and sleepless,
when their relatives, by name and lineage,
give three piṇḍas on the ground upon darbha grass turned to the left,
those offerings indeed satisfy the ones who have reached them, stationed in the realms of the pretas.

children.text: aprāptā yātanāsthānaṃ prabhraṣṭā ye ca pañcadhā
children.translated_text: Those who have not reached a place of torment, and those who have fallen away in five ways,
and those who afterwards, through their own deeds, are among the hosts of beings down to immobile forms,
in the many kinds of species, in animal wombs and bodies,
whatever food these beings have in each such womb here,

children.text: tasmiṁs tasmiṃs tadāhāre śrāddhaṃ dattaṃ tu prīṇayet
children.translated_text: a śrāddha offering made in relation to that very food then pleases them,
when it is presented at the proper time, rightly obtained, to a worthy recipient, and according to rule.
They obtain the food that has been given, wherever they are staying.

children.text: yathā goṣu pranaṣṭāsu vatso vindati mātaram
children.translated_text: Just as, when cows have become lost, a calf finds its mother,

children.text: tathā śrāddheṣu dṛṣṭānto mantraḥ prāpayate tu tam ||
children.translated_text: so this is the illustration in śrāddhas: the mantra causes it to reach that person.
Thus <s>Manu</s> declared that a śrāddha, complete and given with faith, is unfailing.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> spoke, seeing with a divine eye,

children.text: gatāgatajñaḥ pretānāṃ prāptiṃ śrāddhasya caiva hi
children.translated_text: knowing the going and coming of the pretas and also the arrival of the śrāddha offering.
For them the dark fortnight is the day, and the bright fortnight is the night for sleep.

children.text: ityete pitaro devā devāśca pitaraśca vai
children.translated_text: Thus these ancestors are gods, and the gods too are ancestors indeed;
these gods and ancestors in heaven are one another's ancestors.

children.text: ete tu pitaro devā manuṣyāḥ pitaraśca ye
children.translated_text: These ancestors are gods, and those who are human ancestors
are the father, the grandfather, and likewise the great-grandfather.
Thus has been stated the domain of the ancestors who drink Soma;
this greatness of the ancestors has been established in the Purāṇa.
Thus this is the meeting of <s>Aila</s> with <s>Soma</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>,

children.text: avāptiṃ śraddhayā caiva pitṝṇāṃ caiva tarpaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and the attainment through faith and the satisfaction of the ancestors.

children.text: parvaṇāṃ caiva yaḥ kālo yātanāsthānameva ca
children.translated_text: The proper time of the sacred lunar junctures, and the place of torment as well,
have been briefly recounted to you; this is the eternal creation.
All that diversity by which this occurs has been told only in part;
it cannot be fully enumerated, and it should be believed by one who desires prosperity.
This creation of the self-born god has been related by me
in detail and in order. What more shall I tell you?
The sages said:
The four yugas that occurred in the former interval of <s>Svāyambhuva</s>,
their natural number too we wish to hear in detail.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In connection with the earth and heaven I explained this earlier;
now I shall tell that four-yuga cycle in this way, so listen.
I shall reckon its measure fully and in detail.
Using the ordinary measure, one should establish the human year;
reckoning by that here too, I shall describe the four-yuga cycle.
There are times equal to a nimeṣa and syllables obtained as mātrās.

children.text: kāṣṭhā nimeṣā daśa pañca caiva triṃśacca kāṣṭhāṃ gaṇayetkalāṃ tu
children.translated_text: Fifteen nimeṣas are a kāṣṭhā, and one should count thirty kāṣṭhās as a kalā;
thirty kalās make a muhūrta, and by thirty of those night and day are joined.
The sun divides day and night in the human worldly reckoning;
night is for the sleep of beings, and day is for the activity of works.

children.text: pitrye rātryahanī māsaḥ pravibhāgas tayoḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: In the ancestral reckoning, a month is day and night; again there is their division:
the dark fortnight is their day, and the bright fortnight is the night for sleep.

children.text: triṃśadye mānuṣā māsāḥ pitryo māsaḥ sa ucyate
children.translated_text: Thirty human months are called an ancestral month.

children.text: śatāni trīṇi māsānāṃ ṣaṣṭyā cābhyadhikāni tu
children.translated_text: Three hundred months, with sixty added,
are this ancestral year when understood by human measure.
By human measure, whatever would be a hundred years,

children.text: pitṝṇāṃ tāni varṣāṇi saṃkhyātāni tu trīṇi vai
children.translated_text: those years of the ancestors are counted as three indeed,

children.text: daśa ca dvyadhikā māsāḥ pitṛsaṃkhyeha kīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: and twelve months are stated here in the ancestral reckoning.

children.text: laukikena pramāṇena abdo yo mānuṣaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The year remembered as human by ordinary measure
is this divine day-and-night: such is the Vedic statement.
In the divine reckoning, day and night are a year; again there is their division:
the day is the northern course, and the night is the southern course.

children.text: ete rātryahanī divye prasaṃkhyāte tayoḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These have been reckoned as the divine night and day; again, of them,

children.text: triṃśadyāni tu varṣāṇi divyo māsastu sa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: thirty years are remembered as a divine month.

children.text: mānuṣāṇāṃ śataṃ yacca divyā māsāstrayastu vai
children.translated_text: And what is a hundred years of humans is three divine months indeed;

children.text: tathaiva saha saṃkhyāto divya eṣa vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too it is reckoned together; this is remembered as the divine rule.
In this way, three hundred years and likewise sixty years
are proclaimed as a divine year by human measure.
Three thousand years by human measure,
and another thirty years, are remembered as the year of the Seven Seers.

children.text: nava yāni sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ mānuṣāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Nine thousand human years
and ninety years are remembered as the year of <s>Dhruva</s>.
Thirty-six thousand human years,
and sixty thousand as well, are enumerated by number;

children.text: divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu prāhuḥ saṃkhyāvido janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: people who know reckoning call this a thousand divine years.
This has been sung by the sages in divine reckoning, O twice-born ones;
by the divine measure itself the number of the yugas is established.
In <s>Bhārata-varṣa</s>, the sages declared four yugas:

children.text: kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliścaivaṃ caturyugam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s>; thus is the four-yuga cycle.
First is the yuga named <s>Kṛta</s>; after that it is called <s>Tretā</s>.
Then one should reckon <s>Dvāpara</s> and <s>Kali</s> as the yugas.
They say that four thousand years make that <s>Kṛta</s> yuga.

children.text: tasya tāv tī saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaśca tathāvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its dawn is of that same measure, and its twilight portion is of the same kind.
In the other three yugas too, together with their dawns and twilight portions,
the thousands and hundreds decrease by one quarter.
Those who know the reckoning of the yugas know the <s>Tretā</s> to be three thousand years.

children.text: tasyāpi triśatī saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaḥ saṃdhyayā samaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For it also the dawn is three hundred, and the twilight portion is equal to the dawn.

children.text: dve sahasre dvāparaṃ tu saṃdhyāṃśau tu catuḥśatam
children.translated_text: The <s>Dvāpara</s> is two thousand years, and its two twilight portions are four hundred.
The <s>Kali</s> is declared to be one thousand years,

children.text: dve śate ca tathānye ca saṃdhyāsaṃdhyāṃśayoḥ smṛte ||
children.translated_text: and likewise two hundred each are remembered for its dawn and twilight portion.
This is called the twelve-thousandfold reckoning of the yugas:

children.text: kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliśceti catuṣṭayam ||
children.translated_text: the fourfold set consisting of <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s>.
Now understand the human years that are established there.

children.text: niyutāni daśa dve ca pañca caivātra saṃkhyayā
children.translated_text: In number, twelve niyutas and five more,
and twenty-eight thousand, are said to be the <s>Kṛta</s> yuga.

children.text: prayutaṃ tu tathā pūrṇaṃ dve cānye niyute punaḥ
children.translated_text: A full prayuta, and again two other niyutas,
together with ninety-six thousand, are counted by number.
This is the reckoning of the <s>Tretā</s> yuga, stated in human measure.
Eight hundred thousand human years
and sixty-four thousand years make the <s>Dvāpara</s> yuga.
Four niyutas of years are the <s>Kali</s> yuga,
and thirty-two thousand more by reckoning.
This <s>Kali</s> yuga has been stated according to human measure.
This condition of the four yugas is proclaimed in human measure.
The reckoning of a caturyuga has been counted together with its dawns and twilight portions.
This period called a caturyuga, when multiplied by a little more than seventy-one,
together with <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, and the others, is called a manvantara.
Now understand the count of a manvantara in human measure.
Thirty-one koṭis are counted in number by the twice-born,
and likewise ten hundred-thousands more in parts,
and thirty-two thousand, plus eight hundred.
There are also eighty years, and six additional months.
This is proclaimed as the reckoning of a manvantara in human measure.
I shall also state the interval of a <s>Manu</s> according to divine measure.

children.text: sahasrāṇāṃ śatānyāhuḥ sa ca vai parisaṃkhyayā ||
children.translated_text: They say it is a hundred thousands, according to exact calculation.
Forty thousand is called the interval of a <s>Manu</s>.
The duration of a manvantara has been proclaimed together with its yugas.
This period called a caturyuga, a little more than seventy-one times over,
when it has revolved in order, is called a manvantara.
Those who know this say that fourteen times this is a kalpa.

children.text: tatastu pralayaḥ kṛtsnaḥ sa tu saṃpralayo mahān ||
children.translated_text: After that comes the complete dissolution; that is the great saṃpralaya.
By number it becomes twice the measure of a kalpa.

children.text: caturyugākhyā vyākhyātā kṛtaṃ tretāyugaṃ ca vai ||
children.translated_text: The period called a caturyuga has been explained, and also the <s>Kṛta</s> and <s>Tretā</s> yugas.
I shall describe what was created in <s>Tretā</s>, and the <s>Dvāpara</s> and <s>Kali</s> as well.

children.text: yugapatsamavetau dvau dvidhā vaktuṃ na śakyate ||
children.translated_text: The two are joined together at the same time and cannot be described separately in two ways.
This pair of yugas, although coming in sequence, has not been told by me to you,
because the order was disturbed by the occasion of the lineage of sages.
What remains has not been told for the <s>Tretā</s> yuga; I shall tell it, so listen.
Now at the beginning of the <s>Tretā</s> yuga, <s>Manu</s> and the <s>Saptarṣis</s>,
urged on by <s>Brahmā</s>, proclaimed the śrauta and smārta <s>dharma</s>.
The śrauta <s>dharma</s>, rich in such matters as marriage, the agnihotra,
and the collections of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, was taught by the <s>Saptarṣis</s>.
<s>Manu Svāyambhuva</s> taught the smārta <s>dharma</s>, transmitted by tradition,
marked by customary practice and joined with the conduct of the varṇas and āśramas.
Through truthfulness, chastity, learning, and austerity,
and through the sage-lineage of those whose austerity was well practiced,
of the <s>Saptarṣis</s> and of <s>Manu</s>, then at the beginning of the <s>Tretā</s> yuga,
those mantras arose without deliberate contrivance, yet once before as well.
They were manifested through visions of stars and the like.

children.text: ādikalpe tu devānāṃ prādurbhūtāstu te svayam ||
children.translated_text: In the first kalpa those mantras had appeared by themselves among the gods.
Then among the established authorities, and among others too,
the joining with mantras proceeds through thousands of past kalpas.
Those same mantras again stood present before them in reflected form.
The ṛcs, yajuses, sāmans, and the Atharvan mantras,

children.text: saptarṣibhiśca ye proktāḥ smārtaṃ tu manurabravīt ||
children.translated_text: were spoken by the <s>Saptarṣis</s>, while <s>Manu</s> taught the smārta tradition.
At the beginning of <s>Tretā</s> the Vedas were gathered together solely as embankments of <s>dharma</s>.
But because of the contraction of lifespan, they are divided in the <s>Dvāpara</s> age.
The sages study the Vedas day and night through austerity.
They are divine, without beginning or end, and were formerly spoken by <s>Svayambhū</s>.
Enclosed within their own <s>dharma</s> and furnished with their ancillary sciences, age after age, according to <s>dharma</s>,
they alter their own <s>dharma</s>, as the Vedic teachings do according to each age.
Ārambha sacrifices are for the kṣatra; oblation sacrifices are remembered for the vaiśya people.
Service sacrifices belong to the śūdras, and recitation sacrifices to the brāhmaṇas.
Then in <s>Tretā</s> the varṇas arose together, possessing <s>dharma</s>,
active in rites, rich in offspring, prosperous, and happy.
The kṣatriyas are regulated by the brāhmaṇas, the vaiśyas by the kṣatriyas,
and the śūdras follow the vaiśyas, through mutual support.
Their dispositions were auspicious, and their dharmas rested on varṇa and āśrama.
By an act conceived in the mind, by speech, or by the work of the hand,
in the <s>Tretā-yuga</s>, when it is unimpaired, the undertaking of ritual action succeeds.
Length of life, beauty, strength, intelligence, health, and devotion to <s>dharma</s>
all this indeed was common to everyone in the <s>Tretā-yuga</s>.
And <s>Brahmā</s> then made for them the arrangement of <s>varṇāśrama</s> (classes and life-stages),
and likewise the <s>Saṃhitās</s>, the mantras, health, and devotion to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: saṃhitāśca tathā mantrā ṛṣibhir brahmaṇaḥ sutaiḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Saṃhitās</s> and the mantras were likewise set forth by the sages, the sons of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: yajñaḥ pravartitaścaiva tadā hyeva tu daivataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and sacrifice too was then set in motion by the deities.
By the <s>Yāmas</s>, the <s>Śuklas</s>, and the <s>Jayas</s>, furnished with every means,
together with the <s>Viśvasṛjs</s> and the greatly powerful lord of the gods, <s>Indra</s>,
those sacrifices had formerly been set in motion by the gods in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> interval.

children.text: satyaṃ japastapo dānaṃ pūrvadharmo ya ucyate
children.translated_text: Truthfulness, muttered prayer, austerity, and giving are called the earlier <s>dharma</s>;
when <s>dharma</s> diminishes, derivative forms of <s>dharma</s> increase.

children.text: jāyante ca tadā śūrā āyuṣmanto mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: Then heroes are born, long-lived and very strong,
who have laid aside punishment, great yogins, sacrificers, and speakers of sacred knowledge.
They have eyes wide like lotus petals, broad faces, and compact bodies;
with lion-like chests, great in spirit, they move like intoxicated elephants.
Great bowmen, they are cakravartins in the <s>Tretā-yuga</s>,
complete in every auspicious mark and rounded like a banyan tree.

children.text: nyagrodhau tu smṛtau bāhū vyāmo nyagrodha ucyate
children.translated_text: The two arms are remembered as banyan-like; the arm-span is called the banyan measure.

children.text: vyāmena sūcchrayo yasya ata ūrdhvaṃ tu dehinaḥ
children.translated_text: For a person whose height is equal to that span, and thereafter,
whose height and circumference correspond, this is called being rounded like a banyan tree.
The wheel, chariot, jewel, wife, treasure, horse, and elephant
were formerly declared to be the seven jewels in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> interval.
Cakravartins are born on earth as portions of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
in all manvantaras, past and future alike.
Among the <s>Tretā-yugas</s> here, those that have been, those that will be, and those that are present,
in them the cakravartins are born.
For those rulers of the earth these auspicious things are discerned,

children.text: atyadbhutāni catvāri balaṃ dharmaṃ sukhaṃ dhanam ||
children.translated_text: four most marvelous things: strength, <s>dharma</s>, happiness, and wealth.
Without mutual opposition they are obtained equally by the king:

children.text: artho dharmaśca kāmaśca yaśo vijaya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: wealth, <s>dharma</s>, desire, fame, and victory as well.
Endowed with lordly power and strength through sovereignty beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>,
and through learning and austerity, they surpass even the sages.
By that strength these kings surpass the <s>Dānavas</s> and human beings,
and they are born with superhuman marks fixed in their bodies.

children.text: keśāḥ sthitā lalāṭena jihvā ca parimārjanī
children.translated_text: Their hair is set at the forehead, and their tongue serves for wiping;
they are dark in radiance, four-tusked, of good lineage, and with seed turned upward.
Their arms reach to the knees, their hands are like palm trunks, and their forms are bull-like;
measured in breadth and size, they are lion-shouldered and intelligent.
On their feet are the wheel and fish, and on their hands the conch and lotus;
they live eighty-five thousand years, free from old age and disease.
The movements of those cakravartins are unobstructed in four ways:
in the sky, in the oceans, in <s>Pātāla</s>, and in the mountains.

children.text: ijyā dānaṃ tapaḥ satyaṃ tretādharmāstu vai smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Sacrifice, giving, austerity, and truth are remembered as the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>Tretā</s>;
then <s>dharma</s> proceeds according to the division of class and life-stage,
and <s>daṇḍanīti</s> (the policy of punishment and rule) is set in motion for establishing boundaries.
All people are joyful, well nourished, free from disease, and complete in mind.
In <s>Tretā</s>, the one four-footed <s>Veda</s> and its ordinance are remembered;

children.text: trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi jīvante tatra tāḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the people there live for three thousand years.
Surrounded by sons and grandsons, they die in due order.
This is the condition in the <s>Tretā-yuga</s>; now understand the reckoning of <s>Tretā</s>.
By the nature of <s>Tretā-yuga</s>, it proceeds with a quarter of twilight,
and the quarter of twilight is the portion which, by its nature, stands as one quarter.
The sages said:
At the opening of the <s>Tretā-yuga</s>, how did sacrifice begin?
Tell us properly about the earlier creation in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> age.
When the twilight had disappeared together with the <s>Kṛta-yuga</s>,
and when the phase called time had begun, when the <s>Tretā-yuga</s> had then arrived,
when plants had arisen and the sending forth of rain had begun,

children.text: pratiṣṭhitāyāṃ vārttāyāṃ grāmeṣu ca pureṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: when livelihood had been established in villages and towns,
after he had established class and life-stage, and again with those mantras,
having gathered the <s>Saṃhitās</s> well, how was sacrifice set in motion?
Having heard this, <s>Sūta</s> said, 'Listen to that which was prompted.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: mantrānvai yojayitvā tu ihāmutra ca karmasu
children.translated_text: Having applied the mantras to rites here and hereafter,
the lord <s>Indra</s>, the enjoyer of all, then set sacrifice in motion.
Together with the deities, having gathered, furnished with every requisite,
the great sages came together at his extended horse sacrifice.
In the sacrificial rite the officiants first proceeded with the ritual action,
while much varied oblation was being offered into the fire, the divine hotṛ.
When the gods were satisfied and the chanters of sāman sang in a fine voice,
and when the swift adhvaryu-men were moving about,

children.text: ālabdheṣu ca madhye tu tathā paśugaṇeṣu vai
children.translated_text: and when the groups of animals had been seized in the middle,
and when the gods, the eaters of the sacrifice, had then been invoked,
those gods whose nature is the senses and who consume shares of the sacrifice,

children.text: tānyajanti tadā devāḥ kalyādiṣu bhavanti ye ||
children.translated_text: the gods then sacrificed those beings who come into existence in the <s>Kali</s> and other ages.
At the time of the adhvaryu's summons the sages also rose up,
and the great sages, seeing those pitiable groups of animals then,
they asked <s>Viśvabhuj</s>, "How can this be your rule of sacrifice?"
"This is powerful <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), violence committed by you out of desire for <s>dharma</s>.
"A new rule concerning animals has been desired by you in your sacrifice, best of the gods.
"By means of animals you have begun <s>adharma</s> for the destruction of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: nāyaṃ dharmo hyadharmo'yaṃ na hiṃsā dharma ucyate
children.translated_text: "This is not <s>dharma</s>; this is indeed <s>adharma</s>. Violence is not called <s>dharma</s>.
"If you wish, let your lordship perform <s>dharma</s> according to scripture,
"by a sacrifice seen in the proper rule, with <s>dharma</s> and without misfortune,
"with sacrificial seeds, best of gods, freed from the three aims of life.
"This great sacrifice, O <s>Indra</s>, was formerly ordained by <s>Svayambhū</s>."
Thus <s>Indra Viśvabhuj</s>, though addressed by the truth-seeing sages,
did not accept it, for he was filled with pride and delusion.
A very great dispute arose between those sages and <s>Indra</s>,
and it was asked whether one should sacrifice with moving beings or with stationary things.

children.text: te tu khinnā vivādena śaktyā yuktā maharṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those great sages, distressed by the dispute and endowed with power,
made an agreement on equal terms with <s>Indra</s> and asked <s>Vasu</s>, who moved in the sky.
The sages said:
"Greatly wise king, how has the rule of sacrifice been seen by you?
"Descendant of <s>Uttānapāda</s>, lord, tell us and remove our doubt."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Hearing their statement, <s>Vasu</s>, without considering the strength and weakness of the case,
recalled the <s>Veda</s> and śāstra and then declared the truth about sacrifice.
"One should sacrifice with what has been brought near in accordance with rule," the king said.
"One should sacrifice with pure animals, and also with roots and fruits.

children.text: hiṃsā svabhāvo yajñasya iti me darśanāgamaḥ
children.translated_text: "Violence is the nature of sacrifice; this is my view and scriptural tradition.
"So too these mantras, marked by violence, have been contemplated by the great sages,
"who were endowed with long austerity and who understood examples such as <s>Tāraka</s>.
"That authority has been stated by me; therefore you ought to be pacified.

children.text: yadi pramāṇaṃ svānyeva mantravākyāṇi vo dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: "If your own mantra-statements are authority, O twice-born ones,

children.text: tathā pravartatāṃ yajño hyanyathā mānṛtaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "then let the sacrifice proceed accordingly; otherwise let there be no false speech."

children.text: evaṃ kṛtottarāste tu yujyātmānaṃ tato dhiyā
children.translated_text: When they had been answered in this way, they joined their minds with understanding;
seeing him as one who must inevitably fall, they then cursed him downward.
As soon as this was said, the king entered <s>Rasātala</s>.
Having been a king who moved above, he became one who moved in <s>Rasātala</s>.
Because of that statement he became a wanderer on the surface of the earth,
King <s>Vasu</s>, the cutter of doubts about <s>dharmas</s>, had gone below.
Therefore a doubt should not be answered by one man, even if he knows much,
for the course of manifold <s>dharma</s> is subtle and hard to follow.

children.text: tasmānna niścayādvaktuṃ dharmaḥ śakyo hi kenacit
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>dharma</s> cannot be spoken with certainty by anyone,
apart from the gods, the sages, and <s>Manu Svāyambhuva</s>.
Therefore there should be no violence in sacrifice, as was declared by the sages of old.
