Hundreds of thousands of crores of sages have gone to heaven through their own austerities.
Therefore the great sages do not praise a violent sacrifice.
The ascetics gave gleaned grain, roots, fruits, vegetables, and a vessel of water,
each according to his capacity, and became established in the world of heaven.
Non-injury, freedom from greed, self-restraint, compassion for beings, tranquility,
chastity, austerity, purity, pity, patience, and firmness
are the very root of eternal <s>dharma</s>, though hard to attain.
Sacrifice consists of substances and mantras, while austerity consists of equanimity.
Through sacrifices one reaches the gods, and again through austerity the <s>Vairāja</s> state.
Through renunciation of action one reaches the realm of <s>Brahman</s>; through detachment, dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>.
Through knowledge one attains <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation/liberation); these five destinations are remembered.
Thus there was a very great dispute over the setting in motion of sacrifice
between the sages and the deities in the former <s>Svāyambhuva</s> age.

children.text: tataste ṛṣayo dṛṣṭvā hṛtaṃ dharmaṃ balena tu
children.translated_text: Then those sages, seeing that <s>dharma</s> had been taken away by force,
disregarded <s>Vasu</s>'s statement and went back the way they had come.
When the groups of sages had departed, the gods obtained the sacrifice.
For kings such as brahmins, kṣatriyas, and others are heard of as perfected by austerity:
<s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Medhātithi</s>, and <s>Vasu</s>,
<s>Sudhāmā</s>, <s>Virajā</s>, and likewise the kings <s>Śaṅkhapād</s> and <s>Rājasa</s>,
<s>Prācīnabarhis</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Havirdhāna</s>, and other kings.

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavaste tapobhirdivaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These and many others went to heaven through their austerities.
They were great-souled royal sages whose fame was established.
Therefore austerity is superior to sacrifice for every reason.
This whole universe was formerly created by <s>Brahmā</s> through austerity.
Therefore one does not attain that through sacrifice; this is remembered as rooted in austerity.
Such was the setting in motion of sacrifice in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> age.
From that time onward this sacrifice has proceeded together with the ages.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi dvāparasya vidhiṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After this I shall again describe the rule of <s>Dvāpara</s>.
There, when the <s>Tretā-yuga</s> has waned, it enters <s>Dvāpara</s>.

children.text: dvāparādau prajānāṃ tu siddhistretāyuge tu yā
children.translated_text: At the beginning of <s>Dvāpara</s>, that perfection of creatures which existed in the <s>Tretā-yuga</s>

children.text: parivṛtte yuge tasmiṃstataḥ sā vai praṇaśyati ||
children.translated_text: perishes when that age has turned away.

children.text: tataḥ pravartite tāsāṃ prajānāṃ dvāpare punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Dvāpara</s> has again begun for those creatures,
there arise greed, firmness, trade, war, and uncertainty about principles.
There is also the collapse of the social classes and the reversal of rites.

children.text: yātrā vadhaḥ paro daṇḍo māno darpo'kṣamā balam ||
children.translated_text: Wandering, killing, harsh punishment, pride, arrogance, impatience, and force arise.

children.text: tathā rajastamo bhūyaḥ pravṛtte dvāpare punaḥ
children.translated_text: So too rajas and tamas become more abundant when <s>Dvāpara</s> has begun again.

children.text: ādye kṛte nādharmo'sti sa tretāyāṃ pravartitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the first <s>Kṛta</s> age there is no <s>adharma</s>; in <s>Tretā</s> it is set in motion.

children.text: dvāpare vyākulo bhūtvā praṇaśyati kalau punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having become confused in <s>Dvāpara</s>, it perishes again in <s>Kali</s>.
In <s>Dvāpara</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>varṇas</s> and also the <s>āśramas</s> become mixed.
And in that age a twofold division arises in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>.
<s>Śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> become twofold, and certainty is not attained.
Because certainty is not understood, the truth of <s>dharma</s> is not found.
For when the truth of <s>dharma</s> is not known, division of opinion arises.
They are mutually divided through the confusion of their views.
Therefore, by those whose views are divided, this has been made very confused.

children.text: eko vedaścatuṣpādaḥ saṃhṛtya tu punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: The one four-footed <s>Veda</s>, after being gathered together again and again,
is divided here in the <s>Dvāparas</s> because life has become shortened.
And the single <s>Veda</s> is divided into four at the beginnings of the <s>Dvāpara</s> ages.
Again, the <s>Vedas</s> are split by the sons of sages through confusions of vision.
But through the arrangements of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and through reversals of accent and sequence,
the <s>Saṃhitās</s> of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> were collected by those great sages.
From common and altered forms, and by those whose views differ here and there,
the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>Kalpasūtras</s>, and the sciences of commentary likewise arise.

children.text: anye tu prasthitāstānvai kecit tān pratyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Others proceeded along those paths, while some stood opposed to them.
In the <s>Dvāparas</s>, they set out with separate systems, each with different meanings.
Formerly the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> was one; later it again became twofold.
With meanings both common and contrary, this śāstra has been made confused.
And the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> was thrown into confusion in many ways by different schools,
and likewise the traditions of the <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Sāmans</s>, through variants and through their own abridgements.
In the <s>Dvāparas</s>, the meaning is made confused by those with differing views.

children.text: dvāpare saṃnivṛtte te vedā naśyanti vai kalau ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Dvāpara</s> has come to an end, those <s>Vedas</s> perish in <s>Kali</s>.
Born from the reversal of them, such conditions arise again in <s>Dvāpara</s>:
lack of vision, death, and likewise the disturbances caused by disease.
Then, from sufferings produced by speech, mind, and action, disenchantment arises.
From disenchantment there arises for them reflection on release from suffering.
In that reflection there is detachment; from detachment comes the seeing of faults.
And from seeing the faults, the arising of knowledge comes about.
For those intelligent ones, formerly, among mortals in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> interval,
opponents of the śāstras appear here in <s>Dvāpara</s>.
There are variant forms of <s>Āyurveda</s>, of the ancillary sciences, and of <s>Jyotiṣa</s>,
variant forms of <s>Arthaśāstra</s>, and the construction of systems of reasoning.
There are procedures of the <s>Kalpasūtras</s> and variant sciences of commentary,
divisions of the <s>Smṛtiśāstras</s> and separate schools, one by one.
In the <s>Dvāparas</s>, these arise, as do differences in the opinions of people.
With mind, action, and speech, livelihood is achieved only with difficulty.
In <s>Dvāpara</s>, the time of all beings is remembered as full of affliction.
Greed, lack of firmness, trade, war, and uncertainty about principles arise.
There is the composition of <s>Veda</s> and śāstra, and also the mixing of <s>dharmas</s>.
There is the destruction of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, and likewise desire and hatred.
When two thousand years are complete, that is then the highest lifespan of human beings.

children.text: niḥśeṣe dvāpare tasmiṃstasya saṃdhyā tu pādataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that <s>Dvāpara</s> is exhausted, its twilight is a quarter.
They remain devoid of the qualities belonging to the <s>dharma</s> of <s>Dvāpara</s>.
And likewise, by a quarter of the twilight, a portion is established within it.

children.text: dvāparasya tu paryāye puṣyasya ca nibodhata
children.translated_text: Now understand the turn of <s>Dvāpara</s> and of <s>Puṣya</s>.
When only a remnant of <s>Dvāpara</s>'s portion remains, then comes the onset of <s>Kali</s>.
Violence, theft, falsehood, deceit, and hypocrisy among ascetics

children.text: ete svabhāvāḥ puṣyasya sādhayanti ca tāḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are the natural traits of <s>Puṣya</s>, and they overpower those creatures.

children.text: eṣa dharmaḥ smṛtaḥ kṛtsno dharmaśca parihīyate
children.translated_text: This whole <s>dharma</s> is remembered, and <s>dharma</s> also declines.

children.text: manasā karmaṇā vācā vārttāḥ sidhyanti vā na vā ||
children.translated_text: By mind, action, and speech, livelihoods either succeed or do not succeed.

children.text: kaliḥ pramārako rogaḥ satataṃ cāpi kṣudbhayam
children.translated_text: <s>Kali</s> is a destructive sickness, and there is constant fear of hunger.
There is fear of drought, and the overturning of regions.

children.text: na pramāṇe sthitirhyasti puṣye ghore yuge kalau
children.translated_text: There is no stability in any measure in <s>Puṣya</s>, in the terrible age of <s>Kali</s>.
One dies while still in the womb, and another likewise while in youth.

children.text: sthāvirye madhyakaumāre mriyante ca kalau prajāḥ
children.translated_text: In old age, middle age, and childhood, people die in <s>Kali</s>.
In <s>Puṣya</s>, people are of little splendor and strength, sinful, very angry, and unrighteous.
They are devoted to false vows and are greedy, and so the people live in <s>Puṣya</s>.
Through bad sacrifices, bad study, bad conduct, and bad traditions,
through these faults in the rites of the Brahmins, fear arises among the people.
Violence, pride, envy, anger, intolerance, impatience, and lack of firmness

children.text: puṣye bhavanti jantūnāṃ lobho mohaśca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: and greed and delusion in every way arise among living beings in <s>Puṣya</s>.
Very great agitation arises when the age of <s>Kali</s> is reached.
Then the twice-born do not study the <s>Vedas</s>, nor do they sacrifice.

children.text: utsīdanti tathā caiva vaiśyaiḥ sārdhaṃ tu kṣatriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the Kṣatriyas, together with the Vaiśyas, likewise decline.
For Śūdras there is a connection with Brahmins through the source of mantras.
Here in that <s>Kali</s>, it comes about through beds, seats, and meals.
Kings are mostly Śūdras, and the practices of heretics prevail.
There are wearers of ochre, those without proper waist-cloths, and skull-bearers.
And whatever others are vowed to gods, as well as those who corrupt <s>dharma</s>,
and any who have divine-looking conduct and wear signs of <s>śruti</s> for the sake of livelihood,
whoever are of this kind exist here in the age of <s>Kali</s>.
Then Śūdras skilled in <s>dharma</s> and wealth study the <s>Vedas</s>.
Kings born from Śūdra wombs sacrifice with horse sacrifices,
after killing women, children, and cows, and after killing one another.
Having harmed one another in this way, the people then accomplish their aims.
There is an abundance of suffering, shortness of life, devastation of lands, and disease.
Absorption in <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), a conduct wrapped in darkness, is remembered in the <s>Kali</s> age.

children.text: bhrūṇahatyā prajānāṃ na tathā hyevaṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: As for the killing of embryos among the people, it does not proceed in quite this same way.
Therefore lifespan, strength, and beauty decline in the <s>Kali-yuga</s>.
For men overwhelmed by suffering, the utmost span of life is one hundred years.

children.text: bhūtvā ca na bhavantīha vedāḥ kaliyuge'khilāḥ
children.translated_text: Though they have existed, not all the <s>Vedas</s> exist here in the <s>Kali-yuga</s>.
Likewise sacrifices, which alone are causes of <s>dharma</s>, fall into ruin.
This is the state of the <s>Kali-yuga</s>; now understand its twilight portion.

children.text: yuge yuge tu hīyante trīṃstrīnpādāṃśca siddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In each age the perfections diminish by three quarters.
The natures of the yugas remain in the twilights by one quarter.
And the natures of the twilights remain in their own portions by just one quarter.

children.text: evaṃ saṃdhyāṃśake kāle samprāpte tu yugāntike
children.translated_text: Thus, when the time of the twilight portion has arrived at the end of the age,

children.text: teṣāmadharmiṇāṃ śāstā bhṛgūṇāṃ ca kule sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the chastiser of those unrighteous people, established in the family of the <s>Bhṛgus</s>,
of the lineage of <s>Candramas</s> by gotra, is called by the name <s>Pramati</s>.
In the portions of the <s>Kali</s> twilight, in the interval of <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>,
for thirty full years he travels over the earth.
He, active with horses, has an army crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots.
With Brahmins, hundreds and then thousands of them, who have taken up weapons,

children.text: sa tadā taiḥ parivṛto mlecchānsarvān nijaghnivān ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by them at that time, he slays all the <s>Mlecchas</s>.
And after killing all the kings born from <s>Śūdras</s>,
the lord made all the heretics, always and everywhere, utterly without remainder.
And whoever are unrighteous, he kills all of them completely.
The northerners, the peoples of the middle country, and also the mountain peoples,
the easterners and westerners, and those beyond the slopes of the <s>Vindhya</s>,
and likewise the southerners, the <s>Draviḍas</s> together with the <s>Siṃhalas</s>,
the <s>Gāndhāras</s>, <s>Pāradas</s>, <s>Pahlavas</s>, <s>Yavanas</s>, and <s>Śakas</s>,
the <s>Tuṣāras</s>, <s>Barbaras</s>, <s>Śvetas</s>, <s>Hālikas</s>, <s>Daradas</s>, and <s>Khasas</s>,
the <s>Lampakas</s> and <s>Āndhrakas</s>, and likewise the peoples born as thieves,
with his wheel set in motion, powerful, he shone forth as the ender of the <s>Śūdras</s>.
Having scattered all beings, he roamed over this earth.

children.text: mānavasya tu vaṃśe tu nṛdevasyeha jajñivān ||
children.translated_text: He was born here in the human lineage as a king among men.
In a former birth he was <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the mighty one named <s>Pramati</s>.

children.text: sutaḥ sa vai candramasaḥ pūrve kaliyuge prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was indeed the son of <s>Candramas</s>, the lord, in a previous <s>Kali-yuga</s>.
When his thirty-second year had risen, he set out for twenty years.
He slew all human beings everywhere, all of them without exception.

children.text: kṛtvā bījāvaśiṣṭāṃ tāṃ pṛthvīṃ krūreṇa karmaṇā
children.translated_text: By that cruel act he made the earth such that only seed remained.
Through mutual causation and through sudden time,

children.text: saṃsthitā sahasā yā tu senā pramatinā saha
children.translated_text: the army that was with <s>Pramati</s> came to an end all at once.
Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s> it attained perfection through concentration.
Then, when those cruel-doing men had perished in the twilight portion,
after all the earthly kings had been destroyed and those men had passed away,

children.text: tataḥ saṃdhyāṃśake kāle samprāpte ca yugāntike
children.translated_text: then, when the time of the twilight portion had arrived at the end of the age,
while only a few people remained here and there in scattered places,

children.text: svāpradānās tadā te vai lobhāviṣṭāstu vṛndaśaḥ
children.translated_text: then they, not giving up their own property and overcome by greed, gathered in groups.
They harmed one another and plundered one another.
In the lawless portion of the age, when destruction had come near,
all those people were then afflicted by fear of one another.
Distracted and turned back, having abandoned the deity and their homes,
watching over their own lives, pitiless, they were exceedingly miserable.
When <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta dharma</s> had disappeared, they followed the power of desire and anger.
They were without limits, without joy, without affection, and without shame.
When <s>dharma</s> had disappeared, they were obstructed, short-lived, and reduced to twenty-five years.
Abandoning wives and sons, the people were bewildered by despair.
Struck by drought, they abandoned their livelihoods and were miserable.
Leaving their own settled lands, they resorted to border regions.
They frequented rivers, ocean shores, and marshes, and also mountains.
They wore bark garments and black antelope skins, performed no rites, and possessed nothing.
Fallen away from class and life-stage, they entered into a terrible mixture.
Having reached such hardship, only a small remnant of the people was then left.
The living beings, overcome by hunger, came to disgust because of suffering.
And they resorted to those regions, moving round and round like a wheel.

children.text: tataḥ prajāstu tāḥ sarvā māṃsāhārā bhavanti hi
children.translated_text: Then all those people became eaters of meat.
Deer, boars, bulls, and whatever other forest-roaming animals there were,
all of them, both edible and inedible, they ate.

children.text: samudraṃ saṃśritā yāstu nadīścaiva prajāstu tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those people who had resorted to the ocean and to rivers,
they too carried off fish here in every way for the sake of food.
Because of the fault of eating forbidden food, the people came to be of one class.
Just as in the former <s>Kṛta-yuga</s> there was, it is said, one class,
so too at the end of the <s>Kali-yuga</s> the people became <s>Śūdras</s>.

children.text: evaṃ varṣaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ divyaṃ teṣāṃ nyavartata
children.translated_text: Thus a full hundred divine years passed for them.

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśacca sahasrāṇi mānuṣāṇi tu tāni vai ||
children.translated_text: Those were thirty-six thousand human years.
Then, after a long time, birds and beasts as well,
and also fish, were killed everywhere by all those overcome by hunger.
Then, when all fish, birds, and beasts had been exhausted without remainder,

children.text: saṃdhyāṃśe pratipanne tu niḥśeṣāstu tadā kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when the twilight portion had begun, they were then all made extinct without remainder.
Then the creatures, coming together, dug up bulbs and roots,
all feeding on fruits and roots, and likewise without dwellings.
Then bark garments were their clothes, and they lay everywhere on the ground;
they had no possessions, and so they attained purity in regard to wealth.
In this way the creatures will go to destruction then, with only a few left over;
and for those few who remain, growth is said to come from food.
Thus a divine hundred years passes as the twilight portion of that age;
then, at the end of the hundred years, only a few women and children remain.

children.text: mithunāni tu tāḥ sarvā hyanyonyaṃ samprajajñire
children.translated_text: All those pairs then begot offspring from one another,

children.text: tatastāstu mriyante vai pūrvotpannāḥ prajāstu yāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then the creatures that had been born before indeed died.
When the children had only just been born, the <s>Kṛta</s> age then began.

children.text: yathā svarge śarīrāṇi narake caiva dehinām ||
children.translated_text: Just as the bodies of embodied beings in heaven and also in hell
are capable of experience, so it is in the <s>Kṛta-yuga</s> and the other ages.
Such is the continuity of <s>Kṛta</s>, and likewise the decline of <s>Kali</s>.
From reflection comes disenchantment, and likewise from the self established in sameness;
then comes self-awakening, and from awakening comes a disposition toward <s>dharma</s>.
In this way, among those very survivors of <s>Kali</s>, creatures are born as before,
and by the force of what is to come, <s>Kṛta</s> then began.
Whatever things, past and future, occur here in the <s>manvantaras</s>,
these natural conditions of the yugas have been stated by me in brief.
After bowing to <s>Svayambhū</s>, I shall speak of them in detail and in order.

children.text: pravṛtte tu tatastasminpunaḥ kṛtayuge tu vai ||
children.translated_text: Then, when that <s>Kṛta-yuga</s> had again begun,
the creatures born among the survivors of <s>Kali</s> were likewise of the <s>Kṛta</s> age.

children.text: tiṣṭhanti ceha ye siddhā adṛṣṭā viharanti ca ||
children.translated_text: And the perfected beings who remain here, unseen and wandering about,

children.text: saha saptarṣibhirye tu tatra ye ca vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: together with the seven sages, and those who are stationed there,

children.text: brahmakṣatraviśaḥ śūdrā bījārthe ya iha smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>, who are remembered here for the sake of seed,
then became indistinguishable from those born in the <s>Kṛta</s> age.

children.text: teṣāṃ saptarṣayo dharmaṃ kathayantīha teṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: The seven sages teach <s>dharma</s> to them here, among those people,
endowed with the conduct of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, according to the <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> ordinances.

children.text: evaṃ teṣu kriyāvatsu pravartantīha vai kṛte ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when they perform the rites, those practices come into force here in <s>Kṛta</s>.
For those established in <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> <s>dharma</s>, as shown by the seven sages,

children.text: te tu dharmavyavasthārthaṃ tiṣṭhantīha kṛte yuge ||
children.translated_text: they remain here in the <s>Kṛta-yuga</s> for the sake of fixing the order of <s>dharma</s>.
Those sages remain in the administrations of the <s>manvantaras</s>.
Just as, when grasses have been burned by a forest fire, other grass again

children.text: vanānāṃ prathamaṃ vṛṣṭyā teṣāṃ mūleṣu sambhavaḥ
children.translated_text: springs up first in the forests, at their roots, through the rain,
so the continuity of age after age proceeds mutually,
indeed without interruption, until the end of a <s>manvantara</s>.

children.text: sukhamāyurbalaṃ rūpaṃ dharmārthau kāma eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Happiness, lifespan, strength, beauty, <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and desire,

children.text: yugeṣvetāni hīyante trayaḥ pādāḥ krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: these diminish in the yugas, by three quarters, in due sequence.
Thus this juncture of all the four-yuga cycles has been recounted to you, O twice-born ones;
this is the same rule for all the sets of four yugas.
When seventy-one of these four-yuga cycles have been counted,
having revolved in order, that is called the interval of a <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: yugākhyāsu tu sarvāsu bhavatīha yadā ca yat ||
children.translated_text: Whatever happens here in all the states called yugas, whenever it occurs,
that very thing occurs again in the others, in that same order.

children.text: sarge sarge yathā bhedā hyutpadyante tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Just as distinctions arise in each creation, so too
that many are to be understood here among the fourteen <s>manvantaras</s>.
The <s>Āsurī</s>, <s>Yātudhānī</s>, <s>Paiśācī</s>, and <s>Yakṣarākṣasī</s> kinds of beings,

children.text: yuge yuge tadā kāle prajā jāyanti tāḥ śṛṇu
children.translated_text: arise among creatures at that time in every yuga; hear of them.
In accordance with each kalpa, together with the yugas, they possess similar characteristics.
Thus this characteristic of the yugas has been declared in due order.
The turnings of the <s>manvantaras</s>, long set in motion by the nature of the yugas,

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ na saṃtiṣṭhati jīvalokaḥ kṣayodayābhyāṃ parivartamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are such that the world of living beings does not stand still for a moment, changing through decay and arising.
These natural conditions of the yugas have been passed through for you in due order;
now I shall tell the <s>manvantaras</s> that occur in this kalpa.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: manvantarāṇi yāni syuḥ kalpe kalpe caturdaśa
children.translated_text: The <s>manvantaras</s> that occur in each kalpa are fourteen,
those past and future that occur here within the <s>manvantaras</s>.
I shall explain in detail and in order the condition in each yuga,
the birth of those beings in that yuga, and how long their life lasts.

children.text: yugamātraṃ tu jīvanti nyūnaṃ tatsyāddvayena ca
children.translated_text: They live for the measure of a yuga, and that may be less by two;
that many are to be understood here among the fourteen <s>manvantaras</s>.

children.text: manuṣyāṇāṃ paśūnāṃ ca pakṣiṇāṃ sthāvaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: For human beings, animals, birds, and immobile beings as well,
their lifespan has been undertaken in every respect according to the <s>dharmas</s> of the yugas.
Likewise lifespan has turned in every respect according to the <s>dharmas</s> of the yugas.

children.text: asthitiṃ ca kalau dṛṣṭvā bhūtānāmāyuṣaśca vai ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the instability of beings in <s>Kali</s>, and also of their lifespan,
this is remembered as the maximum lifespan of human beings in <s>Kali</s>: one hundred years.
Gods, asuras, human beings, yakṣas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas

children.text: pariṇāhocchraye tulyā jāyante ha kṛte yuge
children.translated_text: are born equal in girth and height in the <s>Kṛta-yuga</s>.
For the eight divine classes, the height is ninety-six fingers,
with the group of eight completed according to a measure of nine fingers.
This is their natural measure when they have reached their full standard.
But human beings living here in the twilight portions of the yugas
have, in order, the measure of gods and asuras at seventy-seven fingers,
and it is remembered as eighty-four fingers according to those born in <s>Kali</s>.
He who is nine tālas from the soles of the feet to the head,
and whose arms, when lowered, reach the knees, is honored by the deities.
And of cows, elephants, buffaloes, and beings whose nature is immobile...
In this sequence, decrease and increase should be understood in each <s>yuga</s>.
An animal should be seventy-six finger-breadths high up to the hump.
The height of elephants is remembered as eight hundred finger-breadths;
and also as a thousand finger-breadths plus forty-two finger-breadths.
But for trees the highest height is half a hundred finger-breadths.
As is the arrangement of the human body,
so the mark of the gods is seen from observing continuity of type.
The body of the gods is said to be endowed with an excellence of intelligence;
and likewise the body without such excellence is called human.

children.text: ityeva hi parikrāntā bhāvā ye divyamānuṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed have been reviewed the beings that are divine and human,

children.text: paśūnāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ caiva sthāvarāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: and those of animals, birds, and all immobile beings in every way.
Cows, goats, horses, elephants, birds, and wild animals should be recognized;
all these are useful in rites and are sacrificial here in every way.
According to their proper order of enjoyment, they are animal forms of the gods.
Stationary and moving beings, with measures corresponding to their forms,
attained happiness there through those pleasing enjoyments.
Now I shall describe the remaining ones, the good people, and then also the virtuous.
The <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the words of <s>śruti</s>, and the animal forms of the gods,
being inwardly joined with <s>brahman</s>, are for that reason called good.

children.text: sāmānyeṣu ca dharmeṣu tathā vaiśiṣikeṣu ca
children.translated_text: In the common <s>dharmas</s> and also in the particular ones,
<s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>vaiśyas</s> are joined to <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> action.
For one engaged in the classes and life-stages, whose result is happiness and whose course is heaven,

children.text: śrautasmārto hi yo dharmo jñānadharmaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s> that is both <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> is called the <s>dharma</s> of knowledge.
Because he accomplishes divine things, the <s>brahmacārin</s> who serves the teacher is a good man.
Because he is a cause and because he accomplishes duties, the householder is called a good man.
Through austerity in the forest, the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> is likewise remembered as a good man.

children.text: yatamāno yatiḥ sādhuḥ smṛto yogasya sādhanāt ||
children.translated_text: The striving ascetic is remembered as a good man because he practices yoga.

children.text: dharmo dharmagatiḥ proktaḥ śabdo hyeṣa kriyātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is said to be the path of <s>dharma</s>; this word has action as its nature.
The Lord declared skillful and unskillful acts to be <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
Now gods, ancestors, sages, and human beings

children.text: ayaṃ dharmo hyayaṃ neti bruvate maunamūrtinā ||
children.translated_text: say, in a silent form, 'This is <s>dharma</s>; this is not.'
The verbal root in <s>dharma</s> is said to mean supporting, and also greatness.

children.text: ādhāraṇe mahattve vā dharmaḥ sa tu nirucyate ||
children.translated_text: Whether in the sense of supporting or in that of greatness, that is how <s>dharma</s> is explained.
There <s>dharma</s> is taught by teachers as that which brings about what is desired.
<s>Adharma</s>, having an undesired fruit, is not taught by teachers.
Elders who are free from greed, self-possessed, and without pretence,
properly disciplined and gentle: these are called teachers.
The <s>dharma</s> ordained by those who know <s>dharma</s> is <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> for the twice-born.
The connection with wife and <s>agnihotra</s>, and sacrifice, are the marks of the <s>śrauta</s>.
The <s>smārta</s> consists of conduct according to class and life-stage, joined with restraints and observances.
Having made the <s>śrauta</s> known here from the earlier ones, the <s>Saptarṣis</s> declared it.

children.text: ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni brahmaṇo'ṅgāni vai śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>ṛcs</s>, <s>yajuses</s>, and <s>sāmans</s>, the limbs of <s>brahman</s>, are <s>śruti</s>.
Remembering that from the past <s>manvantara</s>, <s>Manu</s> declared it.
Therefore, said <s>Sūta</s>, <s>smārta</s> <s>dharma</s> is divided according to class and life-stage.

children.text: evaṃ vai dvividho dharmaḥ śiṣṭācāraḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>dharma</s> is indeed twofold; it is called the conduct of the <s>śiṣṭas</s>.
They explain the word <s>śiṣṭa</s> from the root śiṣ with the suffix niṣṭhā.

children.text: manvantareṣu ye śiṣṭā iha tiṣṭhanti dhārmikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>śiṣṭas</s> in the <s>manvantaras</s> who remain here as righteous men,
<s>Manu</s> and the <s>Saptarṣis</s>, who bring about the continuity of the world,
remain here for the sake of <s>dharma</s>; them they call <s>śiṣṭas</s>.

children.text: taiḥ śiṣṭaiścalito dharmaḥ sthāpyate vai yuge yuge
children.translated_text: When <s>dharma</s> has slipped, it is established again by those <s>śiṣṭas</s> age after age.
The triple <s>Veda</s>, commerce and agriculture, and the science of punishment exist for the sake of subjects, classes, and life-stages.
Because it is practiced by the <s>śiṣṭas</s> again at the end of a <s>Manu</s>,
and because it has been approved by successive predecessors, that conduct of the <s>śiṣṭas</s> is eternal.

children.text: dānaṃ satyaṃ tapo loko vidyejyā pūjanaṃ damaḥ
children.translated_text: Giving, truth, austerity, the world, knowledge, sacrifice, worship, and self-control:
these eight practices are the marks of the conduct of the <s>śiṣṭas</s>.
Because the <s>śiṣṭas</s>, <s>Manu</s>, and the <s>Saptarṣis</s> practice it,
through all the <s>manvantaras</s> it is therefore remembered as the conduct of the <s>śiṣṭas</s>.
What is known from hearing is <s>śrauta</s>; what is known from remembering is called <s>smārta</s>.
The <s>śrauta</s> has sacrifice and the <s>Veda</s> as its nature; the <s>smārta</s> has class and life-stage as its nature.
Now I shall state the individual limbs, the marks of <s>dharma</s> here.

children.text: dṛṣṭānubhūtamarthaṃ ca yaḥ pṛṣṭo na vigūhate
children.translated_text: When asked, one who does not conceal an object that has been seen and experienced,
but speaks of it just as it is: this is the mark of truth.
Celibacy, austerity, silence, and going without food:
this is the form of austerity, very terrible and hard to approach.
The conjunction of animals, sacrificial materials and oblations, and likewise of <s>ṛk</s>, <s>sāman</s>, and <s>yajus</s>,
together with officiating priests and sacrificial fees, is called sacrifice.
One who behaves constantly with gladness toward all beings as toward oneself,

children.text: vartate satataṃ hṛṣṭaḥ kriyā śreṣṭhā dayā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: for their welfare and good: that best action is remembered as compassion.
One who, though abused or struck, does not abuse or strike in return,
and remains uncorrupted in speech, mind, and body: that endurance is remembered as forbearance.
Not taking the property of others, whether guarded by its owner
or left aside in confusion, is called freedom from greed.
Abstention from the practice of sexual intercourse, and likewise from speaking and thinking about it,
is celibacy; and this is the mark of tranquility.

children.text: ātmārthe vā parārthe vā indriyāṇīha yasya vai
children.translated_text: For one whose senses, whether for one's own sake or for another's sake,
do not turn toward their objects here: this is the mark of self-control.
Regarding the fivefold object and the cause characterized by eight marks...

children.text: na krudhyeta pratihataḥ sa jitātmā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: One who does not grow angry when thwarted will become self-controlled.
Whatever possession is most desired, and whatever has come by lawful means,
that should be given to a worthy person; this is the definition of giving.
<s>Dharma</s> is prescribed by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, and consists of the classes and life-stages.
It has grown through the conduct of the cultivated, and this <s>dharma</s> is approved by good people.
There is no hatred toward what is unwanted, and one does not rejoice in what is desired.
The cessation of pleasure, pain, and dejection is detachment.
<s>Saṃnyāsa</s> is the laying down of actions, those done together with those not done.
Abandonment with respect to both good and bad is called renunciation.
In this transformation, extending from the unmanifest down to the particulars, he turns away.

children.text: cetanācetanaṃ jñātvā jñāne jñānī sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the conscious and the unconscious in knowledge, he is called a knower in respect to knowledge.
These are the subsidiary limbs of <s>dharma</s>; this is remembered as its definition,
by the ancient seers who knew the truth of <s>dharma</s>, in the interval of <s>Svāyambhuva</s>.

children.text: atra vo varṇayiṣyāmi vidhiṃ manvantarasya tu
children.translated_text: Here I shall describe to you the rule for the manvantara,
and likewise that of the four priests and indeed of the four social classes.
In each manvantara a different <s>Śruti</s> is prescribed,
the Ṛcs, Yajuses, and Sāmans, properly, for each deity.
The prescribed praise and the hotṛ's rite proceed as before,
as do praise of substance, praise of quality, and praise of action.
Likewise there is praise of lineage; thus praise is fourfold,

children.text: manvantareṣu sarveṣu yathā bhedā bhavanti hi ||
children.translated_text: according to the distinctions that exist in all the manvantaras.

children.text: pravartayanti teṣāṃ vai brahmastotraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: They repeatedly set in motion the brahman-praise for them.
Thus the arising of the qualities of the mantras is fourfold.
In the Atharvan, Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman, among the Vedas here separately,
for those seers who practice the supreme tapas, very hard to perform,
the mantras first become manifest at the beginning of the former manvantara,
in five ways: from dissatisfaction, fear, suffering, delusion, and grief.
By whatever characteristic, as it happens, the seers are guiding stars,
I shall tell here the mark of what the seers are like.
The seerhood of the past and the future is remembered as fivefold.
Likewise I shall tell here the arising of the seers' seerhood.
At that time, at the dissolution of all things, they remain in an equality of the guṇas,
undivided among the gods, in an indescribable mass of darkness.
That proceeds without prior intelligence, for the sake of consciousness.
Therefore what belongs to the seers is preceded by intelligence and is governed even by the conscious one.

children.text: pravartate tathā te tu yathā matsyodakāvubhau
children.translated_text: And so they proceed, like fish and water together.
Everything made of the guṇas proceeded under the authority of consciousness.
Thus it proceeds in the relation of effect and cause.
Object and subjecthood then are both made up of meaning and word,
and the distinctions, causally formed, are to be reached by time.
Then the innate developments, beginning with the great principle, occurred in order.
From the great principle came that ego-maker; from it came the elements and senses.
And the distinctions of the elements were born mutually from the elements.
An effect whose cause is innate evolves immediately.
Just as branches of flame arise at the same time from a firebrand,
so the knowers of the field proceeded at one time from the cause, through time.
Just as a firefly is suddenly seen in darkness,

children.text: tathā nivṛtto hyavyaktaḥ khadyota iva saṃjvalan ||
children.translated_text: so the unmanifest, withdrawn, blazes up like a firefly.
That great self, abiding in the body, proceeds right there in this world.
Beyond the great darkness it is discerned because of its distinct character.
Established there itself, the wise one is heard of as the end of tapas.
As he increased, his intelligence became manifest in four forms:
knowledge, detachment, sovereignty, and <s>dharma</s>; this is the fourfold set.
These are innate, and otherwise they are not evident in him.
For the body of the great self, accomplishment is said to come from consciousness.

children.text: puri śete yataḥ pūrvaṃ kṣetrajñānaṃ tathāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: Because at first he lies in the city, and likewise because of knowledge of the field,
he is called <s>puruṣa</s> from lying in the city, and <s>kṣetrajña</s> from knowledge.
Since he is born from <s>dharma</s>, therefore he is indeed dharmic.
In the innate body, the conscious one is unmanifest through intelligence.
Thus the <s>kṣetrajña</s> unfolds, not deliberately aiming at the field.
At the same time as cessation, that ancient unconscious thing
was recognized by the <s>kṣetrajña</s>: 'This object to be enjoyed is mine.'
The verbal root for <s>ṛṣi</s> is in the senses of harming and going; knowledge, truth, tapas, and sacred learning are heard of.
Since this one is a brāhmaṇa, therefore he is an <s>ṛṣi</s>.
And because this <s>ṛṣi</s>, unmanifest through intelligence, exists at the same time as cessation,
because he goes to the supreme, he is therefore remembered as a <s>paramarṣi</s>.
The verbal root ṛṣ, in the sense of going, is the cause for the derivation of the name.
Because this one is self-born, therefore seerhood is accepted.
Endowed with lordship and self-arisen, they are the mind-born sons of <s>Brahmā</s>.
As they withdrew through intelligence, the supreme great one was encompassed.
Because of their superior vision, together with transcendence, they are therefore great seers.
They are the sons of the lords, both mind-born and bodily.
Because an <s>ṛṣi</s> has superiority, from the element-origin onward they are seers.
The sons of seers are <s>ṛṣīkas</s>, born from the womb through sexual union.
Because they go beyond the elements and the rest, they are therefore <s>ṛṣīkas</s>.

children.text: ṛṣikāṇāṃ sutā ye tu vijñeyā ṛṣiputrakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who are sons of the <s>ṛṣīkas</s> should be known as <s>ṛṣiputrakas</s>.
Having heard the seerhood as supreme, they are 'heard'; therefore they are <s>śrutarṣis</s>.
He is the one whose self is the unmanifest, the great self, and likewise whose self is <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.
He is the self of the elements and the self of the senses; this is called knowledge of them.
Thus this class of <s>ṛṣis</s> is well known as fivefold by name.
<s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Kratu</s>,
<s>Manu</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and also <s>Pulastya</s>: these are the ten.
These mind-born sons of <s>Brahmā</s> arose as self-ruling lords.
Because the seers are regarded as superior, for that reason they are <s>maharṣis</s> (great seers).
Now learn the seers who are the sons of these lords.
<s>Kāvya</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and likewise <s>Cyavana</s>,
<s>Utathya</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Agastya</s>, and <s>Kauśika</s>,
<s>Kardama</s>, the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, <s>Viśravas</s>, and <s>Śaktivardhana</s>:
these are declared to be <s>ṛṣis</s>, having attained the state of seers through austerity.
Now learn their sons, the lesser seers, born from the womb.
<s>Vatsara</s>, <s>Nagnahū</s>, and mighty <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
the seer <s>Dīrghatamas</s>, <s>Bṛhadvakṣas</s>, and <s>Śaradvata</s>,
<s>Vājiśravas</s>, <s>Sucinta</s>, <s>Śāva</s>, together with <s>Parāśara</s>,

children.text: śṛṅgī ca śaṅkhapāc caiva rājā vaiśravaṇastathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapā</s>, and also King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>:

children.text: ityete ṛṣikāḥ sarve satyena ṛṣitāṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: all these lesser seers attained the state of seers through truth.

children.text: īśvarā ṛṣayaścaiva ṛṣīkā ye ca viśrutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The lords, the seers, and the lesser seers who are renowned:
now learn all the makers of mantras in full.
<s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Pracetā</s>, and self-possessed <s>Dadhīca</s>,
<s>Ūrṣa</s>, then <s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Veda</s>, and <s>Sārasvata</s>,
<s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, <s>Vītahavya</s>, together with <s>Vedhas</s>,
<s>Vainya</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s>, <s>Divodāsa</s>, the brahman-knowing <s>Gṛtsa</s> and <s>Śaunaka</s>:
these nineteen <s>Bhṛgus</s> are the foremost makers of mantras.
<s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Trita</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Kṛtavāc</s>, <s>Garga</s>, and also <s>Smṛtisaṃkṛti</s>,
<s>Guruvīta</s>, <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, and likewise <s>Ambarīṣa</s>,
<s>Yuvanāśva</s>, <s>Purukutsa</s>, <s>Svaśravas</s>, and <s>Sadasyavān</s>,
<s>Ajamīḍha</s>, <s>Asvahārya</s>, <s>Utkala</s>, and <s>Kavi</s>,
<s>Pṛṣadaśva</s>, <s>Virūpa</s>, <s>Kāvya</s>, and then <s>Mudgala</s>,
<s>Utathya</s>, <s>Śaradvān</s>, and likewise <s>Vājiśravas</s>,
<s>Apasyauṣa</s>, <s>Sucitti</s>, and also <s>Vāmadeva</s>,
<s>Ṛṣija</s>, <s>Bṛhacchukla</s>, and the seer <s>Dīrghatamas</s>,
and <s>Kakṣīvān</s>: thirty-three are remembered as the excellent <s>Aṅgirases</s>.
All these are makers of mantras; now learn the <s>Kāśyapas</s>.

children.text: kāśyapaḥ sahavatsāro naidhruvo nitya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāśyapa</s>, together with <s>Vatsara</s>, <s>Naidhruva</s>, and <s>Nitya</s>,
<s>Asita</s> and <s>Devala</s>: these six are speakers of brahman.
<s>Atri</s>, <s>Ardhasvana</s>, <s>Śāvāsya</s>, then <s>Gaviṣṭhira</s>,
<s>Karṇaka</s>, the perfected seer, and also that <s>Pūrvātithi</s>:
these six great seers are declared to be the <s>Atris</s>, makers of mantras.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and, third, <s>Parāśara</s>,
then <s>Indrapratima</s>, and fifth <s>Bharadvasu</s>,
sixth <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s>, and seventh <s>Kuṇḍina</s>:
these seven should be known as the <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, speakers of brahman.
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, son of <s>Gādhi</s>, <s>Devarāta</s>, and <s>Bala</s>,
and the learned <s>Madhucchandā</s>, and another seer, <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>,
<s>Aṣṭaka</s>, <s>Lohita</s>, <s>Bhṛtakīla</s>, and <s>Māmbudhi</s>,
<s>Devaśravas</s>, <s>Devarāta</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
<s>Śiśira</s> of great splendor, and <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s>:
these thirteen should be known as the best <s>Kauśikas</s>, most devoted to brahman.
<s>Agastya</s>, then <s>Dṛḍhadyumna</s>, and likewise <s>Indrabāhu</s>:
these three <s>Agastyas</s> are most devoted to brahman and of supreme fame.
<s>Manu Vaivasvata</s> and King <s>Purūravas Aila</s>:
these should be known as the foremost mantra-speakers among kṣatriyas.
<s>Bhalandaka</s>, <s>Vāsāśva</s>, and <s>Saṃkīla</s>: those three

children.text: ete mantrakṛto jñeyā vaiśyānāṃ pravarāḥ sadā
children.translated_text: are always to be known as makers of mantras, the foremost among vaiśyas.
Thus ninety-two have been declared, apart from the mantras.
Brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas: now learn the sons of the seers.
These sons of the lesser seers are the sons of seers, seers by learning.
The seers said:
How was the great slaying of <s>Tāraka</s> told by <s>Matsya</s>?
At what time did this story take place, O son of <s>Sūta</s>?
This story, made of nectar, has arisen from the milk-ocean of your mouth;
as we drink it with our ears, no satisfaction arises in us.
Tell us this, O sage, O greatly wise one; it is in our minds.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When <s>Manu</s> questioned the god <s>Janārdana</s>, who had the form of a fish,

children.text: kathaṃ śaravaṇe jāto devaḥ ṣaḍvadano vibho ||
children.translated_text: "How was the six-faced god born in the reed-thicket, O lord?"
then, having heard this speech of the king of immeasurable might,
the blessed one, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, was pleased and spoke to the greatly wise one.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
There was a daitya named <s>Vajrāṅga</s>; his son was <s>Tāraka</s>.
That very powerful one drove the gods out from their cities.
Then, oppressed by fear, they went into the presence of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Seeing the thirty gods afraid, <s>Brahmā</s> said to them:
"Give up your fear, O gods. A child, the son of <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
the daughter's son of <s>Tuhinācala</s>, will kill that demon."

children.text: tataḥ kāle tu kasmiṃściddṛṣṭvā vai śailajāṃ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, at a certain time, when <s>Śiva</s> saw <s>Śailajā</s>,
for another purpose he released his semen into the mouth of <s>Vahni</s>.
That semen, having reached the mouth of Fire, satisfied the gods.
After tearing open their bellies, O sage, it came out undigested.
It fell into the best of rivers, and from there into a thicket of reeds.
From that was born <s>Guha</s>, shining with the splendor of the sun.
Though a boy only seven days old, he slew <s>Tārakāsura</s>.

children.text: evaṃ śrutvā tato vākyaṃ tam ūcur ṛṣisattamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this statement, the best of sages then said to him:
The sages said:
This story is most wondrous, delightful, and destructive of sin.

children.text: vistareṇa hi no brūhi yāthātathyena śṛṇvatām ||
children.translated_text: Tell it to us in detail, according to the truth, as we listen.

children.text: vajrāṅgo nāma daityendraḥ kasya vaṃśodbhavaḥ purā
children.translated_text: In ancient times, from whose lineage was the lord of daityas named <s>Vajrāṅga</s> born,
whose son was the mighty <s>Tāraka</s>, crusher of the gods?

children.text: nirmitaḥ ko vadhe cābhūttasya daityeśvarasya tu
children.translated_text: Who was created for the killing of that lord of daityas?

children.text: guhajanma tu kārtsnyena asmākaṃ brūhi mānada ||
children.translated_text: And tell us completely of the birth of <s>Guha</s>, O giver of honor.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: mānaso brahmaṇaḥ putro dakṣo nāma prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: The mind-born son of <s>Brahmā</s> was the prajāpati named <s>Dakṣa</s>.
We have heard that he begot sixty daughters on <s>Vairiṇī</s>.

children.text: dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa
children.translated_text: He gave ten to <s>Dharma</s>, thirteen to <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
twenty-seven to <s>Soma</s>, and four to <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>.

children.text: dve vai bāhukaputrāya dve vai cāṅgirase tathā
children.translated_text: The powerful son of <s>Prajāpati</s> gave two to the son of <s>Bāhuka</s>, and likewise two to <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
and two to the learned <s>Kṛśāśva</s>.
<s>Aditi</s>, <s>Diti</s>, <s>Danu</s>, <s>Viśvā</s>, <s>Ariṣṭā</s>, and <s>Surasā</s>,
<s>Surabhi</s>, <s>Vinatā</s>, <s>Tāmrā</s>, <s>Krodhavaśā</s>, <s>Irā</s>,
<s>Kadrū</s> and <s>Muni</s> were mothers of the world, mothers also among cattle.
From them came the birth of worlds consisting of moving and unmoving beings,
of many different kinds; other embodied beings too are remembered as born from them.
<s>Devendra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, and the rest are all regarded as offspring of <s>Aditi</s>.
From <s>Diti</s> came beings such as <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
The <s>Dānavas</s> were sons of <s>Danu</s>, and cows were the children of <s>Surabhi</s>.
Birds, headed by <s>Garuḍa</s>, are remembered as sons of <s>Vinatā</s>.
The serpents are to be known as sons of <s>Kadrū</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s> and the other creatures as well.
The very mighty <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, after conquering <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the three worlds
and chief of all the hosts of immortals, took the kingdom.
Then, after some time, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and the others
were slain by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in battle, and the remaining <s>Dānavas</s> by <s>Indra</s>.
Then <s>Diti</s>, whose sons had been slain, asked for a boon
from her husband, the divine <s>Kaśyapa</s>: another mighty son,
a slayer of <s>Śakra</s> in battle; and that lord granted him to her.

children.text: niyame varta he devi sahasraṃ śucimānasā
children.translated_text: Remain under a vow, O goddess, for a thousand years, with a pure mind.
You will obtain a son; thus addressed, she did so.
While she was living under that vow, the thousand-eyed one, intent upon his purpose,
performed service for her, and she allowed him to do so.
When ten years of the thousand remained, <s>Diti</s>,

children.text: uvāca śakraṃ suprītā varadā tapasi sthitā ||
children.translated_text: very pleased and established in austerity, spoke to <s>Śakra</s> as one granting a boon.
<s>Diti</s> said:
Know me to have nearly crossed beyond the vow for a son, O <s>Pākaśāsana</s>.

children.text: bhaviṣyati ca te bhrātā tena sārdhamimāṃ śriyam ||
children.translated_text: A brother will be born for you; together with him,
enjoy this sovereignty over the three worlds as you wish, child, with its thorns removed.
Having said this, she was overcome by sleep, with the hair of her head pressed by her feet.
Because of the weight of what was to come, she herself slept without proper restraint.
Finding that breach, <s>Pākaśāsana</s>

children.text: cakāra saptadhā garbhaṃ kuliśena tu devarāṭ
children.translated_text: cut the embryo in her womb into seven parts with his thunderbolt, the king of gods.

children.text: ekaikaṃ tu punaḥ khaṇḍaṃ cakāra maghavā tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maghavan</s> again cut each separate piece
sevenfold, seven by seven, in anger. Then <s>Diti</s> awoke.

children.text: vibudhyovāca mā śakra ghātayethāḥ prajāṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: Awakening, she said, Do not, O <s>Śakra</s>, kill my offspring.
Hearing this, <s>Śakra</s> came out and stood in front with joined palms.
Terrified, he spoke words in response to what his mother had said.
<s>Śakra</s> said:
Mother, because you were given to sleeping by day, with your head-hair touched by your feet,
therefore your embryo has been made by me into seven times seven parts.
Your sons have been made into forty-nine portions by the thunderbolt.
I shall give them stations in heaven, honored by the gods.
Thus addressed, that goddess said then, Let it be so.
And again the dark-eyed goddess spoke to her husband:
Give me, O prajāpati, a mighty son who will conquer <s>Śakra</s>,
one who shall not become liable to death by the missiles and weapons of the dwellers in heaven.
Thus addressed, he spoke accordingly to his wife, who was deeply distressed:

children.text: daśa varṣasahasrāṇi tapaḥ kṛtvā tu lapsyase ||
children.translated_text: After performing austerity for ten thousand years, you will obtain
a son with limbs made of the essence of adamant, uncuttable, iron-hard, and firm.
He will be named <s>Vajrāṅga</s>, O you who love your son.

children.text: sā tu labdhavarā devī jagāma tapase vanam
children.translated_text: Having obtained the boon, the goddess went to the forest for austerity.
For ten thousand years she practiced terrible austerity.
At the end of her austerity, the blessed lady gave birth to an unconquerable son,
incapable of being opposed, invincible, and hard to split as adamant.
As soon as he was born, he became skilled in all missiles and weapons.

children.text: uvāca mātaraṃ bhaktyā mātaḥ kiṃ karavāṇyaham ||
children.translated_text: With devotion he said to his mother, Mother, what shall I do?

children.text: tamuvāca tato hṛṣṭā ditirdaityādhipaṃ ca sā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Diti</s>, delighted, spoke to him, the lord of daityas:

children.text: bahavo me hatāḥ putrāḥ sahasrākṣeṇa putraka ||
children.translated_text: Many sons of mine have been killed by the thousand-eyed one, my son.

children.text: teṣāṃ tvaṃ pratikartuṃ vai gaccha śakravadhāya ca
children.translated_text: To avenge them, go and slay <s>Śakra</s>.
Saying to her, Certainly, the powerful one went to heaven.
Then, binding the thousand-eyed one with a noose of unfailing splendor,
he came to his mother's side, like a tiger bringing a small deer.
Meanwhile <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the great ascetic,
came there, to the place where the frightened mother and son were staying.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu tāvuvācedaṃ brahmā kaśyapa eva ca
children.translated_text: Seeing the two of them, <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s> said this:
Release this <s>Devendra</s>, O son; what purpose is served by him?

children.text: apamāno vadhaḥ proktaḥ putra saṃbhāvitasya ca
children.translated_text: For a respected man, humiliation is said to be death, O son.

children.text: asmadvākyena yo mukto viddhi taṃ mṛtameva ca ||
children.translated_text: Know that one who is released at our word is indeed as good as dead.
Released out of regard for another, he carries a burden for his enemies.

children.text: jīvanneva mṛto vatsa divase divase sa tu ||
children.translated_text: Though living, he is dead day after day, my child.
When an enemy has come under the power of the great, there is no longer enmity toward that enemy.
Hearing this, <s>Vajrāṅga</s> bowed down and spoke these words.

children.text: na me kṛtyamanenāsti māturājñā kṛtā mayā
children.translated_text: I have no business with him; I have carried out my mother's command.
You are lord of gods and asuras, and also my great-grandfather.

children.text: kariṣye tvadvaco deva eṣa muktaḥ śatakratuḥ
children.translated_text: I shall do your word, O god; this <s>Śatakratu</s> is released.

children.text: tapase me ratirdeva nirvighnaṃ caiva me bhavet ||
children.translated_text: May my delight be in tapas; may it be free from obstruction for me.
By your grace, blessed lord. Having spoken thus, he stopped.
When that daitya remained silent, the Grandfather said this.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
You have undertaken fierce tapas, standing under our command.

children.text: anayā cittaśuddhyā te paryāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam ||
children.translated_text: With this purity of mind of yours, the fruit of birth is fulfilled.
Having spoken thus, the Lotus-born created a wide-eyed maiden.
The god <s>Padmasambhava</s> gave her to him for the sake of marriage.

children.text: varāṅgīti ca nāmāsyāḥ kṛtvā yātaḥ pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Having given her the name <s>Varāṅgī</s>, the Grandfather departed.

children.text: vajrāṅgo'pi tayā sārdhaṃ jagāma tapase vanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrāṅga</s> too went to the forest with her for tapas.
With arms raised, that lord of daityas practiced austerity for a thousand years,
for that length of time, lotus-petal-eyed, pure-minded, and very ascetic.
For as long again he remained face downward, and for as long again he stood amid the five fires.
Without food, terrible in tapas, he became a mass of austerity.
Then he spent a thousand years under water.
When he had entered within the water, his wife, devoted to a great vow,
remained on the bank of that very lake, out of love for him, observing silence.
Without food, the greatly radiant woman entered into fierce tapas.
While she was engaged in tapas, <s>Indra</s> produced terrors.
Becoming a great monkey there at her hermitage,
he threw into complete disorder the gourds, jars, and baskets.
Then, with the roar of a cloud, he caused great trembling for her.
Then, in the form of a serpent, he bound her two feet,
and dragged her far away, whirling her over this earth.

children.text: tapobalāḍhyā sā tasya na vadhyatvaṃ jagāma ha
children.translated_text: Rich in the power of tapas, she did not become vulnerable to destruction by him.
Then, in the form of a jackal, he defiled her hermitage.
Then, in the form of a cloud, he drenched her hermitage.
<s>Pākaśāsana</s>, tormenting her with frightening frogs,
still did not make <s>Vajrāṅga</s>'s queen desist in this way.

children.text: śailasya duṣṭatāṃ matvā śāpaṃ dātuṃ vyavasthitā ||
children.translated_text: Then, thinking the mountain was wicked, she resolved to utter a curse.
Seeing her intent on a curse, the mountain, in human form,
spoke to that fair-hipped <s>Varāṅgī</s> with a fearful mind.
I am not wicked, lovely woman; I am to be honored by all embodied beings.
It is this angry <s>Pākaśāsana</s> who is causing the disturbance.
Meanwhile a period of a thousand years had come to pass.
When that period had passed, the blessed <s>Kamalasaṃbhava</s>,
pleased, came to <s>Vajrāṅga</s> in his water-abode and spoke.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I grant all your desires; rise, descendant of <s>Diti</s>.
Thus addressed, that lord of daityas, treasure-house of fierce tapas, then arose
and, with joined palms, spoke these words to the Grandfather of all worlds.
<s>Vajrāṅga</s> said:

children.text: āsuro māstu me bhāvaḥ santu lokā mamākṣayāḥ
children.translated_text: May I not have an asuric disposition; may my worlds be imperishable.
May my delight be only in tapas; let bodily life merely continue for sustaining the body.
Saying, So be it, the god went to his own abode.
<s>Vajrāṅga</s> too, when his tapas was completed, firm in self-control,
wishing for food, did not see his wife in his own hermitage.

children.text: kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ sa śailasya gahanaṃ praviveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: Seized by hunger, he entered the mountain thicket.
In order to take fruits and roots, he looked about there.
He saw his dear wife weeping, miserable, her face hidden by a thin covering.

children.text: tāṃ vilokya sa daityendraḥ provāca parisāntvayan ||
children.translated_text: Seeing her, that lord of daityas consoled her and spoke.
<s>Vajrāṅga</s> said:
Who has wronged you, timid one, as though wishing to go to the world of <s>Yama</s>?

children.text: kaṃ vā kāmaṃ prayacchāmi śīghraṃ me brūhi bhāmini ||
children.translated_text: Or what desire shall I grant you? Tell me quickly, beautiful woman.
<s>Varāṅgī</s> said:
I have been frightened, hurled away, struck, and also tormented,
again and again by the fierce king of the gods, like one whose protector had been lost.
Seeing no far shore of suffering, I was resolved to abandon my life.
Give me a son, <s>Tāraka</s>, as a deliverer from the great ocean of sorrow and grief.
Thus addressed, that lord of daityas, his eyes agitated by anger,
though able to retaliate against the king of the gods, that great asura,
the mighty daitya resolved again to perform tapas.

children.text: jñātvā tu tasya saṃkalpaṃ brahmā krūrataraṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing that his resolve was again still more terrible, <s>Brahmā</s>
then came there, to the place where that descendant of <s>Diti</s> was.
The blessed Lord spoke to him in a sweet voice.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
For what purpose, son, do you again desire this fierce discipline?
You were turning toward food, O daitya; tell us that, great-vowed one.
Whatever fruit belongs to one who remains without food for a thousand years...
That is obtained in a single moment by giving up food that has come to hand.

children.text: tyāgo hyaprāptakāmānāṃ kāmebhyo na tathā guruḥ
children.translated_text: For renunciation of desires that have not been attained is not so weighty in regard to objects of desire
as giving up an object of desire that has been attained, O lotus-eyed one.
Having heard this speech of <s>Brahmā</s>, the daitya, with joined palms, spoke,
pondering in his heart what had issued from <s>Brahmā</s>'s mouth, and intent on austerity.
<s>Vajrāṅga</s> said:
When I had risen from concentration at your command, I saw
my queen frightened, miserable, and weeping at the foot of a tree.

children.text: sā mayoktā tu tanvaṅgī dūyamānena cetasā
children.translated_text: With my mind pained, I said to that slender-limbed woman:

children.text: kimevaṃ vartase bhīru vada tvaṃ kiṃ cikīrṣasi ||
children.translated_text: "Why are you in this state, timid one? Tell me what you wish to do."

children.text: ityuktā sā mayā deva provāca skhalitākṣaram
children.translated_text: So addressed by me, O god, that slender-limbed woman spoke with faltering syllables,

children.text: vākyaṃ covāca tanvaṅgī bhītā sā hetusaṃhitam ||
children.translated_text: and, frightened as she was, she uttered words together with their cause.
<s>Varāṅgī</s> said:
I have been terrified, cast aside, dragged about, and tormented
again and again by the fierce king of the gods, as if I had lost my protector.
Seeing no end to my suffering, I had resolved to abandon my life.
Give me a son, <s>Tāraka</s>, to carry me out of this great ocean of sorrow.
Thus addressed, I became agitated and intent on obtaining a son for her.
I shall perform fierce austerity for victory over the dwellers in heaven.
Hearing this speech then, O god, the lotus-born god,
the four-faced one, being pleased, spoke to the king of the daityas.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: alaṃ te tapasā vatsa mā kleśe dustare viśa
children.translated_text: Enough of your austerity, my child; do not enter into unbearable hardship.
A son named <s>Tāraka</s>, very strong, will be born to you.
He will loosen the braided hair of the wives of the gods.
Thus addressed, the lord of the daityas bowed down to the grandsire.
Returning, with a joyful face, he delighted his queen,

children.text: tau dampatī kṛtārthau tu jagmatuḥ svāśramaṃ mudā ||
children.translated_text: and the two spouses, their purpose fulfilled, went happily to their own hermitage.
<s>Varāṅgī</s>, the fair-complexioned one, bore in her womb

children.text: pūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ ca dadhārodara eva hi ||
children.translated_text: for a full thousand years the embryo placed there by <s>Vajrāṅga</s>.
Then, at the end of the thousand years, <s>Varāṅgī</s> gave birth to a son.
When that lord of the daityas was being born, terrifying the worlds,
the whole earth shook, and the oceans trembled.
All the mountains quaked, and dreadful winds blew.
The best of sages muttered their muttered prayers, and serpents and beasts also cried out.
The moon and sun lost their splendor, and the quarters became filled with mist.
When that great asura was born, all the great asuras
came there rejoicing, and so too did the women of the asuras.
Filled with joy they sang, and the asura women danced.
Then a great festival arose among the dānavas, O best of twice-born ones.
At that time the gods, together with <s>Indra</s>, became dejected in mind.
When <s>Varāṅgī</s> saw her own son, she was then filled with joy.

children.text: bahu mene na devendravijayaṃ tu tadeva sā
children.translated_text: She valued that very birth more than victory over the lord of the gods.
As soon as he was born, the daitya lord <s>Tāraka</s>, of fierce valor,
was consecrated by all the asuras, including <s>Kujambha</s> and <s>Mahiṣa</s>,
over the great kingdom of all the asuras, by those capable of weighing down the earth.

children.text: sa tu prāpya mahārājyaṃ tārako munisattamāḥ
children.translated_text: Having obtained that great kingship, <s>Tāraka</s>, O best of sages,
spoke these reasonable words to the foremost dānavas.
<s>Tāraka</s> said:
Listen, all you asuras, mighty ones, to my words.

children.text: śreyase kriyatāṃ buddhiḥ sarvaiḥ kṛtyasya saṃvidhau ||
children.translated_text: Let counsel be taken by all for our welfare in arranging what must be done.
The gods are the destroyers of the lineage of all dānavas.
For us, enmity that has grown firm is the dharma of our race and is imperishable.
Today we shall go to subdue the gods,
all of us relying on the strength of our own arms; there is no doubt.
But I do not think an encounter with the gods should be undertaken by one not joined with austerity.

children.text: ahamādau kariṣyāmi tato ghoraṃ diteḥ sutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: First I shall therefore perform fierce austerity, O sons of <s>Diti</s>.
Then we shall conquer the gods and thereafter enjoy the three worlds.
For a man whose means are firm also becomes firm in prosperity.
One who is unstable cannot protect unstable fortunes.

children.text: tacchrutvā dānavāḥ sarve vākyaṃ tasyāsurasya tu ||
children.translated_text: Having heard that speech of that asura, all the dānavas
said there, with amazement, "Excellent, excellent!"
He went to an excellent cave of Mount <s>Pāriyātra</s>,
covered with flowers of every season and radiant with many kinds of herbs,
variegated by streams of many mineral essences and containing many cave-dwellings,
hidden on every side by thickets and sheltered by wondrous wish-granting trees,
abounding in many forms and crowded with flocks of different birds,
provided with many springs and with many kinds of reservoirs.
Having reached that cave, the daitya practiced vast austerity.
He fasted; he practiced the five-fire austerity; he ate leaves and lived on water.

children.text: śataṃ śataṃ samānāṃ tu tapāṃsyetāni so'karot ||
children.translated_text: He performed each of these austerities for a hundred years at a time.

children.text: tataḥ svadehādutkṛtya karṣaṃ karṣaṃ dine dine
children.translated_text: Then, cutting from his own body piece by piece day after day,
he offered his flesh into the fire, and so he became fleshless.
When he had become fleshless and had become a mass of austerity,
all beings everywhere blazed with his heat.

children.text: udvignāśca surāḥ sarve tapasā tasya bhīṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: All the gods were disturbed and frightened by his austerity.
Meanwhile <s>Brahmā</s> became supremely pleased.
To grant <s>Tāraka</s> a boon, he went from the abode of the thirty gods.

children.text: prāpya taṃ śailarājānaṃ sa gireḥ kandarasthitam
children.translated_text: Having reached that king of mountains, and him staying in the cave of the mountain,

children.text: uvāca tārakaṃ devo girā madhurayā yutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the god addressed <s>Tāraka</s> with a sweet voice.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
My son, enough. Let your austerity cease; now nothing is impossible for you.

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva ruciraṃ yatte manasi vartate ||
children.translated_text: "Choose a fair boon, whatever is present in your mind."
Thus addressed, the daitya <s>Tāraka</s>, bowing to the self-born lord,
spoke, standing with joined palms, bowed down, and wide in stride.
<s>Tāraka</s> said:
O you who dwell in the minds of divine beings, you know the actions of creatures.
People are generally desirous of requiting what has been done to them and eager for victory.
By the law of our birth we have an established enmity with the immortals,

children.text: taiśca niḥśeṣitā daityāḥ krūraiḥ saṃtyajya dharmitām
children.translated_text: and by those cruel ones the daityas have been annihilated, after they abandoned righteousness.
My thought is that I should become their rescuer.
May I be incapable of being slain by all beings and by the weapons of the greatly powerful.

children.text: syāmahaṃ paramo hyeṣa varo mama hṛdi sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is the supreme boon that rests in my heart.

children.text: etanme dehi deveśa nānyo me rocate varaḥ
children.translated_text: Grant this to me, O lord of gods; no other boon pleases me.
Then <s>Viriñci</s>, leader of the gods, said to that daitya:

children.text: na yujyante vinā mṛtyuṃ dehino daityasattama
children.translated_text: Embodied beings cannot rightly exist without death, O best of daityas.
Therefore choose even some form of death from which you feel no fear.
Then the lord of daityas, after considering, chose death from a child of seven days,
the great asura being deluded by arrogance.
And <s>Brahmā</s>, having granted him the boon, whatever was desired in his mind,
went to heaven, the god, and the daitya too went to his own abode.
When that daitya had emerged from his austerities, the lords of the daityas
surrounded him, just as the hosts of gods in heaven surround the thousand-eyed one.
When <s>Tāraka</s>, delight of the daityas, was established in that great kingdom,
the seasons, embodied and augmented by the qualities of their proper times,
became his servants, and so did the guardians of the worlds in every way.
Beauty, brilliance, firmness, intelligence, and fortune, beholding the dānava,
surrounded him, full of virtues, all of them without defect.
His limbs were anointed with black aloe, and he was adorned with a great crown.
His body was bound with lovely armlets, and he sat upon a great lion-throne.
The foremost apsarases fanned him intensely, and they never ceased.
The moon and sun served as lamps on his paths, and the wind served among his fans.
Death became his forerunner, O best of sages.

children.text: evaṃ prayāti kāle tu vitate tārakāsuraḥ
children.translated_text: As time passed in this way over a long span, <s>Tārakāsura</s>
spoke to his ministers, the daitya being puffed up by the abundant boon.
<s>Tāraka</s> said:

children.text: rājyena kāraṇaṃ kiṃ me tvanākramya triviṣṭapam
children.translated_text: What use is kingship to me if I do not invade heaven?
If I do not make the gods pay for their enmity, what peace can there be in my heart?
Even today the immortals still enjoy their shares of sacrifices in heaven.

children.text: viṣṇuḥ śriyaṃ na jahati tiṣṭhate ca gatabhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> does not abandon <s>Śrī</s>, and he stands free from confusion.
The beloveds of the immortals are pressed by heavenly women at ease,
lotus-bearing and fragrant with wine, in the playgrounds of heaven.

children.text: labdhvā janma na yaḥ kaścidghaṭayetpauruṣaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: A man who, having obtained birth, does not somehow exert his manly valor,

children.text: janma tasya vṛthā bhūtam ajanmā tu viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: his birth has become fruitless; non-birth is preferable.

children.text: mātāpitṛbhyāṃ na karoti kāmānbandhūnaśokānna karoti yo vā
children.translated_text: A man who does not fulfill the wishes of his mother and father, or does not make his kinsmen free from sorrow,

children.text: kīrtiṃ hi vā nārjayate himābhāṃ pumānsa jāto'pi mṛto mataṃ me ||
children.translated_text: or does not win fame white as snow, though born, is in my opinion dead.
Therefore, for the conquest of the chief immortals and for the seizure of the fortune of the three worlds, quickly

children.text: saṃyojyatāṃ me rathamaṣṭacakraṃ balaṃ ca me durjayadaityacakram
children.translated_text: let my eight-wheeled chariot be harnessed, and let my force, the unconquerable host of daityas, be readied,

children.text: dhvajaṃ ca me kāñcanapaṭṭanaddhaṃ chattraṃ ca me mauktikajālabaddham ||
children.translated_text: and let my banner, bound with golden cloth, and my parasol, bound with a net of pearls, be prepared.

children.text: tārakasya vacaḥ śrutvā grasano nāma dānavaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Tāraka</s>'s words, a dānava named <s>Grasana</s>,
the strong commander of the daitya king, did just so.
Striking the deep-sounding war drum and quickly summoning the daityas,
he prepared the chariot, adorned with eight wheels and a thousand horses,
embellished with white garments and four yojanas broad,
provided with many pleasure-houses and charming with song and music,
like the aerial car of the god <s>Śatakratu</s>, lord of the gods.
The daityas, lords of ten crores, were of fierce valor among daityas.
At their head was <s>Jambha</s>; next after him was <s>Kujambha</s>;
<s>Mahiṣa</s>, <s>Kuñjara</s>, <s>Megha</s>, <s>Kālanemi</s>, and <s>Nimi</s> likewise,

children.text: mathano jambhakaḥ śumbho daityendrā daśa nāyakāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mathana</s>, <s>Jambhaka</s>, and <s>Śumbha</s>: these ten daitya lords were leaders.
There were also hundreds of others capable of splitting the earth.
The lords of daityas, with bodies like mountains, were of fierce courage.
They bore many kinds of weapons and were skilled in many weapons and missiles.
<s>Tāraka</s>'s emblem was terrible and adorned with gold.
And by a makara-emblem, the general <s>Grasana</s>, destroyer of foes, was marked.
<s>Jambha</s>'s banner had a ghoul-like face made of iron.
On <s>Kujambha</s>'s banner there was a donkey with a shaking tail.
On <s>Mahiṣa</s>'s golden standard there was then a jackal.
On <s>Śumbha</s>'s banner a raven, raised up and made of black iron, stood.
The banners of the others likewise had arrangements of many forms.
With a hundred swift tigers garlanded with gold
<s>Grasana</s>'s chariot was yoked, adorned with a network of small bells.

children.text: śatenāpi ca siṃhānāṃ ratho jambhasya durjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And with a hundred lions was yoked the unconquerable chariot of <s>Jambha</s>.
<s>Kujambha</s>'s chariot was yoked with donkeys with ghoul-like faces.
<s>Mahiṣa</s>'s chariot was drawn by camels, and <s>Gaja</s>'s by horses.
<s>Meṣa</s>'s was drawn by fearsome panthers, and <s>Kālanemi</s>'s by elephants.
<s>Nimi</s>, mounted, was carried by intoxicated great elephants like mountains,
four-tusked, fragrant with rut-fluid, trained, and terrible as clouds.
They also had black horses a hundred hastas long, adorned with gold.
In the southern quarter, adorned with a mass of white fly-whisks,
his limbs beautiful with white sandal paste and gleaming with garlands of many flowers,
the lord of daityas named <s>Mathana</s>, noose in hand, shone forth.
<s>Jambhaka</s> had mounted a camel wreathed in a net of little bells.
The dānava <s>Śumbha</s> had mounted a great black-and-white ram,
and other heroic dānavas too went on many kinds of mounts.
They were fierce, wondrous in deed, adorned with earrings and turbans,
wearing various upper garments and ornamented with many kinds of garlands.
They were rich with many fragrant scents and praised by many groups of bards,
with many musical instruments sounding, and mighty chariot-warriors in the vanguard.
Those great asuras in that army were intent on tales of many acts of valor,
and the force of that lion among daityas appeared terrifying in form.
Crowded with intoxicated, fierce elephants, horses, and chariots,
with many foot-soldiers and standards, it set forth for war against the immortals.
Meanwhile <s>Vāyu</s>, the messenger of the gods, in the aerial realm,
saw that dānava army and went to report it to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: sa gatvā tu sabhāṃ divyāṃ mahendrasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone to the divine assembly of the high-souled <s>Mahendra</s>,
he announced, in the midst of the gods, that matter which had arisen.
Hearing it, the king of the gods closed his eyes,
and at the proper time the mighty-armed one spoke these words to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
<s>Indra</s> said:
This severe clash of the gods with the dānavas has now arrived.
Tell me what should be done here, furnished with policy and expedient means.
Hearing this speech of <s>Mahendra</s>, the lord of speech,
the greatly fortunate <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, noble in understanding, spoke thus.
Policy is remembered as fourfold, beginning with conciliation and bearing its standard.
For those who desire conquest, best of the suras, this is the eternal rule.
Conciliation, division, gift, and punishment are its set of four limbs.
In policy these are applied in order, according to place, time, enemy, fitness, and sequence.
A greedy and cruel man who has gained support is not within the reach of peace;
only when tormented, his confidence broken, does a wicked man become manageable.
Conciliation has no place among the daityas, since they have obtained support.

children.text: jātidharmeṇa vā bhedyā dānaṃ prāptaśriye ca kim ||
children.translated_text: Could they be divided by their inherited nature? And what is a gift to those who have gained prosperity?
Here punishment is the single expedient, if it is acceptable to you.

children.text: durjaneṣu kṛtaṃ sāma mahadyāti ca vandhyatām ||
children.translated_text: Conciliation practiced toward wicked men becomes utterly fruitless.
Cruel men decide that the conciliation of the high-souled arises from fear.
Straightforwardness, noble-mindedness, compassion, and restraint in policy

children.text: manyante durjanā nityaṃ sāma cāpi bhayodayāt
children.translated_text: the wicked always regard in that way, and conciliation too as born from fear.
Therefore reliance on valor is better for attacking a wicked man.
When he has been attacked, proper action is justified; this is the great vow of the good.
A wicked man is never fit to become a good man.
Even a good man may at times wish to abandon his own nature.
Thus my understanding judges; you must decide in this matter.
Thus addressed, the thousand-eyed one said to him, "So indeed it is,"
and after considering what should be done, he spoke in the assembly of the immortals.
<s>Indra</s> said:
Listen attentively to my speech, dwellers in heaven.
You are eaters of the sacrifice, inwardly content, and exceedingly sattvic.

children.text: sve mahimni sthitā nityaṃ jagataḥ paripālakāḥ
children.translated_text: Always established in your own greatness, you are protectors of the world,
yet the lords of the dānavas are oppressing you without cause.

children.text: teṣāṃ sāmādi naivāsti daṇḍa eva vidhīyatām
children.translated_text: For them there is no conciliation and the rest; punishment alone must be prescribed.
Let preparation for battle be made; let my army be assembled.
Let the weapons be honored, and let the weapon-deities be worshiped.
Let the immortals yoke my mounts and vehicles.
Having made <s>Yama</s> the general, act quickly in this way, O dwellers in heaven.
Thus addressed, those who were foremost among the gods armed themselves.
For battle, with ten thousand horses, adorned with golden bells,
endowed with many wondrous qualities and reached by all the deities,
the invincible chariot of the king of the gods was prepared by <s>Mātali</s>.
<s>Yama</s>, mounted on his buffalo, took his place at the front of the army.
He was surrounded on every side by a host of fierce attendants,
his eyes filling the sky with flames blazing like the end of an age.
<s>Hutāśana</s>, mounted on a goat, stood with spear in hand.
<s>Pavana</s>, goad in hand, was spread out with tremendous speed.
The blessed lord of the waters himself had mounted the king of serpents.
The sky-going god, lord of rākṣasas, was in a chariot yoked with men.
Terrible and furnished with a sharp sword, he stood ready in battle.
The god <s>Dhanādhyakṣa</s>, armed with a mace, roared like a great lion.
<s>Candra</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and the two <s>Aśvins</s> were accompanied by fourfold armies.
