children.translated_text: a yakṣa-woman made it like a tree chopped by an axe; taking an elephant's tusk and the casket of its temples,

children.text: vipāṭya mauktikaṃ paraṃ priyaprasādamicchate samāṃsaśoṇitāsavaṃ papuśca yakṣarākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: another, splitting out the excellent pearl, sought her lover's favor. Yakṣas and rākṣasas drank liquor mixed with flesh and blood.

children.text: mṛtāśvakeśavāsitaṃ rasaṃ pragṛhya pāṇinā priyāvimuktajīvitaṃ samānayāsṛgāsavam
children.translated_text: Taking in her hand a juice scented with the hair of dead horses, she said, "Bring the blood-liquor from the dear one whose life has departed.

children.text: na pathyatāṃ prayāti me gataṃ śmaśānagocaraṃ narasya tajjahātyasau praśasya kiṃnarānanam ||
children.translated_text: It does not become palatable to me, being fit for the cremation ground; she abandons that man's face, praising a kiṃnara-face.

children.text: sa nāga eṣa no bhayaṃ dadhāti muktajīvito na dānavasya śakyate mayā tadekayānanam
children.translated_text: This elephant, its life released, gives us no fear; that single vehicle of the <s>dānava</s> cannot be managed by me alone."

children.text: iti priyāya vallabhā vadanti yakṣayoṣitaḥ pare kapālapāṇayaḥ piśācayakṣarākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the yakṣa women speak to their dear beloveds; elsewhere there are piśācas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas with skulls in their hands.

children.text: vadanti dehi dehi me mamātibhakṣyacāriṇaḥ pare'vatīrya śoṇitāpagāsu dhautamūrtayā
children.translated_text: Others, eaters of what is utterly improper as food, cry, "Give, give it to me!" and, descending into rivers of blood with their bodies washed,

children.text: pitṝn pratarpya devatāḥ samarcayanti cāmiṣair gajoḍupe susaṃsthitāstaranti śoṇitaṃ hradam ||
children.translated_text: they satisfy the ancestors and worship the deities with flesh; standing firmly upon elephant-like rafts, they cross the lake of blood.

children.text: iti pragāḍhasaṃkaṭe surāsure susaṃgare bhayaṃ samujhya durjayā bhaṭāḥ sphuṭanti māninaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that deeply crowded, terrible battle between gods and asuras, proud unconquerable warriors, having cast off fear, burst apart.
Then <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Dhaneśa</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Pavana</s>, and <s>Anala</s>,
and also <s>Yama</s> and <s>Nirṛti</s>, all mighty, took up divine weapons.
All those gods released them in the sky, aiming at the dānavas.
The weapons of the gods, directed against the dānavas, came to futility.
Even in fury they fought, massed together and with a tumultuous onset.

children.text: gatiṃ na vividuścāpi śrāntā daityasya devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Exhausted by the daitya, the gods did not even know what course to take.
Their whole bodies split by the daitya's weapons, they had become powerless.
They clung to one another like cows afflicted by cold.
Seeing the gods in that condition, <s>Hari</s> said to <s>Śakra</s>:

children.text: brahmāstraṃ smara devendra yasyāvadhyo na vidyate
children.translated_text: "Remember the <s>brahmāstra</s>, O <s>Devendra</s>; there is no one who cannot be slain by it."
Prompted by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śakra</s> remembered that missile of great power.
Wise <s>Śakra</s> placed on his bow the arrow, always worshiped, destroyer of enemies, consecrated and meant for striking foes;
then his mind was fixed in meditative concentration upon the mantra.

children.text: sa mantramuccārya yatāntarāśayo vadhāya daityasya dhiyābhisaṃdhya tu
children.translated_text: He uttered the mantra, his inner self controlled, and with his thought directed toward the daitya's death.
Drawing the unblunted, radiant arrow back to his ear, he released it, looking upward toward the path of the sky.

children.text: athāsuraḥ prekṣya mahāstramāhitaṃ vihāya māyāmavanau vyatiṣṭhata
children.translated_text: Then the asura, seeing the great missile set in place, abandoned his magic and stood upon the earth.

children.text: pravepamānena mukhena śuṣyatā balena gātreṇa ca saṃbhramākulaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His face trembled and dried up; in strength and body he was shaken and confused.
Then in the great battle the arrow, consecrated by that best of missiles and shaped like a half-moon,
became bound to <s>Purandara</s>'s bowstring, mimicking with its body the disk of a new-risen sun.
<s>Jambha</s>'s head, with its earrings, fell, crowded with the flashing splendor of the points of his crown, fragrant with many flowers placed upon it,
and with hair like a mass of scattered smoke and flame.
When <s>Jambha</s> had been slain, the lords of the dānavas turned their faces away.
Then, their designs shattered, they went to where <s>Tāraka</s> was.
Looking upon them terrified, and hearing what had happened, he went into supreme wrath.

children.text: sa jambhadānavendraṃ tu surai raṇamukhe hatam ||
children.translated_text: For the lord of dānavas <s>Jambha</s> had been killed by the gods at the front of battle.
<s>Tāraka</s> entered a state full of arrogance, fury, pride, and valor,
manifest in gesture yet inwardly controlled.
Mounting his victorious chariot, drawn by a thousand birds,
the lord of dānavas, in fury, went against the gods at the front of battle.
He was equipped with every weapon and protected by every missile.
He possessed the prosperity of the three worlds and had an enormous, wide-open mouth.
Swiftly he rushed into battle, surrounded by a great army.
Leaving aside the elephant <s>Airāvata</s>, whose whole body had been wounded by <s>Jambha</s>'s missiles,
the guardians of the worlds stood around on every side of that chariot of <s>Indra</s>, ready, guarded by <s>Mātali</s>, and radiant with <s>Indra</s>'s splendor,
adorned with refined heated gold and furnished with great jewels,
four yojanas broad and adorned by hosts of siddhas,
sung over by gandharvas and kinnaras, and thronged with the dancing of apsarases,
equipped with every weapon, spacious, and shining with varied workmanship,
that chariot of the king of gods.
Armored, together with the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>, the guardians of the worlds stood there.
Then the earth shook; then a harsh wind blew.
Then the oceans rose up; then the sun's radiance vanished.
Then darkness arose, and after that the stars could not be seen.
Then the weapons blazed; then the army trembled.
On one side stood the daitya <s>Tāraka</s>, and on the other the host of gods.
On one side was the sinking of the worlds, on the other the protection of the universe.
All moving and unmoving beings, divided between gods and asuras,
though split in two, had come into a single confrontation, as spectators saw.
Whatever thing in the three worlds had the nature of existence,
all of it was seen there, with its powers gathered into one mass.

children.text: astrāṇi tejāṃsi dhanāni dhairyaṃ senābalaṃ vīryaparākramau ca
children.translated_text: Weapons, energies, wealth, courage, military strength, heroic power, and valor

children.text: sattvaujasāṃ tannikaraṃ babhūva surāsurāṇāṃ tapaso balena ||
children.translated_text: became that aggregate of the vigor and might of gods and asuras through the power of ascetic force.
Then, as he came toward them, they pierced <s>Tāraka</s> in the heart
with nine arrows whose joints were bent and whose tips were like fire.
The lord of daityas disregarded those arrows of the gods that had entered his heart.
The dānava pierced the gods with nine arrows each.
They were like foremost darts sprung up for the bearing of the world.
Then in the battle the gods released an unbroken mass of arrows.
It was like the ceaseless fall of tears from beloved women.
The dānava destroyed that shower before it even reached him, while it was still in the sky.
Just as a bad son destroys his own great family, famous, supremely advanced, very pure, and descended in proper order,
with ill-conducted acts that have come to prominence,
so, having warded off that net of arrows hurled by the arms of the gods,
the dānava filled the sky, the directions, and the earth with arrows.

children.text: cicheda puṅkhadeśeṣu svake sthāne ca lāghavāt
children.translated_text: With agility he cut them off at the region of their feathered shafts and in their own place.
with nets of arrows whose tips were exceedingly sharp, fletched with feathers of kaṅka birds and peacocks;
drawn back to the ear, spotless, and gleaming with gold and silver,
like meanings of treatises that, when doubt has arisen, are understood otherwise and variously construed.

children.text: tataḥ śatena bāṇānāṃ śakraṃ vivyādha dānavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the dānava pierced <s>Śakra</s> with a hundred arrows,

children.text: nārāyaṇaṃ ca saptatyā navatyā ca hutāśanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with seventy, and <s>Hutāśana</s> with ninety.
He struck <s>Māruta</s> on the head with ten, and <s>Yama</s> likewise with ten,

children.text: dhanadaṃ caiva saptatyā varuṇaṃ ca tathāṣṭabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhanada</s> with seventy, and <s>Varuṇa</s> likewise with eight.
The daitya pierced <s>Nirṛti</s> with twenty, and then again with eight,
and again he pierced each one, one by one, with ten arrows apiece.

children.text: tathā ca mātaliṃ daityo vivyādha tribhirāśugaiḥ
children.translated_text: And the daitya pierced <s>Mātali</s> with three swift shafts,
and he pierced <s>Garuḍa</s> with ten winged arrows.
Again the daitya, with arrows whose joints were bent, reduced the gods'

children.text: cakāra varmajātāni cicheda ca dhanūṃṣi tu
children.translated_text: various coats of armor to particles and cut apart their bows.

children.text: tato vikavacā devā vidhanuṣkāḥ śaraiḥ kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the gods were made armorless and bowless by his arrows.

children.text: athānyāni cāpāni tasminsaroṣā raṇe lokapālā gṛhītvā samantāt
children.translated_text: Then, angrily taking up other bows on every side in that battle, the guardians of the worlds
hacked at the lord of dānavas with inexhaustible arrows. Then the dānava's eyes were reddened with rage.
He showered fire-like arrows upon the immortals; then, taking up an arrow like the fire at the end of an aeon,

children.text: jaghānorasi kṣipramindraṃ subāhuṃ mahendro vyakampadrathopastha eva ||
children.translated_text: he swiftly struck long-armed <s>Indra</s> in the chest, and mighty <s>Indra</s> trembled right on the platform of his chariot.
Then in the sky the dānava looked upon <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose power had arisen, like the disk of a thousand suns,
and playfully struck him at the root of the shoulder with two arrows; then <s>Keśava</s>'s <s>Śārṅga</s> bow fell before him.

children.text: tatastārakaḥ pretanāthaṃ pṛṣatkairvasuṃ tasya savye smarankṣudrabhāvam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Tāraka</s> struck the lord of the dead with shafts and, recalling his weakness, hit the Vasu on his left side;
and in battle the unconquerable daitya king dried up the body of the lord of waters with fire-like arrows.
With fire-like arrows the daitya quickly made the rākṣasas utterly terrified in the quarters,
and with harsh shafts, used for disfigurement, the asura lord brought <s>Anila</s> to distress as if in play.

children.text: kṣaṇāllabdhacittāḥ svayaṃ viṣṇuśakrānalādyāḥ susaṃhatya tīkṣṇaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ
children.translated_text: In a moment <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Anala</s>, and the others regained consciousness, gathered closely, and with sharp shafts

children.text: pracakruḥ pracaṇḍena daityena sārdhaṃ mahāsaṃgaraṃ saṃgaragrāsakalpam ||
children.translated_text: began a great battle with the fierce daitya, as if it were the devouring mouth of war.

children.text: athānamya cāpaṃ haristīkṣṇabāṇair hanatsārathiṃ daityarājasya hṛdyam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s>, bending his bow, struck the charioteer of the daitya king in the heart with sharp arrows;

children.text: dhvajaṃ dhūmaketuḥ kirīṭaṃ mahendro dhaneśo dhanuḥ kāñcanānaddhapṛṣṭham
children.translated_text: <s>Dhūmaketu</s> struck his banner, mighty <s>Indra</s> his crown, and <s>Dhaneśa</s> the bow with its gold-bound back;

children.text: yamo bāhudaṇḍaṃ rathāṅgāni vāyurniśācāriṇām īśvarasyāpi varma ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> struck his staff-like arm, <s>Vāyu</s> the wheels of his chariot, and even the armor of the lord of night-roamers.
Seeing that battle, waged by the immortals with unfeigned valor,
the lord of daityas, whose allies were the pair of his own arms, acted in battle.
He hurled a terrible club at the thousand-eyed one in the fight.
Seeing the irresistible club coming through the sky,
<s>Pākaśāsana</s> leapt from the chariot and went down to the ground.
The club too fell upon the chariot platform with a harsh crash.

children.text: sa rathaṃ cūrṇayāmāsa na mamāra ca mātaliḥ
children.translated_text: It crushed the chariot to powder, but <s>Mātali</s> did not die.
Taking up a paṭṭiśa (spear), the daitya struck <s>Keśava</s> in the chest.
He too sank unconscious upon <s>Garuḍa</s>'s shoulder.
With his sword he cut apart the mount of the lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: yamaṃ ca pātayāmāsa bhūmau daityo bhuśuṇḍinā
children.translated_text: And with a bhuśuṇḍī club the daitya knocked <s>Yama</s> down upon the ground.
With a bhindipāla missile he struck <s>Vahni</s> on the head.
With both arms he lifted <s>Vāyu</s> up and threw him to the earth.
In anger he battered <s>Dhaneśa</s> with the end of his bow.
Then, one by one among the hosts of gods in the battle,
the daitya lord of immeasurable valor struck them with countless weapons.
In a moment <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having regained consciousness, grasped his irresistible discus,
stained with the fat of dānava lords and eagerly faced by flesh-eaters.
<s>Keśava</s> released it against the firm chest of the lord of dānavas.
The discus, shining like the sun, fell upon the daitya's heart.
Then it shattered on his body like a blue lotus on stone.
Then mighty <s>Indra</s> hurled the thunderbolt, long worshipped,
in which <s>Śakra</s>'s hope of victory in battle with the lord of dānavas had rested.
When it reached the body of valorous <s>Tāraka</s>,
it shattered, its flames scattered, broken into a hundred fragments.
The weapon released by <s>Vāyu</s> against the asura's chest came to destruction;
it was a blazing goad, fire-like and resembling a thunderbolt.
Seeing the goad destroyed in battle, <s>Vāyu</s>,
angry, uprooted a lordly mountain, its caves filled with flowering trees,
five yojanas broad, and hurled it at the lord of dānavas.
As that mountain came toward him, the daitya, smiling then,
caught it with his left hand as if playing with a child's ball.
Then <s>Kṛtānta</s>, overcome by anger, raised his staff,

children.text: daityendraṃ mūrdhni cikṣepa bhrāmya vegena durjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whirled it with force, and hurled it at the head of the unconquerable daitya lord.
It fell upon the asura's head, but the daitya did not even notice it.
Then <s>Jvalana</s> hurled an unconquerable, unassailable śakti (spear), shining like the fire at the end of an aeon,
at the lord of dānavas in battle.
It shone on his chest like a fresh garland of śirīṣa flowers.
Then, drawing from its sheath a sword clear as the sky,
even <s>Nirṛti</s>, guardian of the world, brightening the quarters with its dark gleam,

children.text: cikṣepa dānavendrāya tasya mūrdhni papāta ca
children.translated_text: hurled it at the lord of dānavas, and it fell upon his head.
And the sword, having fallen, quickly broke into a hundred fragments.
But the lord of the waters released against the daitya a noose, fierce, hard to withstand, and terrifying with poisonous fire,
desiring to bind his arms.
When that serpent reached the daitya's arm, it perished at once,
its row of teeth cruel like split saws, its jaw immense.
Then the two <s>Aśvins</s>, together with the <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, and the great serpents,
and yakṣas, rākṣasas, and gandharvas, holding many divine weapons,
all gathered together, very powerful, and struck the lord of daityas.
But their weapons did not cling to his body, which was like a mountain of diamond.
Then <s>Tāraka</s>, lord of dānavas, leapt down from his chariot
and struck down gods by the ten millions with his hands and heels alone.
The remnants of the gods' armies fled apart in terror,
abandoning the quarters and their implements of war.
Then in battle the daitya bound the guardians of the worlds, headed by <s>Indra</s>,
together with <s>Keśava</s>, with firm nooses, like a cattle-killer binding animals.
Mounting his chariot again, he went to his own dwelling,
whose wide mountain-peak was filled with the cries of siddhas and gandharvas.
Praised by the sons of <s>Diti</s> and entertained by apsarases,
he entered his own city in that place as though he were the Fortune of the three worlds.
He sat down on a seat fashioned from ruby jewels.
Then, entertained by kinnaras, gandharvas, and nāga women,
and with his jeweled earrings swaying, he passed a moment in pleasure.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
A doorkeeper appeared, clad in garments like white and blue lotuses.

children.text: sa jānubhyāṃ mahīṃ gatvā pihitāsyaḥ svapāṇinā ||
children.translated_text: Going down to the earth on his knees and covering his mouth with his own hand,
he spoke a clear statement, brief in syllables and distinct,
to the king of daityas, who bore a radiant body like a cluster of suns.
"<s>Kālanemi</s> stands at the gate, having brought the gods in bonds.

children.text: sa vijñāpayati stheyaṃ kva bandibhiriti prabho ||
children.translated_text: He asks, lord, where he should remain with the prisoners."
Hearing that speech of the doorkeeper, the daitya replied:
"Let them stay as they wish. The three worlds are my house.
Only let them be freed from the bondage of the nooses without delay."

children.text: evaṃ kṛte tato devā dūyamānena cetasā ||
children.translated_text: When this had been done, the gods, their minds distressed,
went for refuge to see the lotus-born preceptor of the world.
Those gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> were announced, and, with their heads bowed to the ground,
they praised the lotus-seated one with words whose letters and meanings were clear.
The gods said:
You are the syllable <s>oṃ</s>, born first as the sprout of this universe, the self of the world with its endless divisions.
After its arising, you are the form of being; when you desire its dissolution, homage to you in the form of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: vyaktiṃ nītvā tvaṃ vapuḥ svaṃ mahimnā tasmādaṇḍāt sābhidhānādacintyaḥ
children.translated_text: By your greatness you brought your own body into manifestation from that egg, named and inconceivable,
and from that egg you make the division of heaven and earth into upper and lower halves.
What became manifest on <s>Meru</s> as the life of creatures was yours; thus we know that it shines forth, set in motion by you.

children.text: vyaktaṃ devā janmanaḥ śāśvatasya dyauste mūrdhā locane candrasūryau ||
children.translated_text: The gods know the manifest form of your eternal birth: heaven is your head, the moon and sun your two eyes.

children.text: vyālāḥ keśāḥ śrotrarandhrā diśaste pādau bhūmirnābhirandhre samudrāḥ
children.translated_text: Serpents are your hairs, the quarters are the openings of your ears, earth is your feet, and the oceans are the hollow of your navel.

children.text: māyākāraḥ kāraṇaṃ tvaṃ prasiddho vedaiḥ śānto jyotiṣā tvaṃ vimuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are famed by the Vedas as the maker of māyā and the cause; tranquil, you are released through light.

children.text: vedārtheṣu tvāṃ vivṛṇvanti buddhvā hṛtpadmāntaḥsaṃniviṣṭaṃ purāṇam
children.translated_text: Those who understand the meanings of the Vedas expound you as the ancient one established within the lotus of the heart.

children.text: tvāmātmānaṃ labdhayogā gṛṇanti sāṃkhyairyāstāḥ sapta sūkṣmāḥ praṇītāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who have attained yoga praise you as the Self; the seven subtle principles taught by the Sāṃkhyas are yours.

children.text: tāsāṃ heturyāṣṭamī cāpi gītā tasyāṃ tasyāṃ gīyase vai tvamantam
children.translated_text: Their cause is also sung as the eighth; in each of these, indeed, you are sung as the ultimate limit.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā mūrtiṃ sthūlasūkṣmāṃ cakāra devairbhāvāḥ kāraṇaiḥ kaiściduktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having seen your gross and subtle form, some have described the states of being by means of their causes.

children.text: sambhūtāste tvatta evādisarge bhūyastāṃ tāṃ vāsanāṃ te'bhyupeyuḥ
children.translated_text: Those states arose from you alone at the first creation, and again they took on their various latent dispositions from you.
By your resolve, time, hidden by the attainment of endless māyā, becomes measurable, while the alternatives of number are destroyed.
You are the cause of being, non-being, manifestation, and dissolution; you are that endless one, and, O Self, you are its maker.

children.text: ye'nye sūkṣmāḥ santi tebhyo'bhigītaḥ sthūlā bhāvāścāvṛtāraśca teṣām ||
children.translated_text: Whatever other subtle things exist are sung in relation to those; gross states and their coverings also arise from them.

children.text: tebhyaḥ sthūlaistaiḥ purāṇaiḥ pratīto bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ caivamudbhūtibhājām
children.translated_text: Through those gross and ancient principles, the past and future of beings that partake of arising are known.

children.text: bhāve bhāve bhāvitaṃ tvā yunakti yuktaṃ yuktaṃ vyaktibhāvānnirasya
children.translated_text: In each state, what has been brought into being joins itself to you; joined again and again, it casts off the state of manifestation.

children.text: itthaṃ devo bhaktibhājāṃ śaraṇyastrātā goptā no bhavānantamūrtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O god, refuge of those who share in devotion, be our rescuer and protector, you of endless forms.
Having praised the unchanging <s>Brahmā</s>, the immortals ceased.
Then they stood with their minds intent on praying for the attainment of their desired object.

children.text: evaṃ stuto viriñcistu prasādaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus praised, <s>Viriñci</s> entered into supreme grace.
Pointing with his left hand, the boon-giver addressed the immortals.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
"A woman who is suddenly without a husband, her body bereft of ornaments,
does not shine, O <s>Śakra</s>, when her face and hair are withered.
Though freed from fire, you do not shine because of the smoke,
like one long dwelling in a burned forest, covered as if with ash.
In a body filled with the sickness of <s>Yama</s>, you do not shine,
as one who, though not in difficulty, leans on a staff at every step.
Though you are the lord of night-wanderers, why do you speak as if afraid,
O king of rākṣasas, enemy-wounder, as though you had been wounded by an enemy?
Your body is dried up as if by <s>Varuṇa</s>, like one surrounded by fire,
as you look upon the bloodless noose, released, with serpents around it."

children.text: vāyo bhavān vicetaskas tvaṃ snigdhairiva nirjitaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Vāyu</s>, you are bewildered, as if defeated by those who are gentle.

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ bibheṣi dhanada saṃnyasyaiva kuberatām ||
children.translated_text: Why do you fear, O giver of wealth, as though laying aside the very state of <s>Kubera</s>?
You <s>Rudras</s>, though followers of the trident-bearing one, speak now of having many spears.
By whom was that energy hurled away, even the energy belonging to you?
Your hand has come to uselessness; it does not shine.
Enough, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>, with the disk that has the appearance of a blue lotus.
Why do you, with eyes motionless, behold the worlds sunk in distress?
Why is this being done by you, O one whose faces are turned in every direction?
Thus addressed by that <s>Brahmā</s>, whose form was brahman, the gods,
because speech chiefly belonged to him, urged that <s>Māruta</s> to speak.
Then <s>Śvasana</s>, awakened by the gods headed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
spoke then to the four-faced lord, the mighty teacher of moving and unmoving beings.

children.text: na tu vetsi carācarabhūtagataṃ bhavabhāvamatīva mahānucchritaḥ prabhavaḥ
children.translated_text: You do not know the state of existence pervading all moving and unmoving beings; exalted exceedingly is your great power of production.
You have become one whose ears, expanded by the words of petitioners, are filled with a feeling like eager wonder.
You, O endless one, create the world of beings, with its moving and unmoving embryo divided by qualities.
All this, gods and asuras without remainder, is alike in you; indeed, you are the father, since it is so.

children.text: piturasti tathāpi manovikṛtiḥ saguṇo viguṇo balavānabalaḥ
children.translated_text: Even so, a father's mind is altered: one son has virtues, another lacks them; one is strong, another weak.
Fearless because of the boon obtained from you, the son of <s>Diti</s>, sprung from the thunderbolt-limbed line, is exceedingly strong.

children.text: sacarācaranirmathane kimiti kitavastu kṛto vihito bhavatā
children.translated_text: Why, for the churning up of the moving and unmoving world, did you make this cheat?

children.text: kila deva tvayā sthitaye jagatāṃ mahadadbhutacitraviciguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely, O god, he was appointed by you for the stability of the worlds, though his qualities are greatly wondrous, varied, and distorted.

children.text: api tuṣṭikṛtaḥ śrutakāmaphalā vihitā dvijanāyaka devagaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Were the hosts of gods, O lord of twice-born beings, created by you merely to give satisfaction and to yield the desired fruits heard in scripture?
Was heaven indeed made constantly for the eaters of sacrifice only by the force of your appointment?

children.text: apahṛtya vimānagaṇaṃ sa kṛto ditijena mahāmarubhūmisamaḥ
children.translated_text: After stealing away the multitude of aerial cars, it has been made by the daitya like a great desert.
You made the king of mountains, possessing surpassing excellence in every quality and covering the whole earth.

children.text: samamiṅgitabhāvavidhiḥ sa girirgaganena sadocchrayatāṃ hi gataḥ
children.translated_text: That mountain, equal in signs and nature, has indeed always risen upward together with the sky.
Fit for dwelling and recreation, it had its peaks and slopes struck by the thunderbolt among the daitya folk.
Its many jewel-caves have been plundered, and it has been made a refuge for assemblies of many daityas.

children.text: surarāja sa tasya bhayena gataṃ vyadadhādaśarīra ito'pi vṛthā ||
children.translated_text: O king of gods, out of fear of him that one became as though bodiless and went away from here in vain.
Long opened for use, with the faces of the directions filled by stainless radiance,
this inert mass of the gods' weapons was fashioned by you yourself at the beginning of the age.
Having reached the body of the son of <s>Diti</s>, it broke into a hundred pieces, like the confused judgment of a small-minded man.
With our limbs soiled by showers and dust, we stood at his gate as miserable petitioners.
Only with difficulty did we obtain entrance to that enemy of the immortals.
O god, in his assembly the immortals were made to sit even in a low place.
Then, while we were silent before men holding staffs, we were laughed at by them.
You are of great worth, have accomplished every aim, and speak little.
Yet, O immortals, perform flattering service and speak much.
Are you standing in attendance at the appointed time of the lion among daityas together with <s>Śakra</s>?
Speak! Thus the daitya's servants laughed at us greatly.
The seasons, embodied, attend upon him day and night.
Frightened because of some offense committed, they never leave him.
With the rhythm of three strings and measures, by siddhas, gandharvas, and kinnaras,

children.text: surāgam upadhā nityaṃ gīyate tasya veśmasu ||
children.translated_text: divine music is always sung as accompaniment in his mansions.
He strikes down his friends with unprepared instruments, through inversions of importance and insignificance.
He abandons those who have sought refuge and has given up reliance on truth.

children.text: iti niḥśeṣamathavā niḥśeṣaṃ vai na śakyate
children.translated_text: Thus, or rather completely, yet it is not possible completely
to describe his insolence; O creator, you are the final resort there.
Having thus been addressed by the gods about the daitya's conduct, the self-born god,
the blessed lord whose lotus-face was smiling, then spoke to the gods.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
The daitya <s>Tāraka</s> cannot be slain by any of the gods or asuras.

children.text: yasya vadhyaḥ sa nādyāpi jātastribhuvane pumān ||
children.translated_text: The man by whom he is to be slain has not yet been born in the three worlds.
I restrained him with the gift of a boon after satisfying him,
the king whose asceticism at present had the nature of burning the three worlds.

children.text: sa ca vavre vadhaṃ daityaḥ śiśutaḥ saptavāsarāt
children.translated_text: And that daitya chose death from a child seven days old.
That seven-day-old child will come from <s>Śaṃkara</s> and the rest.
He, radiant like the sun, will become the slayer of <s>Tāraka</s>.
But at present the blessed lord <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the master, is without a wife.
As for what I said of him, that he always had his hand turned upward,

children.text: uttāno varadaḥ pāṇireṣa devyāḥ sadaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: this open palm, granting boons, is always for the goddess.

children.text: himācalasya duhitā sā tu devī bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: She will be the goddess, the daughter of <s>Himācala</s>.
From her, <s>Śarva</s>, like fire from the fire-stick in the forest,
will beget that child; when he has obtained him, <s>Tāraka</s> will be overcome.

children.text: mayāpyupāyaḥ sa kṛto yathaivaṃ hi bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: I too have made the means by which this will indeed come to pass.
And the remainder of his power will perish after that.
Wait for a short time with minds free from fear.
Thus addressed by him, by the lotus-born one himself, the thirty gods,
the dwellers in heaven bowed to that lord and departed as was proper.
Then, when the gods had gone, <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire of the worlds,
the blessed lord remembered <s>Night</s>, who had formerly arisen from his own body.
Then the blessed goddess <s>Rātri</s> approached the grandsire.
Seeing her in a secluded place, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to <s>Vibhāvarī</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
O <s>Vibhāvarī</s>, mighty one, this great matter concerning the gods has come before you;

children.text: tatkartavyaṃ tvayā devi śṛṇu kāryasya niścayam ||
children.translated_text: it must be done by you, goddess. Hear the settled course of the task.
There is a lord of daityas named <s>Tāraka</s>, a banner of the gods' enemies, unconquered;
for his destruction the blessed lord <s>Īśvara</s> will beget a son.
That son of his will become the one who brings about the end of <s>Tāraka</s>.
She who was <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s wife, <s>Satī</s>, the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>,
that goddess died in anger, for a certain other cause.
She will become the daughter of <s>Himaśaila</s>, bringing welfare to the worlds.
Through separation from her, <s>Hara</s>, thinking the three worlds empty,
will remain practicing austerity in a cave of <s>Himaśaila</s> frequented by siddhas.
Awaiting her birth, he will dwell there for some time.
From those two, after they have practiced intense austerities, one of great strength will be born;
he will be the destroyer of that daitya <s>Tāraka</s>.

children.text: jātamātrā tu sā devī svalpasaṃjñā ca bhāminī ||
children.translated_text: But as soon as that lovely goddess is born, with only slight awareness,
she will be deeply distressed by separation and eager for union with <s>Hara</s>.
O fair-faced one, the union of those two will come after they have practiced intense austerities.

children.text: tatastābhyāṃ tu janitaḥ svalpo vākkalaho bhavet
children.translated_text: Then a slight quarrel of words will arise between them.
Even from that, still more uncertainty is seen with regard to <s>Tāraka</s>.
Therefore, when those two are united and absorbed in love-play,

children.text: vighnastvayā vidhātavyo yathā tābhyāṃ tathā śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: an obstacle must be contrived by you. Hear how it is to be done for them.

children.text: garbhasthāne ca tanmātuḥ svena rūpeṇa rañjaya
children.translated_text: At the womb-place of that mother, color her with your own form.
Then <s>Śarva</s>, leaving her aside and resting, will jokingly

children.text: bhartsayiṣyati tāṃ devīṃ tataḥ sā kupitā satī
children.translated_text: reproach that goddess; then she, <s>Satī</s>, becoming angry,
will go away to perform austerity. From that austerity again
<s>Śarva</s> will beget one adorned with the radiance of his beloved;
he will certainly be the slayer of the enemies of the gods.
You too, goddess, must slay the dānavas, who are hard for the worlds to conquer.
But as long as <s>Satī</s>, with her collected virtues transferred into another body,
has not united with him, so long you will not be able to slay the daityas.
When this has been done, after practicing austerity, the goddess who brings about creation and dissolution,
<s>Umā</s>, with her observance completed, will come into being.
Then the mountain-born goddess will assume that very form of yours.
Your own body too, innate with her, will become <s>Ekānaṃśā</s>.
United with a portion of that form, you will abide in <s>Umā</s>.
The world will worship you as <s>Ekānaṃśā</s>, giver of boons,
all-pervading, accomplishing desires, in many divisions and manifold forms.
By the expounders of brahman you are called <s>Gāyatrī</s>, whose face is the syllable Oṃ;
by great-armed kings, <s>Ākrānti</s>, with a powerful form.

children.text: tvaṃ bhūriti viśāṃ mātā śūdraiḥ śaivīti pūjitā
children.translated_text: By the common people you are worshiped as <s>Bhū</s>, the mother, and by śūdras as <s>Śaivī</s>.
For sages you are unshakable patience; for the self-restrained you are compassion.
You are a mass of great stratagems, and policy for those who extend governance.
You are the delimitation of objects; you are endeavor, lying in the hearts of living beings.

children.text: tvaṃ muktiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvadehinām
children.translated_text: You are liberation for all beings; you are the path for all embodied creatures.

children.text: tvaṃ ca kīrtimatāṃ kīrtistvaṃ mūrtiḥ sarvadehinām ||
children.translated_text: You are the fame of the famous; you are the form of all embodied beings.
You are passion for those whose minds are impassioned, and delight for those who look with joy.
You are beauty for those adorned with ornaments; you are peace for those afflicted by painful deeds.

children.text: tvaṃ bhrāntiḥ sarvabodhānāṃ tvaṃ gatiḥ kratuyājinām
children.translated_text: You are delusion in all acts of knowing; you are the destination of those who sacrifice at rites.

children.text: jaladhīnāṃ mahāvelā tvaṃ ca līlā vilāsinām ||
children.translated_text: Among oceans you are the great shore, and among the playful you are play.
You are the arising of things; you are their stability, protector of the worlds.
You are <s>Kālarātrī</s>, destroyer of the entire series of worlds without remainder.
You are <s>Vibhāvarī</s>, giving joy through the embrace of a beloved neck.
Thus, goddess, you are worshiped in the world through many kinds of forms.

children.text: ye tvāṃ stoṣyanti varade pūjayiṣyanti vāpi ye
children.translated_text: Those who will praise you, giver of boons, and those who will worship you,
will obtain all desires, if they are disciplined; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: ityuktā tu niśā devī tathetyuktvā kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the goddess <s>Niśā</s> said, 'So be it,' and, with folded hands,

children.text: jagāma tvaritā tūrṇaṃ gṛhaṃ himagireḥ param ||
children.translated_text: went quickly and at once to the excellent house of <s>Himagiri</s>.
There, in a great palace, she saw <s>Menā</s> seated, resting against a jeweled wall,
with the lotus of her face somewhat pale in hue.
Her slightly dark face was bent down by the weight of her swelling, elevated breasts;
she was attended by chief mantras bound together with groups of great herbs.
She bore a great serpent for life-protection, bound with gold,
in a chamber illumined by the great light from rows of jeweled lamps,
strewn with much white mustard seed and furnished with a charming retinue,
bright with bedding spread upon a ground-couch covered by clean cloths,
delightful with the fragrance of incense and prepared with the scent of sarja resin.

children.text: tataḥ krameṇa divase gate dūraṃ vibhāvarī ||
children.translated_text: Then, as the day gradually passed far on, <s>Vibhāvarī</s>
expanded toward a happy outcome in <s>Menā</s>'s great house.
When the people were almost asleep and the attendants had become sleep itself,
when the moon was clear in light and night-birds were wandering,
when the courtyard was covered by hosts of beings that roam at night,
and when beloved fortunate people were fastened in close embraces around the neck,
then, as the two lotus-eyes of <s>Menā</s> became somewhat troubled,
Night entered her mouth, after a long and manifest union,
and gradually entered the belly of the woman who would give birth to the mother of the world.

children.text: āviveśāntaraṃ janma manyamānā kṣapā tu vai
children.translated_text: Indeed, <s>Kṣapā</s>, thinking this an inner, further birth, entered within.
<s>Vibhāvarī</s> colored the complexion of the goddess within the cave-like wilderness.
Then the beloved of <s>Himagiri</s>, the cause of life for the lord of the world,
gave birth at the brāhma muhūrta, O blessed one, to the future mother of <s>Guha</s>.
As she was being born, creatures, both stationary and moving,
All the inhabitants of all the worlds became happy.
Even for those in hell at that time there arose great happiness equal to heaven.
The minds of embodied beings, even of cruel nature, became peaceful.
Even the lights acquired brightness, and the gods rose high.
The forest-dwelling herbs and the fruits became sweet.

children.text: gandhavanti ca mālyāni vimalaṃ ca nabho'bhavat
children.translated_text: The garlands became fragrant, and the sky became stainless.
The wind was pleasant to the touch, and the directions were very charming.
And by that event, shining with the qualities of sprouting, fruiting, and ripening,
the goddess Earth became full also of rows of rice.
The long-practiced austerities of sages whose selves had been purified,
at that time bore fruit for those of stainless mind.
Weapons that had been forgotten came again into manifestation.
The power of the chief tīrthas (sacred fords) then became most holy.
In the sky the gods were present in thousands of aerial cars,
with <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Agni</s> at their head.
They sent down a shower of flowers upon that snowy mountain.
The chief gandharvas sang, and hosts of apsarases danced.
<s>Meru</s> and the other mountains too, embodied and very powerful,
when that great festival had arrived, came with divine gifts in their hands.
The rivers and oceans also came together from every side.
The Snow Mountain became, in the world, so attended by all moving and unmoving beings.
That best of immovable mountains became worthy of service and approach, and most excellent.
Having experienced the festival, the gods gladly went to their own abodes.
Through the qualities of gods, gandharvas, lordly nāgas, mountains, rocks, and the earth,
the goddess, daughter of the Snow Mountain, then by her own prior excellence
was gradually brought to growth, radiant with fortune and brilliance by the wise.
Gradually, through incomparable awakenings of beauty and good fortune,
the mountain-born girl conquered the three worlds and also adorned them.
Meanwhile <s>Śakra</s> remembered <s>Nārada</s>, honored by the gods,
the divine seer, with urgency for the accomplishment of his purpose.

children.text: smṛtiṃ śakrasya vijñāya jātāṃ tu bhagavāṃstadā ||
children.translated_text: Knowing that the thought of <s>Śakra</s> had arisen, the blessed one then
came, joined with joy, to the dwelling of great <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: taṃ sa dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaḥ samutthāya mahāsanāt ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the thousand-eyed one rose from his great seat.
<s>Vāsava</s> honored him with water for the feet and the other due offerings.
Having received according to rule that worship offered by <s>Śakra</s>,
<s>Nārada</s> asked the god, the chastiser of <s>Pāka</s>, about his welfare.

children.text: pṛṣṭe ca kuśale śakraḥ provāca vacanaṃ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he had been asked about his welfare, the lord <s>Śakra</s> spoke these words.
<s>Indra</s> said:
Since the sprout of welfare has now arisen in the three worlds,
be tireless, O sage, in bringing about the attainment of its fruit.
You know all this in its entirety; nevertheless, as one who urges action,
one reaches supreme satisfaction by reporting a matter to a friend.
Therefore, so that the mountain-born goddess may enter union with <s>Pinākin</s>,
let that undertaking be quickly carried out by all who are on our side.
Having understood the whole matter, the blessed <s>Nārada</s> then took leave of <s>Śakra</s>
and went to the abode of the Snow Mountain.
There, at the gate crowded with painted canes and creepers,
the foremost brahmin-sage was greeted by the Snow Mountain, who had come out before him.

children.text: saha praviśya bhavanaṃ bhuvo bhūṣaṇatāṃ gatam
children.translated_text: Entering the palace together, which had become an ornament of the earth,

children.text: nivedite svayaṃ haime himaśaile na vistṛte ||
children.translated_text: when the golden, spacious great seat had been presented by the Snow Mountain himself,
the best of sages, of incomparable splendor, sat down.
As was fitting, the mountain offered him arghya and water for the feet.
The sage then accepted that arghya according to rule.
When the best of sages had accepted the arghya, the mountain asked him in a smooth voice
about the welfare of his austerities, slowly, his lotus-face blooming.
The sage too then asked the king of mountains about his welfare.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Ah, O great mountain, all excellences have descended into your dwelling.
O immovable one, the breadth of your caves is equal to that of the mind.
Your gravity, consisting of a mass of virtues, surpasses even the immovable world.

children.text: prasannatā ca toyasya manaso'pyadhikā ca te ||
children.translated_text: And the clarity of your water is even greater than that of the mind.
O lord of mountains, we do not perceive what remains outside the bellies of your caves.

children.text: na ca lakṣmīstathā svarge kutrādhikatayā sthitā ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there such splendor in heaven; where could any greater abundance be established?
By various austerities, by sages whose brilliance equals fire and the sun,
and who are purifying, you are constantly purified, since they dwell in your caves.
Disdaining aerial cars and dispassionate toward dwelling in heaven,
gods, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras stay near you as if in their father's house.

children.text: aho dhanyo'si śailendra yasya te kandaraṃ haraḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, blessed are you, O lord of mountains, whose cave <s>Hara</s>,
the lord of the worlds himself, inhabits, intent on meditation.
When the divine seer <s>Nārada</s> had spoken thus in a respectful voice,
<s>Menā</s>, queen of the Snow Mountain, wishing to see the sage,
followed by her daughter and by a small group of female attendants,
entered the dwelling, her body bent down with modest affection.

children.text: tatra sthito munivaraḥ śailena sahito vaśī
children.translated_text: The excellent sage, disciplined and standing there together with the mountain,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu tejaso rāśiṃ muniṃ śailapriyā tadā ||
children.translated_text: was seen then by the mountain's beloved wife as a mass of splendor.
With her face veiled, her lotus-hands joined in reverence, she bowed to him.
Seeing her, the greatly blessed great seer of immeasurable radiance
caused her to prosper with blessings whose form was an outpouring of nectar.
Then the goddess, the daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, with astonished mind,
looked up at the sage <s>Nārada</s>, whose form was wondrous.

children.text: ehi vatseti cāpyuktā ṛṣiṇā snigdhayā girā ||
children.translated_text: And she was addressed by the seer in an affectionate voice: "Come, child."
Clasping her father by the neck, she sat down upon his lap.
Her mother said, "Little daughter, bow down to that goddess.
Then you will obtain a blessed, fortunate, and approved husband."
Thus addressed by her mother, with her face covered by the end of her garment,
and with her head trembling a little, she did not say any word at all.

children.text: tataḥ punaruvācedaṃ vākyaṃ mātā sutāṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: Then her mother again spoke these words to her daughter at that time:

children.text: vatse vandaya devarṣiṃ tato dāsyāmi te śubham
children.translated_text: "Dear child, bow to the divine seer; then I shall give you a fine thing,
the lovely jeweled plaything that I have kept for a long time."

children.text: ityuktā tu tato vegāduddhṛtya caraṇau tadā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, she quickly lifted his feet at that time
and bowed, placing the bud of her lotus-hands upon her head.

children.text: kṛte tu vandane tasyā mātā sakhīmukhena tu
children.translated_text: When she had made obeisance, her mother, through the mouth of a friend,
quietly urged him about the signs that indicated her good fortune,
out of curiosity to know the bodily marks,
while, from a woman's nature, she carried anxiety for her daughter in her heart.

children.text: jñātvā tadiṅgitaṃ śailo mahiṣyā hṛdayena tu
children.translated_text: Understanding that gesture and the queen's heart, the mountain-king
kept it unspoken and thought that this pleasant occasion had arisen unharmed.
Then, urged by the friend of the mountain-queen, the best of sages,
the blessed <s>Nārada</s>, with a smiling face, spoke these words:
"Good lady, her husband has not yet been born, and she is devoid of marks.
Her hands are constantly upturned, and her feet are irregular;
she will live by her own shadow. What more need be said at length?"
Hearing this, the mighty great mountain was filled with agitation, his courage shattered,
and with his throat choked by tears he then replied to <s>Nārada</s>.
<s>Himavān</s> said:
"Since the course of this deeply flawed <s>saṃsāra</s> is hard to understand,
and since creation is inevitably brought about by some surpassing maker,
the rule laid down by that maker stands as the boundary for beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: yo jāyate hi yadbījo janituḥ sa hyasārthakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who is born from whatever seed is of no real purpose to the begetter;

children.text: janitā cāpi jātasya na kaściditi yatsphuṭam
children.translated_text: and it is clear that no one is truly the begetter of the one who has been born.
The various classes of beings are born only through their own karma.
One born from an egg, born from an egg-born being, may again be born as a human,
and from a human birth one may be born among creeping creatures, or again in human form.
Even there, in that highest birth, through the strengthening of <s>dharma</s>,
the remaining living beings stand as those born without sons.
Among them humans are born, since they are not all followers of household <s>dharma</s>.
Gradually the attainment of the life-stages comes after the vow of a brahmacārin.
By the command of that creator, by whom <s>saṃsāra</s> was made to increase,
how could <s>saṃsāra</s> grow if all were to refrain from taking wives?

children.text: ataḥ kartrā tu śāstreṣu sutalābhaḥ praśaṃsitaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the scriptures, the obtaining of sons has been praised by the creator,
for the delusion of living beings, under the pretext of rescue from hell.
Creation of beings cannot occur when it is without women.
But womankind by nature is pitiable and speaks in distress;
the capacity for examining scripture has been withheld from them by the ordainer.
In the scriptures it is stated without doubt, many times, and as bearing great fruit:
'A daughter is equal to ten sons, if she is not devoid of good conduct.'
That statement has lost its fruit; it brings the greatest dejection to a man.
For a daughter is pitiable, lamentable, and an increaser of her father's sorrow.
Even if she is fully endowed with everything, with husband, sons, wealth, and the rest,
how much more so if she is unlucky and bereft of husband, sons, wealth, and the rest?
And you have spoken of an accumulation of defects in my daughter's body.

children.text: aho muhyāmi śuṣyāmi glāmi sīdāmi nārada ||
children.translated_text: Ah, I am bewildered; I dry up, I languish, I sink, O <s>Nārada</s>.
Now even what is improper must be spoken, even what is unattainable must be sought.

children.text: anugraheṇa me chinddhi duḥkhaṃ kanyāśrayaṃ mune ||
children.translated_text: By your grace, O sage, cut off my sorrow that rests upon my daughter.
Even when a matter is bounded and beyond doubt, the mind becomes a seat of humiliation;
craving, steeped in desire for its fruit and inauspicious, robs it away.
For women, the highest birth, benefiting both families,
is said to be that called the obtaining of a good husband, for happiness here and hereafter.

children.text: durlabhaḥ satpatiḥ strīṇāṃ viguṇo'pi patiḥ kila
children.translated_text: A good husband is hard for women to obtain; indeed even a husband of poor qualities

children.text: na prāpyate vinā puṇyaiḥ patirnāryā kadācana ||
children.translated_text: is never obtained by a woman without merit.
For a woman's <s>dharma</s> without independent means, her pleasure without measure,
and the wealth sufficient for her life are established in her husband.
Poor, unlucky, foolish, and devoid of every mark though he may be,

children.text: daivataṃ paramaṃ nāryāḥ patiruktaḥ sadaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: a husband is always said to be a woman's supreme deity.

children.text: tvayā coktaṃ hi devarṣe na jāto'syāḥ patiḥ kila
children.translated_text: And you, O divine seer, have said that her husband has indeed not been born.
This misfortune is unequaled, immeasurable, heavy, and hard to bear.

children.text: carācare bhūtasarge yadadyāpi ca no mune
children.translated_text: If in the creation of moving and unmoving beings even today, O sage,

children.text: na sa jāta iti brūṣe tena me vyākulaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you say that he has not been born, then my mind is troubled by that.
Among human and divine births, the indicator of good and bad
is said to be a mark on the hands, feet, and so on, according to the prescribed marks.
This one, O foremost sage, has been called upturned-handed by you.
Upturned-handedness is declared to belong always to those who beg,
never to the blessed and fortunate givers, from whom prosperity arises.
You have said that her feet, through their own shadow, are irregular.

children.text: tatrāpi śreyasāṃ hyāśā mune na pratibhāti naḥ
children.translated_text: In that too, O sage, no hope of better things appears to us.
And the other bodily marks separately indicate their own results:
good fortune, wealth, sons, lifespan, and the gaining of a husband.
You say that she is deprived of all these, O foremost sage.

children.text: tvaṃ me sarvaṃ vijānāsi satyavāgasi cāpyataḥ
children.translated_text: You know everything about me, and you are truthful; therefore,
I am bewildered, tiger among sages; my heart seems to split."
Having spoken thus, the mountain ceased from contemplating his great sorrow.
Having heard all this from the lotus-mouth of that king of mountains,
<s>Nārada</s>, urged by the god, spoke these words, preceded by a smile.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Even in a place of great joy, you are considering sorrow.
Because the meaning of the statement is not fully grasped, O great mountain, you fall into delusion.
Hear from me this speech, fully grounded in a secret matter,
with your mind composed, O great mountain, while reflecting on what I have said.
O <s>Himācala</s>, the husband of this goddess, of whom I spoke, has not been born.
That <s>Mahādeva</s>, source of past, future, and present beings, has not been born.
He is a refuge, eternal, the ruler, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the supreme lord.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the sages are afflicted by birth, death, and old age.
All these, O mountain, are playthings of that supreme lord.
<s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the worlds, exists, arisen by his will.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, of great body and many births, is born in age after age.

children.text: manyase māyayā jātaṃ viṣṇuṃ cāpi yuge yuge
children.translated_text: You think that <s>Viṣṇu</s> too is born in age after age through māyā (cosmic illusion).
For the self there is no destruction, O mountain-bearer, even down to stationary beings.
For an embodied being who is born and is being sustained in saṃsāra (worldly existence),

children.text: naśyate deha evātra nātmano nāśa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: only the body perishes here; destruction of the self is not declared.
This saṃsāra, said to extend from <s>Brahmā</s> down to stationary beings,
afflicted by the pain of birth and death, turns helplessly around.
<s>Mahādeva</s> is unmoving, the fixed one, unborn, the begetter, and undecaying.
He, the lord of the world and free from affliction, will be her husband.

children.text: yaduktaṃ ca mayā devī lakṣaṇairvarjitā tava
children.translated_text: And as for what I said, that your goddess is without marks,
listen to the consideration by which that statement too is rightly understood.
A mark is indeed a divine sign, resting on the limbs of the body,
revealing the measure of one's whole life, wealth, and good fortune.
O mountain-bearer, of her infinite and immeasurable good fortune
no sign in the form of a bodily mark is prescribed on her body.

children.text: ato'syā lakṣaṇaṃ gātre śaila nāsti mahāmate
children.translated_text: Therefore, O mountain of great wisdom, there is no mark on her limbs.
So too I said that her hand is always turned upward.

children.text: uttāno varadaḥ pāṇireṣa devyāḥ sadaiva tu
children.translated_text: This upward-turned hand of the goddess is always a boon-giving palm.
She will grant boons to hosts of gods, asuras, and sages.
As I then declared that her feet do not depart from their own shadow,
hear my reasoned statement about this also, O best of mountains.
Her feet, lotus-like and shining with clear nails,
by the radiance of the crest-jewels of gods and asuras bowing down,
shine with variegated colors reflected in their own brightness.
For she is the wife of the world's teacher, of the bull-marked one, O mountain-bearer.
She is the mother of the <s>dharma</s> (sacred order) of the worlds, born as the nourisher of beings.
This auspicious one, fire-bright, has arisen in your realm only for purification.
Therefore, so that she may very quickly enter union with <s>Pinākin</s>,
you should act duly in that way, O best lord of mountains.
For the gods, O snowy mountain-bearer, have an extremely great task.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ śrutvā tu śailendro nāradātsarvameva hi
children.translated_text: Having heard all this from <s>Nārada</s>, the lord of mountains
then, the husband of <s>Menā</s>, considered himself born anew.
Bowing then to the wise god, the bull-marked one,

children.text: uvāca so'pi saṃhṛṣṭo nāradaṃ tu himācalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Himācala</s> too, filled with joy, spoke to <s>Nārada</s>.
<s>Himavān</s> said:
From a terrible and hard-to-cross hell I have been rescued by you, O sage.
I have been lifted up from the netherworld and made lord of the seven worlds.
I am famed as <s>Himācala</s>; now, by you, best of sages,
upon <s>Himācala</s> I have been brought to an unwavering elevation of qualities.
Now, O sage, my heart, seized by a day of joy,
does not settle upon the analysis and division of duties.
If I were lord of speech, I might examine your virtues.
For people like you, O sage, the sight is certainly unfailing.
Your gracious eagerness toward us is clear to me, O great sage.
It is through men like you that I am made fit as a dwelling for those whose nature is the self,
for sages and deities; even the self-made one removes impurity.
Nevertheless, let an order be given to me in regard to this one matter.
When the mountain lord, filled with joy, had spoken thus,

children.text: tathā ca nārado vākyaṃ kṛtaṃ sarvamiti prabho
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> then said this: All has been done, O lord.
The very purpose in the gods' business is also exceedingly great for you.

children.text: ityuktvā nāradaḥ śīghraṃ jagāma tridivaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Nārada</s> quickly went toward the third heaven.
Having gone, he saw the lord of immortals in <s>Śakra</s>'s palace.
Then that sage, seated on a handsome great seat,
being questioned by <s>Śakra</s>, told the story concerning the daughter of <s>Himā</s>.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: samūhya yattu kartavyaṃ tanmayā kṛtameva hi
children.translated_text: What had to be accomplished by persuasion has indeed been done by me.
But now the time of <s>Pañcaśara</s> himself has arrived.
When the king of gods had been thus addressed by the sage who saw the task,
the blessed <s>Pākaśāsana</s> remembered the one whose weapon is the mango shoot.
Then, quickly remembered by the wise thousand-eyed one,
the fish-bannered one appeared before him, amorous and accompanied by <s>Rati</s>.

children.text: prādurbhūtaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā śakraḥ provāca sādaram ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him thus manifested, <s>Śakra</s> spoke respectfully.
<s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: upadeśena bahunā kiṃ tvāṃ prati vade priyam
children.translated_text: What need is there for me to speak to you, dear one, with much instruction?
You are <s>Manobhava</s>; therefore you know what is present in beings' minds.
So accomplish exactly the beloved purpose of the dwellers in heaven.
Quickly unite <s>Śaṃkara</s> with the mountain's daughter, O <s>Manobhava</s>,
together with <s>Madhu</s>, the unconquerable king of seasons.
Thus addressed by <s>Śakra</s>, for the accomplishment of his own purpose, <s>Madana</s>
then, the five-arrowed one, afraid, spoke these words to <s>Śatakratu</s>.
<s>Kāma</s> said:
With this divine equipment, fearful even to sages and demons,

children.text: duḥsādhyaḥ śaṃkaro devaḥ kiṃ na vetsi jagatprabho ||
children.translated_text: the god <s>Śaṃkara</s> is difficult to master. Do you not know this, O lord of the world?

children.text: tasya devasya vettha tvaṃ kāraṇaṃ tu yadavyayam
children.translated_text: You know the imperishable cause of that god;

children.text: prāyaḥ prasādaḥ kopo'pi sarvo hi mahatāṃ mahān ||
children.translated_text: for, among great beings, both favor and anger are generally great in every way.
The beauties born in heaven are indeed the essence of every enjoyment,
and the happiness on which you have relied has had its activity destroyed.
If, through negligence, it should fall away with regard to the Lord, this must be considered.
Even beforehand, the possible results of actions among beings are visible here.
O <s>Śakra</s>, for those who desire something special, the result is a fall from the common state.
Having heard this speech, <s>Śakra</s>, accompanied by the immortals, said to him:
<s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: vayaṃ pramāṇāste hyatra ratikānta na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: We are your authority in this matter, O beloved of <s>Rati</s>; there is no doubt.
Without an instruction, a capacity to do harm is not admitted.

children.text: kasyacic ca kvaciddṛṣṭaṃ sāmarthyaṃ na tu sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The power of someone has been seen somewhere, but not everywhere.
Thus addressed, <s>Kāma</s> set out, taking his friend <s>Madhu</s> with him,
and, joined by <s>Rati</s>, he quickly went to a slope of the Snow Mountain.
There he reflected on the task, with its means first in view:

children.text: mahārthā ye hi niṣkampā manasteṣāṃ sudurjayam ||
children.translated_text: The minds of those who are steadfast in great purposes are very hard to conquer.
But if it is agitated at the very beginning, it will surely become easy to conquer,
and they may attain success after first unsettling the mind.
How, without following the path of hatred, by means of various states,
shall I employ anger, which comes from a crueler attachment, with terrible jealousy as its great companion,
with restlessness at its head, its support of firmness shattered, and very powerful,
that supreme dark alteration of the mind?
Having closed the doors of firmness and dragged away contentment,

children.text: avagantuṃ hi māṃ tatra na kaścidatipaṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: no one there, however excessively learned, will be able to perceive me.
When there is only the condition of uncertainty, the mind becomes distorted;
afterwards the beginning of the root-action is a deep whirlpool hard to cross.
I shall steal the austerity of <s>Hara</s>, whose self is steady,
enveloping the whole group of senses through an array of charming means.
Having thought thus, <s>Madana</s> went to the hermitage of the lord of beings,
the essence of the earth, with a terrace of sarala trees.
It was filled with peaceful creatures and crowded with motionless animals,
netted with many flowers and creepers, and with lords of the gaṇas stationed in the sky.
Its slopes of blue grass were inhabited by undisturbed bulls.
There he saw a certain beautiful second form belonging to the three-eyed god:
<s>Vīraka</s>, lord of the heroes of the world, with radiance like <s>Īśāna</s>,
his mass of matted hair tawny like heaps of yakṣa-saffron filaments,
holding a staff in his hand, unperturbed, adorned with fierce lordly serpents,
with eyes like the petals of lotuses half closed and half opened,
gazing steadily at the tip of his nose with beautiful eyes,
with an upper garment hanging down, made from the hide of a lordly lion,
tawny with the fiery breaths released from the serpent-hoods at his ears,
with a mass of matted hair hanging down with swinging skulls and gourds at its ends,
placed at the root of the navel upon a couch made of <s>Vāsuki</s>,
adorned with serpents fastened by their tail-tips, held in a reverent fold of hands.
<s>Kāma</s> then saw <s>Śaṃkara</s>, as he gradually came near him,
with the slopes of the trees filled by the humming of bees.
<s>Madana</s> entered the mind of <s>Bhava</s> through the opening of his ear.
Then <s>Śaṃkara</s>, hearing that sweet sound grounded in <s>Madana</s>,
remembered the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, his beloved, his mind impassioned.
Then that exceedingly pure meditative concentration gradually disappeared from him,
though it had stood as a directly perceptible form of its object.
Then, having become absorbed in that, his intention covered by an obstruction,
the Lord, through his self-mastery, recognized the alteration whose nature was <s>Madana</s>.
<s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, slightly filled with anger, took hold of firmness,
and, veiled by yogic māyā, cast off the state produced by <s>Madana</s>.
Then <s>Madana</s>, possessed by that māyā, blazed forth,
hard to conquer, with a body made of desire and deeply grounded in the fault of anger.
Then he, whose nature was the obsession of latent impressions, came out from the heart,
and, taking his stand on the ground outside, the fish-bannered god stood there.
He was followed by his heart-pleasing friend <s>Madhu</s>.
Seeing on a mango tree, shaken by a gentle wind,
a lovely cluster of blossoms, <s>Madana</s> quickly, at <s>Hara</s>'s chest,
released the arrow called Mohana, the makara-bannered one.
Into the pure heart of <s>Śiva</s> that great arrow, destined for destruction,
the harsh, tall, bewildering flower-arrow, fell.
Then <s>Bhava</s>, struck in the heart, became uncertain in his faculties;
although his firmness was comparable to a mountain, he turned toward <s>Madana</s>.
But because of his mastery over states, he did not fall into possession,
though he had encountered many external things capable of producing obstruction.
Then, in his face, terrible with a dreadful roar born from the fire of anger,
there appeared a third eye, filled with flame,
world-destroying and terrifying, belonging to <s>Rudra</s> of fearsome form.
<s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> opened it wide upon <s>Madana</s>, who was standing near.
By the spark from that eye, while the dwellers in heaven cried out,
<s>Kandarpa</s>, breaker of the pride of lovers, was swiftly reduced to ashes.
But that fire, born from <s>Hara</s>'s eye, after reducing him to ashes,
expanded in order to burn the world, devouring with flames and with a huṃkāra.
Then <s>Bhava</s>, for the sake of the world, divided that <s>Jātavedas</s> fire
among the mango tree, spring, the moon, flowers, and still other things,
among bees and the mouths of cuckoos, apportioning the fire of <s>Smara</s>.
That fire of <s>Smara</s>'s arrows, by which <s>Hara</s> had been pierced outwardly and inwardly,
ran within, a fierce blaze kindled by the fuel of passion and affection.
With an irresistible expansion, it caused agitation in the divided worlds.
When, indeed, it reaches the hearts of lovers, saturated with affection,
that terrible one burns day and night, difficult to cure in its very nature.
Seeing <s>Smara</s> made ashes by the flame of <s>Hara</s>'s huṃkāra,

children.text: vilalāpa ratiḥ krūraṃ bandhunā madhunā saha
children.translated_text: <s>Rati</s> lamented bitterly together with her kinsman <s>Madhu</s>.
Then, after much lamentation, consoled by <s>Madhu</s>,
she went for refuge to the god, the three-eyed one whose crest is the moon.
Taking in her hand a flowering mango-born creeper, followed by bees,
as a sacred implement, and a cuckoo as her companion,

children.text: nirbadhya tu jaṭājūṭaṃ kuṭilair alakai ratiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rati</s> bound up her mass of matted hair with curling locks,
and smeared her body with the white, pleasing ashes of <s>Smara</s>.
Going down upon the earth with her knees, she addressed the moon-adorned lord.
<s>Rati</s> said:

children.text: namaḥ śivāyāstu nirāmayāya namaḥ śivāyāstu manomayāya
children.translated_text: Homage be to <s>Śiva</s>, the one free from affliction; homage be to <s>Śiva</s>, the one made of mind.

children.text: namaḥ śivāyāstu surārcitāya tubhyaṃ sadā bhaktakṛpāparāya ||
children.translated_text: Homage be to <s>Śiva</s>, worshiped by the gods; homage always to you, devoted to mercy toward your devotees.

children.text: namo bhavāyāstu bhavodbhavāya namo'stu te dhvastamanobhavāya
children.translated_text: Homage be to <s>Bhava</s>, source of existence; homage to you, destroyer of <s>Manobhava</s>.
Homage to you of the hidden great vow; homage to you who take refuge in the dense mystery of māyā.

children.text: namo'stu śarvāya namaḥ śivāya namo'stu siddhāya purātanāya
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Śarva</s>; homage to <s>Śiva</s>; homage to the perfected, ancient one.

children.text: namo'stu kālāya namaḥ kalāya namo'stu te jñānavarapradāya ||
children.translated_text: Homage to Time; homage to the measure of time; homage to you who bestow the boon of knowledge.
Homage to you who transcend time and its divisions; homage to you whose adornment is stainless by nature.
Homage to the immeasurable crusher of <s>Andhaka</s>; homage to the refuge, homage to the one beyond qualities.
Homage to you who are attended by fearsome hosts; homage to the maker of the many worlds.

children.text: namo'stu nānājagatāṃ vidhātre namo'stu te citraphalaprayoktre ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the ordainer of manifold worlds; homage to you who dispense varied fruits.
At the end of all things, homage to the one whose eye is imperishable; homage to the enjoyer of shares in wondrous sacrifices.

children.text: namo'stu bhaktābhimatapradātre namaḥ sadā te bhavasaṅgahartre ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the giver of what devotees desire; constant homage to you, remover of bondage to becoming.
To you of endless forms, always homage; to you whose wrath is unbearable, homage.
To you marked by the moon, always homage; homage to you, praised and immeasurable in measure.
Homage to the bull-bannered rider, to the destroyer of <s>Pura</s>; homage to the renowned one, the great medicine.
Homage to you who grant what is desired through devotion; homage to you, remover of every distress.
You are the best judge of the conduct of the moving and unmoving world, the teacher who has conceived the creation of beings.

children.text: tvāmindumauliṃ śaraṇaṃ prapannā priyāprameyaṃ mahatāṃ maheśam ||
children.translated_text: I have taken refuge in you, moon-crested, beloved, immeasurable <s>Maheśa</s>, great lord of the great.

children.text: prayaccha me kāmayaśaḥsamṛddhiṃ punaḥ prabho jīvatu kāmadevaḥ
children.translated_text: Grant me the prosperity of desire and fame; let <s>Kāmadeva</s> live again, O lord.

children.text: priyaṃ vinā tvāṃ priyajīviteṣu tvatto'paraḥ ko bhuvaneṣvihāsti ||
children.translated_text: Without my beloved, for those whose life is their beloved, who else besides you exists here in the worlds?
You are the lord of the beloved, the source of beloved ones, who have set forth the successive higher and lower meanings.
You alone are the lord of the world, compassionate, uprooting the fear of your devotees.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: itthaṃ stutaḥ śaṃkara īḍya īśo vṛṣākapirmanmathakāntayā tu
children.translated_text: Thus praised by <s>Manmatha</s>'s beloved, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the laudable lord, <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>,

children.text: tutoṣa doṣākarakhaṇḍadhārī uvāca caināṃ madhuraṃ nirīkṣya ||
children.translated_text: the bearer of the crescent moon, was pleased and spoke to her sweetly, looking upon her.
<s>Śaṃkara</s> said:
So it shall be: this <s>Kāma</s> will again become your beloved in time, before long.

children.text: anaṅga iti lokeṣu sa vikhyātiṃ gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: In the worlds he will become famous as <s>Anaṅga</s>, 'the bodiless one.'
When this had been said, <s>Kāma</s>'s beloved bowed with her head to <s>Giriśa</s>,
and <s>Rati</s> went to a lovely grove of the Snow Mountain.

children.text: ruroda cāpi bahuśo dīnā ramye sthale tu sā
children.translated_text: There, in that beautiful place, the wretched woman wept again and again.
Though resolved upon death, she turned back because of <s>Hara</s>'s command.
Then the Snow Mountain, impelled by <s>Nārada</s>'s words,
took his daughter, adorned with ornaments and furnished with auspicious wedding rites,
wearing a head-garland made of heavenly flowers and clothed in white Chinese silk,

children.text: śarābhyāṃ saṃyutāṃ śailo gṛhītvā svasutāṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: joined with two arrows; taking his own daughter, the mountain then
went forth under an auspicious conjunction, his mind wholly fulfilled.
Passing through forests with their groves and pleasure-woods,
he saw a weeping woman of inconceivably great splendor,
unmatched in beauty in the world, upon the lovely forest slopes.

children.text: kautukena parāmṛśya tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rudatīṃ giriḥ
children.translated_text: Moved by curiosity, the mountain looked upon her as she wept,
and then, approaching close to her, he asked:
<s>Himavān</s> said:

children.text: kāsi kasyāsi kalyāṇi kimarthaṃ cāpi rodiṣi
children.translated_text: Who are you? To whom do you belong, auspicious one? And why do you weep?
I do not think this cause is a small one, O beauty of the world.

children.text: sā tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā uvāca madhunā saha
children.translated_text: Hearing his words, she spoke together with <s>Madhu</s>,
weeping and sighing, uttering words born of grief and increasing her misery.
<s>Rati</s> said:

children.text: kāmasya dayitāṃ bhāryāṃ ratiṃ māṃ viddhi suvrata
children.translated_text: Know me, good-vowed one, to be <s>Rati</s>, the beloved wife of <s>Kāma</s>.
On this mountain, O greatly fortunate one, <s>Giriśa</s> was established in austerity.
Angered by the obstruction, he opened his eye wide and looked,
and that <s>Jhaṣaketu</s>, my exceedingly dear husband, was burned.

children.text: ahaṃ tu śaraṇaṃ yātā taṃ devaṃ bhayavihvalā
children.translated_text: Terrified with fear, I went for refuge to that god,
and praised him with a hymn; after he had been praised, <s>Giriśa</s> then said to me:
'I am pleased, beloved of <s>Kāma</s>; this <s>Kāma</s> of yours shall be restored.'
And the man who recites your praise with devotion, taking refuge in me,
will obtain the desired wish, being turned back from death and the like.
And I, awaiting that word, because of the sway of hope and the rest,
will preserve my body for some time, O greatly radiant one.
When she had spoken thus, the mountain, bewildered and terrified by <s>Rati</s>,
took his daughter by the hand and wished to go to his own city.
Because what is to be must inevitably come to be, she who was destined, knowing past and future,
ashamed, spoke to her father, the mountain, through the mouths of her friends.
The daughter of the Mountain said:
What purpose have I for this body of mine, made unfortunate by ill fortune?

children.text: kathaṃ ca tādṛśaṃ prāptaṃ sukhaṃ me sa patirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: And how could such happiness be obtained by me, that he should become my husband?
The desired object is obtained by austerities; for nothing is impossible for one who practices austerity.

children.text: durbhagatvaṃ vṛthā loko vahate sati sādhane ||
children.translated_text: People bear misfortune in vain when there is a means at hand.
Death is better than an unfortunate life for one who does not practice austerity.

children.text: bhaviṣyāmi na saṃdeho niyamaiḥ śoṣaye tanum ||
children.translated_text: There is no doubt: by observances I shall make my body wither.
In austerity my doubt has fallen away; exertion is for the sake of winning the goal.

children.text: sāhaṃ tapaḥ kariṣyāmi yadahaṃ prāpya durlabhā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall perform austerity, by which I may obtain that hard-to-obtain goal.
When the king of mountains was thus addressed by his daughter, he was overcome with affection,
and the lord of mountains spoke in a voice whose syllables were choked with love.
<s>Himavān</s> said:

children.text: umeti capale putri na kṣamaṃ tāvakaṃ vapuḥ
children.translated_text: "U mā," O restless daughter; your body is not fit
to endure austerity, whose very nature is hardship, O gentle-looking one.
Things that are to be must always be considered carefully;
destined things certainly come to pass, by force, even for one who does not wish them.
Therefore, child, you have no purpose at all in austerity.
Let us go home; there I will think about it.

children.text: ityuktā tu yadā naiva guhāyābhyeti śailajā
children.translated_text: But when <s>Śailajā</s>, though thus addressed, did not come back from the cave,

children.text: tataḥ sa cintayāviṣṭo duhitāṃ praśaśaṃsa ca ||
children.translated_text: then he was filled with anxiety and praised his daughter.
Then in the sky, over the surface of the world, a divine voice arose:

children.text: umeti capale putri tvayoktā tanayā tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because, saying "U mā, O restless daughter," you then addressed your daughter,
therefore in the worlds her name will be <s>Umā</s>;
and this embodied one will accomplish the success she has conceived.
Having heard the word from the sky, the mountain, pale as white kāśa grass,
gave permission to his daughter and quickly went to his own dwelling.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Śailajā</s> too went to a peak inaccessible even to gods,
followed by two friends, restrained, the daughter of the king of mountains.
It was a holy summit of <s>Himavat</s>, adorned with various minerals,
strewn with divine flowering creepers and frequented by siddhas and gandharvas,
crowded with herds of many animals, its trees loud with bees,
provided with divine waterfalls and adorned with long ponds,
filled with many flocks of birds and beautified by cakravākas,
made lovely by blooming flowers born in water and on land,
marked by variegated beautiful caves and charming with cave-dwellings,
inhabited by flocks of birds and dense with wish-granting trees.
There she saw a tree, a great-branched one with green foliage,
bearing flowers in every season and shining with hundreds of desires.
It was covered with many flowers and furnished with many kinds of fruit,
bent by the rays of the sun, with its shoots opened and drawn together.
There <s>Śailajā</s> cast off her garments and ornaments,
and was clothed in divine bark garments, with a girdle made of darbha grass.
Bathing three times daily and eating <s>pāṭala</s> blossoms, she remained for a hundred autumns;
then for a hundred years she lived on a single withered leaf.
For a hundred years she was without food, a treasure-house of austerities;
then all beings were disturbed by the fire of that austerity.
Then the blessed <s>Śatakratu</s> remembered the seven sages,
and those sages all came together, assembled then.
Honored by great <s>Indra</s>, they asked him his purpose:

children.text: kimarthaṃ tu suraśreṣṭha saṃsmṛtāstu vayaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: "For what reason, O best of gods, have we been remembered by you?"
<s>Śakra</s> said: "Let your lordships hear the purpose.
On <s>Himācala</s> the daughter of the mountain is practicing terrible austerity.
You ought to bring about the wish desired by her."
Then, for the sake of the world, they quickly went to the goddess,
saying "So be it," to the lord of mountains frequented by hosts of siddhas.
Having arrived, the sages then spoke to her in sweet syllables:

children.text: putri kiṃ te vyavasitaḥ kāmaḥ kamalalocane ||
children.translated_text: "Daughter, what desire have you resolved upon, lotus-eyed one?"
Then the goddess, out of modest respect, said to those sages:
"O greatly blessed ones, for one performing austerity, having obtained such as you while keeping silence,
the mind, directed to salutation, surely purifies one.
Since your lordships are ready to ask a question, taking a seat first is proper.
When you are seated and free from weariness, then afterwards you may question me."
Having spoken thus, she then caused them to accept seats.
After duly honoring those venerable ones according to rule,
<s>Satī</s> slowly spoke to the seven sages, who shone like the sun.

children.text: tyaktvā vratātmakaṃ maunaṃ maunaṃ jagrāha hrīmayam
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the silence that was the essence of her vow, she adopted a silence made of modesty.

children.text: bhāvaṃ tasyāstu maunāntaṃ tasyāḥ saptarṣayo yathā ||
children.translated_text: The seven seers, perceiving the feeling within her at the end of that silence,
having become subject to respect, asked her again in the same way.
She too, the lovely-smiling one, with a mind filled with respect,
looked at the sages, whose speech and conversation were peaceful, and uttered restrained words:
"Your lordships know the minds and welfare of living beings."
For embodied beings are indeed greatly afflicted by the movements of the mind.
Some skilled ones, however, strive in this matter with efforts worthy of the wise.
Through means, the vigilant attain states that are difficult to attain.
But others, limited in understanding, undertaking efforts of many kinds,
take up a beneficial undertaking for the sake of another embodiment.
