But my mind repeatedly reaches toward one adorned with a garland of flowers born in the sky,

children.text: vandhyā sutaṃ prāptukāmā manaḥ prasarate muhuḥ
children.translated_text: like a barren woman wishing to obtain a son.

children.text: ahaṃ kila bhavaṃ devaṃ patiṃ prāptuṃ samudyatā ||
children.translated_text: I am indeed resolved to obtain the god <s>Bhava</s> as my husband,
who by nature is hard to overcome and is now practicing austerity,
not decisively understood by gods or asuras, and abiding in the practice of the highest reality,
and who even now has burned <s>Madana</s> and is free from passion.
How could one like me worship such a lord, <s>Śiva</s>?
When she had spoken thus, the sages, then wishing to know the steadiness of her mind,
spoke words appropriate to the matter at hand, proceeding in due order.
The sages said:

children.text: dvividhaṃ tu sukhaṃ tāvatputri lokeṣu bhāvyate
children.translated_text: For now, daughter, happiness in the worlds is considered twofold:
the enjoyment of this body through pleasures, and also the contentment of the mind.

children.text: prakṛtyā sa tu digvāsā bhīmaḥ pitṛvaṇeśayaḥ
children.translated_text: But by nature he is clothed in the directions, terrifying, lying in the ancestral forest,
a skull-bearer, a beggar, naked, odd-eyed, and fixed in his practice.
He has the appearance of one intoxicated and mad, and he gathers together horrible things.
What purpose desired by you is there in that ascetic, an embodied misfortune?
For if at present you desire enjoyment for this body,
then how could it come to you from <s>Mahādeva</s>, who inspires fear and disgust,
who is adorned with skulls smeared with dripping blood and fat,
terrible with ornaments made of hissing, fierce serpents upon his arms,
dwelling in the cremation ground and followed, O <s>Satī</s>, by fierce <s>Pramathas</s>?
There is the foe-destroying <s>Hari</s>, whose feet are rubbed by clusters of the lord of gods' crowns;
he is the sustainer of the world, beloved of <s>Śrī</s>, and possessed of endless forms.
There is also <s>Indra</s>, <s>Pākaśāsana</s>, lord of those who receive the sacrificial share.
There is <s>Jvalana</s>, the treasure of the deities and fulfiller of every desire.
There is <s>Vāyu</s>, sustainer of the world, who is the breath of all embodied beings.
Likewise there is King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, mighty, all-prosperous, and powerful.
Why do you not wish to obtain one or another of these?
Or is the happiness desired by your mind to be gained by obtaining another body?
Even so, for you this very place is the source of the riches of heaven;
in this alone all supreme auspicious attainments are yours.
In your father alone exists all that is not found even among the gods.
Therefore hardship for obtaining that would also be fruitless for you here.
Generally, O gracious one, what is sought is very slight and extremely hard to obtain.

children.text: asya te vidhiyogasya dhātā kartātra caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: For this ordained union of yours, the Ordainer himself is the maker here.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ityuktā sā tu kupitā munivaryeṣu śailajā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Śailajā</s> became angry with the best of sages,
and, with eyes reddened by anger and lips quivering, she spoke.
<s>Devī</s> said:
What pleasure is there in false attachment? What restraint can there be of calamity?
By whom are those who understand things perversely set upon the right path?
Do you understand me in this way as foolish, fond of false attachment to an improper object?
There is no reconsideration for me here, as though this were a matter of false attachment and its fault.
All of you are equal to <s>Prajāpati</s>, seeing everything,

children.text: nūnaṃ na vettha taṃ devaṃ śāśvataṃ jagataḥ prabhum ||
children.translated_text: yet surely you do not know that god, the eternal lord of the world,
the unborn ruler, unmanifest, whose arising greatness is immeasurable.
Let the wondrous understanding of the true existence of his dharma remain aside for now;
even the lordly gods, headed by <s>Hari</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, do not know him.
What has expanded in the worlds, arisen from his own power,

children.text: prakaṭaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tadapyatra na vettha kim ||
children.translated_text: and is manifest to all beings--do you not know even that here?
Whose is this vast sky? Whose is fire? Whose is wind?
Whose is the earth? Whose is <s>Varuṇa</s>? Who has the moon and sun as eyes?
Whose <s>liṅga</s> do gods and asuras worship with devotion in the worlds?
Whom do the gods, <s>Vidhi</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the great seers call <s>Īśvara</s>?

children.text: prabhāvaṃ prabhavaṃ caiṣa teṣāmapi na vettha kim
children.translated_text: Do you not know his power and source, and that he is the source even of them?
Of whom is this <s>Aditi</s> the mother? From whom was <s>Janārdana</s> born?
From <s>Aditi</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s> were born the gods, beginning with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Kaśyapa</s> was the son of <s>Marīci</s>, and <s>Aditi</s> was the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>.

children.text: marīciścāpi dakṣaśca putrau tau brahmaṇaḥ kila
children.translated_text: And <s>Marīci</s> and <s>Dakṣa</s>, so it is said, were those two sons of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s>, endowed with divine accomplishment and power, came from the golden egg.
From whose meditation did he come forth, when the elements of <s>prakṛti</s> had been stirred?
In the third state of <s>prakṛti</s> arose the generative act of the foe of <s>Madhu</s>.
Once born, he created the six classes, preceded by intelligence and born from their own actions.
The unborn <s>Vedhas</s> came into being from <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth is unmanifest.
He who, by his own yoga, agitated <s>prakṛti</s> and made this world,
made for <s>Brahmā</s> the lordship with all aims accomplished, the sovereignty of creating the worlds.
And this too <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the others always know through his own greatness:

children.text: kṛtvānyaṃ deham anyā dṛk tādṛk kṛtvā punarhariḥ ||
children.translated_text: assuming another body and another appearance, and again making <s>Hari</s> such as that,
he performs the work of the world, highest, lowest, and middling.
In just this way is <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose nature is birth and death.
This indeed is the fruit of karma, arising in many forms.

children.text: atha nārāyaṇo devaḥ svakāṃ chāyāṃ samāśrayat ||
children.translated_text: Then the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> took refuge in his own shadow;
impelled by that, he brings about birth of many kinds.
That impelling too is said to belong to karma for souls whose selves are constrained.
For, just as the thought of one possessed by madness and the like becomes exactly that kind of thought,
so he regards only the things he desires as real, and contrary things as the opposite.
In the created dealings of the world he always endures them,
and <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is understood in the attainment of the fruits of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
Then, too, his beginninglessness exists because of commonality with that very self;

children.text: na hyasya jīvitaṃ dīrghaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ dehe tu kutracit ||
children.translated_text: for no long life of his has anywhere been seen in a body.
Nor has any interval of him been seen by you, or anything within it;
this indeed is the law of embodied beings: in one place one is born, in another one dies.
Somewhere one perishes while in the womb; somewhere one lives on into the infirmity of old age.
Somewhere one lives a hundred years; somewhere one falls in childhood.
But a man who lives a hundred years is endless to those of brief birth;
while living he does not die before them, and therefore he is called immortal.
In this way <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the others are considered to have unseen birth and death.
Who here in saṃsāra could obtain this wholly purified sovereignty?
There, because of connection with decay and the like, in forms of many wonders,
therefore I do not desire all the heaven-goers, stained and of little prosperity,
O good ladies, except for <s>Śarva</s>, the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>.

children.text: sthitaṃ ca tāratamyena prāṇināṃ paramaṃ tvidam ||
children.translated_text: Among living beings this supreme thing is established by gradation:
the great measure of the great in intelligence, strength, sovereignty, action, and the rest,
from whom there is nothing else and from whom everything proceeds.
I have gone for refuge to him whose sovereignty is without beginning or end.
This is my resolve, long-standing and very much the reverse of another course.
Go or stay, then, O sages who would direct my affairs.
Having thus heard the goddess's words, the best of sages then,
their eyes filled with tears of joy, embraced that ascetic woman.
And, greatly pleased, they spoke sweet words to <s>Śailajā</s>.
The sages said:
How exceedingly wonderful you are, daughter, stainless like an embodiment of knowledge.
Your disposition delights us because it rests on devotion to <s>Bhava</s>.
Indeed, we know the wondrous sovereignty of that god.
We came here to know the firmness of your resolve.
Very soon, slender-limbed one, this desire of yours will come to pass.

children.text: kvādityasya prabhā yāti ratnebhyaḥ kva dyutiḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: Where does the sun's radiance go, and where is brilliance apart from jewels?

children.text: ko'rtho varṇālikāvyaktaḥ kathaṃ tvaṃ giriśaṃ vinā
children.translated_text: What purpose is there in a meaning expressed by a row of syllables? How could you be without <s>Giriśa</s>?
Let us go, not alone in our approach; we will entreat him.

children.text: asmākamapi vai so'rthaḥ sutarāṃ hṛdi vartate
children.translated_text: That same purpose of ours, too, abides all the more in our hearts.
Therefore you yourself are that wisdom, since you yourself are the right course.
Therefore without doubt <s>Śaṃkara</s> also will accomplish the matter.
Having spoken thus, the sages, honored by the mountain's daughter, departed.
They set out to see <s>Giriśa</s> on the great plateau of <s>Himavat</s>,
its body washed by the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with tawny-bound masses of matted locks,
and with a garland of mandāra flowers in hand, followed by bees.

children.text: gireḥ samprāpya te prasthaṃ dadṛśuḥ śaṃkarāśramam ||
children.translated_text: Reaching the mountain plateau, they saw <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s hermitage,
where every host of beings was at peace and the forest was newly stilled,
with silent, unagitated waterfalls in every direction.
Then there at the door they saw <s>Vīraka</s>, staff in hand.

children.text: sapta te munayaḥ pūjyā vinītāḥ kāryagauravāt ||
children.translated_text: Those seven venerable sages, humble because of the gravity of their task,
spoke with sweet-speaking speech, those foremost of eloquent men:
We have come here to see the refuge, the lord of the gaṇas,
the three-eyed one. Know us to be urged on by the business of the gods.
You alone are our path, the truth; let there be no passing beyond the proper time.
This, in general, is our request, O lord who keeps the gate.
Thus addressed by the sages, he then spoke to them with respect:
At the later twilight of the rite he will go to bathe in the water of the <s>Mandākinī</s>.
There, O brahmins, you will see the trident-bearer.
So addressed, the sages stood waiting for that time,
like thirsty cātaka birds awaiting a deep raincloud in the monsoon.
Then, in a moment, when the procedure of meditation had been completed,
the Lord rose from the hero-posture spread with deerskin.
Then, humble, resting his knees on the ground,
<s>Vīraka</s> spoke to the god, wholly devoted to a single act of reverence:

children.text: samprāptā munayaḥ sapta tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ dīptatejasaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven sages of blazing splendor have arrived to see you.
Lord, command; you should consent to be seen and known here.
They said that, on the gods' business, they long for the sight of you.
Thus addressed by the noble <s>Vīraka</s>, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>
then gave them permission to enter by the sign of a movement of his brow.
With a nod of his head, <s>Vīraka</s> too summoned all those great sages,
who were standing not far away, for the sight of the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>.
With their half-crests tied in haste and their deerskin garments hanging down,
they entered <s>Giriśa</s>'s accomplished sacred enclosure, filled with his powers.
Then, with joined handfuls filled with heaps of heavenly flowers,
they bowed to the two feet of <s>Pinākin</s>, worthy of veneration by the dwellers in heaven.
Then the peaceful sages, gently gazed upon by the trident-bearer,
joyfully and respectfully praised together the foe of <s>Manmatha</s>.
The sages said:

children.text: aho kṛtārthā vayameva sāṃprataṃ sureśvaro'pyatra varo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Ah, now we are truly fulfilled; even the lord of the gods will here become the chosen bridegroom.
From the sprinkling of the stainless water of your favor, someone is joined to the fruit of austerity.

children.text: jayatyasau dhanyataro himācalastadāśrayaṃ yasya sutā tapasyati
children.translated_text: Victorious is that most blessed <s>Himācala</s>, whose daughter, taking refuge in him, practices austerity.

children.text: sa daityarājo'pi mahāphalodayo vimūlitāśeṣasuro hi tārakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that king of the Daityas, <s>Tāraka</s>, whose rise has great fruit, has indeed uprooted all the gods.

children.text: tvadīyamaṃśaṃ pravilokya kalmaṣātsvakaṃ śarīraṃ parimokṣyate hi yaḥ
children.translated_text: When he sees your own portion, he will indeed cast off his own body from his sin.
Blessed in understanding is he, the four-faced father of the world, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Hari</s> too, who is kindled by the fire of that alarm.
For those who bear your pair of feet in their heart, it is the sole cause for the appeasing of the great heat of fear.

children.text: tvameva caiko vividhākṛtakriyaḥ kileti vācā vidhurair vibhāṣyate ||
children.translated_text: And you alone, whose actions take manifold forms, are spoken of by the distressed with the words, "Indeed it is so."

children.text: athādya ekastvamavādi nānyathā jagattathā nirghṛṇatāṃ tava spṛśet
children.translated_text: But if today you alone are spoken of and not otherwise, the world would then come into contact with your mercilessness.

children.text: na vetsi vā duḥkhamidaṃ prajātmakaṃ vihanyate te khalu sarvataḥ kriyā ||
children.translated_text: Or else you do not know this suffering that belongs to creatures; surely your activity is being obstructed on every side.

children.text: upekṣase cej jagatāmupadravaṃ dayāmayatvaṃ tava kena kathyate
children.translated_text: If you disregard the affliction of the worlds, by what means can your compassion be proclaimed?
The pure majesty, resting in the cave of the greatness of your own yogamāyā, is not found.

children.text: vayaṃ ca te dhanyatarāḥ śarīriṇāṃ yadīdṛśaṃ tvāṃ pravilokayāmahe
children.translated_text: And we are more blessed than embodied beings, since we behold you in such a form.

children.text: adarśanaṃ tena manoratho yathā prayāti sāphalyatayā manogatam ||
children.translated_text: Through that sight, the wish held in the mind attains fulfillment, as a longing does.
O mouth of the world, in the single method of ordering the world, therefore we, agents of <s>Balabhit</s>, will act.

children.text: vinemuritthaṃ munayo visṛjya tāṃ giraṃ girīśaśrutibhūmisaṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: Thus the sages bowed down and, having uttered that speech within reach of <s>Girīśa</s>'s hearing,
were like farmers on the earth casting a handful of good seed in a choice field for good fruit.

children.text: teṣāṃ śrutvā tu tāṃ ramyāṃ prakramopakramakriyām
children.translated_text: Having heard that charming speech of theirs, which set the undertaking in motion,
the pleased lord of speech spoke words made lovely by a smile.
<s>Śarva</s> said:
I know the excellent good work of arranging the course of the world: the daughter has been born of the snowy mountain.
She is the marking out of the appointed agreement.
It is true that all are eager and intent upon the work of the gods;

children.text: teṣāṃ tvaranti cetāṃsi kiṃtu kāryaṃ vivakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: their minds are hurrying, but the matter that is desired must be stated.
The course of the world must be followed, especially by the wise.

children.text: sevante te yato dharmaṃ tatprāmāṇyātpare sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since they observe <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), on the authority of that they stand in what is higher.
When this had been said, the sages quickly went to <s>Himācala</s>.
There they were honored by that snowy mountain with respect.
Pleased and hurrying, the best sages spoke briefly.
The sages said:
The god <s>Pinākī</s> himself asks for your daughter.
Therefore quickly purify yourself, like an oblation by offering it into the fire.
This work of the gods has been turning for a very long time.
Let this undertaking be made for the uplifting of the world.
Thus addressed by them then, the mountain, filled with joy, spoke to the sages.
Yet, praying to <s>Śiva</s>, he became unable to give an answer.
Then <s>Menā</s>, seeing the sages and shaken by affection, spoke.
Understanding the matter, she took refuge at the feet of both her daughter and those sages.
<s>Menā</s> said:
The very purpose for which a daughter's birth, though people do not desire it, has great fruit,
all that has now come about in due course.
Even if a suitor is endowed with family, birth, age, beauty, splendor, and prosperity,
a daughter should indeed be given to him after inviting him, even when he has not asked.
How will my daughter go to that one who is terrible with every austerity?
From the daughter's word, whatever ought to be done here, let that be done.
Thus addressed by the beloved wife of the mountain-bearing lord, those sages
again spoke a generous matter, one that would bring clarity to a woman's heart.
The sages said:
Understand the lordly power of <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
for his pair of lotus feet is worshiped by gods and asuras who are deeply fulfilled.

children.text: yasyopayogi yadrūpaṃ sā ca tatprāptaye ciram
children.translated_text: Whatever form is suited to him, the girl has long practiced

children.text: ghoraṃ tapasyate bālā tena rūpeṇa nirvṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: terrible austerity to obtain that; by that form there will be fulfillment.
He will bring those divine vows to completion.
Let her remain attentive there until then; from that, service to him will come about.

children.text: ityuktvā giriṇā sārdhaṃ te yayuryatra śailajā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, they went with the mountain to where <s>Śailajā</s> was.
<s>Umā</s>, whose brilliance from austerity surpassed the blaze of sun and fire,
was kindly addressed by the sages, who honored her as she had come upon the path:

children.text: ramyaṃ priyaṃ manohāri mā rūpaṃ tapasā daha ||
children.translated_text: Do not burn with austerity your lovely, dear, and mind-delighting form.
Tomorrow morning <s>Śaṃkara</s> will take your hand, daughter.
Having come earlier, we have made this request of your father.

children.text: pitrā saha gṛhaṃ gaccha vayaṃ yāmaḥ svamandiram ||
children.translated_text: Go home with your father; we shall go to our own abode.

children.text: ityuktā tapasaḥ satyaṃ phalamastīti cintya sā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, she thought, "The fruit of austerity is truly real,"
and, hurrying, went to her father's house, shining with divine wealth.

children.text: sā tatra rajanīṃ mene varṣāyutasamāṃ satī
children.translated_text: There the chaste daughter of <s>Himādri</s> considered that night equal to ten thousand years,
for great longing had arisen in her from the sight of <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: tato muhūrte brāhme tu tasyāścakruḥ surastriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, at the brāhma muhūrta, the women of the gods performed for her
many heaps of auspicious rites, properly and in due order.
In the highly auspicious mansion there was divine adornment for her limbs.
The seasons, embodied and granting every desire, attended upon the mountain.
The winds and clouds were engaged in the rite of sweeping the mountain.
In the palaces the goddess <s>Śrī</s> herself had made many decorations.
Beauty was present in all conditions, and prosperity became abundant.
Wish-fulfilling gems and other jewels attended the mountain on every side.
Trees too, great wish-granting trees, stood near.
The herbs, embodied and furnished with divine medicines, also attended.
Essences and minerals too were all attendants of the mountain.
The servants of that mountain were busy and obedient to his command.

children.text: nadyaḥ samudrā nikhilāḥ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: The rivers, all the oceans, and whatever was stationary or moving...
All that increased the greatness of the snowy mountain.
Sages, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras were there,
and the gods also of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, on <s>Gandhamādana</s> mountain.
All the materials for adornment stood ready, their forms spotless,
and <s>Pitāmaha</s> fastened the crescent moon in the matted crest of <s>Śarva</s>.
His eyes were widened by generous affection as he did so.
<s>Cāmuṇḍā</s> tied a broad garland of skulls upon his head,

children.text: uvāca cāpi vacanaṃ putraṃ janaya śaṃkara
children.translated_text: and she spoke these words: "Generate a son, O <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
who, after slaying the race of the daitya lords, will satisfy me with their blood."
<s>Śauri</s>, taking up a blazing jewel-crested crown, fierce with fire,
and a serpent ornament, stood ready before <s>Śambhu</s>.
<s>Śakra</s> held his elephant-hide garment, its front edge smeared with fat,
eagerly, while his broad lotus-face was beaded with sweat.
And <s>Vāyu</s> adorned the great, mighty bull, broad and sharp-horned,
bright like <s>Himagiri</s>, the vehicle of <s>Hara</s>.
The suns, fires, and moons dwelling in the corners of <s>Śambhu</s>'s eyes
spread their own radiance for the lord of worlds, the witness of the world's deeds.
Having applied cremation-ground ash, silver-bright, upon his skull,
he tied on, with his hand, a garland made of human bones.
The lord of ghosts stood before the doorway, mace in hand.
The ornament of great jewels of many forms, brought by <s>Dhanada</s>,
the Lord set aside; with his own hand and with a bracelet of towering serpent-kings,
he himself made <s>Vāsuki</s> and <s>Takṣaka</s> into ear-pendants.
Separately there was one brought by the lord of waters, wrapped with enduring blossoms.
Then those lords of the <s>gaṇas</s> (attendant hosts), out of discipline, spoke there to <s>Vīraka</s>:
"You, anxious one, report the matter to <s>Śūlin</s>,
that the god, whose ornaments are complete, has been arrayed as Lord with adornments."
The seven oceans stood there to serve as a semblance of a mirror.
Then, seeing himself in the belly of the great ocean's waters,
<s>Keśava</s>, touching the earth with his knees, spoke to <s>Sthāṇu</s>:
"O god, you shine with a form that gives joy to the universe."
The Mothers urged forward the bride of <s>Kāma</s>, marked with signs of widowhood,
recognizing by sign and gesture, "This is the time."
Then, prompted by them, they spoke to the god with smiling faces:
"<s>Rati</s> has come before you; bereft of <s>Madana</s>, she does not shine."
Then, having reassured her, he indicated with the tip of his left hand
his departure, his mind eager for the sight of <s>Girijā</s>'s face.

children.text: tato haro himagirikandarākṛtiṃ sitaṃ kaśāmṛduhatibhiḥ pracodayat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hara</s> urged on, with soft strokes of the whip, the great bull, white as a cave of the snow mountain,
watched by the tumultuous <s>gaṇas</s>, making the mountains tremble like a thunderbolt.
Then <s>Hari</s>, moving with swift steps ahead, approached those gathered in clusters of trees before him,
his ornaments greyed by the dust of the earth, and said, "Go on; do not make his path narrow."

children.text: prabhoḥ punaḥ prathamaniyogamūrjayan suto 'bravīd bhrukuṭimukho'pi vīrakaḥ
children.translated_text: Again <s>Vīraka</s>, his brow furrowed, strengthened the lord's first command and said:

children.text: viyaccarā viyati kimasti kāntakaṃ prayāta no dharaṇidharāvidūrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Sky-goers, what obstruction is there in the sky? Move on, not close beside the mountains.
Great oceans, make your waters like stone, a vast impassable mire for the coming of the foes of the gods.

children.text: gaṇeśvarāś capalatayā na gamyatāṃ sureśvaraiḥ sthiramatibhir nirīkṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Lords of the <s>gaṇas</s>, do not proceed restlessly; you are watched by the steady-minded lords of the gods.

children.text: na bhṛṅgiṇā svatanumavekṣya nīyate pinākinaḥ pṛthumukhamaṇḍam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhṛṅgin</s>, looking at your own body, do not carry the broad-mouthed skull-bowl of <s>Pinākin</s> in front.

children.text: vṛthā yamaḥ prakaṭitadantakoṭaraṃ tvamāyudhaṃ vahasi vihāya saṃbhramam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>, you needlessly display the hollow of your teeth and carry your weapon; give up alarm.

children.text: padaṃ na yadrathaturagaiḥ puradviṣaḥ pramucyate bahutaramātṛsaṃkulam
children.translated_text: Where the path of the foe of the cities cannot be freed by chariot-horses, crowded as it is with many Mothers,

children.text: amī surāḥ pṛthaganuyāyibhirvṛtāḥ padātayo dviguṇapathān harapriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these gods, each surrounded by his own followers, go on foot, dear to <s>Hara</s>, making the road twice as wide.
Go, gods, with your own vehicles, with chowries shaken by the wind, with moving banners, and with sportive bearing.

children.text: surāḥ svakaṃ kimiti sarāgamūrjitaṃ vicāryate niyatalayatrayānugam ||
children.translated_text: Why is your own impassioned and vigorous movement, following the three fixed tempos, still being considered?

children.text: na kiṃnarair abhibhavituṃ hi śakyate vibhūṣaṇacayasamudbhavo dhvaniḥ
children.translated_text: Surely the sound arising from the mass of ornaments cannot be overpowered by the kiṃnaras.

children.text: ajātijāḥ kimiti na ṣaḍjamadhyamapṛthusvaraṃ bahutaramatra vakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Why should the broad notes of <s>ṣaḍja</s> and <s>madhyama</s> not be sounded here in abundance by the musical classes?
Having reached patterns of bent and unbent tones, they have become separately differentiated according to convention;
these <s>Gauḍakas</s>, fearing your very discriminating nature, proceed with swift steps.

children.text: visaṃhatāḥ kimiti na ṣāḍgavādayaḥ svagītakair lalitapadaprayogajaiḥ
children.translated_text: Why are the <s>ṣāḍgava</s> performances not kept distinct through their songs born of graceful verbal usage?

children.text: prabhoḥ puro bhavati hi yasya cākṣataṃ samudgatārthakamiti tatpratīyate ||
children.translated_text: For whatever comes before the lord with its meaning intact is understood as successful.
These many nāga clans, playful and possessed of many <s>gamakas</s> (ornamental turns),
perform a separately composed, charming <s>rāsaka</s> (dance) and a <s>prakīrṇaka</s> (mixed piece) that spreads <s>Giriśa</s>'s fame.

children.text: amī kathaṃ kakubhi kathāḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ dhvananti te vividhavadhūvimiśritāḥ
children.translated_text: How do these tales resound in every direction at every moment, mingled with various women?

children.text: na jātayo dhvanimurajāsamīritā na mūrchitāḥ kimiti ca mūrchanātmakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Are the <s>jātis</s> (melodic modes) not sounded by the murajas, and why, being based on <s>mūrchanā</s> (modal progression), are they not modulated?
Why has <s>Tumburu</s> not sounded the stringed music and the rest, which establish pleasant sequences and variations of movement?

children.text: na hanyate bahuvidhavādyaḍambaraṃ prakīrṇavīṇāmurajādi nāma yat ||
children.translated_text: Nor is the loud array of many instruments struck, what is called the scattered vīṇās, murajas, and so on."

children.text: itīrate girimavadhānaśālinaḥ surāsurāḥ sapadi tu vīrakājñayā
children.translated_text: As they spoke thus, attentive to the mountain, the gods and asuras at once, by <s>Vīraka</s>'s command,
Set in order, they went forth, exceedingly delighted, and filled the whole world, moving and unmoving.
Thus, while the quarters thundered and the great ocean roared, while the clouds thundered and the mountain caves were split,
the mountain, as though tumultuous in the world, was thrown into agitation by <s>Pinākin</s> moving swiftly.
It had thousands of blazing golden gateways, here with terraces of joined emerald mansions,
there with pure beryl platforms, and here and there with lovely waterfalls from flowing clouds.
It was adorned with thousands of excellent fluttering banners, its squares strewn with clusters from divine trees,
colored with mineral hues of white, black, and red, bright with splendor, with broad roads and gateways,
filled with spreading, unequaled sounds like clouds, and charming with fragrant city breezes.
Praised by the foremost gods and demons, <s>Hara</s> reached the city of the great mountain as if in a moment.
When it saw him entering, the city of the lord of mountains became agitated,
filled with busy women, accompanied by cries of victory, its roads rushed upon and its streets crowded with people.
At the palace windows a garland of blue lotuses appeared: the eyes of the immortal women,
clearly visible, though hidden within a canopy of rays from their own ornaments.
One woman, her adornment and ornaments all disordered, abandoning affection for her friend, looked at <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: kāciduvāca kalaṃ gatamānā kātaratāṃ sakhi mā kuru mūḍhe ||
children.translated_text: Another, moving gracefully, said, "Friend, do not become timid, foolish girl.

children.text: dagdhamanobhava eva pinākī kāmayate svayameva vihartum
children.translated_text: The bow-bearing one, by whom <s>Manobhava</s> has been burned, himself desires to sport."

children.text: kācidapi svayameva patantī prāha parāṃ virahaskhalitāṅgīm ||
children.translated_text: Yet another, herself stumbling, spoke to another woman whose limbs were faltering from longing:

children.text: mā capale madanavyatiṣaṅgaṃ śaṃkarajaṃ skhalanena vada tvam
children.translated_text: "Do not, fickle one, call your passionate attachment born of <s>Śaṅkara</s> a mere stumble."
One woman, unable to see because an obstruction had been made, said by inference, "This is surely <s>Giriśa</s>.

children.text: eṣa sa yatra sahasramakhādyā nākasadāmadhipāḥ svayamuktaiḥ
children.translated_text: This is he before whom <s>Sahasramakha</s> and the other lords of the dwellers in heaven,
with names uttered by themselves, bow down to the moon-crested one for the fruit gained by their own service.

children.text: eṣa na caiṣa sa eṣa yadagre carmaparītatanuḥ śaśimaulī
children.translated_text: This is that very one, the moon-crested lord whose body is wrapped in a hide;
before him the vajra-bearing king of the immortals runs to open this road.
This is that <s>Padmabhava</s>; approaching the one concealed by lofty matted hair and a deerskin,
with affection and with his hand at his mouth, he spoke a few measured words into his ear."
Thus the women of the gods became deeply unsettled in mind through great passion,
and they said, "Because of resorting to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the birth of <s>Girijā</s> has attained its highest fruit."
Then there was the house of <s>Himagiri</s>, made by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
with columns of great sapphire and a pavement of blazing gold,
adorned with lattices of pearls and lit by shining herbs,
rich in a thousand pleasure gardens and in long ponds of golden lotuses.
Seeing that wonder, all the gods headed by <s>Mahendra</s>
thought in their minds, "Today our eyes have fulfilled their purpose."
Their armlets worn thin by jostling, blocked at the doorway by <s>Hari</s>,
the chief dwellers in heaven somehow entered there.
Then the four-faced god, honored by the bowing king of mountains,
performed the whole rite according to rule, preceded by the ritual formulas.
The taking of <s>Śarva</s>'s hand was intact, with fire as witness;
the giver was the lord of mountains, and the officiating priest was the four-faced god.
The bridegroom was <s>Paśupati</s> himself, and the bride likewise the universal araṇi (fire-kindling stick);
the moving and unmoving beings, and the best of gods and demons,
there too all these, according to rule, became eager in form.
The earth released all fresh grains, rice crops, juices, and medicinal plants.
The goddess Earth, eager and lovely in every form, stood there;
and <s>Varuṇa</s>, taking all jewels and ornaments,
holy and purifying things made of various gems,
stood adorned, the god giving joy to all embodied beings.
<s>Dhanada</s> too came forward with divine golden ornaments,
variegated with refined gold, intent and reverent.
<s>Vāyu</s>, the all-pervading one, blew very fragrantly and pleasantly to the touch.
And <s>Śatakratu</s>, delighted and garlanded, took up a very white umbrella gleaming like a moonbeam,
with arms decked in many ornaments.
The chief gandharvas sang, and hosts of apsarases danced.
The gandharvas and kinnaras played very sweet music and sang;
the seasons there, embodied, also sang and danced.
The lively gaṇas stood there, shaking <s>Himācala</s>.
Then, rising in due order, <s>Viśvabhuk</s>, the destroyer of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye,
performed the wedding duty with his wife as was proper.
Given arghya by <s>Girirāja</s> and entertained by the hosts of gods,

children.text: avasattāṃ kṣapāṃ tatra patnyā saha purāntakaḥ
children.translated_text: the destroyer of cities spent that night there with his wife.
Then, by the song of the gandharvas and the dancing of the apsarases,
and by the praises of gods and daityas, the lord of the gods awoke.
Taking leave of <s>Himaśailendra</s> in the morning, together with <s>Umā</s>,
he went to <s>Mandara</s> mountain with the speed of wind, mounted on the horned one.

children.text: tato gate bhagavati nīlalohite sahomayā ratimalabhanna bhūdharaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s> had gone with <s>Umā</s>, the mountain found no pleasure;

children.text: sabāndhavo bhavati ca kasya no mano vihvalaṃ ca jagati hi kanyakāpituḥ ||
children.translated_text: for whose mind in this world, together with his kinsmen, does not become bewildered when he is the father of a daughter?
The city was magnificent with blazing jewels, crystal, and gold, with crystal gateways of clear radiance.
Then <s>Hara</s>, after the multitude of immortals had been dismissed, entered his own abode on the mountain, which had long been prepared.
Then the god, together with <s>Umā</s>, the destroyer of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye, sported
in lovely palace gardens and in secluded forests.
His heart deeply attached to the goddess, with <s>Makarāṅka</s> going before him,

children.text: tato bahutithe kāle sutakāmā gireḥ sutā ||
children.translated_text: then, after much time had passed, the daughter of the mountain, desiring a son,
played together with her companions with artificial little sons.
Once, after anointing her body with scented oil, <s>Śailajā</s>
rubbed her body with powders, so that the dirt was separated out.
Taking that rubbing paste, she fashioned an elephant-faced man.
Playing, the goddess made him her little son and also placed him in the water.
Then, through <s>Jāhnavī</s>, <s>Śivā</s>'s friend, he became great-bodied.
With an exceedingly vast body he filled the world at that time.

children.text: putretyuvāca te devī putretyūce ca jāhnavī ||
children.translated_text: The goddess called him "son," and <s>Jāhnavī</s> too said "son."
Honored by the gods as <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, the elephant-faced one became worshiped.
<s>Pitāmaha</s> granted him lordship over the vināyakas.

children.text: punaḥ sā krīḍanaṃ cakre putrārthaṃ varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: Again that fair-complexioned woman made a plaything, desiring a son.
The lovely-faced one raised a charming sprout that had grown from an aśoka tree,
and she caused it too to grow, with auspicious rites and consecrations performed
by brahmins headed by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, with <s>Divaspati</s> going before them.

children.text: tato devaiśca munibhiḥ proktā devī tvidaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the gods and sages spoke this speech to the goddess:
"O <s>Bhavānī</s>, venerable and auspicious lady, you have arisen for the welfare of beings.
For the most part, a world is fruitful through a son, and is obtained through sons and grandsons.
And people without sons are generally seen to be so because of fate.
Now that a path has been shown, you ought to establish a rule.
What fruit will there be, goddess, from imagined tree-sons?"
Thus addressed, <s>Umā</s>, her limbs filled with joy, spoke an auspicious word.

children.text: evaṃ nirudake deśe yaḥ kūpaṃ kārayedbudhaḥ
children.translated_text: "Thus, in a waterless place, the wise man who has a well made

children.text: bindau bindau ca toyasya vasetsaṃvatsaraṃ divi ||
children.translated_text: dwells in heaven for a year for every drop of water.
A vāpī is equal to ten wells, and a lake is equal to ten vāpīs.
A son is equal to ten lakes, and a tree is equal to ten sons.
This alone is my fixed rule, one that will benefit the world."
After they had been addressed thus, the brahmins headed by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>
went to their own houses, having respectfully honored <s>Bhavānī</s>.
When they had gone, the god <s>Śaṃkara</s> too took the daughter of the mountain
by the left hand and gently led the auspicious one inside,
into a palace with gateway after gateway, bringing serenity to the mind,
with long strings of pearls and platforms crowded with garlands,
bright with cleansed silver and charming with pleasure caves,
fragrant with scattered flowers and filled with the humming of rows of intoxicated bees,
with inner walls containing music-halls where kinnaras sang,
filled with masses of fragrant incense, desired by the mind and hard to take in by sight,
surrounded by playing peahens and women, and by players of stringed instruments,
resounding with flocks of haṃsas, with crystal pillars and platforms,
clear, free from confusion, and everywhere crowded with kinnaras,
where parrots strike against walls made of rubies,
mistaking them for pomegranates because they reflect pearls.
There the goddess began to amuse herself with a game of dice.
In that play, seated on a floor-space of clear sapphire,
the two attained bodily companionship and were fulfilled by the flavor of amusement.
While the goddess and <s>Śaṃkara</s> were thus playing there,
a great sound arose within the interior of that house.
Hearing it, the goddess, out of curiosity, asked <s>Śaṃkara</s>, "What is this?"
The fair-bodied one questioned <s>Hara</s> with astonishment.
He said to the goddess, "This has not been seen by you before, greatly amazed one.
These <s>Gaṇeśas</s>, dear to me, always play on this mountain.
By austerity, brahmacarya, restraints, and service at sacred fields,

children.text: yairahaṃ toṣitaḥ pūrvaṃ ta ete manujottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the best of men who formerly pleased me are these.
They have come into my presence and are dear to my heart, lovely-faced one.
They assume forms at will, are of great energy, and are endowed with great beauty and virtues.
I am amazed at the deeds of those strong ones.
They are capable of creating and destroying the moving and unmoving world.
Even when surrounded by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, gandharvas, together with kinnaras and great serpents,
I am never, beloved, separated from these.

children.text: hṛdyā me cārusarvāṅgi ta ete krīḍitā girau
children.translated_text: They are dear to me, charming in every limb; these have been playing on the mountain."

children.text: ityuktā tu tato devī tyaktvā tadvismayākulā ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the goddess, bewildered with that astonishment, left the game,
and, reaching an opening among the windows, looked out with an amazed face.

children.text: yāvantaste kṛśā dīrghā hrasvāḥ sthūlā mahodarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As many as they were, some were thin, tall, short, stout, and pot-bellied;
some had faces of tigers and elephants, and some had the forms of sheep and goats.
They had the forms of many living beings, with flaming mouths, black and tawny.
They were gentle and terrible, smiling-faced, with black and tawny masses of matted hair.
They had faces of many birds and faces of many kinds of beasts.
They wore silk and hides; others were naked and misshapen.
They had cow-ears and elephant-ears, and many mouths, eyes, and bellies.
They had many feet and many arms, and held many divine weapons in their hands.
They wore many flower-crests and were adorned with various serpents.
They had wolf-faces, bore weapons, and were adorned with various armors.
They were mounted on strange vehicles, divine in form, and moved through the sky.
They were filled with the sound of vīṇā music and danced in various positions.
After seeing those <s>Gaṇeśas</s> in that way, the goddess spoke to <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
The goddess said:
How many <s>Gaṇeśas</s> are counted? What are their names? What is their nature?

children.text: ekaikaśo mama brūhi dhiṣṭhitā ye pṛthakpṛthak ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, one by one, of those who are established separately as my own.
<s>Śaṃkara</s> said:
They are numbered by crores, yet innumerable, and are famous for manifold prowess.
The whole world is filled by all these terrible, mighty ones.
In fields of siddhas, in streets, in decayed gardens, and in houses,
in the bodies of dānavas, in children, and in madmen too,
these delighted ones enter, enjoying various foods and wanderings.
Some live on warmth, some on foam, some on smoke, and some drink honey;
some drink blood, some eat everything, some live on wind, and some have water as their food.
They are fond of offerings of song and dance and of the sounds of many instruments.

children.text: na hyeṣāṃ vai anantatvādguṇānvaktuṃ hi śakyate ||
children.translated_text: Because they are endless, it is not possible to speak of their qualities.
The goddess said:
With an upper garment of animal skin, with pure limbs, and with a girdle of muñja grass,
restless, his face colored with a paste of red arsenic,
wearing a tied garland-string of blue lotuses, lovely and sweet in form,
setting in motion bronze cymbals with an upturned shard of stone,
who is this divine lord of gaṇas, and what is his name, attended by kinnaras,
who again and again gives ear to the songs of the gaṇas?

children.text: sa eṣa vīrako devi sadā maddhṛdayapriyaḥ
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>Vīraka</s>, O goddess, always dear to my heart,
a support of many wondrous qualities, honored by the hosts of the lords of gaṇas.
The goddess said:
For such a son I have longing, O destroyer of cities.
When shall I see such a son, a giver of joy?
<s>Śiva</s> said:
Let this very one be your son, the cause of delight to your eyes.
Let <s>Vīraka</s> also be fulfilled by you as his mother, O fair-waisted one.
Thus addressed, the daughter of the mountain sent <s>Vijayā</s>, eager in her joy,
to bring <s>Vīraka</s> quickly.
She descended in haste from the palace that touched the sky.
<s>Vijayā</s>, having entered among the gaṇas, spoke to the lord of gaṇas.
<s>Vijayā</s> said:
Come, <s>Vīraka</s>. Because of your restlessness the god has been angered.
What answer does <s>Śailajā</s> speak about the matter here in the dance-arena?
Thus addressed, he threw aside the shard of stone and wiped his face.
Summoned by her, he indicated the original occasion that had arisen.
Guarded by <s>Vijayā</s>, he slowly came into the presence of the goddess,
from the palace-peak, with a brilliance like a full-blown red lotus.
Seeing him, <s>Girijā</s>'s breasts flowed with abundant sweet milk.
With affection she spoke in a voice sweet in tone.
<s>Umā</s> said:

children.text: ehyehi yāto'si me putratāṃ devadevena datto'dhunā vīraka ||
children.translated_text: Come, come, O <s>Vīraka</s>; you have now entered the state of being my son, given by the God of gods.
Then, placing that sweet-speaking child on her lap, she kissed him on the cheeks.

children.text: mūrdhnyupāghrāya saṃmārjya gātrāṇi bhūṣayāmāsa divyaiḥ svayaṃ bhūṣaṇaiḥ kiṅkiṇīmekhalānūpurair māṇikyakeyūrahārorumūlaguṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Smelling his head and wiping his limbs, she herself adorned him with divine ornaments: tinkling girdles, anklets, jeweled armlets, necklaces, and fine body-bands.

children.text: komalaiḥ pallavaiścitritaiścārubhir divyamantrodbhavais tasya śubhaistato bhūribhiścākaronmiśrasiddhārthakair aṅgarakṣāvidhim ||
children.translated_text: Then, with tender, variegated, lovely leaves born of divine mantras, and with many auspicious mixed mustard seeds, she performed the rite for protecting his body.

children.text: evamādāya covāca kṛtvā srajaṃ mūrdhni gorocanāpatrabhaṅgojjvalam ||
children.translated_text: Taking him up in this way, she placed a garland on his head, bright with leaf-marks of gorocanā, and spoke:

children.text: gaccha gacchādhunā krīḍa sārdhaṃ gaṇairapramatto nage śvabhravarja śanairvyālamālākulāḥ śailasānudrumadantibhir bhinnasārāḥ pare saṅginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Go, go now; play with the gaṇas, but be careful on the mountain. Avoid chasms; move slowly where masses of snakes abound, and where the mountain slopes and trees have been broken by elephants.

children.text: jāhnavīyaṃ jalaṃ kṣubdhatoyākulaṃ kūlaṃ mā viśethā bahuvyāghraduṣṭe vane ||
children.translated_text: Do not enter the water of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, whose stream is turbulent, nor the riverbank in a forest made dangerous by many tigers.
Dear child, among these countless, difficult gaṇa-lords, let <s>Durgā</s> remain inwardly satisfied by the sonship of this <s>Vīraka</s>.
May the auspicious future condition, prayed for by his own paternal people, come to pass.

children.text: so'pi nirvartya sarvān gaṇān sasmayamāha bālatvalīlārasāviṣṭadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: He too, dismissing all the gaṇas, spoke with a smile, his mind absorbed in the flavor of childish play:

children.text: eṣa mātrā svayaṃ me kṛtabhūṣaṇo'tra eṣa paṭaḥ pāṭalairbindubhiḥ sinduvārasya puṣpairiyaṃ mālatīmiśritā mālikā me śirasyāhitā ||
children.translated_text: Here is the ornament made for me by my mother herself; here is a cloth with red dots; this garland, mixed with sinduvāra flowers and mālatī, has been placed on my head.
Who is this gaṇa holding a musical instrument? I shall put this plaything into his hand.

children.text: dakṣiṇātpaścimaṃ paścimāduttaramuttarātpūrvamabhyetya sakhyā yutā prekṣatī taṃ gavākṣāntarādvīrakaṃ śailaputrī bahiḥ krīḍanaṃ yajjaganmāturapyeṣa cittabhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the south to the west, from the west to the north, and from the north to the east, <s>Śailaputrī</s>, together with her friend, watched <s>Vīraka</s> playing outside through a lattice-window; this was a bewilderment of heart even for the Mother of the world.

children.text: putralubdho janastatra ko mohamāyāti na svalpacetā jaḍo māṃsaviṇmūtrasaṃghātadehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When people are greedy for a son, what small-minded, dull person, whose body is a mass of flesh, excrement, and urine, does not fall into delusion?
When the lords dwelling in heaven had entered the inner chamber to see the moon-crested one,

children.text: vāhanātyāvarohā gaṇāstairyuto lokapālāstramūrto hyayaṃ khaḍgo vikhaḍgakaro nirmamaḥ kṛtāntaḥ kasya kenāhato brūta maune bhavanto'stradaṇḍena kiṃ duḥspṛhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the gaṇas, having dismounted from their vehicles, were with them. "This one, weapon-formed like a guardian of the worlds, sword in hand and sword-bearing, pitiless like Death itself: by whom and with what has he been struck? Speak. Why are you silent, holding weapons and staffs?"

children.text: bhīmamūrtyānanenāsti kṛtyaṃ girau ya eṣo'strajñena kiṃ vadhyate ||
children.translated_text: "What business is there on the mountain with this terrible-faced form? By what master of weapons is he to be slain?"

children.text: mā vṛthā lokapālānugacittatā evam evaitad ityūcurasmai tadā devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Do not set your minds vainly upon the attendants of the guardians of the worlds." "So it is indeed," the deities then said to him.

children.text: devadevānugaṃ vīrakaṃ lakṣaṇā prāha devī vanaṃ parvatā nirjharāṇyagnidevyānyatho bhūtapā nirjharāmbhonipāteṣu nimajjata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣaṇā</s>, the goddess, spoke to <s>Vīraka</s>, attendant of the God of gods: "The forest, the mountains, the waterfalls, the fiery goddesses, and then the bhūtas: plunge into the falling waters of the cascades.
In dwellings covered with nets of flowers and in lofty bowers of many mountains, roar back as you wish, through the beating and striking of the golden wind."

children.text: kāñcanottuṅgaśṛṅgāvarohakṣitau hemareṇūtkarāsaṅgadyutiṃ khecarāṇāṃ vanādhāyini ramye bahurūpasaṃpatprakare gaṇānvāsitaṃ mandarakandare sundaramandārapuṣpapravālāmbuje siddhanārībhir āpītarūpāmṛtaṃ vistṛtair netrapātrair anunmeṣibhir vīrake śailaputrī nimeṣāntarād asmaratputragṛdhrī vinodārthinī ||
children.translated_text: In the beautiful cave of <s>Mandara</s>, where the slopes beneath its lofty golden peaks shone with masses of golden dust clinging to them, where forests delighted the sky-goers, where there were troops enriched with manifold beauty, lovely mandāra flowers, shoots, and lotuses, and where the perfected women drank in the nectar of his beauty with wide, unwinking vessels of their eyes, <s>Śailaputrī</s>, desirous of sport and longing for her son, remembered <s>Vīraka</s> in the space of a blink.

children.text: so'pi tādṛkkṣaṇāvāptapuṇyodayo yo'pi janmāntarasyātmajatvaṃ gataḥ krīḍatastasya tṛptiḥ kathaṃ jāyate yo'pi bhāvijagadvedhasā tejasaḥ kalpitaḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ divyagītakṣaṇo nṛtyalolo gaṇeśaiḥ praṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He too, whose rise of merit had been gained in such a moment, who had become her son from another birth, how could satisfaction arise in him as he played? For he had been fashioned for the splendor of the future creator of the world, each moment filled with divine song, fond of dancing, and honored by the leaders of the gaṇas.
For a moment he played on a cheek-like cliff filled with lions' roars, where a web of jewels was being poured forth and great sāla and tāla trees stood;

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ phullanānātamālālikāle kṣaṇaṃ vṛkṣamūle vilolo marāle ||
children.translated_text: for a moment in a grove dark with many blossoming tamāla creepers, and for a moment at the root of a tree where swans moved restlessly;

children.text: kṣaṇe svalpapaṅke jale paṅkajāḍhye kṣaṇaṃ māturaṅke śubhe niṣkalaṅke
children.translated_text: for a moment in shallow mud and in water rich with lotuses, and for a moment in his mother's pure, stainless, auspicious lap.
The lord of the gaṇas, a source of joy to the gods, sported there, enjoying the games of childhood.
In the bowers, sung about by vidyādharas, he moved gracefully with playful charms, like <s>Pinākin</s> himself.
Then, when the sun, after illumining the expanse of the worlds,
had gone afterward to another region, far away to the western mountain,
the mountain that stands before him at his rising and setting
was to be regarded in the heart as one whose friendship with him was very firm.
Though glorious <s>Meru</s>, broad-rooted and lofty, was always worshiped,
he did not make an offering of service to the one who was about to descend.
A wise person might doubt that this same order applies even in water,
but the sun, following the end of day, fulfilled his kinship with his own people.
The sages, with the hollows of their joined hands bound in twilight reverence and facing the sun,
begged for his swift return, while checking the darkness imagined within themselves.

children.text: vyajṛmbhata tathā loke kramād vaibhāvaraṃ tamaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, gradually, night-darkness expanded through the world,
like pollution in the heart of a crooked man, defiling the mind.
In a chamber whose walls were lit by lamps made from the blazing gems on serpents' hoods,
there was a bed with an upper cover and garments white as a mass of moonlight,
imitating a rainbow with the brilliance of many jewels,
with a net of jeweled little bells and hanging clusters of pearls,
its sky-like space covered by a lovely, gently swaying canopy.
In that palace, moving slowly and gently together with <s>Girisutā</s>,
he remained with his neck encircled by the creeper of <s>Girisutā</s>'s arms,
the range of sight filled with the pure white moonlight from the moon on his crest.
<s>Girijā</s> too, dark at the corners of her eyes and with the luster of blue-lotus petals,
mingled with the night and became exceedingly full of darkness.
Then the god spoke to her, who was endowed with the arts of playful dalliance.
<s>Śarva</s> said:
On my fair body, slender-waisted one, you shine with a dark radiance;
pure though you are, you are like a black female serpent embracing a sandalwood tree.
Joined with the moonlight and with your charming garment too,
you give my eyes a blemish, like the night in the dark fortnight.
Thus addressed by <s>Pinākin</s>, whose throat was uncovered,
<s>Girijā</s> spoke, her eyes reddened with anger and her face bent by a frown.
The Goddess said:
Every person is overcome by his own dullness,
and one who asks for something must surely meet with humiliation among people.
That which I sought through long-practiced austerities

children.text: tasyā me niyatastveṣa hyavamānaḥ pade pade ||
children.translated_text: has become for me this fixed insult at every step.

children.text: naivāsmi kuṭilā śarva viṣamā naiva dhūrjaṭe
children.translated_text: I am not crooked, <s>Śarva</s>; I am not harsh, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>.
It is you who have become famous as one who has gone among objects of sense, clearly taking refuge in a mine of faults.

children.text: nāhaṃ pūṣṇo'pi daśanā netre cāsmi bhagasya hi
children.translated_text: I am not the teeth of <s>Pūṣan</s>, nor am I the eyes of <s>Bhaga</s>;
and the blessed twelve-formed <s>Āditya</s> knows this.
You bring a spear upon your own head, blaming me with your own faults,
you who call me 'black,' while you yourself are famed as <s>Mahākāla</s>.
I shall go to the mountain, abandoning myself through austerity;

children.text: jīvantyā nāsti me kṛtyaṃ dhūrtena paribhūtayā ||
children.translated_text: living, I have no task left, humiliated by a cheat.
Hearing her words, sharp in anger, <s>Bhava</s>
spoke in a voice mixed with confusion, agitation, and affection.
<s>Śarva</s> said:
You do not know yourself, <s>Girijā</s>; I am not intent on blaming you.
I took shelter in your name through a mind of devotion toward you.
Even in a settled mind, <s>Girijā</s>, an alternative thought is not a real imagining.

children.text: yadyevaṃ kupitā bhīru tvaṃ tavāhaṃ na vai punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If you are angry in this way, timid one, then I shall not again
speak in jest to you. Abandon your anger, pure-smiling one.
I am bowed with my head, and I have formed this añjali for you.
Even through affection, a person becomes changed when stung by insult and blame;

children.text: tasmānna jātu ruṣṭasya narmaspṛṣṭo janaḥ kila ||
children.translated_text: therefore one should certainly never touch an angry person with joking words.
Though the goddess was instructed by the god with many flatteries,

children.text: kopaṃ tīvraṃ na tatyāja satī marmaṇi ghaṭṭitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Satī</s>, struck in a tender place, did not abandon her intense anger.
Then, shaking loose the garment restrained by <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s hand,
<s>Śailajā</s>, her locks disordered, wished to go away in haste.
As she was going in anger, the destroyer of cities spoke again:
Truly, in every limb you are a daughter resembling your father.
As the sky is hard to penetrate because of those peaks of <s>Himācala</s> crowded with masses of clouds,
so your intention is hard to fathom because of your inaccessible hearts.
Marked by hardness, you have gone from us in many ways to the forests.
And crookedness from the paths, difficulty of being approached even because of snow,
and constant shifting, O slender one, belong to the king of snowy mountains.

children.text: ityuktā sā punaḥ prāha giriśaṃ śailajā tadā
children.translated_text: When she had been addressed in this way, <s>Śailajā</s> then spoke again to <s>Giriśa</s>,
her head trembling with anger and the covering of her teeth quivering.
<s>Umā</s> said:
Do not blame all good people, worthy of no censure, by assigning faults to them.
For in your case too, through contact with the wicked, all this has passed over to you.
From serpents you have many-tonguedness; through ashes, a bond of affection;
from the moon, impurity of heart; and from the bull, even dull incomprehensibility.

children.text: tathā bahu kimuktena alaṃ vācā śrameṇa te
children.translated_text: Likewise, what need is there of saying much? Enough of this weariness of speech for you.

children.text: śmaśānavāsān nirbhīs tvaṃ nagnatvānna tava trapā
children.translated_text: From dwelling in the cremation ground you are fearless; from nakedness you have no shame;
from bearing skulls you are pitiless, and compassion has long since departed from you.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having spoken thus, the daughter of <s>Himādri</s> went out from that mansion.
As she was going, a clamorous cry arose from the gaṇas of the lord of gods:

children.text: kva mātargacchasi tyaktvā rudanto dhāvitāḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Where are you going, mother, abandoning us?' Weeping, they ran after her again.
Planting himself at the goddess's feet, <s>Vīraka</s>, his voice choked with tears,
said, 'Mother, what is this? Where are you going, angry at heart?
I will follow you as you go, devoid of affection toward me;
otherwise, abandoned by you, O steadfast one in austerity, I will fall from the peak.'

children.text: unnāmya vadanaṃ devī dakṣiṇena tu pāṇinā
children.translated_text: The goddess, the mother, lifted his face with her right hand

children.text: uvāca vīrakaṃ mātā śokaṃ putraka mā kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and said to <s>Vīraka</s>, 'My child, do not grieve.

children.text: śailāgrātpatituṃ naiva na cāgantuṃ mayā saha
children.translated_text: It is not fitting for you either to fall from the mountain-top or to come with me.

children.text: yuktaṃ te putra vakṣyāmi yena kāryeṇa tacchṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: Son, I will tell you the task for which you are needed; listen to it.
Called "dark" by <s>Hara</s>, I have been censured, though I am blameless.
Therefore I shall perform austerity by which I may attain the state of <s>Gaurī</s>.
This god is fond of women; after I have gone away,
you must always guard the door, watching carefully for any opening.

children.text: yathā na kācit praviśed yoṣidatra harāntikam
children.translated_text: See that no woman enters here near <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā parāṃstriyaṃ cātra vadethā mama putraka ||
children.translated_text: And if you see another woman here, tell me, my child.
I will then quickly do what is proper afterward.'

children.text: evamastviti devīṃ sa vīrakaḥ prāha sāṃpratam ||
children.translated_text: 'So be it,' <s>Vīraka</s> presently said to the goddess.
His body flooded with the delighting nectar of his mother's command, free from distress,

children.text: jagāma kakṣāṃ saṃdraṣṭuṃ praṇipatya ca mātaram ||
children.translated_text: he bowed to his mother and went to inspect the inner chamber.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The goddess saw approaching an adorned goddess, a friend of her mother,
named <s>Kusumamodinī</s>, the deity of that mountain.
She too, seeing the daughter of the mountain, her mind shaken by affection,
embraced her and said aloud, 'Daughter, where are you going?'
She told her everything, the cause of her anger toward <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
and <s>Girijā</s> again spoke to the deity approved by her mother.
<s>Umā</s> said:
You are always the blameless deity of the lord of mountains;

children.text: sarvataḥ saṃnidhānaṃ te mama cātīva vatsalā ||
children.translated_text: your presence is everywhere, and you are exceedingly affectionate toward me.
Therefore I shall tell you what must be done; keep it in mind then.
You must carefully guard against the entrance of any other woman.
Secretly here on the mountain, always with careful attention in your mind,
if a woman enters the presence of <s>Pinākin</s>, you must tell me, O faultless one.
After that I shall arrange whatever action is to be taken.'

children.text: ityuktā sā tathetyuktvā jagāma svagiriṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: When she had been addressed thus, she said, 'So be it,' and went to her own auspicious mountain.
<s>Umā</s> too, the daughter of the mountain, quickly went to her father's garden,
entering the sky like a flash of radiance into a mass of clouds.
Then, setting aside her ornaments, she wore the bark of trees;
in summer she was scorched by the five fires, and in the rains she dwelt in water.
On winter nights she lay on a dry bare ground,
and in this way she remained there, accomplishing her aim through austerity.

children.text: jñātvā tu tāṃ girisutāṃ daityastatrāntare vaśī
children.translated_text: Meanwhile a deceitful daitya learned that the daughter of the mountain was there:
the proud son of <s>Andhaka</s>, remembering his father's death,
who had conquered all the gods in battle, the battle-fierce brother of <s>Baka</s>,
named <s>Āḍi</s>, always watching for an opening against the moon-crested one.
That enemy of the immortals came to the city of the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>.
Arriving there, he saw <s>Vīraka</s> stationed at the doorway.
He reflected on the boon that had formerly been given by the lotus-born one,
when the daitya <s>Andhaka</s>, enemy of the immortals, had been slain by <s>Giriśa</s>.
<s>Āḍi</s> had performed great and exceedingly dreadful austerity,
and <s>Brahmā</s>, pleased by his austerity, came to him and spoke:
'What, O <s>Āḍi</s>, best of dānavas, do you wish to obtain through austerity?'
The daitya said to <s>Brahmā</s>, 'I choose freedom from death.'
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: na kaścic ca vinā mṛtyuṃ naro dānava vidyate
children.translated_text: No one, O dānava, exists without death, neither man nor anyone else.
Therefore, O lord of daityas, death must somehow be reached by an embodied being.
Thus addressed, the lion among daityas said to the lotus-born one,
'When a transformation of my form should occur, O lotus-born one,
then let death be mine; otherwise I shall indeed be immortal.'
When he had spoken thus, the lotus-born one, pleased, then said:
'When there is a second alteration of your form,

children.text: tadā te bhavitā mṛtyuranyathā na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: then death will come to you; otherwise it will not occur.'
Thus addressed, the mighty son of the daitya considered himself immortal.
At that time, remembering the means of avoiding his own death,
he then set out to avoid the range of <s>Vīraka</s>'s sight.
Taking the form of a serpent, he entered through an opening, outside the path of sight,
and that very hard-to-conquer dānava avoided the lord of the gaṇas.
Then, unnoticed by the lord of gaṇas, he entered the presence of the destroyer of cities.
Abandoning his serpent-form, the great asura then became
one in the form of <s>Umā</s>, dull-minded, in order to deceive <s>Giriśa</s>.
Having produced illusion, he then made a form of inconceivable beauty,
complete in every limb and furnished with every identifying sign.
The daitya made teeth inside his mouth, firm and like thunderbolts,
with sharp points; through delusion of mind he was intent on killing <s>Giriśa</s>.
Having assumed the bodily form of <s>Umā</s>, the daitya went near <s>Hara</s>.
Sinful, yet lovely in appearance, he was adorned with wondrous ornaments and garments.
Seeing him, <s>Giriśa</s> was pleased, and he embraced the great asura,
thinking him to be the mountain's daughter in every one of her limbs.

children.text: apṛcchatsādhu te bhāvo giriputri na kṛtrimaḥ
children.translated_text: He asked, "Your disposition toward me is good, O mountain-born girl, not feigned,

children.text: yā tvaṃ madāśayaṃ jñātvā prāpteha varavarṇinī ||
children.translated_text: since you, knowing my desire, have come here, O fair-complexioned one.
Bereft of you, I have been thinking the three worlds empty.
You have come with a pleased face; such conduct is fitting in you."
Thus addressed, the lord of dānavas then spoke slowly with a smile,
and the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s> did not, for the most part, perceive the distinguishing sign.
The goddess said:
"I went to practice austerity so as to become incomparably dear to you.

children.text: ratiśca tatra me nābhūttataḥ prāptā tvadantikam ||
children.translated_text: But I had no delight there; therefore I have come near you."
Thus addressed, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, feeling a certain suspicion, considered the matter.
The god fixed it in his heart, his face smiling.

children.text: kupitā mayi tanvaṅgī prakṛtyā ca dṛḍhavratā
children.translated_text: "This slender one is angry with me, and by nature she is firm in her vows.
Has she come without attaining her desire? What is this? I have doubt."
Thinking thus, <s>Hara</s> looked for her distinguishing sign.
On the left side of that body he did not see the lotus mark,

children.text: lomāvartaṃ tu racitaṃ tato devaḥ pinākadhṛk
children.translated_text: but instead a fashioned whorl of hair. Then the god, bearer of <s>Pināka</s>,
recognized the dānava's illusion, while concealing his own intention.
Taking a thunderbolt-weapon in his member, he slew that dānava.
<s>Vīraka</s> did not know that the lord of dānavas had been slain.
Seeing the lord of dānavas, in female form, slain by <s>Hara</s>,
and not grasping the true meaning of the matter, she reported it to <s>Śailaputrī</s>.
The mountain-goddess, through a messenger, the swift-moving <s>Māruta</s>,
heard it from the mouth of <s>Vāyu</s>; the goddess's eyes were reddened with anger,
and, with her heart deeply pained, she cursed her son <s>Vīraka</s>.
The goddess said:
"Because you abandoned your mother, who was overcome with affection,
and made an opportunity for women in <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s secret rite,
therefore, harsh, rough, inert, and without heart,
O lord of gaṇas, your mother shall become a stone, caustic in nature."
This occasion became famous as the arising of <s>Vīraka</s>'s stone,
and in its very course it became the basis of a wondrous tale.
Immediately after the mountain's daughter had uttered that curse,
anger came forth from her mouth in the form of a lion, mighty in strength.
That lion had a terrible mouth, with a neck matted by tangled locks,
a long tail tossed high, and jaws made fierce by fangs.
Its mouth was gaping, its tongue lolling, its belly gaunt, and it wished to devour.

children.text: tasyāśu vartituṃ devī vyavasyata satī tadā
children.translated_text: The goddess, being <s>Satī</s>, then resolved quickly to act for him.
Knowing what was in her mind, the four-faced Lord
came then to the hermitage, a seat of prosperity.
Having arrived, the lord of gods spoke to <s>Girijā</s> in clear speech.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: kiṃ putri prāptukāmāsi kimalabhyaṃ dadāmi te
children.translated_text: "What do you wish to obtain, daughter? What unattainable thing shall I give you?
By my command, cease from this excessive hardship of austerity."
Hearing that, <s>Girijā</s> spoke a weighty statement full of reverence for the guru,
with speech whose long-drawn syllables made her desire clear.
The goddess said:
"By difficult austerity I obtained <s>Śaṃkara</s> as my husband.
But <s>Bhava</s> has often called me dark-complexioned.
May I become golden in appearance and endowed with his love.
May I enter one side of the body of my husband, lord of beings, as though one with his body."
Hearing those words of hers, the lotus-seated one said:
"So be it. And further, you shall bear half of your husband's body."
Then she cast off her bee-dark body, whose skin was like a blooming blue lotus.
From that skin there arose a radiant goddess, bell in hand and three-eyed,
with every limb filled with various ornaments, wearing yellow silk.
Then <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to that goddess of blue-lotus luster:
"O <s>Niśā</s>, through contact with the body of the mountain's daughter, by my command,
you have attained fulfillment; in former times you were <s>Ekānaṃśā</s>.

children.text: ya eṣa siṃhaḥ prodbhūto devyāḥ krodhādvarānane ||
children.translated_text: This lion, O fair-faced goddess, has arisen from the goddess's anger.

children.text: sa te'stu vāhanaṃ devi ketau cāstu mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Let him be your vehicle, O goddess, and let the mighty one be on your banner as well.
Go to the Vindhya mountain; there you will accomplish the gods' business.
This yakṣa named <s>Pañcāla</s>, attended by a hundred thousand yakṣa troops,
has been given to you by me as a servant, O goddess, furnished with hundreds of magical powers."

children.text: ityuktā kauśikī devī vindhyaśailaṃ jagāma ha
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the goddess <s>Kauśikī</s> went to the Vindhya mountain.
<s>Umā</s> too, having attained her resolve, went near <s>Giriśa</s>.
As she was entering through the door, the attentive <s>Vīraka</s> pulled her back
and stopped the goddess, holding a golden cane-staff.
He said to her angrily, judging from her appearance that she was false:

children.text: prayojanaṃ na te'stīha gaccha yāvanna bhetsyase ||
children.translated_text: "You have no business here. Go, before you are split apart.

children.text: devyā rūpadharo daityo devaṃ vañcayituṃ tviha
children.translated_text: A daitya, assuming the goddess's form, entered here to deceive the god.

children.text: praviṣṭo na ca dṛṣṭo'sau sa vai devena ghātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was not seen, and indeed he was killed by the god."
And when he had been slain, I was commanded by angry <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>:

children.text: dvāreṣu nāvadhānaṃ te yasmātpaśyāmi vai tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Since I indeed see no vigilance of yours at the doors,
therefore you shall not stand at my doorway for many heaps of years.

children.text: ataste'tra na dāsyāmi praveśaṃ gamyatāṃ drutam ||
children.translated_text: So I shall not grant you entrance here; go quickly.'
<s>Vīraka</s> said:
Having spoken in this way, the daughter of the mountain, my affectionate and loving mother, said,
'No other woman obtains entrance, O lotus-eyed one.'

children.text: ityuktā tu tadā devī cintayāmāsa cetasā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the goddess then reflected in her mind:

children.text: na sā nārīti daityo'sau vāyurme yāmabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: 'That was not a woman; it was the very daitya of whom <s>Vāyu</s> spoke to me.
<s>Vīraka</s> was cursed by me in vain, overcome by anger.
A wrong deed is often done by fools when they are driven by anger.

children.text: krodhena naśyate kīrtiḥ krodho hanti sthirāṃ śriyam
children.translated_text: Through anger fame is destroyed; anger destroys stable prosperity.
Without discerning the true facts, I have cursed my son.
For those whose understanding has reversed the matter, the rise of misfortune is easy.'
Having reflected thus, <s>Śailajā</s> spoke these words to <s>Vīraka</s>,
with a lotus-bright face transformed by modesty and embarrassment.
The goddess said:

children.text: ahaṃ vīraka te mātā mā te'stu manaso bhramaḥ
children.translated_text: I am your mother, O <s>Vīraka</s>; let there be no confusion in your mind.
I am the beloved of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the daughter of the snow mountain.

children.text: mama gātracchavibhrāntyā mā śaṅkāṃ putra bhāvaya
children.translated_text: Do not, my son, hold suspicion because of the change in the color of my limbs.
This fair complexion of mine was given by the pleased lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>.
You were cursed by me when I did not know the event contrived by the daitya,

children.text: jñātvā nārīpraveśaṃ tu śaṃkare rahasi sthite ||
children.translated_text: after I had learned of a woman's entrance while <s>Śaṃkara</s> was staying in private.

children.text: na nivartayituṃ śakyaḥ śāpaḥ kiṃ tu bravīmi te
children.translated_text: The curse cannot be turned back; but I tell you this:
you will soon return from human birth, fulfilled in your desire.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: śirasā tu tato vandya mātaraṃ pūrṇamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, bowing with his head to his mother, his mind made whole,
he spoke to the daughter of the Snow Mountain, whose radiance was like the risen full moon.
<s>Vīraka</s> said:
O daughter of the mountain, whose fierce nails are marked by the clustered brilliance of jewels meeting on the crowns of gods and asuras who bow,
O <s>Nagasutā</s>, affectionate to those who seek refuge, I bow to you, destroyer of the distress of those who bow.
O you whose shoulders are encircled by the disk of the sun, whose radiance is that of broad golden mountains,
adorned with a quiver of poisonous serpents, daughter of the mountain, I take refuge in you.

children.text: jagati kaḥ praṇatābhimataṃ dadau jhaṭiti siddhanute bhavatī yathā
children.translated_text: Who in the world gives the desired object of those who bow as quickly as you, O praised by siddhas?

children.text: jagati kāṃ ca na vāñchati śaṃkaro bhuvanadhṛttanaye bhavatīṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: And whom in the world does <s>Śaṃkara</s> desire, O daughter of the supporter of worlds, as he desires you?
In the sphere of <s>Maheśvara</s>, unconquerable, fashioned by pure yoga, equal to your own body,
you were first praised by the best of the gods when you had split apart the host of <s>Andhaka</s>'s kinsmen.
Mounted on a chariot drawn by a great lion, its neck raised with the burden of masses of white mane,
you crushed great asuras with the mass of your long arms, tawny like flames from the tips of pure spears.
Thus you are called <s>Caṇḍikā</s> by the worlds, O mother, slayer of <s>Śumbha</s> and <s>Niśumbha</s>,
swiftly delighting in granting what is thought of by those who bow and in crushing dānava demons.

children.text: viyati vāyupathe jvalanojjvale'vanitale tava devi ca yadvapuḥ
children.translated_text: In the sky, on the path of wind, in blazing fire, or on the earth, O goddess, whatever form of yours there is,
I bow to that unconquered, unmatched form of yours, O creator of beings, beloved of <s>Bhava</s>.
The oceans with graceful heaving waves, the fires with their radiance, and all that moves and does not move,
and the serpents bearing a thousand hoods will become fear-dispelling for me through your name.
O blessed one, refuge of steadfast devotees, I have gone to the refuge of your feet.
May this whole set of my faculties here be steady, because my aim is the fruit obtained from even a little praise.
Be appeased toward me, O loving mother; homage to you, refuge of the three worlds.

children.text: tvayi mamāstu matiḥ satataṃ śive śaraṇago'smi nato'smi namo'stu te
children.translated_text: May my thought always be fixed on you, O <s>Śivā</s>; I have taken refuge, I bow, homage to you.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: prasannā tu tato devī vīrakasyeti saṃstutā
children.translated_text: Then the goddess, pleased when she had been praised in this way by <s>Vīraka</s>,
the daughter of the mountain entered her husband's auspicious palace.

children.text: atha rudro mahāgaurīṃ gaurīṃ dṛṣṭvā tu sundarīm
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rudra</s>, seeing <s>Gaurī</s>, the very fair and beautiful <s>Gaurī</s>,
whose form bewildered the mind and whose gait was like that of a rutting elephant-cow,
slender, with a full-moon face, broad hips and heavy breasts,
thin in the middle and showering the nectar of undiminished beauty,
adorned in front with every ornament and moving with slow intoxication,

children.text: sakāmaḥ śaṅkito dīno raudro vīro bhayānakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became desirous, doubtful, pitiable, fierce, heroic, and terrifying;
<s>Hara</s> also became, in some measure, tender, comic, and disgusted.
Wishing to kill, in accordance with the god's word, he assumed a <s>Bhairava</s> body.

children.text: sā cāpi bhairavī jātā devasya pratirūpiṇī
children.translated_text: She too became <s>Bhairavī</s>, taking a form corresponding to the god.
The mountain-dweller saw thousands of her forms.
When the thousand forms had been absorbed and the form of <s>Tārā</s> was displayed,
then <s>Śaṃkara</s> became free from doubt because of <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā jaganmayīṃ tāṃ tu rarāma suratapriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing her as consisting of the whole universe, the lover of lovemaking delighted in her,
having again obtained <s>Himātmajā</s>, his wife who had been yearning in separation.
For the span of a thousand years, while the two remained in private,
their continuous amorous play went on, joined with manifold acts and positions.
Standing at the door, <s>Vīraka</s> dismissed the gods who desired to see <s>Hara</s>,
respectfully sending them back to their own homes.
'There is no opportunity here, O gods; <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> is with the goddess,
sporting in seclusion.' Thus told, they went back as they had come.
But when a thousand years had passed, the gods, urgent in mind,
impelled <s>Jvalana</s> to learn <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s activity.
<s>Hutāśana</s>, in the form of a parrot, entered through a lattice-opening.

children.text: dadṛśe śayane śarvaṃ rataṃ girijayā saha ||
children.translated_text: He saw <s>Śarva</s> on the bed, engaged in love with <s>Girijā</s>.

children.text: dadṛśe taṃ ca deveśo hutāśaṃ śukarūpiṇam
children.translated_text: And the lord of gods saw that <s>Hutāśa</s>, in the form of a parrot.
<s>Mahādeva</s>, somewhat filled with anger, said to him:
<s>Śarva</s> said:
Half of my seed has been deposited in the goddess, O one with a parrot body.
Since she has stopped out of modesty, you must drink the other half, O <s>Pāvaka</s>.
Because the obstruction was caused by you, therefore it properly falls upon you.
Thus addressed, <s>Vahni</s>, with joined palms, drank the deposited seed.
By it he filled those gods, and, as their respective bodies split apart,

children.text: vipāṭya jaṭharaṃ teṣāṃ vīryaṃ māheśvaraṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the seed of <s>Maheśvara</s> then burst forth from their bellies.
When it had come out, like molten gold, it spread through <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s hermitage.
There a great lake arose, spotless and many yojanas wide.
It was filled with blossoming golden lotuses and resounded with many kinds of birds.
Then the goddess, hearing of that great body of water with golden trees,
went there, filled with curiosity, to that lake with golden lotuses.
There, after sporting in the water and making a crest-ornament from its lotuses,
the goddess sat on its bank with her companions.
Wishing to drink that water, sweet, clear, and lotus-filled,
she saw the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, bathed and resembling six suns in splendor.
Taking that water on a lotus leaf, they came before her.
With delight she said, "I see water resting on a lotus leaf."
Then all the <s>Kṛttikās</s> said to the daughter of the snow mountain:
The <s>Kṛttikās</s> said:

children.text: dāsyāmo yadi te garbhaḥ sambhūto yo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: We shall give it, if the child who will be born from this pregnancy
will also be our son and will bear our name.
