Let him be famous in all the worlds, O fair-faced one.
Thus addressed, <s>Girijā</s> said, "How could one born from my body,
complete with all his limbs, become a son for you?"
Then the <s>Kṛttikās</s> said to her, "We shall surely arrange for him
excellent chief limbs, if this is to be so."
When they had spoken, the daughter of the mountain said, "Let it be so, O blameless ones."
Then they, filled with joy, gave her the water resting on the lotus leaf.

children.text: tasyai dadustayā cāpi tatpītaṃ kramaśo jalam
children.translated_text: She too drank that water gradually when it was given by them.
When that water had been drunk, then in that lake
a wondrous child arose, splitting open the goddess's right flank.
He came forth, illuminating all the worlds.
He had the form of the sun's radiance and the luster of shining gold.
He was six-faced, holding a spotless, uplifted spear and trident.
He blazed, golden in hue, to slay the contemptible daityas.
For this divine reason he also became <s>Kumāra</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: vāmaṃ vidārya niṣkrāntaḥ suto devyāḥ punaḥ śiśuḥ
children.translated_text: Again, the goddess's son, a child, came out after splitting open her left side.
Because of the spilling from <s>Skanda</s>, from <s>Vahni</s>'s mouth, and from the seed, he was fair-faced and a slayer of enemies.
Because of the union with the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, and especially through the branches,
the names connected with branches were declared, extending over his six faces.
For that reason he is known in the worlds as <s>Viśākha</s>, the six-faced one.
He is renowned as <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, six-faced, and <s>Kārttikeya</s>.
On the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight of <s>Caitra</s>, the two mighty ones,
sunlike, were born in the broad reed forest.
On the fifth day of the bright fortnight of that same <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Pākaśāsana</s>
made the two boys one, thinking it would be for the welfare of the immortals.
Then, on the sixth day of that same fortnight, lord <s>Guha</s> was consecrated
by all the hosts of immortals, with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and <s>Bhāskara</s>.
With auspicious perfumes, garlands, incense, and also toys,
with umbrellas, masses of yak-tail fans, ornaments, and unguents,
the lord <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> was duly consecrated according to rule.
<s>Śakra</s> gave him his daughter, renowned as <s>Devasenā</s>.
For a wife for the god of gods he gave her, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> gave him his weapon.
The lord of wealth gave him ten lakhs of yakṣas.
<s>Hutāśana</s> gave him fiery energy, and <s>Vāyu</s> gave him a mount.
<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> gave him as a toy a rooster able to take any desired form.
Thus all those gods, with joyful minds,
gave an unsurpassed retinue to <s>Skanda</s>, who had the splendor of the sun.
Standing on their knees upon the earth, the hosts of gods praised him,
the boon-giving, chief <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>, with this hymn.
The gods said:

children.text: namaḥ kumārāya mahāprabhāya skandāya ca skanditadānavāya
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Kumāra</s> of great radiance, and to <s>Skanda</s>, who has made the dānavas fall.

children.text: navārkavidyuddyutaye namo'stu te namo'stu te ṣaṇmukha kāmarūpa ||
children.translated_text: Homage to you, whose splendor is like a new sun and lightning; homage to you, O six-faced one of form at will.
Homage to you, adorned with many ornaments, the lord; homage to you who tears apart the dānavas in battle.

children.text: namo'stu te'rkapratimaprabhāya namo'stu guhyāya guhāya tubhyam ||
children.translated_text: Homage to you, whose radiance is like the sun; homage to you, the hidden one, <s>Guha</s>.

children.text: namo'stu trailokyabhayāpahāya namo'stu te bāla kṛpāparāya
children.translated_text: Homage to you who remove the fear of the three worlds; homage to you, O child, who are intent on compassion.
Homage to you of broad, stainless eyes; homage to <s>Viśākha</s>, the great-vowed one.

children.text: namo namaste 'stu manoharāya namo namaste'stu raṇotkaṭāya
children.translated_text: Repeated homage to the charming one; repeated homage to the one fierce in battle.
Homage to the one whose peacock mount shines brightly; homage to you who wear armlets.

children.text: namo dhṛtodagrapatākine namaste namaḥ prabhāvapraṇatāya te'stu
children.translated_text: Homage to you who hold a lofty banner; homage, homage to you before whom the powerful bow down.

children.text: namaste namaste varavīryaśāline kṛpāparo no bhava bhavyamūrte ||
children.translated_text: Homage, homage to you, endowed with excellent valor; be compassionate to us, O auspicious form.

children.text: kriyāparā yajñapatiṃ ca stutvā vinemurevaṃ tvamarādhipādyāḥ
children.translated_text: Intent on ritual action, after praising the lord of sacrifice in this way, the chiefs of the immortals bowed down.

children.text: evaṃ tadā ṣaḍvadanastu sendrānuvāca tuṣṭaśca guhastatastān
children.translated_text: Then, pleased, the six-faced <s>Guha</s> looked at the lords of the gods, including <s>Indra</s>, and addressed them.
Looking at the divine lords with stainless eyes, he said, 'I shall slay the enemies; be free from distress.'
<s>Kumāra</s> said:

children.text: kaṃ vaḥ kāmaṃ prayacchāmi devatā brūta nirvṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: What wish shall I grant you, O deities? Speak, and be content.

children.text: yadyapyasādhyaṃ hṛdyaṃ vo hṛdaye cintitaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: Even if the dearest thing in your hearts, the supreme thing contemplated there, is difficult to accomplish.
Thus addressed by him, the gods, with bowed heads, spoke
all of them to the great-souled <s>Guha</s>, their minds fixed on him.
There is a lord of daityas named <s>Tāraka</s>, destroyer of all the families of the immortals;
powerful, hard to conquer, wicked, ill-conducted, and exceedingly wrathful.
Slay him alone. This is the beloved aim of ours, the remover of our fear.
Thus addressed, he said, 'So be it,' and, with all the immortals following his steps,
the lord of the worlds went forth, praised by the lords of the immortals.
And for the slaying of <s>Tāraka</s>, who was indeed a thorn to the world,
<s>Śakra</s>, having obtained a protector, then sent
a messenger to the lion among dānavas, one who spoke harsh words.
He went and, fearless and terrible to behold, spoke to the daitya.
The messenger said:
<s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, O banner of the daityas, lord of heaven, says this to you.
O <s>Tārakāsura</s>, having heard it, exert yourself with whatever strength you wish.
O dānava, whatever guilt you have incurred by crushing the world,
for that I am your chastiser today; I am king in the three worlds.
Hearing this speech of the messenger, his eyes reddened with anger,
the wicked-souled one, whose prosperity was almost ruined, spoke to the messenger.
<s>Tāraka</s> said:

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ te pauruṣaṃ śakra raṇeṣu śataśo mayā
children.translated_text: I have seen your valor, O <s>Śakra</s>, hundreds of times in battles.

children.text: nistrapatvānna te lajjā vidyate śakra durmate ||
children.translated_text: Because you are shameless, no shame exists in you, O evil-minded <s>Śakra</s>.
When this had been said and the messenger had gone, the dānava reflected:
<s>Śakra</s> could not rightly speak in this way unless he had obtained support.
That conquered <s>Śakra</s> does not, without cause, become one who relies upon a refuge.
And he, of wicked conduct, saw evil portents.
There was a rain of dust and a fall of blood from the sky onto the surface of the earth,
trembling of arms and eyes, dryness of mouth, and bewilderment of mind.
He observed the fading of the lotus-faces of his own beloved women,
and he saw fierce, ominous creatures, signs of evil.
Without thinking of that, the son of <s>Diti</s> at once laid aside his worry for a moment,
until he saw it roaring with the ringing clangor of bells on masses of elephants,
and likewise tawny with the dust of the ground crushed by troops of horses,
shining with rows of banners raised high on restless chariots,
with aerial cars of wondrous shape and yak-tail fans of the moving immortals,
adorned with ornaments and resounding with the songs of kinnaras,
bearing clusters of blossoming flowers from many kinds of trees,
furnished with unsheathed weapons and displaying spotless armor,
filled with the proclaimed sound of bards' praises and resounding with many instruments,
the army of the dwellers in heaven, while the daitya stood in his palace.
Then, with his mind somewhat agitated, he considered:

children.text: apūrvaḥ ko bhavedyoddhā yo mayā na vinirjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who might this unprecedented warrior be, one who has not been conquered by me?
Then the daitya, troubled by anxiety, heard harsh words,
this heart-rending proclamation cried out by siddhas and bards.
Now the song:
Victory, O tawny one with the radiance of incomparable power, fierce in the battle-fury of your staff-like arms;
O moon that makes the water-lily grove of the gods' faces bloom, O <s>Kumāra</s>, victory; O submarine fire to the great ocean of the daitya race.
O six-faced one, whose mount is the sweet-calling peacock, whose foot-nail shoots are struck by the tips of the gods' crowns,
victory, O lovely one with graceful crest and locks, charming as a fresh spotless lotus petal, unbearable forest fire to the daitya lineage.

children.text: jaya viśākha vibho jaya sakalalokatāraka jaya devasenānāyaka
children.translated_text: Victory, O <s>Viśākha</s>, lord; victory, savior of all worlds; victory, leader of the army of the gods.

children.text: skanda jaya gaurīnandana ghaṇṭāpriya priya viśākha vibho dhṛtapatākaprakīrṇapaṭala
children.translated_text: Victory, O <s>Skanda</s>, son of <s>Gaurī</s>, lover of bells, beloved <s>Viśākha</s>, lord, with a spread mass of held banners,
adorned with gold and shining with the splendor of the blazing sun.

children.text: jaya janitasaṃbhrama līlālūnākhilārāte jaya sakalalokatāraka ditijāsuravaratārakāntaka
children.translated_text: Victory, creator of terror, who in sport has cut down all enemies; victory, savior of all worlds, ender of <s>Tāraka</s>, best of daitya-asuras.

children.text: skanda jaya bāla saptavāsara jaya bhuvanāvaliśokavināśana ||
children.translated_text: Victory, O <s>Skanda</s>, O child of seven days; victory, destroyer of the grief of the rows of worlds.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Hearing all this proclaimed by the bards of the gods, <s>Tāraka</s>
remembered the word of <s>Brahmā</s>, that death from a child had now arrived.
Remembering it, with all his limbs wet with sweat, on foot and without attendants,
he quickly went out from his palace with a mind seized by grief.
The daityas, headed by <s>Kālanemi</s>, their minds whirled by agitation,
then, in their respective armies, with minds startled by haste,
cried, 'Warriors, run! Take up your arms! Yoke the army!'
Seeing <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Tāraka</s>, dreadful in form, addressed him:
Why, child, do you wish to fight? Play at the game of balls.
You have not seen the dānavas, terrifying in the clash of battle.
Or, because of childhood, your understanding is so short-sighted.
<s>Kumāra</s> too, standing before him and gladdening the gods, addressed him:
Listen, <s>Tāraka</s>; the point of your doctrine is now being explained.
In battle, fearless warriors do not discern their aims by treatises.
Do not despise my childhood; a child may be the serpent of Time.
The young sun is hard to look upon; likewise I am a child hard to conquer.

children.text: alpākṣaro na mantraḥ kiṃ susphuro daitya dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Is a mantra nothing because it has few syllables? O daitya, it is seen to be very potent.
When <s>Kumāra</s> had spoken thus, the daitya hurled a club.
Then <s>Kumāra</s> repelled it with the vajra of unfailing splendor.
Then the lord of the daityas hurled an iron bhindipāla-dart.
<s>Kārtikeya</s>, slayer of the enemies of the immortals, caught that in his hand.
The six-faced one released against the daitya a mace of tremendous sound.
Struck by it, the daitya then trembled like the king of mountains.

children.text: mene ca durjayaṃ daityastadā ṣaḍvadanaṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: Then the daitya considered the six-faced one unconquerable in battle.

children.text: cintayāmāsa buddhyā vai prāptaḥ kālo na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He thought in his mind, 'The time has come; there is no doubt.'
Seeing him enraged, those headed by <s>Kālanemi</s>
all the daitya lords struck <s>Kumāra</s>, terrible in battle.
But the greatly radiant one was untouched by those blows, which brought only futile exertion.
The daitya lords, fierce in battle, again with prāsa-javelins and arrows
struck <s>Kumāra</s> and the immortals, those powerful thorns of the gods.
Yet no pain arose for <s>Kumāra</s>, though he had been struck by the daityas' missiles.
The battle with the dānavas had become life-ending for the gods.
Seeing the gods oppressed, <s>Kumāra</s> entered into wrath.
Then with missiles he checked the army of the dānavas.
Then, struck by those irresistible weapons, the thorns of the gods
all, headed by <s>Kālanemi</s>, turned their faces away from battle.
When the daityas had fled and had been slain on every side,
then the enraged great daitya <s>Tāraka</s>, leader of the asuras,
grasped a divine mace adorned with a golden network.
Wearing armlets of refined gold, he struck <s>Kumāra</s> with the mace.
And with arrows feathered with peacock plumes he turned the gods away.
Likewise, with other great broad-headed arrows he pierced the peacock, <s>Guha</s>'s vehicle.
The enraged <s>Tāraka</s>, leader of the asuras, did this amid the army.
Seeing the gods turned away and his own mount shedding blood,
the six-faced one seized in battle a spotless śakti-spear adorned with gold.
With his arm made beautiful by a golden armlet,
then swift <s>Mahāsena</s> addressed <s>Tāraka</s>, lord of the dānavas:
'Stand, stand, very foolish one; look upon the world of the living.

children.text: hato'syadya mayā śaktyā smara śastraṃ suśikṣitam ||
children.translated_text: Today you are slain by me with the śakti-spear; remember your well-trained weapon.'

children.text: ityuktvā ca tataḥ śaktiṃ mumoca ditijaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he then released the śakti-spear against the son of <s>Diti</s>.
That spear, cast from <s>Kumāra</s>'s arm, followed by the ringing of his armlet,
split the daitya's heart, hard as a vajra and a lordly mountain.

children.text: gatāsuḥ sa papātorvyāṃ pralaye bhūdharo yathā
children.translated_text: Lifeless, he fell to the earth like a mountain at the dissolution of the world.
His crown and turban were scattered, and all his ornaments had slipped loose.
When that daitya had been slain, amid the great festival of the thirty gods,

children.text: nābhūt kaścit tadā duḥkhī narakeṣvapi pāpakṛt ||
children.translated_text: there was then no one sorrowful, even among sinful doers in the hells.
The gods, praising the six-faced one and sporting with hosts of women,
eagerly went to their own abundant abodes.

children.text: daduścāpi varaṃ sarve devāḥ skandamukhaṃ prati
children.translated_text: And all the gods also granted a boon, turning toward <s>Skanda</s>,
pleased, having obtained all their desires, together with siddhas rich in austerity.
The gods said:
'A high-minded mortal who reads the story connected with <s>Skanda</s>,
or hears it, or causes it to be heard, that man shall become famous.
He shall be long-lived, fortunate, prosperous, radiant, and auspicious to behold,
fearless of beings and free from every suffering.

children.text: saṃdhyāmupāsya yaḥ pūrvāṃ skandasya caritaṃ paṭhet
children.translated_text: Whoever, having observed the morning twilight worship, reads <s>Skanda</s>'s deed,
freed from all sins, he shall become a lord of great wealth.
For children afflicted by disease and for those who attend at the king's gate,
that supreme, divine account always grants every desire.
And at the wasting away of the body, a man attains union with the six-faced one.'
The sages said:
'Now we wish to hear of the killing of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>,
the greatness of <s>Narasiṃha</s>, and likewise the destruction of sins.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Formerly, in the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>, O brahmins, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, the lord,
the primal person among the daityas, performed a great austerity.
For ten thousand years and ten hundred years
he dwelt in water, holding a vow of bathing and silence.

children.text: tataḥ śamadamābhyāṃ ca brahmacaryeṇa caiva hi
children.translated_text: Then, through tranquility and self-restraint, and indeed through celibacy,
<s>Brahmā</s> became pleased by his austerity and discipline.
Then the blessed <s>Svayambhū</s> himself came there
in a shining, sun-colored aerial car yoked with swans,
with the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, and other deities,
with the <s>Rudras</s> and <s>Viśvasahāyas</s>, and with yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pannagas,

children.text: digbhiś caiva vidigbhiś ca nadībhiḥ sāgaraistathā
children.translated_text: with the quarters and intermediate quarters, and also with rivers and oceans,
with lunar mansions, muhūrtas, sky-goers, and great planets,
with the gods and brahmarṣis, together with siddhas and the seven seers,
with righteous royal seers and hosts of gandharvas and apsarases.
The glorious teacher of the moving and unmoving world, surrounded by all the dwellers in heaven,
<s>Brahmā</s>, best of the knowers of brahman, spoke this word to the daitya:
'I am pleased with you, my devotee, by this austerity, good-vowed one.

children.text: varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yatheṣṭaṃ kāmamāpnuhi ||
children.translated_text: Choose a boon; good fortune to you. Obtain whatever wish you desire.'
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> said:
'May neither gods, asuras, gandharvas, nor yakṣas, serpents, or rākṣasas,

children.text: na mānuṣāḥ piśācā vā hanyurmāṃ devasattama ||
children.translated_text: nor humans or piśācas kill me, O best of gods.

children.text: ṛṣayo vā na māṃ śāpaiḥ śapeyuḥ prapitāmaha
children.translated_text: Nor may seers curse me with curses, O great-grandfather.

children.text: yadi me bhagavānprīto vara eṣa vṛto mayā ||
children.translated_text: If the blessed lord is pleased with me, this is the boon chosen by me.'

children.text: na cāstreṇa na śastreṇa giriṇā pādapena ca
children.translated_text: Not by missile, not by weapon, not by a mountain or by a tree,

children.text: na śuṣkeṇa na cārdreṇa na divā na niśātha vā ||
children.translated_text: not by a dry thing, not by a wet thing, not by day nor indeed by night.
May I myself become the sun, the moon, the wind, and the sacrificial fire,

children.text: salilaṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca nakṣatrāṇi diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: and the waters, the midspace, the stars, and the ten directions.

children.text: ahaṃ krodhaśca kāmaśca varuṇo vāsavo yamaḥ
children.translated_text: I shall be anger and desire, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, and <s>Yama</s>,
the giver of wealth, the overseer of wealth, a <s>Yakṣa</s>, and lord of the <s>Kiṃpuruṣas</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
These wondrous divine boons, dear one, have been granted to you by me.

children.text: sarvānkāmānsadā vatsa prāpsyasi tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: My child, you will always obtain all your desires; there is no doubt.
Having spoken thus, the blessed one went away through the sky itself,
to the <s>Vairāja</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>'s abode, attended by hosts of brahmarṣis.

children.text: tato devāśca nāgāśca gandharvā ṛṣibhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Then the gods, nāgas, gandharvas, together with the sages,
having heard of the granting of the boon, approached the grandsire.
Because of the granting of the boon, blessed lord, that asura will kill us.
Therefore be gracious at once, blessed lord; let some death for him too be considered.
Blessed lord, you are the first maker of all beings, the self-existent master,
the creator of oblations to gods and ancestors, the wise one whose nature is unmanifest.
Hearing words meant for the welfare of all worlds, the god <s>Prajāpati</s>
reassured the gods with waters of speech that were very cooling.
Gods, the fruit of his asceticism must necessarily be obtained by him;
at the end of his ascetic power, the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> will accomplish his death.
Having heard this word of the lotus-born one, all the wise gods
departed joyfully to their own divine stations.

children.text: labdhamātre vare cātha sarvāḥ so'bādhata prajāḥ
children.translated_text: But as soon as he had obtained the boon, he oppressed all creatures,
the daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, made arrogant by the granting of the boon.
In hermitages the dānava assailed highly blessed sages of praiseworthy vows,
devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), self-controlled and restrained.
After defeating the gods who dwell in the three worlds, the great asura,
bringing the three worlds under his power, dwelt in heaven.
Then, swollen with the pride of the boon and driven by the law of time,
the daitya made the daityas fit for sacrifice and the gods unfit for sacrifice.
Then the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśve Devas</s>, and likewise the <s>Vasus</s>,
the hosts of gods with <s>Indra</s>, the yakṣas, siddhas, brahmins, and great sages,
approached mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the refuge and the one fit to be sought as refuge,
the god of gods, consisting of sacrifice, eternal <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
The gods said:
O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, greatly blessed one, the gods have come to you for refuge.
Save us; slay the lord of daityas, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, O master.

children.text: tvaṃ hi naḥ paramo dhātā tvaṃ hi naḥ paramo guruḥ
children.translated_text: For you are our supreme sustainer; you are our supreme teacher.

children.text: tvaṃ hi naḥ paramo devo brahmādīnāṃ surottama ||
children.translated_text: You are our supreme god, best of gods, above <s>Brahmā</s> and the others.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> said:
Put fear aside, immortals; I grant you freedom from fear.
And, gods, return to heaven without delay.
Here I am: I will kill that lord of dānavas, proud from the granting of the boon,
the lord of daityas, together with his followers, invulnerable to the lords of the immortals.
Having spoken thus, the blessed lord dismissed the rulers of the thirty gods,
and the master resolved upon the death of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
The great-armed one quickly took <s>Oṃkāra</s> as an aid,
and then the blessed, imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>, assisted by <s>Oṃkāra</s>,
<s>Hari</s>, the lord, went to the dwelling of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
In splendor he had the form of the sun, and in beauty he was like another moon.
Having made half his body that of a man and half his body that of a lion,
in a <s>Nārasiṃha</s> form he touched hand with hand.
Then he saw the broad, divine, lovely, delightful,
bright assembly hall of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, endowed with every desire.
It extended a hundred yojanas in breadth and a hundred and a half in length,
moving through the air at will and five yojanas wide.
Free from old age, sorrow, and weariness, unmoving, auspicious, and pleasant,
lovely with mansions and palaces, it blazed as if with splendor.
It had water within and had been fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
furnished with trees made of divine jewels, bearing fruits and flowers.
With canopies blue, yellow, white, dark, black, and red,
and also with shrubs bearing hundreds of clusters of blossoms,
it appeared like a mass of white clouds, as though floating.
It was radiant, shining, and delightful with divine fragrance.

children.text: susukhā na ca duḥkhā sā na śītā na ca gharmadā
children.translated_text: It was very pleasant and not painful, neither cold nor giving heat;

children.text: na kṣutpipāse glāniṃ vā prāpya tāṃ prāpnuvanti te ||
children.translated_text: those who reached it did not experience hunger, thirst, or fatigue.
It was adorned with various forms, wondrous and exceedingly brilliant,

children.text: stambhairna vibhṛtā sā vai śāśvatī cākṣapā sadā ||
children.translated_text: and was not supported by pillars; it was eternal and always without night.

children.text: ati candraṃ ca sūryaṃ ca śikhinaṃ ca svayaṃprabhā
children.translated_text: Beyond the moon, the sun, and fire, it was self-luminous,
and, standing on the back of heaven, it shone as if illuminating the sun.

children.text: sarve ca kāmāḥ pracurā ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ
children.translated_text: All desires were abundant there, both divine and human,
and there was endless food to be chewed and eaten, rich with flavor and plentiful.
Here were garlands of holy fragrance and trees always bearing flowers and fruit;

children.text: uṣṇe śītāni toyāni śīte coṣṇāni santi ca ||
children.translated_text: there was cool water in the heat and warm water in the cold.
Great-branched trees had flowering tips and bore coral-red sprouts,
covered with spreading creepers, beside rivers and lakes.
There the mighty lord, the lion among beasts, saw many kinds of trees,

children.text: gandhavanti ca puṣpāṇi rasavanti phalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and fragrant flowers and flavorful fruits.

children.text: nātiśītāni noṣṇāni tatra tatra sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: And here and there were lakes that were neither too cold nor hot.
In his hall that lord saw all the sacred bathing places.
They were covered with blue lotuses, white lotuses, and fragrant hundred-petalled lotuses,
and also with red and blue water-lilies and with night-lotuses.
With lovely geese, dhārtarāṣṭra birds, and most pleasant royal swans,
with kāraṇḍavas, cakravākas, cranes, and kuraras as well,
with pure birds like crystal and with pale wings,
they were sung over by many swans and resounded with cranes.
There he saw fragrant, auspicious creepers bearing full clusters of blossoms,
on the mountain peaks, bearing many kinds of flowers.
Ketakas, aśokas, saralas, puṃnāgas, tilakas, and arjunas,

children.text: cūtā nīpāḥ prasthapuṣpāḥ kadambā bakulā dhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: mangoes, nīpas, prasthapuṣpas, kadambas, bakulas, and dhavas,
priyaṅgus, pāṭalas, vṛkṣas, śālmalis, and haridrakas,
sālas, tālas, tamālas, and charming campakas,
and likewise other blossoming trees shone in the hall.
Coral trees and other trees had a brilliance like blazing fire.
They had trunks and beautiful branches, rising as high as many palm trees,
and there were many wonderful trees, dark as añjana and colored like aśoka.
Varuṇas, vatsanābhas, jackfruit trees together with sandal trees,
nīpas, sumanases, nimbs, aśvatthas, and tindukas,
pārijātas, lodhras, mallikās, and bhadradārus,
āmalakīs, jambūs, lakucas, and śailavālukas,
date-palms and coconuts, harītakīs and vibhītakas,
kālīyakas, drukālas, hiṅgus, and pāriyātrakas,
mandāras, kundas, laktās, pataṅgas, and kuṭajas too,
red kuraṇṭakas, and blue ones together with agaru trees,
kadambas, bhavyas, pomegranates, and citron trees,
saptaparṇas and bilvas, likewise covered with bees,
aśokas and tamālas, surrounded by many kinds of shrubs and creepers,
madhūkas, saptaparṇas, and many milk-sapped trees,
and creepers of various forms, furnished with leaves, flowers, and fruits:

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavastatra kānanajā drumāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these and many other forest-born trees were there.
Endowed with many kinds of flowers and fruits, they shone on every side.
Cakoras, śatapatras, intoxicated cuckoos, and śārikās were there.
The great trees, flowering and with flowering tips, seemed to fly down together.
Birds red, yellow, and tawny were there on the tops of the trees.
Joyful jīvajīvaka birds looked at one another.
In that assembly hall the lord of daityas, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, then
surrounded by thousands of women and wearing varied ornaments and garments,
with earrings blazing with crests of priceless gems and diamond rays,
was seated on a splendid throne measuring ten nalvas,
divine, like the sun, and spread with a divine coverlet.
There a very pleasant wind blew, carrying divine fragrance.
The daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> sat there with blazing earrings.
Then they attended upon the great daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
The best of the Gandharvas sang songs in a divine strain.
<s>Viśvācī</s>, <s>Sahajanyā</s>, and the renowned <s>Pramlocā</s>,
then the divine <s>Saurabheyī</s>, <s>Samīcī</s>, and <s>Puñjikasthalī</s>,

children.text: miśrakeśī ca rambhā ca citralekhā śucismitā
children.translated_text: <s>Miśrakeśī</s>, <s>Rambhā</s>, <s>Citralekhā</s> of pure smile,

children.text: cārukeśī ghṛtācī ca menakā corvaśī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Cārukeśī</s>, <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, <s>Menakā</s>, and also <s>Urvaśī</s>:
these and thousands of others, skilled in dance and song,
attended upon the king, the lord <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
All the sons of <s>Diti</s>, having obtained boons, worshipfully served
the mighty-armed lord <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, seated there.
By hundreds and then by thousands they served him, whose deeds were without equal.
There were <s>Bali</s>, <s>Virocana</s>, <s>Naraka</s>, son of the Earth,
<s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Vipracitti</s>, and <s>Gaviṣṭha</s>, the great asura,
<s>Surahantā</s>, <s>Sunāmā</s>, <s>Pramati</s>, and excellent <s>Sumati</s>,
<s>Ghaṭodara</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, <s>Krathana</s>, and <s>Piṭhara</s>,
<s>Viśvarūpa</s>, <s>Surūpa</s>, <s>Svabala</s>, and <s>Mahābala</s>,
<s>Daśagrīva</s>, <s>Vālī</s>, and <s>Meghavāsā</s>, the great asura,
<s>Ghaṭāsya</s>, <s>Akampana</s>, <s>Prajana</s>, and <s>Indratāpana</s>.
Those hosts of daityas and dānavas all had blazing earrings.
All wore garlands, all were eloquent, and all always observed vows.
All had obtained boons, all were heroes, and all were free from death.

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavo hiraṇyakaśipuṃ prabhum ||
children.translated_text: These and many others attended upon the lord <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>,
the great-souled one, all having divine accoutrements.
With aerial cars of various shapes, shining as if with fires,
all with bodies like <s>Mahendra</s>'s and with arms bearing varied armlets,
the adorned sons of <s>Diti</s> attended upon him on every side.
In that divine assembly hall the asuras, like mountains,
all had golden bodies and splendor equal to the sun.

children.text: na śrutaṃ naiva dṛṣṭaṃ hi hiraṇyakaśiporyathā
children.translated_text: Never had anything been heard or seen like <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>'s
sovereign power, the power of that great-souled lion among daityas.
On a platform variegated with gold and silver, with splendid streets adorned by gems,
in the hall beautified by jewel windows made by the gods, the lord of beasts saw him.
The lord of beasts saw the son of <s>Diti</s>, his body adorned with spotless golden necklaces,
blazing with the great splendor of the sun and served by hundreds of thousands of daityas.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then, seeing the great-souled one come as if he were the wheel of Time,
hidden in the form of <s>Narasiṃha</s>, like fire covered with ashes,
the valiant son of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, named <s>Prahlāda</s>,
with divine sight saw the lion, the god, who had arrived.
Seeing him, resembling a mountain of gold and assuming an unprecedented body,
all the dānavas were astonished, and so was that <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
<s>Prahlāda</s> said:
O mighty-armed great king, first source of the daityas,

children.text: na śrutaṃ na ca no dṛṣṭaṃ nārasiṃhamidaṃ vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Narasiṃha</s> body has not been heard of by us, nor seen.
Divine, arisen from the unmanifest: what is this form that has come?
It is dreadful and causes the end of daityas; my mind is as if in doubt.

children.text: asya devāḥ śarīrasthāḥ sāgarāḥ saritaśca yāḥ
children.translated_text: The gods are stationed in his body, and the oceans and rivers too,
<s>Himavat</s> and <s>Pāriyātra</s>, and whatever other family-mountains there are.
The moon with the constellations, together with the Ādityas and Vasus,
<s>Dhanada</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of <s>Śacī</s>,
the Maruts, the divine gandharvas, and the seers rich in austerity,
nāgas, yakṣas, piśācas, and rākṣasas of terrible valor,
the god <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Paśupati</s>: surely they move, standing in his forehead.

children.text: sthāvarāṇi ca sarvāṇi jaṅgamāni tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: So too all things fixed and all things moving.
You too, together with us, surrounded by all the hosts of daityas,
and likewise your assembly, crowded with hundreds of aerial cars,
the whole threefold world, O king, and the eternal laws of the worlds,
are seen in this <s>Narasiṃha</s>, and likewise this entire universe.
Here too are <s>Prajāpati</s>, the great-souled <s>Manu</s>, the planets, conjunctions, and trees,

children.text: utpātakālaśca dhṛtirmatiśca ratiśca satyaṃ ca tapo damaśca ||
children.translated_text: the time of portents, firmness, understanding, delight, truth, austerity, and self-restraint.

children.text: sanatkumāraśca mahānubhāvo viśve ca devā ṛṣayaśca sarve
children.translated_text: <s>Sanatkumāra</s> of great power is here, and the Viśve Devas and all the seers,

children.text: krodhaśca kāmaśca tathaiva harṣo dharmaśca mohaḥ pitaraśca sarve ||
children.translated_text: anger, desire, joy as well, <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), delusion, and all the ancestors.
Hearing <s>Prahlāda</s>'s words, lord <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>,
the lord of hosts, spoke to all the dānavas and to his companies:
Seize this lord of beasts, who has assumed an unprecedented body;
or, if there is any doubt, let the forest-roamer be killed.
All those hosts of dānavas, surrounding the lion of terrible valor,
joyfully tried to frighten him by their might.
Then, letting loose a lion's roar, mighty <s>Narasiṃha</s>

children.text: babhañja tāṃ sabhāṃ divyāṃ vyāditāsya ivāntakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: broke that divine assembly hall, like Death with gaping mouth.
As the assembly hall was being broken, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> himself,
his eyes confused by anger, hurled weapons at the lion.
First among all weapons, the most terrible staff-mantra,
the dreadful wheel of Time, and also the supreme discus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
the exceedingly fierce weapon of the Grandfather, great burner of the three worlds,
a wondrous thunderbolt, and the two thunderbolts, dry and wet,

children.text: raudraṃ tathograṃ śūlaṃ ca kaṅkālaṃ musalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: the Raudra weapon, the fierce spear, the Kaṅkāla, and the club,
Mohana, Śoṣaṇa, Saṃtāpana, and Vilāpana,
the Vāyavya, Mathana, Kāpāla, and then the Kaiṅkara,
an irresistible spear, and likewise the Krauñca weapon,
the Brahmaśiras weapon, the Soma weapon, and the chilling Śiśira,

children.text: kampanaṃ śātanaṃ caiva tvāṣṭraṃ caiva subhairavam ||
children.translated_text: Kampana, Śātana, and the very terrible Tvāṣṭra,
the Time-mace, Akṣobhya, and Tapana of great power,

children.text: saṃvartanaṃ mohanaṃ ca tathā māyādharaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: Saṃvartana, Mohana, and the supreme Māyādhara,
the beloved Gāndharva weapon, and the jeweled sword <s>Nandaka</s>,
Prasvāpana, Pramathana, and the excellent Vāruṇa weapon,
and the Pāśupata weapon, whose course is unobstructed,
the Hayaśiras weapon and likewise the Brāhma weapon,
the Nārāyaṇa weapon, the Aindra, and the marvelous serpent weapon,
the unconquered Paiśāca weapon, the drying weapon, and the pacifying one,
the mighty Bhāvana, and Prasthāpana and Vikampana,
these divine weapons <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> then
released against <s>Narasiṃha</s>, like oblations into blazing fire.
With flaming weapons the best of asuras covered the lion,
as the sun in the hot season covers <s>Himavat</s> with rays.
That ocean of a daitya army, arisen from the wind of wrath,
flooded him in an instant, as the ocean flooded <s>Maināka</s>.
With lances, nooses, swords, maces, and clubs,
with vajras, thunderbolts, fiery missiles, and great trees,
with mallets, bhindipālas, rocks, mortars, and mountains,
with blazing śataghnīs and with very terrible staffs,
those dānavas, their hands holding nooses, with the speed of <s>Mahendra</s>'s thunderbolt and vajra,
stood on every side with arms and bodies upraised, like three-headed serpent-nooses.
Their limbs were adorned with tangled golden garlands, their bodies bright with the sweep of yellow garments,
their flanks graced by strings and cords of pearls; they shone like haṃsas with broad wings.
And of those whose force was like the wind, fierce with armlets, crowns, and bracelets,
those noble heads shone all around, with splendor like the rays of the morning sun.

children.text: kṣipadbhir ugrair jvalitair mahābalair mahāstrapūgaiḥ susamāvṛto babhau
children.translated_text: Covered completely by the fierce, blazing, mighty masses of great weapons they hurled, he shone forth.
like a mountain whose inner caves are made dark by trees and by clouds that pour down continual rain.
Though struck by those nets of great weapons, together with the daitya hosts of immense strength,
the glorious lord did not tremble in battle; by nature he stood firm in his power, like the immovable <s>Himavān</s>.
Terrified by him, who had the form of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> and a brilliance equal to fire, the sons of <s>Diti</s>
moved about in fear, their limbs shaken, like waves born from ocean-water when stirred by the wind.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Donkeys and donkey-faced beings, makaras and beings with the faces of venomous snakes,
others with the faces of forest beasts, and others fixed in the form of boars' faces,
others with faces like the young sun, and likewise with comet-like faces,
some half-moon-faced and half-mouthed, and likewise with faces blazing like fire,
with the faces of swans and cocks, with gaping mouths, terrifying,
lion-mouthed and licking their lips, and likewise crow-faced and vulture-faced,
double-tongued, crooked-headed, and likewise fixed with meteor-like faces,
others with the faces of great sea-monsters: such dānavas were arrogant with strength.
With showers of arrows on the body of him whose form was like a mountain mass,
they caused no pain in battle to the invulnerable lion.
Then again, in anger, the lords of the dānavas discharged other dreadful missiles
against the lion, as if they were serpents hissing.
Those dreadful dānava arrows, driven on by the lord of the dānavas,
perished in the sky like fireflies against a mountain.
Then the daityas, filled with anger, quickly hurled divine discus-weapons,
blazing on every side, against the lion.
With those discuses flying together here and there, the sky became filled,
shining as at the end of an age with the moon, sun, and planets.
All those discuses, then, by the great-souled lion,
were swallowed up, though uplifted and equal to flames of fire.

children.text: tāni cakrāṇi vadane viśamānāni bhānti vai
children.translated_text: Those discuses, entering his mouth, indeed shone
like the moon, sun, and planets in the cavernous hollows within clouds.
The daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> again sent forth a mighty
terrible, blazing spear, bright as lightning from a polished weapon.
Seeing that radiant spear falling upon him, the lion,
the lord, broke it then merely with a fierce roar of 'huṃ'.
Broken by the lion, that spear shone on the earth,
spark-scattering and blazing, like a great meteor fallen from heaven.
A row of iron arrows that had come near the lion shone
like a garland of blue-lotus petals, brilliant to behold.

children.text: sa garjitvā yathānyāyaṃ vikramya ca yathāsukham
children.translated_text: Having roared properly and advanced as he pleased,
he drove away that army as the wind drives away the tips of grass.
Then the daitya lords, positioned in the sky, released a rain of stones,
with rock-fragments the size of mountains and with mountain peaks of great splendor.
That great stone-rain, falling upon the lion's head,

children.text: diśo daśa vikīrṇā vai khadyotaprakarā iva ||
children.translated_text: was scattered into the ten directions like a mass of fireflies.
Then again the daitya hosts covered the lion, destroyer of enemies,
with floods of stones, as clouds cover a mountain with streams of rain.
But the daitya masses did not move that best of gods,
any more than the ocean, with its terrible force, moves <s>Mandara</s>, best of mountains.
Then, when the stone-rain had been repelled, immediately a rain of water
appeared everywhere, with streams as large as axles.
Streams fell from the sky everywhere with sharp force,
covering the whole firmament on all sides, and the quarters and intermediate quarters as well.

children.text: dhārā divi ca sarvatra vasudhāyāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: There were streams everywhere in heaven and everywhere on the earth,

children.text: na spṛśanti ca tā devaṃ nipatantyo'niśaṃ bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: yet, as they fell unceasingly to the ground, they did not touch the god.
They rained their rain outside him, but they did not rain from above
upon the one who, by māyā, stood in battle in the likeness of a lion.
When the tumultuous stone-rain had been struck down and the water-rain dried up,
that dānava created a māyā driven by fire and wind.
The thousand-eyed <s>Mahendra</s>, of great brilliance, together with the rain-clouds,
extinguished the fire with a great shower of water.

children.text: tasyāṃ pratihatāyāṃ tu māyāyāṃ yudhi dānavaḥ
children.translated_text: When that māyā too had been countered in battle, the dānava
created a fierce-seeming, intense darkness on every side.
When the world was covered with darkness and the daityas had taken up their weapons,
he, surrounded by his own brilliance, shone like the sun.
In battle the dānavas saw his three-crested frown,
standing on his forehead, marked with a trident, like the <s>Gaṅgā</s> that goes by three paths.
Then, when all their māyās had been destroyed, the sons of <s>Diti</s>,
pale-faced, went for refuge to the daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
Then he blazed up with anger, as if burning everything with his splendor;
and when that lord of daityas was enraged, the world became filled with darkness.
<s>Āvaha</s>, <s>Pravaha</s>, <s>Vivaha</s>, and then <s>Udāvaha</s>,
<s>Parāvaha</s> and <s>Saṃvaha</s>, mighty in strength and valor,
and likewise the splendid <s>Parivaha</s>, announcers of danger from portents,
thus the seven winds that move in the sky were disturbed.

children.text: ye grahāḥ sarvalokasya kṣaye prādurbhavanti vai
children.translated_text: Those planets that appear at the destruction of the whole world

children.text: te sarve gagane dṛṣṭā vyacaranta yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: were all seen in the sky, moving about as they pleased.
And at night the night-wanderer moved on an improper path,
together with planets and with constellations, the lord of the sky, O subduer of enemies.
And the glorious sun in heaven became discolored.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ kabandhaṃ ca tathā lakṣyate sumahaddivi ||
children.translated_text: A dark headless trunk, and likewise a very great one, was seen in the sky.
Fire, moving over the earth, released a mass of flames,
and the blessed radiant one, standing in the sky, was seen again and again.

children.text: sapta dhūmranibhā ghorāḥ sūryā divi samutthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Seven terrible suns, smoke-colored, arose in heaven.
Planets stood at the horns of the moon as it stood in the sky.

children.text: vāme tu dakṣiṇe caiva sthitau śukrabṛhaspatī
children.translated_text: <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> stood on the left and on the right,
and <s>Śanaiścara</s> and the red-limbed one had a brilliance equal to blazing fire.
All those sky-roaming bodies mounted up together,
slowly and terribly, as planets revolving at the end of the age, upon the horns.
The moon, the dispeller of darkness, together with the constellations and planets,
did not favor <s>Rohiṇī</s>, for the destruction of moving and unmoving beings.
The moon, seized by <s>Rāhu</s>, was struck by meteors.
Blazing meteors moved about on the moon as they pleased.
Even he who is the god of the gods rained down blood.
Meteors fell from the sky, lightning-like and making a great sound.

children.text: akāle ca drumāḥ sarve puṣpanti ca phalanti ca
children.translated_text: Out of season all the trees flowered and bore fruit,
and all the creepers bore fruit, as did those plants said to foretell the destruction of daityas.

children.text: phalaiḥ phalānyajāyanta puṣpaiḥ puṣpaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: From fruits other fruits were born, and likewise from flowers a flower.

children.text: unmīlanti nimīlanti hasanti ca rudanti ca ||
children.translated_text: They opened and shut their eyes; they laughed and wept.

children.text: vikrośanti ca gambhīrā dhūmayanti jvalanti ca
children.translated_text: They cried out deeply, smoked, and burned.
The images of all the gods announced a great fear.
Wild and domestic animals and birds mingled together,
and there, when the great battle had arrived, they made a most terrifying sound.
The rivers flowed against their currents, with turbid waters.
The directions did not shine, being filled with red dust.
Sacred trees, though worthy of worship, were in no way honored.
They were struck by the force of the wind, broken, and bent down.

children.text: yadā ca sarvabhūtānāṃ chāyā na parivartate
children.translated_text: When the shadows of all beings no longer shifted,
though the sun had reached the afternoon, at the destruction of the worlds at the end of the age,
then above the mansion of the daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>,
honey appeared lodged in the treasury and armory.
For the destruction of the asuras and for the victory of the gods,
various terrible portents, signs of terror, were seen.

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavo ghorotpātāḥ samutthitāḥ
children.translated_text: These and many other dreadful portents arose,
fashioned by Time and seen for the destruction of the lord of daityas.
When the earth was trembling because of the great-souled lord of daityas,
mountains and hosts of nāgas of immeasurable power fell down.
With mouths filled with flames of poison, they released fire:
four-headed, five-headed, and seven-headed serpents.
<s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
<s>Elāmukha</s>, <s>Kāliya</s>, and the mighty <s>Mahāpadma</s>,
and the thousand-headed nāga, the lord <s>Hematāladhvaja</s>,
<s>Śeṣa Ananta</s>, greatly blessed and hard to shake, was shaken.
The blazing supports of the earth that stand within the waters,
were then shaken on every side by that great enraged one.
Those nāgas too, bearers of fiery power and dwellers on the floor of <s>Pātāla</s>,
were touched by the daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> when he touched the earth.
He bit the edges of his lips in anger, like the primeval boar.

children.text: nadī bhāgīrathī caiva sarayūḥ kauśikī tathā ||
children.translated_text: The river <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, and also <s>Sarayū</s> and <s>Kauśikī</s>,

children.text: yamunā tvatha kāverī kṛṣṇaveṇā ca nimnagā
children.translated_text: <s>Yamunā</s>, then <s>Kāverī</s>, and the descending river <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇā</s>,

children.text: suveṇā ca mahābhāgā nadī godāvarī tathā ||
children.translated_text: the greatly blessed <s>Suveṇā</s>, and likewise the river <s>Godāvarī</s>,
<s>Carmaṇvatī</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, and likewise the lord of streams and rivers,
<s>Kamalaprabhava</s>, and <s>Śoṇa</s> with jewel-like waters,

children.text: narmadā śubhatoyā ca tathā vetravatī nadī
children.translated_text: <s>Narmadā</s> of auspicious waters, and likewise the river <s>Vetravatī</s>,
<s>Gomatī</s>, crowded with cattle, and likewise the eastern <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Mahī</s>, <s>Kālamahī</s>, and <s>Tamasā Puṣpavāhinī</s>,
<s>Jambūdvīpa</s> and <s>Ratnavaṭa</s>, adorned with every jewel,
<s>Suvarṇaprakaṭa</s>, adorned with mines of gold,
<s>Mahānada</s> and <s>Lauhitya</s>, beautiful with mountains and forests,
the town <s>Kośakaraṇa</s>, a source of sages and heroic people,
the <s>Māgadhas</s>, the great villages, the <s>Muṇḍas</s>, and likewise the <s>Śuṅgas</s>,
the <s>Suhmās</s>, <s>Mallas</s>, <s>Videhas</s>, <s>Mālavas</s>, <s>Kāśis</s>, and <s>Kosalas</s>,
and the dwelling of <s>Vainateya</s> were shaken by the lord of daityas.
It had the form of the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s> and had been made by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
The red-watered, very terrible sea named <s>Lauhitya</s>,
and <s>Udaya</s>, the great mountain, rising up a hundred yojanas,
splendid, with golden terraces and attended by rows of clouds,
shining with trees made of gold and resembling the sun,
with flowering <s>śāla</s>, <s>tāla</s>, <s>tamāla</s>, and <s>karṇikāra</s> trees,
and the famous mountain <s>Ayomukha</s>, adorned with minerals,
and the auspicious mountain <s>Malaya</s>, fragrant with groves of <s>tamāla</s>,
the <s>Surāṣṭras</s> together with the <s>Bāhlīkas</s>, the <s>Śūras</s>, and likewise the <s>Ābhīras</s>,
the <s>Bhojas</s>, <s>Pāṇḍyas</s>, <s>Vaṅgas</s>, <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, and <s>Tāmraliptakas</s>,
and likewise the <s>Auṇḍras</s>, <s>Pauṇḍras</s>, <s>Vāmacūḍas</s>, and <s>Keralas</s>,
were shaken by that daitya, together with the gods and hosts of apsarases.
And the dwelling of <s>Agastya</s>, which had been made inaccessible in ancient times,
and the lovely assembly of siddhas and cāraṇas, was scattered,
with many varied birds and great trees in full flower,
with peaks made of gold and resounding with hosts of apsarases.
And <s>Giripuṣpitaka</s>, <s>Lakṣmīvān</s>, and pleasant-looking <s>Priyadarśana</s>,
rising up and splitting the ocean, the resting place of the moon and the sun,
shone with very great peaks, as if scratching the sky.
With rays like those of the moon and sun, covered with the ocean's waters,
the splendid <s>Vidyutvān</s> extended a hundred yojanas on every side.
There, on that best of mountains, lightning-flashes fall down.
And the mountain <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, splendid, known by the name <s>Vṛṣabha</s>,
the splendid mountain <s>Kuñjara</s>, where stands the auspicious house of <s>Agastya</s>,
and <s>Viśālākṣa</s>, hard to assail, the city that is the abode of serpents,
and likewise <s>Bhogavatī</s> also, were shaken by the lord of daityas.
And the mountain <s>Mahāsena</s> and the mountain <s>Pāriyātra</s>,
and <s>Cakravān</s>, best of mountains, and the mountain <s>Vārāha</s>,
and auspicious <s>Prāgjyotiṣapura</s>, made of gold,
in which lives the wicked-minded dānava named <s>Naraka</s>,
and <s>Megha</s>, best of mountains, with a sound deep as thunderclouds:
there, O best of twice-born ones, are sixty thousand mountains.
There is <s>Meru</s>, the great mountain, shining like the young sun,
its caves always frequented by yakṣas, rākṣasas, and gandharvas.
<s>Hemagarbha</s> is a great mountain there, and likewise the mountain <s>Hemasakha</s>.
And <s>Kailāsa</s>, lord of mountains, was shaken by the lord of dānavas.
By him the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> lake, covered with golden lotuses,
and <s>Mānasa</s>, thronged with geese and kāraṇḍava ducks, were also shaken.
And the three-peaked mountain, and <s>Kumārī</s>, best of rivers,
and the mountain <s>Mandara</s>, covered with heaps of snow,
and the mountain <s>Uśīrabindu</s>, and <s>Candraprastha</s>, king of mountains,
and <s>Prajāpatigiri</s>, and likewise the mountain <s>Puṣkara</s>,
and the mountain <s>Devābhra</s>, and likewise the mountain <s>Reṇuka</s>,
<s>Krauñca</s>, the mountain of the Seven Sages, and the smoke-colored mountain,

children.text: ete cānye ca girayo deśā janapadāstathā ||
children.translated_text: these and other mountains, and regions and countries as well,
and all the rivers together with the seas, that dānava shook.
And <s>Kapila</s>, son of the earth, and <s>Vyāghravān</s> too were shaken.
The sky-goers, the sons of <s>Satī</s>, dwelling in the levels of the underworld,
and another fierce host named <s>Megha</s>, armed with a goad,
the upward-going one of terrible speed: all of them were shaken.
Then <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, mace-bearing, spear-bearing, and fearsome,
dark like a mass of dense clouds, with a sound like a mass of dense clouds,
with a roar like a mass of dense clouds, swift like a cloud-bank,
the heroic son of <s>Diti</s>, enemy of the gods, rushed upon <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>.
Then, springing up, he was torn apart by the lion-lord
with sharp, great claws, and, with the aid of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, was slain in battle.

children.text: mahī ca kālaśca śaśī nabhaśca grahāśca sūryaśca diśaśca sarvāḥ
children.translated_text: The earth, Time, the moon, the sky, the planets, the sun, and all the directions,

children.text: nadyaśca śailāśca mahārṇavāśca gatāḥ prasādaṃ ditiputranāśāt ||
children.translated_text: the rivers, mountains, and great oceans became serene at the destruction of <s>Diti</s>'s son.
Then the delighted gods and the sages rich in austerity
praised the eternal primordial god with divine names.
"O god, this <s>Nārasiṃha</s> body which you have assumed:
people who know the higher and lower realities will worship precisely this."
The gods said:
"You are <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>, and great <s>Indra</s>, O best of gods.
You are the maker and unmaker of the worlds, their imperishable source.

children.text: parāṃ ca siddhiṃ ca paraṃ ca devaṃ paraṃ ca mantraṃ paramaṃ haviśca
children.translated_text: The supreme perfection, the supreme god, the supreme mantra, and the supreme oblation,

children.text: paraṃ ca dharmaṃ paramaṃ ca viśvaṃ tvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam ||
children.translated_text: the supreme <s>dharma</s> (sacred order) and the supreme universe: they call you the foremost, ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: paraṃ śarīraṃ paramaṃ ca brahma paraṃ ca yogaṃ paramāṃ ca vāṇīm
children.translated_text: The supreme body, the supreme <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality), the supreme yoga, and the supreme speech,

children.text: paraṃ rahasyaṃ paramāṃ gatiṃ ca tvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam ||
children.translated_text: the supreme secret and the supreme goal: they call you the foremost, ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ parasyāpi paraṃ padaṃ yatparaṃ parasyāpi paraṃ ca devam
children.translated_text: Thus that supreme state which is beyond even the beyond, and the god beyond even the beyond,

children.text: paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ ca bhūtaṃ tvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam ||
children.translated_text: and the being beyond even the beyond: they call you the foremost, ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ rahasyaṃ paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ mahattvam
children.translated_text: The secret beyond even the beyond, the greatness beyond even the beyond,

children.text: paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ mahadyattvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam ||
children.translated_text: and that great thing beyond even the beyond: they call you the foremost, ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ nidhānaṃ paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ pavitram
children.translated_text: The resting place beyond even the beyond, the purifier beyond even the beyond,

children.text: paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ ca dāntaṃ tvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam ||
children.translated_text: and the restrained one beyond even the beyond: they call you the foremost, ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>."
Having spoken thus, the blessed lord, grandsire of all the worlds,

children.text: stutvā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ brahmalokaṃ gataḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: praised the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and the lord went to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Then, while musical instruments resounded and apsarases danced,
<s>Hari</s>, the lord and master, went to the northern shore of the Milk Ocean.
The god established the very radiant <s>Nārasiṃha</s> body there,
and, assuming his ancient form, <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s> departed.
In a radiant vehicle with eight wheels, attended by beings,
the lord, the god whose nature is unmanifest prakṛti, went to his own place.
The sages said:
"The greatness of <s>Narasiṃha</s> has been told in detail.
Tell at length again another account of that very greatness.
How did this world, having the form of a lotus, become golden?
And how, in ancient times, did the Vaiṣṇava creation arise in the middle of the lotus?"
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard the greatness of <s>Narasiṃha</s>, the son of the Sun
with eyes widened and blooming in wonder again asked <s>Keśava</s>.
<s>Manu</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ pādme mahākalpe tava padmamayaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: How, in the great <s>Padma</s> kalpa, did your lotus-formed world
arise here in your navel while you were within the ocean of waters, O <s>Janārdana</s>?
By the power of <s>Padmanābha</s>, as he slept in the waters of the ocean,

children.text: puṣkare ca kathaṃ bhūtā devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: how in the lotus, formerly, did beings, gods, and the hosts of seers come to be?
Tell me all this fully, O lord of those who know yoga,
for as I listen to his glory no satiety arises in me.

children.text: kiyatā caiva kālena śete vai puruṣottamaḥ
children.translated_text: For how long does <s>Puruṣottama</s> indeed sleep,

children.text: kiyantaṃ vā svapiti ca ko'sya kālasya saṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and how long does he slumber? What is the origin of this time?
After how long a time does the greatly renowned one rise,
and how, having risen, does the blessed lord create the entire world?
Who, then, were the Prajāpatis at first, O great sage,
and how did he fashion the marvelous, eternal world?
When there was one ocean, empty, with the stationary and moving world destroyed,
with gods, asuras, and men burned up, and serpents and rākṣasas gone,
when wind and fire were gone from the world, and sky and earth had disappeared,
when it had become only a cavernous mass through the reversal of the great elements,
how does the all-pervading lord of the great elements, great in splendor and great in form,
the best of the excellent gods, remain there, knowing yoga and adopting the proper rule?
With highest devotion I would hear this completely, O <s>Brahmā</s>;
you should speak, most righteous one, the glory whose essence is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Blessed lord, you should speak to us who are seated here with faith.
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: nārāyaṇasya yaśasaḥ śravaṇe yā tava spṛhā
children.translated_text: The desire that you have to hear the glory of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>
is proper for one born in the succession of that lineage, O bull of the solar race.
Listen, as it has been heard in the ancient Purāṇas and from the Vedas,

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ ca vadatāṃ śrutvā vai sumahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: and as I heard it from the greatly virtuous brahmins who recited it,
and as, having seen it through austerity, the splendid son of <s>Parāśara</s>,
<s>Dvaipāyana</s>, the teacher equal in brilliance to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, declared it.
I shall tell that to you according to my ability and according to what I have heard,
as much as can be known by me, a mere seer, O best ones.
Who can undertake to know the supreme reality whose essence is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
which even <s>Brahmā</s>, source of the universe, does not truly understand?
That is the act of all the Vedas; that is the secret of the great seers.
He is the lord of all sacrifices and the truth contemplated by all who see.
He is what is pondered by knowers of the self, and he is hell for those who act wrongly.
He is the divine principle called <s>adhidaiva</s> and that which is well known as <s>adhiyajña</s>.
He is the being and the <s>adhibhūta</s>; he is the supreme object of the supreme seers.
He is the sacrifice prescribed by the Veda; the poets know him as austerity.

children.text: yaḥ kartā kārako buddhirmanaḥ kṣetrajña eva ca ||
children.translated_text: He is the agent, the instrument, intellect, mind, and the knower of the field.
He is understood as the praṇava, the <s>puruṣa</s>, the ruler, and the one.

children.text: prāṇaḥ pañcavidhaścaiva dhruva akṣara eva ca ||
children.translated_text: He is the fivefold breath, the fixed one, and the imperishable one.

children.text: kālaḥ pākaśca paktā ca draṣṭā svādhyāya eva ca
children.translated_text: He is time, ripening, the ripener, the seer, and sacred recitation.

children.text: ucyate vividhairdevaiḥ sa evāyaṃ na tatparam ||
children.translated_text: By the various gods he is spoken of in many ways; he alone is this, and there is nothing beyond him.

children.text: sa eva bhagavānsarvaṃ karoti vikaroti ca
children.translated_text: That blessed lord alone does everything and transforms everything.
He causes all of us to act, and he passes beyond us when we have been thrown into confusion.
We worship him alone as the first; fulfilled, we desire him alone.

children.text: yo vaktā yacca vaktavyaṃ yaccāhaṃ tadbravīmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever is the speaker, whatever is to be spoken, and whatever I am, that I speak to you.
Whatever is heard, whatever is fit to be heard, and whatever else is discussed,

children.text: yāḥ kathāścaiva vartante śrutayo vātha tatparāḥ
children.translated_text: whatever narratives proceed, and whatever sacred revelations are concerned with that,

children.text: viśvaṃ viśvapatiryaśca sa tu nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the universe and the lord of the universe: he is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: yatsatyaṃ yadamṛtamakṣaraṃ paraṃ yadyadbhūtaṃ paramamidaṃ ca yadbhaviṣyat
children.translated_text: Whatever is truth, immortal, imperishable, and supreme; whatever has been and whatever here will be,

children.text: yatkiṃcic caramacaraṃ yadasti cānyattatsarvaṃ puruṣavaraḥ prabhuḥ purāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever moving or unmoving thing exists, and whatever else there is: all that is the ancient lord, the best of persons.
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: catvāryāhuḥ sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tu kṛtaṃ yugam
children.translated_text: They say that the <s>Kṛta</s> yuga consists of four thousand years,
and its twilight is so many hundreds, with a second such interval, O son of the Sun.
In it <s>dharma</s> stands on four feet, while <s>adharma</s> has the form of one foot,
and in it good human beings are born devoted to their own <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: viprāḥ sthitā dharmaparā rājavṛttau sthitā nṛpāḥ
children.translated_text: Brahmins stand intent on <s>dharma</s>; kings stand in the conduct proper to rulers.
Vaiśyas are devoted to agriculture, and śūdras remain eager to serve.

children.text: tadā satyaṃ ca śaucaṃ ca dharmaścaiva vivardhate
children.translated_text: Then truth, purity, and <s>dharma</s> indeed increase,

children.text: sadbhirācaritaṃ karma kriyate khyāyate ca vai ||
children.translated_text: and the action practiced by the good is performed and becomes renowned.
This course of the <s>Kṛta</s> yuga has been described for all, O king,
even for living beings attached to <s>dharma</s>, even those of low birth.
The <s>Tretā</s> yuga is here said to be three thousand years,
and its twilight is proclaimed as so many hundreds, with a second such interval.
<s>Adharma</s> is established on two feet, while <s>dharma</s> stands on three,

children.text: yatra satyaṃ ca sattvaṃ ca tretādharmo vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: where truth and goodness are present; such is declared to be the <s>dharma</s> of <s>Tretā</s>.

children.text: tretāyāṃ vikṛtiṃ yānti varṇāstvete na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Tretā</s> these varṇas undergo alteration; there is no doubt.
Because of the alteration of the four-varṇa order, the āśramas become weakened.
This is the varied course of the <s>Tretā</s> yuga, fashioned by the gods.

children.text: dvāparasya tu yā ceṣṭā tāmapi śrotumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: You should also hear the activity that belongs to <s>Dvāpara</s>.

children.text: dvāparaṃ dve sahasre tu varṣāṇāṃ ravinandana
children.translated_text: <s>Dvāpara</s>, O son of the Sun, is two thousand years,
and its twilight is called so many hundreds, with a second interval completing the yuga.

children.text: tatra cārthaparāḥ sarve prāṇino rajasā hatāḥ
children.translated_text: There all creatures are intent on gain and are struck down by rajas,
and all are deceitful and petty, O son of the Sun.
<s>Dharma</s> stands on two feet, while <s>adharma</s> has risen on three,
and through reversal <s>dharma</s> gradually comes to destruction in the <s>Kali</s> yuga.
then likewise the eagerness for the state of brahmanical conduct falls apart.
Vows and fasts are abandoned at the turn of the <s>Dvāpara</s> age.

children.text: tathā varṣasahasraṃ tu varṣāṇāṃ dve śate api
children.translated_text: Thus one thousand years, and two hundred years as well,

children.text: saṃdhyayā saha saṃkhyātaṃ krūraṃ kaliyugaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: counted together with its twilight period, are remembered as the cruel <s>Kali</s> age.
There <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) stands on four feet, while <s>dharma</s> has the form of a single foot;
there human beings are born lustful and devoid of austerity.

children.text: naivātisāttvikaḥ kaścin na sādhurna ca satyavāk
children.translated_text: No one at all is very sattvic, no one is virtuous, and no one speaks truth;

children.text: nāstikā brahmabhaktā vā jāyante tatra mānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor are believers, or devotees of <s>Brahman</s>, born there among human beings.
They are seized by ego, and the bonds of affection have withered away;

children.text: viprāḥ śūdrasamācārāḥ santi sarve kalau yuge ||
children.translated_text: in the <s>Kali</s> age all brahmins follow the conduct of śūdras.
In the <s>Kali</s> age a reversal of the āśramas comes about,
and at the end of the age there is confusion among the varṇas, O son of the Sun.
One should know the period called a yuga, established before, as consisting of twelve thousand years;
and when this extends to a thousand such cycles, it is called a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Then, when that day has passed, for all living beings
he sees the cessation of their bodies, with the thought of destroying the worlds.
Of all the gods, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, O lord of the earth,
and of the <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Dānavas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and birds,
of <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, and serpents, O king,

children.text: parvatānāṃ nadīnāṃ ca paśūnāṃ caiva sattama
children.translated_text: of mountains and rivers, and of animals as well, O best of beings,
and of creatures born in animal wombs, and of worms too,
the lord of the great elements, the maker of beings, withdraws the five elements,
and for the destruction of the world he brings about a great slaughter.

children.text: bhūtvā sūryaścakṣuṣī cādadāno bhūtvā vāyuḥ prāṇināṃ prāṇajālam
children.translated_text: Having become the sun, he takes away the eyes; having become wind, he takes away the network of breaths of living beings;
having become fire, he burns all the worlds; having become a cloud again, fierce though he is, he rains.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Having become <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the yogin, the radiant one whose form is sattva,
he dries up the oceans with blazing rays.
Then, after drinking all the oceans, and the rivers and wells everywhere,
and taking all the water of the mountains with his rays,
he splits the earth with those rays, goes to <s>Rasātala</s>,
takes the water of <s>Pātāla</s>, and drinks the finest essence.
Whatever urine, blood, moisture, and anything else certainly exists in living beings,
all that the lotus-eyed supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> takes away.
And, becoming a mighty wind and shaking the whole world,
<s>Hari</s> draws out the vital winds, beginning with prāṇa, apāna, and samāna.

children.text: tato devagaṇāḥ sarve bhūtānyeva ca yāni tu
children.translated_text: Then all the hosts of gods, and whatever beings there are,

children.text: gandho ghrāṇaṃ śarīraṃ ca pṛthivīṃ saṃśritā guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and smell, the organ of smell, the body, and the qualities that rest in earth,

children.text: jihvā rasaśca snehaśca saṃśritāḥ salile guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: the tongue, taste, and fluidity, the qualities that rest in water,
form, the eye, and digestion, the qualities that rest in fire,

children.text: sparśaḥ prāṇaśca ceṣṭā ca pavane saṃśritā guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: touch, breath, and motion, the qualities that rest in wind,

children.text: śabdaḥ śrotraṃ ca khānyeva gagane saṃśritā guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: sound, hearing, and the cavities themselves, the qualities that rest in space,
the world's māyā is destroyed by the Blessed Lord in a moment.

children.text: mano buddhiśca sarveṣāṃ kṣetrajñaśceti yaḥ śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mind and intellect of all beings, and that which is known as the knower of the field,
<s>Parameṣṭhī</s> takes refuge in that most excellent <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>.
Then, surrounded by the rays of that Blessed Lord,
and lodged in the branches of trees as they are assailed by the wind,
fire, born from their friction, blazes up a hundredfold.
Then the saṃvartaka fire, enclosing it, burned everything,
together with mountains, trees, thickets, creepers, vines, and grasses.

children.text: vimānāni ca divyāni purāṇi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Divine aerial cars and various cities too,
all things that were places of refuge: all of these he burned.
Then, having reduced all the worlds to ashes, <s>Hari</s>, the teacher of the worlds,
again quenched them by the act belonging to the end of the age.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, mighty in strength, became a thousandfold rain in a hundred forms,
and with divine water as an oblation he satisfied the earth.
Then, through a mass of milk, through sweet and supreme water,
auspicious and holy, the earth attained supreme quiescence.

children.text: tena rodhena saṃchannā payasāṃ varṣato dharā
children.translated_text: Covered by that damming mass of waters as rain fell, the earth
became a single ocean of water, devoid of all living beings.
Even the great beings entered the all-powerful lord of immeasurable splendor,
when the sun, wind, and sky had vanished, and the subtle world was enclosed.
Having by himself dried up the oceans and embodied beings,

children.text: dagdhvā saṃplāvya ca tathā svapityekaḥ sanātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having burned and flooded them in this way, the one eternal being sleeps.
Assuming his ancient form, he of immeasurable valor sleeps;
as a yogin absorbed in yoga, he pervades the water of the single ocean.
For many thousands of yugas, in the water of the single ocean,
no one is able to know him, whether unmanifest or manifest.

children.text: kaścaiva puruṣo nāma kiṃyogaḥ kaśca yogavān
children.translated_text: What indeed is the being called <s>Puruṣa</s>? What is yoga, and who is possessed of yoga?

children.text: asau kiyantaṃ kālaṃ ca ekārṇavavidhiṃ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For how long will that lord perform the rite of the single ocean?
No one understands, 'Thus the Blessed Lord will do this.'

children.text: na draṣṭā naiva gamitā na jñātā naiva pārśvagaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no seer, no one who goes to him, no knower, and no attendant at his side;
nothing whatever of him is known, except by that best of gods himself.

children.text: nabhaḥ kṣitiṃ pavanam apaḥ prakāśakaṃ prajāpatiṃ bhuvanadharaṃ sureśvaram
children.translated_text: The sky, earth, wind, waters, the radiant one, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the bearer of worlds, the lord of gods,

children.text: pitāmahaṃ śrutinilayaṃ mahāmuniṃ praśāmya bhūyaḥ śayanaṃ hyarocayat ||
children.translated_text: the Grandsire, the abode of revelation, the great sage: having stilled them, he again took pleasure in sleep.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Thus, when the world has become a single ocean, the greatly radiant one lies there,
covering the earth with water, then as <s>Haṃsa Nārāyaṇa</s>.
In the midst of the great expanse of rajas, indeed in the waters of the great ocean,
they know as <s>brahman</s> (absolute reality) that which is free from rajas, mighty-armed, and imperishable.
The lord, covered by darkness, through the manifestation of his own nature,
having established the sāttvika mind, dwelt there as that truth.

children.text: yāthātathyaṃ paraṃ jñānaṃ bhūtaṃ tadbrahmaṇā purā
children.translated_text: That true supreme knowledge, the real, was formerly taught by <s>Brahmā</s>,
proclaimed in the secret forest-teachings, and remembered as what belongs to the Upaniṣads.
That which is celebrated as supreme, namely, '<s>Puruṣa</s> is sacrifice,'
and whatever other being is called <s>Puruṣa</s>: this is that supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: ye ca yajñakarā viprā ye cartvija iti smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: And the brahmins who perform sacrifice, and those remembered as officiating priests,

children.text: asmādeva purā bhūtā yajñebhyaḥ śrūyatāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: came into being from him alone in ancient times; now hear likewise about the sacrifices.
From his mouth the lord first created the brahman priest, and the udgātṛ, the singer of Sāmans,
and also the hotṛ and the adhvaryu from his two arms.
From the brahman priest came the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and in every way the prastotṛ;
those two, the maitrāvaruṇa and also the pratiprastātṛ, came from his back.
From his belly came the pratihartṛ and the potṛ, O king,
and from his thighs the acchāvāka and also the neṣṭṛ, O king.
From his hands came the agnīdhra, and know that the subrahmaṇya came from his knees;
from his feet came the grāvastut and the unnetṛ skilled in the Yajus.
In just this way the blessed lord, the ruler of the world,
created these sixteen foremost officiants, the expounders of all sacrifices.
This, then, is the Veda-formed <s>Puruṣa</s>, called sacrifice;
and all the Vedas, with their ancillary disciplines, Upaniṣads, and rites, consist of him.
When he slept in the single ocean, a wonder happened long ago;
hear how that curiosity of <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> arose, O brahmins.
The great sage, swallowed by that blessed lord, remained in his belly,
living for many thousands of years by the boon of that very lord's splendor.
Wandering in connection with pilgrimages over the earth, the field of sacred bathing places,
and through holy hermitages and temples of the deities,
through various lands, kingdoms, and cities of many kinds,
devoted to recitation and oblation, peaceful, and undertaking terrible austerity,
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> then slowly came out from his mouth;
but as he came out, because of the god's māyā (power of illusion), he did not know himself.
Having come out from his mouth, <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> then beheld the world as a single ocean,
covered on every side by darkness.
A sharp fear arose in him, and doubt about his own life;
yet he was thrilled at seeing the god and was filled with the greatest wonder.
Standing in the midst of the waters, <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, full of apprehension, reflected:

children.text: kiṃ nu syānmama cinteyaṃ mohaḥ svapno'nubhūyate ||
children.translated_text: 'What can this thought of mine be? Is a delusion or a dream being experienced?
Clearly one or another state among these has come about for me,
for such a world, afflicted and unfit, cannot truly deserve reality.
When moon, sun, and wind have vanished, and mountains and the surface of the earth have vanished,
what world can this be?' Thus he remained absorbed in thought.
And he saw a <s>Puruṣa</s>, mountain-like in size, asleep,
half submerged in the water, like a cloud in the ocean,
as if blazing with radiances, like the sun joined with rays,
as if awake in the night, shining with his own brilliance.
In wonder he asked, 'Who are you, who have come here to see the god?'

children.text: tathaiva sa muniḥ kukṣiṃ punareva praveśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then that same sage was made to enter the belly again.
Having again entered the belly, <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> was exceedingly amazed,
and again, just as before, he understood it as a vision seen in a dream.

children.text: sa tathaiva yathāpūrvaṃ yo dharāmaṭate purā
children.translated_text: In the same way as before, he roamed over the earth,
filled with waters of holy fords, and through various hermitages.
He saw sacrificers whose rites had been completed with excellent gifts,
and hundreds of twice-born priests, all standing within the god's belly.
All the social classes, beginning with the brahmins, were established in good conduct,
and the four āśramas (life-stages) were properly present, just as I have described them to you.
Thus, for more than a hundred years, while wise <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>

children.text: carataḥ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ na kukṣyantaḥ samīkṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: wandered over the whole earth, the end of the belly was not seen.
Then at some time he once more came out through the mouth,
and saw a single child asleep on the branch of a banyan tree.
There too, in the water of the single ocean, while the sky was veiled with mist,
he played undisturbed in a world devoid of all beings.
The sage, filled with wonder and possessed by curiosity,
could not look directly at the child, who resembled the sun.
Thinking thus, he stood alone near the water,
and, made doubtful by the god's māyā (power of illusion), considered it something seen before.
In that unfathomable water <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, full of wonder,
floated there and became distressed, his eyes terrified from fear.
Then the blessed lord, endowed with childlike yogic power, said to him, 'Welcome,'
and the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> spoke with a voice like a cloud.
'Do not be afraid, child; there is nothing to fear. Come here to my side.'
Exhausted by weariness, the sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> addressed that child.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: ko māṃ nāmnā kīrtayati tapaḥ paribhavanmama
children.translated_text: 'Who calls me by name, as though despising my austerity,
and as though challenging my age, famed as thousands of divine years?

children.text: na hyeṣa vaḥ samācāro deveṣvapi mamocitaḥ
children.translated_text: For such conduct toward me is not proper even among the gods;

children.text: māṃ brahmāpi hi deveśo dīrghāyuriti bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the gods, calls me long-lived.
Who today, having reached this terrible darkness and having abandoned life,
is fit to look upon death after calling me, "<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>"?'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having addressed him thus in anger, the great sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>
was again addressed in just the same way by the blessed <s>Madhusūdana</s>.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: ahaṃ te janako vatsa hṛṣīkeśaḥ pitā guruḥ
children.translated_text: I am your begetter, child; <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> is your father and guru,

children.text: āyuṣpradātā paurāṇaḥ kiṃ māṃ tvaṃ nopasarpasi ||
children.translated_text: the giver of life and the ancient one. Why do you not draw near to me?

children.text: māṃ putrakāmaḥ prathamaṃ pitā te'ṅgiraso muniḥ
children.translated_text: Your father, the sage <s>Aṅgiras</s>, desiring a son, first
worshiped me, resorting to severe austerity.
Then through terrible austerity he chose you, of immeasurable splendor,
and I spoke to the great seer of immeasurable splendor who dwelt within me.

children.text: kaḥ samutsahate cānyo yo na bhūtātmakātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: For who else could be capable, if he were not my son whose self is formed of beings,
of seeing me in the single ocean, playing along the path of yoga?
Then, with a joyful face and eyes wide open in wonder,
the greatly austere <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, holding his joined palms at his head,
declared his name and lineage; long-lived and honored by the worlds,
he then made obeisance with devotion to that Blessed One.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
I wish to know truly this <s>māyā</s> of yours, O sinless one,
by which you remain in the middle of the single ocean, having the form of a child.
By what name, O lord, are you known in the world?

children.text: tarkaye tvāṃ mahātmānaṃ ko hyanyaḥ sthātumarhati ||
children.translated_text: I judge you to be a great-souled one; for who else would be able to remain here?
