The Blessed Lord said:
I am <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, O brahman, the destroyer of all beings.
I am the one called thousand-headed, who is designated by the sacred words.
I am the <s>Puruṣa</s>, sun-colored; in the sacrifice I am the brahman-formed sacrifice.
I am <s>Agni</s>, carrier of oblations, and the imperishable lord of aquatic beings.
In <s>Indra</s>'s station I am <s>Śakra</s>; among years I am the full year.

children.text: ahaṃ yogī yugākhyasya yugāntāvarta eva ca ||
children.translated_text: I am the yogin of what is called the age, and the turning at the end of the age.
I am all beings, and all the deities without exception.
Among serpents I am <s>Śeṣa</s>, and among all birds I am <s>Tārkṣya</s>.
I am the end-maker of all beings, known as Time over all the universe.
I am <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), and I am austerity for those dwelling in all the āśramas.
I am the divine river, the Milk Ocean, and the great ocean.
That supreme truth is I; I alone am <s>Prajāpati</s>.
I am <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, and I am also yoga; I am that supreme state.
I am sacrifice and ritual action, and I am remembered as the lord of knowledge.
I am light, I am wind, I am earth, I am the sky.
I am the waters and the oceans, the lunar mansions and the ten directions.
I am rain, I am <s>Soma</s>, I am <s>Parjanya</s>, and I am the sun.
In the Milk Ocean and in the sea I am <s>Vaḍavāmukha</s>,
having become the fire of dissolution and drinking the water-formed oblation.
I am ancient, and likewise I am the supreme refuge.
I am the origin of what has been, what will be, and what is present.
Whatever you see, O brahmin, and whatever you hear at all,
and whatever you experience in the world, remember all that as me.

children.text: viśvaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ sṛjyaṃ cādyāpi paśya mām ||
children.translated_text: The universe was created by me before; see me even now as what is to be created.

children.text: yuge yuge ca srakṣyāmi mārkaṇḍeyākhilaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Age after age, O <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, I shall create the whole world.
Understand all this in its entirety, O <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>.

children.text: śuśrūṣurmama dharmāṃśca kukṣau cara sukhaṃ mama
children.translated_text: Wishing to hear my <s>dharmas</s> (sacred teachings), move happily within my belly.

children.text: mama brahmā śarīrastho devaiśca ṛṣibhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, together with the gods and sages, abides in my body.
Know me, enemy of the asuras, as the union of the manifest and the unmanifest.
I am the one-syllabled mantra, the imperishable one, and the liberating syllable.
The <s>oṃkāra</s>, beyond the three aims, is the indicator of the meanings of the three aims.
As the wise lord of the primordial Purāṇa was speaking in this way,
he quickly drew the great sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> into his mouth.
Then that best of sages entered the Blessed One's belly.
There, in that secluded place, he dwelt happily, wishing to serve the imperishable <s>Haṃsa</s>.
He who am I myself, assuming various bodies and resting in the great ocean when moon and sun have vanished,
that lord, though moving slowly and known as <s>Haṃsa</s>, creates the world and wanders at the turn of time.
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: āpavaḥ sa vibhurbhūtvā cārayāmāsa vai tapaḥ
children.translated_text: That mighty lord, having become <s>Āpava</s>, indeed practiced austerity,
covering his own body, born from the race of aquatic beings.
Then the great-souled and very powerful one set his mind on creating the world.
Universal himself, he contemplated the universe of the five great elements.
While he was thinking, in the motionless ocean,
in the subtle, deep, water-filled world without sky,
he slightly stirred that ocean, the receptacle of waters.
Then, long ago, through endless waves, a subtle opening arose.
From that, in response to sound, wind arose, born from the opening.
Having found a space, the unshakable wind increased.
As it grew strong, the ocean was violently agitated by its speed.
When that ocean was agitated and its waters were churned,
the great <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the lordly fire with a black path, came into being.
Then the fire dried up much water.
Through the diminution of the water-mass, the opening became the vast sky.
The holy waters arose from his own splendor and were like the essence of nectar.
Space was born from the opening, and wind was born from space.
From the friction of these two arose fire, born from wind.
Seeing this, <s>Mahādeva</s>, who manifests the great elements, was pleased.
Having seen the beings, the Blessed One, for the sake of world-creation, saw the supreme...
The many-formed one reflected on the birth of <s>Brahmā</s> as well.
When four yugas are reckoned, in a cycle of a thousand yugas,
the world-soul, born many times, is indeed called the oblation of <s>Brahmā</s>.
The knowledge that belongs on earth to the best of the twice-born,

children.text: jñānaṃ vṛṣṭaṃ tu viśvārthe yogināṃ yāti mukhyatām ||
children.translated_text: to those whose selves have been purified by austerity, is rained down for the good of the universe and attains preeminence among yogins.
Knowing him to be endowed with yoga and with complete supreme sovereignty,
the knower of yoga appointed the lord of the universe to the station of <s>Brahman</s>.
Then, in that great water, the lord of the earth, <s>Hari</s>, the unfailing one,
playing in the water according to rule, rejoiced as the maker of all worlds.
Then he produced a single lotus arising from his navel,
with a thousand petals, stainless, golden, and like the sun.
It stood there with a radiance blazing like the flaming crest of fire,
shining as a lotus of noble splendor, the lovely body-born growth of the great one.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Then he created the best of those endowed with yoga, abundant in splendor,
<s>Brahmā</s>, the creator of all worlds, facing every direction.
In that golden lotus, extending for many yojanas,
made of every brilliance and quality and furnished with earthly marks,
that lotus, knowers of the purāṇas say, is the supreme form of the earth;
the great seers declare that it arose from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: yā padmā sā rasā devī pṛthivī paricakṣyate
children.translated_text: The lotus is the goddess <s>Rasā</s>; she is called the earth.
Those heavy with the lotus's pith they know as the divine mountains.

children.text: himavantaṃ ca meruṃ ca nīlaṃ niṣadhameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Himavat</s>, <s>Meru</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and <s>Niṣadha</s>,
<s>Kailāsa</s>, <s>Muñjavant</s>, and also another, <s>Gandhamādana</s>,

children.text: puṇyaṃ triśikharaṃ caiva kāntaṃ mandarameva ca
children.translated_text: holy <s>Triśikhara</s>, <s>Kānta</s>, and <s>Mandara</s>,

children.text: udayaṃ piñjaraṃ caiva vindhyavantaṃ ca parvatam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Udaya</s>, <s>Piñjara</s>, and the mountain <s>Vindhyavant</s>:

children.text: ete devagaṇānāṃ ca siddhānāṃ ca mahātmanām
children.translated_text: these are refuges of the hosts of gods and of the great-souled siddhas,
of the pure in conduct, and they grant the fruit of every desire.
Between these is the region remembered as <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>;

children.text: jambūdvīpasya saṃsthānaṃ yajñiyā yatra vai kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: this is the arrangement of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, where sacrificial rites indeed take place.
The water that flows from these, resembling the flavor of divine nectar,
is remembered as delightful rivers, supports of hundreds of divine tīrthas.
What are remembered all around as the filaments of the lotus,
those on earth are the innumerable mineral mountains of the universe.

children.text: yāni padmasya parṇāni bhūrīṇi tu narādhipa
children.translated_text: The many petals of the lotus, O lord of men,
are imagined as inaccessible, mountain-covered lands of mlecchas.
The petals on the lower part are, by division, the dwellings
of daityas, serpents, and birds, O king.
Where their great ocean is, that is designated <s>Rasā</s>;
there human beings who have committed great sins sink down.
The earth within the lotus, situated in the single ocean,
was then said to have four reservoirs of water in all the directions.
Thus, for <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s purpose, the earth was born from the lotus;
therefore this manifestation is known by the name <s>Puṣkara</s>.
For this reason, by those who know it, by ancient supreme seers,
by ritualists, and through Vedic examples, the lotus rite is remembered in sacrifice.
Thus by that blessed lord the method for sustaining all beings

children.text: parvatānāṃ nadīnāṃ ca hradānāṃ caiva nirmitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was fashioned, including mountains, rivers, and lakes.
The all-pervading one, of incomparable power, sun-like, watery, and white in brightness,

children.text: śanaiḥ svayaṃbhūḥ śayanaṃ sṛjattadā jaganmayaṃ padmavidhiṃ mahārṇave ||
children.translated_text: then, the self-born, slowly created in the great ocean that lotus-formation, filled with the world, as his couch.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
An obstacle to austerity arose: a great asura named <s>Madhu</s>.

children.text: tenaiva ca sahodbhūto hyasuro nāma kaiṭabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with him arose the asura named <s>Kaiṭabha</s>.

children.text: tau rajastamasau viṣṇoḥ sambhūtau tāmasau gaṇau
children.translated_text: Those two, born from the rajas and tamas of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, were a dark pair,
of great strength, agitating the whole world in the single ocean.
They wore divine red garments and had white, blazing, terrible fangs.
They were lofty with crowns and earrings and shone with armlets and bracelets.
Their coppery eyes were opened wide; their chests were full and their arms were great.
They had the build of a great mountain, like two moving mountains.
They resembled new clouds, with faces like the sun,
and with their two hands, bright as lightning and grasping maces, they were exceedingly terrifying.
By setting down their feet, the two seemed to toss up the ocean,
and to shake <s>Hari</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>, as he lay there.

children.text: tau tatra vicarantau sma puṣkare viśvatomukham
children.translated_text: As the two were wandering there in the lotus, they approached the all-faced one,
and then saw the blazing best of yogins.
Appointed by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, he was creating all creatures,
the gods and all beings: mind-born asuras and seers.
Then those two excellent asuras spoke there to <s>Brahmā</s>,
shining, intent on killing him, enraged, their eyes disturbed by anger.
Who are you, standing in the middle of the lotus, white-turbaned and four-armed?
Assuming restraint out of delusion, you sit there free from distress.
Come here, approach. Give battle to us, O lotus-born one.
Against us, supreme lords, you are powerless here in the ocean.

children.text: tatra kaścodbhavastubhyaṃ kena vāsi na yojitaḥ
children.translated_text: What origin do you have there, and by whom have you been placed here?

children.text: kaḥ sraṣṭā kaśca te goptā kena nāmnā vidhīyase ||
children.translated_text: Who is your creator, and who is your protector? By what name are you designated?
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
The one is spoken of by people as inconceivable, the thousand-eyed one.
Through connection with him, let both of you understand your deed and your names.
<s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> said:
There is nothing higher than the two of us in the world, O great-minded one;

children.text: āvābhyāṃ chādyate viśvaṃ tamasā rajasātha vai ||
children.translated_text: by us indeed the universe is covered with <s>tamas</s> (darkness) and then with <s>rajas</s> (passion).
We two are made of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, not to be overstepped even by seers;
while we cover even those devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), we are hard for all embodied beings to cross.
By us the world is bewildered, hard as we are to master, age after age;
we two are <s>artha</s> (material aim) and <s>kāma</s> (desire), sacrifice, and the attainment of heaven.

children.text: sukhaṃ yatra mudā yuktaṃ yatra śrīḥ kīrtireva ca
children.translated_text: Where there is pleasure joined with delight, where there are prosperity and fame,
whatever anyone longs for, think that very thing to be us two.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: yatnād yogavato dṛṣṭyā yogaḥ pūrvaṃ mayārjitaḥ
children.translated_text: With effort, through the vision of one possessed of yoga, yoga was formerly won by me;
having composed it with its qualities, I have taken refuge in <s>sattva</s> (clarity).
He who is supreme, intent on yoga, called Yoga, and is <s>sattva</s> itself,
who is the creator of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> and the origin of the universe,
from him arise beings, both sāttvika and otherwise;

children.text: sa eva hi yuvāṃ nāṃśe vaśī devo haniṣyati ||
children.translated_text: that very self-controlled god, and no mere portion of him, will slay you both.
Then, as he slept, the glorious one, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>,
made an arm extending many yojanas by his own māyā (power of illusion).
Then, dragged by the arm of that strong-armed one,
those two moved about, slipping away like two plump birds.
Then both of them went and addressed that eternal god;
having bowed down to <s>Padmanābha</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, they stood there together.
We know you as the womb of the universe, you alone as the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>;
protect us two; this is our purpose, the cause of our understanding.

children.text: amoghadarśanaḥ sa tvaṃ yatastvāṃ vidvaḥ śāśvatam
children.translated_text: You are he whose vision is unfailing, since we know you to be eternal;
therefore the two of us have come to look upon you from nearby.
Therefore we wish for a wonderful boon from you, O god, subduer of enemies;
your vision is unfailing. Homage to you, victor in battle.
The blessed lord said:

children.text: kimarthaṃ hi drutaṃ brūtaṃ varaṃ hyasurasattamau
children.translated_text: Tell me quickly what you seek as a boon, best of asuras;

children.text: dattāyuṣkau punar bhūyo raho jīvitum icchathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having been granted long life, do you wish once more to live on in secrecy?
<s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> said:
In whatever place no one has died, O god, O lord, declare our death there;
we desire that death, and may our death come from you, O great-vowed one.
The blessed lord said:
So be it. You two excellent ones, when the future time arises,
will indeed be; there is no doubt. I speak this truth to you both.

children.text: varaṃ pradāyātha mahāsurābhyāṃ sanātano viśvavaraḥ surottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after granting the boon to the two great asuras, the eternal lord, the best of gods and blessing of the universe,

children.text: rajastamovargabhavāyanau yamau mamantha tāvūrutalena vai prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the powerful one crushed those two twins, whose source was the class born of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, upon the surface of his thighs.
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: sthitvā ca tasminkamale brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Standing upon that lotus, <s>Brahmā</s>, best of those who know brahman,
with arms raised upward and of great brilliance, undertook terrible austerity.
Blazing as it were with his powers and dispelling darkness with his own radiances,
established in every <s>dharma</s> (sacred law), he shone like the thousand-rayed sun with its rays.
Then, assuming another form, the imperishable <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as <s>Śaṃbhu</s>,
of great splendor, famous and teacher of yoga, came there.
And wise <s>Kapila</s>, the teacher of Sāṃkhya, the excellent brahmin,
both great-souled, intent on the field, praised him.
Having arrived there, the two spoke to <s>Brahmā</s> of immeasurable power,
knowers of the distinction between higher and lower, and honored by the great seers.
Firmly bound to the self that is brahman, vast, abiding in the world,
<s>Brahmā</s>, leader of all beings, was honored by the three worlds.
Hearing the words of those two, <s>Brahmā</s>, knower of yoga, addressed in return,
made these three worlds, as this is the sacred revelation of <s>Brahmā</s>.
And the sage produced one son for <s>Śaṃbhu</s>;
before him <s>Brahmā</s> stood restraining his speech, as the imperishable tāmasa form.
As soon as he was born, the mind-born son said to <s>Brahmā</s>,
What help shall we perform for you? Let the blessed seer command.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
This <s>Kapila</s>, O brahman, is also made of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;
whatever truth he tells you, do that, O great-minded one.

children.text: brahmaṇastu tadarthaṃ tu tadā bhūyaḥ samutthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then for that purpose he rose up again before <s>Brahmā</s>,
saying, With folded hands I wish to serve you two; what shall I do?
The blessed lord said:
That which is true, imperishable brahman is indeed eighteenfold;
that which is truth and that which is cosmic order, remember that as the supreme state.
Having heard this speech alone, he went to the northern direction;
and, going there, he attained the state of <s>Brahmā</s> through the splendor of knowledge.
Then lord <s>Brahmā</s> created a second one named <s>Bhuva</s>,
having conceived him with his mind, that very great-minded one.
Then he spoke this statement: What shall I do, grandfather?
commanded by the grandfather, he approached <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Bhuva</s> then practiced brahman and went to the earth;

children.text: prāptaśca paramaṃ sthānaṃ sa tayoḥ pārśvamāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having reached the supreme station, he came to the side of those two.
When that son also had gone, the lord created a third,
a mighty one skilled in the path of liberation, named <s>Bhūrbhuva</s>.
Having attained lordship as protector, he too reached the same course as those two.
Thus these three sons of great-souled <s>Śaṃbhu</s> have been declared.
Taking those sons of his, he went to the state won by himself;
so did blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Kapila</s>, lord of ascetics.

children.text: yaṃ kālaṃ tau gatau muktau brahmā taṃ kālameva hi
children.translated_text: At the very time when those two, liberated, had departed, <s>Brahmā</s> then

children.text: tato ghoratamaṃ bhūyaḥ saṃśritaḥ paramaṃ vratam ||
children.translated_text: again undertook the most terrible supreme vow.
Then thereafter <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord, did not delight while practicing austerity alone.
Then from half of his body he produced a beautiful wife,

children.text: tapasā tejasā caiva varcasā niyamena ca
children.translated_text: a goddess equal to himself in austerity, brilliance, splendor, and restraint,
and capable of creating the worlds.
Together with her, concentrated there, <s>Brahmā</s> delighted while practicing austerity.
Then he uttered the three-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s>, honored by the Veda.
While creating, the mighty one created the lords of creatures and the oceans,
and also the four other Vedas, born from <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
The Grandfather created sons like himself,

children.text: viśve prajānāṃ patayo yebhyo lokā viniḥsṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: universal lords of creatures, from whom the worlds issued forth.
First of all he created <s>Viśveśa</s>, his own son, a great ascetic,

children.text: sarvamantrahitaṃ puṇyaṃ nāmnā dharmaṃ sa sṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: holy and endowed with all mantras, named <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: dakṣaṃ marīcimatriṃ ca pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum
children.translated_text: He created <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Kratu</s>,
and also <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and <s>Manu</s>.
And these, known also as the wondrous paternal seers,
the great seers, received <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with thirteen qualities.
<s>Aditi</s>, <s>Diti</s>, <s>Danu</s>, <s>Kālā</s>, <s>Anāyu</s>, <s>Siṃhikā</s>, and <s>Muni</s>,

children.text: tāmrā krodhātha suratā vinatā kadrureva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmrā</s>, <s>Krodhā</s>, then <s>Suratā</s>, <s>Vinatā</s>, and <s>Kadru</s> too:
these twelve daughters, O king, were the offspring of <s>Dakṣa</s>.
<s>Kaśyapa</s>, son of <s>Marīci</s>, was fashioned, it is said, by austerity.

children.text: tasmai kanyā dvādaśānyā dakṣastāḥ pradadau tadā
children.translated_text: To him <s>Dakṣa</s> then gave those twelve maidens,

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi ca somāya tadā vai dattavānṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the seer also gave the lunar mansions to <s>Soma</s> at that time,
all the auspicious ones beginning with <s>Rohiṇī</s>, O son of <s>Ravi</s>.

children.text: lakṣmīrmarutvatī sādhyā viśveśā ca matā śubhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Marutvatī</s>, <s>Sādhyā</s>, and auspicious <s>Viśveśā</s> are so regarded,

children.text: devī sarasvatī caiva brahmaṇā nirmitāḥ purā
children.translated_text: and the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> too: these were created of old by <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: etāḥ pañca variṣṭhā vai suraśreṣṭhāya pārthiva ||
children.translated_text: These five most excellent ones, O king,
were given by <s>Brahmā</s>, whose work had been seen, to the blessed <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: yā tu rūpavatī patnī brahmaṇaḥ kāmarūpiṇī ||
children.translated_text: But the beautiful wife of <s>Brahmā</s>, who could assume forms at will,

children.text: surabhiḥ sā hitā bhūtvā brahmāṇaṃ samupasthitā
children.translated_text: became <s>Surabhi</s> and, being kindly disposed, attended upon <s>Brahmā</s>.
Then the world-honored <s>Brahmā</s> approached her for sexual union.
The best of beings knew the cause of world-creation and acted for the sake of cattle.
In her were born his sons, vast and smoke-colored,
resembling night, twilight, and clouds, blazing with fierce brilliance.
They cried out, ran about, and reproached the Grandfather.
Because of their crying and running, they were thereafter remembered as <s>Rudras</s>.
<s>Nirṛti</s>, <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, and, third, <s>Aparājita</s>,
<s>Mṛgavyādha</s>, <s>Kapardī</s>, <s>Dahana</s>, and then <s>Īśvara</s>,
blessed <s>Ahirbudhnya</s>, <s>Kapālī</s>, and also <s>Piṅgala</s>,
and <s>Senānī</s>, great in splendor: these are remembered as the eleven <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: tasyāmeva surabhyāṃ ca gāvo yajñeśvarāśca vai ||
children.translated_text: From that same <s>Surabhi</s> came cows and the lords of sacrifice,
and from <s>Surabhi</s> came excellent, imperishable animals and wondrous powers.
Goats too, and geese, and likewise the supreme nectar,
and the foremost herbs arose from excellent <s>Surasā</s>.
From <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s> bore <s>Kāma</s>, and <s>Sādhyā</s> gave birth to the <s>Sādhyas</s>:

children.text: bhavaṃ ca prabhavaṃ caiva hīśaṃ cāsurahaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Prabhava</s>, <s>Hīśa</s>, and also <s>Asurahan</s>,
<s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Āruṇi</s>, <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, <s>Bala</s>, and <s>Dhruva</s>,
<s>Haviṣya</s>, <s>Vitāna</s>, and also <s>Vidhāna</s> and <s>Śamita</s>,
<s>Vatsara</s>, <s>Bhūti</s>, and <s>Sarvāsuraniṣūdana</s>,
and <s>Suparvāṇa</s> and <s>Bṛhatkānti</s>: these <s>Sādhyas</s> are honored by the worlds.
The goddess who followed <s>Vāsava</s> indeed gave birth to the gods.

children.text: varaṃ vai prathamaṃ devaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhruvamavyayam
children.translated_text: She bore first the excellent god, and second the imperishable <s>Dhruva</s>,
third <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, and fourth the lord <s>Soma</s>.
Then came <s>Anurūpa</s> and <s>Māya</s>, and after them <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: saptamaṃ ca tathā vāyumaṣṭamaṃ nirṛtiṃ vasum ||
children.translated_text: then seventh <s>Vāyu</s>, and eighth <s>Nirṛti</s> the <s>Vasu</s>.
This offspring of <s>Dharma</s> was born from <s>Sudevī</s>.

children.text: viśve devāśca viśvāyāṃ dharmājjātā iti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the <s>Viśve Devas</s>, according to tradition, were born from <s>Dharma</s> in <s>Viśvā</s>.
<s>Dakṣa</s>, mighty-armed, and <s>Puṣkarasvana</s>,
the <s>Cākṣuṣa Manu</s>, and also <s>Madhu</s> and great-serpent <s>Mahoraga</s>,
<s>Viśrāntaka</s>, <s>Vapur</s>, <s>Bāla</s>, and glorious <s>Viṣkambha</s>,
and <s>Garuḍa</s>, of surpassing strength and vigor, with brilliance like the sun:
the divine mother <s>Viśveśā</s> gave birth to these sons, the <s>Viśve Devas</s>.
<s>Marutvatī</s> gave birth to sons, the gods called <s>Marutvats</s>.

children.text: agniṃ cakṣuṃ ravirjyotiḥ sāvitraṃ mitrameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Cakṣus</s>, <s>Ravi</s>, <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Sāvitra</s>, and <s>Mitra</s>,

children.text: amaraṃ śaravṛṣṭiṃ ca sukarṣaṃ ca mahābhujam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Amara</s>, <s>Śaravṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Sukarṣa</s> the mighty-armed,

children.text: virājaṃ caiva vācaṃ ca viśvāvasumatiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Virāja</s>, <s>Vāc</s>, and likewise <s>Viśvāvasumatī</s>,
<s>Aśvamitra</s>, <s>Citraraśmi</s>, and <s>Niṣadhana</s>, O king,
<s>Hūyanta</s>, <s>Vāḍava</s>, <s>Cāritra</s>, and <s>Mandapannaga</s>,

children.text: bṛhantaṃ vai bṛhadrūpaṃ tathā vai pūtanānugam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhanta</s>, <s>Bṛhadrūpa</s>, and likewise <s>Pūtanānuga</s>:

children.text: marutvatī purā jajña etānvai marutāṃ gaṇān
children.translated_text: of old <s>Marutvatī</s> gave birth to these hosts of <s>Maruts</s>.
<s>Aditi</s> bore from <s>Kaśyapa</s> precisely the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>:
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, and <s>Ravi</s>,

children.text: pūṣā mitraśca dhanado dhātā parjanya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, and <s>Parjanya</s>.
These are the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, the most excellent dwellers in heaven.

children.text: ādityasya sarasvatyāṃ jajñāte dvau sutau varau ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Sarasvatī</s>, two excellent sons were born to <s>Āditya</s>,
supreme in austerity, supreme in qualities, and honored even in heaven.
But <s>Danu</s> bore the <s>Dānavas</s>, and <s>Diti</s> gave birth to the <s>Daityas</s>.

children.text: kālā tu vai kālakeyānasurānsurasā tu vai
children.translated_text: <s>Kālā</s> bore the <s>Kālakeya</s> asuras, and <s>Surasā</s> also bore asuras.
The sons of <s>Anāyuṣā</s> were diseases, exceedingly powerful.
<s>Siṃhikā</s> indeed was the mother of the grahas, and <s>Muni</s> the mother of the gandharvas;
while <s>Tāmrā</s>, O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>, was the mother of the apsarases and of the meritorious ones.
From <s>Krodhā</s>, O <s>Pārthiva</s>, all beings were born, and also piśācas;
and she gave birth to hosts of yakṣas and also to rākṣasas, O lord of the people.
Four-footed creatures were born, and likewise the fragrant cows;
and <s>Vinatā</s> gave birth to the suparṇas and the birds.
The goddess <s>Kadrū</s> gave birth to all the nāgas, the mountain-supporters of the earth;
in this way all the worlds grew and prospered, O scorcher of foes.
Then, O king, there was the manifestation called <s>Pauṣkara</s> of the great-souled one;
that <s>Pauṣkara</s> manifestation has been declared to you by me, as <s>Dvaipāyana</s> taught it.
The ancient Person, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Hari</s>, the lord,
has been described to you by me in due order, praised by the supreme seers.

children.text: yaścedamagryaṃ śṛṇuyātpurāṇaṃ sadā naraḥ parvasu gauraveṇa
children.translated_text: And the man who always hears this foremost Purāṇa with reverence on festival days,

children.text: avāpya lokānsa hi vītarāgaḥ paratra ca svargaphalāni bhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: having reached those worlds, free from passion, enjoys the fruits of heaven hereafter.

children.text: cakṣuṣā manasā vācā karmaṇā ca caturvidham
children.translated_text: In the fourfold way, by eye, mind, speech, and action,
whoever pleases <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in turn is gracious to him.
A king obtains a kingdom, and a poor man obtains excellent wealth;
one whose life is diminished obtains long life, and one desiring a son obtains a son.
Sacrifices, Vedas, desires, and various austerities too,

children.text: prāpnoti vividhaṃ puṇyaṃ viṣṇubhakto dhanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: the devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> obtains varied merit and also riches.
Whatever thing he desires, that very thing comes from the lord of the world.

children.text: sarvaṃ vihāya ya imaṃ paṭhetpauṣkarakaṃ hareḥ ||
children.translated_text: The man who, abandoning everything, recites this <s>Pauṣkara</s>

children.text: prādurbhāvaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha na tasya hyaśubhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: manifestation of <s>Hari</s>, O best of kings, has no misfortune at all.
This manifestation of the great-souled one is called <s>Pauṣkara</s>;
it has been recounted to you, O greatly fortunate one, on the authority of what was heard from <s>Vyāsa</s>.
<s>Matsya</s> said:

children.text: viṣṇutvaṃ śṛṇu viṣṇośca haritvaṃ ca kṛte yuge
children.translated_text: Hear of the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and of his <s>Hari</s>-hood in the Kṛta age,

children.text: vaikuṇṭhatvaṃ ca deveṣu kṛṣṇatvaṃ mānuṣeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: his <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>-hood among the gods and his <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-hood among human beings.

children.text: īśvarasya hi tasyaiṣā karmaṇāṃ gahanā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: For the course of that lord's actions is profound;
now hear, O king, exactly as it is, of what is past and what is to come.
He who is unmanifest, abiding in a manifest sign, this blessed lord,
is indeed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, endless in self, the source and the undecaying one.
This same eternal <s>Hari</s>, having become <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, was

children.text: brahmā vāyuśca somaśca dharmaḥ śakro bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
He also becomes the son of <s>Aditi</s> again and again, age after age;
this all-pervading one is famed as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the younger brother of <s>Indra</s>.
The cause of <s>Aditi</s>'s having a son was born from the favor of this mighty one,
for the sake of slaying the enemies of the gods, the daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas.
Formerly this lord, whose self is primordial nature, created <s>Brahmā</s>;
and that primal person created the prajāpatis in the ancient kalpa.
There they created unsurpassed humans belonging to the lineage of <s>Brahmā</s>;
from those great-souled ones the eternal sacred knowledge arose in many forms.
This is the recounting of the deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, wondrous in being,
worthy to be proclaimed in the worlds; understand it from me as it is proclaimed.

children.text: vṛte vṛtravadhe tatra vartamāne kṛte yuge
children.translated_text: There, when the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s> had been undertaken, in the Kṛta age,
there was a battle famous throughout the three worlds, called <s>Tārakāmaya</s>.

children.text: yatra te dānavā ghorāḥ sarve saṅgrāmadurjayāḥ
children.translated_text: In that battle those dreadful dānavas, all hard to conquer in combat,
were striking down all the hosts of gods, together with yakṣas, serpents, and rākṣasas.
Being struck down, turning away, their weapons exhausted in battle,
the gods went in their minds to the lord god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as their protector.
At that moment clouds, with the luster of extinguished embers,
covered the expanse of the sky together with the sun, moon, and host of planets.
Fierce, accompanied by masses of lightning and making terrible roars,
the winds blew together, struck by one another's force.
With blazing waters, thunderbolt-flashes, and fires and winds swift as the thunderbolt,
the sky, with exceedingly dreadful sounds and portents, seemed as though it were burning.
Then thousands of meteors fell, even those moving in the sky;
and heavenly aerial cars fell and flew upward in confusion.
The fear that would arise for the worlds at the close of the four ages
took visible forms amid those ominous signs.

children.text: jātaṃ ca niṣprabhaṃ sarvaṃ na prājñāyata kiṃcana
children.translated_text: Everything became bereft of light, and nothing could be discerned;
surrounded by a mass of darkness, the ten directions did not shine.
Kālī, embodied, entered, veiled by black clouds of Time;
the sky did not shine, its sun overwhelmed, covered by terrible darkness.
Then the lord, casting aside with his two arms those dense clouds filled with darkness,
revealed his divine form, <s>Hari</s> with a dark body.
It was like a rain cloud and collyrium, with body hair like rain clouds,
dark in brilliance and in body, like a black, unmoving mountain.
He wore a blazing yellow garment and ornaments of heated gold;
his body was like smoke and darkness, as though the fire at the end of the age had arisen.
His shoulders were stout, four times doubled, and his hair was covered by a crown;
he shone, adorned with weapons bright like refined gold.
With the radiance of the rays of moon and sun, he rose up like a mountain peak;
his hand was gladdened by <s>Nandaka</s>, and he bore arrows like venomous serpents.
Lofty with wondrous strength and a spear, bearing conch, discus, and mace,
he was a mountain of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, rooted in the earth, a tree of fortune with <s>Śārṅga</s> as its horn.
He gave generous fruit to the thirty gods and had lovely shoots in the women of heaven;
he was beloved by the minds of all worlds and charming to all beings.
with many celestial chariot-platforms as its branches, streaming water, cloud-water, and honey,
rich in knowledge and ego as its essence, with the great elements as its sprouts;
covered with the leaves of particularized beings, flowering with planets and stars,
having the daitya-world as its great trunk and made manifest in the mortal world;
roaring with the form of the ocean, with the netherworld as its great support,
spread out with lion-snares and frequented by birds and living creatures;
rich in the lovely fragrance of virtue and wealth, the great tree of all worlds,
with the unmanifest as its endless water and the manifest ego as its foam;
with masses of waves that are the great elements, and planets and stars as its bubbles,
covered by celestial vehicles as birds and noisy with clouds;
filled with multitudes of fish-like creatures and furnished with groups of mountains as shells,
with whirlpools made of the three guṇas and their objects, and with all the worlds as great sea-monsters;
with heroic trees, creepers, and shrubs, and with serpents as the raised-up seaweed,
with the twelve suns as great islands and the eleven Rudras as towns;
with the eight Vasus as mountains, the great ocean of the waters of the three worlds,
with the waters of dawn and dusk as numbered waves, attended by <s>Suparṇa</s> and the wind;
with hosts of daityas and rākṣasas as crocodiles, crowded with yakṣas and serpents as fish,
possessing the great power of <s>Pitāmaha</s> and adorned with all jewel-like women;
beautified by rivers that are <s>Śrī</s>, fame, beauty, and prosperity,
swift in its great tidal moments of time, yoga, dissolution, and creation;
that great ocean of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, whose far shore is great yoga,
the god above the gods, the boon-giver, tender toward the devotion of his devotees,
the gracious god, auspicious, bringing peace to the faculties,
in a chariot yoked with bay horses and served by a <s>Suparṇa</s>-banner,
fashioned with planets, moon, and sun, surrounded by the excellent eyes of <s>Mandara</s>,
furnished with endless rays, broad in the cavern of <s>Meru</s>,
flowered with bright stars and beautiful with planets and constellations,
in the sky, giving fearlessness amid dangers, the gods, defeated by the daityas,

children.text: dadṛśuste sthitaṃ devaṃ divye lokamaye rathe
children.translated_text: saw that god standing in a divine chariot composed of the worlds.
All those gods, with <s>Śakra</s> at their head, joined their palms;
placing cries of victory before them, they went for refuge to him who gives refuge.

children.text: sa teṣāṃ tāṃ giraṃ śrutvā viṣṇurdaivatadaivatam ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the divinity of the gods, had heard that speech of theirs,
he set his mind on the destruction of the dānavas in the great battle.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, standing in the sky and assuming the highest form,
spoke this pledged word to all the deities:

children.text: śāntiṃ vrajata bhadraṃ vo mā bhaiṣṭa marutāṃ gaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Go to peace; welfare to you. Do not fear, hosts of the Maruts.

children.text: jitā me dānavāḥ sarve trailokyaṃ parigṛhyatām
children.translated_text: All the dānavas have been conquered by me. Let the three worlds be taken back.
Satisfied by the words of that truth-pledged <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
the gods came to joy, as though they had drunk the finest nectar.
Then that darkness was gathered up, and the clouds vanished.

children.text: pravavuśca śivā vātāḥ praśāntāśca diśo daśa
children.translated_text: Auspicious winds blew, and the ten directions became calm.
The luminaries and the moon, pure in radiance, made a clockwise circuit.
The planets did not come into conflict, and the oceans too grew calm.
The paths of the three classes beginning with the heavenly host became free of dust.
The rivers flowed according to their proper courses, and the seas did not swell.
Auspicious senses arose within the inner selves of men.
The great seers, free from sorrow, recited the Vedas aloud.

children.text: yajñeṣu ca haviḥ pākaṃ śivamāpa ca pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the sacrifices the fire brought the oblation to auspicious cooking.
The worlds became engaged in dharma, their minds joyful,
when they heard <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s pledged speech about the death of the enemies.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Then, having heard <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s fearless word, the daityas and dānavas
made vast preparations for battle and for victory.
But <s>Maya</s> made a golden, imperishable chariot, three nalvas in length,
with four wheels, very broad, and with a great yoke well fitted;
resounding with a network of small bells and adorned with leopard-skins,
beautiful and shining with nets of jewels and nets of gold;
filled with herds of artificial deer and bright with rows of birds,
bearing divine weapons and quivers, rumbling like a cloud;
with fine axles, noble as the best of chariots, having a good platform and resembling the sky,
filled with maces and iron clubs, like the ocean embodied;
with golden armlets and bracelets, and with a circular golden pole-box,
furnished with banners and standards, like <s>Mandara</s> together with the sun;
at times having the bulk of a lordly elephant, at times the brilliance of a lion,
yoked with a thousand bears and filled with the sound of prosperous clouds;
blazing, moving through the sky, divine, and crushing enemy chariots,
he mounted that chariot, eager for battle, like the blazing sun mounting <s>Meru</s>.
A chariot as wide as the distance of a loud cry, entirely made of gold,
mountain-shaped, unobstructed, and resembling a mass of dark collyrium;
divine, made of black iron, with its pole-box bound by iron shafts,
emitting rays of darkness and roaring like a cloud;
covered with a great iron mesh fitted with windows,
filled with iron clubs, missiles, and hammers;
spread with spears, nooses, and detached spikes,
adorned with terrifying devices, javelins, and battle-axes;
rising up for the sake of the enemies, like a second <s>Mandara</s>,
and yoked with a thousand asses: he mounted that excellent chariot.
But <s>Virocana</s>, enraged, stood with mace in hand
at the front of that army, like a mountain with blazing peaks.
The dānava <s>Hayagrīva</s>, however, was accompanied by a thousand chariots.
The crusher of rival armies drove his chariot.
He stretched and twanged a great bow a thousand kiṣkus long.
<s>Varāha</s> stood at the front like a mountain covered with shoots.
But <s>Khara</s>, streaming pride and water born of anger from his eyes,
with teeth, lips, and eyes quivering, longed for battle.
The powerful <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, the <s>Dānava</s>, mounted a terrible crafted elephant as his vehicle,
and moved about to arrange the <s>Dānava</s> battle formation.
<s>Śveta</s>, son of <s>Vipracitti</s>, adorned with white earrings,
looking like a white mountain, stood facing the battle.
<s>Ariṣṭa</s>, son of <s>Bali</s>, and <s>Variṣṭha</s>, whose weapon was a slab of rock,
stood facing the battle, making the earth and mountains tremble.
And <s>Kiśora</s>, in excessive excitement, was urged on as <s>Kiśora</s>;
and the <s>Dānavas</s> with their forces armed themselves in due order.
In the midst of the <s>Daitya</s> army he appeared like the risen sun;
<s>Lamba</s>, dark like a fresh cloud, was adorned with trailing garments.
Standing in the <s>Daitya</s> array, he shone like the sun amid mist;
and <s>Svarbhānu</s>, who fought with his mouth, had teeth, lips, and eyes as weapons.
Laughing, that great seizer stood at the front of the <s>Daityas</s>.
Some there were mounted on horses, and others on the shoulders of elephants;
others were mounted on lions and tigers, and still others on boars and bears.
Some rode donkeys and camels, and some had beasts of prey as their mounts.
Other <s>Daityas</s> were foot soldiers, terrifying and misshapen-faced;
one-footed and half-footed, they danced, eager for battle.
Many slapped their arms, and others likewise uttered war-cries;
the foremost <s>Dānavas</s> roared with the cry of delighted tigers.
They bore terrible clubs and iron bars, with rocks and pestles in their hands,
and threatened the gods with arms shaped like iron bars.
With nooses, lances, iron bars, javelins, hooks, and paṭṭiśas,
they sported with śataghnīs and with hundred-edged hammers.
With boulder-peaks and mountains, and with bars of the finest iron,
and with discus weapons, the foremost <s>Daityas</s> made the army rejoice.
That entire <s>Dānava</s> army, fierce with the intoxication of battle,
stood facing the gods like a swelling mass of clouds.
That wondrous force, packed with thousands of <s>Daityas</s>, like wind, fire, mountains, cloud, and water,
surging up as the flood of battle arose, seemed mad with the desire to fight.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
You have heard the extent of the <s>Daitya</s> army, O son of <s>Ravi</s>;
now hear the Vaiṣṇava extent of the army of the gods.

children.text: ādityā vasavo rudrā aśvinau ca mahābalau
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, and the two mighty <s>Aśvins</s>,
with their forces and attendants, armed themselves in due order.
<s>Puruhūta</s>, the thousand-eyed guardian of the world, stood in front;
the leader of all the gods mounted the elephant of the gods.
In its midst was his chariot, like a supreme swan among all birds,
with beautiful wheel-feet, adorned with gold and vajra.
It was followed by hosts of gods, Gandharvas, and Yakṣas in their thousands,
and praised by shining officiants and brahmarṣis.
It was joined to masses of clouds born from the pealing of the thunderbolt and lit by lightning and rainbows,
like mountains moving at will.
Mounted on it, the blessed one travels around the whole world;
at the opening of the sacrifice, priests stationed at the havirdhānas sing.
In heaven, as <s>Śakra</s> proceeds and the divine instruments resound,
hundreds of bands of beautiful <s>Apsarases</s> dance all around.
Shining with the serpent-king as his banner, like the sun,
and yoked with a thousand horses as swift as mind and wind,

children.text: sa syandanavaro bhāti gupto mātalinā tadā
children.translated_text: that best of chariots, then guided by <s>Mātali</s>, shone,
like the whole of <s>Meru</s> surrounded by the brilliance of the sun.
<s>Yama</s>, raising his staff, and <s>Kāla</s> with his mace,
stood in the army of the gods, terrifying the <s>Daityas</s> with their roar.
Accompanied by the four oceans and by flickering serpents,
wearing conch, pearl, and armlets, and bearing a body made of water,
casting about the nooses of Time, with horses like moonbeams,
wind-driven and water-like, performing thousands of sportful maneuvers,
with pale garments shaken out and coral-bright armlets,
excellent, with a fine body dark as a jewel, set upon a tawny team,
<s>Varuṇa</s>, noose in hand, stood in the midst of the gods' army,
longing for the hour of battle, like an ocean that had burst its shore.
With an army of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, and also with hosts of Guhyakas,
and joined by the treasures <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Padma</s>, the powerful lord of treasures,
the splendid lord of kings, mace in hand, was seen;
<s>Dhanada</s>, fighting from the sky-chariot, stood in the <s>Puṣpaka</s> aerial car.
That king of kings, seeking battle and borne by men, shone,
mounted on a bull in combat, like <s>Śiva</s> himself visibly present.
The thousand-eyed one guarded the eastern wing; the king of the ancestors guarded the southern;
<s>Varuṇa</s> guarded the western wing, and the man-borne one the northern.
Thus the four mighty Lokapālas were assigned to the four quarters;

children.text: svāsu dikṣu svarakṣanta tasya devabalasya te ||
children.translated_text: each in his own direction, they guarded that army of the gods.
The Sun, with a chariot yoked to seven horses and ranging without limit,
blazing with splendor and with shining rays...
With the wheel of rising and setting, going to Mount <s>Meru</s>,
with the blazing wheel that is the gate of heaven, heating the imperishable world,
endowed with a thousand rays and gleaming with radiance,
the twelve-formed lord of day moved in the midst of the worlds.
<s>Soma</s>, possessed of cool rays, shines in a chariot with white horses,
delighting the world with beams filled with the waters of the snowy mountain.
The dānavas saw that cool-rayed lord of the twice-born, followed by hosts of constellations,
his body marked with the shadow of a hare, the destroyer of night darkness,
the lord of the luminaries in the sky, the master who gives sap to the saps,
the storehouse of thousands of herbs and of nectar,

children.text: jagataḥ prathamaṃ bhāgaṃ saumyaṃ satyamayaṃ ratham
children.translated_text: the first share of the world, gentle, truth-formed, a chariot of calmness,
<s>Soma</s>, standing there with frost as his weapon.

children.text: yaḥ prāṇaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ pañcadhā bhidyate nṛṣu
children.translated_text: He who is the breath of all beings, divided fivefold among men,
who, abiding in the seven bodily constituents, upheld and traversed the three worlds,
whom they call the kindler of fire, the lord who is the source of all,
and who, present in the seven notes, is constantly uttered by voices,
whom they call the highest being, whom they call bodiless,
whom they call sky-going, swift-moving, and joined with sound,
that <s>Vāyu</s>, the life of all beings, arisen by his own power,
blew against them together with rain-clouds, shaking the daityas.
The Maruts, together with divine gandharvas and bands of vidyādharas,
played with bright swords like serpents newly released.
The serpent-lords, producing fierce poison made of water,
moved through the sky as arrows for the lords of heaven, with mouths gaping wide.
With mountains, rocky peaks, and hundreds of trees,
the hosts of gods came forward to strike the army of dānavas.
That god who is <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Padmanābha</s>, and <s>Trivikrama</s>,
dark like the fire at the end of an age, lord of the whole universe,
source of all births, slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, eater of oblations, established in sacrifice,
whose self consists of earth, water, sky, and the elements, dark-hued, peace-making, destroyer of foes,
the mace-bearer, slayer of the enemies of the immortals, took up his discus that destroys foes,
and raised it with supreme brilliance, like the sun rising from among serpents.
With his left hand he grasped the great mace, destroyer of all asuras,
black in form and giving the time of death to enemies.
With his other arms the mighty lord, whose banner bears the enemy of serpents,
held the blazing array of weapons, <s>Śārṅga</s> and the rest.
He mounted the bird, son of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, twice-born, eater of serpents,
swifter in flight than the wind and shaking the sky,
made splendid by the lord of serpents lodged in his mouth,
lofty like Mount <s>Mandara</s>, released at the beginning of the nectar-churning,
whose valor had been seen many times in clashes of gods and asuras,
and who, for the sake of nectar, had been marked by <s>Mahendra</s>'s thunderbolt.
He was crested and strong, adorned with heated earrings,
clothed in variegated feathers, like a mountain rich in minerals.
A shining jewel, equal in brilliance to the cool-rayed moon, hung from his broad chest,
attached to the coil of a serpent and radiant with gem-light.
With his two wings, beautiful in their feathers, he covered the sky in play,
like two clouds with rainbows covering the firmament at the end of an age.
He was adorned with blue, red, and yellow banners,
his vast body hidden beneath the appearance of standards.
In the battle the glorious lord mounted the younger brother of <s>Aruṇa</s>,
<s>Suparṇa</s>, the best of sky-goers, whose body was golden in color.
The hosts of gods and the concentrated sages followed him,
and with hymns and supreme mantras they praised <s>Janārdana</s>.
That army, joined with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> and led by <s>Vaivasvata</s>,
surrounded by the king of the twice-born and made splendid by the king of the gods,
vast with the moon's radiance, turned toward battle,
resounding as it was struck by the wind and with sacrificial fire blazing.
By the splendor of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the victorious and brilliant one, its darkness was covered over,
and that strong, mighty, uplifted army turned toward battle.
"May there be welfare for the gods," <s>Bṛhaspati</s> said.
"May there be welfare in the dānava army," <s>Uśanas</s> uttered his words.
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Then a tumultuous conflict arose between those two armies,
of the gods and the asuras, each seeking victory over the other.
The dānavas, together with the deities, raised many kinds of weapons,
and, fighting, they met one another like mountains against mountains.
That battle, joined by gods and asuras, appeared exceedingly wondrous,
joined with dharma and adharma, with pride and humility.
Then, with chariots torn away from their teams and with elephants driven on,
and with warriors flying up on every side into the sky, swords in hand,
with pestles being hurled and arrows falling down,
with bows being drawn and hammers being made to fall,
that terrible battle, thronged with gods and dānavas, arose,
bringing terror to the world and resembling the dissolution at the end of an age.
With clubs hurled from their hands and with mountains torn loose,
the dānavas struck the gods in battle, with <s>Indra</s> at their head.
Being slain by the powerful dānavas, whose splendor seemed victorious,
the gods, their faces downcast, reached extreme distress in the fight.
They were crushed by missiles and spears, their heads split by clubs,
Their chests split by the sons of <s>Diti</s>, they vomited much blood from their wounds.
Surrounded by nets of arrows and rendered helpless by the asuras,

children.text: praviṣṭā dānavīṃ māyāṃ na śekuste viceṣṭitum ||
children.translated_text: they had fallen under the dānava māyā and could not move.
The army seemed to have gone to its setting, its form like something lifeless;
the force of the gods had been made by the asuras into one whose weapons could make no effort.
Cutting off with the thunderbolt those terrible arrows loosed from daitya bows,
<s>Śakra</s>, the many-eyed one, entered the terrible army of the daityas.
Having killed the foremost daityas, he then attacked that great dānava army
and made it darkness itself with a net of tāmasa weapons.
They could not recognize one another, nor the vehicles of the gods,
being possessed by dreadful darkness through the splendor of <s>Puruhūta</s>.
But the best of the gods, freed from the bonds of māyā and exerting themselves,
struck down the bodies of the daitya-lions that had become darkness.
Shattered and unconscious because of the blue-hued darkness,
those hosts of dānavas fell like mountains whose wings had been cut off.
Then the darkness around the daitya lords, grown dense, was like darkness in the ocean;
the dānava, destroyer of the gods, seemed to have become darkness itself.
Then <s>Maya</s>, blazing, released that great dark māyā,
created by the <s>Aurva</s> fire and producing a blaze like that at the end of an age.
Then that māyā devised by <s>Maya</s> burned all things,
and the daityas, their bodies like suns, immediately rose up in the battle.
As the heaven-dwellers were being burned, having encountered the <s>Aurva</s> māyā,
they resorted to the sphere of the moon, which gives water with cool rays.
Their minds lost as they were burned by the <s>Aurva</s> fire,
the scorched gods, seeking refuge, spoke to the wielder of the thunderbolt.

children.text: saṃtate māyayā sainye hanyamāne ca dānavaiḥ
children.translated_text: When the army was enveloped by māyā and was being slain by the dānavas,
<s>Varuṇa</s>, urged by the king of the gods, spoke these words:
In ancient times, O <s>Śakra</s>, a son of a brahmarṣi practiced very terrible austerity,
<s>Ūrva</s>, endowed with ancient splendor and equal to <s>Brahmā</s> in qualities.
While he, like the sun, was scorching the imperishable world with his austerity,
hosts of sages attended upon him, together with divine seer-gods.
And <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, the dānava lord of the dānavas,
also petitioned that supremely radiant seer in ancient days.
The brahmarṣis spoke to him a speech joined with dharma:
Blessed one, among the lineages of seers this station has had its root cut off.
You are alone and without offspring, and there is no other born in the lineage;
having undertaken the vow of youth, you follow only hardship.
Many lineages, O brahmin, of purified-minded sages
stand as single bodies, isolated and without progeny.
With roots cut off in this way, there is no means for us through sons;
but you are foremost through austerity, with splendor equal to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
Therefore turn yourself toward the lineage; increase yourself by yourself.

children.text: tvayā dharmo'rjitastena dvitīyāṃ kuru vai tanum ||
children.translated_text: Since dharma has been won by you, make indeed a second body.

children.text: sa evamukto munibhir munir marmasu tāḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the munis, the muni, struck to the quick,
rebuked those groups of seers and spoke this word:

children.text: yathāyaṃ vihito dharo munīnāṃ śāśvataḥ purā
children.translated_text: As this eternal dharma of munis was ordained long ago,
for one who practices the seerly rite and eats forest roots and fruits,
for a Brahmin born from the source of <s>Brahmā</s> and seeing the self,
well-practiced brahmacarya would move even <s>Brahmā</s>.
There are three ways of life for people who dwell in the householder stage;
but for us who dwell in the forest stage, this way of life is best.
Those who live on water, those who live on air, and those whose teeth are mortars,
those who crush with stones, those who do not eat, and those who endure the five fires,
these stand in tapas through vows that are extremely hard to perform,
putting brahmacarya first and seeking the highest goal.
From brahmacarya a Brahmin's Brahminhood is ordained;
so say people in the higher world who know brahmacarya.

children.text: brahmacarye sthitaṃ satyaṃ brahmacarye sthitaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Truth is established in brahmacarya; tapas is established in brahmacarya.

children.text: ye sthitā brahmacarye tu brāhmaṇā divi saṃsthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Brahmins who are established in brahmacarya are established in heaven.

children.text: nāsti yogaṃ vinā siddhirna vā siddhiṃ vinā yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no siddhi without yoga, nor fame without siddhi;
in the world there is no tapas, the root of fame, higher than brahmacarya.
He who restrains the whole group of the senses and the fivefold group of beings,
and undertakes brahmacarya: what tapas is higher than this?
Keeping hair without yoga, performing vows without resolve,

children.text: abrahmacarye caryā ca trayaṃ syād dambhasaṃjñakam ||
children.translated_text: and practice without brahmacarya: these three are called hypocrisy.

children.text: kva dārāḥ kva ca saṃyogaḥ kva ca bhāvaviparyayaḥ
children.translated_text: What have wives to do with this? What has union to do with it? What has reversal of true condition to do with it?

children.text: nanviyaṃ brahmaṇā sṛṣṭā manasā mānasī prajā ||
children.translated_text: Was not this mind-born progeny created by <s>Brahmā</s> with his mind?
If there is power in the tapas of you whose selves are known,
then create mind-born sons by the act of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
A womb made by the mind is to be established by ascetics;

children.text: na dārayogo bījaṃ vā vratamuktaṃ tapasvinām ||
children.translated_text: neither union with a wife nor seed is declared to be the vow of ascetics.
This statement here, aiming at the loss of dharma, which you have uttered fearlessly,
though you are good men, I judge it to be altogether as if uttered by the bad.
Having made this body into a mind-made form with blazing inner self,
without union with a wife I shall create a son born from my own body.
Thus my own self will beget for me a second self,
by this forest rule, as though wishing to burn up creatures.
But <s>Ūrva</s>, possessed by austerity, placed his thigh in the sacrificial fire.
With a single blade of darbha grass he churned the fire-stick that was the source of a son.
Suddenly splitting his thigh, flame-garlanded and without fuel,
a son, <s>Agni</s>, was born, eager to burn the world.
Breaking forth from <s>Ūrva</s>'s thigh, the fire named <s>Aurva</s>, the destroyer,
was born, exceedingly wrathful, as if he wished to burn the three worlds.
As soon as he was born, he spoke to his father in a faint voice:

children.text: kṣudhā me bādhate tāta jagadbhakṣye tyajasva mām ||
children.translated_text: "Hunger torments me, father; release me to eat the world."
Yawning with flames that rose to the third heaven and filled the ten directions,
that destroying fire grew, burning all beings.
Meanwhile <s>Brahmā</s>, honoring the sage <s>Ūrva</s>,

children.text: uvāca vāryatāṃ putro jagataśca dayāṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: said, "Let your son be restrained, and have compassion for the world.
For this offspring of yours, O brahmin, I shall make an excellent place.

children.text: tathyametadvacaḥ putra śṛṇu tvaṃ vadatāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: This word is true, my son; listen, best of speakers."
<s>Ūrva</s> said:
"Blessed am I and favored, since today the lord gives
this thought concerning my child here as a supreme kindness.
When morning has arrived, at the desired time of meeting,
with what oblations, O lord, will my son be satisfied and attain happiness?

children.text: kutra cāsya nivāsaḥ syādbhojanaṃ vā kimātmakam
children.translated_text: And where will his dwelling be? What will his food consist of?
May the lord prescribe here what befits the power of the greatly mighty one."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
"His dwelling shall be in the ocean, in the mare's mouth.

children.text: mama yonirjalaṃ vipra tasya pītavataḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: Water is my womb, O brahmin; happiness will be his when he has drunk it.
Where I remain constantly, drinking the water-formed oblation,
that oblation and that abode I assign to your son.

children.text: tato yugānte bhūtānāmeṣa cāhaṃ ca putraka
children.translated_text: Then, at the end of the age, this one and I, my son,
shall wander together among beings, taking away the debt of those without sons.

children.text: eṣo'gnir antakāle tu salilāśī mayā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: At the final time this fire has been made by me an eater of waters,
the burner of all beings, together with gods, asuras, and rākṣasas."
Saying "So be it," that fire, his circle of flames drawn in,
entered the ocean's mouth after casting his radiance upon his father.

children.text: pratiyātastato brahmā ye ca sarve maharṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> returned, and all the great seers,

children.text: aurvasyāgneḥ prabhāṃ jñātvā svāṃ svāṃ gatimupāśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: having understood the splendor of <s>Aurva</s>'s fire, resorted each to his own path.
Seeing that great wonder then, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>,
bowing deeply with all his limbs, spoke these words:
"Lord, this astonishing thing has occurred before the witness of the world.
By your ascetic power, best of sages, the Grandfather has been pleased.

children.text: ahaṃ tu tava putrasya tava caiva mahāvrata
children.translated_text: But I am to be understood as the servant of your son and of you yourself,
O great-vowed one, if any task here can be accomplished by action.
Therefore see me as fully arrived, devoted to your worship alone.
If I should fail, best of sages, that would indeed be your defeat."
<s>Aurva</s> said:
"Blessed am I and favored, since I have become your guru.
Through this ascetic power I have no fear here today, O good-vowed one.

children.text: tāmeva māyāṃ gṛhṇīṣva mama putreṇa nirmitām
children.translated_text: Take that very māyā, made by my son,
fire-formed, without fuel, and hard to assail even for fires.
For the subduing of enemies it will be obedient to you and to your lineage;
it will protect your own side and burn up the opposing side."
Saying "So be it," he accepted it, bowed to the foremost sage,
and the lord of the dānavas went joyfully to heaven, his purpose fulfilled.
This unbearable māyā, difficult even for the gods to approach,
was formerly made by <s>Aurva</s>, the son of <s>Ūrva</s>, through the fire.

children.text: tasmiṃstu vyutthite daitye nirvīryaiṣā na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: But when that daitya has risen up, it is powerless; there is no doubt.

children.text: śāpo hyasyāḥ purā dattaḥ sṛṣṭā yenaiva tejasā ||
children.translated_text: For a curse was formerly pronounced upon it by the very energy by which it was created.
If this is to be repelled and the lord is to be made happy,
give me as a companion, O <s>Śakra</s>, the night-maker whose source is water.
Together with him, and surrounded by aquatic beings,
I shall destroy this māyā by your favor; there is no doubt."
<s>Matsya</s> said:
Then <s>Śakra</s>, delighted, the increaser of the thirty gods,
ordered <s>Soma</s>, whose weapon is coldness, to the front for battle:

children.text: gaccha soma sahāyatvaṃ kuru pāśadharasya vai
children.translated_text: "Go, <s>Soma</s>; give aid to the noose-holder
for the destruction of the asuras and for the victory of the dwellers in heaven.
You are a power matching me, and the lord of lords among the luminaries.
Those who know rasa know the essence in all worlds to consist of you.
Your waning and waxing are manifest in the disk, like those of the ocean;
you revolve day and night, setting time in motion in the world.
Your mark, resembling a hare, is made of the shadow of the world;

children.text: na viduḥ soma devāpi ye ca nakṣatrayonayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: not even the gods, nor those born from the constellations, know it, O <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: tvam ādityapathād ūrdhvaṃ jyotiṣāṃ copari sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: You stand above the path of the sun and above the luminaries;
driving away darkness with your radiance, you illuminate the whole world.
White-rayed, cold-bodied, the moon, lord of the luminaries,
appointed over the conjunctions of time, beloved, the imperishable rasa of sacrifice,
lord of herbs, source of rites, sharer in <s>Hara</s>'s crest,
cool-rayed, receptacle of nectar, restless, with a white vehicle,

children.text: tvaṃ kāntiḥ kāntivapuṣāṃ tvaṃ somaḥ somapāyinām
children.translated_text: you are the beauty of those whose bodies are beautiful; you are <s>Soma</s> for the soma-drinkers.
You are gentle to all beings; you are the dispeller of darkness and king of the stars.
Therefore go, mighty one, with <s>Varuṇa</s> and his army;

children.text: śamaya tvāsurīṃ māyāṃ yayā dahyāma saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: pacify the asuric māyā by which we are burned in battle."
<s>Soma</s> said:
"What you tell me for the sake of battle, O king of gods, giver of boons,
I pour down this cold, which draws away the daityas' magic.
Look at these, burned by my cold and wrapped in frost,
the lion-like daityas in the great battle, bereft of magic and bereft of pride.
Having spoken thus, the lord of the stars, together with the lord of waters, with auspicious waters
flooded the armies of the gods for the increase of peace.
The snowy showers, sent forth by the maker of cold and furnished with nooses,
surrounded those dreadful daityas like masses of clouds.
